# Phase 1: Decision Core Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Build the rest of `core` (the typed disc model, identification, the title planner, the audio and subtitle track rules, naming and track layout, the verification rule, the disposition, the job state reducer) and the `lazymkv-dev plan` command plus the `decide` extension, so that a recording's plan, decisions, confidences and review reasons print as JSON on any OS.

**Architecture:** Every new rule is a pure function in `crates/core` over typed inputs: the parsed scan becomes a `Disc`, the recorded or synthetic database answers become `lookup` types, and the facts the engine will measure in phase 2 (packet MD5s, ffprobe profiles, subtitle events, the content and text verdicts, library facts, the owner's review decisions) are explicit input structs, so nothing in `core` reads a file, runs a program or touches the network. The disc phase is `plan::plan` (identity, kind, titles, mode, two confidences) and the file phase is `decision::decide` (audio, subtitles, layout, path, three confidences, disposition); `verify` checks a ripped or remuxed file against the scan or the decision, and `job::reduce` is the state machine the phase 2 engine will drive. `crates/dev` does the reading: `plan` prints the disc phase for a recording or a pinned scan log, and `decide` gains `plan` and `decision` sections while its existing sections and goldens stay byte-identical.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 1.99.0, edition 2021; `serde` (derive), `serde_json` (`preserve_order`, `float_roundtrip`), `regex`, `unicode-normalization` (NFC for 8.9), `md-5`, `sha1`, all already in the workspace. No new dependency.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-04-lazymkv-design.md` (the design spec; sections 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.4, 9.5, 10.1, 10.2, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16 bind this plan) and `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-rust-port-design.md` (what already exists; its rulings RP1 to RP9). The rulings RP10 to RP20 of this plan's brief (RP15 as RP25 amends it), and RP21 to RP27 made while writing it, are recorded in full in section "Rulings" of the plan's front matter and bind every task.

**Branch:** `phase-1-decision-core`, from `main` (at `666fc16`, the merge of pull request #2).

## Global Constraints

- Toolchain Rust 1.99.0, edition 2021 (`Cargo.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml`); every `cargo` command runs on the mini PC through `scripts/box.sh cargo <args>` (never two at once); CI builds and tests on Linux, macOS and Windows without the evidence clone.
- No new dependency: only `serde`, `serde_json` (`preserve_order`, `float_roundtrip`), `regex`, `fancy-regex`, `unicode-normalization`, `md-5`, `sha1`; no `chrono`, no `clap`, no `bitflags` crate (flags are a plain `u32` newtype).
- `core` has no I/O (spec 4.2, RP19): every new function takes parsed values, text or `&dyn Tree`; reading recordings, printing and exit codes live in `crates/dev`.
- No new crate; new `core` modules go under `crates/core/src/`, new commands under `crates/dev/src/cmd/`, dev integration tests under `crates/dev/tests/`.
- The one-copy rule: never redefine `Scan`, `Attrs`, `Message`, `duration_seconds`, `int_attr`, `segments`, `dvd_scan`, the language tables (`B_TO_T`, `norm_lang`, `NO_LANGUAGE`, `TMDB_NO_LANGUAGE`, `ISO639`, `iso639`), `align::events`, `align::aligned`, `align::is_text`, `text::{Track, Decision, Role, Rule, decide}`, `reconcile::{removed_streams, expected_rows, DURATION_TOLERANCE_S}`, `audio::labels::DERIVED`, `recording::files::{Tmdb, thediscdb_answer, lookup_statuses}`, `hit_rate::{lookup, statuses}`, `DecideDoc`, `pyjson::dumps`. `audio::reference::{is_lossless, rank, placed_first, programme_reference}` stay the Python-exact rule the content rule and its goldens use (RP6, RP7); `tracks::audio::{rank_key, guards}` and `codec::Codec.lossless` are the product's 8.6 steps 3 and 4 over scan facts (RP20) and are the only other copy. The 8.7 thresholds live once in `subtitle::text::Rule`; `Settings::text_rule` builds it from the settings and `tracks::subtitle`'s two fixed values are pinned equal to it by a test.
- `core::reconcile` and its goldens stay byte-identical (RP6, RP11); `decide`'s existing sections `slug`, `label`, `reconcile`, `audio`, `subtitles`, `reviews` and their goldens stay byte-identical (RP14): new sections are appended after `reviews`.
- New modules are written from the spec, not from any Python (RP20): no `py_*` spellings, no `Ordered` in new types; `BTreeMap` for every keyed collection, with string or integer keys only, and no map keyed by an integer or a struct in a type that is serialised inside a document, a stored file or an event (a sorted `Vec` of named entries instead, RP23 and the conventions' "Keyed collections"); `serde` derives with the struct's field order and the spec's snake_case key spellings.
- Review reasons and notes are closed sets: the spec's exact snake_case strings, as enums with `as_str()` and `#[serde(rename = "...")]` to that spelling; every rule's confidence is an `f64` holding the spec's exact constant: identity 1.00, 0.99, 0.95, 0.90 (capped at 0.84 with `tmdb_only_autofile` off), 0.50, 0; title 0.98, 0.90, 0.85, 0.60; audio 0.95; subtitles 0.95, 0.90, 0.85, 0.60; 1.00 for whatever a remembered or review decision covers (spec 5, 8.8); `auto_threshold` 0.85.
- The fixed values of spec 14 are named constants, never settings: the 3% and 15% runtime checks, the 2 s duration match (`disc::DURATION_MATCH_S`, pinned equal to `reconcile::DURATION_TOLERANCE_S`), the 10% full-track share and the 150-event forced limit, the 256 kb/s guard G1, the 768 kb/s and 1.5 Mb/s tier thresholds, the 10% rival band and 0.25 segment difference of 8.3, the 45-minute `feature_min_minutes` default, the 15 to 120 minute episode band and 15% spread of 8.2, the 1% DVD duration band of 6.2, the 255-byte, 90-character and 32-character caps of 8.9 and 8.4, the 64-byte `sub_clear_max_bytes` default, the 5% and 2% space margins of section 7, the 10-minute and hourly retry waits of 10.1.
- Settings (spec 14) are one `core::settings::Settings` struct with the spec's defaults; every pure rule takes `&Settings` by reference and reads only the keys it needs.
- Every public item has a `///` doc saying what it is and the spec section it implements; every file starts with a `//!` paragraph naming its spec sections. Prose: plain sentences, no em-dashes, acronyms expanded at first use.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the bottom of the file, or a sibling `tests.rs` for a module above about 900 lines (counting the module's code; Task 3's `lookup/discdb.rs` and Task 5's `plan/movie.rs` keep their tests in-file by design); test names in snake_case that read as sentences. Tests that read the evidence clone (`corpus/owner`) live in `crates/dev/tests/` (Task 2's `disc_model.rs`, Task 3's `lookup_answers.rs`, Task 12's `verify.rs`, Task 15's `plan.rs`, Task 16's `decide.rs`, Task 17's `labels_subtitles.rs`, Task 18's `retune_subtitles.rs`) and print `skipped: <reason>` through `lazymkv_dev::evidence::skip` and pass when it is absent, never silently and never failing for a missing input (core cannot call the dev crate: dev depends on core). `core`'s unit tests read only `corpus/thediscdb`, `corpus/thediscdb-api` and synthetic inputs; those always run.
- Synthetic TMDb fixtures follow TMDb's documented shapes (`/search/multi`, `/movie/{id}`, `/tv/{id}`, `/tv/{id}/season/{n}`) since no search answer or full record is recorded; the plan says so where they are used, and phase 2's client verifies the shape live.
- One commit per task; the message only, no attribution line; the executor commits with the owner's signing configuration and checks `git log -1 --format='%G? %an <%ae> %cn <%ce>%n%B'` for `G` and `krcm0209 <17315774+krcm0209@users.noreply.github.com>`.
- Nothing under `corpus/owner/` is ever written by a test or a command of this plan (the evidence clone is read-only here); nothing under the repository is written by the plan's authoring.
- `lazymkv-dev plan` and the `decide` extension print JSON through `pyjson::dumps` with `Style::INDENT1_ASCII` as `decide` does today. `lazymkv-dev plan` exits 0 (planned, with or without review reasons or settings problems), 2 (an argument error, an unreadable scan, or a lookup, settings, TMDb or remembered file that does not parse) and 3 (a slug given and the evidence clone absent), never 1 (RP24); `decide` keeps 0, 1, 2, 3 with the port spec's meanings (3.4: 0; 1 a reconcile verdict is no; 2 unreadable or not a rip label; 3 no evidence).

## Review Focus

1. **A DVD's titles: shared segment maps, and no source file.** On a DVD the segment numbers restart at 1 in every title (`audio::titles` says so; Knowing's titles 3 to 6 all carry `26 = "1"`) and no title has attribute 16; TheDiscDB writes the DVD title number (attribute 24, `"01"`, Firefly disc 2's `"11"`) in `source_file`. Task 2's `Title::source` and `same_source` compare a DVD title by attribute 24 as a number, and every matcher uses them: Task 2's `same_scan_title`, Task 3's `same_title` (pinned by `a_dvd_title_matches_thediscdb_by_its_attribute_24` on Knowing's `disc01.txt` and `disc01.json`), Task 6's `remembered::match_title` (pinned by `on_a_dvd_a_remembered_title_matches_by_dvd_title_number_not_segment_map`). Task 5's `groups` keys a DVD group by (attribute 24, segment map), pinned by `on_a_dvd_titles_with_the_same_segment_map_are_separate_groups` on Knowing's log; a DVD title without attribute 24 is a group of its own, keyed `#<title number>`, pinned by `a_dvd_title_without_attribute_24_is_a_group_of_its_own`.
2. **A TMDb record without a runtime.** TMDb returns `runtime: null` for many films and no episode runtimes for many seasons; 8.1 step 4 requires "the runtime check passes". Task 4's `identify` treats an absent runtime as a failed check (step 5, 0.50, `identity_ambiguous`) rather than a pass, and its test `a_tmdb_record_without_a_runtime_cannot_pass_step_4` pins it.
3. **An episode title with a slash and a long non-ASCII title.** TheDiscDB's episode titles can hold a slash (the Office recording's two-episode title has one); 8.9 removes `/` and caps components at 255 bytes. Task 11's `sanitise` must cut on a character boundary, and its tests `a_slash_in_an_episode_title_is_removed` and `the_255_byte_cap_never_splits_a_character` pin both.
4. **A forced-only subtitle stream without a preceding same-language stream.** 8.7 defines the parent as "the nearest preceding non-derived subtitle stream of the same language"; a disc may list a forced-only stream first, or after streams of another language only. Task 9's `parent_of` returns `None` and the stream is set aside with no parent (never a panic, never adopted by another language), pinned by `a_forced_only_stream_without_a_same_language_parent_is_set_aside_alone`.
5. **Library roots that differ only by case or a trailing separator.** Spec 7 and 14 refuse a staging root inside a library root; the owner's roots are UNC paths on a case-insensitive share, typed by hand. Task 1's `path_inside` normalises separators, trailing separators and case, pinned by `a_root_inside_another_is_refused_whatever_the_case_or_trailing_separator`.
6. **The label variant chosen before the original language is known.** 8.3 rule 2 picks, within a cut, the variant covering the most wanted languages, but the wanted languages need TMDb's original language, which 8.1 gives only after the structural pass. Task 7's `plan` runs `by_labels` with English only, then again with the identity's original language when it is not English, and only the variant within a cut may change; pinned by `the_label_variant_is_rechosen_once_the_original_language_is_known`.
7. **Owner question: a movie disc with an extras play-all.** Spec 8.3 rule 3.1, read literally, makes any group whose segments are two or more other groups' in order a "play all" title, and then the disc is TV. Smile's deleted-scenes playlist (title 117, `596,597`) is such a group, so on a movie disc with an extras play-all and neither a TheDiscDB match (rule 1) nor Java labels (rule 2), Task 5's `by_structure` answers `PlayAll` and Task 7's `plan` plans the disc as TV, unless TheDiscDB's record states the disc is a movie (8.2 "TheDiscDB states the kind"): then Task 7 keeps the movie and runs rule 3 again without the play-all groups (`a_play_all_title_on_a_disc_thediscdb_calls_a_movie_leaves_it_a_movie`). Should 3.1 be limited to play-all titles whose parts are episode-length groups (8.2's 15 to 120 minutes)? Until the owner rules, the plan keeps the literal reading, pinned by Task 5's `a_play_all_group_makes_the_structure_rule_answer_tv`. Segment playlists count too: on the Expendables log 11 of title 41's 17 segments are candidate groups (SEG FPL_xx titles), and only its six segments under two minutes keep rule 3.1 from calling the feature itself a play-all title; a limit by episode length alone would not prevent that (segments 290 and 294 last 1574 and 1591 seconds), so the owner may prefer requiring the parts to pass structure_says_tv's 15% spread. Task 5's `a_feature_whose_segments_are_listed_as_playlists_is_play_all_under_the_literal_reading` shows that consequence on a synthetic disc.
8. **Owner question: two label cuts with the same edition name.** 8.3 rule 2's table names both the `none` row and the `_R` row "Theatrical Cut", and its rows are read literally as two cuts, so a Java disc carrying both `FPL_MainFeature` and `FPL_MainFeature_R` would plan two theatrical features whose final paths collide. No pinned disc has both. Task 5's `by_labels` plans such a disc at 0.60 with `title_ambiguous` and the evidence sentence `two cuts are both named Theatrical Cut` rather than at 0.90, pinned by `two_cuts_with_the_same_edition_name_are_ambiguous`; the owner may instead rule that `none` and `_R` are one cut, or that the literal 0.90 stands. Task 5's `by_database` applies the same guard to TheDiscDB main movies that would both be filed under one name (`Film` beside `Film (Theatrical Cut)`: 0.60 with `title_ambiguous` rather than 0.98), pinned by `two_main_movies_with_the_same_edition_name_are_ambiguous`.
9. **Owner question: the default subtitle when the default audio is not English and no regular English track is kept.** 8.10 names only the regular track; Task 11's `default_subtitle` makes the SDH track default, pinned by `with_other_audio_and_no_regular_track_the_sdh_track_is_the_default_subtitle`; the owner may rule that no subtitle is default.
10. **Owner question: leading periods in a path component.** 8.9 trims trailing spaces and periods only; a title that begins with periods (TMDb's `...And Justice for All`, 1979) would give a folder and a file name that begin with `.`, a hidden entry on the Linux NAS and under Samba's default `hide dot files`, which the servers' library scans skip. Task 11's `sanitise` drops leading periods as well as leading spaces (`And Justice for All (1979) {tmdb-ID}`), pinned by `leading_periods_are_dropped_so_no_component_is_hidden` and `a_leading_period_is_dropped_so_the_folder_is_not_hidden`; the owner may confirm it or rule another treatment.
11. **What a subtitle label records (Tasks 17 and 18), settled by ruling RP25.** RP25 amends RP15: `subtitle-labels.json` mirrors `audio-labels.json`, and besides RP15's fields (`label`, `stream`, `kind`, `how`, `sure`, `date`, `note`) every track has `saw_verdict: bool` after `date` (required; true when the owner saw the rule's verdict before labelling, and such a label never counts: section 17 row 14 (a)'s "checked before the verdict", as the audio harness treats it) and `style` after `note` (`null` or `"uk"`: a UK-style SDH track, speakers by colour and sounds without brackets, which row 14 asks for if the owner has a UK disc). `how` gains `flag`, row 14's "a flag" (the commentary flag 1, the forced flag 4096), so `HOW` has seven entries with `("flag", "a flag in MakeMKV's scan (an observation: does not count on its own, D23)")` after `menu`, and `OBSERVATION_HOW` is `["packaging", "menu", "flag", "player", "thediscdb"]`. Task 17's `SubtitleLabel` carries both fields, `problems` checks them (`saw_verdict must be true or false`, `style <x> is not null or 'uk'`), and `labels --subtitles set` requires `--saw-verdict yes|no`, as the audio `set` does, and takes `--style uk`; pinned by Task 17's `a_missing_or_unknown_key_of_a_track_is_a_problem`, `saw_verdict_and_sure_must_be_true_or_false`, `the_how_must_be_one_of_the_seven_sources`, `the_style_is_null_or_uk` and `set_records_a_uk_style_sdh_track_with_style_uk`. Task 18 counts a label only when its `how` is `read` or `watched`, the owner is sure, its `saw_verdict` is false and it is off the fitting discs, and counts row 14's UK-style SDH track from `style == "uk"` on such an `sdh` label (reported against row 14's count, never a missing kind, since row 14 asks for it only if the owner has a UK disc); pinned by Task 18's `a_label_made_after_seeing_the_verdict_or_from_an_observation_never_counts` and `a_uk_style_sdh_label_counts_towards_row_14s_uk_style_track_only_when_the_label_counts`. The owner may still change the vocabulary (a kind, a source or a style); Tasks 17 and 18 then change with it.

## Rulings (RP10 to RP27)

The rulings RP10 to RP20 were made with the plan's brief (RP15 is written here as RP25 amended it); RP21 to RP27 were made while writing the plan, in answer to the task writers' concerns. They bind every task; where a task's text or an open point contradicts one, the ruling wins. The owner can overturn any of them. RP27 lists four note spellings for the owner's confirmation.

- RP10. Scope: phase 1 = spec section 16's decision core, nothing of phase 2. The spec's "to be designed in phase 1" items that concern the engine (D17's bundling table in 4.4 and 19, the app's own recording format, the tuning-evidence form, the OCR bitmap decoding, code signing) are phase 2 design work, not this plan.
- RP11. The spec's verification rule (6.2 step 7, 6.4 step 14: caption-first order, the DVD duration band "from 2 s shorter to 1% longer", codec through attributes 41/42, `MSG:4047` mapped through the selection, MakeMKV-only flags carried onto output tracks) is a NEW module `core::verify`, built on `reconcile`'s row builders where they fit, with its own tests over the recordings' `mkvmerge.json` files. `core::reconcile` and its goldens stay byte-identical (it is the Python's rule, RP6; `lazymkv-dev reconcile` keeps it).
- RP12. The job state reducer of spec 10.1 is in this plan (spec 4.2 puts it in `core`; it is pure): every state, event and action of 10.1 as enums, `reduce(state, event) -> (state, actions)`, the transition table, the waiting state's "return to" state, and the resume rules, with a test per transition and per resume rule. The engine (phase 2) performs the actions.
- RP13. The identification rule (8.1) is pure over recorded or synthetic answers: `core::lookup` holds the typed TheDiscDB and TMDb answers, the disc-name parsing and cleaning, plausibility, the runtime checks and the confidence table. The DVD disc ID (libdvdread's) stays unimplemented (spec 5 says so; nothing to verify it against); a DVD is looked up by fingerprint alone.
- RP14. The phase 1 command is `lazymkv-dev plan <slug|dir|scan.txt>` (the disc phase: identity, kind, titles, mode, confidences, review reasons, from the scan plus the recorded lookups when present) and the existing `lazymkv-dev decide <slug> <label>` extended with two sections, `plan` (the same document) and `decision` (the file phase for that rip label's title: audio and subtitle tracks kept, order, flags, names, the final path, the three confidences, the disposition, review reasons and notes), keeping its existing sections and goldens byte-identical. Both print JSON with `pyjson::dumps` indent 1 as `decide` does. Phase 2 folds them into `lazymkvctl`.
- RP15. (As amended by RP25.) Spec 15's "the subtitle text rule's thresholds (8.7) are brought under `retune` in phase 1" is in this plan: a subtitle labels file (`subtitle-labels.json`, format string `lazymkv subtitle labels v1`, beside `audio-labels.json` in a recording, mirroring its shape: per track `label`, `stream` (mkvmerge's track id, as in the audio file), `kind` in {`regular`, `sdh`, `forced`, `commentary`, `trivia`, `lyrics`, `translation`, `dub-transcript`, `closed-captions`, `other`}, `how` in {`read` (counting, D23), `watched` (counting), `packaging`, `menu`, `flag`, `player`, `thediscdb` (observations)}, `sure: bool`, `date`, `saw_verdict: bool` (required; true when the owner saw the rule's verdict before labelling, and such a label never counts, as the audio harness treats it), `note`, and `style` (`null` or `"uk"`: a UK-style SDH track, speakers by colour and sounds without brackets, which row 14 asks for)) and `lazymkv-dev retune --subtitles [--text DIR]`, which judges every labelled English or no-language track with the text rule (`core::subtitle::text::decide`) and spec 8.7's classifier, counts the labels that count (`how` `read` or `watched`, the owner sure, `saw_verdict` false) against spec section 17 row 14's required kinds (read from the spec text as the audio harness reads row 13) and row 14's UK-style SDH track from `style`, prints the costly verdicts as row 14 defines them, and exits 1 on any costly verdict. `lazymkv-dev labels` gains the same edits for subtitles (`labels --subtitles set|unset|check`, `set` taking `--saw-verdict yes|no` and `--style uk`), reusing the audio labels' validation code where it is shared.
- RP16. Remembered decisions (spec 5, 8.1 step 1, section 11 "Remember") are a `core` type and two pure functions (match a remembered title to a scan title by source file, segment map and duration within 2 s; apply audio and subtitle overrides keyed by the stream signature (type, language, codec, channels, position among identical streams)); persistence is phase 2.
- RP17. Season sessions (8.5) are a `core` record type with pure functions (`find`, `suggest`, `assign`, `close`); persistence is phase 2.
- RP18. Edition naming (8.4) takes the "library folder already holds an edition-named file" and "an earlier filed copy of that cut" facts as inputs (`LibraryFacts`); phase 2 reads the library.
- RP19. `core` stays free of I/O: every new function takes parsed values, text, or `&dyn Tree`; the dev crate reads the recording. No new crate; new modules go under `crates/core/src/` and `crates/dev/src/cmd/`.
- RP20. New modules are written from the spec, not from any Python: Python-exactness (loop order, `py_*` spellings, `Ordered`) binds only the ported modules. New JSON documents use `serde` derives with the field order of the struct and spec spellings; `BTreeMap` for keyed collections (in a type that is serialised, RP23 replaces an integer-keyed map with a sorted `Vec` of named entries).
- RP21. **No private-corpus content in the public repository.** A test in `crates/` never holds a byte copy of a file from `corpus/owner/` (the navigation files under `nav/` are verbatim files of commercial discs, and `tmdb.json` is TMDb's data under TMDb's terms; that is why the evidence repository is private), and never a value copied from the clone that a reader could not have derived from the public spec or the pinned MIT fixtures. Task 2's `RECORDED_BDMT` unit-test constant becomes a synthetic bdmt file (a made-up disc name such as `Example Film`, two made-up thumbnail names, the same byte-order mark and CRLF form, and the test asserts the made-up name, not a length of 533); the dev test over the clone (`disc_model.rs`) keeps reading the real file. Task 16's `TWIN_A`/`TWIN_B` become made-up 32-hex values (for example `0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef` and a second, different one) and the sentence that says they are copied from the clone goes. Playlist numbers, segment maps, durations and sizes that the spec or the pinned TheDiscDB fixtures already publish may stay.
- RP22. **Settings reading.** `Settings::from_json(text: &str) -> Result<(Settings, Vec<SettingsProblem>), String>`: `Err` only when the text is not a JSON object or a key's value cannot be read into its type (one sentence naming the key); on `Ok` the settings are returned together with `validate()`'s problems (possibly empty), so a caller that needs a valid file checks the vector and a caller that plans with the defaults (`lazymkv-dev plan`, which prints the problems and plans anyway) does not. Task 1's signature, doc, implementation and tests change; the private `parse_json` goes away; Task 15's `read_settings` calls `from_json` and no longer repeats the parse. The interfaces entry follows. (A key the settings lack is a value that cannot be read: `Settings` is `deny_unknown_fields`, so a misspelt key is refused naming it rather than left at its default; text that is not JSON is serde_json's message.)
- RP23. **No integer-keyed map in a serialised type.** serde's buffered content (every `#[serde(untagged)]` or internally tagged enum, and `#[serde(flatten)]`) cannot read a `BTreeMap<u32, V>` back from JSON, and `DecideDoc` is deserialised by three existing unit tests. So in every type that derives `Serialize` in this plan (`Plan`, `PlanEvidence`, `PlannedTitle` and whatever else holds one, `SeasonSession`, `remembered::Overrides` and its entries, `FileDecision`, `job::Event`, `PlanDoc`, the `decide` sections), a `BTreeMap<u32, V>` or `BTreeMap<(u32, u32), V>` becomes `Vec<E>` where `E` is a named entry struct whose first field is the key (`title: u32`, or `stream: u32`, or both), kept sorted by key, with a small `pub fn get(&self, key) -> Option<&V>` (or `find`) on the owning type where lookups are needed. Types that are never serialised keep their maps. Tasks 6, 7, 13, 14, 15 and 16 and the interfaces follow; every test that built or asserted such a map changes to the entry form; Task 16's note about the round trip is removed because it no longer applies.
- RP24. **Exit codes.** `lazymkv-dev plan` exits 0 (planned, with or without review reasons or settings problems), 2 (an argument error, an unreadable scan, a lookup, settings, TMDb or remembered file that does not parse) and 3 (a slug given and the evidence clone absent); never 1. `decide` keeps 0, 1, 2, 3. Global Constraints line about the two commands' exit codes says exactly this; Task 15, Task 19 and the port spec row in Task 19 agree.
- RP25. **Subtitle labels, amended RP15.** The labels file `subtitle-labels.json` (`lazymkv subtitle labels v1`) mirrors `audio-labels.json`: per track `label`, `stream` (mkvmerge's track id, as the audio file), `kind` in {regular, sdh, forced, commentary, trivia, lyrics, translation, dub-transcript, closed-captions, other}, `how` in {read, watched, packaging, menu, player, thediscdb, flag} (`read` and `watched` count under D23; the rest are observations), `sure: bool`, `date`, `saw_verdict: bool` (required; true when the owner saw the rule's verdict before labelling, and such a label never counts, as the audio harness treats it), `note`, and `style` (`null` or `"uk"`: a UK-style SDH track, speakers by colour and sounds without brackets, which row 14 asks for). Tasks 17 and 18 add the two fields and the `flag` source to the file format, the validation sentences, `set`'s flags (`--saw-verdict`, `--style uk`), the harness's counting rule and row 14's UK count (from `style`), and their tests; the interfaces entry follows. (The plan lists the sources in row 14's order, `flag` after `menu`: read, watched, packaging, menu, flag, player, thediscdb.)
- RP26. **VC-1.** `core::codec` gains the family `Vc1` (attribute 5 `V_MS/VFW/WVC1`; attribute 6 and 7 spellings not yet seen in a recording, so the match is on attribute 5; display name `VC-1`; mkvmerge name `VC-1`; video, no tier). Task 1 adds the row, its test and the `Family` variant; the interfaces table follows. Open point 34 is rewritten to say so.

No change; the owner is asked to confirm these four spellings (Task 1's `Note` gives them as `as_str()` and serde names, pinned by its round-trip tests).

## Shared interfaces

Every item below crosses a task boundary: one task defines it, later tasks call it. A task that needs an item not listed here keeps it private to its own file. Signatures are exact; bodies are left out (`;` in place of a body). Each item carries a one-line doc, the spec section it implements, the task that defines it (`Def:`) and the tasks that use it (`Use:`); a `Use:` never names a task before its `Def:`. Data types are given in full, every field with its type and the spec sentence or scan attribute that fills it, because a later task's writer sees only this file.

### Conventions every task follows

- **Names.** Rust names are the spec's words in snake_case (`auto_threshold`, `feature_min_minutes`, `tv_unmapped`); a MakeMKV attribute is named by what it holds, with its number in the doc (`source_file` "attribute 16"). Types are named by the spec's nouns: `Disc`, `Title`, `Stream`, `Plan`, `FileDecision` (not `Decision`, which is `subtitle::text::Decision`); `lookup::name::fold_name` is not `subtitle::text::fold`.
- **Closed sets are enums.** Every closed set of spec strings (review reasons, notes, states, failure classes, roles, kinds, edition styles, item types, verdict mappings, notification events, tools) is an enum with `pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str` giving the spec spelling, `#[serde(rename = "...")]` on every variant to that spelling (or `rename_all = "snake_case"` where every variant spells itself), `FromStr` accepting only those spellings, and `pub const ALL: [Self; N]` in spec order. The one exception is `ItemType::Unknown` (`#[serde(other)]`), which reads a TheDiscDB type outside the spec's seven and is not in `ALL`. `codec::Family`, `codec::Tier`, `codec::ObjectAudio` and `tracks::SubtitleRole` are written by the rules and read back only through serde, never parsed from a bare string: they carry `as_str` and their serde spellings, no `FromStr`, and `ALL` only where listed (`Family::ALL`, `SubtitleRole::ALL`).
- **Errors.** A function that can refuse its input returns `Result<T, String>` with one plain sentence naming the input (`"title 3 has no duration (attribute 9)"`); a function that classifies never fails. Typed errors are used only where a caller matches on them: `SettingsProblem`, `job::Rejected`.
- **No I/O in `core`.** Every `core` function takes text, parsed values or `&dyn Tree`; the dev crate reads files and decides exit codes.
- **Keyed collections** are `BTreeMap` (and sets `BTreeSet`), keyed by the scan's title number (`u32`) or stream number (`u32`) or a string; vectors keep the scan's or the decision's order. A map keyed by a struct is never serialised: it is a `Vec` of entries. A type serialised inside a document, a stored file or an event (`Plan` and everything in it, `SeasonSession`, `Remembered`, `Overrides`, `FileDecision`, `job::Event`, `PlanDoc`, `decide`'s sections) holds no `BTreeMap<u32, V>` or `BTreeMap<(u32, u32), V>` either, but a `Vec` of a named entry struct whose first field is the key (`DiscDbMatch`, `AssignedEpisode`, `TitleOverrideEntry`, `AudioTrackOverride`, `SubtitleTrackOverride`), kept sorted by key, with a lookup method on the owning type where one is needed (`SeasonSession::get`, `Overrides::title_role`, `audio_of`, `subtitles_of`), because serde's buffered content (every untagged or internally tagged enum, and `#[serde(flatten)]`), through which `decide`'s untagged sections and `job::Event` read these types back, cannot turn JSON's string keys back into integer keys (RP23); types never serialised (`AudioFacts`, `SubtitleFacts`, `match_titles`' result, the rules' private maps) keep their maps, and so does `Disc.titles`, since `Disc` is serialised only on its own (Task 2's round trip), never inside a document.
- **Settings** are passed as `&Settings`; a rule reads only its keys and names them in its doc.
- **Confidence** is `f64`; the spec's constants are `pub const` items named after their rule (`DATABASE_TITLE_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.98`) and compared with `>=` against `settings.auto_threshold`.
- **Review reasons and notes** are `review::ReviewReason` and `review::Note`; a function that can raise them returns them in its result struct's `reviews: Vec<ReviewReason>` (sorted, unique, through `review::sorted_unique`) and `notes: Vec<Noted>` (in the order raised), never as strings.
- **Serialisation.** Every result type that a document prints derives `serde::Serialize` and `serde::Deserialize` with the struct's field order; `Option` fields are written as `null`, never skipped, so documents have a fixed key set; `f64` fields are written as JSON numbers (`float_roundtrip` keeps `0.85` as `0.85`). Every type a test asserts on derives `Debug` and `PartialEq`.
- **Doc comments.** Every public item: `/// <what it is>. Spec <section>.`; every file: a `//!` paragraph naming the spec sections it implements and the tasks that use it.
- **Tests** sit in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the bottom (a sibling `tests.rs` for `tracks/audio.rs`, `tracks/subtitle.rs`, `job.rs`, `lookup/mod.rs`); names read as sentences; fixtures are built with `testsupport::scan_text` and the TMDb builders, or read from `corpus/thediscdb*` with `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")`. A test over `corpus/owner` is a dev integration test (Global Constraints).
- **Inputs the engine supplies later** (library facts, lookup answers, packet MD5s, ffprobe facts, subtitle events, content and text verdicts, the copy's scan, the owner's review decisions) are explicit input structs defined here (`LibraryFacts`, `LookupInputs`, `AudioFacts`, `SubtitleFacts`, `RuntimeFacts`, `Overrides`); the dev crate fills them from a recording, phase 2 from the live tools and the review queue.

```rust
/// Every key of spec 14 with its default (`Settings::default()` is the table's Default column). A settings file may name

pub struct Settings {

    pub tv_root: Option<String>,

    /// true: D9, a TMDb-only identification may file automatically (8.1's 0.84 cap when false).

    pub prefer_most_channels: bool,
    /// true: D9, original-language audio first for non-English works (8.6 step 5).
    pub original_language_first: bool,
    /// 300: start-time tolerance for subtitle alignment, ms (8.7).
    pub subs_tolerance_ms: u32,
    /// 0.70 and 0.30: the provisional alignment bands (8.7).
    pub subs_same_min: f64,
    pub subs_diff_max: f64,
    /// 64: image-subtitle packets this small clear the screen (8.7).

    /// Combined (8.9).

    /// false: add the square-bracket ID tag (8.9).

    /// 7: days raw data of filed jobs is kept (7).
    pub retention_days: u32,
    /// true: D16.
    pub keep_tuning_evidence: bool,
    /// None; required while keep_tuning_evidence is on; not inside staging_root or a library root (7, 14).
    pub tuning_root: Option<String>,
    /// 1, 10, 120, 30, 300, 20, 30 (spec 14, in its order).
    pub file_phase_concurrency: u32,
    pub drive_settle_s: u32,
    pub drive_ready_timeout_s: u32,
    pub scan_timeout_min: u32,
    pub stall_timeout_s: u32,
    pub read_error_rate: u32,
    pub exit_wait_min: u32,

}
impl Default for Settings { fn default() -> Settings; }

/// One refused setting: the key and a plain sentence. Spec 7 and 14. Def: T1. Use: T15 (printed when a settings file is given; phase 2 the UI).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct SettingsProblem { pub key: String, pub problem: String }

impl Settings {
    /// Every problem, in key order: staging_root inside movies_root or tv_root (or equal to one); tuning_root inside
    /// staging_root or a library root; tuning_root absent (or blank: no path component) while keep_tuning_evidence is on;
    /// auto_threshold outside 0.0..=1.0; subs_diff_max above subs_same_min; minlength_s, feature_min_minutes,
    /// file_phase_concurrency 0; makemkv_min_version not `N.N.N` (`version_triple`). Empty when valid.
    /// `Settings::default().validate()` is exactly one problem, keyed `tuning_root` (spec 14's defaults turn
    /// keep_tuning_evidence on and leave tuning_root unset); `lazymkv-dev plan` prints the problems and plans with them.
    /// Spec 7, 14. Def: T1. Use: T15.
    pub fn validate(&self) -> Vec<SettingsProblem>;
    /// A JSON settings text, read and checked (ruling RP22): keys absent from the text take Settings::default()'s value.
    /// Err, one sentence, only when the text cannot be read: text that is not JSON (serde_json's message), text that is
    /// not one JSON object (`a settings file is one JSON object of spec 14's keys`), or a key the settings lack or whose
    /// value cannot be read into its type (`<key>: <serde's message>`, the first such key in the text's order). Ok holds
    /// the settings with validate()'s problems, possibly none: a caller that needs a valid file checks the vector, and
    /// `lazymkv-dev plan` prints them and plans anyway. Spec 14. Def: T1. Use: T15.
    pub fn from_json(text: &str) -> Result<(Settings, Vec<SettingsProblem>), String>;
    /// Milliseconds as seconds for the alignment rule (`subs_tolerance_ms as f64 / 1000.0`). Def: T1. Use: T9.
    pub fn subs_tolerance_s(&self) -> f64;
    /// The text rule with this file's subtitle settings: CLEAR_MAX_BYTES = sub_clear_max_bytes, TOL_S = subs_tolerance_s(),
    /// SAME_MIN = subs_same_min, DIFF_MAX = subs_diff_max, every other field `subtitle::text::Rule::default()`'s; pinned by
    /// `the_subtitle_defaults_equal_the_text_rules_defaults` (`Settings::default().text_rule() == text::Rule::default()`).
    /// Spec 8.7, 14, RP15. Def: T1. Use: T16, T18.
    pub fn text_rule(&self) -> crate::subtitle::text::Rule;
}

/// True when `inner` is `outer` or a path below it: both split on '/' and '\\', empty and trailing components dropped,
/// compared component by component ignoring ASCII case (Windows and SMB shares are case-insensitive); a UNC prefix
/// `\\server\share` is two components. Spec 7 "The staging root may not be inside a library root". Def: T1. Use: T1 (validate).
pub fn path_inside(inner: &str, outer: &str) -> bool;

/// The version string `N.N.N` as a comparable triple; None otherwise. Spec 9.1. Def: T1. Use: T1 (validate), T2 (makemkv version).
pub fn version_triple(text: &str) -> Option<(u32, u32, u32)>;
```

```rust
/// Attribute 22 as a bitmask (spec 9.5). Unknown bits are kept in the value and ignored by every query. Def: T2. Use: T6 (signature), T8, T9, T10, T12.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]

    /// Attribute 14.
    pub channels: Option<u32>,
    /// Attributes 17 and 18.
    pub sample_rate: Option<u32>,
    pub sample_size: Option<u32>,
    /// Attribute 19 "WxH" as (width, height).
    pub video_size: Option<(u32, u32)>,
    /// Attribute 22 (`Flags::of`).
    pub flags: Flags,
    /// Attribute 30 ("PGS English  (forced only)", "CC->Text English ( Lossy conversion )").
    pub tree_info: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 40 ("stereo", "5.1(side)", "7.1").
    pub layout_name: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 41 (only on a converted stream: "Text") and 42 ("( Lossless conversion )", "( Lossy conversion )").
    pub output_codec: Option<String>,
    pub conversion: Option<String>,
}

/// How the matching rules know a title (spec 5, 6.2 step 6, 6.3 step 8, 8.3): its source file (attribute 16) on a Blu-ray,
/// else its DVD title number (attribute 24 parsed as a number: "01" and "1" are equal; TheDiscDB writes the same number in
/// its `source_file` on a DVD), else Unknown. Def: T2. Use: T2, T3, T6.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "by")]
pub enum TitleSource { File { name: String }, DvdTitle { number: u32 }, Unknown }
/// `source_file` when Some and not empty, else `dvd_title` parsed as a number, else Unknown. Def: T2. Use: T3, T6.
pub fn title_source(source_file: Option<&str>, dvd_title: Option<&str>) -> TitleSource;
/// Equal and not Unknown (an Unknown never matches anything). Def: T2. Use: T2, T3, T6.
pub fn same_source(a: &TitleSource, b: &TitleSource) -> bool;

/// One title of the scan, typed. Def: T2. Use: T3 to T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Title {
    /// The scan's title number (sparse numbering kept).
    pub number: u32,
    /// Attribute 2.
    pub name: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 8; 0 when absent.
    pub chapters: u32,
    /// Attribute 9 through `robot::duration_seconds`; None when absent or unparsable.
    pub seconds: Option<u32>,
    /// Attribute 11, bytes.
    pub size: Option<u64>,
    /// Attribute 16 (a Blu-ray's playlist, "00800.mpls"); a DVD has none.
    pub source_file: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 24 as text ("01"), the DVD title number.
    pub dvd_title: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 25.
    pub segment_count: Option<u32>,
    /// Attribute 26 as text ("" when absent) and `audio::titles::segments` of it; `truncated` when the text ends in "...".
    pub segment_map: String,
    pub segments: Vec<i64>,
    pub truncated: bool,
    /// Attribute 27, MakeMKV's output file name.
    pub output_name: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 49 ("FPL_MainFeature_UR", "SEG FPL_02", "A1").
    pub comment: Option<String>,
    /// The streams in scan order. A stream whose attribute 1 is not Video, Audio or Subtitles (or is absent) is left out;
    /// the other streams keep their scan numbers.
    pub streams: Vec<Stream>,
}
impl Title {
    /// The streams of one kind, in scan order. Def: T2. Use: T5, T8, T9, T10, T11.
    pub fn streams_of(&self, kind: StreamKind) -> Vec<&Stream>;
    /// The height of the first video stream's attribute 19 (8.9's resolution label). Def: T2. Use: T11, T13.
    pub fn video_height(&self) -> Option<u32>;
    /// Minutes as f64 (seconds / 60.0); None without a duration. Def: T2. Use: T5.
    pub fn minutes(&self) -> Option<f64>;
    /// The (kind, language, codec family, channels) of every audio and subtitle stream as a set, for 8.3 rule 3.4's
    /// "superset of every other title's" test. Def: T2. Use: T5.
    pub fn signature_set(&self) -> BTreeSet<(StreamKind, Option<String>, Family, Option<u32>)>;
    /// `title_source(source_file, dvd_title)`. Def: T2. Use: T2, T3, T6.
    pub fn source(&self) -> TitleSource;
}

/// CINFO 1: 6209 "Blu-ray disc", 6206 "DVD disc"; a UHD is a Blu-ray disc here (the resolution tells them apart, 8.9). Def: T2. Use: T3, T5, T7, T12.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
pub enum DiscKind { BluRay, Dvd, Unknown }
impl DiscKind { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; }

/// The typed disc (spec 9.4 CINFO and the two messages of 6.1 step 4). Def: T2. Use: T3 to T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Disc {
    pub kind: DiscKind,
    /// CINFO 2 ("Pan's Labyrinth", "THE OFFICE S3D3", "Short Circuit 2").
    pub name: Option<String>,
    /// CINFO 30.
    pub tree_name: Option<String>,
    /// CINFO 32 ("PANS_LABYRINTH", "DVD_VIDEO").
    pub volume_label: Option<String>,
    /// CINFO 49 ("UHD-141056_Smile_WW").
    pub comment: Option<String>,
    /// CINFO 28.
    pub metadata_language: Option<String>,
    /// MSG:1005's last parameter ("MakeMKV v2.0.0 win(x64-release)") and the "2.0.0" inside it (`version_triple` parses it).
    pub makemkv_banner: Option<String>,
    pub makemkv_version: Option<String>,
    /// MSG:3344 seen (6.1 step 4; 8.3 rule 2 trusts labels only then).
    pub java_in_use: bool,
    /// `audio::titles::dvd_scan`, which also holds when CINFO 1 is absent (a DVD log pinned without CINFO).
    pub is_dvd: bool,
    /// Every title that has a TINFO line, by number (SINFO lines of a title without one are not typed).
    pub titles: BTreeMap<u32, Title>,
    /// MSG:2003 lines in the scan (the count; 6.2 step 7 reports them on a rip).
    pub scan_read_errors: u32,
}
impl Disc {
    /// `titles.get(&number)` with the sentence "the scan lists no title <n>" as Err. Def: T2. Use: T7, T13, T15, T16.
    pub fn title(&self, number: u32) -> Result<&Title, String>;
}

/// The typed disc of a parsed scan; Err only where an attribute the model needs is malformed, naming the title and the
/// stream: `title <t> stream <s>: attribute 22 (flags): <why>` (`<why>` is `Flags::of`'s text: attribute 22 not a number,
/// or outside 0 to u32::MAX) and `title <t> stream <s>: attribute 19 (video size) is '<text>', not WxH` (a non-empty
/// attribute 19 that is not WxH). A title is in `Disc.titles` only when the scan has a TINFO line for it; its streams are
/// its SINFO lines in stream order, without a stream whose attribute 1 is not Video, Audio or Subtitles. Spec 9.4, 9.5.
/// Def: T2. Use: T3 to T16.
pub fn disc(scan: &Scan) -> Result<Disc, String>;

/// Spec 14's "2-second duration match": the one copy for every new matcher (8.3, 5, 6.3 step 8, 6.2 step 7); equal to
/// reconcile::DURATION_TOLERANCE_S (pinned by a test). Def: T2. Use: T2, T3, T6, T12.
pub const DURATION_MATCH_S: u32 = 2;

/// Spec 8.3 first paragraph: two segment maps agree when equal; when either ends in "..." only the untruncated prefix is
/// compared (the prefix is the text before "...", with a trailing partial number or comma dropped), and the other map must
/// start with it. Def: T2. Use: T2, T3, T6.
pub fn segment_maps_agree(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool;

/// Spec 6.3 step 8: two scans' titles are the same title when `same_source(a.source(), b.source())`, their segment maps
/// agree (`segment_maps_agree`) and their durations are within DURATION_MATCH_S (both durations present). Def: T2. Use: phase 2
/// (the copy's scan against the disc-time scan); `remembered::match_title` and `lookup::discdb::same_title` follow the same
/// three tests over their own records.
pub fn same_scan_title(a: &Title, b: &Title) -> bool;

/// The `<di:name>` text of `BDMV/META/DL/bdmt_*.xml`: the first `<di:name>` element (a start tag with attributes, such as
/// `<di:name xml:lang="en">`, counts; a longer tag name, such as `<di:names>`, does not), its text with the five entities
/// `&amp;`, `&lt;`, `&gt;`, `&quot;`, `&apos;` and the numeric character references (`&#233;`, `&#xE9;`) decoded once
/// each (`&amp;lt;` gives `&lt;`), any other entity (`&copy;`) and a bare `&` left as written, surrounding whitespace
/// trimmed, a leading byte-order mark ignored. None when there is no such element, or it is empty (`<di:name/>` or
/// `<di:name></di:name>`), whitespace only or unclosed. Spec 6.1 step 2, 8.1. Def: T2. Use: T15.
pub fn bdmt_name(xml: &str) -> Option<String>;

/// The bdmt file names of a recording's nav tree, English first ("bdmt_eng.xml", then the others in name order), so the
/// caller reads the first. Spec 6.1 step 2. Def: T2. Use: T15.
pub fn bdmt_candidates(names: &[String]) -> Vec<String>;
```

### `core::lookup::discdb` (Task 3)

TheDiscDB's answers in the exact shape of spec 8.1's last bullet. The same structs also read the pinned data-repository form of `corpus/thediscdb/**/discNN.json` through `#[serde(alias = "...")]` on every title, item and track field (`Titles`, `Index`, `SourceFile`, `SegmentMap`, `Duration`, `Size`, `Comment`, `Tracks`, `Item`, `Title`, `Type`, `Season`, `Episode`, `Name`, `Resolution`, `AspectRatio`, `AudioType`, `LanguageCode`, `Language`, `Description`, `ContentHash`, `GlobalDiscId`, `Format`), so one type serves both fixture sets. The pinned form has no `media`, `release` or `disc` object (hence the `Option`s), but carries the disc's facts at the top level as `Index`, `Name` and `Slug`, read into `pinned_index` and `pinned_name`. On a DVD, TheDiscDB writes the DVD title number (MakeMKV's attribute 24) in `source_file` (Knowing `"01"` to `"07"`, Firefly disc 2 `"01"`, `"02"`, `"03"`, `"11"`), never attribute 16.

```rust
/// `item.type` of a described title (spec 8.1): the seven values of the fixtures, and Unknown (`#[serde(other)]`) for any
/// other TheDiscDB type, so one unknown item never fails a whole record. Def: T3. Use: T5, T6.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub enum ItemType { MainMovie, Episode, Extra, Featurette, DeletedScene, Trailer, Other, #[serde(other)] Unknown }
impl ItemType { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; pub const ALL: [ItemType; 7]; } // ALL: the seven spec values, without Unknown

/// A described title's item. `season` and `episode` are strings as the API gives them ("01", "1", "12-13"). Def: T3. Use: T5, T6, T11.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct DiscDbItem {
    #[serde(alias = "Title")] pub title: String,
    #[serde(rename = "type", alias = "Type")] pub item_type: ItemType,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Season")] pub season: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Episode")] pub episode: Option<String>,
}

/// One track of a TheDiscDB title: `type` is Video, Audio or Subtitles; `name` is MakeMKV's attribute 7 (the long codec

/// "MpegH HEVC Main10@L5.1 (dvhe.07.06 BL+FEL+RPU)"); an audio track has `audio_type` ("Stereo", "Surround 5.1",
/// "Surround 7.1"; no channel count), `language_code` (three letters) and `language` ("English"); a subtitle track

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct DiscDbTrack {
    #[serde(alias = "Index")] pub index: u32,
    #[serde(rename = "type", alias = "Type")] pub track_type: String,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Name")] pub name: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Resolution")] pub resolution: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "AspectRatio")] pub aspect_ratio: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "AudioType")] pub audio_type: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "LanguageCode")] pub language_code: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Language")] pub language: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Description")] pub description: Option<String>,
}
impl DiscDbTrack {
    /// Video, Audio or Subtitles as a StreamKind; None for anything else. Def: T3. Use: T8.
    pub fn kind(&self) -> Option<StreamKind>;
    /// "Stereo" 2, "Surround 5.1" 6, "Surround 7.1" 8, "Mono" 1, "Surround 5.0" 5, "Surround 6.1" 7; None otherwise. Def: T3. Use: T8.
    pub fn channels(&self) -> Option<u32>;
}

/// One chapter of a TheDiscDB title. Def: T3. Use: none beyond parsing (kept for the full shape).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct DiscDbChapter { #[serde(alias = "Index")] pub index: u32, #[serde(default, alias = "Title")] pub title: Option<String> }

pub struct DiscDbExternalIds { pub tmdb: Option<String>, pub imdb: Option<String> }
/// `release`: title, year, slug, locale ("en-us"), region_code, upc. Def: T3.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct DiscDbRelease { pub title: Option<String>, pub year: Option<i32>, pub slug: Option<String>, pub locale: Option<String>, pub region_code: Option<String>, pub upc: Option<String> }

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
```

```rust
/// Spec 8.1's table rows, after the owner's review: Reviewed is spec 11's Set identity (8.8 "A review decision sets the
/// confidences it covers to 1.00"). Def: T4. Use: T7, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum IdentityStep { Reviewed, Remembered, DiscdbBoth, DiscdbOne, TmdbOne, TmdbSeveral, Nothing }
impl IdentityStep { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; pub const ALL: [IdentityStep; 7]; }

/// The confidence constants of 8.1 steps 1 to 6 and the cap of "When tmdb_only_autofile is off"; a review decision is
/// REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE too (1.00, 8.8). Def: T4. Use: T4, T7, T8, T10, T13.
pub const REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 1.00;
pub const DISCDB_BOTH_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.99;
pub const DISCDB_ONE_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.95;
pub const TMDB_ONE_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.90;
pub const TMDB_ONE_CAPPED_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.84;
pub const TMDB_SEVERAL_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.50;
pub const NOTHING_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.0;
/// (confidence, review reason) of a step: Reviewed and Remembered 1.00; reads settings.tmdb_only_autofile for TmdbOne (0.84
/// and IdentityAmbiguous when off); TmdbSeveral gives IdentityAmbiguous, Nothing gives IdentityUnknown. Def: T4. Use: T4, T7.
pub fn identity_confidence(step: IdentityStep, settings: &Settings) -> (f64, Option<ReviewReason>);

/// What the runtime checks compare against (8.1 "Runtime check"): the planned features' or cuts' durations (8.3, 8.4), the
/// longest rival when none is planned, and the durations of the disc's episode-length groups (8.2). The planner fills it
/// from the structural pass before the TMDb match (6.1 step 5's order). Def: T4. Use: T4, T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct RuntimeFacts { pub feature_seconds: Vec<u32>, pub longest_rival_seconds: Option<u32>, pub episode_group_seconds: Vec<u32> }

pub const MOVIE_RUNTIME_TOLERANCE: f64 = 0.03;
pub const TV_RUNTIME_TOLERANCE: f64 = 0.15;
/// Movies: at least one of `feature_seconds` (else `longest_rival_seconds`) within 3% of `runtime_min * 60`; false without a
/// runtime or without any duration. Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub fn movie_runtime_ok(facts: &RuntimeFacts, runtime_min: Option<u32>) -> bool;
/// TV: the median of `episode_runtimes_min` within 15% of the median of `episode_group_seconds / 60`; false when either list is
/// empty. The median of an even count is the mean of the two middle values. Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub fn tv_runtime_ok(facts: &RuntimeFacts, episode_runtimes_min: &[u32]) -> bool;
/// |a - b| <= tolerance * b. Def: T4. Use: T4, T5 (rule 4's 10%), T6 (suggest_by_runtime's 15%).
pub fn within(a: f64, b: f64, tolerance: f64) -> bool;

/// A TheDiscDB description's meaning (8.1 last bullet, D14, 8.7 "the one TheDiscDB describes as subtitles or SDH"):
/// "comment" gives Commentary; "audio desc", "descriptive", "DVS", "visually impaired" give AudioDescription; "SDH",
/// "hearing" give Sdh; "isolated score", "score only" give IsolatedScore; "music and effects", "music & effects", "M&E" give
/// MusicAndEffects; "subtitle", or a description that after trimming and case-folding equals the track's own `language`
/// (TheDiscDB's language name: "English"; Knowing's "ENglish" included), gives Dialogue. All case-insensitive, substring
/// matches, in this order; a text can carry several. IsolatedScore, MusicAndEffects and Dialogue are provisional: TheDiscDB's
/// wording for them is not yet known (8.1's last bullet names no such word; every subtitle description in the 18 answers
/// and the pinned files is a bare language name). Def: T4. Use: T8, T9, T10.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum DescriptionKind { Commentary, AudioDescription, Sdh, IsolatedScore, MusicAndEffects, Dialogue }
pub fn description_kinds(text: &str, language: Option<&str>) -> Vec<DescriptionKind>;

/// What the lookups gave (recorded, synthetic, or live in phase 2). `pending` flags say the answer is not in yet (8.1 "the
/// lookup is recorded as pending"). Def: T4. Use: T7, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct LookupInputs<'a> {
    /// The disc's own name, built by the caller with `name::disc_name` (a generic name is signalled by `DiscName.generic`, not by None).
    pub name: Option<&'a DiscName>,
    /// `/api/discid/{id}`: the first record of the array that has titles, or None (a miss, or no disc ID: a DVD).
    pub discdb_by_disc_id: Option<&'a DiscDbRecord>,
    /// `/api/dischash/{hash}`.
    pub discdb_by_fingerprint: Option<&'a DiscDbRecord>,
    pub discdb_pending: bool,
    /// The search 8.1 runs on the cleaned name (or on TheDiscDB's title and year when the entry has no TMDb ID).
    pub search: Option<&'a TmdbSearch>,
    /// The record fetched for the identity in hand.
    pub record: Option<&'a TmdbRecord>,
    pub tmdb_pending: bool,
    /// Step 1: the TMDb identity of a remembered decision for this fingerprint (`Remembered.tmdb`); plan::plan fills it from
    /// PlanInputs.remembered.
    pub remembered: Option<TmdbIdentity>,
    /// The owner's Set identity (spec 11), before step 1; plan::plan fills it from PlanInputs.overrides.
    pub reviewed: Option<TmdbIdentity>,
}

/// The identity 8.1 fixes at planning time. Def: T4. Use: T7, T11, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Identity {
    pub step: IdentityStep,
    pub confidence: f64,
    pub tmdb: Option<TmdbIdentity>,
    /// From the record when fetched, else from TheDiscDB's media, else from the one plausible result.
    pub title: Option<String>,
    pub year: Option<i32>,
    pub original_language: Option<String>,
    pub review: Option<ReviewReason>,
    /// The plausible results' identities (several in step 5; one in step 4).
    pub plausible: Vec<TmdbIdentity>,
    /// Whether a runtime check ran and what it said (None: not applicable, no record, or no runtime).
    pub runtime_check: Option<bool>,
    /// Pending lookups (8.1: planning proceeds on structure alone; the file phase waits in AwaitingLookup).
    pub lookup_pending: bool,
    /// One sentence per piece of evidence, in order ("TheDiscDB knows the fingerprint", "name 'JOHN_WICK_UHD' cleaned to 'JOHN WICK'").
    pub evidence: Vec<String>,
}

/// Spec 8.1 steps 1 to 6 in order, after the owner's review: `inputs.reviewed` is Some (Reviewed, 1.00, that identity);
/// `inputs.remembered` is Some (Remembered, 1.00, that identity); TheDiscDB by both disc ID and fingerprint (0.99: both
/// records present and their TMDb IDs equal, or one of them lacking an ID) or by one (0.95); else the search on a
/// non-generic cleaned name: exactly one plausible result and the runtime check passes (0.90, or 0.84 plus
/// identity_ambiguous when tmdb_only_autofile is off); several plausible results or a failed or impossible runtime check
/// (0.50, identity_ambiguous); else nothing (0, identity_unknown). The runtime check run is the one for the plausible
/// result's own TmdbKind (movie_runtime_ok for Movie, tv_runtime_ok for Tv), whatever `kind` is ("Movies and TV are searched
/// together"); `kind` (the structural kind) is used only to prefer results of that kind when several are plausible. A
/// generic name is never searched. A pending lookup does not lower the step reached by the answers in hand; it sets
/// lookup_pending. Def: T4. Use: T7.
pub fn identify(inputs: &LookupInputs<'_>, kind: Kind, runtime: &RuntimeFacts, settings: &Settings) -> Identity;
```

```rust
/// Expendables 3's title 41 `FPL_MainFeature_UR` gets "Unrated Cut"); `theatrical` as Feature's doc says. Two or more
/// MainMovies of which a later one still has no edition: 0.60 with unnamed_cut; two features given the same edition name
/// make it 0.60 with title_ambiguous (Review Focus 8). None when TheDiscDB marks no main movie or any MainMovie title does
/// not reconcile. Def: T5. Use: T5, T7.
pub fn by_database(record: &DiscDbRecord, matches: &BTreeMap<u32, u32>, disc: &Disc) -> Option<MoviePlan>;
/// Rule 2: only when `disc.java_in_use`; labels grouped by suffix without the language code, one cut per group, in order of
/// each cut's lowest title number; within a cut the variant whose audio covers the most of `wanted`'s languages, then the
/// one without a language suffix, then the lower title number; Narrative variants ignored. Exactly one cut 0.90; several
/// with recognised suffixes 0.90 as editions, except that two cuts given the same edition name (the `none` and `_R` rows
/// are both "Theatrical Cut") make it 0.60 with title_ambiguous (Review Focus 8); any Other suffix 0.60 with unnamed_cut.
/// None when no label is found. When Java was not reported, returns None and plan::plan adds the note
/// LabelRuleUnavailable. Def: T5. Use: T5, T7.
pub fn by_labels(disc: &Disc, wanted: &Wanted) -> Option<MoviePlan>;
/// What rule 3 found. Def: T5. Use: T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum StructureOutcome { PlayAll { group: usize }, Plan(MoviePlan) }
/// Rule 3 on the groups: 3.1 play-all (the disc is TV); 3.2 keep groups >= settings.feature_min_minutes, else the longest; 3.3
/// rivals within RIVAL_BAND of the longest kept; 3.4 in each rival the title with chapters, then the one whose audio and
/// subtitle stream signatures (kind, language, codec family, channels) are a superset of every other's, else 0.60
/// title_ambiguous; 3.5 one rival 0.85; 3.6 every pair's segment_difference <= 0.25 gives 0.60 title_ambiguous; 3.7 else 0.60
/// multiple_features. Def: T5. Use: T5, T7.
pub fn by_structure(disc: &Disc, groups: &[Group], settings: &Settings) -> StructureOutcome;
/// Segments in exactly one of the two lists, divided by the longer list's length; 0.0 for two empty lists. Spec 8.3 rule 3.6. Def: T5. Use: T5.
pub fn segment_difference(a: &[i64], b: &[i64]) -> f64;
/// Rule 4: a plan from rule 3 whose every feature's duration (`plan.feature_seconds`) is more than 10% from
/// `runtime_min * 60` drops to 0.60 with title_ambiguous (Open point 35); rule 1 and 2 plans and None runtimes are
/// returned unchanged. Def: T5. Use: T7.
pub fn runtime_sanity(plan: MoviePlan, runtime_min: Option<u32>) -> MoviePlan;
/// First applicable rule (8.3): by_database, else by_labels, else by_structure. Def: T5. Use: T7.
pub fn movie_plan(disc: &Disc, discdb: Option<&DiscDbRecord>, matches: &BTreeMap<u32, u32>, groups: &[Group], wanted: &Wanted, settings: &Settings) -> StructureOutcome;

/// What phase 2 reads from the library for 8.4 (RP18). Def: T5. Use: T7, T11, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct LibraryFacts {
    /// "the film's library folder already holds an edition-named file".
    pub folder_has_edition_named_file: bool,
    /// Earlier filed copies of this film: cut key ("theatrical", or the lower-cased edition name) to the edition name used
    /// ("" when that copy was filed without an edition name; this cut then gets None).
    pub earlier_edition_names: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    /// Spec 7: the final path already exists and is not this job's file. Phase 2 checks the plain path (no copy label);
    /// under the owner's Resolve collision "keep both" it must also check the copy-labelled path (`- 2160p 2`) before
    /// filing and hold the job with path_collision when that one is taken too (Open point 39).
    pub path_collision: bool,
}
/// 8.4's three rules, per feature in order: a non-theatrical cut always carries its name, even when it is the only cut; the
/// theatrical cut carries "Theatrical Cut" only when `features.len() >= 2` or `facts.folder_has_edition_named_file`; an
/// earlier filed copy's name (`earlier_edition_names`) replaces either. Names are raw here; naming::edition_label sanitises
/// and caps them. Def: T5. Use: T7, T13.
pub fn edition_names(features: &[Feature], facts: &LibraryFacts) -> Vec<Option<String>>;
pub const THEATRICAL_CUT: &str = "Theatrical Cut";
/// An edition name that names the theatrical or main cut (8.4): none at all, or a name containing the word Theatrical
/// (ignoring ASCII case), such as TheDiscDB's "Theatrical Version". The one test of "theatrical" for every rule and caller.
/// Def: T5. Use: T5, T13.
pub fn is_theatrical(edition: Option<&str>) -> bool;
```

```rust
/// One remembered audio override: the stream's signature and the action, flattened into one JSON object
/// (`{"signature": {...}, "action": "keep", "order": 1, "default": true}`). A list, not a map: serde_json writes no map
/// keyed by a struct. Spec 5. Def: T6. Use: T8, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct SubtitleOverrideEntry { pub signature: StreamSignature, #[serde(flatten)] pub action: SubtitleOverride }

    pub subtitles: Vec<SubtitleOverrideEntry>,
}

/// The remembered title is this scan title: `disc::same_source(&title_source(rem.source_file, rem.dvd_title), &title.source())`
/// (source file on a Blu-ray; on a DVD, both source files None, attribute 24 equal as numbers), `disc::segment_maps_agree`,
/// and duration within `disc::DURATION_MATCH_S`; never by title key. Def: T6. Use: T6, T7.

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Collision { KeepBoth, Replace, Discard }
impl Collision { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; pub const ALL: [Collision; 3]; }
/// Only the three spec spellings; Err "'x' is not a collision action (keep_both, replace or discard)".
impl std::str::FromStr for Collision { type Err = String; fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<Collision, String>; }

/// One title of the owner's Assign titles: the scan title number and its role, flattened into one JSON object
/// (`{"title": 3, "role": "episodes", "season": 3, "episodes": [12, 13]}`). Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T7, T13, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct TitleOverrideEntry { pub title: u32, #[serde(flatten)] pub role: TitleRole }
/// One track of the owner's Override tracks: the scan title and stream numbers and the action, flattened into one JSON

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct SubtitleTrackOverride { pub title: u32, pub stream: u32, #[serde(flatten)] pub action: SubtitleOverride }

/// The owner's review decisions on one job (spec 11 Set identity, Assign titles, Override tracks, Resolve collision); each
/// sets the confidence it covers to 1.00 (8.8). Assign titles and Override tracks are lists of entries keyed by the scan's
/// title number (and stream number) of this job, sorted by those keys, one entry per key. Def: T6. Use: T7, T13, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]

impl Overrides {

    /// The same for subtitles (`SubtitleFacts.reviewed`). Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T13.
```

```rust
/// out of the episode-length groups, 8.5 "play all titles are dropped"); identify (8.1) over `inputs.lookups` with
/// `remembered` set to `inputs.remembered.map(|r| r.tmdb)` and `reviewed` to `inputs.overrides.and_then(|o| o.identity)`;
/// when `identity.original_language` is Some and not English, by_labels runs again with
/// `wanted_languages(identity.original_language)` and its features replace the first pass's (cuts, editions and confidence
/// never change between the passes, only the variant chosen within a cut); `Plan.wanted` is
/// `wanted_languages(identity.original_language)` for every title rule (English only when the original language is unknown
/// or English); rule 4; a remembered decision (`remembered::apply_titles`, when every remembered title that is not
/// Ignored matches a scan title) or the owner's Assign titles (`overrides.titles`, which win) replace the planned titles
/// and set title confidence to 1.00, and Set identity or a remembered identity sets identity confidence to 1.00;
/// `overrides.season` fills a planned episode whose season is None (else the disc name's season does); the mode; reviews

/// kind is not the planned kind adds identity_ambiguous, a provisional rule left to the owner). `Plan.titles` order
/// (which fixes the keys' NN through `title_key(position, ..)`): movies in feature order (database index order for rule
/// 1, each cut's lowest title number for rule 2, group order for rule 3), TV by (season, first episode) with season None
/// last in title order. The identity is confirmed when its step is Reviewed, Remembered, DiscdbBoth or DiscdbOne (8.5
/// "when its identity is confirmed (by TheDiscDB or in review)"). With a mapped TV plan and the identity confirmed (or
/// episodes assigned by a remembered decision or the owner), a TMDb show identity and a season, `Plan.session` is
/// `tv::find(..)`'s session or `SeasonSession::new(show_id, season, the record's episode_count for that season)`, with
/// the plan's episodes assigned (`assign` with the fingerprint, when given); with an unmapped plan the found session
/// gives `start` (and the season when none was parsed), and when the identity is confirmed and the season is known,
/// `Plan.session` is that session or a new one with the disc recorded and no episode assigned (`assign` with the
/// fingerprint and no pair; spec 11 Set identity "attaches the disc to a season session"); None otherwise. Err only when
/// the disc has no title at all. Def: T7. Use: T15.
pub fn plan(inputs: &PlanInputs<'_>) -> Result<Plan, String>;

/// Spec 7 "Space checks": 5% over the planned titles' sizes before a Direct rip. Def: T7. Use: phase 2.
pub const DIRECT_SPACE_MARGIN: f64 = 0.05;
/// Spec 7 "Space checks": 2% over the disc size before a whole-disc copy. Def: T7. Use: phase 2.
pub const COPY_SPACE_MARGIN: f64 = 0.02;
/// Spec 7 "Space checks": 5% over the files to be written before extraction or remux. Def: T7. Use: phase 2.
pub const WRITE_SPACE_MARGIN: f64 = 0.05;
/// Bytes needed on staging for the plan's mode: Direct, the sum of `PlannedTitle.size` (a title without a size counts 0)
/// times 1.05; Copy, `disc_size` times 1.02; rounded up. Def: T7. Use: phase 2.
pub fn staging_bytes_needed(plan: &Plan, disc_size: u64) -> u64;
/// `bytes` times 1.05, rounded up (before extraction or remux). Def: T7. Use: phase 2.
pub fn write_bytes_needed(bytes: u64) -> u64;
```

```rust
/// Commentary, AudioDescription, IsolatedScore or MusicAndEffects through `descriptions` when the alignment is unique;
/// unwanted language; a remembered or review Drop or Commentary); keep the rest and any no-language stream; rank with
/// `rank_key`; guards G1 and G2; order by language (original first when settings.original_language_first and the
/// original is not English, else English first; no language last), default on the very first track, original flag on
/// the original-language tracks (the English ones for an English work); notes possible_commentary,
/// lossless_original_available, no_english_audio, lossy_before_lossless (D9); reviews original_language_missing,
/// no_wanted_audio; verdicts apply only when `facts.verdict_reference` and the decision's `reference` are both Some (a
/// title without a kept original-language or English track has nothing to judge, spec 8.6 "Content"): when they differ

/// (D21: the rule confirms no commentary on the title), only audio_reference_unclear is raised and no verdict is mapped;
/// otherwise, for the kept streams in a wanted language (Original or English group; no-language streams are not judged,
/// spec 8.6 "Content"), ReferenceUnclear adds audio_reference_unclear, Commentary and CommentaryCrossLanguage add
/// commentary_detected (nothing dropped, D15), AdPattern, NoteCommentary and NoteAd add notes; a remembered or review

/// lookup::REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE (1.00) when every audio stream of the title has a remembered or review override. At
/// planning time `facts` is empty and the ffprobe criterion is skipped (8.3). Def: T8. Use: T13, T16.

/// descending, bitrate descending for lossy only, disc position); with settings.prefer_most_channels off, tier comes before
/// channels. An unknown tier sorts after Low; a lossy track without bitrate text sorts after every lossy track with one.
/// The product's copy beside audio::reference::rank (Global Constraints). Def: T8. Use: T8.

/// lossy top track with <= 2 channels that is not first of its language and beats the first on channel count but on no later
/// criterion gives way to the first. Returns the language's tracks reordered. Def: T8. Use: T8.
pub fn guards(ranked: Vec<AudioTrack>, settings: &Settings) -> Vec<AudioTrack>;
/// Spec 8.6 step 1: TheDiscDB's whole track list (every kind, index order) against the title's whole stream list (scan
/// order), pairwise on kind (`DiscDbTrack::kind`), language (`norm_lang` of `language_code` against `norm_lang` of attribute
/// 3; video compares no language), codec as attribute 7 (`Stream.codec_long == DiscDbTrack.name`) and channels
/// (`DiscDbTrack::channels` against attribute 14, audio only); tried on all streams and on the streams without flag 2048;
/// Some only when exactly one of the two aligns completely (equal lengths, every pair equal). A title without derived
/// streams has one list, tried once (Full when it aligns); an empty TheDiscDB track list never aligns. The map is scan
/// stream number to TheDiscDB track index. Def: T8. Use: T8.
pub fn align_descriptions(title: &Title, discdb: &DiscDbTitle) -> Option<(Alignment, BTreeMap<u32, u32>)>;
/// Every scan stream (any kind) whose aligned TheDiscDB track has a description, to `lookup::description_kinds(description,
/// track.language)`; with the alignment used. Empty and None without a record or without a unique alignment. Def: T8. Use: T8, T9, T10.
pub fn descriptions(title: &Title, discdb: Option<&DiscDbTitle>) -> (Option<Alignment>, BTreeMap<u32, Vec<DescriptionKind>>);
```

```rust
/// Spec 8.7 in full, in order: `set_aside`; a counted stream in the file that TheDiscDB describes as commentary (not as
/// dialogue or SDH) is set aside and dropped (OutsideDialogueGroup; R6, D15); events from `facts.events`; full =
/// `is_full` against the largest English track's events (a stream flagged forced, 4096 without 2048, is never full: its
/// flag makes it a forced source); `alignment_groups` over the full tracks with the three bands (a Between pair raises
/// subtitle_ambiguous); `dialogue_group` with the parents of forced-only streams that have events and
/// `tracks::audio::descriptions` (None, two largest groups of equal size included, raises subtitle_ambiguous, and the
/// first group stands in for the regular and SDH roles); regular and SDH (up to two: more events is SDH, a description
/// saying SDH overrides; the closed-caption stream is SDH when the group has none; more than two gives
/// subtitle_ambiguous, and a track described SDH is one of the two kept); full tracks outside a picked group dropped
/// (OutsideDialogueGroup; with no pick, or with a Between band against a track of the picked group, they are kept as
/// regular under the review, never dropped unconfirmed or by position); forced (first: a forced-only stream with events
/// whose parent is the regular track, then the SDH track's; then a DVD stream flagged forced; then a separately
/// authored track that is not full with fewer than FORCED_MAX_EVENTS events); other not-full tracks with
/// FORCED_MAX_EVENTS or more events dropped with partial_subtitle_dropped, those with no events dropped NoEvents;
/// `text_disagreements` (subtitle_ambiguous and one subtitle_text_disagrees note per stream); the confidence case;
/// remembered then review overrides applied last (decided_by "remembered" or "reviewed"; an override naming a stream
/// that is not an English or no-language subtitle stream is ignored), with confidence lookup::REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE
/// (1.00) and subtitle_ambiguous cleared when every English and no-language subtitle stream of the title still in the
/// file (not in facts.removed) has an override (other-language streams are dropped by 8.7's first sentence; the case
/// unchanged). A title with one English stream and no events keeps it as Regular "English" (row 14 (b) fallback), case
/// OneFull; when that stream is flagged forced (4096 without 2048) it is kept as Forced by its flag, case
/// FlagsOrDescriptions. Def: T10. Use: T13, T16, T18.
pub fn decide_subtitles(title: &Title, facts: &SubtitleFacts<'_>, settings: &Settings) -> SubtitleDecision;
/// 8.7 "Text": the streams where a text decision differs from the counts, for any English or no-language stream: its
/// role (Regular, Sdh, Forced, Drop) differs from the kept role (or kept against a Drop, or dropped against a kept
/// role). SetAside never disagrees; Keep, and any verdict carrying the text rule's review, always disagree
/// (text::before_yes's reading: text::decide writes Keep only with its own review).
/// The public form of the rule's text check, which decide_subtitles reaches through the private `disagreements`; kept
/// for phase 2's review view. Def: T10. Use: T10.
pub fn text_disagreements(decision: &SubtitleDecision, text: &BTreeMap<u32, crate::subtitle::text::Decision>) -> Vec<u32>;
```

```rust
pub const EPISODE_TITLE_MAX_CHARS: usize = 90;
```

```rust
    pub rip_reviews: Vec<ReviewReason>,

/// One title's file-phase decision (6.4 step 11). Not `Decision`, which is `subtitle::text::Decision`. Def: T13. Use: T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct FileDecision {
    pub title_key: String,
    pub audio: AudioDecision,
    pub subtitles: SubtitleDecision,
    pub layout: Layout,

    pub edition: Option<String>,
    pub path: Option<NamedPath>,
    pub confidences: Confidences,
    pub reviews: Vec<ReviewReason>,
    pub notes: Vec<Noted>,
    pub read_errors: Vec<ReadError>,
    pub disposition: Disposition,
}

/// 6.4 step 11 and 8.8: decide_audio (with the wanted languages of the identity the job is filed under: the plan's, or,
/// when the owner's Set identity names another work than the plan's and its record is given, `wanted_languages` of that
/// record's original language; R4, 8.6 "Languages") and decide_subtitles (facts with `reviewed` set from
/// `overrides.audio_of(title.number)` and `overrides.subtitles_of(title.number)`), layout, the path (movie_path for a
/// feature, tv_path for an episode, by the filed role: the owner's Assign titles when it names any title, which then wins
/// whole as in a re-plan (Err for a planned title it ignores or does not name), else the planned role; no path when the
/// record's kind does not match the role (a movie record for a feature, a show record for an episode); resolution from
/// title.video_height, the edition through edition_names and edition_label; a planned Episode with season None builds no
/// path (path None) and adds tv_unmapped;
/// overrides.collision KeepBoth (copy Some(2) while the collision exists) and Replace leave path_collision unraised;
/// Discard never reaches decide, the engine discards the job), the three confidences (identity and
/// title from the plan; identity 1.00 when overrides.identity is Some, title 1.00 when overrides.titles is not empty; track
/// = min(audio, subtitle) after the remembered and review overrides set the parts they cover to 1.00), reviews = plan's
/// (less the reasons the owner's review answers: identity_unknown and identity_ambiguous when overrides.identity is Some;
/// title_ambiguous, multiple_features, unnamed_cut and tv_unmapped when overrides.titles is not empty) + audio's +
/// subtitles' + rip_reviews + path_collision when library.path_collision (and not KeepBoth or Replace) + read_errors
/// exactly when `read_errors` is not empty, notes likewise, read_errors carried unchanged, disposition; NeedsReview
/// whenever path is None. Verification lowers no
/// confidence: a failed or read-error rip holds the job through its review reason, which has the same effect on the
/// disposition as a confidence below auto_threshold (8.8). Def: T13. Use: T16.
pub fn decide(inputs: &DecisionInputs<'_>) -> Result<FileDecision, String>;

pub fn track_confidence(audio: &AudioDecision, subtitles: &SubtitleDecision) -> f64;
```
