```rust
/// Spec 10.1's fixed waits: AwaitingNetwork "retried every 10 minutes", AwaitingLookup "retried hourly". Def: T14. Use: T14.
pub const NETWORK_RETRY_MIN: u32 = 10;
pub const LOOKUP_RETRY_MIN: u32 = 60;

/// Spec 10.2's classes. Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "PascalCase")]
pub enum FailureClass { DriveIncapable, MediaReadError, Licence, NeedsMakeMkvUpdate, NeedsNetwork, Output, LookupUnavailable, ToolMissing, Unknown }
impl FailureClass { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; pub const ALL: [FailureClass; 9]; }

/// What an Output failure was (10.2's Output row: "share unreachable, out of space, or a write error"). Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum OutputCause { ShareUnreachable, OutOfSpace, WriteError }

/// A failing step's class, and for Output its cause (None for every other class). Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Failure { pub class: FailureClass, pub output: Option<OutputCause> }

/// The programs 10.2's ToolMissing row names (4.4, plus ffmpeg of 6.4 step 10a). Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Tool { Makemkvcon, Mkvmerge, Ffprobe, Ffmpeg, Java }
impl Tool { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; pub const ALL: [Tool; 5]; }

/// Why a job is held (10.1's two NeedsReview rows). Def: T14. Use: T14.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Held { AfterCopy, DispositionGate }

/// 10.1's states. `Planned` carries the mode the plan chose; `RipVerified` and `Ejected` whether they follow a whole-disc
/// copy (then the job is held next, 6.3 step 7) or a Direct rip (then it waits for the file-phase slot, spec 6); waiting
/// states carry the state they return to; `Decided` whether the owner approved the job (8.8); Failed carries its class
/// and the state that failed. Disc-phase states: Detected, Fingerprinted, Scanned, Planned, Ripping, Copying,
/// RipVerified. File-phase states: Ejected, Extracting, Inspecting, Decided, Remuxing, Verified.
/// Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "state")]
pub enum State {
    Detected, Fingerprinted, Scanned, Planned { mode: Mode }, Ripping, Copying, RipVerified { after_copy: bool }, Ejected { after_copy: bool },
    Inspecting, Decided { approved: bool }, Remuxing, Verified, Filed,
    NeedsReview { held: Held }, Extracting,
    AwaitingShare { return_to: Box<State> }, AwaitingSpace { return_to: Box<State> }, AwaitingMakeMkv { return_to: Box<State> },
    AwaitingNetwork { return_to: Box<State> }, AwaitingLookup { return_to: Box<State> }, AwaitingTool { return_to: Box<State> },
    Failed { class: FailureClass, from: Box<State> }, Discarded,
}
impl State { pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str; pub fn is_disc_phase(&self) -> bool; pub fn is_file_phase(&self) -> bool; pub fn is_waiting(&self) -> bool; }

/// The `reason` of spec 12's `waiting` event. Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum WaitReason { Share, Space, Makemkv, Network, Lookup, Tool }

/// Spec 12's notification events, a closed set (the engine adds job_id, fingerprint, title, drive, message, time). Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "event")]
pub enum NotifyEvent {
    DiscDone, AlreadyRipped, Filed,
    NeedsReview { reasons: Vec<ReviewReason> },
    Waiting { reason: WaitReason },
    Resumed,
    Failed { class: FailureClass },
    EjectFailed,
}

/// 10.1's events, plus the engine's answers the reducer needs to walk the main line (SpaceOk for the space checks of 7,
/// FilePhaseSlot for spec 6's one-job file phase, which phase 2 also grants by delivering ReviewApproved, ReFinalise, or
/// Retry of a job that failed in its file phase; HoldForReview for 6.3 step 7's hold after a copy; FileDone for the rename
/// of 6.4 step 14). Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "event")]
pub enum Event {
    MediaArrived, MediaRemoved,
    FingerprintDone, FingerprintFailed { failure: Failure },
    ScanDone, ScanFailed { failure: Failure },
    PlanDone { mode: Mode }, PlanFailed { failure: Failure },
    SpaceOk, SpaceShort, SpaceFreed,
    TitleRipped, TitleRipFailed { failure: Failure },
    /// `last`: no planned (or assigned) title is left to rip or extract.
    TitleVerified { last: bool },
    /// 6.2 step 7: a mismatch; the first is re-ripped, the second goes on (the engine records verify_failed for the decision).
    TitleVerifyFailed { second: bool, last: bool },
    /// `hash_errors`: MSG:5079 (6.3 step 6); the engine carries copy_hash_errors into HoldForReview's reasons.
    CopyDone { scan_listed_titles: bool, hash_errors: bool }, CopyFailed { failure: Failure, second: bool },
    TitleExtracted, ExtractFailed { failure: Failure },
    Ejected, EjectFailed,
    HoldForReview { reasons: Vec<ReviewReason> },
    FilePhaseSlot,
    ProbeDone, ProbeFailed { failure: Failure },
    DecisionDone { disposition: Disposition, reasons: Vec<ReviewReason> }, DecisionFailed { failure: Failure },
    RemuxDone, RemuxFailed { failure: Failure },
    FileVerified, FileVerifyFailed { failure: Failure },
    FileDone, FileFailed { failure: Failure },
    ShareLost, ShareBack,
    LicenceMessage, VersionMessage, MakeMkvChanged, NetworkNeeded, NetworkRetry,
    LookupPending, LookupAnswered,
    ToolMissing { tool: Tool }, ToolFound { tool: Tool },
    /// Spec 11 Approve. Phase 2 delivers it only once spec 6's file-phase slot is free for this job, as FilePhaseSlot is for a
    /// Direct job in Ejected; the job holds the slot until it reaches Filed, NeedsReview, Failed or Discarded.
    ReviewApproved { overrides: Overrides },
    ReviewDiscarded,
    /// Spec 11 Retry. For a job that failed in its file phase, phase 2 delivers it only once spec 6's file-phase slot is free
    /// for this job, as for ReviewApproved.
    Retry,
    RipAgain,
    /// Spec 11 Re-finalise. Phase 2 delivers it only once spec 6's file-phase slot is free for this job, as FilePhaseSlot is
    /// for a Direct job in Ejected; the job holds the slot until it reaches Filed, NeedsReview, Failed or Discarded.
    ReFinalise,
    EngineRestart { disc_present: bool },
}

/// 10.1's actions, plus Fingerprint and Plan (the main line implies them: 10.1's list omits them), CheckSpace (section 7),
/// the resume housekeeping of "Resuming after a restart", and ArmRipAgain (6.1 step 2: the engine marks the job so the next
/// insertion of its fingerprint starts a new job). RunScan also starts 6.1 step 3's database lookups beside the scan.
/// Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "action")]
pub enum Action {
    Fingerprint, RunScan, Plan, CheckSpace, RipTitle, CopyDisc, ExtractTitle, VerifyFile, Eject, Probe, ExtractSubtitleEvidence, Decide, Remux, File,
    Notify { event: NotifyEvent }, StartTimer { minutes: u32 }, DeleteJobData,
    EmptyTitleDirectory, EmptyCopyDirectory, DeletePartialFile, WaitForDisc, RecordNote { note: Note }, ArmRipAgain,
}

/// An event the state does not take. Def: T14. Use: T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Rejected { pub state: State, pub event: Event }

/// A new job's first state and actions: (Detected, [Fingerprint]) (6.1 steps 1 and 2; the engine creates it on MediaArrived
/// when `job_lookup` gives NewJob, or before the fingerprint is known). Def: T14. Use: phase 2.
pub fn new_job() -> (State, Vec<Action>);
/// (new state, actions) for every row of the reducer table below; every other pair is Rejected. Def: T14. Use: phase 2.
pub fn reduce(state: &State, event: &Event) -> Result<(State, Vec<Action>), Rejected>;
/// "Resuming after a restart" (and the actions of a waiting state's return): Detected [Fingerprint]; Fingerprinted
/// [RunScan]; Scanned [Plan]; Planned [CheckSpace]; Decided { .. } [Decide] (Decided { approved: true } may be entered
/// with Decide pending, after approval or re-finalise; Decided { approved: false } decides again too, and is gated
/// again on NeedsReview); Ripping [EmptyTitleDirectory, RipTitle]; Extracting [EmptyTitleDirectory, ExtractTitle];
/// Copying [EmptyCopyDirectory, CopyDisc]; RipVerified (either after_copy) [Eject]; Inspecting [Probe]; Remuxing [DeletePartialFile, Remux];
/// Verified [File]; Ejected nothing (it waits for FilePhaseSlot or HoldForReview); a disc-phase state with `disc_present`
/// false [WaitForDisc]; waiting, held, failed, filed and discarded states nothing, except AwaitingNetwork
/// [StartTimer { minutes: NETWORK_RETRY_MIN }] and AwaitingLookup [StartTimer { minutes: LOOKUP_RETRY_MIN }]. The state is
/// returned unchanged. Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
pub fn resume(state: &State, disc_present: bool) -> (State, Vec<Action>);
/// 10.2's Result column: DriveIncapable, MediaReadError and Unknown give Failed { class, from }; Licence and
/// NeedsMakeMkvUpdate AwaitingMakeMkv; NeedsNetwork AwaitingNetwork; Output with OutOfSpace AwaitingSpace, with
/// ShareUnreachable, WriteError or None AwaitingShare (a write error is treated as a share fault, 10.2's last paragraph);
/// LookupUnavailable AwaitingLookup; ToolMissing AwaitingTool; each waiting state returning to `from`. Def: T14. Use: T14.
pub fn failure_outcome(failure: Failure, from: &State) -> State;
/// 10.2's last paragraph, checked in this order: the share unreachable gives Output { ShareUnreachable }; out of space
/// Output { OutOfSpace }; a write error Output { WriteError }; read errors seen, a stalled read, or a process that did not
/// exit (10.2's table, 10.4) with the share healthy MediaReadError: pass `read_errors` true for each; else Unknown.
/// Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
pub fn classify_title_failure(share_healthy: bool, out_of_space: bool, write_error: bool, read_errors: bool) -> Failure;

/// Spec 5: `<fingerprint>-<n>`, n one more than the highest n among `earlier` ids of this fingerprint (ids of other
/// fingerprints and malformed ids ignored), 1 for the first. Def: T14. Use: phase 2.
pub fn job_id(fingerprint: &str, earlier: &[&str]) -> String;
/// Spec 6.1 step 2's three outcomes. Def: T14. Use: phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum JobLookup { Resume(String), AlreadyRipped(String), NewJob }
/// Spec 6.1 step 2 over the earlier jobs of this fingerprint as (job id, state, rip again armed); the one with the highest n
/// decides: Resume when it has not finished its disc phase (a disc-phase state, or a waiting state returning to one) or is
/// Failed { MediaReadError }; AlreadyRipped when it is past the disc phase (a file-phase state, NeedsReview, Filed, a
/// waiting state returning to a file-phase state, or Failed with another class from a file-phase state) and not armed;
/// NewJob otherwise (armed, Discarded, Failed with another class from a disc-phase state, or no earlier job). Def: T14.
/// Use: phase 2.
pub fn job_lookup(earlier: &[(String, State, bool)]) -> JobLookup;
```

The reducer table (`reduce`, spec 10.1 and 10.2). "Return" means: the waiting state's `return_to`, with `resume(return_to, true)`'s actions followed by `Notify { Resumed }`; phase 2 performs a disc-phase action only with the job's disc in a drive, and when the disc is gone it performs none and feeds `MediaRemoved`, which gives `[WaitForDisc]` (it does not feed the media removal its own `Eject` causes). "Outcome" means: `failure_outcome(failure, state)`, with `[Notify { Failed { class } }]` for a Failed state, and for a waiting state `[Notify { Waiting { reason } }]` preceded by `StartTimer { minutes: NETWORK_RETRY_MIN }` for AwaitingNetwork or `StartTimer { minutes: LOOKUP_RETRY_MIN }` for AwaitingLookup.

| From | Event | To | Actions |
|---|---|---|---|
| (new job, `new_job`) | | `Detected` | `[Fingerprint]` |
| `Detected` | `FingerprintDone` | `Fingerprinted` | `[RunScan]` |
| `Fingerprinted` | `ScanDone` | `Scanned` | `[Plan]` |
| `Scanned` | `PlanDone { mode }` | `Planned { mode }` | `[CheckSpace]` |
| `Planned { Direct }` | `SpaceOk` | `Ripping` | `[RipTitle]` |
| `Planned { Copy }` (10.1 "title confidence below threshold") | `SpaceOk` | `Copying` | `[CopyDisc]` |
| `Ripping` | `TitleRipped` | `Ripping` | `[VerifyFile]` |
| `Ripping` | `TitleVerified { last: false }`, or `TitleVerifyFailed { second: true, last: false }` | `Ripping` | `[RipTitle]` (the next title) |
| `Ripping` | `TitleVerifyFailed { second: false, .. }` | `Ripping` | `[RipTitle]` (the same title again, 6.2 step 7) |
| `Ripping` | `TitleVerified { last: true }`, or `TitleVerifyFailed { second: true, last: true }` | `RipVerified { after_copy: false }` | `[Eject]` |
| `RipVerified { after_copy: false }` | `Ejected` | `Ejected { after_copy: false }` | `[Notify { DiscDone }]` |
| `RipVerified { after_copy: false }` | `EjectFailed` | `Ejected { after_copy: false }` | `[Notify { EjectFailed }]` (the disc phase is over; the disc is removed by hand, 10.3, 12) |
| `Ejected { after_copy: false }` | `FilePhaseSlot` | `Inspecting` | `[Probe]` |
| `Inspecting` | `ProbeDone` | `Inspecting` | `[ExtractSubtitleEvidence, Decide]` (performed in order) |
| `Inspecting` | `DecisionDone { AutoFile, .. }` | `Decided { approved: false }` | `[CheckSpace]` |
| `Inspecting` | `DecisionDone { NeedsReview, reasons }` (10.1 "Decided, review reason or low confidence") | `NeedsReview { DispositionGate }` | `[Notify { NeedsReview { reasons } }]` |
| `Decided { .. }` | `SpaceOk` | `Remuxing` | `[Remux]` |
| `Remuxing` | `RemuxDone` | `Remuxing` | `[VerifyFile]` |
| `Remuxing` | `FileVerified` | `Verified` | `[File]` |
| `Verified` | `FileDone` | `Filed` | `[Notify { Filed }]` |
| `Copying` | `CopyDone { scan_listed_titles: true, .. }` (10.1's main line "Ripping (or Copying) → RipVerified → Ejected": a restart or a Return before the eject ejects and never empties the finished copy to copy again) | `RipVerified { after_copy: true }` | `[Eject]` |
| `RipVerified { after_copy: true }` | `Ejected` | `Ejected { after_copy: true }` | `[Notify { DiscDone }]` |
| `RipVerified { after_copy: true }` | `EjectFailed` | `Ejected { after_copy: true }` | `[Notify { EjectFailed }]` |
| `Ejected { after_copy: true }` | `HoldForReview { reasons }` (10.1 "Ejected, then NeedsReview") | `NeedsReview { AfterCopy }` | `[Notify { NeedsReview { reasons } }]` |
| `Copying` | `CopyDone { scan_listed_titles: false, .. }` (D18) | `Planned { Direct }` | `[RecordNote { DirectModeFallback }, CheckSpace]` (the copy is kept; 6.3 step 6a's "waiting in AwaitingSpace if they do not fit") |
| `Copying` | `CopyFailed { failure, second: false }` | Outcome (a read failure: `Failed { MediaReadError, from: Copying }`) | as Outcome |
| `Copying` | `CopyFailed { failure: MediaReadError, second: true }` (10.1 "second read failure") | `Planned { Direct }` | `[RecordNote { DirectModeFallback }, CheckSpace]` |
| `NeedsReview { AfterCopy }` | `ReviewApproved { overrides }` | `Extracting` | `[CheckSpace]` |
| `Extracting` | `SpaceOk` | `Extracting` | `[ExtractTitle]` |
| `Extracting` | `TitleExtracted` | `Extracting` | `[VerifyFile]` |
| `Extracting` | `TitleVerified { last: false }` | `Extracting` | `[ExtractTitle]` |
| `Extracting` | `TitleVerified { last: true }` | `Inspecting` | `[Probe]` |
| `Extracting` | `TitleVerifyFailed { second: false, .. }`, or `TitleVerifyFailed { second: true, last: false }` | `Extracting` | `[ExtractTitle]` (the same title again after a first failure, the next after a second: 6.3 step 8 "verified as in 6.2 step 7") |
| `Extracting` | `TitleVerifyFailed { second: true, last: true }` | `Inspecting` | `[Probe]` |
| `NeedsReview { DispositionGate }` | `ReviewApproved { overrides }` | `Decided { approved: true }` | `[Decide]` (with the owner's overrides) |
| `Decided { approved: true }` | `DecisionDone { .. }` (any disposition: the owner approved, 8.8) | unchanged | `[CheckSpace]` |
| `Decided { approved: false }` | `DecisionDone { AutoFile, .. }` (the decision made again after a restart, a Return or a Retry of an auto-filed job) | unchanged | `[CheckSpace]` |
| `Decided { approved: false }` | `DecisionDone { NeedsReview, reasons }` (6.4 step 12: an auto-filed job whose decision, made again, now needs review is gated again) | `NeedsReview { DispositionGate }` | `[Notify { NeedsReview { reasons } }]` |
| `NeedsReview { .. }` | `ReviewDiscarded` | `Discarded` | `[DeleteJobData]` |
| `Filed` | `ReFinalise` | `Decided { approved: true }` | `[Decide]` |
| `Filed`, `NeedsReview { .. }`, any file-phase state, `Failed { from, .. }` with `from` a file-phase state, any waiting state whose `return_to` is a file-phase state | `RipAgain` | unchanged | `[ArmRipAgain]` |
| any disc- or file-phase state | `ShareLost` | `AwaitingShare { return_to: state }` | `[Notify { Waiting { Share } }]` |
| any disc- or file-phase state | `SpaceShort` | `AwaitingSpace { return_to: state }` | `[Notify { Waiting { Space } }]` |
| `AwaitingShare` / `AwaitingSpace` | `ShareBack` / `SpaceFreed` | Return | as Return |
| `Scanned`, `Ripping`, `Copying` | `LicenceMessage`, `VersionMessage` | `AwaitingMakeMkv { return_to: state }` | `[Notify { Waiting { Makemkv } }]` |
| `AwaitingMakeMkv` | `MakeMkvChanged` | Return | as Return |
| `Scanned`, `Ripping`, `Copying` (only these) | `NetworkNeeded` | `AwaitingNetwork { return_to: state }` | `[StartTimer { minutes: NETWORK_RETRY_MIN }, Notify { Waiting { Network } }]` |
| `AwaitingNetwork` | `NetworkRetry` | Return | as Return |
| `Ejected { .. }`, `Inspecting` | `LookupPending` | `AwaitingLookup { return_to: state }` | `[StartTimer { minutes: LOOKUP_RETRY_MIN }, Notify { Waiting { Lookup } }]` |
| `AwaitingLookup` | `LookupPending` (the hourly retry found it still pending) | unchanged | `[StartTimer { minutes: LOOKUP_RETRY_MIN }]` |
| `AwaitingLookup` | `LookupAnswered` | Return | as Return |
| any disc-phase state, `Extracting` | `ToolMissing { Makemkvcon }` | `AwaitingTool { return_to: state }` | `[Notify { Waiting { Tool } }]` |
| any disc- or file-phase state | `ToolMissing { Mkvmerge }` | `AwaitingTool { return_to: state }` | `[Notify { Waiting { Tool } }]` |
| any file-phase state | `ToolMissing { Ffprobe }`, `ToolMissing { Ffmpeg }` | `AwaitingTool { return_to: state }` | `[Notify { Waiting { Tool } }]` |
| any disc-phase state | `ToolMissing { Ffprobe }`, `ToolMissing { Ffmpeg }` | unchanged (the disc phase runs; the job waits when it would enter Inspecting) | `[]` |
| any state | `ToolMissing { Java }` | unchanged | `[RecordNote { LabelRuleUnavailable }]` |
| `AwaitingTool` | `ToolFound { .. }` | Return | as Return |
| the state whose step failed, in the order of the events: `Detected`, `Fingerprinted`, `Scanned`, `Ripping`, `Extracting`, `Inspecting`, `Inspecting` or `Decided { .. }`, `Remuxing`, `Remuxing`, `Verified` | `FingerprintFailed`, `ScanFailed`, `PlanFailed`, `TitleRipFailed`, `ExtractFailed`, `ProbeFailed`, `DecisionFailed`, `RemuxFailed`, `FileVerifyFailed`, `FileFailed` | Outcome | as Outcome |
| `Failed { class, from }`, class not DriveIncapable | `Retry` | `from` | `resume(from, true)`'s actions (phase 2 performs a disc-phase action only with the job's disc in a drive; when the disc is gone it performs none and feeds `MediaRemoved`, which gives `[WaitForDisc]`) |
| `Failed { DriveIncapable, .. }` | `Retry` | Rejected (10.2 "no retry") | |
| `Failed { MediaReadError, from }` | `MediaArrived` (the disc inserted again, either drive) | `from` | `resume(from, true)`'s actions, then `[Notify { Resumed }]` |
| any disc-phase state | `MediaRemoved` | unchanged | `[WaitForDisc]` |
| any disc-phase state | `MediaArrived` | unchanged | `resume(state, true)`'s actions |
| any state | `EngineRestart { disc_present }` | `resume(state, disc_present)` | its actions |

```rust
/// recording's two TheDiscDB files; for tmdb.json no status line n/a, 404 miss, 200 with the record read hit, anything
/// else failed (`tmdb_answer`); for a pinned log "hit" when a record was read, else "n/a". Def: T15. Use: T15, T16.

pub struct LookupFile { pub path: Option<String>, pub answer: String }

    pub remembered: Option<String>,
}
/// `lazymkv-dev plan`'s document: the slug or path, the inputs found, the settings in force (defaults, or --settings FILE)
/// with their problems (`Settings::validate`; printed, and the plan is made with them), and the Plan. Task 15 reads
/// --settings FILE with `Settings::from_json`, which returns the settings with validate's problems, so a file whose only
/// problems are validate's still plans; only from_json's Err refuses the file. Def: T15. Use: T15, T16, T19.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct PlanDoc { pub slug: String, pub inputs: PlanInputsSummary, pub settings: Settings, pub settings_problems: Vec<SettingsProblem>, pub plan: Plan }
/// The argument, borrowed: a resolved recording, or a bare scan file. Def: T15. Use: T15, T16.
pub enum PlanSource<'a> { Recording(&'a Recording), ScanFile(&'a std::path::Path) }
/// The optional files. Def: T15. Use: T15, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct PlanOptions { pub settings: Option<std::path::PathBuf>, pub tmdb_search: Option<std::path::PathBuf>, pub tmdb_record: Option<std::path::PathBuf>, pub remembered: Option<std::path::PathBuf> }
/// A recording (slug or directory): reads scan.txt, meta.json (fingerprint, disc_id), the first of
/// `disc::bdmt_candidates` under nav/BDMV/META/DL through `disc::bdmt_name`, thediscdb-hash.json (`parse_dischash`),
/// thediscdb-discid.json (`parse_discid`), tmdb.json (`parse_recorded`), lookup-status.txt; an absent lookup file means that
/// lookup was not made, an answer file whose status line is not 200 is not parsed (the recorder keeps the error body of a
/// 404 or a failed lookup), and only a file that exists, answered 200 or has no status line, and does not parse is
/// Refused { code: 2 }. A bare scan file
/// `<dir>/discNN.txt` is a pinned log: its fingerprint is `fingerprint::content_hash(&fingerprint::hashed_files(log))` of
/// its HSH lines; `discdb_by_fingerprint` is `corpus/thediscdb-api/dischash-<fingerprint>.json` under `repo_root(ctx.cwd)`
/// when present (it carries media), else `<dir>/discNN.json` with the same stem (no media: kind and TMDb ID then unknown);
/// `discdb_by_disc_id` is None (TheDiscDB's global_disc_id is not the disc ID, spec 5); no TMDb answer. A directory argument
/// is always a recording. Then --tmdb-search, --tmdb-record, --remembered and --settings when given; the disc name with
/// `lookup::name::disc_name(bdmt, disc.volume_label)`; PlanInputs with no sessions, no overrides and default LibraryFacts;
/// `plan::plan`. Refused { code: 2 } only; exit 3 comes from the caller's resolve_recording. Def: T15. Use: T15, T16.
pub fn plan_doc(ctx: &Ctx, source: &PlanSource<'_>, options: &PlanOptions) -> Result<PlanDoc, Refused>;
/// `plan`'s entry point: tests `ctx.abs(arg).is_file()` first (a scan file), and only otherwise calls `resolve_recording`
/// (which refuses a path-shaped argument that is not a directory, so `plan corpus/owner/x/scan.txt` would exit 2). Exit 0 when
/// the plan is printed, with or without review reasons or settings problems; 2 for an argument error or any refusal of
/// plan_doc (an unreadable scan, or a lookup, settings, TMDb or remembered file that does not parse, and also a scan that
/// cannot be typed or planned and a remembered file for another fingerprint); 3 when a slug is given and the evidence clone
/// is absent; never 1 (RP24). Def: T15. Use: T15.
pub fn run(ctx: &Ctx, args: &[String], out: &mut dyn Write, err: &mut dyn Write) -> i32;
```

`cmd::plan::run` is registered in `COMMANDS` as `("plan", cmd::plan::run as Command, "<slug|recording dir|scan file> [--evidence DIR] [--settings FILE] [--tmdb-search FILE] [--tmdb-record FILE] [--remembered FILE]")`, placed after `decide`; Task 19 adds the same row to the port spec's section 3.4 after `decide`, so `COMMANDS` stays in that section's order.

```rust
#[serde(untagged)]
pub enum PlanEntry { Results(PlanDoc), Skipped { skipped: String } }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(untagged)]
pub enum DecisionEntry { Results(DecisionDoc), Skipped { skipped: String } }
/// `DecideDoc` gains, after `reviews`: `pub plan: PlanEntry` and `pub decision: DecisionEntry`. `decide_doc` gains the
/// parameter `settings` (decide's `--settings FILE`, which plan_doc takes against ctx.cwd) and fills both after `reviews`:
/// `plan_doc(ctx, &PlanSource::Recording(rec), &PlanOptions { settings: settings.map(Path::to_path_buf), ..PlanOptions::default() })`
/// (Skipped with the refusal's line when it refuses, a refused settings file included), then `decision_doc` (Skipped with
/// its Err sentence when the plan does not include the label's title or an input cannot be read). The existing goldens
/// stay safe because tests/decide.rs compares section by section. Def: T16. Use: T16.
pub fn decide_doc(ctx: &Ctx, rec: &Recording, label: &str, text: Option<&Path>, selection: Option<Selection>, settings: Option<&Path>) -> Result<DecideDoc, Refused>;
pub fn decision_doc(ctx: &Ctx, rec: &Recording, label: &str, plan: &PlanDoc, doc: &DecideDoc) -> Result<DecisionDoc, String>;
```

And in `crates/dev/src/cmd/plan.rs` (beside Task 15's private `recording_inputs`, which they call):

```rust
/// A recording's parsed lookup answers exactly as `plan_doc` reads them (`recording_inputs`: an answer file whose
/// lookup-status.txt line is not 200 is left unparsed), so decide's decision section reads them through the same code as
/// plan_doc and never differently (one copy). Def: T16. Use: T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) struct RecordedAnswers { pub by_fingerprint: Option<DiscDbRecord>, pub by_disc_id: Vec<DiscDbRecord>, pub recorded: Option<TmdbRecord> }
/// The three answers of `recording_inputs(rec)?`, its refusal unchanged. Def: T16. Use: T16.
pub(crate) fn recorded_answers(rec: &Recording) -> Result<RecordedAnswers, Refused>;
```

`cmd::decide::run` takes `--settings FILE`, and its `COMMANDS` row becomes `("decide", cmd::decide::run as Command,
"(<slug> <label> | --rec DIR) [--text DIR] [--selection all|eng] [--settings FILE]")`; Task 19 writes the same synopsis
into the port spec's section 3.4 `decide` row.

`retune`'s synopsis gains `[--subtitles] [--text DIR]` (Task 18) and `labels`' gains `[--subtitles]` (Task 17).

## Open points settled by this file (each is a choice a task's tests pin)

1. DVD groups (8.2) are keyed by (attribute 24, segment map) because a DVD's segments restart at 1 in every title; attribute 24 is unique per DVD title, so on a DVD every title is its own group and rule 3.4's "within each rival group" never compares two DVD titles; `play_all` is not applied on a DVD.
2. A TMDb record without a runtime (or a season without episode runtimes) fails the runtime check: step 4 cannot pass, step 5 applies (0.50, identity_ambiguous).
3. Identity step 2 ("both") requires both TheDiscDB records present and, when both carry a TMDb ID, the same ID; with different IDs the fingerprint's record wins at step 3 and the disagreement is written to `evidence`.
4. TheDiscDB's "reconciles with the scan" (8.3 rule 1) means every MainMovie title matches a scan title through `match_titles`; if any MainMovie title matches none, the record falls to rule 2.
5. A MainMovie's edition comes from its item title beyond the media title, else (Java in use and a label on the scan title) from the label table: Expendables 3's only MainMovie, title 41 `FPL_MainFeature_UR`, gets `Unrated Cut` under rule 1, pinned by `expendables_main_movie_takes_its_edition_from_the_label_table`; a second MainMovie left without an edition is an unnamed cut (0.60, unnamed_cut).
6. The DVD closed-caption stream is recognised by codec family ClosedCaptions (attribute 5 `S_CC608/DVD`), not by attribute 41 alone.
7. Isolated-score, music-and-effects and plain-subtitle (Dialogue) descriptions (D14, 8.7) are recognised only by the phrases `description_kinds` lists, marked provisional since TheDiscDB's wording is not yet known.
8. The object-based extension is read from ffprobe's profile when it contains "Atmos" or "DTS:X", else from the scan's attribute 7 ("TrueHD Atmos"); both spellings are provisional (EXP-06 not run). mkvmerge's name for an Atmos stream is accepted as "TrueHD" or "TrueHD Atmos".
9. The 8.6 rank key puts a track with no bitrate text after every track with one among lossy tracks, and an Unknown codec family after Tier::Low; G1 treats a lossy track with no bitrate as at or below 256 kb/s.
10. `channel_layout` names counts the spec does not list as "<n>.0" (3.0, 4.0, 5.0); 0 gives "0.0".
11. A derived forced-only stream whose parent cannot be found is set aside with no parent and can never become the forced track (Review Focus 4).
12. A title with exactly one English subtitle stream and no events (step 10 skipped) keeps it as Regular "English" at 0.90 (row 14 (b)).
13. The text rule's disagreement (8.7 "Text") compares the text's role (Regular, Sdh, Forced, Drop) against the kept role or the drop; `SetAside` never disagrees; `Keep` always disagrees (`text::decide` writes Keep only with its own review), and so does any verdict other than `SetAside` that carries the text rule's review, whatever its role (`text::before_yes`'s reading); streams dropped as another language and streams with an override are not compared; the text never changes a role, a drop or a flag; each disagreeing stream raises subtitle_ambiguous with one subtitle_text_disagrees note, in stream order.
14. 8.9 paths use the root's own separator ('\\' when the root holds one or is UNC, else '/'); `core` never consults the host OS.
15. The 255-byte cap cuts on a character boundary after NFC; the 32- and 90-character caps count Unicode scalar values.
16. The reserved-name rule applies to the component's stem before any extension, case-insensitively (`con.mkv` becomes `con_.mkv`).
17. `movie_path` and `tv_path` with `year: None` write `Title {tmdb-ID}` without " (Year)". `compat_tag` does not depend on the year and returns None in exactly two cases: compat is off, or the TMDb ID is year-like and the IMDb (movie) or TVDB (show) ID is absent; only the second adds compat_tag_omitted.
18. The title key on a DVD keeps attribute 24's text as MakeMKV wrote it (`t00-title01`), so keys stay stable across scans of the same disc.
19. `identify` with a pending lookup uses what is in hand and sets `lookup_pending`; the planner never lowers a step for a pending answer (8.1 "planning proceeds on structure alone").
20. `path_inside` is lexical, case-insensitive, separator-agnostic; it does not resolve symbolic links or mapped drives (phase 2 may add a resolved check).
21. `Settings::validate` also refuses `auto_threshold` outside 0..=1, `subs_diff_max > subs_same_min`, and zero for `minlength_s`, `feature_min_minutes`, `file_phase_concurrency`, since the rules divide by or compare against them; the defaults raise exactly the `tuning_root` problem.
22. `verify_rip`'s track match requires every expected track to pair in order (as 6.2 step 7's "ordered match") and tolerates no extra file track; `unknown_removed` lists MSG:4047 indices beyond the selection, as `reconcile` does.
23. `read_errors` keys by offset text, keeping the first message per offset and counting the lines (the DVD rip has 3 at offset 1048576); it keeps the `%1` error text only, never the drive's name or serial.
24. The job reducer models "a job in a waiting state stores the state it will return to" as `return_to: Box<State>` inside each waiting variant; `Failed` carries `from` for Retry; `RipAgain` is accepted on Filed, NeedsReview, the file-phase states, a Failed job whose `from` is a file-phase state and a waiting state returning to a file-phase state (which `job_lookup` counts as past the disc phase, Task 14's settled choice 15) and produces `ArmRipAgain` (the engine marks the job so the next insertion of its fingerprint starts a new job, 6.1 step 2) without changing the state.
25. The subtitle labels harness counts a label only when `how` is `read` or `watched` (D23), the owner is sure and `saw_verdict` is false (RP25), and counts row 14's UK-style SDH track from `style` "uk" on such an `sdh` label, never as a missing kind; labels on the two fitting discs named in row 14 are reported but never counted, as the audio harness treats row 13's disc.
26. `lazymkv-dev plan <dir>/discNN.txt` (a pinned log, `PlanSource::ScanFile`) takes its fingerprint from the log's HSH lines, its TheDiscDB answer from `corpus/thediscdb-api/dischash-<fingerprint>.json` when present, else from `discNN.json` with the same stem beside it, and takes no TMDb answer (identity then stops at step 3 with TheDiscDB's TMDb ID, or at step 6 when only the pinned form, without media, is found); a directory argument is always a recording (scan.txt).
27. `Wanted.original_is_english` is true when TMDb's code is absent, "en", "xx" or not in the ISO639 table; `wanted_languages(None)` therefore yields English only and `original_language_missing` is never raised without a known original language.
28. On a DVD, TheDiscDB's `source_file` is the DVD title number (attribute 24), compared as numbers through `disc::TitleSource`; pinned by `a_dvd_title_matches_thediscdb_by_its_attribute_24` (Knowing) and `firefly_disc_2_maps_title_5_to_episode_7` (Firefly disc 2's `"11"`).
29. A plain subtitle description is the `Dialogue` kind: one containing "subtitle", or one equal after trimming and case-folding to the track's own language name ("English", "ENglish"); provisional, since 8.1's last bullet names no such word. 8.7's "the one TheDiscDB describes as subtitles or SDH" is the group holding a track whose aligned description is Dialogue or Sdh.
30. Verification lowers no confidence. A failed or read-error rip holds the job through its review reason (verify_failed, read_errors), which has the same effect on the disposition as a confidence below auto_threshold (8.8).
31. 8.3 rule 2 runs before identification with English only and again with the identity's original language when it is not English (Review Focus 6); only the variant within a cut can change between the passes.
32. The owner's review decisions are `remembered::Overrides`; each covers one confidence (Set identity the identity, Assign titles the title, Override tracks every stream it names) and sets it to 1.00; a later re-plan (`PlanInputs.overrides`) and the decision (`DecisionInputs.overrides`) both apply them, so a job approved at the disposition gate (`[Decide]` in the reducer) needs no re-plan. An assigned episode carries no name of its own in both the decision and the re-plan, so both file it under TMDb's episode name.
33. 10.1's two transitions to `Ripping` from `Copying` (a copy whose scan failed, a second read failure) pass through `Planned { Direct }` and its space check, as 6.3 step 6a's "waiting in AwaitingSpace if they do not fit" requires; `EjectFailed` ends the disc phase like `Ejected` and notifies `eject_failed` instead of `disc_done`. A copy whose scan lists titles leaves `Copying` for `RipVerified { after_copy: true }` before its eject (10.1's main line "Ripping (or Copying) → RipVerified → Ejected"), so a restart or a Return in that window ejects and never empties the finished copy to copy again (`resuming_rip_verified_ejects_after_a_rip_or_a_copy`).
34. VC-1 video (attribute 5 `V_MS/VFW/WVC1`, common on older Blu-rays; no recording or pinned log holds one) is the codec family `Family::Vc1` (ruling RP26): display name "VC-1", mkvmerge name "VC-1" (mkvmerge's documented spelling, not yet seen), video, no tier. Its attributes 6 and 7 are not yet seen in a recording, so the row matches attribute 5 alone (pinned by Task 1's `vc_1_video_reads_as_vc_1_by_attribute_5_alone`, with made-up attributes 6 and 7, and by the `Vc1` line of `mkvmerge_names_are_the_ones_6_2_step_7_records_for_every_family`). A VC-1 title therefore verifies against mkvmerge's "VC-1" like any other known codec (Task 12's `a_codec_the_table_does_not_know_never_verifies_and_fails_twice_into_review` pins the contrast: a DTS Express stream, still `Family::Unknown`, never verifies; a VC-1 stream does). Open: the first VC-1 recording confirms the attribute 6 and 7 spellings and mkvmerge's name; if mkvmerge writes another name, the `Vc1` entry of `mkvmerge_names` changes with it.
35. 8.3 rule 4 lowers a rule 3 plan only when every feature is more than 10% from TMDb's runtime (the interfaces wording of `runtime_sanity`); the spec's "a feature chosen by rule 3" is read as such for a one-feature plan, the only rule 3 plan at 0.85. The readings differ only for a several-feature plan already at 0.60, where "every" adds no `title_ambiguous` while one feature is close. Pinned by Task 5's `runtime_sanity_holds_while_any_feature_is_close`; if the owner prefers the spec text, `all` becomes `any` in `runtime_sanity` and that test's `one_close` case drops to 0.60 with `title_ambiguous`.
36. TheDiscDB maps a TV disc (8.5 first bullet, 0.98) only when every Episode item of the record matches a scan title through `match_titles`, as Open point 4 requires of every MainMovie; if any Episode item matches none, `tv::by_discdb` returns None and the disc is planned as unmapped (0.60, `tv_unmapped`, whole-disc copy), because a Direct job holds only its planned titles (8.8 "Limits of D1") and would leave that episode off without the owner knowing (D1, R1). Pinned by Task 6's `an_episode_item_that_matches_no_scan_title_leaves_the_disc_unmapped`; every Episode item of the four pinned TV records and of the Office's record reconciles, so no expected plan changes.
37. `verify_final` checks tracks (type, language, name, four flags) and duration only; `Layout` carries no chapter count, codec or channels, so a remux that drops chapters passes (6.4 step 14 asks for an exact match with the decision; 8.10 says "Chapters are kept"). Phase 2's remux verification adds the staged file's chapter count (from `verify_rip`'s `file_chapters`) as an input. Recorded as a known limitation in Task 12's settled point 7.
38. A FileDecision without a path is NeedsReview even with no review reason; 8.8's closed set has no reason for it, so Task 14's NeedsReview notification may carry an empty list until the owner adds one. Task 13's `decide` builds no path without a TMDb record or identity, without the library root of the role (`movies_root`, `tv_root`; both None in spec 14's defaults), without a video height for a feature, when the record's kind does not match the filed role (a feature needs a movie record, an episode a show record: TMDb numbers the two kinds separately, 8.1), or for an episode without a season or episode number (which alone raises `tv_unmapped`); pinned by Task 13's `without_a_movies_root_no_path_is_built_and_the_job_is_held_without_a_review_reason` and `a_role_whose_kind_differs_from_the_records_builds_no_path`.
39. `LibraryFacts.path_collision` is one fact about the plain final path (no copy label); phase 2 computes it before `decide`. Under the owner's Resolve collision "keep both", `decide` files to the copy-labelled path (` 2` after the resolution label or the episode code) and raises no `path_collision`, so phase 2 also checks that labelled path before filing: when it is taken too (a third copy), the engine does not file and holds the job with `path_collision` (spec 7: lazymkv never overwrites a file it did not create, and "a path collision with any other file adds the review reason `path_collision`"). A second `LibraryFacts` field for the labelled path (and a higher copy number) is left to the plan's owner. Recorded by Task 13's settled choice 5.

```rust
impl std::str::FromStr for EditionStyle { type Err = String; fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<EditionStyle, String>; }

/// only the keys it changes: absent keys take the default (`#[serde(default)]`); an unknown key is refused

/// One refused setting: the key and a plain sentence. Spec 7 and 14. Def: T1. Use: T15 (printed when a settings file is given; phase 2 the UI).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct SettingsProblem { pub key: String, pub problem: String }

impl Settings {
    /// Every problem, in key order: staging_root inside movies_root or tv_root (or equal to one); tuning_root inside
    /// staging_root or a library root; tuning_root absent (or blank: no path component) while keep_tuning_evidence is on;
    /// auto_threshold outside 0.0..=1.0; subs_diff_max above subs_same_min; minlength_s, feature_min_minutes,
    /// file_phase_concurrency 0; makemkv_min_version not `N.N.N` (`version_triple`). Empty when valid.
    /// `Settings::default().validate()` is exactly one problem, keyed `tuning_root` (spec 14's defaults turn
    /// keep_tuning_evidence on and leave tuning_root unset); `lazymkv-dev plan` prints the problems and plans with them.
    /// Spec 7, 14. Def: T1. Use: T15.
    pub fn validate(&self) -> Vec<SettingsProblem>;
    /// A JSON settings text, read and checked (ruling RP22): keys absent from the text take Settings::default()'s value.
    /// Err, one sentence, only when the text cannot be read: text that is not JSON (serde_json's message), text that is
    /// not one JSON object (`a settings file is one JSON object of spec 14's keys`), or a key the settings lack or whose
    /// value cannot be read into its type (`<key>: <serde's message>`, the first such key in the text's order). Ok holds
    /// the settings with validate()'s problems, possibly none: a caller that needs a valid file checks the vector, and
    /// `lazymkv-dev plan` prints them and plans anyway. Spec 14. Def: T1. Use: T15.
    pub fn from_json(text: &str) -> Result<(Settings, Vec<SettingsProblem>), String>;
    /// Milliseconds as seconds for the alignment rule (`subs_tolerance_ms as f64 / 1000.0`). Def: T1. Use: T9.
    pub fn subs_tolerance_s(&self) -> f64;
    /// The text rule with this file's subtitle settings: CLEAR_MAX_BYTES = sub_clear_max_bytes, TOL_S = subs_tolerance_s(),
    /// SAME_MIN = subs_same_min, DIFF_MAX = subs_diff_max, every other field `subtitle::text::Rule::default()`'s; pinned by
    /// `the_subtitle_defaults_equal_the_text_rules_defaults` (`Settings::default().text_rule() == text::Rule::default()`).
    /// Spec 8.7, 14, RP15. Def: T1. Use: T16, T18.
    pub fn text_rule(&self) -> crate::subtitle::text::Rule;
}
```

Where this task settles what the spec and the interfaces leave open (each choice is pinned by a test below):

1. **The order and wording of `validate`'s problems.** "In key order" is the order of spec 14's table, which is the struct's field order: `staging_root` (one problem for each library root it is inside, `movies_root` first), `minlength_s`, `auto_threshold`, `feature_min_minutes`, `subs_diff_max`, `tuning_root` (absent while `keep_tuning_evidence` is on, else one problem for each of `staging_root`, `movies_root`, `tv_root` it is inside), `file_phase_concurrency`, `makemkv_min_version`. Each sentence names the key, the value and the rule, and ends with its spec section; the tests pin every sentence exactly. Not-a-number (NaN) for `auto_threshold` is outside 0 to 1.
2. **What `from_json` refuses and how it names the key of a bad value (ruling RP22).** `from_json` is the one reader of a settings text, and its `Err` is one sentence, only for text it cannot read; everything `validate` finds comes back on `Ok` beside the settings, so a caller that needs a valid file checks the vector and `lazymkv-dev plan --settings FILE` (Task 15) prints the problems and plans with them, as `PlanDoc`'s doc requires. serde's message for a wrong type names no key, so `from_json` reads the text as a JSON object first and then deserialises every key on its own: the first key in the text's order that the settings lack (`deny_unknown_fields`; a misspelt key is refused rather than silently left at its default) or whose value cannot be read into its type is the `Err`, `<key>: <serde's message>` (pinned with two bad keys out of alphabetical order, so the key named is the file's first and not a sorted map's). Text that is not JSON is serde_json's message alone. Text that is JSON but not an object (`[]`, `null`) is `a settings file is one JSON object of spec 14's keys`: without that check serde would read `[]` as a sequence into the defaults. There is no second, unchecked reader: a caller that wants the settings without the problems ignores the vector.
3. **`path_inside` and an empty path.** A path with no component (empty text, or separators only, so `/` and `\\` too) holds nothing and is inside nothing: a blank root is a missing setting, not the file system's root. `validate` therefore reads a blank `tuning_root` as not set: with `keep_tuning_evidence` on it raises the same `tuning_root is not set` problem as an absent one (spec 14's "required while keep_tuning_evidence is on"; pinned by `a_blank_tuning_root_is_not_set`). The comparison is lexical (Open point 20) and folds ASCII case only.
4. **The codec table's matching.** Attribute 5 decides the family, by exact match, with three prefix rows for codec IDs MakeMKV documents with suffixes (an ID starting `A_PCM` is LPCM, one starting `A_MPEG/` is MPEG audio, one starting `A_AAC/` is AAC). `A_DTS` is told apart by attribute 6, then attribute 7: `DTS-HD MA` or `DTS-HD Master Audio`, `DTS-HD HR` or `DTS-HD High Resolution Audio`, `DTS` or `DTS`; a 6 or 7 containing `DTS:X` is DTS-HD MA with the DTS:X extension (DTS:X is carried on a DTS-HD MA core; spelling not yet seen in a recording); any other `A_DTS` is Unknown. The object extension is read from attribute 7, then 6, and only for an audio family. VC-1 video (`V_MS/VFW/WVC1`) is the family `Vc1` (ruling RP26: display `VC-1`, mkvmerge name `VC-1`, video, no tier); no recording or pinned log holds a VC-1 stream, so its attributes 6 and 7 are not yet seen and the row matches attribute 5 alone (interfaces Open point 34).
5. **Attribute 13's grammar.** A number of ASCII digits with at most one `.`, one space, and `Kb/s` or `Mb/s` exactly (the two units of all 415 attribute 13 values: 365 in the pinned logs, 50 in the four recordings); anything else, and a value above `u32::MAX` kilobits, is None.
6. **Case in language codes.** `wanted_languages` looks TMDb's code up lower-cased (TMDb writes lower case; `ES` reads as `es`) and keeps `original_two_letter` as given; `Wanted::contains`, `Wanted::is_original` and `is_english` compare ignoring ASCII case. A code that names no language is never contained: such a stream belongs to no language (8.6 "Languages").
7. **The four note spellings the spec does not write.** `possible_audio_description`, `lossy_before_lossless`, `direct_mode_fallback` and `label_rule_unavailable` are this plan's snake_case of the notes the spec describes in words (RP7, D9, 6.3 step 6a, 8.3 rule 2 and 10.2); the other eight are the spec's own strings. Ruling RP27 keeps these four spellings as they are, pending the owner's confirmation; if the owner rules another spelling, every occurrence of the old string or its variant in the plan's code and tests changes with it.
8. **`FromStr` refusals.** Each refusal is one sentence quoting the text: `"<text>" is not a review reason (spec 8.8)`, `"<text>" is not a note (spec 8.6, 8.7, 8.9, 7)`, `"<text>" is not an edition style (combined, plex or jellyfin; spec 8.9)`. Only the exact spellings are accepted (no case folding). `Family`, `Tier`, `ObjectAudio` and `SubtitleRole` have no `FromStr` (and `Tier` and `ObjectAudio` no `ALL`): the rules write them and read them back only through serde, never from a bare string, as the interfaces' Conventions say for these four.

```rust
//! The closed sets of review reasons and notes: design spec 8.8's table of review reasons with 8.6 "Content"'s
//! `commentary_detected`, and the notes of 8.6 step 6,
//! 8.7 "Text" and "Other tracks", 8.9, 7, 6.3 step 6a, 10.2 (ToolMissing), D9 and RP7. Every rule of phase 1 returns
//! these enums, never strings: a result's `reviews` field holds `ReviewReason`s sorted by the table's order and
//! unique (`sorted_unique`), its `notes` field holds `Noted` entries in the order the rule raised them. The serde and
//! `as_str` spellings are the spec's snake_case strings; four notes the spec describes only in words take this plan's
//! spelling (`possible_audio_description`, `lossy_before_lossless`, `direct_mode_fallback`, `label_rule_unavailable`).
//! Written from the spec (RP20); used by Tasks 4 to 18.

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use serde_json::{json, Value};

    /// One review reason: its spec spelling through as_str, serde both ways and FromStr, and its place in ALL.
    fn reason_round_trips(reason: ReviewReason, text: &str) {
        assert_eq!(reason.as_str(), text);
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(reason).unwrap(), Value::String(text.to_string()));
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_value::<ReviewReason>(Value::String(text.to_string())).unwrap(), reason);
        assert_eq!(text.parse::<ReviewReason>(), Ok(reason));
        assert!(ReviewReason::ALL.contains(&reason), "{text} is missing from ALL");
    }

    /// One note, checked the same four ways.
    fn note_round_trips(note: Note, text: &str) {
        assert_eq!(note.as_str(), text);
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(note).unwrap(), Value::String(text.to_string()));
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_value::<Note>(Value::String(text.to_string())).unwrap(), note);
        assert_eq!(text.parse::<Note>(), Ok(note));
        assert!(Note::ALL.contains(&note), "{text} is missing from ALL");
    }

    /// One #[test] function per row: `name: value => "spelling",`, each calling `$check(value, "spelling")`.
    macro_rules! round_trips {
        ($check:ident { $($name:ident: $value:expr => $text:literal,)* }) => {
            $(
                #[test]
                fn $name() {
                    $check($value, $text);
                }
            )*
        };
    }

    round_trips!(reason_round_trips {
        review_reason_identity_unknown_round_trips: ReviewReason::IdentityUnknown => "identity_unknown",
        review_reason_identity_ambiguous_round_trips: ReviewReason::IdentityAmbiguous => "identity_ambiguous",
        review_reason_title_ambiguous_round_trips: ReviewReason::TitleAmbiguous => "title_ambiguous",
        review_reason_multiple_features_round_trips: ReviewReason::MultipleFeatures => "multiple_features",
        review_reason_unnamed_cut_round_trips: ReviewReason::UnnamedCut => "unnamed_cut",
        review_reason_tv_unmapped_round_trips: ReviewReason::TvUnmapped => "tv_unmapped",
        review_reason_original_language_missing_round_trips: ReviewReason::OriginalLanguageMissing => "original_language_missing",
        review_reason_no_wanted_audio_round_trips: ReviewReason::NoWantedAudio => "no_wanted_audio",
        review_reason_audio_reference_unclear_round_trips: ReviewReason::AudioReferenceUnclear => "audio_reference_unclear",
        review_reason_commentary_detected_round_trips: ReviewReason::CommentaryDetected => "commentary_detected",
        review_reason_subtitle_ambiguous_round_trips: ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous => "subtitle_ambiguous",
        review_reason_path_collision_round_trips: ReviewReason::PathCollision => "path_collision",
        review_reason_copy_hash_errors_round_trips: ReviewReason::CopyHashErrors => "copy_hash_errors",
        review_reason_verify_failed_round_trips: ReviewReason::VerifyFailed => "verify_failed",
        review_reason_read_errors_round_trips: ReviewReason::ReadErrors => "read_errors",
    });

    round_trips!(note_round_trips {
        note_possible_commentary_round_trips: Note::PossibleCommentary => "possible_commentary",
        note_possible_audio_description_round_trips: Note::PossibleAudioDescription => "possible_audio_description",
        note_lossless_original_available_round_trips: Note::LosslessOriginalAvailable => "lossless_original_available",
        note_no_english_audio_round_trips: Note::NoEnglishAudio => "no_english_audio",
        note_lossy_before_lossless_round_trips: Note::LossyBeforeLossless => "lossy_before_lossless",
        note_partial_subtitle_dropped_round_trips: Note::PartialSubtitleDropped => "partial_subtitle_dropped",
        note_subtitle_text_disagrees_round_trips: Note::SubtitleTextDisagrees => "subtitle_text_disagrees",

    #[test]
    fn all_review_reasons_are_8_8s_fourteen_and_8_6s_commentary_detected_in_order() {
        let spellings: Vec<&str> = ReviewReason::ALL.iter().map(|reason| reason.as_str()).collect();
        assert_eq!(
            spellings,
            [
                "identity_unknown",
                "identity_ambiguous",
                "title_ambiguous",
                "multiple_features",
                "unnamed_cut",
                "tv_unmapped",
                "original_language_missing",
                "no_wanted_audio",
                "audio_reference_unclear",
                "commentary_detected",
                "subtitle_ambiguous",
                "path_collision",
                "copy_hash_errors",
                "verify_failed",
                "read_errors",
            ]
        );
        assert!(ReviewReason::ALL.windows(2).all(|pair| pair[0] < pair[1]), "ALL is in the enum's order");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_string_outside_the_review_reasons_is_refused() {
        assert_eq!(
            "Identity_Unknown".parse::<ReviewReason>(),
            Err("\"Identity_Unknown\" is not a review reason (spec 8.8)".to_string())
        );
        assert_eq!("".parse::<ReviewReason>(), Err("\"\" is not a review reason (spec 8.8)".to_string()));
        assert!(serde_json::from_value::<ReviewReason>(json!("possible_commentary")).is_err());
        assert!(serde_json::from_value::<ReviewReason>(json!("identity unknown")).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn all_notes_are_the_twelve_in_spec_order() {
        let spellings: Vec<&str> = Note::ALL.iter().map(|note| note.as_str()).collect();
        assert_eq!(
            spellings,
            [
                "possible_commentary",
                "possible_audio_description",
                "lossless_original_available",
                "no_english_audio",
                "lossy_before_lossless",
                "partial_subtitle_dropped",
                "subtitle_text_disagrees",
                "compat_tag_omitted",
                "old_file_kept",
                "tuning_evidence_pending",
                "direct_mode_fallback",
                "label_rule_unavailable",
            ]
        );
        assert!(Note::ALL.windows(2).all(|pair| pair[0] < pair[1]), "ALL is in the enum's order");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_string_outside_the_notes_is_refused() {
        assert_eq!(
            "commentary_detected".parse::<Note>(),
            Err("\"commentary_detected\" is not a note (spec 8.6, 8.7, 8.9, 7)".to_string())
        );
        assert_eq!("Possible_Commentary".parse::<Note>(), Err("\"Possible_Commentary\" is not a note (spec 8.6, 8.7, 8.9, 7)".to_string()));
        assert!(serde_json::from_value::<Note>(json!("read_errors")).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_noted_note_writes_its_note_stream_and_detail_in_that_order() {
        let named = Noted {
            note: Note::PossibleCommentary,
            stream: Some(3),
            detail: "stream 3 is lossy with 2 channels and not the first eng track".to_string(),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            serde_json::to_string(&named).unwrap(),
            r#"{"note":"possible_commentary","stream":3,"detail":"stream 3 is lossy with 2 channels and not the first eng track"}"#
        );
        let unnamed = Noted {
            note: Note::NoEnglishAudio,
            stream: None,
            detail: "no English stream; the original language spa is present".to_string(),
        };
        let text = serde_json::to_string(&unnamed).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(text, r#"{"note":"no_english_audio","stream":null,"detail":"no English stream; the original language spa is present"}"#);
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<Noted>(&text).unwrap(), unnamed);
    }

    #[test]
    fn sorted_unique_sorts_by_the_table_order_and_drops_repeats() {
        assert_eq!(
            sorted_unique(vec![
                ReviewReason::ReadErrors,
                ReviewReason::IdentityUnknown,
                ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous,
                ReviewReason::IdentityUnknown,
                ReviewReason::NoWantedAudio,
                ReviewReason::ReadErrors,
            ]),
            vec![
                ReviewReason::IdentityUnknown,
                ReviewReason::NoWantedAudio,
                ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous,
                ReviewReason::ReadErrors,
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(sorted_unique(Vec::new()), Vec::<ReviewReason>::new());
        assert_eq!(sorted_unique(vec![ReviewReason::PathCollision]), vec![ReviewReason::PathCollision]);
    }
}
```

```rust
/// A reason that holds a job for review: spec 8.8's table in its order, with 8.6 "Content"'s commentary_detected placed
/// after audio_reference_unclear (the derived order, which `sorted_unique` sorts by). The serde and `as_str` spelling is
/// the spec's snake_case string.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum ReviewReason {
    /// Spec 8.1 step 6: nothing identified the work (identity confidence 0).
    IdentityUnknown,
    /// Spec 8.1 step 5: several plausible TMDb results or a failed runtime check (0.50), or a TMDb-only identification
    /// with `tmdb_only_autofile` off (capped at 0.84).
    IdentityAmbiguous,
    /// Spec 8.3 rules 3.4, 3.6 and 4: the feature cannot be told from its rivals, or its runtime is far from TMDb's.
    TitleAmbiguous,
    /// Spec 8.3 rule 3.7: the rival titles are largely different content.
    MultipleFeatures,
    /// Spec 8.3 and 8.4: a cut without an edition name.
    UnnamedCut,
    /// Spec 8.5: a TV disc no database maps to episodes.
    TvUnmapped,
    /// Spec 8.6 step 6: the original language is wanted but no stream carries it.
    OriginalLanguageMissing,
    /// Spec 8.6 step 6: no stream in a wanted language and none without a language.
    NoWantedAudio,
    /// Spec 8.6 "Content" and D21: the content rule's veto (the programme reference is not the first track of its
    /// language, and that first track is lossless or has more than two channels).
    AudioReferenceUnclear,
    /// Spec 8.6 "Content", RP7 and section 17 row 13's fallback: the content rule found the commentary pattern.
    CommentaryDetected,
    /// Spec 8.7: an alignment in the in-between band, no dialogue group, more than two dialogue tracks, or text that
    /// disagrees with the counts and timing.
    SubtitleAmbiguous,
    /// Spec 7 and 8.9: the final path is taken by a file this job did not create.
    PathCollision,
    /// Spec 6.3 step 6: the whole-disc copy completed with hash failures (MSG:5079).
    CopyHashErrors,
    /// Spec 6.2 step 7: a title failed verification a second time.
    VerifyFailed,
    /// Spec 6.2 step 7: a saved title logged read errors (MSG:2003).
    ReadErrors,
}

impl ReviewReason {
    /// Every review reason: spec 8.8's table in its order, with commentary_detected (8.6 "Content") after
    /// audio_reference_unclear. Spec 8.8.
    pub const ALL: [ReviewReason; 15] = [
        ReviewReason::IdentityUnknown,
        ReviewReason::IdentityAmbiguous,
        ReviewReason::TitleAmbiguous,
        ReviewReason::MultipleFeatures,
        ReviewReason::UnnamedCut,
        ReviewReason::TvUnmapped,
        ReviewReason::OriginalLanguageMissing,
        ReviewReason::NoWantedAudio,
        ReviewReason::AudioReferenceUnclear,
        ReviewReason::CommentaryDetected,
        ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous,
        ReviewReason::PathCollision,
        ReviewReason::CopyHashErrors,
        ReviewReason::VerifyFailed,
        ReviewReason::ReadErrors,
    ];

    /// The spec's snake_case spelling, the same string serde writes. Spec 8.8.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            ReviewReason::IdentityUnknown => "identity_unknown",
            ReviewReason::IdentityAmbiguous => "identity_ambiguous",
            ReviewReason::TitleAmbiguous => "title_ambiguous",
            ReviewReason::MultipleFeatures => "multiple_features",
            ReviewReason::UnnamedCut => "unnamed_cut",
            ReviewReason::TvUnmapped => "tv_unmapped",
            ReviewReason::OriginalLanguageMissing => "original_language_missing",
            ReviewReason::NoWantedAudio => "no_wanted_audio",
            ReviewReason::AudioReferenceUnclear => "audio_reference_unclear",
            ReviewReason::CommentaryDetected => "commentary_detected",
            ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous => "subtitle_ambiguous",
            ReviewReason::PathCollision => "path_collision",
            ReviewReason::CopyHashErrors => "copy_hash_errors",
            ReviewReason::VerifyFailed => "verify_failed",
            ReviewReason::ReadErrors => "read_errors",
        }
    }
}

impl std::str::FromStr for ReviewReason {
    type Err = String;

    /// Only the exact spellings of `as_str` are accepted.
    fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<ReviewReason, String> {
        ReviewReason::ALL
            .into_iter()
            .find(|reason| reason.as_str() == text)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("\"{text}\" is not a review reason (spec 8.8)"))
    }
}

/// A note on a job: recorded with the decision, never holding the job (spec 8.6 step 6, 8.7, 8.9, 7, 6.3 step 6a,
/// 10.2, D9, RP7). The serde and `as_str` spelling is the spec's snake_case string, or this plan's for the four the
/// spec describes in words.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Note {
    /// Spec 8.6 step 6: a kept track that is lossy, has two channels or fewer and is not the first of its language;
    /// names the track.
    PossibleCommentary,
    /// RP7: the content rule's ad-pattern and note-ad verdicts (a possible audio description).
    PossibleAudioDescription,
    /// Spec 8.6 step 6: the first track is lossy while a lossless track of the same language with fewer channels exists.
    LosslessOriginalAvailable,
    /// Spec 8.6 step 6: no English stream, but the original language is present.
    NoEnglishAudio,
    /// D9's first default: a lossy track with more channels was placed before a lossless one; names the lossy track.
    LossyBeforeLossless,
    /// Spec 8.7 "Other tracks": a track that is not full and has 150 events or more was dropped; names the track.
    PartialSubtitleDropped,
    /// Spec 8.7 "Text": the text's verdict differs from the counts and timing; names the track.
    SubtitleTextDisagrees,
    /// Spec 8.9: the Jellyfin 10 compatibility tag was left out (a year-like TMDb ID without an IMDb or TVDB ID).
    CompatTagOmitted,
    /// Spec 7 "Overwriting": a recorded file that no longer matches its record was left alone.
    OldFileKept,
    /// Spec 7 "Tuning evidence": tuning_root was unreachable or short of space; the evidence is written later.
    TuningEvidencePending,
    /// Spec 6.3 step 6a and its second read failure: the job switched to Direct mode ("a note records the switch").
    DirectModeFallback,
    /// Spec 8.3 rule 2 and 10.2 ToolMissing: MakeMKV did not report Java, so the label rule does not apply ("a note
    /// records why").
    LabelRuleUnavailable,
}

impl Note {
    /// Every note, in the order of the enum. Spec 8.6, 8.7, 8.9, 7.
    pub const ALL: [Note; 12] = [
        Note::PossibleCommentary,
        Note::PossibleAudioDescription,
        Note::LosslessOriginalAvailable,
        Note::NoEnglishAudio,
        Note::LossyBeforeLossless,
        Note::PartialSubtitleDropped,
        Note::SubtitleTextDisagrees,
        Note::CompatTagOmitted,
        Note::OldFileKept,
        Note::TuningEvidencePending,
        Note::DirectModeFallback,
        Note::LabelRuleUnavailable,
    ];

    /// The snake_case spelling, the same string serde writes. Spec 8.6, 8.7, 8.9, 7.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Note::PossibleCommentary => "possible_commentary",
            Note::PossibleAudioDescription => "possible_audio_description",
            Note::LosslessOriginalAvailable => "lossless_original_available",
            Note::NoEnglishAudio => "no_english_audio",
            Note::LossyBeforeLossless => "lossy_before_lossless",
            Note::PartialSubtitleDropped => "partial_subtitle_dropped",
            Note::SubtitleTextDisagrees => "subtitle_text_disagrees",
            Note::CompatTagOmitted => "compat_tag_omitted",
            Note::OldFileKept => "old_file_kept",
            Note::TuningEvidencePending => "tuning_evidence_pending",
            Note::DirectModeFallback => "direct_mode_fallback",
            Note::LabelRuleUnavailable => "label_rule_unavailable",
        }
    }
}

impl std::str::FromStr for Note {
    type Err = String;

    /// Only the exact spellings of `as_str` are accepted.
    fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<Note, String> {
        Note::ALL
            .into_iter()
            .find(|note| note.as_str() == text)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("\"{text}\" is not a note (spec 8.6, 8.7, 8.9, 7)"))
    }
}

/// A note as a rule raised it: which note, the scan stream it names (PossibleCommentary, PartialSubtitleDropped,
/// LossyBeforeLossless, SubtitleTextDisagrees; None for a note on the title or the job) and one plain sentence of
/// detail. Spec 8.6 step 6, 8.7, 8.9, 7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Noted {
    /// Which note.
    pub note: Note,
    /// The scan's stream number the note names, or None.
    pub stream: Option<u32>,
    /// One plain sentence of detail.
    pub detail: String,
}

/// `reasons` sorted by the enum's order (spec 8.8's table, with commentary_detected after audio_reference_unclear) and
/// without repeats: the form of every `reviews` field.
pub fn sorted_unique(reasons: Vec<ReviewReason>) -> Vec<ReviewReason> {
    let mut reasons = reasons;
    reasons.sort();
    reasons.dedup();
    reasons
}
```

```rust
/// The role of a kept English subtitle track (spec 8.7 "Regular and SDH" and "Forced"). The derived order is 8.10's
/// output order: forced, regular, then SDH (subtitles for the deaf and hard of hearing).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum SubtitleRole {
    /// The forced track, flagged forced (8.7 "Forced").
    Forced,
    /// The regular dialogue track (8.7 "Regular and SDH").
    Regular,
    /// The hearing-impaired dialogue track, flagged hearing-impaired (8.7 "Regular and SDH").
    Sdh,
}

impl SubtitleRole {
    /// Every role, in 8.10's output order.
    pub const ALL: [SubtitleRole; 3] = [SubtitleRole::Forced, SubtitleRole::Regular, SubtitleRole::Sdh];

    /// The snake_case spelling, the same string serde writes. Spec 8.7, 8.10.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            SubtitleRole::Forced => "forced",
            SubtitleRole::Regular => "regular",
            SubtitleRole::Sdh => "sdh",
        }
    }

    /// 8.7's track names: "English (Forced)", "English", "English (SDH)".
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            SubtitleRole::Forced => "English (Forced)",
            SubtitleRole::Regular => "English",
            SubtitleRole::Sdh => "English (SDH)",
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
        assert_eq!(wanted.original_two_letter.as_deref(), Some("qq"));
        assert_eq!(wanted.original, Vec::<String>::new());
        assert!(wanted.original_is_english);
        assert!(!wanted.contains("qqq"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_tmdb_code_in_capitals_is_looked_up_lower_case() {
        let spanish = wanted_languages(Some("ES"));
        assert_eq!(spanish.original_two_letter.as_deref(), Some("ES"));
        assert_eq!(spanish.original, codes(&["spa"]));
        assert!(!spanish.original_is_english);
        let english = wanted_languages(Some("EN"));
        assert_eq!(english.original, Vec::<String>::new());
        assert!(english.original_is_english);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_stream_without_a_language_is_never_a_wanted_language() {
        let wanted = wanted_languages(Some("es"));
        for code in ["und", "", "-", "zxx", "mul", "mis"] {
            assert!(!wanted.contains(code), "{code:?}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn is_english_accepts_eng_and_en_in_any_case_only() {
        for code in ["eng", "en", "ENG", "En"] {
            assert!(is_english(code), "{code:?}");
        }
        for code in ["enm", "spa", "", "und", "e"] {
            assert!(!is_english(code), "{code:?}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn is_no_language_reads_none_and_the_six_no_language_codes() {
        assert!(is_no_language(None));
        for code in ["", "-", "und", "UND", "zxx", "mul", "mis"] {
            assert!(is_no_language(Some(code)), "{code:?}");
        }
        for code in ["eng", "spa", "en", "xx"] {
            assert!(!is_no_language(Some(code)), "{code:?}");
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
//! reconciler's bibliographic-to-terminology mapping (compare_tracks.B_TO_T) and the audio rule's tables
//! (audio_similarity.ISO639, NO_LANGUAGE, TMDB_NO_LANGUAGE; spec 8.6 "Languages").
```

```rust
//! Phase 1 adds the wanted languages of R4 and spec 8.6 "Languages" over the same tables (`Wanted`,
```

and replace it with

```rust
pub fn iso639(code: &str) -> Option<&'static [&'static str]> {
    ISO639.iter().find(|(two, _)| *two == code).map(|(_, three)| *three)
}

/// The wanted languages of one work (R4, spec 8.6 "Languages"): English always, plus the original language when TMDb
/// gives one that is not English. Built by `wanted_languages`.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Wanted {
    /// TMDb's two-letter code as given (None when TMDb is unknown).
    pub original_two_letter: Option<String>,
    /// The original language's three-letter codes (empty for English, "xx", None, or a code the table lacks).
    pub original: Vec<String>,
    /// ["eng"] always.
    pub english: Vec<String>,
    /// True when the original language is English, unknown, none, or absent from the table (8.6 "Content": English is
    /// then the reference language).
    pub original_is_english: bool,
}

/// The wanted languages (R4, spec 8.6 "Languages"): English always, plus the original language's three-letter codes
/// through `iso639` when TMDb's code is Some and not "en" and not `TMDB_NO_LANGUAGE`. The code is looked up
/// lower-cased (TMDb writes it lower-case, so "ES" reads as "es"); `original_two_letter` keeps it as given.
pub fn wanted_languages(original_language: Option<&str>) -> Wanted {
    let original: Vec<String> = match original_language.map(str::to_ascii_lowercase) {
        Some(code) if code != "en" && code != TMDB_NO_LANGUAGE => match iso639(&code) {
            Some(three) => three.iter().map(|code| code.to_string()).collect(),
            None => Vec::new(),
        },
        _ => Vec::new(),
    };
    let original_is_english = original.is_empty();
    Wanted {
        original_two_letter: original_language.map(str::to_string),
        original,
        english: vec!["eng".to_string()],
        original_is_english,
    }
}

impl Wanted {
    /// A stream's attribute 3 is a wanted code: English (`is_english`) or one of the original language's codes,
    /// ignoring ASCII case. A code that names no language is never wanted: such a stream is kept as belonging to no
    /// language (spec 8.6 "Languages").
    pub fn contains(&self, code: &str) -> bool {
        is_english(code) || self.is_original(code)
    }

    /// A stream's code is one of the original language's codes, ignoring ASCII case (never, for an English work).
    /// Spec 8.6 "Languages".
    pub fn is_original(&self, code: &str) -> bool {
        self.original.iter().any(|original| original.eq_ignore_ascii_case(code))
    }
}

/// "eng" or "en", ignoring ASCII case: an English stream (spec 8.6, 8.7).
pub fn is_english(code: &str) -> bool {
    code.eq_ignore_ascii_case("eng") || code.eq_ignore_ascii_case("en")
}

/// A stream that belongs to no language (spec 8.6 "Languages": no code, or "und"): `NO_LANGUAGE.contains(code)` after
/// lower-casing; None counts as no language.
pub fn is_no_language(code: Option<&str>) -> bool {
    match code {
        None => true,
        Some(code) => NO_LANGUAGE.contains(&code.to_lowercase().as_str()),
    }
}
```

```rust
    fn pinned_logs() -> Vec<PathBuf> {
        fn walk(dir: &Path, found: &mut Vec<PathBuf>) {
            for entry in fs::read_dir(dir).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{}: {e}", dir.display())) {
                let path = entry.unwrap().path();
                let name = path.file_name().unwrap().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
                if path.is_dir() {
                    walk(&path, found);
                } else if name.starts_with("disc") && name.ends_with(".txt") && !name.ends_with("-summary.txt") {
                    found.push(path);
                }
            }
        }
        let root = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../corpus/thediscdb");

        found.sort();

        found
    }

                parse(&text).streams.into_values()
            })
            .collect()
```

```rust
/// A codec family the rules name (spec 8.6 "Codecs", 8.6 step 3's tiers, 6.2 step 7's mkvmerge names). The serde and
/// `as_str` spelling is the variant's name in kebab-case.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
pub enum Family {
    /// HEVC video (attribute 5 `V_MPEGH/ISO/HEVC`), Dolby Vision included.
    Hevc,
    /// AVC video (`V_MPEG4/ISO/AVC`).
    Avc,
    /// MPEG-2 video (`V_MPEG2`).
    Mpeg2,
    /// VC-1 video (`V_MS/VFW/WVC1`, ruling RP26; matched on attribute 5 alone, its attributes 6 and 7 not yet seen in a
    /// recording).
    Vc1,
    /// Dolby TrueHD (`A_TRUEHD`), with or without Atmos.
    TrueHd,
    /// DTS-HD Master Audio (`A_DTS`, attribute 6 `DTS-HD MA`), and DTS:X carried on it.
    DtsHdMa,
    /// DTS-HD High Resolution Audio (`A_DTS`, attribute 6 `DTS-HD HR`; spelling not yet seen in a recording).
    DtsHdHr,
    /// DTS (`A_DTS`, attribute 6 `DTS`).
    Dts,
    /// Dolby Digital, AC-3 (`A_AC3`).
    Ac3,
    /// Dolby Digital Plus, E-AC-3 (`A_EAC3`; spelling not yet seen in a recording).
    Eac3,
    /// Linear PCM (`A_LPCM`, or a codec ID starting `A_PCM`; spelling not yet seen in a recording).
    Lpcm,
    /// FLAC (`A_FLAC`; spelling not yet seen in a recording).
    Flac,
    /// MPEG audio (`A_MPEG/L2` and the other layers; spelling not yet seen in a recording).
    MpegAudio,
    /// AAC (`A_AAC`, with or without a profile suffix; spelling not yet seen in a recording).
    Aac,
    /// Blu-ray PGS subtitles (`S_HDMV/PGS`).
    Pgs,
    /// DVD subtitles (`S_VOBSUB`).
    VobSub,
    /// A DVD's closed captions (`S_CC608/DVD`), which MakeMKV converts to text (8.7 "Set aside first").
    ClosedCaptions,
    /// Any other codec (DTS Express, for one).
    Unknown,
}

impl Family {
    /// Every family, in the order of the enum. Spec 8.6 "Codecs".
    pub const ALL: [Family; 18] = [
        Family::Hevc,
```
