```rust
    ];

    /// The kebab-case spelling, the same string serde writes. Spec 8.6 "Codecs".
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Family::Hevc => "hevc",
            Family::Avc => "avc",
            Family::Mpeg2 => "mpeg2",
            Family::Vc1 => "vc1",
            Family::TrueHd => "true-hd",
            Family::DtsHdMa => "dts-hd-ma",
            Family::DtsHdHr => "dts-hd-hr",
            Family::Dts => "dts",
            Family::Ac3 => "ac3",
            Family::Eac3 => "eac3",
            Family::Lpcm => "lpcm",
            Family::Flac => "flac",
            Family::MpegAudio => "mpeg-audio",
            Family::Aac => "aac",
            Family::Pgs => "pgs",
            Family::VobSub => "vob-sub",
            Family::ClosedCaptions => "closed-captions",
            Family::Unknown => "unknown",
        }
    }
}

/// Spec 8.6 step 3.3's object-based extension. The serde and `as_str` spelling is the format's own name.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub enum ObjectAudio {
    /// Dolby Atmos (seen on TrueHD: attribute 7 `TrueHD Atmos`).
    #[serde(rename = "Atmos")]
    Atmos,
    /// DTS:X (on DTS-HD MA; spelling not yet seen in a recording).
    #[serde(rename = "DTS:X")]
    DtsX,
}

impl ObjectAudio {
    /// "Atmos" or "DTS:X", the same string serde writes. Spec 8.6 step 3.3.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            ObjectAudio::Atmos => "Atmos",
            ObjectAudio::DtsX => "DTS:X",
        }
    }
}

/// What the table says about one stream's codec (spec 8.6 "Codecs").
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Codec {
    /// The codec family.
    pub family: Family,
    /// The display name 8.10 uses ("TrueHD", "DTS-HD MA", "DTS", "Dolby Digital", "Dolby Digital Plus", "DTS-HD HR",
    /// "LPCM", "FLAC", "MPEG Audio", "AAC", "HEVC", "AVC", "MPEG-2", "VC-1", "PGS", "VobSub", "Closed Captions");
    /// attribute 6, else 7, else 5, for Unknown.
    pub display: String,
    /// From attribute 7 at scan time: "TrueHD Atmos" gives Atmos, a 7 containing "DTS:X" gives DtsX (spelling not yet
    /// seen).
    pub object: Option<ObjectAudio>,
    /// True for TrueHd, DtsHdMa, Lpcm, Flac (8.6 step 3.2 (a)); false for every other family. The product's copy
    /// beside audio::reference::is_lossless (Global Constraints, one-copy rule).
    pub lossless: bool,
}

/// The table row for MakeMKV's attributes 5 (codec ID), 6 (short name) and 7 (long name); never fails: an unknown
/// trio is `Family::Unknown`, named by attribute 6, else 7, else 5. Attribute 5 decides the family (exactly, or by
/// the prefixes `A_PCM`, `A_MPEG/` and `A_AAC/`); `A_DTS` is told apart by attribute 6, then 7. The object-based
/// extension is read from attribute 7, then 6, for an audio family only. Rows from the recordings: V_MPEGH/ISO/HEVC,
/// V_MPEG4/ISO/AVC, V_MPEG2, A_TRUEHD, A_DTS with short "DTS-HD MA" or "DTS", A_AC3, S_HDMV/PGS, S_VOBSUB,
/// S_CC608/DVD; rows the spec names but no recording shows, with MakeMKV's documented spellings: A_DTS "DTS-HD HR"
/// and "DTS:X", A_EAC3 "E-AC3", A_PCM or A_LPCM "LPCM", A_FLAC "FLAC", A_MPEG/L2 "Mpeg", A_AAC "AAC"; and
/// V_MS/VFW/WVC1, VC-1 (ruling RP26), matched on attribute 5 alone. Spec 8.6 "Codecs".
pub fn codec(id: &str, short: &str, long: &str) -> Codec {
    let family = family_of(id, short, long);
    let display = match display_name(family) {
        Some(name) => name.to_string(),
        None => [short, long, id].into_iter().find(|text| !text.is_empty()).unwrap_or("").to_string(),
    };
    let object = if is_audio(family) { object_in(long).or_else(|| object_in(short)) } else { None };
    Codec { family, display, object, lossless: is_lossless(family) }
}

/// The family attribute 5 names, with `A_DTS` told apart by attributes 6 and 7.
fn family_of(id: &str, short: &str, long: &str) -> Family {
    match id {
        "V_MPEGH/ISO/HEVC" => Family::Hevc,
        "V_MPEG4/ISO/AVC" => Family::Avc,
        "V_MPEG2" => Family::Mpeg2,
        "V_MS/VFW/WVC1" => Family::Vc1,
        "A_TRUEHD" => Family::TrueHd,
        "A_DTS" => dts_family(short, long),
        "A_AC3" => Family::Ac3,
        "A_EAC3" => Family::Eac3,
        "A_LPCM" => Family::Lpcm,
        "A_FLAC" => Family::Flac,
        "A_AAC" => Family::Aac,
        "S_HDMV/PGS" => Family::Pgs,
        "S_VOBSUB" => Family::VobSub,
        "S_CC608/DVD" => Family::ClosedCaptions,
        _ if id.starts_with("A_PCM") => Family::Lpcm,
        _ if id.starts_with("A_MPEG/") => Family::MpegAudio,
        _ if id.starts_with("A_AAC/") => Family::Aac,
        _ => Family::Unknown,
    }
}

/// An `A_DTS` stream's family: DTS:X (in attribute 6 or 7) rides on DTS-HD MA; else attribute 6 "DTS-HD MA",
/// "DTS-HD HR" or "DTS", else attribute 7 "DTS-HD Master Audio", "DTS-HD High Resolution Audio" or "DTS"; else
/// Unknown (DTS Express, for one).
fn dts_family(short: &str, long: &str) -> Family {
    if short.contains("DTS:X") || long.contains("DTS:X") {
        return Family::DtsHdMa;
    }
    match (short, long) {
        ("DTS-HD MA", _) | (_, "DTS-HD Master Audio") => Family::DtsHdMa,
        ("DTS-HD HR", _) | (_, "DTS-HD High Resolution Audio") => Family::DtsHdHr,
        ("DTS", _) | (_, "DTS") => Family::Dts,
        _ => Family::Unknown,
    }
}

/// 8.10's display name of a known family; None for Unknown.
fn display_name(family: Family) -> Option<&'static str> {
    let name = match family {
        Family::Hevc => "HEVC",
        Family::Avc => "AVC",
        Family::Mpeg2 => "MPEG-2",
        Family::Vc1 => "VC-1",
        Family::TrueHd => "TrueHD",
        Family::DtsHdMa => "DTS-HD MA",
        Family::DtsHdHr => "DTS-HD HR",
        Family::Dts => "DTS",
        Family::Ac3 => "Dolby Digital",
        Family::Eac3 => "Dolby Digital Plus",
        Family::Lpcm => "LPCM",
        Family::Flac => "FLAC",
        Family::MpegAudio => "MPEG Audio",
        Family::Aac => "AAC",
        Family::Pgs => "PGS",
        Family::VobSub => "VobSub",
        Family::ClosedCaptions => "Closed Captions",
        Family::Unknown => return None,
    };
    Some(name)
}

/// The audio families.
fn is_audio(family: Family) -> bool {
    matches!(
        family,
        Family::TrueHd
            | Family::DtsHdMa
            | Family::DtsHdHr
            | Family::Dts
            | Family::Ac3
            | Family::Eac3
            | Family::Lpcm
            | Family::Flac
            | Family::MpegAudio
            | Family::Aac
    )
}

/// 8.6 step 3.2 (a): TrueHD, DTS-HD MA, LPCM, FLAC.
fn is_lossless(family: Family) -> bool {
    matches!(family, Family::TrueHd | Family::DtsHdMa | Family::Lpcm | Family::Flac)
}

/// The extension a text names: "Atmos" anywhere gives Atmos, else "DTS:X" anywhere gives DtsX.
fn object_in(text: &str) -> Option<ObjectAudio> {
    if text.contains("Atmos") {
        Some(ObjectAudio::Atmos)
    } else if text.contains("DTS:X") {
        Some(ObjectAudio::DtsX)
    } else {
        None
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 20: Write the bit rate and the tiers**

Insert into `crates/core/src/codec.rs`, after `object_in` (the last function Step 16 wrote) and above `#[cfg(test)]`:

```rust
/// Attribute 13 text ("1.5 Mb/s", "192 Kb/s", "9.8 Mb/s") as kilobits per second, rounded to the nearest whole
/// number; None for anything else. The grammar is the one every recorded and pinned value follows: ASCII digits with
/// at most one '.', one space, then "Kb/s" or "Mb/s" exactly; a value above u32::MAX kilobits is None. Spec 9.4
/// "Attribute 13 is text with units".
pub fn bitrate_kbps(text: &str) -> Option<u32> {
    let (number, unit) = text.split_once(' ')?;
    let factor = match unit {
        "Kb/s" => 1.0,
        "Mb/s" => 1000.0,
        _ => return None,
    };
    let digits = number.bytes().filter(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit()).count();
    let dots = number.bytes().filter(|byte| *byte == b'.').count();
    if digits == 0 || dots > 1 || digits + dots != number.len() {
        return None;
    }
    let kbps = (number.parse::<f64>().ok()? * factor).round();
    if kbps > f64::from(u32::MAX) {
        return None;
    }
    Some(kbps as u32)
}

/// Spec 8.6 step 3.2's fidelity tiers, in rank order: the derived order sorts the better tier first.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Tier {
    /// (a) Lossless: TrueHD, DTS-HD MA, LPCM, FLAC.
    Lossless,
    /// (b) High-rate lossy: DTS-HD High Resolution, E-AC-3 at 768 kb/s or more, DTS at 1.5 Mb/s or more.
    HighRateLossy,
    /// (c) Other lossy: AC-3, lower-rate E-AC-3 and DTS.
    OtherLossy,
    /// (d) MPEG audio and AAC.
    Low,
}

impl Tier {
    /// The snake_case spelling, the same string serde writes. Spec 8.6 step 3.2.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Tier::Lossless => "lossless",
            Tier::HighRateLossy => "high_rate_lossy",
            Tier::OtherLossy => "other_lossy",
            Tier::Low => "low",
        }
    }
}

/// Spec 8.6 step 3.2's E-AC-3 line: at this rate or more an E-AC-3 track is high-rate lossy (a fixed value of spec 14).
pub const EAC3_HIGH_RATE_KBPS: u32 = 768;

/// Spec 8.6 step 3.2's DTS line, 1.5 Mb/s: at this rate or more a DTS track is high-rate lossy (a fixed value of
/// spec 14).
pub const DTS_HIGH_RATE_KBPS: u32 = 1500;

/// Spec 8.6 step 3.2: (a) Lossless for the lossless families (`is_lossless`'s set, not repeated here); (b)
/// HighRateLossy for DtsHdHr, Eac3 at EAC3_HIGH_RATE_KBPS or more, Dts at DTS_HIGH_RATE_KBPS or more; (c) OtherLossy
/// for Ac3, lower-rate or unknown-rate Eac3 and Dts; (d) Low for MpegAudio and Aac; None for Unknown and for video and
/// subtitle families.
pub fn tier(family: Family, bitrate_kbps: Option<u32>) -> Option<Tier> {
    let at_least = |line: u32| bitrate_kbps.is_some_and(|rate| rate >= line);
    match family {
        family if is_lossless(family) => Some(Tier::Lossless),
        Family::DtsHdHr => Some(Tier::HighRateLossy),
        Family::Eac3 if at_least(EAC3_HIGH_RATE_KBPS) => Some(Tier::HighRateLossy),
        Family::Dts if at_least(DTS_HIGH_RATE_KBPS) => Some(Tier::HighRateLossy),
        Family::Ac3 | Family::Eac3 | Family::Dts => Some(Tier::OtherLossy),
        Family::MpegAudio | Family::Aac => Some(Tier::Low),
        // Video, subtitle and Unknown families have no tier. The guard arm above took the lossless families (the one
        // copy of the set is `is_lossless`); a guard does not count toward exhaustiveness, so a wildcard ends it.
        _ => None,
    }
}
```

```rust
        assert_eq!(names(Family::Ac3), ["AC-3"]);
        assert_eq!(names(Family::Eac3), ["E-AC-3"]);
        assert_eq!(names(Family::Lpcm), ["PCM"]);
        assert_eq!(names(Family::Flac), ["FLAC"]);
        assert_eq!(names(Family::MpegAudio), ["MP2"]);
        assert_eq!(names(Family::Aac), ["AAC"]);
        assert_eq!(names(Family::Pgs), ["HDMV PGS"]);
        assert_eq!(names(Family::VobSub), ["VobSub"]);
        assert_eq!(names(Family::ClosedCaptions), ["SubRip/SRT"]);
        assert!(names(Family::Unknown).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_recorded_codecs_give_the_names_mkvmerge_wrote_for_them() {
        for (id, short, long, written) in [
            ("V_MPEGH/ISO/HEVC", "MpegH", "MpegH HEVC Main10@L5.1", "HEVC/H.265/MPEG-H"),
            ("V_MPEG4/ISO/AVC", "Mpeg4", "Mpeg4 AVC High@L4.1", "AVC/H.264/MPEG-4p10"),
            ("V_MPEG2", "Mpeg2", "Mpeg2", "MPEG-1/2"),
            ("A_DTS", "DTS-HD MA", "DTS-HD Master Audio", "DTS-HD Master Audio"),
            ("A_DTS", "DTS", "DTS", "DTS"),
            ("A_AC3", "DD", "Dolby Digital", "AC-3"),
            ("S_HDMV/PGS", "PGS", "HDMV PGS Subtitles", "HDMV PGS"),
            ("S_VOBSUB", "", "Dvd Subtitles", "VobSub"),
            ("S_CC608/DVD", "CC", "Closed Captions", "SubRip/SRT"),
        ] {
            assert!(mkvmerge_names(&codec(id, short, long)).contains(&written), "{id} {short} {long}");
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
/// Spec 8.6 "Codecs": 1 "1.0", 2 "2.0", 6 "5.1", 7 "6.1", 8 "7.1"; any other count "<n>.0" (3, 4, 5 give "3.0",
/// "4.0", "5.0"; 0 gives "0.0"; Open point 10).
pub fn channel_layout(channels: u32) -> String {
    match channels {
        6 => "5.1".to_string(),
        7 => "6.1".to_string(),
        8 => "7.1".to_string(),
        other => format!("{other}.0"),
    }
}

/// ffprobe's profile string to the object-based extension (6.4 step 9; EXP-06 not run, so provisional): a profile
/// containing "Atmos" gives Atmos, one containing "DTS:X" gives DtsX, else None (Open point 8).
pub fn object_audio(ffprobe_profile: Option<&str>) -> Option<ObjectAudio> {
    ffprobe_profile.and_then(object_in)
}

/// The codec names `mkvmerge -J` may write for a stream of this codec, as 6.2 step 7 records them; `verify_rip`
/// accepts any of them. Hevc ["HEVC/H.265/MPEG-H"], Avc ["AVC/H.264/MPEG-4p10"], Mpeg2 ["MPEG-1/2"], TrueHd
/// ["TrueHD", "TrueHD Atmos"] (the second provisional: an Atmos stream's spelling is not yet seen), DtsHdMa
/// ["DTS-HD Master Audio"], DtsHdHr ["DTS-HD High Resolution Audio"], Dts ["DTS"], Ac3 ["AC-3"], Eac3 ["E-AC-3"], Lpcm
/// ["PCM"], Flac ["FLAC"], MpegAudio ["MP2"], Aac ["AAC"], Pgs ["HDMV PGS"], VobSub ["VobSub"], ClosedCaptions
/// ["SubRip/SRT"] (converted through attribute 41 "Text"), Vc1 ["VC-1"] (ruling RP26), Unknown []. The names seen in
/// the recordings are HEVC, DTS-HD Master Audio, DTS, AC-3, HDMV PGS, MPEG-1/2, VobSub, SubRip/SRT and AVC; the
/// others are mkvmerge's documented spellings, not yet seen. Spec 6.2 step 7.
pub fn mkvmerge_names(codec: &Codec) -> &'static [&'static str] {
    match codec.family {
        Family::Hevc => &["HEVC/H.265/MPEG-H"],
        Family::Avc => &["AVC/H.264/MPEG-4p10"],
        Family::Mpeg2 => &["MPEG-1/2"],
        Family::Vc1 => &["VC-1"],
        Family::TrueHd => &["TrueHD", "TrueHD Atmos"],
        Family::DtsHdMa => &["DTS-HD Master Audio"],
        Family::DtsHdHr => &["DTS-HD High Resolution Audio"],
        Family::Dts => &["DTS"],
        Family::Ac3 => &["AC-3"],
        Family::Eac3 => &["E-AC-3"],
        Family::Lpcm => &["PCM"],
        Family::Flac => &["FLAC"],
        Family::MpegAudio => &["MP2"],
        Family::Aac => &["AAC"],
        Family::Pgs => &["HDMV PGS"],
        Family::VobSub => &["VobSub"],
        Family::ClosedCaptions => &["SubRip/SRT"],
        Family::Unknown => &[],
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 28: Write the settings and their defaults**

Insert into `crates/core/src/settings.rs`, between the `//!` header and `#[cfg(test)]`:

```rust
/// The edition layout of spec 8.9's table (setting `edition_style`, spec 14). The serde and `as_str` spelling is the
/// table's lower-case name.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum EditionStyle {
    /// The default: one folder, files named `- <Res> <Ed> {edition-<Ed>}` (a Plex edition and a Jellyfin version
    /// label; not yet verified, EXP-09 not run).
    Combined,
    /// One folder per edition, named with `{edition-<Ed>}` (the layout Plex documents).
    Plex,
    /// One folder, files named `- <Res> <Ed>` (Jellyfin's version picker).
    Jellyfin,
}

impl EditionStyle {
    /// Every style, in spec 8.9's table order.
    pub const ALL: [EditionStyle; 3] = [EditionStyle::Combined, EditionStyle::Plex, EditionStyle::Jellyfin];

    /// "combined", "plex" or "jellyfin", the same string serde writes. Spec 8.9.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            EditionStyle::Combined => "combined",
            EditionStyle::Plex => "plex",
            EditionStyle::Jellyfin => "jellyfin",
        }
    }
}

impl std::str::FromStr for EditionStyle {
    type Err = String;

    /// Only the exact spellings of `as_str` are accepted.
    fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<EditionStyle, String> {
        EditionStyle::ALL
            .into_iter()
            .find(|style| style.as_str() == text)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("\"{text}\" is not an edition style (combined, plex or jellyfin; spec 8.9)"))
    }
}

/// Spec 14 "tool paths": overrides for 4.4's programs (MakeMKV, MKVToolNix, ffprobe, the Java runtime) plus ffmpeg
/// (6.4 step 10a); None means auto. A settings file may name only the programs it overrides; an unknown program is
/// refused.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct ToolPaths {
    /// MakeMKV's `makemkvcon` (4.4).
    pub makemkvcon: Option<String>,
    /// MKVToolNix's `mkvmerge` (4.4).
    pub mkvmerge: Option<String>,
    /// FFmpeg's `ffprobe` (4.4).
    pub ffprobe: Option<String>,
    /// `ffmpeg`, which 6.4 step 10a runs.
    pub ffmpeg: Option<String>,
    /// The Java runtime MakeMKV uses for Blu-ray menus (4.4; 8.3 rule 2 needs it).
    pub java: Option<String>,
}

/// Every key of spec 14 with its default (`Settings::default()` is the table's Default column), in the table's
/// order. A settings file may name only the keys it changes: absent keys take the default (`#[serde(default)]`); an
/// unknown key is refused (`deny_unknown_fields`).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Settings {
    /// Spec 7: where rips and disc copies are staged, a local or UNC path; None until set. Required by the engine,
    /// not by any rule here.
    pub staging_root: Option<String>,
    /// Spec 7 and 8.9: the movie library's root; None until set.
    pub movies_root: Option<String>,
    /// Spec 7 and 8.9: the TV library's root; None until set.
    pub tv_root: Option<String>,
    /// 120: MakeMKV's minimum title length in seconds (`--minlength`, 9.2; 8.2's candidate filter reads it).
    pub minlength_s: u32,
    /// 1024: MakeMKV's read cache in MB (`--cache`, 9.2; not yet verified, EXP-04 not run).
    pub cache_mb: u32,
    /// 0.85: the confidence needed to file automatically (8.8; 6.2 and 6.3 choose the mode by it).
    pub auto_threshold: f64,
    /// 45: the shortest title considered a feature, in minutes (8.3 rule 3.2).
    pub feature_min_minutes: u32,
    /// true: D9, a TMDb-only identification may file automatically (8.1 caps it at 0.84 when false).
    pub tmdb_only_autofile: bool,
    /// true: D9, channel count is compared before fidelity tier when ordering audio (8.6 step 3).
    pub prefer_most_channels: bool,
    /// true: D9, original-language audio first for non-English works (8.6 step 5).
    pub original_language_first: bool,
    /// 300: the start-time tolerance of subtitle alignment, in milliseconds (8.7 "Alignment").
    pub subs_tolerance_ms: u32,
    /// 0.70: two full tracks aligned at least this much are in the same group (8.7; provisional, EXP-06 not run).
    pub subs_same_min: f64,
    /// 0.30: two full tracks aligned at most this much are in different groups (8.7; provisional, EXP-06 not run).
    pub subs_diff_max: f64,
    /// 64: image-subtitle packets this small clear the screen and are not events (8.7 "Events").
    pub sub_clear_max_bytes: i64,
    /// Combined: the edition layout (8.9; not yet verified, EXP-09 not run).
    pub edition_style: EditionStyle,
    /// false: add the square-bracket ID tag for Jellyfin 10.x (8.9).
    pub jellyfin10_compat: bool,
    /// 7: days the raw data of filed jobs is kept (7 "Retention").
    pub retention_days: u32,
    /// true: D16, keep the tuning evidence of every ripped title (6.4 step 10a, 7 "Tuning evidence").
    pub keep_tuning_evidence: bool,
    /// None: where the tuning evidence is kept; required while keep_tuning_evidence is on; not inside staging_root or
    /// a library root (7, 14).
    pub tuning_root: Option<String>,
    /// 1: simultaneous file-phase jobs (6).
    pub file_phase_concurrency: u32,
    /// 10: seconds to wait after a disc arrives before touching the drive (6.1 step 1).
    pub drive_settle_s: u32,
    /// 120: seconds to wait for the volume to mount (6.1 step 1).
    pub drive_ready_timeout_s: u32,
    /// 30: the longest allowed scan, in minutes (10.4).
    pub scan_timeout_min: u32,
    /// 300: the watchdog's stall time, in seconds (10.4).
    pub stall_timeout_s: u32,
    /// 20: read errors per minute that mark a drive as struggling (10.4).
    pub read_error_rate: u32,
    /// 30: minutes to wait for a stuck makemkvcon to exit (10.4).
    pub exit_wait_min: u32,
    /// "2.0.0": the lowest supported MakeMKV (9.1); `version_triple` reads it.
    pub makemkv_min_version: String,
    /// Auto: overrides for the external programs (spec 14 "tool paths").
    pub tool_paths: ToolPaths,
}

impl Default for Settings {
    /// Spec 14's Default column.
    fn default() -> Settings {
        Settings {
            staging_root: None,
            movies_root: None,
            tv_root: None,
            minlength_s: 120,
            cache_mb: 1024,
            auto_threshold: 0.85,
            feature_min_minutes: 45,
            tmdb_only_autofile: true,
            prefer_most_channels: true,
            original_language_first: true,
            subs_tolerance_ms: 300,
            subs_same_min: 0.70,
            subs_diff_max: 0.30,
            sub_clear_max_bytes: 64,
            edition_style: EditionStyle::Combined,
            jellyfin10_compat: false,
            retention_days: 7,
            keep_tuning_evidence: true,
            tuning_root: None,
            file_phase_concurrency: 1,
            drive_settle_s: 10,
            drive_ready_timeout_s: 120,
            scan_timeout_min: 30,
            stall_timeout_s: 300,
            read_error_rate: 20,
            exit_wait_min: 30,
            makemkv_min_version: "2.0.0".to_string(),
            tool_paths: ToolPaths::default(),
        }
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 32: Write `path_inside` and `version_triple`**

Insert into `crates/core/src/settings.rs`, after `impl Default for Settings` (the last item Step 28 wrote) and above `#[cfg(test)]`:

```rust
/// True when `inner` is `outer` or a path below it: both split on '/' and '\\', empty and trailing components
/// dropped, compared component by component ignoring ASCII case (Windows and SMB shares are case-insensitive); a UNC
/// prefix `\\server\share` is two components. A path with no component (empty, or separators only) holds nothing and
/// is inside nothing: a blank root is a missing setting. Lexical only: no link or mapped drive is resolved (Open
/// point 20). Spec 7 "The staging root may not be inside a library root".
pub fn path_inside(inner: &str, outer: &str) -> bool {
    let inner = components(inner);
    let outer = components(outer);
    !outer.is_empty()
        && inner.len() >= outer.len()
        && outer.iter().zip(&inner).all(|(outer, inner)| outer.eq_ignore_ascii_case(inner))
}

/// A path's components: split on '/' and '\\', empty ones dropped.
fn components(path: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
    path.split(|c: char| c == '/' || c == '\\').filter(|component| !component.is_empty()).collect()
}

/// The version string `N.N.N` (three runs of ASCII digits joined by '.') as a comparable triple; None otherwise (a
/// sign, a prefix, a suffix, a missing or fourth part, or a part above u32::MAX). Spec 9.1.
pub fn version_triple(text: &str) -> Option<(u32, u32, u32)> {
    let parts: Vec<&str> = text.split('.').collect();
    let [major, minor, patch] = parts.as_slice() else {
        return None;
    };
    Some((version_part(major)?, version_part(minor)?, version_part(patch)?))
}

/// One part of a version: ASCII digits only, at least one, within u32.
fn version_part(part: &str) -> Option<u32> {
    if part.is_empty() || !part.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit()) {
        return None;
    }
    part.parse().ok()
}
```

- [ ] **Step 36: Write `validate`**

Insert into `crates/core/src/settings.rs`, after `version_part` (the last function Step 32 wrote) and above `#[cfg(test)]`:

```rust
/// One refused setting (spec 7, 14): the key it concerns, as spec 14 spells it, and one plain sentence naming the value
/// and the rule it breaks.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct SettingsProblem {
    /// The settings key.
    pub key: String,
    /// The sentence.
    pub problem: String,
}

/// A SettingsProblem for `key`.
fn problem(key: &str, text: impl Into<String>) -> SettingsProblem {
    SettingsProblem { key: key.to_string(), problem: text.into() }
}

impl Settings {
    /// Every problem, in key order (spec 14's table order, which is the struct's): staging_root inside movies_root or
    /// tv_root, or equal to one (one problem per root, by `path_inside`); minlength_s 0; auto_threshold outside
    /// 0.0..=1.0 (not-a-number included); feature_min_minutes 0; subs_diff_max above subs_same_min; tuning_root
    /// absent or blank (no path component, so it is inside nothing) while keep_tuning_evidence is on, else tuning_root
    /// inside staging_root or a library root (one problem per root); file_phase_concurrency 0; makemkv_min_version not
    /// `N.N.N` (`version_triple`). Empty when valid.
    /// `Settings::default().validate()` is exactly one problem, keyed `tuning_root` (spec 14's defaults turn
    /// keep_tuning_evidence on and leave tuning_root unset); `lazymkv-dev plan` prints the problems and plans with
    /// them. Spec 7, 14, Open point 21.
    pub fn validate(&self) -> Vec<SettingsProblem> {
        let mut problems = Vec::new();
        if let Some(staging) = &self.staging_root {
            for (key, library) in [("movies_root", &self.movies_root), ("tv_root", &self.tv_root)] {
                if let Some(library) = library {
                    if path_inside(staging, library) {
                        problems.push(problem(
                            "staging_root",
                            format!(
                                "staging_root {staging} is inside {key} {library}: the staging root may not be inside a library root (spec 7)"
                            ),
                        ));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        if self.minlength_s == 0 {
            problems.push(problem(
                "minlength_s",
                "minlength_s is 0: MakeMKV's minimum title length must be at least 1 second (spec 14)",
            ));
        }
        if !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&self.auto_threshold) {
            problems.push(problem(
                "auto_threshold",
                format!("auto_threshold {} is outside 0 to 1: it is a confidence (spec 8.8)", self.auto_threshold),
            ));
        }
        if self.feature_min_minutes == 0 {
            problems.push(problem(
                "feature_min_minutes",
                "feature_min_minutes is 0: the shortest feature must be at least 1 minute (spec 8.3)",
            ));
        }
        if self.subs_diff_max > self.subs_same_min {
            problems.push(problem(
                "subs_diff_max",
                format!(
                    "subs_diff_max {} is above subs_same_min {}: the two alignment bands may not overlap (spec 8.7)",
                    self.subs_diff_max, self.subs_same_min
                ),
            ));
        }
        let tuning = self.tuning_root.as_deref().filter(|text| !components(text).is_empty());
        match tuning {
            None => {
                if self.keep_tuning_evidence {
                    problems.push(problem(
                        "tuning_root",
                        "tuning_root is not set: it is required while keep_tuning_evidence is on (spec 7, 14)",
                    ));
                }
            }
            Some(tuning) => {
                let roots = [
                    ("staging_root", &self.staging_root),
                    ("movies_root", &self.movies_root),
                    ("tv_root", &self.tv_root),
                ];
                for (key, other) in roots {
                    if let Some(other) = other {
                        if path_inside(tuning, other) {
                            problems.push(problem(
                                "tuning_root",
                                format!(
                                    "tuning_root {tuning} is inside {key} {other}: the tuning root may not be inside the staging root or a library root (spec 7)"
                                ),
                            ));
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        if self.file_phase_concurrency == 0 {
            problems.push(problem(
                "file_phase_concurrency",
                "file_phase_concurrency is 0: at least one file-phase job must be able to run (spec 6, 14)",
            ));
        }
        if version_triple(&self.makemkv_min_version).is_none() {
            problems.push(problem(
                "makemkv_min_version",
                format!(
                    "makemkv_min_version {} is not a version of the form N.N.N (spec 9.1)",
                    self.makemkv_min_version
                ),
            ));
        }
        problems
    }
}
```

```rust
impl Settings {
    /// A JSON settings text, read and checked (ruling RP22): keys absent from the text take Settings::default()'s
    /// value. Err, one sentence, only when the text cannot be read: text that is not JSON (serde_json's message),
    /// text that is not one JSON object, or a key the settings lack or whose value cannot be read into its type
    /// (`<key>: <serde's message>`, the first such key in the text's order: each key is read on its own as a Settings
    /// with only that key, so serde's message is tied to it). Ok holds the settings with validate()'s problems,
    /// possibly none: a caller that needs a valid file checks the vector, and `lazymkv-dev plan` (Task 15) prints
    /// them and plans anyway. Spec 14.
    pub fn from_json(text: &str) -> Result<(Settings, Vec<SettingsProblem>), String> {
        let value: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(text).map_err(|err| err.to_string())?;
        let serde_json::Value::Object(map) = value else {
            return Err("a settings file is one JSON object of spec 14's keys".to_string());
        };
        for (key, value) in &map {
            let mut one = serde_json::Map::new();
            one.insert(key.clone(), value.clone());
            if let Err(err) = serde_json::from_value::<Settings>(serde_json::Value::Object(one)) {
                return Err(format!("{key}: {err}"));
            }
        }
        let settings: Settings = serde_json::from_value(serde_json::Value::Object(map)).map_err(|err| err.to_string())?;
        let problems = settings.validate();
        Ok((settings, problems))
    }
}
```

```rust
impl Settings {
    /// Milliseconds as seconds for the alignment rule (`subs_tolerance_ms as f64 / 1000.0`; 300 gives 0.3). Spec 8.7.
    pub fn subs_tolerance_s(&self) -> f64 {
        f64::from(self.subs_tolerance_ms) / 1000.0

    /// subs_tolerance_s(), SAME_MIN = subs_same_min, DIFF_MAX = subs_diff_max, every other field

    /// (`Settings::default().text_rule() == text::Rule::default()`). Spec 8.7, 14, RP15.
    pub fn text_rule(&self) -> crate::subtitle::text::Rule {
        crate::subtitle::text::Rule {
            CLEAR_MAX_BYTES: self.sub_clear_max_bytes,
            TOL_S: self.subs_tolerance_s(),
            SAME_MIN: self.subs_same_min,
            DIFF_MAX: self.subs_diff_max,
            ..crate::subtitle::text::Rule::default()
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
    Pgs, VobSub, ClosedCaptions,              // subtitles

}
```

```rust
/// Attribute 1 of a stream: 6201 "Video", 6202 "Audio", 6203 "Subtitles". Spec 9.4. Def: T2. Use: T3, T6, T8, T9, T10, T11, T12.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum StreamKind { Video, Audio, Subtitles }
impl StreamKind { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; pub fn from_attr(text: &str) -> Option<StreamKind>; }

/// Attribute 22 as a bitmask (spec 9.5). Unknown bits are kept in the value and ignored by every query. Def: T2. Use: T6 (signature), T8, T9, T10, T12.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Flags(pub u32);
impl Flags {
    pub const DIRECTORS_COMMENTS: u32 = 1;
    pub const ALT_DIRECTORS_COMMENTS: u32 = 2;
    pub const VISUALLY_IMPAIRED: u32 = 4;
    pub const CORE_AUDIO: u32 = 256;
    pub const SECONDARY_AUDIO: u32 = 512;
    pub const HAS_CORE_AUDIO: u32 = 1024;
    /// The same bit as audio::labels::DERIVED (pinned by a test: `Flags::DERIVED as i64 == audio::labels::DERIVED`).
    pub const DERIVED: u32 = 2048;
    pub const FORCED: u32 = 4096;
    /// The bits 9.5 names; every other bit (16384, 32768, 65536 seen) is ignored.
    pub const KNOWN: u32 = 1 | 2 | 4 | 256 | 512 | 1024 | 2048 | 4096;
    /// `robot::int_attr(attrs, 22)` as Flags (0 for an absent or empty attribute); Err with int_attr's text when attribute 22
    /// is not a number (never seen), and Err `attribute 22 is <n>, outside the flag range 0 to 4294967295` when it is
    /// negative or above u32::MAX. Spec 9.5.
    pub fn of(attrs: &Attrs) -> Result<Flags, String>;
    /// True when `bit` is one or more known bits and every one of them is set; false when `bit` is 0 or holds any bit
    /// outside KNOWN. Spec 9.5.
    pub fn has(self, bit: u32) -> bool;
    /// Flags 1, 2 or 4 (8.6 step 1's "director's comments, alternate director's comments or visually impaired").
    pub fn commentary(self) -> bool;
    /// 4096 and 2048 together (8.7 "derived forced-only").
    pub fn derived_forced_only(self) -> bool;
    /// 4096 without 2048 (8.7 "a DVD stream flagged forced").
    pub fn forced_authored(self) -> bool;
    /// The known bits only.
    pub fn known(self) -> u32;
}

    pub language: Option<String>,

    pub codec_id: String,

    /// Attribute 14.
    pub channels: Option<u32>,
    /// Attributes 17 and 18.
    pub sample_rate: Option<u32>,
    pub sample_size: Option<u32>,
    /// Attribute 19 "WxH" as (width, height).
    pub video_size: Option<(u32, u32)>,
    /// Attribute 22 (`Flags::of`).
    pub flags: Flags,
    /// Attribute 30 ("PGS English  (forced only)", "CC->Text English ( Lossy conversion )").
    pub tree_info: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 40 ("stereo", "5.1(side)", "7.1").
    pub layout_name: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 41 (only on a converted stream: "Text") and 42 ("( Lossless conversion )", "( Lossy conversion )").
    pub output_codec: Option<String>,
    pub conversion: Option<String>,

/// Equal and not Unknown (an Unknown never matches anything). Def: T2. Use: T2, T3, T6.
pub fn same_source(a: &TitleSource, b: &TitleSource) -> bool;

    pub fn signature_set(&self) -> BTreeSet<(StreamKind, Option<String>, Family, Option<u32>)>;

    pub fn source(&self) -> TitleSource;
}

/// CINFO 1: 6209 "Blu-ray disc", 6206 "DVD disc"; a UHD is a Blu-ray disc here (the resolution tells them apart, 8.9). Def: T2. Use: T3, T5, T7, T12.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
pub enum DiscKind { BluRay, Dvd, Unknown }
impl DiscKind { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; }

/// The typed disc (spec 9.4 CINFO and the two messages of 6.1 step 4). Def: T2. Use: T3 to T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Disc {
    pub kind: DiscKind,
    /// CINFO 2 ("Pan's Labyrinth", "THE OFFICE S3D3", "Short Circuit 2").
    pub name: Option<String>,
    /// CINFO 30.
    pub tree_name: Option<String>,
    /// CINFO 32 ("PANS_LABYRINTH", "DVD_VIDEO").
    pub volume_label: Option<String>,
    /// CINFO 49 ("UHD-141056_Smile_WW").
    pub comment: Option<String>,
    /// CINFO 28.
    pub metadata_language: Option<String>,
    /// MSG:1005's last parameter ("MakeMKV v2.0.0 win(x64-release)") and the "2.0.0" inside it (`version_triple` parses it).
    pub makemkv_banner: Option<String>,
    pub makemkv_version: Option<String>,

    pub java_in_use: bool,

    pub is_dvd: bool,
    /// Every title that has a TINFO line, by number (SINFO lines of a title without one are not typed).
    pub titles: BTreeMap<u32, Title>,
    /// MSG:2003 lines in the scan (the count; 6.2 step 7 reports them on a rip).
    pub scan_read_errors: u32,
}

    /// `titles.get(&number)` with the sentence "the scan lists no title <n>" as Err. Def: T2. Use: T7, T13, T15, T16.
    pub fn title(&self, number: u32) -> Result<&Title, String>;

/// The typed disc of a parsed scan; Err only where an attribute the model needs is malformed, naming the title and the
/// stream: `title <t> stream <s>: attribute 22 (flags): <why>` (`<why>` is `Flags::of`'s text: attribute 22 not a number,
/// or outside 0 to u32::MAX) and `title <t> stream <s>: attribute 19 (video size) is '<text>', not WxH` (a non-empty
/// attribute 19 that is not WxH). A title is in `Disc.titles` only when the scan has a TINFO line for it; its streams are
/// its SINFO lines in stream order, without a stream whose attribute 1 is not Video, Audio or Subtitles. Spec 9.4, 9.5.
/// Def: T2. Use: T3 to T16.
pub fn disc(scan: &Scan) -> Result<Disc, String>;

/// Spec 14's "2-second duration match": the one copy for every new matcher (8.3, 5, 6.3 step 8, 6.2 step 7); equal to
/// reconcile::DURATION_TOLERANCE_S (pinned by a test). Def: T2. Use: T2, T3, T6, T12.
pub const DURATION_MATCH_S: u32 = 2;

/// Spec 8.3 first paragraph: two segment maps agree when equal; when either ends in "..." only the untruncated prefix is
/// compared (the prefix is the text before "...", with a trailing partial number or comma dropped), and the other map must
/// start with it. Def: T2. Use: T2, T3, T6.
pub fn segment_maps_agree(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool;

/// Spec 6.3 step 8: two scans' titles are the same title when `same_source(a.source(), b.source())`, their segment maps
/// agree (`segment_maps_agree`) and their durations are within DURATION_MATCH_S (both durations present). Def: T2. Use: phase 2
/// (the copy's scan against the disc-time scan); `remembered::match_title` and `lookup::discdb::same_title` follow the same
/// three tests over their own records.
pub fn same_scan_title(a: &Title, b: &Title) -> bool;

/// The `<di:name>` text of `BDMV/META/DL/bdmt_*.xml`: the first `<di:name>` element (a start tag with attributes, such as
/// `<di:name xml:lang="en">`, counts; a longer tag name, such as `<di:names>`, does not), its text with the five entities
/// `&amp;`, `&lt;`, `&gt;`, `&quot;`, `&apos;` and the numeric character references (`&#233;`, `&#xE9;`) decoded once
/// each (`&amp;lt;` gives `&lt;`), any other entity (`&copy;`) and a bare `&` left as written, surrounding whitespace
/// trimmed, a leading byte-order mark ignored. None when there is no such element, or it is empty (`<di:name/>` or
/// `<di:name></di:name>`), whitespace only or unclosed. Spec 6.1 step 2, 8.1. Def: T2. Use: T15.
pub fn bdmt_name(xml: &str) -> Option<String>;

/// The bdmt file names of a recording's nav tree, English first ("bdmt_eng.xml", then the others in name order), so the
/// caller reads the first. Spec 6.1 step 2. Def: T2. Use: T15.
pub fn bdmt_candidates(names: &[String]) -> Vec<String>;
```

Where this task settles what the spec and the interfaces leave open (each choice is pinned by a test below):

1. **A stream whose attribute 1 names no kind** (not `Video`, `Audio` or `Subtitles`, or absent) is left out of its title's `streams`; the other streams keep their scan numbers. No recorded or pinned scan has one (the evidence test checks every title's stream count against the scan). The interfaces allow `disc` to refuse only a malformed attribute 22 or 19, and `StreamKind` has three values, so leaving it out is the one choice that fits both. SINFO lines of a title that has no TINFO line are not typed either (the title does not exist in the model).
2. **Absent and empty attributes.** A text attribute that is absent or empty reads as None; a number attribute (8, 11, 14, 17, 18, 25) that is absent or not a number reads as None (`chapters` as 0). Only attribute 22 (through `int_attr`, so its error text is the parser's) and a non-empty attribute 19 that is not `WxH` refuse the scan, naming the title and the stream: `title <t> stream <s>: attribute 22 (flags): <why>` and `title <t> stream <s>: attribute 19 (video size) is '<text>', not WxH`.
3. **The disc kind** is read from CINFO 1's text exactly as MakeMKV writes it (`Blu-ray disc`, `DVD disc`; the parser keeps the text, not the code); anything else, and an absent CINFO 1, is `Unknown`. `is_dvd` is `dvd_scan`, independent of `kind`.
4. **The MakeMKV version** is the word after `MakeMKV v` in the first MSG:1005's last parameter, kept only when `version_triple` reads it (`2.0 beta` gives None); the banner is kept either way.
5. **`Flags::has`** holds when its argument is one or more known bits, all set; an argument holding an unknown bit, or 0, never holds. `Flags::of` refuses a negative or too large number with `attribute 22 is <n>, outside the flag range 0 to 4294967295`.
6. **Truncated segment maps.** A map that ends in `...` is truncated. Its known parts are the comma-separated parts before the dots, trimmed, empty parts dropped, and without the last part unless the text before the dots ends in a comma (that part may be a number MakeMKV cut). Parts are compared whole, never as text prefixes (`28` does not start `281`). Two untruncated maps agree only when their texts are equal (TheDiscDB's `SegmentMap` equals the scan's attribute 26 text for every title of the nine pinned logs). Two truncated maps agree when the shorter known prefix starts the longer.
7. **`bdmt_name`** reads the first `<di:name` start tag (`<di:name>`, or one with attributes such as `<di:name xml:lang="en">`; a longer tag name such as `<di:names>` is skipped), returns None for an empty element (`<di:name/>`, or nothing but whitespace) or an unclosed one, and decodes the five entities the interfaces name and the numeric character references (`&#` and decimal digits, or `&#x` and hexadecimal digits, then `;`, when `char::from_u32` accepts the value: `&#233;` and `&#xE9;` give `é`), each once (`&amp;lt;` gives `&lt;`), as every XML reader must, so a name such as `Caf&#233;` reaches spec 8.1's cleaning as `Café`; any other entity (`&copy;`) and a bare `&` are left as written.
8. **`bdmt_candidates`** keeps the names matching `bdmt_*.xml` ignoring ASCII case, without duplicates, `bdmt_eng.xml` (any case) first, the rest in byte order of the name.
9. **`hashed_files`** skips a line with fewer than four fields, an empty name or a size that is not a number, where the test copy panicked; it accepts CRLF line ends and a byte-order mark.
10. **The TMDb builders' synthetic IDs** (TMDb gives these; the builders need fixed values the later tasks can assert): `external_ids.imdb_id` is `tt` and the TMDb ID in seven digits (`1417` gives `tt0001417`), `tvdb_id` is 100000 plus the TMDb ID, `original_name` of a show is its `name`, and `search_json` wraps the results as TMDb does (`page` 1, `total_pages` 1, `total_results` the count); a result whose `media_type` is not `movie` is written in the TV form (`name`, `original_name`, `first_air_date`). The shapes are TMDb's documented ones (`/movie/{id}`, `/tv/{id}` with `/tv/{id}/season/{n}` merged, `/search/multi`); phase 2's client verifies them live.
11. **Settings.** No code of this task reads a setting (spec 14's 2 s duration match is the fixed constant `DURATION_MATCH_S`), so no setting test is due here.

```rust
//! The typed disc model of spec 9.4 ("Output parsing": the attribute ids and value formats) and 9.5 ("Stream flags"):
//! `disc` turns a parsed robot-mode scan (`robot::Scan`) into a `Disc` of typed `Title`s and `Stream`s, with the
//! MakeMKV version banner (MSG:1005) and the Java runtime message (MSG:3344) that spec 6.1 step 4 records. It also holds
//! the title matching that spec 5 ("titles are matched by source file, segment map and duration within 2 s"), 6.3 step 8
//! and 8.3's first paragraph share (`TitleSource`, `title_source`, `same_source`, `segment_maps_agree`,
//! `DURATION_MATCH_S`, `same_scan_title`), and the disc-name reader of spec 6.1 step 2 over the text of
//! `BDMV/META/DL/bdmt_*.xml` (`bdmt_name`, `bdmt_candidates`). No I/O: callers hand in the parsed scan and the XML text.
//! Used by Tasks 3 to 16 of the phase 1 plan.

use crate::robot::{int_attr, Attrs};

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Attributes from (id, value) pairs, as the parser stores them.
    fn attrs(pairs: &[(u32, &str)]) -> Attrs {
        pairs.iter().map(|&(id, value)| (id, value.to_string())).collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn flags_name_the_bits_of_spec_9_5() {
        assert_eq!(
            [
                Flags::DIRECTORS_COMMENTS,
                Flags::ALT_DIRECTORS_COMMENTS,
                Flags::VISUALLY_IMPAIRED,
                Flags::CORE_AUDIO,
                Flags::SECONDARY_AUDIO,
                Flags::HAS_CORE_AUDIO,
                Flags::DERIVED,
                Flags::FORCED,
            ],
            [1, 2, 4, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096]
        );
        assert_eq!(Flags::KNOWN, 7943);
        assert_eq!(Flags::default(), Flags(0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_derived_bit_is_the_audio_labels_derived_bit() {
        assert_eq!(Flags::DERIVED as i64, crate::audio::labels::DERIVED);
    }

    #[test]
    fn flags_of_reads_attribute_22_and_is_zero_when_it_is_absent_or_empty() {
        assert_eq!(Flags::of(&attrs(&[(22, "2304")])), Ok(Flags(2304)));
        assert_eq!(Flags::of(&attrs(&[(22, "65536")])), Ok(Flags(65536)));
        assert_eq!(Flags::of(&attrs(&[(22, "4294967295")])), Ok(Flags(u32::MAX)));
        assert_eq!(Flags::of(&attrs(&[(22, "")])), Ok(Flags(0)));
        assert_eq!(Flags::of(&attrs(&[(1, "Audio")])), Ok(Flags(0)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn flags_of_refuses_text_and_numbers_outside_the_u32_range() {
        assert_eq!(
            Flags::of(&attrs(&[(22, "x")])),
            Err("invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'x'".to_string())
        );
        assert_eq!(
            Flags::of(&attrs(&[(22, "-1")])),
            Err("attribute 22 is -1, outside the flag range 0 to 4294967295".to_string())
        );
        assert_eq!(
            Flags::of(&attrs(&[(22, "4294967296")])),
            Err("attribute 22 is 4294967296, outside the flag range 0 to 4294967295".to_string())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn unknown_bits_are_kept_in_the_value_and_ignored_by_every_query() {
        let unknown = Flags(65536);
        assert_eq!(unknown.0, 65536);
        assert_eq!(unknown.known(), 0);
        assert!(!unknown.has(65536));
        assert!(!unknown.commentary());
        assert!(!unknown.derived_forced_only());
        assert!(!unknown.forced_authored());
        let mixed = Flags(16384 | 32768 | 65536 | 4096);
        assert_eq!(mixed.known(), 4096);
        assert!(mixed.has(Flags::FORCED));
        assert!(mixed.forced_authored());
        assert!(!mixed.has(Flags::FORCED | 65536));
    }

    #[test]
    fn has_needs_every_known_bit_of_its_argument_and_never_holds_for_zero() {
        assert!(Flags(6144).has(Flags::FORCED | Flags::DERIVED));
        assert!(Flags(6144).has(Flags::FORCED));
        assert!(!Flags(4096).has(Flags::FORCED | Flags::DERIVED));
        assert!(!Flags(6144).has(0));
        assert!(!Flags(0).has(0));
        assert!(Flags(2304).has(Flags::CORE_AUDIO) && Flags(2304).has(Flags::DERIVED));
        assert!(Flags(1024).has(Flags::HAS_CORE_AUDIO) && !Flags(1024).has(Flags::DERIVED));
        assert!(Flags(512).has(Flags::SECONDARY_AUDIO));
    }

    #[test]
    fn commentary_holds_for_flags_1_2_and_4_only() {
        for bits in [1, 2, 4, 1 | 4, 1 | 2304] {
            assert!(Flags(bits).commentary(), "{bits}");
        }
        for bits in [0, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 2304, 4096, 6144, 65536] {
            assert!(!Flags(bits).commentary(), "{bits}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn derived_forced_only_is_4096_with_2048_and_forced_authored_is_4096_without_it() {
        assert!(Flags(6144).derived_forced_only() && !Flags(6144).forced_authored());
        assert!(Flags(4096).forced_authored() && !Flags(4096).derived_forced_only());
        assert!(!Flags(2048).derived_forced_only() && !Flags(2048).forced_authored());
        assert!(!Flags(0).derived_forced_only() && !Flags(0).forced_authored());
    }

    #[test]
    fn flags_serialise_as_the_plain_number() {
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&Flags(6144)).unwrap(), "6144");
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<Flags>("65536").unwrap(), Flags(65536));
    }

    #[test]
    fn stream_kinds_read_attribute_1_as_makemkv_spells_it() {
        assert_eq!(StreamKind::from_attr("Video"), Some(StreamKind::Video));
        assert_eq!(StreamKind::from_attr("Audio"), Some(StreamKind::Audio));
        assert_eq!(StreamKind::from_attr("Subtitles"), Some(StreamKind::Subtitles));
        for other in ["video", "Subtitle", "", "Data"] {
            assert_eq!(StreamKind::from_attr(other), None, "{other:?}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn stream_kinds_spell_as_serde_does() {
        let kinds = [StreamKind::Video, StreamKind::Audio, StreamKind::Subtitles];
        assert_eq!(kinds.map(StreamKind::as_str), ["video", "audio", "subtitles"]);
        for kind in kinds {
            assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&kind).unwrap(), format!("\"{}\"", kind.as_str()));
            assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<StreamKind>(&format!("\"{}\"", kind.as_str())).unwrap(), kind);
        }
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement `StreamKind` and `Flags`**

In `crates/core/src/disc.rs`, insert this code on its own lines between the line `use crate::robot::{int_attr, Attrs};` and the line `#[cfg(test)]`:

```rust
/// Attribute 1 of a stream: 6201 "Video", 6202 "Audio", 6203 "Subtitles". Spec 9.4.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum StreamKind {
    Video,
    Audio,
    Subtitles,
}

impl StreamKind {
    /// "video", "audio" or "subtitles": the serde spelling. Spec 9.4.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            StreamKind::Video => "video",
            StreamKind::Audio => "audio",
            StreamKind::Subtitles => "subtitles",
        }
    }

    /// The kind attribute 1's text names, spelt as MakeMKV writes it ("Video", "Audio", "Subtitles"); None for any other
    /// text. Spec 9.4.
    pub fn from_attr(text: &str) -> Option<StreamKind> {
        match text {
            "Video" => Some(StreamKind::Video),
            "Audio" => Some(StreamKind::Audio),
            "Subtitles" => Some(StreamKind::Subtitles),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// Attribute 22 as a bitmask (spec 9.5). Unknown bits are kept in the value and ignored by every query.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Flags(pub u32);

impl Flags {
    /// Spec 9.5: director's comments.
    pub const DIRECTORS_COMMENTS: u32 = 1;
    /// Spec 9.5: alternate director's comments.
    pub const ALT_DIRECTORS_COMMENTS: u32 = 2;
    /// Spec 9.5: visually impaired.
    pub const VISUALLY_IMPAIRED: u32 = 4;
    /// Spec 9.5: core audio.
    pub const CORE_AUDIO: u32 = 256;
    /// Spec 9.5: secondary audio.
    pub const SECONDARY_AUDIO: u32 = 512;
    /// Spec 9.5: has core audio.
    pub const HAS_CORE_AUDIO: u32 = 1024;
    /// Spec 9.5: derived stream. The same bit as audio::labels::DERIVED (pinned by a test: `Flags::DERIVED as i64 ==
    /// audio::labels::DERIVED`).
    pub const DERIVED: u32 = 2048;
    /// Spec 9.5: forced subtitles.
    pub const FORCED: u32 = 4096;
    /// The bits 9.5 names; every other bit (16384, 32768, 65536 seen) is ignored.
    pub const KNOWN: u32 = 1 | 2 | 4 | 256 | 512 | 1024 | 2048 | 4096;

    /// `robot::int_attr(attrs, 22)` as Flags (0 for an absent or empty attribute); Err with int_attr's text when attribute 22
    /// is not a number (never seen), and Err `attribute 22 is <n>, outside the flag range 0 to 4294967295` when it is
    /// negative or above u32::MAX. Spec 9.5.
    pub fn of(attrs: &Attrs) -> Result<Flags, String> {
        let value = int_attr(attrs, 22)?;
        u32::try_from(value)
            .map(Flags)
            .map_err(|_| format!("attribute 22 is {value}, outside the flag range 0 to {}", u32::MAX))
    }

    /// True when `bit` is one or more known bits and every one of them is set; an argument holding a bit outside KNOWN
    /// never holds, and neither does 0. Spec 9.5.
    pub fn has(self, bit: u32) -> bool {
        bit != 0 && bit & !Flags::KNOWN == 0 && self.0 & bit == bit
    }

    /// Flags 1, 2 or 4 (8.6 step 1's "director's comments, alternate director's comments or visually impaired"). Spec 9.5.
    pub fn commentary(self) -> bool {
        self.0 & (Flags::DIRECTORS_COMMENTS | Flags::ALT_DIRECTORS_COMMENTS | Flags::VISUALLY_IMPAIRED) != 0
    }

    /// 4096 and 2048 together (8.7 "derived forced-only"). Spec 9.5.
    pub fn derived_forced_only(self) -> bool {
        self.has(Flags::FORCED | Flags::DERIVED)
    }

    /// 4096 without 2048 (8.7 "a DVD stream flagged forced"). Spec 9.5.
    pub fn forced_authored(self) -> bool {
        self.has(Flags::FORCED) && !self.has(Flags::DERIVED)
    }

    /// The known bits only. Spec 9.5.
    pub fn known(self) -> u32 {
        self.0 & Flags::KNOWN
    }
}

```

- [ ] **Step 8: Implement the title source, `DURATION_MATCH_S` and `segment_maps_agree`**

In `crates/core/src/disc.rs`, insert this code on its own lines immediately before the line `#[cfg(test)]`:

```rust
/// How the matching rules know a title (spec 5, 6.2 step 6, 6.3 step 8, 8.3): its source file (attribute 16) on a Blu-ray,
/// else its DVD title number (attribute 24 parsed as a number: "01" and "1" are equal; TheDiscDB writes the same number in
/// its `source_file` on a DVD), else Unknown.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "by")]
pub enum TitleSource {
    /// Attribute 16 as the scan wrote it ("00800.mpls", "00007.m2ts").
    File { name: String },
    /// Attribute 24 as a number.
    DvdTitle { number: u32 },
    /// Neither: such a title matches nothing.
    Unknown,
}

/// `source_file` when Some and not empty, else `dvd_title` parsed as a number (surrounding whitespace ignored), else
/// Unknown. Spec 5, 6.2 step 6.
pub fn title_source(source_file: Option<&str>, dvd_title: Option<&str>) -> TitleSource {
    match source_file {
        Some(name) if !name.is_empty() => TitleSource::File { name: name.to_string() },
        _ => match dvd_title.and_then(|text| text.trim().parse::<u32>().ok()) {
            Some(number) => TitleSource::DvdTitle { number },
            None => TitleSource::Unknown,
        },
    }
}

/// Equal and not Unknown (an Unknown never matches anything). Spec 5, 8.3.
pub fn same_source(a: &TitleSource, b: &TitleSource) -> bool {
    *a != TitleSource::Unknown && a == b
}

/// Spec 14's "2-second duration match": the one copy for every new matcher (8.3, 5, 6.3 step 8, 6.2 step 7); equal to
/// reconcile::DURATION_TOLERANCE_S (pinned by a test).
pub const DURATION_MATCH_S: u32 = 2;

/// Spec 8.3 first paragraph: two segment maps agree when equal; when either ends in "..." only the untruncated prefix is
/// compared (the prefix is the text before "...", with a trailing partial number or comma dropped), and the other map must
/// start with it. Parts are compared whole; of two truncated maps, the shorter known prefix must start the longer.
pub fn segment_maps_agree(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool {
    let (a_parts, a_truncated) = known_parts(a);
    let (b_parts, b_truncated) = known_parts(b);
    match (a_truncated, b_truncated) {
        (false, false) => a == b,
        (true, false) => b_parts.starts_with(&a_parts),
        (false, true) => a_parts.starts_with(&b_parts),
        (true, true) => {
            if a_parts.len() <= b_parts.len() {
                b_parts.starts_with(&a_parts)
            } else {
                a_parts.starts_with(&b_parts)
            }
        }
    }
}

/// A segment map's parts that are known whole, and whether the map was truncated: for a map ending in "...", the parts
/// before the dots without the last one unless the text before the dots ends in a comma (that last part may be a number
/// MakeMKV cut). Spec 8.3.
fn known_parts(map: &str) -> (Vec<&str>, bool) {
    match map.strip_suffix("...") {
        None => (clip_parts(map), false),
        Some(body) => {
            let mut parts = clip_parts(body);
            if !body.trim_end().ends_with(',') {
                parts.pop();
            }
            (parts, true)
        }
    }
}

/// The comma-separated parts of a segment map, trimmed, empty parts dropped.
fn clip_parts(text: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
    text.split(',').map(str::trim).filter(|part| !part.is_empty()).collect()
}
```

and replace it with:

```rust
/// The AACS disc ID: the SHA-1 of the bytes of `AACS/Unit_Key_RO.inf`, as uppercase hex.
pub fn aacs_disc_id(unit_key_ro: &[u8]) -> String {
    hex_upper(Sha1::digest(unit_key_ro).as_slice())
}

/// The files of a TheDiscDB scan log's `HSH:index,name,time,size` lines, in log order: a name ending in `.m2ts` (any
/// case) under `BDMV/STREAM`, any other under `VIDEO_TS`, so `content_hash` of them is the log's fingerprint. A line
/// with fewer than four fields, an empty name or a size that is not a number is skipped; CRLF line ends and a leading
/// byte-order mark are accepted. Spec 5.
pub fn hashed_files(log: &str) -> Vec<DiscFile> {
    log.lines()
        .filter_map(|line| line.trim_start_matches('\u{feff}').strip_prefix("HSH:"))
        .filter_map(|rest| {
            let fields: Vec<&str> = rest.split(',').collect();
            if fields.len() < 4 {
                return None;
            }
            let name = fields[1].trim();
            if name.is_empty() {
                return None;
            }
            let size: u64 = fields[fields.len() - 1].trim().parse().ok()?;
            let folder = if name.to_ascii_lowercase().ends_with(".m2ts") { "BDMV/STREAM" } else { "VIDEO_TS" };
            Some(DiscFile { path: format!("{folder}/{name}"), size })
        })
        .collect()
}
```

```rust
/// `HSH:index,name,time,size` lines list every file TheDiscDB hashed.
fn hashed_files(log: &str) -> Vec<DiscFile> {
    log.lines()
        .filter(|line| line.starts_with("HSH:"))
        .map(|line| {
            let fields: Vec<&str> = line.split(',').collect();
            let name = fields[1];
            let size: u64 = fields[fields.len() - 1].trim().parse().unwrap();
            let folder = if name.to_ascii_lowercase().ends_with(".m2ts") {
                "BDMV/STREAM"
            } else {
                "VIDEO_TS"
            };
            DiscFile { path: format!("{folder}/{name}"), size }
        })
        .collect()
}
```

```rust
/// A robot-mode value in quotes, with `"` and `\` backslash-escaped, as spec 9.4 says MakeMKV writes them.
fn robot_quoted(value: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(value.len() + 2);
    out.push('"');
    for c in value.chars() {
        if c == '"' || c == '\\' {
            out.push('\\');
        }
        out.push(c);
    }
    out.push('"');
    out
}

/// A robot log from a compact description: the CINFO lines, then per title (number, attrs) its TINFO lines and per stream
/// (number, attrs) its SINFO lines; `attrs` are (attribute id, value) pairs written as `CINFO:id,0,"value"`,
/// `TINFO:title,id,0,"value"` and `SINFO:title,stream,id,0,"value"`, in the order given, each line ending in "\n". A
/// title with no attrs writes no TINFO line (its SINFO lines are still written). Tests of Tasks 3 to 16 build scans with
/// it instead of long literals. Spec 9.4.
pub fn scan_text(disc: &[(u32, &str)], titles: &[(u32, &[(u32, &str)], &[(u32, &[(u32, &str)])])]) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    for (id, value) in disc {
        out.push_str(&format!("CINFO:{},0,{}\n", id, robot_quoted(value)));
    }
    for (title, attrs, streams) in titles {
        for (id, value) in attrs.iter() {
            out.push_str(&format!("TINFO:{},{},0,{}\n", title, id, robot_quoted(value)));
        }
        for (stream, stream_attrs) in streams.iter() {
            for (id, value) in stream_attrs.iter() {
                out.push_str(&format!("SINFO:{},{},{},0,{}\n", title, stream, id, robot_quoted(value)));
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

/// The same text with the MSG:1005 banner for version `version` (`MakeMKV v<version> win(x64-release)`) and, when `java`
/// is true, an MSG:3344 line naming `C:\Program Files\Java\bin\java.exe`, both before the CINFO lines as in the recorded
/// scans. Spec 9.4, 6.1 step 4.
pub fn scan_text_with_messages(
    version: &str,
    java: bool,
    disc: &[(u32, &str)],
    titles: &[(u32, &[(u32, &str)], &[(u32, &[(u32, &str)])])],
) -> String {
    let banner = format!("MakeMKV v{version} win(x64-release)");
    let mut out = format!(
        "MSG:1005,0,1,{},\"%1 started\",{}\n",
        robot_quoted(&format!("{banner} started")),
        robot_quoted(&banner)
    );
    if java {
        let java_path = r"C:\Program Files\Java\bin\java.exe";
        out.push_str(&format!(
            "MSG:3344,0,1,{},\"Using Java runtime from %1\",{}\n",
            robot_quoted(&format!("Using Java runtime from {java_path}")),
            robot_quoted(java_path)
        ));
    }
    out.push_str(&scan_text(disc, titles));
    out
}

/// A `/movie/{id}` answer as TMDb documents it: id, title, original_title, release_date, original_language, runtime
/// (None writes null), external_ids {imdb_id}. The IMDb ID is synthetic: `tt` and the TMDb ID in seven digits. Spec 8.1.
pub fn tmdb_movie_json(
    id: i64,
    title: &str,
    original_title: &str,
    release_date: &str,
    original_language: &str,
    runtime: Option<u32>,
) -> String {
    serde_json::json!({
        "id": id,
        "title": title,
        "original_title": original_title,
        "release_date": release_date,
        "original_language": original_language,
        "runtime": runtime,
        "external_ids": {"imdb_id": format!("tt{id:07}")},
    })
    .to_string()
}

/// A `/tv/{id}` answer with its seasons expanded as `/tv/{id}/season/{n}` gives them: id, name, original_name (the name
/// again), first_air_date, original_language, external_ids {imdb_id, tvdb_id}, seasons[] {season_number, episode_count
/// (the episodes given), episodes[] {episode_number, name, runtime}}. The IDs are synthetic: `tt` and the TMDb ID in seven
/// digits, and 100000 plus the TMDb ID. Spec 8.1, 8.5.
pub fn tmdb_tv_json(
    id: i64,
    name: &str,
    first_air_date: &str,
    original_language: &str,
    seasons: &[(u32, &[(u32, &str, Option<u32>)])],
) -> String {
    let seasons: Vec<serde_json::Value> = seasons
        .iter()
        .map(|(season_number, episodes)| {
            let episodes: Vec<serde_json::Value> = episodes
                .iter()
                .map(|(episode_number, episode_name, runtime)| {
                    serde_json::json!({"episode_number": episode_number, "name": episode_name, "runtime": runtime})
                })
                .collect();
            serde_json::json!({"season_number": season_number, "episode_count": episodes.len(), "episodes": episodes})
        })
        .collect();
    serde_json::json!({
        "id": id,
        "name": name,
        "original_name": name,
        "first_air_date": first_air_date,
        "original_language": original_language,
        "external_ids": {"imdb_id": format!("tt{id:07}"), "tvdb_id": id + 100_000},
        "seasons": seasons,
    })
    .to_string()
}

/// A `/search/multi` answer: results[] {media_type, id, title|name, original_title|original_name,
/// release_date|first_air_date} from (media_type, id, title, original title, date), the movie fields for "movie" and the
/// TV fields for any other media type, wrapped as TMDb pages it (page 1, total_pages 1, total_results). Spec 8.1.
pub fn search_json(results: &[(&str, i64, &str, &str, &str)]) -> String {
    let rows: Vec<serde_json::Value> = results
        .iter()
        .map(|&(media_type, id, title, original, date)| {
            if media_type == "movie" {
                serde_json::json!({"media_type": media_type, "id": id, "title": title, "original_title": original, "release_date": date})
            } else {
                serde_json::json!({"media_type": media_type, "id": id, "name": title, "original_name": original, "first_air_date": date})
            }
        })
        .collect();
    serde_json::json!({"page": 1, "results": rows, "total_pages": 1, "total_results": results.len()}).to_string()
}
```

```rust
    fn a_malformed_flag_or_video_size_refuses_the_scan_naming_the_title_and_stream() {
        let with = |stream: &[(u32, &str)]| parse(&scan_text(&[], &[(2, &[(9, "0:01:00")], &[(3, stream)])]));
        assert_eq!(
            disc(&with(&[(1, "Audio"), (22, "lots")])),
            Err("title 2 stream 3: attribute 22 (flags): invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'lots'".to_string())
        );
        assert_eq!(
            disc(&with(&[(1, "Audio"), (22, "-4")])),
            Err("title 2 stream 3: attribute 22 (flags): attribute 22 is -4, outside the flag range 0 to 4294967295"
                .to_string())
        );
        assert_eq!(
            disc(&with(&[(1, "Video"), (19, "1920 by 1080")])),
            Err("title 2 stream 3: attribute 19 (video size) is '1920 by 1080', not WxH".to_string())
        );
        assert_eq!(
            disc(&with(&[(1, "Video"), (19, "1920x")])),
            Err("title 2 stream 3: attribute 19 (video size) is '1920x', not WxH".to_string())
        );
        let empty_size = disc(&with(&[(1, "Video"), (19, "")])).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(empty_size.title(2).unwrap().streams[0].video_size, None);
        // A stream left out for its attribute 1 is not read further.
        assert!(disc(&with(&[(1, "Data"), (22, "lots")])).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_disc_kind_is_read_from_cinfo_1_and_spelt_as_serde_does() {
        let kind_of = |cinfo: &[(u32, &str)]| disc(&parse(&scan_text(cinfo, &[]))).unwrap().kind;
        assert_eq!(kind_of(&[(1, "Blu-ray disc")]), DiscKind::BluRay);
        assert_eq!(kind_of(&[(1, "DVD disc")]), DiscKind::Dvd);
        assert_eq!(kind_of(&[(1, "HD-DVD disc")]), DiscKind::Unknown);
        assert_eq!(kind_of(&[(2, "No kind")]), DiscKind::Unknown);
        for (kind, spelt) in [(DiscKind::BluRay, "blu-ray"), (DiscKind::Dvd, "dvd"), (DiscKind::Unknown, "unknown")] {
            assert_eq!(kind.as_str(), spelt);
            assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&kind).unwrap(), format!("\"{spelt}\""));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_dvd_is_detected_as_dvd_scan_detects_it_even_without_cinfo() {
        let dvd_video = scan_text(&[], &[(0, &[(9, "1:38:24"), (24, "01")], &[(0, &[(1, "Video"), (5, "V_MPEG2")])])]);
        let typed = disc(&parse(&dvd_video)).unwrap();
        assert!(typed.is_dvd);
        assert_eq!(typed.kind, DiscKind::Unknown);
        let with_playlist = scan_text(
            &[(1, "DVD disc")],
            &[(0, &[(9, "1:38:24"), (16, "00001.mpls")], &[(0, &[(1, "Video"), (5, "V_MPEG2")])])],
        );
        assert!(!disc(&parse(&with_playlist)).unwrap().is_dvd);
        let blu_ray =
            scan_text(&[(1, "Blu-ray disc")], &[(0, &[(9, "1:38:24")], &[(0, &[(1, "Video"), (5, "V_MPEG4/ISO/AVC")])])]);
        assert!(!disc(&parse(&blu_ray)).unwrap().is_dvd);
        assert!(disc(&parse(&scan_text(&[(1, "DVD disc")], &[]))).unwrap().is_dvd);
    }

    #[test]
    fn disc_title_names_a_title_the_scan_lacks() {
        let typed = disc(&parse(&full_scan())).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(typed.title(7), Err("the scan lists no title 7".to_string()));
        assert!(typed.title(0).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_title_gives_its_streams_of_a_kind_its_video_height_and_its_minutes() {
        let typed = disc(&parse(&full_scan())).unwrap();
        let title = typed.title(0).unwrap();
        let numbers = |kind| title.streams_of(kind).iter().map(|stream| stream.number).collect::<Vec<u32>>();
        assert_eq!(numbers(StreamKind::Video), [0]);
        assert_eq!(numbers(StreamKind::Audio), [1, 2]);
        assert_eq!(numbers(StreamKind::Subtitles), [4]);
        assert_eq!(title.video_height(), Some(2160));
        assert_eq!(title.minutes(), Some(7150.0 / 60.0));
        let text = scan_text(&[], &[(0, &[(8, "1")], &[(0, &[(1, "Video")]), (1, &[(1, "Video"), (19, "1920x1080")])])]);
        let bare = disc(&parse(&text)).unwrap();
        let untimed = bare.title(0).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(untimed.minutes(), None);
        // The first video stream has no attribute 19; a later one's size does not stand in for it.
        assert_eq!(untimed.video_height(), None);
        assert!(untimed.streams_of(StreamKind::Audio).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_signature_set_holds_each_audio_and_subtitle_stream_once_by_kind_language_codec_and_channels() {
        let typed = disc(&parse(&full_scan())).unwrap();
        let expected: BTreeSet<(StreamKind, Option<String>, Family, Option<u32>)> = [
            (StreamKind::Audio, Some("spa".to_string()), Family::DtsHdMa, Some(6)),
            (StreamKind::Audio, Some("spa".to_string()), Family::Dts, Some(6)),
            (StreamKind::Subtitles, Some("eng".to_string()), Family::Pgs, None),
        ]
        .into_iter()
        .collect();
        assert_eq!(typed.title(0).unwrap().signature_set(), expected);
        let twins = scan_text(
            &[],
            &[(
                0,
                &[(9, "0:21:18")],
                &[
                    (0, &[(1, "Video"), (5, "V_MPEG4/ISO/AVC")]),
                    (1, &[(1, "Audio"), (3, "eng"), (5, "A_AC3"), (6, "DD"), (7, "Dolby Digital"), (14, "2")]),
                    (2, &[(1, "Audio"), (3, "eng"), (5, "A_AC3"), (6, "DD"), (7, "Dolby Digital"), (14, "2")]),
                ],
            )],
        );
        let both = disc(&parse(&twins)).unwrap();
        let set: Vec<(StreamKind, Option<String>, Family, Option<u32>)> =
            both.title(0).unwrap().signature_set().into_iter().collect();
        assert_eq!(set, [(StreamKind::Audio, Some("eng".to_string()), Family::Ac3, Some(2))]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_truncated_segment_map_is_marked_and_its_whole_numbers_kept() {
        let text = scan_text(
            &[],
            &[(0, &[(9, "0:05:40"), (26, "27,28,29,3...")], &[]), (1, &[(9, "1:41:13"), (26, "1-3,7")], &[])],
        );
        let typed = disc(&parse(&text)).unwrap();
        let cut = typed.title(0).unwrap();
        assert_eq!((cut.segment_map.as_str(), cut.truncated), ("27,28,29,3...", true));
        assert_eq!(cut.segments, [27, 28, 29]);
        let whole = typed.title(1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!((whole.segment_map.as_str(), whole.truncated), ("1-3,7", false));
        assert_eq!(whole.segments, [1, 2, 3, 7]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_title_is_known_by_its_source_file_or_its_dvd_title_number() {
        let typed = disc(&parse(&full_scan())).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(typed.title(0).unwrap().source(), TitleSource::File { name: "00800.mpls".to_string() });
        let dvd = disc(&parse(&scan_text(&[(1, "DVD disc")], &[(1, &[(9, "0:02:20"), (24, "03")], &[])]))).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(dvd.title(1).unwrap().source(), TitleSource::DvdTitle { number: 3 });
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_disc_round_trips_through_json_in_field_order() {
        let text = format!("{}{}", scan_text_with_messages("2.0.0", true, &[], &[]), full_scan());
        let typed = disc(&parse(&text)).unwrap();
        let json = serde_json::to_string(&typed).unwrap();
        assert!(
            json.starts_with(concat!(
                r#"{"kind":"blu-ray","name":"Pan's Labyrinth","tree_name":"Pan's Labyrinth","#,
                r#""volume_label":"PANS_LABYRINTH","comment":"Retail","metadata_language":"eng","#,
                r#""makemkv_banner":"MakeMKV v2.0.0 win(x64-release)","makemkv_version":"2.0.0","#,
                r#""java_in_use":true,"is_dvd":false,"titles":{"0":{"number":0,"name":"Pan's Labyrinth","#,
            )),
            "{json}"
        );
        assert!(json.ends_with(r#""scan_read_errors":0}"#), "{json}");
        let back: Disc = serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(back, typed);
    }
```

```rust
const JOHN_WICK_BLU_RAY: &str = "movie/John Wick (2014)/4k-ultra-hd--blu-ray/disc02.txt";

fn corpus() -> PathBuf {
    Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../corpus/thediscdb")
}

/// The pinned log at `log` (a path below corpus/thediscdb), parsed.
fn pinned_scan(log: &str) -> Scan {
    let path = corpus().join(log);
    let bytes = fs::read(&path).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{}: {}", path.display(), error));
    let text = decode_text(&bytes, Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Replace).unwrap();
    parse(&text)
}

/// The pinned log at `log`, typed.
fn pinned(log: &str) -> Disc {
    let scan = pinned_scan(log);
    disc(&scan).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{log}: {error}"))
}

/// What the disc model gives for one pinned log. `streams` is (video, audio, subtitles); the flag columns count the
/// streams of every title for which the query holds; `unknown_bits` counts streams with a bit outside Flags::KNOWN.

    log: &'static str,
    kind: DiscKind,
    name: &'static str,
    volume_label: &'static str,

    commentary: usize,
    derived_forced_only: usize,
    forced_authored: usize,
    derived: usize,
    unknown_bits: usize,
}

#[test]
fn the_disc_model_types_every_pinned_log() {
    for want in &PINNED {
        let log = want.log;
        let scan = pinned_scan(log);
        let got = disc(&scan).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{log}: {error}"));
        assert_eq!(got.kind, want.kind, "{log}");
        assert_eq!(got.name.as_deref(), Some(want.name), "{log}");
        assert_eq!(got.tree_name.as_deref(), Some(want.name), "{log}: CINFO 30 equals CINFO 2 on every pinned log");
        assert_eq!(got.volume_label.as_deref(), Some(want.volume_label), "{log}");
        assert_eq!(got.comment.as_deref(), want.comment, "{log}");
        assert_eq!(got.metadata_language.as_deref(), want.metadata_language, "{log}");
        assert_eq!(got.makemkv_banner.as_deref(), Some(want.banner), "{log}");
        assert_eq!(got.makemkv_version.as_deref(), Some(want.version), "{log}");
        assert_eq!(got.java_in_use, want.java, "{log}");
        assert_eq!(got.is_dvd, want.is_dvd, "{log}");
        assert_eq!(got.scan_read_errors, 0, "{log}");
        assert_eq!(got.titles.len(), want.titles, "{log}");
        let seconds: u64 = got
            .titles
            .values()
            .map(|title| u64::from(title.seconds.unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{log} title {}: no duration", title.number))))
            .sum();
        assert_eq!(seconds, want.seconds, "{log}");
        let bytes: u64 = got.titles.values().filter_map(|title| title.size).sum();
        assert_eq!(bytes, want.bytes, "{log}");
        let chapters: u64 = got.titles.values().map(|title| u64::from(title.chapters)).sum();
        assert_eq!(chapters, want.chapters, "{log}");
        for title in got.titles.values() {
            let in_scan = scan.streams.keys().filter(|(number, _)| *number == title.number).count();
            assert_eq!(title.streams.len(), in_scan, "{log} title {}: every stream has a known type", title.number);
            let by_dvd_title = matches!(title.source(), TitleSource::DvdTitle { .. });
            assert_eq!(by_dvd_title, want.is_dvd, "{log} title {}", title.number);
        }
        let all: Vec<&lazymkv_core::disc::Stream> = got.titles.values().flat_map(|title| title.streams.iter()).collect();
        let count = |kind: StreamKind| all.iter().filter(|stream| stream.kind == kind).count();
        assert_eq!(
            (count(StreamKind::Video), count(StreamKind::Audio), count(StreamKind::Subtitles)),
            want.streams,
            "{log}"
        );
        let flagged = |query: fn(Flags) -> bool| all.iter().filter(|stream| query(stream.flags)).count();
        assert_eq!(flagged(Flags::commentary), want.commentary, "{log}: commentary");
        assert_eq!(flagged(Flags::derived_forced_only), want.derived_forced_only, "{log}: derived forced-only");
        assert_eq!(flagged(Flags::forced_authored), want.forced_authored, "{log}: forced");
        assert_eq!(flagged(|flags: Flags| flags.has(Flags::DERIVED)), want.derived, "{log}: derived");
        assert_eq!(flagged(|flags: Flags| flags.0 & !Flags::KNOWN != 0), want.unknown_bits, "{log}: unknown bits");
    }
}

#[test]
fn pinned_titles_carry_their_sources_comments_durations_and_segment_maps() {
    let wick = pinned(JOHN_WICK_UHD);
    let feature = wick.title(0).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(feature.source(), TitleSource::File { name: "00001.mpls".to_string() });
    assert_eq!((feature.seconds, feature.chapters, feature.size), (Some(6073), 16, Some(67_757_930_496)));
    assert_eq!((feature.segment_count, feature.segment_map.as_str(), feature.truncated), (Some(1), "1", false));
    assert_eq!(feature.segments, [1]);
    assert_eq!(feature.output_name.as_deref(), Some("title_t00.mkv"));
    assert_eq!((feature.name.as_deref(), feature.comment.as_deref()), (None, None));
    assert_eq!(feature.video_height(), Some(2160));
    let clip = wick.title(2).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(clip.source(), TitleSource::File { name: "00007.m2ts".to_string() });
    assert_eq!((clip.seconds, clip.chapters), (Some(360), 0));
    assert_eq!(pinned(JOHN_WICK_BLU_RAY).title(0).unwrap().video_height(), Some(1080));

    let knowing = pinned(KNOWING);
    let main = knowing.title(0).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(main.source(), TitleSource::DvdTitle { number: 1 });
    assert_eq!((main.source_file.as_deref(), main.dvd_title.as_deref()), (None, Some("01")));
    assert_eq!(main.comment.as_deref(), Some("B1"));
    assert_eq!((main.seconds, main.chapters, main.size), (Some(7274), 18, Some(7_098_400_768)));
    assert_eq!(main.segment_map, "1-19");
    assert_eq!(main.segments, (1..=19).collect::<Vec<i64>>());
    assert_eq!(main.output_name.as_deref(), Some("title.mkv"));
    assert_eq!(main.video_height(), Some(480));

    let smile = pinned(SMILE);
    let main_feature = smile.title(14).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(main_feature.source(), TitleSource::File { name: "00040.mpls".to_string() });
    assert_eq!(main_feature.comment.as_deref(), Some("FPL_MainFeature"));
    assert_eq!(main_feature.name.as_deref(), Some("Smile"));
    assert_eq!((main_feature.seconds, main_feature.segment_map.as_str()), (Some(6937), "294"));

    let expendables = pinned(EXPENDABLES);
    let unrated = expendables.title(41).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(unrated.source(), TitleSource::File { name: "00756.mpls".to_string() });
    assert_eq!(unrated.comment.as_deref(), Some("FPL_MainFeature_UR"));
    assert_eq!((unrated.seconds, unrated.segment_count, unrated.segments.len()), (Some(7891), Some(17), 17));
    assert_eq!(unrated.segments[0], 280);
    let rated = expendables.title(54).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(rated.source(), TitleSource::File { name: "00820.mpls".to_string() });
    assert_eq!((rated.comment.as_deref(), rated.seconds), (Some("FPL_MainFeature_R"), Some(7587)));

    let firefly = pinned(FIREFLY_2);
```
