#[test]
fn pinned_streams_carry_their_codecs_bitrates_layouts_and_flags() {
    let wick = pinned(JOHN_WICK_UHD);
    let feature = wick.title(0).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(feature.streams.iter().map(|stream| stream.number).collect::<Vec<u32>>(), (0..12).collect::<Vec<u32>>());
    assert_eq!(
        (feature.streams_of(StreamKind::Audio).len(), feature.streams_of(StreamKind::Subtitles).len()),
        (5, 6)
    );
    let video = &feature.streams[0];
    assert_eq!(
        (video.kind, video.language.clone(), video.codec.family, video.video_size, video.flags),
        (StreamKind::Video, None, Family::Hevc, Some((3840, 2160)), Flags(65536))
    );
    assert_eq!(video.codec_long, "MpegH HEVC Main10@L5.1 (dvhe.07.06 BL+FEL+RPU)");
    let atmos = &feature.streams[1];
    assert_eq!(
        (atmos.kind, atmos.name.as_deref(), atmos.language.as_deref(), atmos.codec.family),
        (StreamKind::Audio, Some("Surround 7.1"), Some("eng"), Family::TrueHd)
    );
    assert_eq!(atmos.codec_long, "TrueHD Atmos");
    assert_eq!((atmos.bitrate_text.as_deref(), atmos.bitrate_kbps), (Some("128 Kb/s"), Some(128)));
    assert_eq!((atmos.channels, atmos.sample_rate, atmos.sample_size), (Some(8), Some(48000), Some(24)));
    assert_eq!((atmos.flags, atmos.layout_name.as_deref()), (Flags(1024), Some("7.1")));
    assert_eq!((atmos.output_codec.as_deref(), atmos.conversion.as_deref()), (None, Some("( Lossless conversion )")));
    let core = &feature.streams[2];
    assert_eq!((core.codec.family, core.bitrate_kbps, core.flags), (Family::Ac3, Some(640), Flags(2304)));
    assert!(core.flags.has(Flags::DERIVED) && core.flags.has(Flags::CORE_AUDIO));
    let forced = &feature.streams[9];
    assert_eq!(
        (forced.kind, forced.language.as_deref(), forced.codec.family, forced.flags),
        (StreamKind::Subtitles, Some("eng"), Family::Pgs, Flags(6144))
    );
    assert!(forced.flags.derived_forced_only());
    assert_eq!(forced.tree_info.as_deref(), Some("PGS English  (forced only)"));

    let knowing = pinned(KNOWING);
    let main = knowing.title(0).unwrap();
    let commentary: Vec<(u32, StreamKind)> =
        main.streams.iter().filter(|stream| stream.flags.commentary()).map(|stream| (stream.number, stream.kind)).collect();
    assert_eq!(commentary, [(3, StreamKind::Audio), (6, StreamKind::Subtitles), (7, StreamKind::Subtitles)]);
    assert_eq!((main.streams[0].codec.family, main.streams[0].bitrate_kbps), (Family::Mpeg2, Some(9800)));
    assert_eq!(main.streams[3].bitrate_kbps, Some(192));
    let vobsub = &main.streams[4];
    assert_eq!((vobsub.codec.family, vobsub.codec_short.as_str(), vobsub.codec_long.as_str()), (Family::VobSub, "", "Dvd Subtitles"));
    assert_eq!((vobsub.language.as_deref(), vobsub.tree_info.as_deref()), (Some("eng"), Some(" English")));

    let firefly = pinned(FIREFLY_1);
    let pilot = firefly.title(0).unwrap();
    let forced: Vec<u32> =
        pilot.streams.iter().filter(|stream| stream.flags.forced_authored()).map(|stream| stream.number).collect();
    assert_eq!(forced, [7, 8]);
    let captions = &pilot.streams[9];
    assert_eq!(
        (captions.kind, captions.language.as_deref(), captions.codec.family),
        (StreamKind::Subtitles, Some("eng"), Family::ClosedCaptions)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        (captions.output_codec.as_deref(), captions.conversion.as_deref(), captions.bitrate_kbps),
        (Some("Text"), Some("( Lossy conversion )"), Some(9800))
    );
}

/// One stream of a title, typed (spec 9.4's attribute list).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Stream {
    /// The scan's stream number (0-based, within the title).
    pub number: u32,
    /// Attribute 1.
    pub kind: StreamKind,
    /// Attribute 2 ("Surround 5.1", "Stereo"); None when absent or empty.
    pub name: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 3 lower-cased; None when absent or empty (a video stream carries none). "und" stays "und".
    pub language: Option<String>,
    /// `codec::codec(attribute 5, 6, 7)`.
    pub codec: Codec,
    /// Attributes 5, 6, 7 as the scan wrote them ("" when absent). `codec_long` is what TheDiscDB's track `name` holds
    /// ("DTS-HD Master Audio", "TrueHD Atmos", "Dvd Subtitles"), so 8.6 step 1's alignment compares it.
    pub codec_id: String,
    pub codec_short: String,
    pub codec_long: String,
    /// Attribute 13 as text, and `codec::bitrate_kbps` of it.
    pub bitrate_text: Option<String>,
    pub bitrate_kbps: Option<u32>,
    /// Attribute 14.
    pub channels: Option<u32>,
    /// Attributes 17 and 18.
    pub sample_rate: Option<u32>,
    pub sample_size: Option<u32>,
    /// Attribute 19 "WxH" as (width, height).
    pub video_size: Option<(u32, u32)>,
    /// Attribute 22 (`Flags::of`).
    pub flags: Flags,
    /// Attribute 30 ("PGS English  (forced only)", "CC->Text English ( Lossy conversion )").
    pub tree_info: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 40 ("stereo", "5.1(side)", "7.1").
    pub layout_name: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 41 (only on a converted stream: "Text") and 42 ("( Lossless conversion )", "( Lossy conversion )").
    pub output_codec: Option<String>,
    pub conversion: Option<String>,
}

/// One title of the scan, typed. Spec 9.4.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Title {
    /// The scan's title number (sparse numbering kept).
    pub number: u32,
    /// Attribute 2.
    pub name: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 8; 0 when absent.
    pub chapters: u32,
    /// Attribute 9 through `robot::duration_seconds`; None when absent or unparsable.
    pub seconds: Option<u32>,
    /// Attribute 11, bytes.
    pub size: Option<u64>,
    /// Attribute 16 (a Blu-ray's playlist, "00800.mpls"); a DVD has none.
    pub source_file: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 24 as text ("01"), the DVD title number.
    pub dvd_title: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 25.
    pub segment_count: Option<u32>,
    /// Attribute 26 as text ("" when absent) and `audio::titles::segments` of it; `truncated` when the text ends in "...".
    pub segment_map: String,
    pub segments: Vec<i64>,
    pub truncated: bool,
    /// Attribute 27, MakeMKV's output file name.
    pub output_name: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 49 ("FPL_MainFeature_UR", "SEG FPL_02", "A1").
    pub comment: Option<String>,
    /// The streams in scan order; a stream whose attribute 1 names no kind is left out (no recorded or pinned scan has
    /// one).
    pub streams: Vec<Stream>,
}

impl Title {
    /// The streams of one kind, in scan order. Spec 9.4.
    pub fn streams_of(&self, kind: StreamKind) -> Vec<&Stream> {
        self.streams.iter().filter(|stream| stream.kind == kind).collect()
    }

    /// The height of the first video stream's attribute 19 (8.9's resolution label); None when the title has no video
    /// stream or its first one has no size.
    pub fn video_height(&self) -> Option<u32> {
        self.streams
            .iter()
            .find(|stream| stream.kind == StreamKind::Video)
            .and_then(|stream| stream.video_size)
            .map(|(_, height)| height)
    }

    /// Minutes as f64 (seconds / 60.0); None without a duration. Spec 8.3.
    pub fn minutes(&self) -> Option<f64> {
        self.seconds.map(|seconds| f64::from(seconds) / 60.0)
    }

    /// The (kind, language, codec family, channels) of every audio and subtitle stream as a set, for 8.3 rule 3.4's
    /// "superset of every other title's" test.
    pub fn signature_set(&self) -> BTreeSet<(StreamKind, Option<String>, Family, Option<u32>)> {
        self.streams
            .iter()
            .filter(|stream| stream.kind != StreamKind::Video)
            .map(|stream| (stream.kind, stream.language.clone(), stream.codec.family, stream.channels))
            .collect()
    }

    /// `title_source(source_file, dvd_title)`. Spec 5.
    pub fn source(&self) -> TitleSource {
        title_source(self.source_file.as_deref(), self.dvd_title.as_deref())
    }
}

/// CINFO 1: 6209 "Blu-ray disc", 6206 "DVD disc"; a UHD is a Blu-ray disc here (the resolution tells them apart, 8.9).
/// Spec 9.4.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
pub enum DiscKind {
    BluRay,
    Dvd,
    Unknown,
}

impl DiscKind {
    /// "blu-ray", "dvd" or "unknown": the serde spelling. Spec 9.4.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            DiscKind::BluRay => "blu-ray",
            DiscKind::Dvd => "dvd",
            DiscKind::Unknown => "unknown",
        }
    }
}

/// The typed disc (spec 9.4 CINFO and the two messages of 6.1 step 4).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Disc {
    pub kind: DiscKind,
    /// CINFO 2 ("Pan's Labyrinth", "THE OFFICE S3D3", "Short Circuit 2").
    pub name: Option<String>,
    /// CINFO 30.
    pub tree_name: Option<String>,
    /// CINFO 32 ("PANS_LABYRINTH", "DVD_VIDEO").
    pub volume_label: Option<String>,
    /// CINFO 49 ("UHD-141056_Smile_WW").
    pub comment: Option<String>,
    /// CINFO 28.
    pub metadata_language: Option<String>,
    /// MSG:1005's last parameter ("MakeMKV v2.0.0 win(x64-release)") and the "2.0.0" inside it (`version_triple` parses it).
    pub makemkv_banner: Option<String>,
    pub makemkv_version: Option<String>,
    /// MSG:3344 seen (6.1 step 4; 8.3 rule 2 trusts labels only then).
    pub java_in_use: bool,
    /// `audio::titles::dvd_scan`, which also holds when CINFO 1 is absent (a DVD log pinned without CINFO).
    pub is_dvd: bool,
    /// Every title that has a TINFO line, by number (SINFO lines of a title without one are not typed).
    pub titles: BTreeMap<u32, Title>,
    /// MSG:2003 lines in the scan (the count; 6.2 step 7 reports them on a rip).
    pub scan_read_errors: u32,
}

impl Disc {
    /// `titles.get(&number)` with the sentence "the scan lists no title <n>" as Err. Spec 9.4.
    pub fn title(&self, number: u32) -> Result<&Title, String> {
        self.titles.get(&number).ok_or_else(|| format!("the scan lists no title {number}"))
    }
}

/// The typed disc of a parsed scan; Err only where an attribute the model needs is malformed (attribute 22 not a number,
/// attribute 19 not WxH), naming the title and the stream. A title exists when the scan has a TINFO line for it; its
/// streams are its SINFO lines in stream order, without a stream whose attribute 1 names no kind. Spec 9.4, 9.5, 6.1
/// step 4.
pub fn disc(scan: &Scan) -> Result<Disc, String> {
    let mut titles = BTreeMap::new();
    for (&number, attrs) in &scan.titles {
        let mut streams = Vec::new();
        for (&(_, stream_number), stream_attrs) in scan.streams.range((number, 0)..=(number, u32::MAX)) {
            if let Some(stream) = typed_stream(number, stream_number, stream_attrs)? {
                streams.push(stream);
            }
        }
        titles.insert(number, typed_title(number, attrs, streams));
    }
    let makemkv_banner =
        scan.messages.iter().find(|message| message.code == 1005).and_then(|message| message.params.last().cloned());
    let makemkv_version = makemkv_banner.as_deref().and_then(version_in_banner);
    let read_errors = scan.messages.iter().filter(|message| message.code == 2003).count();
    Ok(Disc {
        kind: disc_kind(scan.disc.get(&1).map(String::as_str)),
        name: text_attr(&scan.disc, 2),
        tree_name: text_attr(&scan.disc, 30),
        volume_label: text_attr(&scan.disc, 32),
        comment: text_attr(&scan.disc, 49),
        metadata_language: text_attr(&scan.disc, 28),
        makemkv_banner,
        makemkv_version,
        java_in_use: scan.messages.iter().any(|message| message.code == 3344),
        is_dvd: dvd_scan(scan),
        titles,
        scan_read_errors: u32::try_from(read_errors).unwrap_or(u32::MAX),
    })
}

/// CINFO 1's text as MakeMKV writes it: "Blu-ray disc" or "DVD disc"; anything else (or nothing) is Unknown.
fn disc_kind(text: Option<&str>) -> DiscKind {
    match text {
        Some("Blu-ray disc") => DiscKind::BluRay,
        Some("DVD disc") => DiscKind::Dvd,
        _ => DiscKind::Unknown,
    }
}

/// The "N.N.N" word after "MakeMKV v" in the banner, kept only when `version_triple` reads it. Spec 9.1.
fn version_in_banner(banner: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let word = banner.strip_prefix("MakeMKV v")?.split_whitespace().next()?;
    version_triple(word).map(|_| word.to_string())
}

/// Attribute `id` as text; None when it is absent or empty.
fn text_attr(attrs: &Attrs, id: u32) -> Option<String> {
    attrs.get(&id).filter(|value| !value.is_empty()).cloned()
}

/// Attribute `id` as a number (surrounding whitespace ignored); None when it is absent, empty or not a number.
fn number_attr<T: std::str::FromStr>(attrs: &Attrs, id: u32) -> Option<T> {
    attrs.get(&id).and_then(|value| value.trim().parse().ok())
}

/// Attribute 19's "WxH" as (width, height).
fn parse_video_size(text: &str) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
    let (width, height) = text.split_once('x')?;
    Some((width.parse().ok()?, height.parse().ok()?))
}

/// One stream, typed; None when attribute 1 names no kind (the stream is then left out of its title and not read
/// further). Err for a malformed attribute 22 or a non-empty attribute 19 that is not WxH.
fn typed_stream(title: u32, number: u32, attrs: &Attrs) -> Result<Option<Stream>, String> {
    let Some(kind) = attrs.get(&1).and_then(|text| StreamKind::from_attr(text)) else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    let flags = Flags::of(attrs).map_err(|why| format!("title {title} stream {number}: attribute 22 (flags): {why}"))?;
    let video_size = match attrs.get(&19).filter(|text| !text.is_empty()) {
        None => None,
        Some(text) => Some(parse_video_size(text).ok_or_else(|| {
            format!("title {title} stream {number}: attribute 19 (video size) is '{text}', not WxH")
        })?),
    };
    let codec_id = attrs.get(&5).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    let codec_short = attrs.get(&6).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    let codec_long = attrs.get(&7).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    let bitrate_text = text_attr(attrs, 13);
    Ok(Some(Stream {
        number,
        kind,
        name: text_attr(attrs, 2),
        language: text_attr(attrs, 3).map(|code| code.to_lowercase()),
        codec: codec(&codec_id, &codec_short, &codec_long),
        codec_id,
        codec_short,
        codec_long,
        bitrate_kbps: bitrate_text.as_deref().and_then(bitrate_kbps),
        bitrate_text,
        channels: number_attr(attrs, 14),
        sample_rate: number_attr(attrs, 17),
        sample_size: number_attr(attrs, 18),
        video_size,
        flags,
        tree_info: text_attr(attrs, 30),
        layout_name: text_attr(attrs, 40),
        output_codec: text_attr(attrs, 41),
        conversion: text_attr(attrs, 42),
    }))
}

/// One title, typed, with its typed streams.
fn typed_title(number: u32, attrs: &Attrs, streams: Vec<Stream>) -> Title {
    let segment_map = attrs.get(&26).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    Title {
        number,
        name: text_attr(attrs, 2),
        chapters: number_attr(attrs, 8).unwrap_or(0),
        seconds: attrs.get(&9).and_then(|text| duration_seconds(text)),
        size: number_attr(attrs, 11),
        source_file: text_attr(attrs, 16),
        dvd_title: text_attr(attrs, 24),
        segment_count: number_attr(attrs, 25),
        segments: segments(&segment_map),
        truncated: segment_map.ends_with("..."),
        segment_map,
        output_name: text_attr(attrs, 27),
        comment: text_attr(attrs, 49),
        streams,
    }
}

/// Spec 6.3 step 8: two scans' titles are the same title when `same_source(a.source(), b.source())`, their segment maps
/// agree (`segment_maps_agree`) and their durations are within DURATION_MATCH_S (both durations present); the title
/// numbers are never compared (spec 5). Used by phase 2 for the copy's scan against the disc-time scan;
/// `remembered::match_title` and `lookup::discdb::same_title` follow the same three tests over their own records.
pub fn same_scan_title(a: &Title, b: &Title) -> bool {
    let durations_match = match (a.seconds, b.seconds) {
        (Some(x), Some(y)) => x.abs_diff(y) <= DURATION_MATCH_S,
        _ => false,
    };
    same_source(&a.source(), &b.source()) && segment_maps_agree(&a.segment_map, &b.segment_map) && durations_match
}

- [ ] **Step 30: Implement `bdmt_name` and `bdmt_candidates`**

In `crates/core/src/disc.rs`, insert this code on its own lines immediately before the line `#[cfg(test)]`:

```rust
/// The `<di:name>` text of `BDMV/META/DL/bdmt_*.xml` (the first `<di:name>` element's text, entities `&amp;`, `&lt;`, `&gt;`,
/// `&quot;`, `&apos;` decoded, surrounding whitespace trimmed, a leading byte-order mark ignored); None when the text has
/// none, when that element is empty or holds only whitespace, or when it is not closed. A start tag with attributes
/// (`<di:name xml:lang="en">`) counts; a longer tag name (`<di:names>`) does not; numeric character references
/// (`&#233;`, `&#xE9;`) are decoded too, and any other entity (`&copy;`) is left as written. Spec 6.1 step 2, 8.1.
pub fn bdmt_name(xml: &str) -> Option<String> {
    const OPEN: &str = "<di:name";
    let mut rest = xml.trim_start_matches('\u{feff}');
    let body = loop {
        let at = rest.find(OPEN)?;
        let after = &rest[at + OPEN.len()..];
        match after.chars().next() {
            Some('>') => break &after[1..],
            Some(c) if c == '/' || c.is_whitespace() => {
                let close = after.find('>')?;
                if after[..close].ends_with('/') {
                    return None;
                }
                break &after[close + 1..];
            }
            _ => rest = after,
        }
    };
    let end = body.find("</di:name>")?;
    let decoded = decode_entities(&body[..end]);
    let name = decoded.trim();
    if name.is_empty() {
        None
    } else {
        Some(name.to_string())
    }
}

/// The numeric character references and the five XML entities of `bdmt_name` decoded, each once, left to right; any
/// other `&` is kept.
fn decode_entities(text: &str) -> String {
    const ENTITIES: [(&str, char); 5] = [("&amp;", '&'), ("&lt;", '<'), ("&gt;", '>'), ("&quot;", '"'), ("&apos;", '\'')];
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
    let mut rest = text;
    while let Some(at) = rest.find('&') {
        out.push_str(&rest[..at]);
        let tail = &rest[at..];
        if let Some((character, length)) = character_reference(tail) {
            out.push(character);
            rest = &tail[length..];
            continue;
        }
        match ENTITIES.iter().find(|(entity, _)| tail.starts_with(*entity)) {
            Some((entity, character)) => {
                out.push(*character);
                rest = &tail[entity.len()..];
            }
            None => {
                out.push('&');
                rest = &tail[1..];
            }
        }
    }
    out.push_str(rest);
    out
}

/// The character a numeric character reference at the start of `tail` names (`&#` and decimal digits, or `&#x` and
/// hexadecimal digits, then `;`) and the reference's length in bytes; None when `tail` does not start with one, or when
/// `char::from_u32` refuses its value (a surrogate, above U+10FFFF, or too many digits for a u32).
fn character_reference(tail: &str) -> Option<(char, usize)> {
    let body = tail.strip_prefix("&#")?;
    let (marker, radix) = if body.starts_with('x') { (1, 16) } else { (0, 10) };
    let digits_on = &body[marker..];
    let end = digits_on.find(';')?;
    let digits = &digits_on[..end];
    if digits.is_empty() || !digits.chars().all(|c| c.is_digit(radix)) {
        return None;
    }
    let character = char::from_u32(u32::from_str_radix(digits, radix).ok()?)?;
    Some((character, "&#".len() + marker + end + 1))
}

/// The bdmt file names of a recording's nav tree, English first ("bdmt_eng.xml", then the others in name order), so the
/// caller reads the first: the names matching `bdmt_*.xml` ignoring ASCII case, without duplicates, `bdmt_eng.xml` (any
/// case) first, the rest in byte order. Spec 6.1 step 2.
pub fn bdmt_candidates(names: &[String]) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut found: Vec<String> = names
        .iter()
        .filter(|name| {
            let lower = name.to_ascii_lowercase();
            lower.starts_with("bdmt_") && lower.ends_with(".xml")
        })
        .cloned()
        .collect();
    found.sort();
    found.dedup();
    if let Some(at) = found.iter().position(|name| name.eq_ignore_ascii_case("bdmt_eng.xml")) {
        let english = found.remove(at);
        found.insert(0, english);
    }
    found
}

```

Create `crates/dev/tests/disc_model.rs` with exactly this content:

```rust
//! The typed disc model of spec 9.4 and 9.5 (`lazymkv_core::disc`, phase 1 Task 2) over every recorded `scan.txt` of
//! the evidence clone, the title matching of spec 6.3 step 8 on titles that share a segment map or a duration, and the
//! disc name of spec 6.1 step 2 from each recording's `nav/BDMV/META/DL/bdmt_*.xml`. Each recording has a test that
//! writes out only the values the public spec, docs and fixtures publish and compares every other value with the raw
//! attribute of the same scan (ruling RP21); a recording added later is listed by
//! recordings_without_a_test_are_listed_as_not_covered until it gets its test here. Without the clone, or without one
//! recording, a test prints "skipped: <reason>" and passes. The scans are never printed: their DRV lines can carry a
//! drive serial. Input: LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE, else corpus/owner under the repository root.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use lazymkv_core::audio::titles::segments;
use lazymkv_core::codec::{bitrate_kbps, Family};
use lazymkv_core::disc::{
    bdmt_candidates, bdmt_name, disc, same_scan_title, Disc, DiscKind, Flags, StreamKind, TitleSource,
};
use lazymkv_core::recording::{decode_text, Encoding, Errors};
use lazymkv_core::robot::{duration_seconds, parse, Scan};
use lazymkv_dev::evidence::skip;

/// The recordings with a test here.
const RECORDINGS: [&str; 4] =
    ["pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd", "short-circuit-1986-dvd", "short-circuit-2-1988-dvd", "the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray"];

/// The evidence clone: LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE, else corpus/owner under the repository root.
fn evidence() -> PathBuf {
    match std::env::var("LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE") {
        Ok(dir) if !dir.is_empty() => PathBuf::from(dir),
        _ => Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../corpus/owner"),
    }
}

/// The slugs of the clone's recordings that have a scan.txt (never the golden folder), sorted; None, with the skip line
/// written, when the clone is absent.
fn recorded_slugs() -> Option<Vec<String>> {
    let root = evidence();
    if !root.is_dir() {
        skip(&format!("no evidence clone at {}", root.display()));
        return None;
    }
    let mut slugs = Vec::new();
    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(&root).unwrap() {
        let dir = entry.unwrap().path();
        let name = dir.file_name().unwrap().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        if name != "golden" && dir.join("scan.txt").is_file() {
            slugs.push(name);
        }
    }
    slugs.sort();
    Some(slugs)
}

/// The parsed scan.txt of `slug`; None, with the skip line written, when the clone or the recording is absent.
fn recorded_scan(slug: &str) -> Option<Scan> {
    let path = evidence().join(slug).join("scan.txt");
    if !path.is_file() {
        skip(&format!("no {} (the evidence clone or this recording is absent)", path.display()));
        return None;
    }
    let bytes = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{}: {}", path.display(), error));
    let text = decode_text(&bytes, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Replace)
        .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{}: {}", path.display(), error));
    Some(parse(&text))
}

/// Disc attribute (CINFO) `id` of `scan` as the scan wrote it; None when absent. Ruling RP21: a value the public docs
/// do not publish is compared with the raw attribute of the same scan, never written in this file.
fn disc_attr(scan: &Scan, id: u32) -> Option<&str> {
    scan.disc.get(&id).map(String::as_str)
}

/// Title attribute `id` of `scan` as the scan wrote it; None when absent.
fn title_attr(scan: &Scan, title: u32, id: u32) -> Option<&str> {
    scan.titles.get(&title).and_then(|attrs| attrs.get(&id)).map(String::as_str)
}

/// Title attribute `id` read as a number; None when absent or not a number.
fn title_number(scan: &Scan, title: u32, id: u32) -> Option<u64> {
    title_attr(scan, title, id).and_then(|text| text.parse().ok())
}

/// Title attribute 9 through `robot::duration_seconds`; None when absent or unparsable.
fn title_seconds(scan: &Scan, title: u32) -> Option<u32> {
    title_attr(scan, title, 9).and_then(duration_seconds)
}

/// `codec::bitrate_kbps` of stream attribute 13; None when absent or unreadable.
fn stream_kbps(scan: &Scan, title: u32, stream: u32) -> Option<u32> {
    scan.streams.get(&(title, stream)).and_then(|attrs| attrs.get(&13)).and_then(|text| bitrate_kbps(text))
}

/// The typed disc of `slug`'s scan; a refusal fails the test with its sentence.
fn typed_disc(slug: &str, scan: &Scan) -> Disc {
    disc(scan).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{slug}: {error}"))
}

/// The disc name of `slug`'s nav files: the first of `bdmt_candidates` in nav/BDMV/META/DL, read through `bdmt_name`;
/// None when that folder or a bdmt file is absent (a DVD, or a Blu-ray recorded without disc metadata).
fn recorded_bdmt_name(slug: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let folder = evidence().join(slug).join("nav/BDMV/META/DL");
    let entries = std::fs::read_dir(&folder).ok()?;
    let names: Vec<String> = entries.map(|entry| entry.unwrap().file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned()).collect();
    let first = bdmt_candidates(&names).into_iter().next()?;
    let bytes = std::fs::read(folder.join(&first)).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{first}: {error}"));
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes).into_owned();
    bdmt_name(&text)
}

#[test]
fn every_recorded_scan_gives_a_typed_disc() {
    let Some(slugs) = recorded_slugs() else { return };
    if slugs.is_empty() {
        skip(&format!("no recording with a scan.txt under {}", evidence().display()));
        return;
    }
    for slug in &slugs {
        let scan = recorded_scan(slug).unwrap();
        let typed = typed_disc(slug, &scan);
        assert_eq!(typed.titles.len(), scan.titles.len(), "{slug}: titles");
        for title in typed.titles.values() {
            let in_scan = scan.streams.keys().filter(|(number, _)| *number == title.number).count();
            assert_eq!(title.streams.len(), in_scan, "{slug} title {}: every stream has a known type", title.number);
            assert!(title.seconds.is_some(), "{slug} title {}: no duration", title.number);
            let by_dvd_title = matches!(title.source(), TitleSource::DvdTitle { .. });
            assert_eq!(by_dvd_title, typed.is_dvd, "{slug} title {}: known by attribute 24 on a DVD only", title.number);
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn pans_labyrinth_2006_uhd() {
    let slug = "pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd";

    assert_eq!(forced, [5, 7]);

    let menu = pans.title(1).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(menu.source(), TitleSource::File { name: "00055.mpls".to_string() });
    assert_eq!((menu.seconds, menu.chapters, menu.segment_count), (Some(340), 34, Some(34)));
    assert_eq!(menu.segments, (27..=60).collect::<Vec<i64>>());
    assert_eq!(menu.streams.len(), 1);
    assert!(same_scan_title(feature, feature));
    assert!(!same_scan_title(feature, menu));

    assert_eq!(recorded_bdmt_name(slug).as_deref(), Some("Pan's Labyrinth"));
}

#[test]
fn short_circuit_1986_dvd() {
    let slug = "short-circuit-1986-dvd";
    let Some(scan) = recorded_scan(slug) else { return };
    let dvd = typed_disc(slug, &scan);
    assert_eq!(dvd.kind, DiscKind::Dvd);
    assert!(dvd.name.is_some() && dvd.volume_label.is_some(), "CINFO 2 and 32 are present");
    assert_eq!(
        (dvd.name.as_deref(), dvd.tree_name.as_deref(), dvd.volume_label.as_deref()),
        (disc_attr(&scan, 2), disc_attr(&scan, 30), disc_attr(&scan, 32))
    );
    assert_eq!(dvd.metadata_language.as_deref(), disc_attr(&scan, 28));
    assert_eq!((dvd.makemkv_version.as_deref(), dvd.java_in_use), (Some("2.0.0"), false));
    assert_eq!((dvd.is_dvd, dvd.scan_read_errors), (true, 0));
    assert_eq!(dvd.titles.keys().copied().collect::<Vec<u32>>(), [0]);

    let main = dvd.title(0).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(main.source(), TitleSource::DvdTitle { number: 1 });
    assert_eq!((main.source_file.as_deref(), main.dvd_title.as_deref()), (None, Some("01")));
    assert!(main.comment.is_some(), "attribute 49 is present");
    assert_eq!(main.comment.as_deref(), title_attr(&scan, 0, 49));
    assert_eq!(main.seconds, Some(5904));
    assert_eq!((Some(u64::from(main.chapters)), main.size), (title_number(&scan, 0, 8), title_number(&scan, 0, 11)));
    let map = title_attr(&scan, 0, 26).unwrap();
    assert_eq!((main.segment_map.as_str(), main.segments.clone()), (map, segments(map)));
    assert_eq!(main.video_height(), Some(480));
    let kinds: Vec<StreamKind> = main.streams.iter().map(|stream| stream.kind).collect();
    assert_eq!(kinds, [StreamKind::Video, StreamKind::Audio, StreamKind::Audio]);
    let families: Vec<(Family, Option<u32>)> =
        main.streams.iter().map(|stream| (stream.codec.family, stream.channels)).collect();
    assert_eq!(families, [(Family::Mpeg2, None), (Family::Ac3, Some(6)), (Family::Ac3, Some(2))]);
    for stream in &main.streams {
        assert!(stream.bitrate_kbps.is_some(), "stream {}: attribute 13 is read", stream.number);
        assert_eq!(stream.bitrate_kbps, stream_kbps(&scan, 0, stream.number), "stream {}: attribute 13", stream.number);
    }
    assert!(main.streams_of(StreamKind::Subtitles).is_empty());
    assert!(main.streams.iter().all(|stream| stream.flags == Flags(0)));

    assert_eq!(recorded_bdmt_name(slug), None);
}

#[test]
fn short_circuit_2_1988_dvd() {
    let slug = "short-circuit-2-1988-dvd";
    let Some(scan) = recorded_scan(slug) else { return };
    let dvd = typed_disc(slug, &scan);
    assert_eq!(dvd.kind, DiscKind::Dvd);
    assert_eq!(
        (dvd.name.as_deref(), dvd.tree_name.as_deref(), dvd.volume_label.as_deref()),
        (Some("Short Circuit 2"), Some("Short Circuit 2"), Some("DVD_VIDEO"))
    );
    assert_eq!((dvd.makemkv_version.as_deref(), dvd.java_in_use), (Some("2.0.0"), false));
    assert_eq!((dvd.is_dvd, dvd.scan_read_errors), (true, 3));
    let sources: Vec<TitleSource> = dvd.titles.values().map(|title| title.source()).collect();
    assert_eq!(sources, [1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8].map(|number| TitleSource::DvdTitle { number }));
    for title in dvd.titles.values() {
        assert_eq!(title.seconds, title_seconds(&scan, title.number), "title {}: attribute 9", title.number);
    }

    let main = dvd.title(0).unwrap();
    assert!(main.comment.is_some(), "attribute 49 is present");
    assert_eq!((main.seconds, main.chapters, main.comment.as_deref()), (Some(6606), 28, title_attr(&scan, 0, 49)));
    let map = title_attr(&scan, 0, 26).unwrap();
    assert_eq!((main.segment_map.as_str(), main.segments.clone()), (map, segments(map)));
    let captions = &main.streams[12];
    assert_eq!(
        (captions.kind, captions.language.as_deref(), captions.codec.family),
        (StreamKind::Subtitles, Some("eng"), Family::ClosedCaptions)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        (captions.output_codec.as_deref(), captions.conversion.as_deref()),
        (Some("Text"), Some("( Lossy conversion )"))
    );
    assert_eq!(captions.tree_info.as_deref(), Some("CC\u{2192}Text English ( Lossy conversion )"));
    let vobsub = &main.streams[5];
    assert_eq!(
        (vobsub.codec.family, vobsub.codec_short.as_str(), vobsub.codec_long.as_str()),
        (Family::VobSub, "", "Dvd Subtitles")
    );

    // Titles 1 to 6 share one segment map; attribute 24 still tells every title apart.
    let shared = dvd.title(1).unwrap().segment_map.clone();
    assert!(!shared.is_empty());
    assert!((1..=6).all(|number| dvd.title(number).unwrap().segment_map == shared));
    for a in dvd.titles.values() {
        for b in dvd.titles.values() {
            assert_eq!(same_scan_title(a, b), a.number == b.number, "titles {} and {}", a.number, b.number);
        }
    }

    assert_eq!(recorded_bdmt_name(slug), None);
}

#[test]
fn the_office_2005_s3d3_bluray() {
    let slug = "the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray";
    let Some(scan) = recorded_scan(slug) else { return };
    let office = typed_disc(slug, &scan);
    assert_eq!(office.kind, DiscKind::BluRay);
    assert_eq!(
        (office.name.as_deref(), office.tree_name.as_deref(), office.volume_label.as_deref()),
        (Some("THE OFFICE S3D3"), Some("THE OFFICE S3D3"), Some("THE OFFICE S3D3"))
    );
    assert_eq!(office.metadata_language, None);
    assert_eq!((office.makemkv_version.as_deref(), office.java_in_use), (Some("2.0.0"), false));
    assert_eq!((office.is_dvd, office.scan_read_errors), (false, 0));
    assert_eq!(office.titles.keys().copied().collect::<Vec<u32>>(), (0..11).collect::<Vec<u32>>());
    for title in office.titles.values() {
        assert_eq!(title.seconds, title_seconds(&scan, title.number), "title {}: attribute 9", title.number);
    }

    let episode = office.title(1).unwrap();
    // Which playlist title 1 is stays in the clone (RP21): the source is attribute 16 of the same scan.
    let playlist = title_attr(&scan, 1, 16).expect("title 1 has attribute 16");
    assert_eq!(episode.source(), TitleSource::File { name: playlist.to_string() });
    assert_eq!(
        (Some(u64::from(episode.chapters)), Some(episode.segment_map.as_str())),
        (title_number(&scan, 1, 8), title_attr(&scan, 1, 26))
    );
    assert_eq!(episode.video_height(), Some(1080));
    let audio: Vec<(u32, Family, Flags)> = episode
        .streams_of(StreamKind::Audio)
        .iter()
        .map(|stream| (stream.number, stream.codec.family, stream.flags))
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(
        audio,
        [
            (1, Family::DtsHdMa, Flags(1024)),
            (2, Family::Dts, Flags(2304)),
            (3, Family::DtsHdMa, Flags(1024)),
            (4, Family::Dts, Flags(2304)),
        ]
    );
    let (twin_a, twin_b) = (&episode.streams[1], &episode.streams[3]);
    assert_eq!(
        (&twin_a.codec, twin_a.channels, twin_a.language.as_deref(), twin_a.tree_info.as_deref()),
        (&twin_b.codec, twin_b.channels, twin_b.language.as_deref(), twin_b.tree_info.as_deref())
    );

    // Titles 1, 2 and 6 run equally long and are still three titles.
    for (a, b) in [(1, 2), (1, 6), (2, 6)] {
        let (first, second) = (office.title(a).unwrap(), office.title(b).unwrap());
        assert!(first.seconds.is_some(), "title {a}: no duration");
        assert_eq!(first.seconds, second.seconds, "titles {a} and {b}: durations");
        assert!(!same_scan_title(first, second), "titles {a} and {b}");
    }
    let clip = office.title(7).unwrap();
    let clip_file = title_attr(&scan, 7, 16).unwrap();
    assert!(clip_file.ends_with(".m2ts"), "title 7 is a clip, not a playlist: {clip_file}");
    assert_eq!((clip.source(), clip.chapters), (TitleSource::File { name: clip_file.to_string() }, 0));
    // Title 3 holds two episodes (S03E12-E13): it lasts about twice title 1, within a tenth of title 1.
    let double = office.title(3).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(Some(double.segment_map.as_str()), title_attr(&scan, 3, 26));
    let (double_seconds, single_seconds) = (double.seconds.unwrap(), episode.seconds.unwrap());
    assert!(
        double_seconds.abs_diff(2 * single_seconds) * 10 < single_seconds,
        "title 3 runs {double_seconds} s, title 1 {single_seconds} s"
    );
    let two_clips = office.title(4).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(two_clips.segments, segments(title_attr(&scan, 4, 26).unwrap()));
    assert_eq!((two_clips.segment_count, two_clips.segments.len()), (Some(2), 2));

    assert_eq!(recorded_bdmt_name(slug), None);
}

```rust
// lazymkv_core::disc (T2)
/// Attribute 1 of a stream: 6201 "Video", 6202 "Audio", 6203 "Subtitles". Spec 9.4. Def: T2. Use: T3, T6, T8, T9, T10, T11, T12.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum StreamKind { Video, Audio, Subtitles }
impl StreamKind { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; pub fn from_attr(text: &str) -> Option<StreamKind>; }

/// How the matching rules know a title (spec 5, 6.2 step 6, 6.3 step 8, 8.3): its source file (attribute 16) on a Blu-ray,
/// else its DVD title number (attribute 24 parsed as a number: "01" and "1" are equal; TheDiscDB writes the same number in
/// its `source_file` on a DVD), else Unknown. Def: T2. Use: T2, T3, T6.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "by")]
pub enum TitleSource { File { name: String }, DvdTitle { number: u32 }, Unknown }
/// `source_file` when Some and not empty, else `dvd_title` parsed as a number, else Unknown. Def: T2. Use: T3, T6.
pub fn title_source(source_file: Option<&str>, dvd_title: Option<&str>) -> TitleSource;
/// Equal and not Unknown (an Unknown never matches anything). Def: T2. Use: T2, T3, T6.
pub fn same_source(a: &TitleSource, b: &TitleSource) -> bool;

/// One title of the scan, typed. Def: T2. Use: T3 to T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Title {
    /// The scan's title number (sparse numbering kept).
    pub number: u32,
    /// Attribute 2.
    pub name: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 8; 0 when absent.
    pub chapters: u32,
    /// Attribute 9 through `robot::duration_seconds`; None when absent or unparsable.
    pub seconds: Option<u32>,
    /// Attribute 11, bytes.
    pub size: Option<u64>,
    /// Attribute 16 (a Blu-ray's playlist, "00800.mpls"); a DVD has none.
    pub source_file: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 24 as text ("01"), the DVD title number.
    pub dvd_title: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 25.
    pub segment_count: Option<u32>,
    /// Attribute 26 as text ("" when absent) and `audio::titles::segments` of it; `truncated` when the text ends in "...".
    pub segment_map: String,
    pub segments: Vec<i64>,
    pub truncated: bool,
    /// Attribute 27, MakeMKV's output file name.
    pub output_name: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 49 ("FPL_MainFeature_UR", "SEG FPL_02", "A1").
    pub comment: Option<String>,
    /// The streams in scan order.
    pub streams: Vec<Stream>,
}
impl Title {
    /// The streams of one kind, in scan order. Def: T2. Use: T5, T8, T9, T10, T11.
    pub fn streams_of(&self, kind: StreamKind) -> Vec<&Stream>;
    /// The height of the first video stream's attribute 19 (8.9's resolution label). Def: T2. Use: T11, T13.
    pub fn video_height(&self) -> Option<u32>;
    /// Minutes as f64 (seconds / 60.0); None without a duration. Def: T2. Use: T5.
    pub fn minutes(&self) -> Option<f64>;
    /// The (kind, language, codec family, channels) of every audio and subtitle stream as a set, for 8.3 rule 3.4's
    /// "superset of every other title's" test. Def: T2. Use: T5.
    pub fn signature_set(&self) -> BTreeSet<(StreamKind, Option<String>, Family, Option<u32>)>;
    /// `title_source(source_file, dvd_title)`. Def: T2. Use: T2, T3, T6.
    pub fn source(&self) -> TitleSource;
}

/// CINFO 1: 6209 "Blu-ray disc", 6206 "DVD disc"; a UHD is a Blu-ray disc here (the resolution tells them apart, 8.9). Def: T2. Use: T3, T5, T7, T12.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
pub enum DiscKind { BluRay, Dvd, Unknown }
impl DiscKind { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; }

/// The typed disc (spec 9.4 CINFO and the two messages of 6.1 step 4). Def: T2. Use: T3 to T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Disc {
    pub kind: DiscKind,
    /// CINFO 2 ("Pan's Labyrinth", "THE OFFICE S3D3", "Short Circuit 2").
    pub name: Option<String>,
    /// CINFO 30.
    pub tree_name: Option<String>,
    /// CINFO 32 ("PANS_LABYRINTH", "DVD_VIDEO").
    pub volume_label: Option<String>,
    /// CINFO 49 ("UHD-141056_Smile_WW").
    pub comment: Option<String>,
    /// CINFO 28.
    pub metadata_language: Option<String>,
    /// MSG:1005's last parameter ("MakeMKV v2.0.0 win(x64-release)") and the "2.0.0" inside it (`version_triple` parses it).
    pub makemkv_banner: Option<String>,
    pub makemkv_version: Option<String>,
    /// MSG:3344 seen (6.1 step 4; 8.3 rule 2 trusts labels only then).
    pub java_in_use: bool,
    /// `audio::titles::dvd_scan`, which also holds when CINFO 1 is absent (a DVD log pinned without CINFO).
    pub is_dvd: bool,
    /// Every title, by number.
    pub titles: BTreeMap<u32, Title>,
    /// MSG:2003 lines in the scan (the count; 6.2 step 7 reports them on a rip).
    pub scan_read_errors: u32,
}
impl Disc {
    /// `titles.get(&number)` with the sentence "the scan lists no title <n>" as Err. Def: T2. Use: T7, T13, T15, T16.
    pub fn title(&self, number: u32) -> Result<&Title, String>;
}

/// The typed disc of a parsed scan; Err only where an attribute the model needs is malformed (attribute 22 not a number,
/// attribute 19 not WxH). Spec 9.4. Def: T2. Use: T3 to T16.
pub fn disc(scan: &Scan) -> Result<Disc, String>;

/// Spec 14's "2-second duration match": the one copy for every new matcher (8.3, 5, 6.3 step 8, 6.2 step 7); equal to
/// reconcile::DURATION_TOLERANCE_S (pinned by a test). Def: T2. Use: T2, T3, T6, T12.
pub const DURATION_MATCH_S: u32 = 2;

/// Spec 8.3 first paragraph: two segment maps agree when equal; when either ends in "..." only the untruncated prefix is
/// compared (the prefix is the text before "...", with a trailing partial number or comma dropped), and the other map must
/// start with it. Def: T2. Use: T2, T3, T6.
pub fn segment_maps_agree(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool;

// lazymkv_core::testsupport (T2; unit tests only)
/// A robot log from a compact description: the CINFO lines, then per title (number, attrs) its TINFO lines and per stream
/// (number, attrs) its SINFO lines; `attrs` are (attribute id, value) pairs written as `KIND:...,id,0,"value"`. Tests of
/// Tasks 3 to 16 build scans with it instead of long literals. Def: T2. Use: T3 to T16.
pub fn scan_text(disc: &[(u32, &str)], titles: &[(u32, &[(u32, &str)], &[(u32, &[(u32, &str)])])]) -> String;
/// A `/movie/{id}` answer as TMDb documents it: id, title, original_title, release_date, original_language, runtime
/// (None writes null), external_ids {imdb_id}. Def: T2. Use: T3, T4, T5, T7, T15.
pub fn tmdb_movie_json(id: i64, title: &str, original_title: &str, release_date: &str, original_language: &str, runtime: Option<u32>) -> String;
/// A `/tv/{id}` answer with its seasons expanded as `/tv/{id}/season/{n}` gives them: name, original_name, first_air_date,
/// original_language, external_ids {imdb_id, tvdb_id}, seasons[] {season_number, episode_count, episodes[] {episode_number,
/// name, runtime}}. Def: T2. Use: T3, T4, T6, T7, T15.
pub fn tmdb_tv_json(id: i64, name: &str, first_air_date: &str, original_language: &str, seasons: &[(u32, &[(u32, &str, Option<u32>)])]) -> String;
/// A `/search/multi` answer: results[] {media_type, id, title|name, original_title|original_name, release_date|first_air_date}. Def: T2. Use: T3, T4, T7, T15.
pub fn search_json(results: &[(&str, i64, &str, &str, &str)]) -> String;

pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Scan;

On a DVD, TheDiscDB writes the DVD title number (MakeMKV's attribute 24) in `source_file` (Knowing `"01"` to `"07"`, Firefly disc 2 `"01"`, `"02"`, `"03"`, `"11"`), never attribute 16.

Also defined here, beyond the entries above, because the conventions require them of every closed set ("`FromStr` accepting only those spellings, and `pub const ALL: [Self; N]` in spec order"): `Kind::ALL: [Kind; 2]` and `impl std::str::FromStr for Kind` (error `"<text>" is not a disc kind (movie or tv)`), `TmdbKind::ALL: [TmdbKind; 2]` and `impl std::str::FromStr for TmdbKind` (error `"<text>" is not a TMDb kind (movie or tv)`), `impl std::str::FromStr for ItemType` (the seven spellings only; error `"<text>" is not a TheDiscDB item type (MainMovie, Episode, Extra, Featurette, DeletedScene, Trailer or Other)`). Private to `lookup`: `without_bom(text: &str) -> &str` and `parse_json<T: DeserializeOwned>(text: &str, shown: &str) -> Result<T, String>` in `lookup/mod.rs`, visible to `discdb` and `tmdb` as their parent's items.

Where this task settles what the spec and the interfaces leave open (each choice is pinned by a test below):

1. **The sibling test file.** The conventions give `lookup/mod.rs` a sibling `tests.rs`; this task creates `crates/core/src/lookup/tests.rs` with the two `Kind` tests and `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` in `mod.rs`, so Task 4 appends its identification tests there. `tmdb.rs` keeps its tests in `mod tests` at the bottom (about 920 lines in all, at the "about 900" limit). `discdb.rs` also keeps its tests inline although the module comes to about 1,300 lines (about 400 of code and about 900 of tests): this is a deliberate exception to the Global Constraints' sibling-`tests.rs` rule, taken so that every later "In `discdb.rs`'s test module, find" anchor stays valid, and a reviewer should not flag it. Moving it to `lookup/discdb/tests.rs` is a pure follow-up refactor.
2. **Pinned files through `parse_dischash`.** `recording::files::thediscdb_answer` (the Python's `hit_rate.lookup`, used by `hit-rate`) looks only at a lowercase `titles` key, so a pinned `discNN.json` (`Titles`) is not a hit by it. `parse_dischash` counts an object with a non-empty `Titles` array as a hit too, so Task 15's pinned-log form of `lazymkv-dev plan` reads `<dir>/discNN.json` through the same function; `thediscdb_answer` itself is unchanged. A non-empty array in a dischash file is refused with `<shown>: a dischash answer is one object, not an array` (an empty array is a miss, as `thediscdb_answer` says).
3. **Byte-order marks and errors.** Every parser drops one leading byte-order mark (the recorder's PowerShell jobs write one, as `read_json` already allows for). An error is `<shown>: <serde_json's message>`, or one of the sentences the tests pin (`the movie record <id> has no title`, `the TV record <id> has no name`, `the record has no id`, `the record has neither a title (a movie) nor a name (a TV show)`, `a season answer belongs to a TV record, not to movie <id>`).
4. **`same_title`'s order of tests.** Source first: a scan title with a non-empty attribute 16 needs TheDiscDB's `source_file` to be the same text; a scan title without one compares through `disc::title_source(None, db.source_file)` and `disc::same_source` (numbers on a DVD; a playlist name never equals a DVD title number; Unknown never matches). Then `disc::segment_maps_agree` (a database title without a segment map compares as `""`), the exact size when both sides carry one, and the duration within `disc::DURATION_MATCH_S` when both sides carry one (a side without a duration never matches, as `disc::same_scan_title` requires).
5. **`match_titles`' order.** Database titles in index order (whatever order the record lists them in), each taking the first scan title, in title-number order, that is not yet taken; a repeated database index keeps its first match.
6. **TMDb's unknown values.** A runtime of 0 minutes reads as None (TMDb writes 0 for an unknown runtime as often as null, and Review Focus 2 needs an absent runtime to fail the runtime check), for the record and for each episode; blank strings read as None; the embedded `external_ids.imdb_id` wins over the top-level `imdb_id` of `/movie/{id}`; a TVDB ID of 0 or less is None; the year is the four leading digits of the date before its first `-` (`""`, `"206-10-11"`, `"10/11/2006"` have none).
7. **The whole series' runtimes.** `episode_runtimes(None)` ("of the whole series when no season was parsed", spec 8.1) takes every season numbered 1 or more, in the record's order, and leaves out season 0, TMDb's specials, which are not episodes of the series' aired order (spec 8.5 "Episode numbers follow TMDb's aired order").
8. **Merging a season.** `merge_season` replaces the episodes of the season with that number; a season the record lacks is added and the seasons re-sorted by number; an `episode_count` of None takes the count merged; a movie record refuses the merge before the text is read.
9. **The slim `tmdb.json`.** Its new fields are read leniently (a value of another type is None, never an error), so the text rule's reader in `subtitle::text::subs_run`, which reads only `original_language` through the same struct, accepts every file it accepted before.
10. **`DiscDbTrack::channels`** matches the six layout names exactly (TheDiscDB's spelling; `"stereo"` is None); `DiscDbTrack::kind` is `StreamKind::from_attr` of `type`.
11. **The two recorded answers** ("the owner's 2 recorded answers" of spec 8.1) live in the evidence clone, which `core`'s tests may not read (Global Constraints), so `crates/dev/tests/lookup_answers.rs` tests them, skipping with its reason when the clone is absent; it also checks spec 8.1's counts ("58 of 877 audio and 30 of 2018 subtitle tracks") over the 18 API answers plus the 2 recorded ones.
12. **Synthetic TMDb answers.** No TMDb search answer and no full TMDb record is recorded anywhere, so `tmdb.rs`'s tests use answers in TMDb's documented shapes (`/search/multi`, `/movie/{id}?append_to_response=external_ids`, `/tv/{id}?append_to_response=external_ids`, `/tv/{id}/season/{n}`), with values made up where they are not public facts of the two works; phase 2's client verifies the shapes live. The slim `tmdb.json` is tested on synthetic files in the two recorded files' shape in core (ruling RP21: no copy of a recorded file and no external ID copied from one; the IMDb and TVDB IDs follow Task 2's builders, `tt` and the TMDb ID in seven digits, and 100000 plus the TMDb ID) and on the files themselves in `lookup_answers.rs`.

use std::str::FromStr;

/// The disc kind of spec 8.2 (TheDiscDB's "Movie" or "Series", or the structural decision); defined here because 8.1's
/// identification and runtime checks are kind-aware; `plan::kind` re-exports it. Spec 8.2. Def: T3. Use: T4 to T7,
/// T11, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Kind {
    Movie,
    Tv,
}

impl Kind {
    /// Both kinds in spec 8.2's order: a movie (the default), then TV.
    pub const ALL: [Kind; 2] = [Kind::Movie, Kind::Tv];

    /// "movie" or "tv", the serde spelling. Spec 8.2.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Kind::Movie => "movie",
            Kind::Tv => "tv",
        }
    }
}

/// "movie" or "tv" exactly; any other text is refused with a sentence naming it. Spec 8.2.
impl FromStr for Kind {
    type Err = String;

    fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<Kind, String> {
        Kind::ALL
            .into_iter()
            .find(|kind| kind.as_str() == text)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("{text:?} is not a disc kind (movie or tv)"))
    }
}

/// Movie to Movie, Tv to Tv (the two enums name the same two kinds; `TmdbKind` is TMDb's numbering space). Spec 8.1.
/// Def: T3. Use: T4, T7, T13.
impl From<tmdb::TmdbKind> for Kind {
    fn from(kind: tmdb::TmdbKind) -> Kind {
        match kind {
            tmdb::TmdbKind::Movie => Kind::Movie,
            tmdb::TmdbKind::Tv => Kind::Tv,
        }
    }
}

/// Movie to Movie, Tv to Tv: the TMDb kind a disc of this kind is searched and paired as. Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T4,
/// T7, T13.
impl From<Kind> for tmdb::TmdbKind {
    fn from(kind: Kind) -> tmdb::TmdbKind {
        match kind {
            Kind::Movie => tmdb::TmdbKind::Movie,
            Kind::Tv => tmdb::TmdbKind::Tv,
        }
    }
}

use std::str::FromStr;

/// TMDb's two kinds; an identity is always the pair (8.1 "the two kinds number their records separately"). Spec 8.1.
/// Def: T3. Use: T4 to T7, T11, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum TmdbKind {
    Movie,
    Tv,
}

impl TmdbKind {
    /// Both kinds, in TMDb's own order (movie, then tv).
    pub const ALL: [TmdbKind; 2] = [TmdbKind::Movie, TmdbKind::Tv];

    /// "movie" or "tv": TMDb's `media_type` spelling and the serde one. Spec 8.1.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            TmdbKind::Movie => "movie",
            TmdbKind::Tv => "tv",
        }
    }
}

/// "movie" or "tv" exactly (a search result's `media_type`); "person" and every other text is refused. Spec 8.1.
impl FromStr for TmdbKind {
    type Err = String;

    fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<TmdbKind, String> {
        TmdbKind::ALL
            .into_iter()
            .find(|kind| kind.as_str() == text)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("{text:?} is not a TMDb kind (movie or tv)"))
    }
}

/// A TMDb identity: the kind and the ID within that kind's numbering. Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T4, T6, T7, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct TmdbIdentity {
    pub kind: TmdbKind,
    pub id: i64,
}

    #[test]
    fn item_types_spell_themselves_and_an_unknown_type_reads_as_unknown() {
        let spellings = ["MainMovie", "Episode", "Extra", "Featurette", "DeletedScene", "Trailer", "Other"];
        assert_eq!(ItemType::ALL.map(ItemType::as_str), spellings);
        for item_type in ItemType::ALL {
            let json = serde_json::to_string(&item_type).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(json, format!("\"{}\"", item_type.as_str()));
            assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<ItemType>(&json).unwrap(), item_type);
            assert_eq!(item_type.as_str().parse::<ItemType>(), Ok(item_type));
        }
        // A type outside the seven (spec 8.1 lists them) reads as Unknown instead of failing the record.
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<ItemType>("\"BonusDisc\"").unwrap(), ItemType::Unknown);
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<ItemType>("\"mainmovie\"").unwrap(), ItemType::Unknown);
        assert_eq!(ItemType::Unknown.as_str(), "Unknown");
        assert!(!ItemType::ALL.contains(&ItemType::Unknown));
        assert_eq!(
            "Unknown".parse::<ItemType>(),
            Err("\"Unknown\" is not a TheDiscDB item type (MainMovie, Episode, Extra, Featurette, DeletedScene, Trailer or Other)"
                .to_string())
        );
    }

        assert_eq!((unknown.title.as_str(), unknown.item_type), ("Smile (Commercial)", ItemType::Unknown));

    }

    #[test]
    fn an_api_answer_reads_into_the_typed_record_field_by_field() {
        let record: DiscDbRecord = serde_json::from_str(FIREFLY_API_EXCERPT).unwrap();
        let mut titles = firefly_titles();
        titles[0].resolution = Some("480p".to_string());
        titles[1].resolution = Some("480p".to_string());
        titles[1].file_name = Some("Firefly.S01.E07.Jaynestown.mkv".to_string());
        titles[1].chapters = vec![chapter(1, "Mud Buyers"), chapter(2, "Main Titles"), chapter(3, "The Statue")];
        let expected = DiscDbRecord {
            content_hash: Some("294A3E64C457A1BC9A0833335C090568".to_string()),
            global_disc_id: Some("C5B150FCB154727FAF60C1BEFA1DCB88".to_string()),
            format: Some("DVD".to_string()),
            media: Some(DiscDbMedia {
                title: Some("Firefly".to_string()),
                full_title: Some("Firefly".to_string()),
                year: Some(2002),
                media_type: Some("Series".to_string()),
                external_ids: DiscDbExternalIds { tmdb: Some("1437".to_string()), imdb: Some("tt0303461".to_string()) },
            }),
            release: Some(DiscDbRelease {
                title: Some("The Complete Series DVD".to_string()),
                year: Some(2003),
                slug: Some("2003-dvd-the-complete-series".to_string()),
                locale: Some("en-us".to_string()),
                region_code: Some("1".to_string()),
                upc: Some("024543089292".to_string()),
            }),
            disc: Some(DiscDbDisc { index: Some(2), name: Some("Disc 2".to_string()), slug: Some("disc-2".to_string()) }),
            pinned_index: None,
            pinned_name: None,
            titles,
        };
        assert_eq!(record, expected);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_pinned_file_reads_through_the_pascal_case_aliases() {
        let record: DiscDbRecord = serde_json::from_str(FIREFLY_PINNED_EXCERPT).unwrap();
        let mut titles = firefly_titles();
        titles[0].comment = Some("A1_t03_t05.mkv".to_string());
        titles[1].comment = Some("F1_t05_t11.mkv".to_string());
        let expected = DiscDbRecord {
            content_hash: Some("294A3E64C457A1BC9A0833335C090568".to_string()),
            global_disc_id: Some("C5B150FCB154727FAF60C1BEFA1DCB88".to_string()),
            format: Some("DVD".to_string()),
            pinned_index: Some(2),
            pinned_name: Some("Disc 2".to_string()),
            titles,
            ..bare_record()
        };
        assert_eq!(record, expected);
        assert_eq!(record.disc_number(), Some(2));
    }

    #[test]
    fn track_kinds_and_channel_counts_come_from_type_and_audio_type() {
        assert_eq!(track(0, "Video", "Mpeg2").kind(), Some(StreamKind::Video));
        assert_eq!(track(1, "Audio", "DTS").kind(), Some(StreamKind::Audio));
        assert_eq!(track(2, "Subtitles", "HDMV PGS Subtitles").kind(), Some(StreamKind::Subtitles));
        assert_eq!(track(3, "Data", "Text").kind(), None);
        assert_eq!(track(4, "audio", "DTS").kind(), None);
        // audio_type is a layout name with no channel count (spec 8.1); each name the fixtures or MakeMKV use gives one.
        let layouts = [
            ("Mono", Some(1)),
            ("Stereo", Some(2)),
            ("Surround 5.0", Some(5)),
            ("Surround 5.1", Some(6)),
            ("Surround 6.1", Some(7)),
            ("Surround 7.1", Some(8)),
            ("Surround 9.1", None),
            ("stereo", None),
            ("", None),
        ];
        for (layout, channels) in layouts {
            let audio = DiscDbTrack { audio_type: Some(layout.to_string()), ..track(1, "Audio", "Dolby Digital") };
            assert_eq!(audio.channels(), channels, "{layout:?}");
        }
        assert_eq!(track(1, "Audio", "Dolby Digital").channels(), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_title_gives_its_seconds_and_its_tracks_of_one_kind_in_index_order() {
        let title = DiscDbTitle {
            duration: Some("1:41:13".to_string()),
            tracks: vec![
                track(2, "Audio", "DTS"),
                track(0, "Video", "Mpeg2"),
                track(3, "Subtitles", "HDMV PGS Subtitles"),
                track(1, "Audio", "DTS-HD Master Audio"),
            ],
            ..bare_title(0)
        };
        assert_eq!(title.seconds(), Some(6073));
        let audio = title.tracks_of(StreamKind::Audio);
        assert_eq!(audio.iter().map(|track| track.index).collect::<Vec<u32>>(), vec![1, 2]);
        let video = title.tracks_of(StreamKind::Video);
        assert_eq!(video.iter().map(|track| track.index).collect::<Vec<u32>>(), vec![0]);
        let subtitles = title.tracks_of(StreamKind::Subtitles);
        assert_eq!(subtitles.iter().map(|track| track.index).collect::<Vec<u32>>(), vec![3]);
        assert_eq!(DiscDbTitle { duration: Some("101:13".to_string()), ..bare_title(0) }.seconds(), None);
        assert_eq!(bare_title(0).seconds(), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_record_gives_its_kind_tmdb_identity_title_and_year_and_disc_number() {
        let record: DiscDbRecord = serde_json::from_str(FIREFLY_API_EXCERPT).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(record.kind(), Some(Kind::Tv));
        assert_eq!(record.tmdb_identity(), Some(TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::Tv, id: 1437 }));
        assert_eq!(record.title_and_year(), Some(("Firefly".to_string(), Some(2002))));
        assert_eq!(record.disc_number(), Some(2));

        let media = |media_type: &str, tmdb: Option<&str>| DiscDbMedia {
            title: Some("Knowing".to_string()),
            full_title: None,
            year: Some(2009),
            media_type: Some(media_type.to_string()),
            external_ids: DiscDbExternalIds { tmdb: tmdb.map(str::to_string), imdb: None },
        };
        let with = |media: Option<DiscDbMedia>| DiscDbRecord { media, ..bare_record() };
        let movie = with(Some(media("Movie", Some("13811"))));
        assert_eq!(movie.kind(), Some(Kind::Movie));
        assert_eq!(movie.tmdb_identity(), Some(TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::Movie, id: 13811 }));
        assert_eq!(movie.title_and_year(), Some(("Knowing".to_string(), Some(2009))));
        // A type other than Movie or Series states no kind, so its TMDb ID cannot be paired with one.
        let other = with(Some(media("Collection", Some("13811"))));
        assert_eq!((other.kind(), other.tmdb_identity()), (None, None));
        // An absent, empty, non-numeric or zero TMDb ID gives no identity; the kind still holds.
        for tmdb in [None, Some(""), Some("tt0448011"), Some("0")] {
            let record = with(Some(media("Movie", tmdb)));
            assert_eq!((record.kind(), record.tmdb_identity()), (Some(Kind::Movie), None), "{tmdb:?}");
        }
        // No media (the pinned form): no kind, no identity, no title for 8.1's search; the top-level Index is the disc.
        let pinned = DiscDbRecord { pinned_index: Some(1), ..bare_record() };
        assert_eq!(
            (pinned.kind(), pinned.tmdb_identity(), pinned.title_and_year(), pinned.disc_number()),
            (None, None, None, Some(1))
        );
        // disc.index wins over a pinned Index; a media without a title gives no title and year.
        let both = DiscDbRecord {
            disc: Some(DiscDbDisc { index: Some(3), name: None, slug: None }),
            pinned_index: Some(1),
            media: Some(DiscDbMedia { title: None, ..media("Movie", None) }),
            ..bare_record()
        };
        assert_eq!((both.disc_number(), both.title_and_year()), (Some(3), None));
        assert_eq!(bare_record().disc_number(), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn main_movies_and_episodes_are_listed_in_index_order() {
        let item = |item_type: ItemType| Some(DiscDbItem { title: "x".to_string(), item_type, season: None, episode: None });
        let record = DiscDbRecord {
            titles: vec![
                DiscDbTitle { item: item(ItemType::Episode), ..bare_title(5) },
                DiscDbTitle { item: item(ItemType::Episode), ..bare_title(2) },
                DiscDbTitle { item: item(ItemType::MainMovie), ..bare_title(7) },
                DiscDbTitle { item: item(ItemType::Extra), ..bare_title(1) },
                bare_title(3),
                DiscDbTitle { item: item(ItemType::MainMovie), ..bare_title(0) },
            ],
            ..bare_record()
        };
        assert_eq!(indices(record.main_movies()), vec![0, 7]);
        assert_eq!(indices(record.episodes()), vec![2, 5]);
    }
}

```rust
use std::str::FromStr;

use super::tmdb::{TmdbIdentity, TmdbKind};
use super::Kind;
use crate::disc::StreamKind;
use crate::robot::duration_seconds;

/// `item.type` of a described title (spec 8.1): the seven values of the fixtures, and Unknown (`#[serde(other)]`) for any
/// other TheDiscDB type, so one unknown item never fails a whole record. Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T5, T6.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub enum ItemType {
    MainMovie,
    Episode,
    Extra,
    Featurette,
    DeletedScene,
    Trailer,
    Other,
    #[serde(other)]
    Unknown,
}

impl ItemType {
    /// The seven types spec 8.1 lists, in its order; Unknown is not one of them.
    pub const ALL: [ItemType; 7] = [
        ItemType::MainMovie,
        ItemType::Episode,
        ItemType::Extra,
        ItemType::Featurette,
        ItemType::DeletedScene,
        ItemType::Trailer,
        ItemType::Other,
    ];

    /// TheDiscDB's spelling ("MainMovie", "DeletedScene"), which is also the serde one; "Unknown" for a type outside
    /// the seven. Spec 8.1.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            ItemType::MainMovie => "MainMovie",
            ItemType::Episode => "Episode",
            ItemType::Extra => "Extra",
            ItemType::Featurette => "Featurette",
            ItemType::DeletedScene => "DeletedScene",
            ItemType::Trailer => "Trailer",
            ItemType::Other => "Other",
            ItemType::Unknown => "Unknown",
        }
    }
}

/// One of the seven spellings exactly; "Unknown" and every other text is refused. Spec 8.1.
impl FromStr for ItemType {
    type Err = String;

    fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<ItemType, String> {
        ItemType::ALL.into_iter().find(|item_type| item_type.as_str() == text).ok_or_else(|| {
            format!(
                "{text:?} is not a TheDiscDB item type (MainMovie, Episode, Extra, Featurette, DeletedScene, Trailer or Other)"
            )
        })
    }
}

/// A described title's item. `season` and `episode` are strings as the API gives them ("01", "1", "12-13"). Spec 8.1.
/// Def: T3. Use: T5, T6, T11.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct DiscDbItem {
    #[serde(alias = "Title")]
    pub title: String,
    #[serde(rename = "type", alias = "Type")]
    pub item_type: ItemType,
    /// Present where the item belongs to an episode (an Episode, or the Office's DeletedScene items).
    #[serde(default, alias = "Season")]
    pub season: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Episode")]
    pub episode: Option<String>,
}

/// One track of a TheDiscDB title: `type` is Video, Audio or Subtitles; `name` is MakeMKV's attribute 7 (the long codec
/// name: "Dolby Digital", "DTS-HD Master Audio", "TrueHD Atmos", "HDMV PGS Subtitles", "Dvd Subtitles", "Mpeg2",
/// "MpegH HEVC Main10@L5.1 (dvhe.07.06 BL+FEL+RPU)"); an audio track has `audio_type` ("Stereo", "Surround 5.1",
/// "Surround 7.1"; no channel count), `language_code` (three letters) and `language` ("English"); a subtitle track
/// `language_code` and `language`; `description` sometimes ("ENglish", "Spanish", "Director Commentary"). Spec 8.1.
/// Def: T3. Use: T8, T9.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct DiscDbTrack {
    #[serde(alias = "Index")]
    pub index: u32,
    #[serde(rename = "type", alias = "Type")]
    pub track_type: String,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Name")]
    pub name: Option<String>,
    /// Video only ("720x480", "3840x2160").
    #[serde(default, alias = "Resolution")]
    pub resolution: Option<String>,
    /// Video only ("16:9", "4:3").
    #[serde(default, alias = "AspectRatio")]
    pub aspect_ratio: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "AudioType")]
    pub audio_type: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "LanguageCode")]
    pub language_code: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Language")]
    pub language: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Description")]
    pub description: Option<String>,
}

impl DiscDbTrack {
    /// TheDiscDB's `type` is spelt as MakeMKV's attribute 1 ("Video", "Audio", "Subtitles"), so
    /// `disc::StreamKind::from_attr` reads it (one copy); None for anything else. Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T8.
    pub fn kind(&self) -> Option<StreamKind> {
        StreamKind::from_attr(&self.track_type)
    }

    /// "Stereo" 2, "Surround 5.1" 6, "Surround 7.1" 8, "Mono" 1, "Surround 5.0" 5, "Surround 6.1" 7; None otherwise
    /// (spec 8.1: `audio_type` is the layout, there is no channel count). Def: T3. Use: T8.
    pub fn channels(&self) -> Option<u32> {
        match self.audio_type.as_deref()? {
            "Mono" => Some(1),
            "Stereo" => Some(2),
            "Surround 5.0" => Some(5),
            "Surround 5.1" => Some(6),
            "Surround 6.1" => Some(7),
            "Surround 7.1" => Some(8),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// One chapter of a TheDiscDB title. Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: none beyond parsing (kept for the full shape).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct DiscDbChapter {
    #[serde(alias = "Index")]
    pub index: u32,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Title")]
    pub title: Option<String>,
}

/// One title of the answer. `duration` is "H:MM:SS", `size` bytes, `segment_map` MakeMKV's text (may end in "...").
/// Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T5, T6, T8, T9, T10.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct DiscDbTitle {
    #[serde(alias = "Index")]
    pub index: u32,
    /// Attribute 16 on a Blu-ray; the DVD title number (attribute 24's text) on a DVD.
    #[serde(default, alias = "SourceFile")]
    pub source_file: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "SegmentMap")]
    pub segment_map: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Duration")]
    pub duration: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Size")]
    pub size: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "DisplaySize")]
    pub display_size: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Resolution")]
    pub resolution: Option<String>,
    /// MakeMKV's attribute 27, the output file name ("title.mkv", "Smile.mkv"); never compared with Title.comment
    /// (attribute 49). Only the pinned form has it.
    #[serde(default, alias = "Comment")]
    pub comment: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Chapters")]
    pub chapters: Vec<DiscDbChapter>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Tracks")]
    pub tracks: Vec<DiscDbTrack>,
    /// Only on a title TheDiscDB has described (with `item`), and only in the API's form.
    #[serde(default, alias = "FileName")]
    pub file_name: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Item")]
    pub item: Option<DiscDbItem>,
}

impl DiscDbTitle {
    /// `robot::duration_seconds(duration)`; None without a duration or for one that is not "H:MM:SS". Spec 8.1.
    /// Def: T3. Use: T3 (`same_title`).
    pub fn seconds(&self) -> Option<u32> {
        self.duration.as_deref().and_then(duration_seconds)
    }

    /// The tracks of one kind, in index order (whatever order the answer lists them in). Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T8.
    pub fn tracks_of(&self, kind: StreamKind) -> Vec<&DiscDbTrack> {
        let mut tracks: Vec<&DiscDbTrack> = self.tracks.iter().filter(|track| track.kind() == Some(kind)).collect();
        tracks.sort_by_key(|track| track.index);
        tracks
    }
}

/// `media`: `type` is "Movie" or "Series"; `external_ids.tmdb` and `.imdb` are strings ("1437", "tt0303461"). Spec 8.1.
/// Def: T3. Use: T3, T4, T5, T11.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct DiscDbMedia {
    pub title: Option<String>,
    pub full_title: Option<String>,
    pub year: Option<i32>,
    #[serde(rename = "type")]
    pub media_type: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub external_ids: DiscDbExternalIds,
}

/// `media.external_ids`: TMDb's and IMDb's IDs as strings. Spec 8.1. Def: T3.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct DiscDbExternalIds {
    pub tmdb: Option<String>,
    pub imdb: Option<String>,
}

/// `release`: title, year, slug, locale ("en-us"), region_code, upc. Spec 8.1. Def: T3.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct DiscDbRelease {
    pub title: Option<String>,
    pub year: Option<i32>,
    pub slug: Option<String>,
    pub locale: Option<String>,
    pub region_code: Option<String>,
    pub upc: Option<String>,
}

/// The API's `disc` object: index, name ("Season Three Disc Three"), slug (the pinned form has none: its disc facts are
/// DiscDbRecord's `pinned_index` and `pinned_name`). Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T3 (`DiscDbRecord::disc_number`).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct DiscDbDisc {
    pub index: Option<i64>,
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub slug: Option<String>,
}

/// One TheDiscDB object (a `dischash` answer, or one element of a `discid` answer, or a pinned `discNN.json`). Spec 8.1.
/// Def: T3. Use: T4 to T11, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct DiscDbRecord {
    #[serde(default, alias = "ContentHash")]
    pub content_hash: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "GlobalDiscId")]
    pub global_disc_id: Option<String>,
    /// "UHD", "Blu-ray", "Blu-Ray", "DVD".
    #[serde(default, alias = "Format")]
    pub format: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub media: Option<DiscDbMedia>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub release: Option<DiscDbRelease>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub disc: Option<DiscDbDisc>,
    /// The pinned form's top-level disc facts (`Index` 1 or 2, `Name`); None in an API answer.
    #[serde(default, rename = "Index")]
    pub pinned_index: Option<i64>,
    #[serde(default, rename = "Name")]
    pub pinned_name: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Titles")]
    pub titles: Vec<DiscDbTitle>,
}

impl DiscDbRecord {
    /// `media.type` "Movie" gives Kind::Movie, "Series" Kind::Tv; None otherwise (8.2 "TheDiscDB states the kind"; a
    /// pinned record has no media, so None). Spec 8.1, 8.2. Def: T3. Use: T5.
    pub fn kind(&self) -> Option<Kind> {
        match self.media.as_ref()?.media_type.as_deref()? {
            "Movie" => Some(Kind::Movie),
            "Series" => Some(Kind::Tv),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// `media.external_ids.tmdb` parsed (a positive whole number) and paired with the kind (8.1 "A match supplies a TMDb
    /// ID"); None without a kind or without such an ID. Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T4, T7.
    pub fn tmdb_identity(&self) -> Option<TmdbIdentity> {
        let kind = self.kind()?;
        let id = self.media.as_ref()?.external_ids.tmdb.as_deref()?.trim().parse::<i64>().ok().filter(|&id| id > 0)?;
        Some(TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::from(kind), id })
    }

    /// The titles whose item type is MainMovie, in index order. Spec 8.1 "The main movie is the title whose item.type is
    /// MainMovie". Def: T3. Use: T5.
    pub fn main_movies(&self) -> Vec<&DiscDbTitle> {
        self.titles_of(ItemType::MainMovie)
    }

    /// The titles whose item type is Episode, in index order. Spec 8.1, 8.5. Def: T3. Use: T6.
    pub fn episodes(&self) -> Vec<&DiscDbTitle> {
        self.titles_of(ItemType::Episode)
    }

    /// `media.title` (trimmed, not empty) and `media.year` for the TMDb search of 8.1 ("TMDb is searched with the entry's
    /// title and year"). Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T4.
    pub fn title_and_year(&self) -> Option<(String, Option<i32>)> {
        let media = self.media.as_ref()?;
        let title = media.title.as_deref().map(str::trim).filter(|title| !title.is_empty())?;
        Some((title.to_string(), media.year))
    }

    /// The disc's number on its release: `disc.index`, else `pinned_index`. Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: phase 2.
    pub fn disc_number(&self) -> Option<i64> {
        self.disc.as_ref().and_then(|disc| disc.index).or(self.pinned_index)
    }

    /// The titles whose item has `item_type`, in index order.
    fn titles_of(&self, item_type: ItemType) -> Vec<&DiscDbTitle> {
        let mut titles: Vec<&DiscDbTitle> = self
            .titles
            .iter()
            .filter(|title| title.item.as_ref().is_some_and(|item| item.item_type == item_type))
            .collect();
        titles.sort_by_key(|title| title.index);
        titles
    }
}
