    /// A path under the repository's corpus folder (tracked, so on every OS and in CI).
    fn corpus(path: &str) -> PathBuf {
        Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../corpus").join(path)
    }

    /// A file's text, read lossily as `crates/core/tests/thediscdb_corpus.rs` reads the pinned logs.
    fn read(path: &Path) -> String {
        let bytes = fs::read(path).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{}: {error}", path.display()));
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes).into_owned()
    }

    /// Every answer of corpus/thediscdb-api in name order, as (file name, records): a dischash file's one record, a
    /// discid file's array.
    fn api_answers() -> Vec<(String, Vec<DiscDbRecord>)> {
        let dir = corpus("thediscdb-api");
        let mut names: Vec<String> = fs::read_dir(&dir)
            .unwrap()
            .map(|entry| entry.unwrap().file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned())
            .filter(|name| name.ends_with(".json"))
            .collect();
        names.sort();
        names
            .into_iter()
            .map(|name| {
                let text = read(&dir.join(&name));
                let records = if name.starts_with("dischash-") {
                    parse_dischash(&text, &name).unwrap().into_iter().collect()
                } else {
                    parse_discid(&text, &name).unwrap()
                };
                (name, records)
            })
            .collect()
    }

    /// The dischash answer of one content hash.
    fn api_record(hash: &str) -> DiscDbRecord {
        let name = format!("dischash-{hash}.json");
        parse_dischash(&read(&corpus("thediscdb-api").join(&name)), &name).unwrap().unwrap()
    }

    /// The nine pinned logs, by stem under corpus/thediscdb, with their discNN.json's top-level Index, Name and
    /// ContentHash and their title count.
    const PINNED: [(&str, i64, &str, &str, usize); 9] = [
        ("movie/John Wick (2014)/4k-ultra-hd--blu-ray/disc01", 1, "4K Ultra HD", "76E63EBB5B66F73B0C37BFAB59B8ABA5", 10),
        ("movie/John Wick (2014)/4k-ultra-hd--blu-ray/disc02", 2, "Blu-ray", "BB9E6C963A4E2EAAB46C748CD4C00B69", 9),
        ("movie/Knowing (2009)/2010-dvd/disc01", 1, "DVD", "631BD77872C157D7C436E6F48F06A478", 7),
        ("movie/Smile (2022)/2022-4k/disc01", 1, "4K", "E826F0C64B04079EA83094AC046E8709", 236),
        (
            "movie/The Expendables 3 (2014)/the-expendables-3-film-collection/disc01",
            1,
            "The Expendables 3",
            "545411B47060B18FD7F8D94599F24708",
            64,
        ),
        ("series/Chernobyl (2019)/2020-4k-US/disc01", 1, "4K Disc One", "D11592C9B2D252937C22EDF01DBD1E05", 33),
        ("series/Chernobyl (2019)/2020-4k-US/disc02", 2, "4K Disc Two", "59796E40C7ABE16ACD9B259E732D392B", 31),
        ("series/Firefly (2002)/2003-dvd-the-complete-series/disc01", 1, "Disc 1", "5A961BC67EB34171F24852D3A7688020", 5),
        ("series/Firefly (2002)/2003-dvd-the-complete-series/disc02", 2, "Disc 2", "294A3E64C457A1BC9A0833335C090568", 6),
    ];

    /// A pinned discNN.json through parse_dischash (an object with a non-empty `Titles` is a hit).
    fn pinned_record(stem: &str) -> DiscDbRecord {
        let path = corpus("thediscdb").join(format!("{stem}.json"));
        parse_dischash(&read(&path), &path.display().to_string()).unwrap().unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_dischash_reads_one_object_and_returns_none_for_an_empty_body_or_a_non_hit() {
        // A miss is HTTP 404 with an empty body, which the recorder saves as an empty file (spec 8.1).
        for empty in ["", "\u{feff}", " \r\n"] {
            assert_eq!(parse_dischash(empty, "hash.json"), Ok(None), "{empty:?}");
        }
        assert_eq!(parse_dischash(r#"{"titles": []}"#, "hash.json"), Ok(None));
        assert_eq!(parse_dischash(r#"{"error": "not found"}"#, "hash.json"), Ok(None));
        assert_eq!(parse_dischash(r#""error""#, "hash.json"), Ok(None));
        assert_eq!(parse_dischash("[]", "hash.json"), Ok(None));
        let hit = parse_dischash("\u{feff}{\"content_hash\": \"ABC\", \"titles\": [{\"index\": 0}]}", "hash.json")
            .unwrap()
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!((hit.content_hash.as_deref(), hit.titles.len(), hit.titles[0].index), (Some("ABC"), 1, 0));
        // The pinned form's capitalised Titles makes a hit too; an empty list of them does not.
        let pinned = parse_dischash(r#"{"Index": 1, "Name": "DVD", "Titles": [{"Index": 0}]}"#, "disc01.json")
            .unwrap()
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!((pinned.pinned_index, pinned.pinned_name.as_deref(), pinned.titles.len()), (Some(1), Some("DVD"), 1));
        assert_eq!(parse_dischash(r#"{"Titles": []}"#, "disc01.json"), Ok(None));
        assert_eq!(
            parse_dischash(r#"[{"titles": [{"index": 0}]}]"#, "hash.json"),
            Err("hash.json: a dischash answer is one object, not an array".to_string())
        );
        let broken = parse_dischash("{\"titles\": [", "hash.json").unwrap_err();
        assert!(broken.starts_with("hash.json: EOF while parsing"), "{broken}");
        let mistyped = parse_dischash(r#"{"titles": [{"index": "zero"}]}"#, "hash.json").unwrap_err();
        assert!(mistyped.starts_with("hash.json: invalid type: string \"zero\""), "{mistyped}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_discid_reads_an_array_and_an_empty_body_as_no_records() {
        assert_eq!(parse_discid("", "discid.json"), Ok(Vec::new()));
        assert_eq!(parse_discid("\u{feff}", "discid.json"), Ok(Vec::new()));
        assert_eq!(parse_discid("[]", "discid.json"), Ok(Vec::new()));
        let two = parse_discid(
            r#"[{"disc": {"index": 1}, "titles": [{"index": 0}]}, {"disc": {"index": 3}, "titles": []}]"#,
            "discid.json",
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(two.iter().map(DiscDbRecord::disc_number).collect::<Vec<_>>(), vec![Some(1), Some(3)]);
        let object = parse_discid(r#"{"titles": [{"index": 0}]}"#, "discid.json").unwrap_err();
        assert!(object.starts_with("discid.json: invalid type: map"), "{object}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_api_answer_parses_and_names_its_own_hash_or_disc_id() {
        let answers = api_answers();
        assert_eq!(answers.len(), 18);
        for (name, records) in &answers {
            let key = name.trim_end_matches(".json");
            if let Some(hash) = key.strip_prefix("dischash-") {
                assert_eq!(records.len(), 1, "{name}");
                assert_eq!(records[0].content_hash.as_deref(), Some(hash), "{name}");
            } else {
                let id = key.strip_prefix("discid-").unwrap();
                let expected = if id == "B8C1624CF3BFCB2B49697266B06D308E29746B4A" { 2 } else { 1 };
                assert_eq!(records.len(), expected, "{name}");
                for record in records {
                    assert_eq!(record.global_disc_id.as_deref(), Some(id), "{name}");
                    // Each disc ID's record is the record of one of the nine fingerprints.
                    let hash = record.content_hash.as_deref().unwrap();
                    assert!(answers.iter().any(|(other, _)| *other == format!("dischash-{hash}.json")), "{name}");
                }
            }
        }
        let records: Vec<&DiscDbRecord> = answers.iter().flat_map(|(_, records)| records).collect();
        assert_eq!(records.len(), 19);
        assert_eq!(records.iter().map(|record| record.titles.len()).sum::<usize>(), 866);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_api_answers_hold_the_field_values_spec_8_1_lists() {
        let answers = api_answers();
        let records: Vec<&DiscDbRecord> = answers.iter().flat_map(|(_, records)| records).collect();
        let formats: BTreeSet<&str> = records.iter().filter_map(|record| record.format.as_deref()).collect();
        assert_eq!(formats, BTreeSet::from(["Blu-Ray", "Blu-ray", "DVD", "UHD"]));
        let media_types: BTreeSet<&str> =
            records.iter().filter_map(|record| record.media.as_ref()?.media_type.as_deref()).collect();
        assert_eq!(media_types, BTreeSet::from(["Movie", "Series"]));
        let locales: BTreeSet<&str> =
            records.iter().filter_map(|record| record.release.as_ref()?.locale.as_deref()).collect();
        assert_eq!(locales, BTreeSet::from(["en-us"]));
        for record in &records {
            assert!(record.kind().is_some() && record.tmdb_identity().is_some(), "{:?}", record.content_hash);
            assert!(record.disc.is_some() && record.pinned_index.is_none(), "{:?}", record.content_hash);
        }

        let titles: Vec<&DiscDbTitle> = records.iter().flat_map(|record| &record.titles).collect();
        // file_name and item "only when TheDiscDB has described the title".
        assert!(titles.iter().all(|title| title.file_name.is_some() == title.item.is_some()));
        let mut item_types: BTreeMap<&str, usize> = BTreeMap::new();
        for item in titles.iter().filter_map(|title| title.item.as_ref()) {
            *item_types.entry(item.item_type.as_str()).or_default() += 1;
            // season and episode "where the item belongs to an episode": every one here is an Episode.
            let episode = item.item_type == ItemType::Episode;
            assert_eq!((item.season.is_some(), item.episode.is_some()), (episode, episode), "{}", item.title);
        }
        assert_eq!(
            item_types,
            BTreeMap::from([
                ("DeletedScene", 5),
                ("Episode", 24),
                ("Extra", 68),
                ("Featurette", 4),
                ("MainMovie", 11),
                ("Other", 6),
                ("Trailer", 2),
            ])
        );
        assert_eq!(titles.iter().map(|title| title.chapters.len()).sum::<usize>(), 224);

        let tracks: Vec<&DiscDbTrack> = titles.iter().flat_map(|title| &title.tracks).collect();
        let mut by_type: BTreeMap<&str, (usize, usize)> = BTreeMap::new();
        for track in &tracks {
            let entry = by_type.entry(track.track_type.as_str()).or_default();
            entry.0 += 1;
            entry.1 += usize::from(track.description.is_some());
            // The fields of each kind of track as spec 8.1 lists them; every language code has three letters.
            let fields_hold = match track.kind() {
                Some(StreamKind::Video) => {
                    track.resolution.is_some()
                        && track.aspect_ratio.is_some()
                        && track.audio_type.is_none()
                        && track.language_code.is_none()
                }
                Some(StreamKind::Audio) => {
                    track.channels().is_some() && track.language.is_some() && track.resolution.is_none()
                }
                Some(StreamKind::Subtitles) => {
                    track.language.is_some() && track.audio_type.is_none() && track.resolution.is_none()
                }
                None => false,
            };
            assert!(fields_hold, "{track:?}");
            if track.kind() != Some(StreamKind::Video) {
                assert_eq!(track.language_code.as_deref().map(str::len), Some(3), "{track:?}");
            }
        }
        // (tracks, tracks with a description) per type: 58 of 837 audio and 30 of 2002 subtitle tracks here; the
        // owner's 2 recorded answers bring them to spec 8.1's 877 and 2018 (crates/dev/tests/lookup_answers.rs).
        assert_eq!(by_type, BTreeMap::from([("Audio", (837, 58)), ("Subtitles", (2002, 30)), ("Video", (866, 0))]));
    }

```rust
/// An answer's text without the one byte-order mark a Windows recorder may write before it (the recorder's PowerShell
/// jobs write UTF-8 with one, as `recording::read_json` allows for).
fn without_bom(text: &str) -> &str {
    text.strip_prefix('\u{feff}').unwrap_or(text)
}

/// An answer's JSON (after `without_bom`) as `T`; Err is serde_json's message after `shown` and ": ".
fn parse_json<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(text: &str, shown: &str) -> Result<T, String> {
    serde_json::from_str(without_bom(text)).map_err(|error| format!("{shown}: {error}"))
}
```

use serde_json::Value;

use super::tmdb::{TmdbIdentity, TmdbKind};
use super::{parse_json, without_bom, Kind};
use crate::disc::StreamKind;
use crate::recording::files::{thediscdb_answer, DiscDbAnswer};

```rust
/// A `dischash` answer: None for an empty body (the recorder writes an empty file on 404) or when
/// `recording::files::thediscdb_answer` of the parsed value is not Hit; else the object. A pinned `discNN.json` (an object
/// whose capitalised `Titles` is a non-empty array) is a hit too, so the pinned files read through this function; a
/// non-empty array is refused (a dischash answer is one object). Err is serde_json's message prefixed by `shown`.
/// Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T15.
pub fn parse_dischash(text: &str, shown: &str) -> Result<Option<DiscDbRecord>, String> {
    if without_bom(text).trim().is_empty() {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let value: Value = parse_json(text, shown)?;
    let pinned = value.get("Titles").and_then(Value::as_array).is_some_and(|titles| !titles.is_empty());
    if thediscdb_answer(&value) != DiscDbAnswer::Hit && !pinned {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    if !value.is_object() {
        return Err(format!("{shown}: a dischash answer is one object, not an array"));
    }
    serde_json::from_value(value).map(Some).map_err(|error| format!("{shown}: {error}"))
}

/// A `discid` answer: an array (empty on a miss), or an empty body as an empty array. Err is serde_json's message
/// prefixed by `shown` (an object is not an array). Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T15.
pub fn parse_discid(text: &str, shown: &str) -> Result<Vec<DiscDbRecord>, String> {
    if without_bom(text).trim().is_empty() {
        return Ok(Vec::new());
    }
    parse_json(text, shown)
}

    /// A database title with a source file, segment map, duration and size, and nothing else.
    fn db_title(index: u32, source_file: Option<&str>, segment_map: &str, duration: &str, size: Option<u64>) -> DiscDbTitle {
        DiscDbTitle {
            source_file: source_file.map(str::to_string),
            segment_map: Some(segment_map.to_string()),
            duration: Some(duration.to_string()),
            size,
            ..bare_title(index)
        }
    }

    /// A Blu-ray disc from (title number, TINFO attributes) rows, through `testsupport::scan_text`, `robot::parse` and
    /// `disc::disc`; no streams.
    fn scan_disc(titles: &[(u32, Vec<(u32, &str)>)]) -> Disc {
        let no_streams: &[(u32, &[(u32, &str)])] = &[];
        let rows: Vec<(u32, &[(u32, &str)], &[(u32, &[(u32, &str)])])> =
            titles.iter().map(|(number, attrs)| (*number, attrs.as_slice(), no_streams)).collect();
        disc(&parse(&scan_text(&[(1, "Blu-ray disc")], &rows))).unwrap()
    }

    /// The typed disc of a pinned log.
    fn pinned_disc(stem: &str) -> Disc {
        disc(&parse(&read(&corpus("thediscdb").join(format!("{stem}.txt"))))).unwrap()

    fn a_blu_ray_title_matches_on_source_file_segment_map_size_and_duration() {
        let base: Vec<(u32, &'static str)> = vec![(9, "1:59:10"), (11, "55613952000"), (16, "00800.mpls"), (26, "6")];
        let with = |id: u32, value: &'static str| -> Vec<(u32, &'static str)> {
            base.iter().map(|&(key, old)| if key == id { (key, value) } else { (key, old) }).collect()
        };
        let scan = scan_disc(&[
            (0, base.clone()),

            (4, with(9, "1:59:12")),

            (6, with(9, "1:59:13")),
            (7, with(9, "1:59:07")),

        // Exact source file, segment map and size; the duration within 2 s either way (DURATION_MATCH_S).

    #[test]
    fn match_titles_takes_each_scan_title_once_in_database_index_order() {
        let twin: Vec<(u32, &str)> = vec![(9, "0:05:00"), (11, "1000"), (16, "00010.m2ts"), (26, "10")];
        let scan = scan_disc(&[(3, twin.clone()), (4, twin)]);
        let same = |index: u32| db_title(index, Some("00010.m2ts"), "10", "0:05:00", Some(1000));
        // Listed out of order: index 0 is matched first and takes title 3, index 1 takes title 4, index 2 finds none left.
        let record = DiscDbRecord { titles: vec![same(2), same(1), same(0)], ..bare_record() };
        assert_eq!(match_titles(&record, &scan), BTreeMap::from([(0, 3), (1, 4)]));
        // A database index the record repeats keeps its first match and takes no second scan title.
        let repeated = DiscDbRecord { titles: vec![same(0), same(0)], ..bare_record() };
        assert_eq!(match_titles(&repeated, &scan), BTreeMap::from([(0, 3)]));
    }

        assert_eq!((eight.segment_map.as_str(), eight.seconds, eight.size), ("1", Some(6073), Some(67757930496)));
        assert_eq!((zero.source_file.as_deref(), eight.source_file.as_deref()), (Some("00001.mpls"), Some("00001.m2ts")));
        let record = api_record("76E63EBB5B66F73B0C37BFAB59B8ABA5");
        assert!(same_title(&record.titles[0], zero));
        assert!(!same_title(&record.titles[0], eight));
        let matches = match_titles(&record, &scan);
        assert_eq!((matches.get(&0), matches.get(&8)), (Some(&0), Some(&8)));
    }

```rust
/// A database title matches a scan title (spec 8.3 "on source file name and segment map, then exact size and duration
/// within 2 s"): source first: when the scan title has attribute 16, `db.source_file == title.source_file`; otherwise
/// `disc::same_source(&title_source(None, db.source_file), &title.source())` (on a DVD TheDiscDB writes attribute 24 in
/// source_file, compared as numbers); a title with neither never matches. Then `disc::segment_maps_agree` (a database
/// title without a segment map compares as ""), exact size when both carry one, and duration within
/// `disc::DURATION_MATCH_S` (a side without a duration never matches). MakeMKV title numbers are never used. Spec 8.3.
/// Def: T3. Use: T3.
pub fn same_title(db: &DiscDbTitle, title: &Title) -> bool {
    let source_matches = match title.source_file.as_deref().filter(|name| !name.is_empty()) {
        Some(name) => db.source_file.as_deref() == Some(name),
        None => same_source(&title_source(None, db.source_file.as_deref()), &title.source()),
    };
    if !source_matches || !segment_maps_agree(db.segment_map.as_deref().unwrap_or(""), &title.segment_map) {
        return false;
    }
    if let (Some(db_size), Some(scan_size)) = (db.size, title.size) {
        if db_size != scan_size {
            return false;
        }
    }
    match (db.seconds(), title.seconds) {
        (Some(db_seconds), Some(scan_seconds)) => db_seconds.abs_diff(scan_seconds) <= DURATION_MATCH_S,
        _ => false,
    }
}

/// Every database title matched to the first scan title it matches, in database index order; a scan title is taken once.
/// Key: database index; value: scan title number. A database index the record repeats keeps its first match. Spec 8.3
/// "Database titles are matched to scan titles". Def: T3. Use: T5, T6, T7, T8, T9, T16.
pub fn match_titles(record: &DiscDbRecord, disc: &Disc) -> BTreeMap<u32, u32> {
    let mut by_index: Vec<&DiscDbTitle> = record.titles.iter().collect();
    by_index.sort_by_key(|db| db.index);
    let mut taken: BTreeSet<u32> = BTreeSet::new();
    let mut matches = BTreeMap::new();
    for db in by_index {
        if matches.contains_key(&db.index) {
            continue;
        }
        let found = disc.titles.values().find(|title| !taken.contains(&title.number) && same_title(db, title));
        if let Some(title) = found {
            taken.insert(title.number);
            matches.insert(db.index, title.number);
        }
    }
    matches
}

            year: Some(2006),
            original_language: Some("es".to_string()),
            runtime: Some(119),
            imdb_id: Some("tt0001417".to_string()),
            tvdb_id: None,
            seasons: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    fn season(season_number: u32, episode_count: u32) -> TmdbSeason {
        TmdbSeason { season_number, episode_count: Some(episode_count), episodes: Vec::new() }
    }

    fn episode(episode_number: u32, name: &str, runtime: Option<u32>) -> TmdbEpisode {
        TmdbEpisode { episode_number, name: Some(name.to_string()), runtime }
    }

    fn the_office() -> TmdbRecord {
        TmdbRecord {
            identity: TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::Tv, id: 2316 },
            title: "The Office".to_string(),
            original_title: "The Office".to_string(),
            year: Some(2005),
            original_language: Some("en".to_string()),
            runtime: None,
            imdb_id: Some("tt0002316".to_string()),
            tvdb_id: Some(102316),
            seasons: vec![season(0, 26), season(1, 6), season(2, 22), season(3, 25)],
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_search_answer_keeps_movie_and_tv_results_and_drops_other_media_types() {
        let search = parse_search(SEARCH, "search.json").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            search.results,
            vec![
                TmdbSearchResult {
                    media_type: "movie".to_string(),
                    id: 1417,
                    title: Some("Pan's Labyrinth".to_string()),
                    name: None,
                    original_title: Some("El laberinto del fauno".to_string()),
                    original_name: None,
                    release_date: Some("2006-10-11".to_string()),
                    first_air_date: None,
                },
                TmdbSearchResult {
                    media_type: "tv".to_string(),
                    id: 2316,
                    title: None,
                    name: Some("The Office".to_string()),
                    original_title: None,
                    original_name: Some("The Office".to_string()),
                    release_date: None,
                    first_air_date: Some("2005-03-24".to_string()),
                },
            ]
        );
        // Movies and TV are searched together, and an identity is the pair of kind and ID (spec 8.1).
        let identities: Vec<Option<TmdbIdentity>> = search.results.iter().map(TmdbSearchResult::identity).collect();
        assert_eq!(
            identities,
            vec![Some(TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::Movie, id: 1417 }), Some(TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::Tv, id: 2316 })]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_search_result_reads_its_title_original_and_year_by_its_media_type() {
        let search = parse_search(SEARCH, "search.json").unwrap();
        let (movie, show) = (&search.results[0], &search.results[1]);
        assert_eq!((movie.display_title(), movie.original(), movie.year()), ("Pan's Labyrinth", "El laberinto del fauno", Some(2006)));
        assert_eq!((show.display_title(), show.original(), show.year()), ("The Office", "The Office", Some(2005)));
        // A movie's name and first_air_date are not its title and date; a missing one reads as "" or None.
        let crossed = TmdbSearchResult {
            media_type: "movie".to_string(),
            id: 1,
            title: None,
            name: Some("Name".to_string()),
            original_title: None,
            original_name: Some("Name".to_string()),
            release_date: None,
            first_air_date: Some("2001-01-01".to_string()),
        };
        assert_eq!((crossed.display_title(), crossed.original(), crossed.year()), ("", "", None));
        let other = TmdbSearchResult { media_type: "person".to_string(), ..crossed.clone() };
        assert_eq!((other.identity(), other.display_title(), other.original(), other.year()), (None, "", "", None));
        // The year is the four digits before the date's first '-'.
        for (date, year) in
            [("2006-10-11", Some(2006)), ("2006", Some(2006)), ("", None), ("206-10-11", None), ("20o6-10-11", None), ("10/11/2006", None)]
        {
            let result = TmdbSearchResult { release_date: Some(date.to_string()), ..crossed.clone() };
            assert_eq!(result.year(), year, "{date:?}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_search_answer_without_results_is_empty_and_a_malformed_one_is_refused() {
        let none = r#"{"page": 1, "results": [], "total_pages": 0, "total_results": 0}"#;
        assert_eq!(parse_search(none, "search.json"), Ok(TmdbSearch::default()));
        assert_eq!(parse_search("\u{feff}{}", "search.json"), Ok(TmdbSearch::default()));
        // A result whose media type is not movie or tv is dropped before it is read, whatever its shape.
        let dropped = r#"{"results": [{"media_type": "person"}, {"name": "no media type"}]}"#;
        assert_eq!(parse_search(dropped, "search.json"), Ok(TmdbSearch::default()));
        let empty = parse_search("", "search.json").unwrap_err();
        assert!(empty.starts_with("search.json: EOF while parsing"), "{empty}");
        let no_id = parse_search(r#"{"results": [{"media_type": "movie", "title": "Untitled"}]}"#, "search.json").unwrap_err();
        assert!(no_id.starts_with("search.json: missing field `id`"), "{no_id}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_movie_record_reads_title_year_language_runtime_and_external_ids() {
        assert_eq!(parse_movie(MOVIE, "movie.json"), Ok(pans_labyrinth()));
        assert_eq!(parse_movie(&format!("\u{feff}{MOVIE}"), "movie.json"), Ok(pans_labyrinth()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_movie_record_falls_back_to_its_top_level_imdb_id_and_reads_unknown_values_as_none() {
        let bare = r#"{"id": 1417, "title": "Pan's Labyrinth", "imdb_id": "tt0001417", "runtime": null, "release_date": "2006-10-11"}"#;
        assert_eq!(
            parse_movie(bare, "movie.json"),
            Ok(TmdbRecord {
                original_title: "Pan's Labyrinth".to_string(),
                original_language: None,
                runtime: None,
                ..pans_labyrinth()
            })
        );
        // TMDb writes 0 minutes and empty strings for what it does not know (Review Focus 2: no runtime, no pass).
        let unknown = r#"{"id": 1417, "title": "Pan's Labyrinth", "original_title": " ", "original_language": "", "release_date": "",
            "runtime": 0, "imdb_id": "", "external_ids": {"imdb_id": null, "tvdb_id": null}}"#;
        assert_eq!(
            parse_movie(unknown, "movie.json"),
            Ok(TmdbRecord {
                original_title: "Pan's Labyrinth".to_string(),
                year: None,
                original_language: None,
                runtime: None,
                imdb_id: None,
                ..pans_labyrinth()
            })
        );
        // The embedded external_ids win over the top-level imdb_id.
        let both = r#"{"id": 1417, "title": "Pan's Labyrinth", "imdb_id": "tt0000001", "external_ids": {"imdb_id": "tt0001417"}}"#;
        assert_eq!(parse_movie(both, "movie.json").unwrap().imdb_id.as_deref(), Some("tt0001417"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_record_without_a_title_or_a_name_or_an_id_is_refused() {
        assert_eq!(
            parse_movie(r#"{"id": 1417, "title": ""}"#, "movie.json"),
            Err("movie.json: the movie record 1417 has no title".to_string())
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parse_tv(r#"{"id": 2316, "title": "The Office"}"#, "tv.json"),
            Err("tv.json: the TV record 2316 has no name".to_string())
        );
        let no_id = parse_movie(r#"{"title": "Pan's Labyrinth"}"#, "movie.json").unwrap_err();
        assert!(no_id.starts_with("movie.json: missing field `id`"), "{no_id}");
        let broken = parse_tv("{", "tv.json").unwrap_err();
        assert!(broken.starts_with("tv.json: EOF while parsing"), "{broken}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_tv_record_reads_its_seasons_and_its_imdb_and_tvdb_ids() {
        let record = parse_tv(TV, "tv.json").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(record, the_office());
        assert_eq!(record.season(3), Some(&season(3, 25)));
        assert_eq!(record.season(4), None);
        // A /tv answer whose seasons already hold their episodes (a merged answer, a test fixture) reads them too.
        let expanded = r#"{"id": 2316, "name": "The Office", "seasons": [{"season_number": 3, "episode_count": 2, "episodes": [
            {"episode_number": 12, "name": "Traveling Salesmen", "runtime": 22}, {"episode_number": 13, "name": "The Return", "runtime": 0}]}]}"#;
        let record = parse_tv(expanded, "tv.json").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            record.seasons,
            vec![TmdbSeason {
                season_number: 3,
                episode_count: Some(2),
                episodes: vec![episode(12, "Traveling Salesmen", Some(22)), episode(13, "The Return", None)],
            }]
        );
        assert_eq!((record.original_title.as_str(), record.year, record.imdb_id, record.tvdb_id), ("The Office", None, None, None));
        // A TVDB ID of 0 or less is no ID.
        assert_eq!(parse_tv(r#"{"id": 2316, "name": "The Office", "external_ids": {"tvdb_id": 0}}"#, "tv.json").unwrap().tvdb_id, None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_season_answer_merges_its_episodes_into_the_tv_record() {
        let mut record = parse_tv(TV, "tv.json").unwrap();
        merge_season(&mut record, SEASON_3, "season-3.json").unwrap();
        let episodes = vec![
            episode(12, "Traveling Salesmen", Some(22)),
            episode(13, "The Return", Some(22)),
            episode(14, "Ben Franklin", None),
            episode(15, "Phyllis' Wedding", None),
        ];
        assert_eq!(record.season(3), Some(&TmdbSeason { season_number: 3, episode_count: Some(25), episodes }));
        // Merging again replaces that season's episodes; the other seasons are untouched.
        let again = r#"{"season_number": 3, "episodes": [{"episode_number": 12, "name": "Traveling Salesmen", "runtime": 23}]}"#;
        merge_season(&mut record, again, "season-3.json").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(record.season(3).map(|season| season.episodes.clone()), Some(vec![episode(12, "Traveling Salesmen", Some(23))]));
        assert_eq!(record.seasons.iter().map(|season| season.season_number).collect::<Vec<u32>>(), vec![0, 1, 2, 3]);
        assert!(record.seasons.iter().filter(|season| season.season_number != 3).all(|season| season.episodes.is_empty()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_season_answer_for_a_season_the_record_lacks_is_added_in_season_order() {
        let mut record = TmdbRecord { seasons: vec![season(1, 6), season(3, 25)], ..the_office() };
        let season_2 = r#"{"season_number": 2, "episodes": [{"episode_number": 1, "name": "The Dundies", "runtime": 22},
            {"episode_number": 2, "name": "Sexual Harassment"}]}"#;
        merge_season(&mut record, season_2, "season-2.json").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(record.seasons.iter().map(|season| season.season_number).collect::<Vec<u32>>(), vec![1, 2, 3]);
        assert_eq!(
            record.season(2),
            Some(&TmdbSeason {
                season_number: 2,
                episode_count: Some(2),
                episodes: vec![episode(1, "The Dundies", Some(22)), episode(2, "Sexual Harassment", None)],
            })
        );
        // A listed season without an episode count takes the count of the episodes merged.
        let mut record = TmdbRecord { seasons: vec![TmdbSeason { season_number: 3, episode_count: None, episodes: Vec::new() }], ..the_office() };
        merge_season(&mut record, SEASON_3, "season-3.json").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(record.season(3).and_then(|season| season.episode_count), Some(4));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_season_answer_cannot_be_merged_into_a_movie_record_or_be_malformed() {
        let mut movie = pans_labyrinth();
        assert_eq!(
            merge_season(&mut movie, SEASON_3, "season-3.json"),
            Err("season-3.json: a season answer belongs to a TV record, not to movie 1417".to_string())
        );
        assert_eq!(movie, pans_labyrinth());
        let mut show = the_office();
        let no_number = merge_season(&mut show, r#"{"episodes": []}"#, "season.json").unwrap_err();
        assert!(no_number.starts_with("season.json: missing field `season_number`"), "{no_number}");
        assert_eq!(show, the_office());
    }

    #[test]
    fn episode_runtimes_are_one_seasons_or_every_regular_seasons() {
        let record = TmdbRecord {
            seasons: vec![
                TmdbSeason { season_number: 0, episode_count: Some(1), episodes: vec![episode(1, "The Accountants", Some(5))] },
                TmdbSeason {
                    season_number: 1,
                    episode_count: Some(2),
                    episodes: vec![episode(1, "Pilot", Some(23)), episode(2, "Diversity Day", Some(22))],
                },
                TmdbSeason {
                    season_number: 3,
                    episode_count: Some(3),
                    episodes: vec![
                        episode(12, "Traveling Salesmen", Some(22)),
                        episode(14, "Ben Franklin", None),
                        episode(13, "The Return", Some(21)),
                    ],
                },
            ],
            ..the_office()
        };
        // One season's runtimes in the answer's order, without the unknown ones.
        assert_eq!(record.episode_runtimes(Some(3)), vec![22, 21]);
        assert_eq!(record.episode_runtimes(Some(0)), vec![5]);
        assert_eq!(record.episode_runtimes(Some(2)), Vec::<u32>::new());
        // The whole series (no season parsed, spec 8.1): every regular season in order, without season 0's specials.
        assert_eq!(record.episode_runtimes(None), vec![23, 22, 22, 21]);
        assert_eq!(pans_labyrinth().episode_runtimes(None), Vec::<u32>::new());
    }

    #[test]
    fn work_takes_title_year_and_ids_from_the_same_record() {
        assert_eq!(
            pans_labyrinth().work(),
            Work {
                kind: TmdbKind::Movie,
                tmdb_id: 1417,

    #[test]
    fn the_testsupport_builders_parse_through_the_same_parsers() {
        let text = tmdb_movie_json(1417, "Pan's Labyrinth", "El laberinto del fauno", "2006-10-11", "es", Some(119));

        assert_eq!(

                (Some(TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::Tv, id: 2316 }), "The Office", "The Office", Some(2005)),
            ]

    }

/// One `/search/multi` result: `media_type` "movie" or "tv" (a "person" result is dropped by the parser). Spec 8.1.
/// Def: T3. Use: T4.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct TmdbSearchResult {
    pub media_type: String,
    pub id: i64,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub title: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub name: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub original_title: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub original_name: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub release_date: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub first_air_date: Option<String>,
}

impl TmdbSearchResult {
    /// The (kind, ID) pair of a movie or tv result; None for any other media type. Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T4.
    pub fn identity(&self) -> Option<TmdbIdentity> {
        Some(TmdbIdentity { kind: self.kind()?, id: self.id })
    }

    /// `title` for a movie, `name` for tv; "" when absent (or for another media type). Spec 8.1. Def: T3.
    pub fn display_title(&self) -> &str {
        let text = match self.kind() {
            Some(TmdbKind::Movie) => &self.title,
            Some(TmdbKind::Tv) => &self.name,
            None => return "",
        };
        text.as_deref().unwrap_or("")
    }

    /// `original_title` for a movie, `original_name` for tv; "" when absent (or for another media type). Spec 8.1
    /// "its title or original title". Def: T3.
    pub fn original(&self) -> &str {
        let text = match self.kind() {
            Some(TmdbKind::Movie) => &self.original_title,
            Some(TmdbKind::Tv) => &self.original_name,
            None => return "",
        };
        text.as_deref().unwrap_or("")
    }

    /// The year of release_date (a movie) or first_air_date (tv): the four digits before the first '-'. Spec 8.1.
    /// Def: T3.
    pub fn year(&self) -> Option<i32> {
        match self.kind()? {
            TmdbKind::Movie => year_of(self.release_date.as_deref()),
            TmdbKind::Tv => year_of(self.first_air_date.as_deref()),
        }
    }

    /// The media type as a TMDb kind; None for "person" and any other.
    fn kind(&self) -> Option<TmdbKind> {
        self.media_type.parse().ok()
    }
}

/// The first page of `/search/multi` (8.1 "Only the first page of results is considered"). Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T4,
/// T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct TmdbSearch {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub results: Vec<TmdbSearchResult>,
}

/// Parses the answer, keeping movie and tv results only (a result of another media type is dropped before it is read);
/// the page number and totals are not read. Err is serde_json's message prefixed by `shown`. Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T15.
pub fn parse_search(text: &str, shown: &str) -> Result<TmdbSearch, String> {
    #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
    struct Page {
        #[serde(default)]
        results: Vec<Value>,
    }
    let page: Page = parse_json(text, shown)?;
    let mut results: Vec<TmdbSearchResult> = Vec::new();
    for result in page.results {
        if matches!(result.get("media_type").and_then(Value::as_str), Some("movie") | Some("tv")) {
            results.push(serde_json::from_value(result).map_err(|error| format!("{shown}: {error}"))?);
        }
    }
    Ok(TmdbSearch { results })
}

/// One episode of `/tv/{id}/season/{n}`: `runtime` minutes may be null; 0 reads as None (parse_tv, merge_season).
/// Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T6.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct TmdbEpisode {
    pub episode_number: u32,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub name: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub runtime: Option<u32>,
}

/// One season: `season_number` (0 is specials), `episode_count`, and the episodes once the season call is merged in
/// (empty until then). Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T4, T6.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct TmdbSeason {
    pub season_number: u32,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub episode_count: Option<u32>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub episodes: Vec<TmdbEpisode>,
}

/// The TMDb record 8.1 fetches: title, year, original language, runtime, the IMDb and TVDB IDs and, for TV, seasons and
/// episodes with runtimes. Read from `/movie/{id}` (`title`, `release_date`, `runtime`), `/tv/{id}` (`name`,
/// `first_air_date`, `seasons`), their `external_ids`, and the recording's slim `tmdb.json` (which has no runtime and no
/// seasons). Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T4 to T7, T11, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct TmdbRecord {
    pub identity: TmdbIdentity,
    /// `title` or `name`.
    pub title: String,
    /// `original_title` or `original_name` (the title when TMDb gives none).
    pub original_title: String,
    /// The year of `release_date` or `first_air_date`; None when absent.
    pub year: Option<i32>,
    /// `original_language`, two letters ("es", "en", "xx").
    pub original_language: Option<String>,
    /// `runtime` minutes (movies); None when TMDb has none (null or 0).
    pub runtime: Option<u32>,
    /// `external_ids.imdb_id` ("tt0001417") and `external_ids.tvdb_id`.
    pub imdb_id: Option<String>,
    pub tvdb_id: Option<i64>,
    /// TV only; empty for a movie.
    pub seasons: Vec<TmdbSeason>,
}

impl TmdbRecord {
    /// The season with `season_number == n`. Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T4, T6, T7.
    pub fn season(&self, n: u32) -> Option<&TmdbSeason> {
        self.seasons.iter().find(|season| season.season_number == n)
    }

    /// Every episode runtime of season `n`, or of every season when `n` is None (8.1 "of the whole series when no season
    /// was parsed"; the whole series is every season numbered 1 or more, without season 0's specials), in the record's
    /// order, leaving out episodes without a runtime. Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T4.
    pub fn episode_runtimes(&self, season: Option<u32>) -> Vec<u32> {
        self.seasons
            .iter()
            .filter(|listed| match season {
                Some(n) => listed.season_number == n,
                None => listed.season_number != 0,
            })
            .flat_map(|listed| listed.episodes.iter().filter_map(|episode| episode.runtime))
            .collect()
    }

    /// Spec 8.9 "Title and year always come from the same TMDb record as the ID": the Work for naming. Def: T3. Use: T11,
    /// T13.
    pub fn work(&self) -> Work {
        Work {
            kind: self.identity.kind,
            tmdb_id: self.identity.id,
            title: self.title.clone(),
            year: self.year,
            imdb_id: self.imdb_id.clone(),
            tvdb_id: self.tvdb_id,
        }
    }
}

/// Title, year and IDs from one TMDb record, as naming reads them (8.9). Spec 8.9. Def: T3. Use: T11, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Work {
    pub kind: TmdbKind,
    pub tmdb_id: i64,
    pub title: String,
    pub year: Option<i32>,
    pub imdb_id: Option<String>,
    pub tvdb_id: Option<i64>,
}

/// The external IDs `append_to_response=external_ids` embeds; their other keys (wikidata_id, facebook_id) are not read.
#[derive(Default, serde::Deserialize)]
struct RawExternalIds {
    #[serde(default)]
    imdb_id: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    tvdb_id: Option<i64>,
}

/// The keys of `/movie/{id}` and `/tv/{id}` a record reads; every other key is ignored.
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct RawRecord {
    id: i64,
    #[serde(default)]
    title: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    name: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    original_title: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    original_name: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    release_date: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    first_air_date: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    original_language: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    runtime: Option<u32>,
    #[serde(default)]
    imdb_id: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    external_ids: Option<RawExternalIds>,
    #[serde(default)]
    seasons: Vec<TmdbSeason>,
}

/// `/movie/{id}` text (with `external_ids` appended or embedded as `append_to_response` gives it): the IMDb ID from
/// `external_ids.imdb_id`, else the top-level `imdb_id`; a runtime of 0 is None. Err without a title. Spec 8.1. Def: T3.
/// Use: T15.
pub fn parse_movie(text: &str, shown: &str) -> Result<TmdbRecord, String> {
    let raw: RawRecord = parse_json(text, shown)?;
    let id = raw.id;
    let title = present(raw.title).ok_or_else(|| format!("{shown}: the movie record {id} has no title"))?;
    let original_title = present(raw.original_title).unwrap_or_else(|| title.clone());
    let (imdb_id, tvdb_id) = external_ids(raw.external_ids, raw.imdb_id);
    Ok(TmdbRecord {
        identity: TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::Movie, id },
        title,
        original_title,
        year: year_of(raw.release_date.as_deref()),
        original_language: present(raw.original_language),
        runtime: known_minutes(raw.runtime),
        imdb_id,
        tvdb_id,
        seasons: Vec::new(),
    })
}

/// `/tv/{id}` text; `seasons[].episodes` are read when present (a test fixture or a merged season call), an episode
/// runtime of 0 as None. Err without a name. Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T15.
pub fn parse_tv(text: &str, shown: &str) -> Result<TmdbRecord, String> {
    let raw: RawRecord = parse_json(text, shown)?;
    let id = raw.id;
    let title = present(raw.name).ok_or_else(|| format!("{shown}: the TV record {id} has no name"))?;
    let original_title = present(raw.original_name).unwrap_or_else(|| title.clone());
    let (imdb_id, tvdb_id) = external_ids(raw.external_ids, raw.imdb_id);
    let seasons = raw
        .seasons
        .into_iter()
        .map(|season| TmdbSeason { episodes: season.episodes.into_iter().map(known_episode).collect(), ..season })
        .collect();
    Ok(TmdbRecord {
        identity: TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::Tv, id },
        title,
        original_title,
        year: year_of(raw.first_air_date.as_deref()),
        original_language: present(raw.original_language),
        runtime: None,
        imdb_id,
        tvdb_id,
        seasons,
    })
}

/// A season answer merged into `record.seasons` (replacing that season's episodes; a season the record lacks is added
/// and the seasons kept in number order; an absent episode_count takes the count merged). Err for a movie record, before
/// the text is read, and for a malformed answer. Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: none in phase 1 (phase 2's TMDb client merges
/// its season calls).
pub fn merge_season(record: &mut TmdbRecord, season_text: &str, shown: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
    struct SeasonAnswer {
        season_number: u32,
        #[serde(default)]
        episodes: Vec<TmdbEpisode>,
    }
    if record.identity.kind != TmdbKind::Tv {
        return Err(format!("{shown}: a season answer belongs to a TV record, not to movie {}", record.identity.id));
    }
    let answer: SeasonAnswer = parse_json(season_text, shown)?;
    let episodes: Vec<TmdbEpisode> = answer.episodes.into_iter().map(known_episode).collect();
    let count = u32::try_from(episodes.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
    if let Some(season) = record.seasons.iter_mut().find(|season| season.season_number == answer.season_number) {
        season.episode_count = season.episode_count.or(Some(count));
        season.episodes = episodes;
        return Ok(());
    }
    record.seasons.push(TmdbSeason { season_number: answer.season_number, episode_count: Some(count), episodes });
    record.seasons.sort_by_key(|season| season.season_number);
    Ok(())
}

/// The IMDb ID (the embedded `external_ids.imdb_id`, else the top-level one) and the TVDB ID (positive only).
fn external_ids(ids: Option<RawExternalIds>, top_level_imdb: Option<String>) -> (Option<String>, Option<i64>) {
    let ids = ids.unwrap_or_default();
    (present(ids.imdb_id).or_else(|| present(top_level_imdb)), ids.tvdb_id.filter(|&tvdb| tvdb > 0))
}

/// Text that holds something other than white space, trimmed; None for absent, empty or blank text.
fn present(text: Option<String>) -> Option<String> {
    text.map(|text| text.trim().to_string()).filter(|text| !text.is_empty())
}

/// The year of a TMDb date ("2006-10-11"): the four ASCII digits before the first '-'; None otherwise.
fn year_of(date: Option<&str>) -> Option<i32> {
    let year = date?.split('-').next()?;
    if year.len() == 4 && year.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit()) {
        year.parse().ok()
    } else {
        None
    }
}

/// A runtime in minutes, with TMDb's 0 for "unknown" read as None.
fn known_minutes(minutes: Option<u32>) -> Option<u32> {
    minutes.filter(|&minutes| minutes > 0)
}

/// An episode with `known_minutes` of its runtime.
fn known_episode(episode: TmdbEpisode) -> TmdbEpisode {
    TmdbEpisode { runtime: known_minutes(episode.runtime), ..episode }
}
```

```rust
/// tmdb.json, slimmed: original_language and fetched_at, as the text rule reads them (subtitle::text::subs_run), and the
/// record's id, title (a movie) or name (a TV show), original title or name, release or first-air date and external IDs,
/// which `lookup::tmdb::parse_recorded` maps to a record (spec 8.1). The record's fields are lenient: a value of another
/// type reads as None, never as an error, so every file the text rule read before they were added still reads.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Tmdb {
    pub original_language: Option<String>,
    pub fetched_at: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = "lenient_i64")]
    pub id: Option<i64>,
    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = "lenient_string")]
    pub title: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = "lenient_string")]
    pub name: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = "lenient_string")]
    pub original_title: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = "lenient_string")]
    pub original_name: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = "lenient_string")]
    pub release_date: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = "lenient_string")]
    pub first_air_date: Option<String>,
    /// `imdb_id` (a string), `tvdb_id` (a number) and keys no rule reads (`wikidata_id`).
    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = "lenient_object")]
    pub external_ids: Option<serde_json::Map<String, Value>>,
}

/// A tmdb.json field that is a whole number, else None.
fn lenient_i64<'de, D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Option<i64>, D::Error> {
    Ok(<Value as serde::Deserialize>::deserialize(deserializer)?.as_i64())
}

/// A tmdb.json field that is a string, else None.
fn lenient_string<'de, D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Option<String>, D::Error> {
    Ok(match <Value as serde::Deserialize>::deserialize(deserializer)? {
        Value::String(text) => Some(text),
        _ => None,
    })
}

/// A tmdb.json field that is an object, else None.
fn lenient_object<'de, D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(
    deserializer: D,
) -> Result<Option<serde_json::Map<String, Value>>, D::Error> {
    Ok(match <Value as serde::Deserialize>::deserialize(deserializer)? {
        Value::Object(map) => Some(map),
        _ => None,
    })
}

```rust
/// The recording's slim `tmdb.json`, read as `recording::files::Tmdb` (extended by this task with the optional fields
/// `id`, `title`, `name`, `original_title`, `original_name`, `release_date`, `first_air_date: Option<String>` and
/// `external_ids: Option<serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>>`, read leniently: a value of another type is None,
/// never an error; unknown keys stay ignored and its existing readers are untouched), then mapped: a movie when it has
/// `title`, tv when it has `name`; `fetched_at` is ignored. No runtime and no seasons (the slim file has neither); the IMDb
/// ID is `external_ids.imdb_id`, the TVDB ID `external_ids.tvdb_id`.
/// Err without an id, or with neither a title nor a name. Spec 8.1. Def: T3. Use: T15.
pub fn parse_recorded(text: &str, shown: &str) -> Result<TmdbRecord, String> {
    let slim: Tmdb = parse_json(text, shown)?;
    let id = slim.id.ok_or_else(|| format!("{shown}: the record has no id"))?;
    let ids = slim.external_ids.unwrap_or_default();
    let imdb_id = present(ids.get("imdb_id").and_then(Value::as_str).map(str::to_string));
    let tvdb_id = ids.get("tvdb_id").and_then(Value::as_i64).filter(|&tvdb| tvdb > 0);
    let (kind, title, original, date) = match (present(slim.title), present(slim.name)) {
        (Some(title), _) => (TmdbKind::Movie, title, slim.original_title, slim.release_date),
        (None, Some(name)) => (TmdbKind::Tv, name, slim.original_name, slim.first_air_date),
        (None, None) => {
            return Err(format!("{shown}: the record has neither a title (a movie) nor a name (a TV show)"));
        }
    };
    let original_title = present(original).unwrap_or_else(|| title.clone());
    Ok(TmdbRecord {
        identity: TmdbIdentity { kind, id },
        title,
        original_title,
        year: year_of(date.as_deref()),
        original_language: present(slim.original_language),
        runtime: None,
        imdb_id,
        tvdb_id,
        seasons: Vec::new(),
    })
}

The test reads the answers' format, disc number, titles and item names from those files at run time (RP21) and asserts as literals only what the Expected plans table publishes: on the Office disc the database index and the scan title number part from index 4 on (index 4, `00000.mpls(1)` of 23 seconds, is not in the scan, which lists no title shorter than MakeMKV's minimum length; nor are indices 12 and 13), so the matching cannot lean on the numbers.

```rust
//! TheDiscDB's and TMDb's recorded answers in the evidence clone through `lazymkv_core::lookup` (spec 8.1, last
//! bullet: "the owner's 2 recorded answers"; spec 8.3, first paragraph): the two `thediscdb-hash.json` hits parse and
//! their titles match the recordings' scans, the empty answers read as misses, the slim `tmdb.json` files map to
//! records, and the 18 API answers with the 2 recorded ones hold the track counts spec 8.1 states. Every test skips with
//! its reason when the clone is absent (it is git-ignored and not on CI), never failing for the missing input.

use std::collections::BTreeSet;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use lazymkv_core::disc::{disc, StreamKind};
use lazymkv_core::lookup::discdb::{match_titles, parse_dischash, parse_discid, DiscDbRecord};
use lazymkv_core::lookup::tmdb::{parse_recorded, TmdbIdentity, TmdbKind, TmdbRecord};
use lazymkv_core::lookup::Kind;
use lazymkv_core::robot::parse;
use lazymkv_dev::evidence::{repo_root, resolve_evidence, skip, Ctx};

/// The evidence clone as every dev command finds it (`resolve_evidence`: LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE, else corpus/owner under the
/// repository root), or None after printing the skip line with the refusal's text.
fn evidence() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    match resolve_evidence(&Ctx::from_process(), None) {
        Ok(root) => Some(root),
        Err(refused) => {
            skip(&format!("no evidence clone: {}", refused.line));
            None
        }
    }
}

fn text(path: &Path) -> String {
    let bytes = std::fs::read(path).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{}: {error}", path.display()));
    String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes).into_owned()
}

/// A recording's thediscdb-hash.json, which must be a hit.
fn recorded_hit(root: &Path, slug: &str) -> DiscDbRecord {
    let path = root.join(slug).join("thediscdb-hash.json");
    parse_dischash(&text(&path), &path.display().to_string()).unwrap().unwrap()
}

fn indices(titles: Vec<&lazymkv_core::lookup::discdb::DiscDbTitle>) -> Vec<u32> {
    titles.iter().map(|title| title.index).collect()
}

#[test]
fn the_two_recorded_dischash_answers_parse_and_match_their_scans() {
    let Some(root) = evidence() else { return };

    let pans = recorded_hit(&root, "pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd");
    assert_eq!(pans.kind(), Some(Kind::Movie));
    assert_eq!(pans.tmdb_identity(), Some(TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::Movie, id: 1417 }));
    assert_eq!(pans.title_and_year(), Some(("Pan's Labyrinth".to_string(), Some(2006))));
    // The format, disc number, title count and title items are read from the recorded file at run time (RP21).
    let pans_raw = raw_json(&root.join("pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd/thediscdb-hash.json"));
    assert_eq!((pans.format.clone(), pans.disc_number(), pans.titles.len()), raw_head(&pans_raw));
    assert_eq!(indices(pans.main_movies()), vec![0]);
    let pans_scan = disc(&parse(&text(&root.join("pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd/scan.txt")))).unwrap();
    // The Expected plans table publishes database title 0 as scan title 0; every MainMovie or Episode title matches.
    let pans_matched = match_titles(&pans, &pans_scan);
    assert_eq!(pans_matched.get(&0), Some(&0), "{pans_matched:?}");
    for index in raw_indices_of(&pans_raw, "MainMovie").into_iter().chain(raw_indices_of(&pans_raw, "Episode")) {
        assert!(pans_matched.contains_key(&index), "database title {index} matches no scan title: {pans_matched:?}");
    }

    let office = recorded_hit(&root, "the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray");
    assert_eq!(office.kind(), Some(Kind::Tv));
    assert_eq!(office.tmdb_identity(), Some(TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::Tv, id: 2316 }));
    assert_eq!(office.title_and_year(), Some(("The Office".to_string(), Some(2005))));
    let office_raw = raw_json(&root.join("the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray/thediscdb-hash.json"));
    assert_eq!((office.format.clone(), office.disc_number(), office.titles.len()), raw_head(&office_raw));
    let episodes = raw_indices_of(&office_raw, "Episode");
    assert_eq!(indices(office.episodes()), episodes);
    // The Expected plans table maps six episode titles.
    assert_eq!(episodes.len(), 6);
    assert!(office.main_movies().is_empty());
    let double = office.titles.iter().find(|title| title.index == 3).and_then(|title| title.item.as_ref()).unwrap();
    // Season 3 and episodes 12-13 are published by the Expected plans table; the item's name is the file's.
    assert_eq!((double.season.as_deref(), double.episode.as_deref()), (Some("3"), Some("12-13")));
    let double_raw = raw_titles(&office_raw).iter().find(|title| raw_index(title) == Some(3)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(Some(double.title.clone()), string_at(double_raw, "/item/title"));
    let office_scan = disc(&parse(&text(&root.join("the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray/scan.txt")))).unwrap();
    // Values are read from the recorded file at run time (RP21). MakeMKV title numbers are never used for matching
    // (spec 8.3); the Expected plans table publishes the scan titles of the six episodes.
    let matched = match_titles(&office, &office_scan);
    let in_file: BTreeSet<u32> = raw_titles(&office_raw).iter().filter_map(raw_index).collect();
    assert!(matched.keys().all(|index| in_file.contains(index)), "{matched:?}");
    assert!(episodes.iter().all(|index| matched.contains_key(index)), "{matched:?}");
    let episode_scans: BTreeSet<u32> = episodes.iter().map(|index| matched[index]).collect();
    assert_eq!(episode_scans, BTreeSet::from([0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6]));
    let scans: BTreeSet<&u32> = matched.values().collect();
    assert_eq!(scans.len(), matched.len(), "a scan title is matched twice: {matched:?}");
}

#[test]
fn the_recorded_empty_answers_read_as_misses() {
    let Some(root) = evidence() else { return };
    for slug in ["short-circuit-1986-dvd", "short-circuit-2-1988-dvd"] {
        let path = root.join(slug).join("thediscdb-hash.json");
        assert_eq!(parse_dischash(&text(&path), &path.display().to_string()), Ok(None), "{}", path.display());
    }
    for slug in ["pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd", "the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray"] {
        let path = root.join(slug).join("thediscdb-discid.json");
        assert_eq!(parse_discid(&text(&path), &path.display().to_string()), Ok(Vec::new()), "{}", path.display());
    }
}

/// A recorded tmdb.json or thediscdb-hash.json as raw JSON (a leading byte-order mark dropped), so the fields no public
/// source gives (the original title, the IMDb and TVDB IDs, TheDiscDB's format, disc number, titles and item names) are
/// compared with the file itself when the test runs, never written here as values copied from the private clone
/// (ruling RP21).
fn raw_json(path: &Path) -> serde_json::Value {
    serde_json::from_str(text(path).trim_start_matches('\u{feff}'))
        .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{}: {error}", path.display()))
}

/// The `titles` array of a recorded thediscdb-hash.json, read raw.
fn raw_titles(value: &serde_json::Value) -> &Vec<serde_json::Value> {
    value.pointer("/titles").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array).expect("a dischash answer has a titles array")
}

/// A raw title's `index`.
fn raw_index(title: &serde_json::Value) -> Option<u32> {
    title.pointer("/index").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_u64).and_then(|index| u32::try_from(index).ok())
}

/// The indices of a recorded answer's titles whose item type is `item_type`, read raw, in index order.
fn raw_indices_of(value: &serde_json::Value, item_type: &str) -> Vec<u32> {
    let mut found: Vec<u32> = raw_titles(value)
        .iter()
        .filter(|title| string_at(title, "/item/type").as_deref() == Some(item_type))
        .filter_map(raw_index)
        .collect();
    found.sort_unstable();
    found
}

/// A recorded answer's format, disc number (`disc.index`) and title count, read raw.
fn raw_head(value: &serde_json::Value) -> (Option<String>, Option<i64>, usize) {
    let disc_number = value.pointer("/disc/index").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_i64);
    (string_at(value, "/format"), disc_number, raw_titles(value).len())
}

/// The string at `pointer` in `value`, or None.
fn string_at(value: &serde_json::Value, pointer: &str) -> Option<String> {
    value.pointer(pointer).and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).map(str::to_string)
}

#[test]
fn the_recorded_tmdb_json_files_map_to_their_records() {
    let Some(root) = evidence() else { return };
    let path = root.join("pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd/tmdb.json");
    let raw = raw_json(&path);
    let pans = parse_recorded(&text(&path), &path.display().to_string()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        pans,
        TmdbRecord {
            identity: TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::Movie, id: 1417 },
            title: "Pan's Labyrinth".to_string(),
            original_title: string_at(&raw, "/original_title").expect("the recorded movie has an original title"),
            year: Some(2006),
            original_language: Some("es".to_string()),
            runtime: None,
            imdb_id: string_at(&raw, "/external_ids/imdb_id"),
            tvdb_id: None,
            seasons: Vec::new(),
        }
    );
    // The embedded external ID is read, and the recorder kept one.
    assert!(pans.imdb_id.as_deref().is_some_and(|id| id.starts_with("tt")), "{:?}", pans.imdb_id);
    assert_ne!(pans.original_title, pans.title, "Pan's Labyrinth is a Spanish film with a Spanish original title");
    let path = root.join("the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray/tmdb.json");
    let raw = raw_json(&path);
    let office = parse_recorded(&text(&path), &path.display().to_string()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        office,
        TmdbRecord {
            identity: TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::Tv, id: 2316 },
            title: "The Office".to_string(),
            original_title: "The Office".to_string(),
            year: Some(2005),
            original_language: Some("en".to_string()),
            runtime: None,
            imdb_id: string_at(&raw, "/external_ids/imdb_id"),
            tvdb_id: raw.pointer("/external_ids/tvdb_id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_i64),
            seasons: Vec::new(),
        }
    );
    assert!(office.imdb_id.as_deref().is_some_and(|id| id.starts_with("tt")), "{:?}", office.imdb_id);
    assert!(office.tvdb_id.is_some_and(|id| id > 0), "{:?}", office.tvdb_id);
}

#[test]
fn the_api_answers_and_the_two_recorded_ones_hold_the_track_counts_spec_8_1_states() {
    let Some(root) = evidence() else { return };
    let api = repo_root(Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))).unwrap().join("corpus/thediscdb-api");
    let mut paths: Vec<PathBuf> = std::fs::read_dir(&api)
        .unwrap()
        .map(|entry| entry.unwrap().path())
        .filter(|path| path.extension().is_some_and(|extension| extension == "json"))
        .collect();
    paths.sort();
    assert_eq!(paths.len(), 18);
    let mut records: Vec<DiscDbRecord> = Vec::new();
    for path in &paths {
        let shown = path.display().to_string();
        if path.file_name().is_some_and(|name| name.to_string_lossy().starts_with("dischash-")) {
            records.push(parse_dischash(&text(path), &shown).unwrap().unwrap());
        } else {
            records.extend(parse_discid(&text(path), &shown).unwrap());
        }
    }
    records.push(recorded_hit(&root, "pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd"));
    records.push(recorded_hit(&root, "the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray"));
    let (mut audio, mut audio_described, mut subtitles, mut subtitles_described) = (0, 0, 0, 0);
    for track in records.iter().flat_map(|record| &record.titles).flat_map(|title| &title.tracks) {
        match track.kind() {
            Some(StreamKind::Audio) => {
                audio += 1;
                audio_described += usize::from(track.description.is_some());
            }
            Some(StreamKind::Subtitles) => {
                subtitles += 1;
                subtitles_described += usize::from(track.description.is_some());
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    // "An audio or subtitle track sometimes has description (58 of 877 audio and 30 of 2018 subtitle tracks)".
    assert_eq!((audio_described, audio, subtitles_described, subtitles), (58, 877, 30, 2018));
}

/// "Surround 7.1"; no channel count), `language_code` (three letters) and `language` ("English"); a subtitle track
/// `language_code` and `language`; `description` sometimes ("ENglish", "Spanish", "Director Commentary"). Def: T3. Use: T8, T9.

    #[serde(default, alias = "AspectRatio")] pub aspect_ratio: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "AudioType")] pub audio_type: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "LanguageCode")] pub language_code: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Language")] pub language: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, alias = "Description")] pub description: Option<String>,
}
impl DiscDbTrack {
    /// Video, Audio or Subtitles as a StreamKind; None for anything else. Def: T3. Use: T8.

    /// "Stereo" 2, "Surround 5.1" 6, "Surround 7.1" 8, "Mono" 1, "Surround 5.0" 5, "Surround 6.1" 7; None otherwise. Def: T3. Use: T8.
    pub fn channels(&self) -> Option<u32>;
}

/// `seasons`), their `external_ids`, and the recording's slim `tmdb.json` (which has no runtime and no seasons). Def: T3. Use: T4 to T7, T11, T13, T15.
