Produces (exactly the `core::lookup::name (Task 4)` and `core::lookup identification (Task 4, in lookup/mod.rs)` entries of the Shared interfaces, plus Task 4's line of the module root; Tasks 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13 and 15 rely on them):

```rust
// lazymkv_core::lookup module root (Task 4's line)
pub mod name;                          // Task 4

// lazymkv_core::lookup::name (Task 4)
/// Where the disc's own name came from (8.1 "the bdmt disc name, else the volume label"). Def: T4. Use: T4, T7.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum NameSource { Bdmt, VolumeLabel }

/// The disc's own name with the evidence parsed from it before cleaning. Def: T4. Use: T4 (identify), T5 (season marker), T6 (season), T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct DiscName {
    pub raw: String,
    pub source: NameSource,
    /// `parse_season(raw)`.
    pub season: Option<u32>,
    /// `parse_disc_number(raw)`.
    pub disc: Option<u32>,
    /// `clean(raw)`.
    pub cleaned: String,
    /// `is_generic(raw, cleaned)`.
    pub generic: bool,
    /// `has_season_marker(raw)` (8.2).
    pub season_marker: bool,
}
/// The bdmt name when Some and not blank, else the volume label when Some and not blank, else None. The caller builds it
/// once (`disc_name(bdmt, disc.volume_label.as_deref())`), searches TMDb with its `cleaned`, and passes it as
/// `LookupInputs.name`; `plan::plan` reads it from there and copies it into `PlanEvidence.name`. Def: T4. Use: T7 (tests), T15.
pub fn disc_name(bdmt: Option<&str>, volume_label: Option<&str>) -> Option<DiscName>;

/// A season number from `season N`, `series N`, `sN` or `sNN` (case-insensitive; `S3D3` gives 3; tokens split on spaces,
/// underscores, hyphens and the letter boundary of `S3D3`). Spec 8.1 "a season number and a disc number are parsed". Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub fn parse_season(raw: &str) -> Option<u32>;
/// A disc number from `disc N`, `disc_N`, `discN`, `dN`, `D1` (`CHERNOBYL_D1` gives 1, `S3D3` gives 3). Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub fn parse_disc_number(raw: &str) -> Option<u32>;
/// Spec 8.2: the name contains `season`, `series` or `s` followed by a number (as `parse_season` finds it). A disc number alone never counts. Def: T4. Use: T4, T5.
pub fn has_season_marker(raw: &str) -> bool;
/// Spec 8.1 "Cleaning": underscores to spaces; disc numbers (`DISC 1`, `D1`, `DISC_1`), season markers (`SEASON 3`, `S3`,
/// `S3D3`, `SERIES 2`), region and format tags (whole tokens, case-insensitive: UHD, 4K, BD, BD50, BLURAY, BLU-RAY, BDROM, DVD,
/// DVD9, NTSC, PAL, US, UK, EU, WW, DOM, INT, R1 to R6, RETAIL) and a trailing year (1900 to 2099 as the last token) removed;
/// repeated spaces collapsed; trimmed. A bare number that is not a tag stays (`EXPENDABLES_3` gives `EXPENDABLES 3`). Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub fn clean(raw: &str) -> String;
/// Spec 8.1: `DVD_VIDEO`, `DISC_1`, `LOGICAL_VOLUME_ID`, `VOLUME_SET_ID`, `BLURAY`, `BDROM`, `UNTITLED`, `UNDEFINED`, a cleaned name
/// that is empty, or one with no letter. Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub fn is_generic(raw: &str, cleaned: &str) -> bool;
pub const GENERIC_NAMES: [&str; 8];
/// Case-folded (Unicode lowercase), every character that is not alphanumeric or a space removed, spaces collapsed and trimmed
/// (`Pan's Labyrinth` and `PANS LABYRINTH` both give `pans labyrinth`). Spec 8.1 "after case-folding and removing punctuation".
/// It does not call `subtitle::text::fold` (ASCII folding for the text rule, other semantics). Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub fn fold_name(text: &str) -> String;
/// A result is plausible when `fold_name` of its title or original title equals `fold_name(cleaned)`. Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub fn plausible(result: &TmdbSearchResult, cleaned: &str) -> bool;

// lazymkv_core::lookup identification (Task 4, in lookup/mod.rs)
/// Spec 8.1's table rows, after the owner's review: Reviewed is spec 11's Set identity (8.8 "A review decision sets the
/// confidences it covers to 1.00"). Def: T4. Use: T7, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum IdentityStep { Reviewed, Remembered, DiscdbBoth, DiscdbOne, TmdbOne, TmdbSeveral, Nothing }
impl IdentityStep { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; pub const ALL: [IdentityStep; 7]; }

/// The confidence constants of 8.1 steps 1 to 6 and the cap of "When tmdb_only_autofile is off"; a review decision is
/// REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE too (1.00, 8.8). Def: T4. Use: T4, T7, T8, T10, T13.
pub const REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 1.00;
pub const DISCDB_BOTH_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.99;
pub const DISCDB_ONE_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.95;
pub const TMDB_ONE_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.90;
pub const TMDB_ONE_CAPPED_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.84;
pub const TMDB_SEVERAL_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.50;
pub const NOTHING_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.0;
/// (confidence, review reason) of a step: Reviewed and Remembered 1.00; reads settings.tmdb_only_autofile for TmdbOne (0.84
/// and IdentityAmbiguous when off); TmdbSeveral gives IdentityAmbiguous, Nothing gives IdentityUnknown. Def: T4. Use: T4, T7.
pub fn identity_confidence(step: IdentityStep, settings: &Settings) -> (f64, Option<ReviewReason>);

/// What the runtime checks compare against (8.1 "Runtime check"): the planned features' or cuts' durations (8.3, 8.4), the
/// longest rival when none is planned, and the durations of the disc's episode-length groups (8.2). The planner fills it
/// from the structural pass before the TMDb match (6.1 step 5's order). Def: T4. Use: T4, T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct RuntimeFacts { pub feature_seconds: Vec<u32>, pub longest_rival_seconds: Option<u32>, pub episode_group_seconds: Vec<u32> }

pub const MOVIE_RUNTIME_TOLERANCE: f64 = 0.03;
pub const TV_RUNTIME_TOLERANCE: f64 = 0.15;
/// Movies: at least one of `feature_seconds` (else `longest_rival_seconds`) within 3% of `runtime_min * 60`; false without a
/// runtime or without any duration. Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub fn movie_runtime_ok(facts: &RuntimeFacts, runtime_min: Option<u32>) -> bool;
/// TV: the median of `episode_runtimes_min` within 15% of the median of `episode_group_seconds / 60`; false when either list is
/// empty. The median of an even count is the mean of the two middle values. Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub fn tv_runtime_ok(facts: &RuntimeFacts, episode_runtimes_min: &[u32]) -> bool;
/// |a - b| <= tolerance * b. Def: T4. Use: T4, T5 (rule 4's 10%), T6 (suggest_by_runtime's 15%).
pub fn within(a: f64, b: f64, tolerance: f64) -> bool;

/// A TheDiscDB description's meaning (8.1 last bullet, D14, 8.7 "the one TheDiscDB describes as subtitles or SDH"):
/// "comment" gives Commentary; "audio desc", "descriptive", "DVS", "visually impaired" give AudioDescription; "SDH",
/// "hearing" give Sdh; "isolated score", "score only" give IsolatedScore; "music and effects", "music & effects", "M&E" give
/// MusicAndEffects; "subtitle", or a description that after trimming and case-folding equals the track's own `language`
/// (TheDiscDB's language name: "English"; Knowing's "ENglish" included), gives Dialogue. All case-insensitive, substring
/// matches, in this order; a text can carry several. IsolatedScore, MusicAndEffects and Dialogue are provisional: TheDiscDB's
/// wording for them is not yet known (8.1's last bullet names no such word; every subtitle description in the 18 answers
/// and the pinned files is a bare language name). Def: T4. Use: T8, T9, T10.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum DescriptionKind { Commentary, AudioDescription, Sdh, IsolatedScore, MusicAndEffects, Dialogue }
pub fn description_kinds(text: &str, language: Option<&str>) -> Vec<DescriptionKind>;

/// What the lookups gave (recorded, synthetic, or live in phase 2). `pending` flags say the answer is not in yet (8.1 "the
/// lookup is recorded as pending"). Def: T4. Use: T7, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct LookupInputs<'a> {
    /// The disc's own name, built by the caller with `name::disc_name` (a generic name is signalled by `DiscName.generic`, not by None).
    pub name: Option<&'a DiscName>,
    /// `/api/discid/{id}`: the first record of the array that has titles, or None (a miss, or no disc ID: a DVD).
    pub discdb_by_disc_id: Option<&'a DiscDbRecord>,
    /// `/api/dischash/{hash}`.
    pub discdb_by_fingerprint: Option<&'a DiscDbRecord>,
    pub discdb_pending: bool,
    /// The search 8.1 runs on the cleaned name (or on TheDiscDB's title and year when the entry has no TMDb ID).
    pub search: Option<&'a TmdbSearch>,
    /// The record fetched for the identity in hand.
    pub record: Option<&'a TmdbRecord>,
    pub tmdb_pending: bool,
    /// Step 1: the TMDb identity of a remembered decision for this fingerprint (`Remembered.tmdb`); plan::plan fills it from
    /// PlanInputs.remembered.
    pub remembered: Option<TmdbIdentity>,
    /// The owner's Set identity (spec 11), before step 1; plan::plan fills it from PlanInputs.overrides.
    pub reviewed: Option<TmdbIdentity>,
}

/// The identity 8.1 fixes at planning time. Def: T4. Use: T7, T11, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Identity {
    pub step: IdentityStep,
    pub confidence: f64,
    pub tmdb: Option<TmdbIdentity>,
    /// From the record when fetched, else from TheDiscDB's media, else from the one plausible result.
    pub title: Option<String>,
    pub year: Option<i32>,
    pub original_language: Option<String>,
    pub review: Option<ReviewReason>,
    /// The plausible results' identities (several in step 5; one in step 4).
    pub plausible: Vec<TmdbIdentity>,
    /// Whether a runtime check ran and what it said (None: not applicable, no record, or no runtime).
    pub runtime_check: Option<bool>,
    /// Pending lookups (8.1: planning proceeds on structure alone; the file phase waits in AwaitingLookup).
    pub lookup_pending: bool,
    /// One sentence per piece of evidence, in order ("TheDiscDB knows the fingerprint", "name 'JOHN_WICK_UHD' cleaned to 'JOHN WICK'").
    pub evidence: Vec<String>,
}

/// Spec 8.1 steps 1 to 6 in order, after the owner's review: `inputs.reviewed` is Some (Reviewed, 1.00, that identity);
/// `inputs.remembered` is Some (Remembered, 1.00, that identity); TheDiscDB by both disc ID and fingerprint (0.99: both
/// records present and their TMDb IDs equal, or one of them lacking an ID) or by one (0.95); else the search on a
/// non-generic cleaned name: exactly one plausible result and the runtime check passes (0.90, or 0.84 plus
/// identity_ambiguous when tmdb_only_autofile is off); several plausible results or a failed or impossible runtime check
/// (0.50, identity_ambiguous); else nothing (0, identity_unknown). The runtime check run is the one for the plausible
/// result's own TmdbKind (movie_runtime_ok for Movie, tv_runtime_ok for Tv), whatever `kind` is ("Movies and TV are searched
/// together"); `kind` (the structural kind) is used only to prefer results of that kind when several are plausible. A
/// generic name is never searched. A pending lookup does not lower the step reached by the answers in hand; it sets
/// lookup_pending. Def: T4. Use: T7.
pub fn identify(inputs: &LookupInputs<'_>, kind: Kind, runtime: &RuntimeFacts, settings: &Settings) -> Identity;
```

Also added, not in the Shared interfaces (the closed-set convention of "Conventions every task follows" asks for them): `NameSource::as_str`, `NameSource::ALL` and `FromStr for NameSource`; `FromStr for IdentityStep`; `DescriptionKind::as_str`, `DescriptionKind::ALL` and `FromStr for DescriptionKind`. Nothing else is public.

Where this task settles what the spec and the interfaces leave open (each choice is pinned by a test below):

1. **The shared `lookup/mod.rs`.** Task 3 owns the top of the file (its `//!` paragraph, `pub mod discdb; pub mod tmdb;`, `Kind` and whatever `use` lines it needs). This task adds no `use` line there: its items name `crate::settings::Settings`, `crate::review::ReviewReason` and the child modules' items (`tmdb::TmdbRecord`, `discdb::DiscDbRecord`, `name::DiscName`) by path, so no import can clash with one Task 3 wrote. Every block this task adds to `mod.rs` goes directly above Task 3's `#[cfg(test)]` / `mod tests;`, so the test-module declaration stays the file's last item. Its tests go where the conventions put the tests of `lookup/mod.rs`: Task 3's sibling `lookup/tests.rs`, appended after Task 3's two `Kind` tests. That file's two `use` lines (`use super::tmdb::TmdbKind;` and `use super::Kind;`) are replaced by this task's import block, which names `TmdbKind` and imports `super::*` (so `Kind` too); keeping them beside it would import `TmdbKind` twice (error E0252). Its `//!` line is rewritten to name both tasks' tests. The run filter is `lookup::tests::`, and its counts include Task 3's 2 tests.
2. **Tokens, parts and pieces of a name.** Spec 8.1 parses a season and a disc number "before cleaning" and removes "disc numbers (`DISC 1`, `D1`), season markers". A name is read as whitespace tokens (underscores read as spaces), each token as hyphen parts, each part as runs of ASCII digits and runs of other characters. A season marker is a piece `season`, `series` or `s` followed by a digit piece; a disc number a piece `disc` or `d` followed by a digit piece; the first of each is the parsed number. So `S3D3` gives season 3 and disc 3, `Ocean's 11` gives no season (`Ocean's` is one piece), and `EXPENDABLES_3` gives neither (`a_bare_number_that_is_not_a_tag_or_a_marker_stays`). A number too large for `u32` is not a marker.
3. **What cleaning removes.** A hyphen part whose pieces all belong to markers (`D1`, `S3D3`, the `DISC` and `1` of `DISC 1`), a token or a hyphen part that is a region or format tag (the interface's 24, in any case, with or without round or square brackets: `(UHD)`), then the last token when it is a year from 1900 to 2099 and another token remains (so `1917` stays `1917`, and is generic anyway for having no letters). Tags as hyphen parts (`X-MEN-UHD` gives `X-MEN`) and markers as hyphen parts (`MOVIE-D2` gives `MOVIE`) go one step past the interface's "whole tokens"; `Spider-Man` keeps its hyphen. A tag token is removed wherever it sits, as the interface's tag list reads, so a real word that is also a tag is lost: `THE UK FILES` cleans to `THE FILES`, `MY_PAL_GUS` to `MY GUS`, `THE US OPEN` to `THE OPEN`, and a disc labelled `US` (the film Us) cleans to nothing and is generic, so it is never searched. These losses are listed for the owner and pinned by `every_region_and_format_tag_is_removed_as_a_whole_token_in_any_case` (and, for `US` being generic, by `a_name_with_no_letters_or_nothing_left_after_cleaning_is_generic`); removing tags only from the end of the name is the alternative if the owner prefers it. A stereoscopic 3D label is also lost to spec 8.2's literal rule, and is listed for the owner too: `HUGO_S3D` has the pieces `HUGO`, `S`, `3`, `D`, so it parses as season 3 and has a season marker (8.2 then plans the movie disc as TV unless TheDiscDB states the kind), and cleaning keeps `S3D` (its `D` piece belongs to no marker), so `HUGO S3D` matches no TMDb title and identity is step 6 unless TheDiscDB knows the disc (`a_3d_label_s3d_reads_as_season_3_by_spec_8_2s_literal_rule`); treating `S3D` and `3D` as format tags and not as season markers is the alternative if the owner prefers it.
4. **Generic names** compare the raw name upper-cased with spaces read as underscores (`dvd video` is `DVD_VIDEO`); `DVD_VIDEO` is generic by its raw name although it cleans to `VIDEO` (`dvd_video_is_generic_by_its_raw_name_though_it_cleans_to_video`). "A name with no letters" is read on the cleaned name, which also makes generic every name cleaning empties (`DISC_2`, `BLU-RAY`, `S3D3`).
5. **A TheDiscDB entry without a TMDb ID** (8.1 "TMDb is searched with the entry's title and year"). The search in hand (`LookupInputs.search`) is taken as that search: a result is plausible when its title or original title folds to the entry's title; several are narrowed to TheDiscDB's kind, then to the entry's year. Exactly one keeps the TheDiscDB step (0.99 or 0.95) with that result's identity and no runtime check, unless its kind or year contradicts TheDiscDB's: one result whose kind or year contradicts TheDiscDB's is step 5 (0.50, `identity_ambiguous`) with that result's identity in `tmdb` and the evidence sentence `movie 1002 is not TheDiscDB's kind and year` (`an_entry_without_a_tmdb_id_never_takes_a_result_of_another_year_or_kind`). TMDb's `/search/multi` takes no year, so the year is checked here and not only used to break ties; a kind or a year TheDiscDB does not state is not checked. Several give step 5 (0.50, `identity_ambiguous`); none give step 6. When both TheDiscDB records are in hand and neither has a TMDb ID, the fingerprint's record is searched, unless only the disc ID record has a title: then the disc ID record's title is searched (`when_neither_thediscdb_record_has_a_tmdb_id_the_one_with_a_title_is_searched`, beside `thediscdb_by_both_without_a_tmdb_id_searches_the_entry_title_at_0_99`). An entry with neither a TMDb ID nor a title (a pinned `discNN.json` has no `media`) falls through to the disc name's search, steps 4 to 6, which keeps Open point 26 (a pinned log with no TMDb answer stops at step 6).
6. **"Prefer" in `identify`.** In the disc name's search (steps 4 and 5), when several results are plausible and some but not all are of the structural `kind`, preferring picks the result shown for review: when one is left it becomes `Identity.tmdb` and its runtime check runs, but the identity stays step 5 (0.50, `identity_ambiguous`) whatever the check says, because spec 8.1 row 4 needs "exactly one plausible result" and row 5 gives 0.50 to "TMDb search with several plausible results" (`the_structural_kind_picks_the_result_shown_but_several_plausible_stay_step_5`). `Identity.plausible` there is the full plausible list, before preferring; the evidence sentence names it first, then what preferring left. In an entry's search (item 5) TheDiscDB's kind and then its year narrow the list, because that search is the one with the entry's title and year: one left there counts as the entry's one result, and `Identity.plausible` is the list after narrowing.
7. **Step 4 against step 5.** Step 4 needs exactly one plausible result before any preferring (item 6) and `runtime_check == Some(true)`. One plausible result with a failed check (`Some(false)`), with no record for it (or a record of another identity), or with a record that has no runtime (a movie's `runtime: null`, a season without episode runtimes) is step 5 with that result's identity in `tmdb` (Review Focus 2, Open point 2). `runtime_check` is None in the last two cases.
8. **Where title, year and original language come from**: the fetched record when its identity is the identity reached; else TheDiscDB's media (`title_and_year`) when the step is TheDiscDB's, or for a reviewed or remembered identity a TheDiscDB record with that same TMDb ID; else the one plausible result (`display_title`, `year`). The original language comes only from the record.
9. **Evidence sentences** are fixed strings (the tests pin them): pending lookups first, then the name (`name 'JOHN_WICK_UHD' cleaned to 'JOHN WICK'`, `season 3 parsed from the name`, `disc 3 parsed from the name`), then the step's own sentences.
10. **`fold_name`** follows the interface: Unicode lower-case, no accent folding (`AMELIE` does not fold to `Amélie`'s `amélie`), hyphens removed without a space (`SPIDER_MAN` does not match `Spider-Man`). Both are listed for the owner, not changed here.

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement tokens, pieces, markers and the parsed numbers**

Insert into `crates/core/src/lookup/name.rs`, directly above the line `#[cfg(test)]`:

```rust
/// One piece of a name (see the module doc): a run of ASCII digits or a run of other characters, inside one hyphen
/// part of one token.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Piece {
    /// The index of the token (a whitespace-separated word once underscores are spaces).
    token: usize,
    /// The index of the hyphen-separated part within that token.
    part: usize,
    text: String,
    digits: bool,
}

/// The tokens of a name: underscores read as spaces (spec 8.1 "Cleaning replaces underscores with spaces"), then split
/// on whitespace.
fn tokens(raw: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    raw.replace('_', " ").split_whitespace().map(str::to_string).collect()
}

/// Every piece of `tokens`, in order.
fn pieces(tokens: &[String]) -> Vec<Piece> {
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    for (token, word) in tokens.iter().enumerate() {
        for (part, text) in word.split('-').enumerate() {
            let mut run = String::new();
            let mut run_digits = false;
            for character in text.chars() {
                let digit = character.is_ascii_digit();
                if !run.is_empty() && digit != run_digits {
                    found.push(Piece { token, part, text: std::mem::take(&mut run), digits: run_digits });
                }
                run_digits = digit;
                run.push(character);
            }
            if !run.is_empty() {
                found.push(Piece { token, part, text: run, digits: run_digits });
            }
        }
    }
    found
}

/// What a marker numbers.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum MarkerKind {
    Season,
    Disc,
}

/// A season marker or a disc number: its number, and the indices of its word piece and its digit piece.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Marker {
    kind: MarkerKind,
    number: u32,
    word: usize,
    digits: usize,
}

/// The words that start a season marker (spec 8.2 "`season`, `series` or `s` followed by a number").
const SEASON_WORDS: [&str; 3] = ["season", "series", "s"];
/// The words that start a disc number (spec 8.1 "`DISC 1`, `D1`").
const DISC_WORDS: [&str; 2] = ["disc", "d"];

/// Every marker of `pieces`, left to right; a digit piece belongs to one marker at most.
fn markers(pieces: &[Piece]) -> Vec<Marker> {
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    let mut index = 0;
    while index + 1 < pieces.len() {
        let (word, next) = (&pieces[index], &pieces[index + 1]);
        if !word.digits && next.digits {
            let lower = word.text.to_ascii_lowercase();
            let kind = if SEASON_WORDS.contains(&lower.as_str()) {
                Some(MarkerKind::Season)
            } else if DISC_WORDS.contains(&lower.as_str()) {
                Some(MarkerKind::Disc)
            } else {
                None
            };
            if let (Some(kind), Ok(number)) = (kind, next.text.parse::<u32>()) {
                found.push(Marker { kind, number, word: index, digits: index + 1 });
                index += 2;
                continue;
            }
        }
        index += 1;
    }
    found
}

/// The number of the first marker of `kind` in `raw`.
fn first_marker(raw: &str, kind: MarkerKind) -> Option<u32> {
    markers(&pieces(&tokens(raw))).into_iter().find(|marker| marker.kind == kind).map(|marker| marker.number)
}

/// A season number from `season N`, `series N`, `sN` or `sNN` (case-insensitive; `S3D3` gives 3; tokens split on
/// spaces, underscores, hyphens and the letter boundary of `S3D3`). Spec 8.1 "a season number and a disc number are
/// parsed". Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub fn parse_season(raw: &str) -> Option<u32> {
    first_marker(raw, MarkerKind::Season)
}

/// A disc number from `disc N`, `disc_N`, `discN`, `dN`, `D1` (`CHERNOBYL_D1` gives 1, `S3D3` gives 3). Spec 8.1.
/// Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub fn parse_disc_number(raw: &str) -> Option<u32> {
    first_marker(raw, MarkerKind::Disc)
}

/// Spec 8.2: the name contains `season`, `series` or `s` followed by a number (as `parse_season` finds it). A disc
/// number alone never counts. Def: T4. Use: T4, T5.
pub fn has_season_marker(raw: &str) -> bool {
    parse_season(raw).is_some()
}
```

Insert directly above the line `#[cfg(test)]` of `crates/core/src/lookup/name.rs`:

```rust
/// The region and format tags spec 8.1's cleaning removes ("region and format tags"), upper-case.
const TAGS: [&str; 24] = [
    "UHD", "4K", "BD", "BD50", "BLURAY", "BLU-RAY", "BDROM", "DVD", "DVD9", "NTSC", "PAL", "US", "UK", "EU", "WW", "DOM",
    "INT", "R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5", "R6", "RETAIL",
];

/// `token` without surrounding round or square brackets (`(UHD)`, `[2006]`).
fn unbracketed(token: &str) -> &str {
    token.trim_matches(|character: char| matches!(character, '(' | ')' | '[' | ']'))
}

/// A region or format tag, in any case, with or without brackets.
fn is_tag(token: &str) -> bool {
    TAGS.contains(&unbracketed(token).to_ascii_uppercase().as_str())
}

/// A year from 1900 to 2099, with or without brackets (spec 8.1 "trailing years").
fn is_year(token: &str) -> bool {
    let digits = unbracketed(token);
    digits.len() == 4
        && digits.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit())
        && matches!(digits.parse::<u32>(), Ok(1900..=2099))
}

/// Spec 8.1 "Cleaning": underscores to spaces; disc numbers (`DISC 1`, `D1`, `DISC_1`), season markers (`SEASON 3`,
/// `S3`, `S3D3`, `SERIES 2`), region and format tags (whole tokens, case-insensitive: UHD, 4K, BD, BD50, BLURAY,
/// BLU-RAY, BDROM, DVD, DVD9, NTSC, PAL, US, UK, EU, WW, DOM, INT, R1 to R6, RETAIL) and a trailing year (1900 to 2099
/// as the last token) removed; repeated spaces collapsed; trimmed. A bare number that is not a tag stays
/// (`EXPENDABLES_3` gives `EXPENDABLES 3`). A marker or a tag that is a whole hyphen part goes too (`MOVIE-D2` gives
/// `MOVIE`, `X-MEN-UHD` gives `X-MEN`); a tag may sit in round or square brackets; a year that is the only token left
/// stays. Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub fn clean(raw: &str) -> String {
    let tokens = tokens(raw);
    let pieces = pieces(&tokens);
    let in_marker: BTreeSet<usize> =
        markers(&pieces).iter().flat_map(|marker| [marker.word, marker.digits]).collect();
    let mut kept: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for (token, word) in tokens.iter().enumerate() {
        if is_tag(word) {
            continue;
        }
        let mut parts: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
        for (part, text) in word.split('-').enumerate() {
            let of_part: Vec<usize> = pieces
                .iter()
                .enumerate()
                .filter(|(_, piece)| piece.token == token && piece.part == part)
                .map(|(index, _)| index)
                .collect();
            let marker_only = !of_part.is_empty() && of_part.iter().all(|index| in_marker.contains(index));
            if !marker_only && !is_tag(text) {
                parts.push(text);
            }
        }
        let joined = parts.join("-");
        if !joined.is_empty() {
            kept.push(joined);
        }
    }
    if kept.len() > 1 && kept.last().is_some_and(|last| is_year(last)) {
        kept.pop();
    }
    kept.join(" ")
}
```

```rust
/// Spec 8.1's generic or placeholder names ("for example `DVD_VIDEO`, `DISC_1`, `LOGICAL_VOLUME_ID`, `VOLUME_SET_ID`")
/// and the other placeholders a disc carries, compared upper-case with spaces read as underscores. Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub const GENERIC_NAMES: [&str; 8] =
    ["DVD_VIDEO", "DISC_1", "LOGICAL_VOLUME_ID", "VOLUME_SET_ID", "BLURAY", "BDROM", "UNTITLED", "UNDEFINED"];

/// Spec 8.1: `DVD_VIDEO`, `DISC_1`, `LOGICAL_VOLUME_ID`, `VOLUME_SET_ID`, `BLURAY`, `BDROM`, `UNTITLED`, `UNDEFINED`, a
/// cleaned name that is empty, or one with no letter. The raw name is compared upper-case, its underscores and spaces
/// read alike (`dvd video` is `DVD_VIDEO`); a generic name is never searched (identity step 6). Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub fn is_generic(raw: &str, cleaned: &str) -> bool {
    let key = tokens(raw).join("_").to_ascii_uppercase();
    GENERIC_NAMES.contains(&key.as_str()) || !cleaned.chars().any(char::is_alphabetic)
}
```

- [ ] **Step 16: Implement folding and plausibility**

Insert directly above the line `#[cfg(test)]` of `crates/core/src/lookup/name.rs`:

```rust
/// Case-folded (Unicode lowercase), every character that is not alphanumeric or a space removed, spaces collapsed and
/// trimmed (`Pan's Labyrinth` and `PANS LABYRINTH` both give `pans labyrinth`). Spec 8.1 "after case-folding and
/// removing punctuation". Any whitespace counts as a space; accents stay (`Amélie` gives `amélie`). It does not call
/// `subtitle::text::fold` (ASCII folding for the text rule, other semantics). Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub fn fold_name(text: &str) -> String {
    let kept: String = text
        .to_lowercase()
        .chars()
        .map(|character| if character.is_whitespace() { ' ' } else { character })
        .filter(|character| character.is_alphanumeric() || *character == ' ')
        .collect();
    kept.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<&str>>().join(" ")
}

/// A result is plausible when `fold_name` of its title or original title equals `fold_name(cleaned)` (spec 8.1 "A TMDb
/// search result is plausible when its title or original title equals the cleaned name after case-folding and
/// removing punctuation"); a cleaned name that folds to nothing makes no result plausible. `display_title` and
/// `original` give `name` and `original_name` for a TV result. Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub fn plausible(result: &TmdbSearchResult, cleaned: &str) -> bool {
    let wanted = fold_name(cleaned);
    !wanted.is_empty() && (fold_name(result.display_title()) == wanted || fold_name(result.original()) == wanted)
}
```

```rust
/// Where the disc's own name came from (8.1 "the bdmt disc name, else the volume label"). Def: T4. Use: T4, T7.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum NameSource {
    /// The `<di:name>` of `BDMV/META/DL/bdmt_*.xml` (6.1 step 2; `disc::bdmt_name` reads it).
    Bdmt,
    /// CINFO 32, the volume label.
    VolumeLabel,
}

impl NameSource {
    /// The serde spelling: "bdmt" or "volume_label". Spec 8.1.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            NameSource::Bdmt => "bdmt",
            NameSource::VolumeLabel => "volume_label",
        }
    }

    /// Both sources, in 8.1's order of preference. Spec 8.1.
    pub const ALL: [NameSource; 2] = [NameSource::Bdmt, NameSource::VolumeLabel];
}

impl std::str::FromStr for NameSource {
    type Err = String;

    /// Only the `as_str` spellings.
    fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<NameSource, String> {
        NameSource::ALL
            .into_iter()
            .find(|source| source.as_str() == text)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("'{text}' is not a name source (bdmt or volume_label)"))
    }
}

/// The disc's own name with the evidence parsed from it before cleaning. Spec 8.1, 8.2. Def: T4. Use: T4 (identify),
/// T5 (season marker), T6 (season), T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct DiscName {
    /// The name as given, trimmed.
    pub raw: String,
    pub source: NameSource,
    /// `parse_season(raw)`.
    pub season: Option<u32>,
    /// `parse_disc_number(raw)`.
    pub disc: Option<u32>,
    /// `clean(raw)`.
    pub cleaned: String,
    /// `is_generic(raw, cleaned)`.
    pub generic: bool,
    /// `has_season_marker(raw)` (8.2).
    pub season_marker: bool,
}

/// `text` trimmed, when Some and not blank.
fn given(text: Option<&str>) -> Option<&str> {
    text.map(str::trim).filter(|text| !text.is_empty())
}

/// The bdmt name when Some and not blank, else the volume label when Some and not blank, else None. The caller builds
/// it once (`disc_name(bdmt, disc.volume_label.as_deref())`), searches TMDb with its `cleaned`, and passes it as
/// `LookupInputs.name`; `plan::plan` reads it from there and copies it into `PlanEvidence.name`. Spec 8.1 "The disc's
/// own name is the `bdmt` disc name, else the volume label". Def: T4. Use: T7 (tests), T15.
pub fn disc_name(bdmt: Option<&str>, volume_label: Option<&str>) -> Option<DiscName> {
    let (raw, source) = match (given(bdmt), given(volume_label)) {
        (Some(name), _) => (name, NameSource::Bdmt),
        (None, Some(label)) => (label, NameSource::VolumeLabel),
        (None, None) => return None,
    };
    let cleaned = clean(raw);
    Some(DiscName {
        raw: raw.to_string(),
        source,
        season: parse_season(raw),
        disc: parse_disc_number(raw),
        generic: is_generic(raw, &cleaned),
        season_marker: has_season_marker(raw),
        cleaned,
    })
}
```

Insert into `crates/core/src/lookup/mod.rs`, directly above Task 3's two lines `#[cfg(test)]` / `mod tests;`:

```rust
// Spec 8.1's identification (Task 4). These items add no `use` line to this file: they name
// `crate::settings::Settings`, `crate::review::ReviewReason` and the child modules `discdb`, `tmdb` and `name` by
// path, so they never clash with the imports Task 3 wrote above.

/// Spec 8.1's table rows, after the owner's review: Reviewed is spec 11's Set identity (8.8 "A review decision sets the
/// confidences it covers to 1.00"). Def: T4. Use: T7, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum IdentityStep {
    /// Spec 11's Set identity: the owner chose the identity (1.00, 8.8).
    Reviewed,
    /// Step 1: a remembered decision for this fingerprint (1.00).
    Remembered,
    /// Step 2: TheDiscDB match on both the disc ID and the fingerprint (0.99).
    DiscdbBoth,
    /// Step 3: TheDiscDB match on one of them (0.95).
    DiscdbOne,
    /// Step 4: TMDb search on the disc's own name, exactly one plausible result, and the runtime check passes (0.90,
    /// or 0.84 with identity_ambiguous when tmdb_only_autofile is off).
    TmdbOne,
    /// Step 5: several plausible results, or a failed runtime check (0.50, identity_ambiguous).
    TmdbSeveral,
    /// Step 6: nothing (0, identity_unknown).
    Nothing,
}

impl IdentityStep {
    /// The serde spelling (snake_case of the variant). Spec 8.1.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            IdentityStep::Reviewed => "reviewed",
            IdentityStep::Remembered => "remembered",
            IdentityStep::DiscdbBoth => "discdb_both",
            IdentityStep::DiscdbOne => "discdb_one",
            IdentityStep::TmdbOne => "tmdb_one",
            IdentityStep::TmdbSeveral => "tmdb_several",
            IdentityStep::Nothing => "nothing",
        }
    }

    /// Every step, in the order `identify` tries them. Spec 8.1.
    pub const ALL: [IdentityStep; 7] = [
        IdentityStep::Reviewed,
        IdentityStep::Remembered,
        IdentityStep::DiscdbBoth,
        IdentityStep::DiscdbOne,
        IdentityStep::TmdbOne,
        IdentityStep::TmdbSeveral,
        IdentityStep::Nothing,
    ];
}

impl std::str::FromStr for IdentityStep {
    type Err = String;

    /// Only the `as_str` spellings.
    fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<IdentityStep, String> {
        IdentityStep::ALL
            .into_iter()
            .find(|step| step.as_str() == text)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("'{text}' is not an identity step"))
    }
}

/// Step 1, and a review decision (8.8): 1.00. Def: T4. Use: T4, T7, T8, T10, T13.
pub const REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 1.00;
/// Step 2. Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub const DISCDB_BOTH_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.99;
/// Step 3. Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub const DISCDB_ONE_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.95;
/// Step 4. Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub const TMDB_ONE_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.90;
/// Step 4 "When `tmdb_only_autofile` is off, step 4 is capped at 0.84 and adds `identity_ambiguous`". Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub const TMDB_ONE_CAPPED_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.84;
/// Step 5. Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub const TMDB_SEVERAL_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.50;
/// Step 6. Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub const NOTHING_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.0;

/// (confidence, review reason) of a step: Reviewed and Remembered 1.00; reads settings.tmdb_only_autofile for TmdbOne
/// (0.84 and IdentityAmbiguous when off); TmdbSeveral gives IdentityAmbiguous, Nothing gives IdentityUnknown. Spec 8.1
/// table, 8.8. Reads only `tmdb_only_autofile`. Def: T4. Use: T4, T7.
pub fn identity_confidence(
    step: IdentityStep,
    settings: &crate::settings::Settings,
) -> (f64, Option<crate::review::ReviewReason>) {
    use crate::review::ReviewReason;
    match step {
        IdentityStep::Reviewed | IdentityStep::Remembered => (REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE, None),
        IdentityStep::DiscdbBoth => (DISCDB_BOTH_CONFIDENCE, None),
        IdentityStep::DiscdbOne => (DISCDB_ONE_CONFIDENCE, None),
        IdentityStep::TmdbOne if settings.tmdb_only_autofile => (TMDB_ONE_CONFIDENCE, None),
        IdentityStep::TmdbOne => (TMDB_ONE_CAPPED_CONFIDENCE, Some(ReviewReason::IdentityAmbiguous)),
        IdentityStep::TmdbSeveral => (TMDB_SEVERAL_CONFIDENCE, Some(ReviewReason::IdentityAmbiguous)),
        IdentityStep::Nothing => (NOTHING_CONFIDENCE, Some(ReviewReason::IdentityUnknown)),
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 28: Implement the runtime checks**

Insert into `crates/core/src/lookup/mod.rs`, directly above Task 3's two lines `#[cfg(test)]` / `mod tests;`:

```rust
/// What the runtime checks compare against (8.1 "Runtime check"): the planned features' or cuts' durations (8.3, 8.4),
/// the longest rival when none is planned, and the durations of the disc's episode-length groups (8.2). The planner
/// fills it from the structural pass before the TMDb match (6.1 step 5's order). Def: T4. Use: T4, T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct RuntimeFacts {
    /// The planned features or cuts, seconds, in plan order.
    pub feature_seconds: Vec<u32>,
    /// The longest rival, seconds, for a movie with no planned feature.
    pub longest_rival_seconds: Option<u32>,
    /// The episode-length groups (`plan::kind::episode_length_groups`), seconds, in group order.
    pub episode_group_seconds: Vec<u32>,
}

/// Spec 8.1 "within 3% of the TMDb runtime": a fixed value (spec 14), not a setting. Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub const MOVIE_RUNTIME_TOLERANCE: f64 = 0.03;
/// Spec 8.1 "within 15% of the median duration of the disc's episode-length groups": a fixed value. Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub const TV_RUNTIME_TOLERANCE: f64 = 0.15;

/// Movies: at least one of `feature_seconds` (else `longest_rival_seconds`) within 3% of `runtime_min * 60`; false
/// without a runtime or without any duration. Spec 8.1 "Runtime check for movies". Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub fn movie_runtime_ok(facts: &RuntimeFacts, runtime_min: Option<u32>) -> bool {
    let Some(minutes) = runtime_min else {
        return false;
    };
    let target = f64::from(minutes) * 60.0;
    let durations: Vec<u32> = if facts.feature_seconds.is_empty() {
        facts.longest_rival_seconds.into_iter().collect()
    } else {
        facts.feature_seconds.clone()
    };
    durations.iter().any(|&seconds| within(f64::from(seconds), target, MOVIE_RUNTIME_TOLERANCE))
}

/// TV: the median of `episode_runtimes_min` within 15% of the median of `episode_group_seconds / 60`; false when
/// either list is empty. The median of an even count is the mean of the two middle values. Spec 8.1 "For TV". Def: T4.
/// Use: T4.
pub fn tv_runtime_ok(facts: &RuntimeFacts, episode_runtimes_min: &[u32]) -> bool {
    let tmdb: Vec<f64> = episode_runtimes_min.iter().map(|&minutes| f64::from(minutes)).collect();
    let disc: Vec<f64> = facts.episode_group_seconds.iter().map(|&seconds| f64::from(seconds) / 60.0).collect();
    match (median_of(&tmdb), median_of(&disc)) {
        (Some(tmdb_median), Some(disc_median)) => within(tmdb_median, disc_median, TV_RUNTIME_TOLERANCE),
        _ => false,
    }
}

/// |a - b| <= tolerance * b. Spec 8.1's "within N% of" (b is the figure the percentage is of). Def: T4. Use: T4, T5
/// (rule 4's 10%), T6 (suggest_by_runtime's 15%).
pub fn within(a: f64, b: f64, tolerance: f64) -> bool {
    (a - b).abs() <= tolerance * b
}

/// The median of `values`: the middle value of an odd count, the mean of the two middle values of an even count; None
/// for none. A separate copy on purpose: `audio::measures::py_median` is the Python-exact rule of the ported module
/// (RP6, RP20) and private to it, and `lazymkv-dev`'s `ocr_compare::median` lives in a crate core cannot call.
fn median_of(values: &[f64]) -> Option<f64> {
    let mut sorted = values.to_vec();
    sorted.sort_by(f64::total_cmp);
    let count = sorted.len();
    if count == 0 {
        None
    } else if count % 2 == 1 {
        Some(sorted[count / 2])
    } else {
        Some((sorted[count / 2 - 1] + sorted[count / 2]) / 2.0)
    }
}
```

```rust
fn knowings_described_tracks_read_as_dialogue_and_commentary() {

#[test]
fn every_described_track_of_the_18_answers_is_commentary_or_its_own_language() {
    let folder = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../corpus/thediscdb-api");
    let mut files: Vec<String> = fs::read_dir(&folder)
        .unwrap()
        .map(|entry| entry.unwrap().file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned())
        .filter(|file| file.ends_with(".json"))
        .collect();
    files.sort();
    assert_eq!(files.len(), 18);
    let (mut commentary, mut dialogue) = (0, 0);
    for file in &files {
        let text = corpus(&format!("thediscdb-api/{file}"));
        let records: Vec<DiscDbRecord> = if file.starts_with("dischash-") {
            parse_dischash(&text, file).unwrap().into_iter().collect()
        } else {
            parse_discid(&text, file).unwrap()
        };
        for track in records.iter().flat_map(|record| &record.titles).flat_map(|title| &title.tracks) {
            let Some(description) = track.description.as_deref() else {
                continue;
            };
            let kinds = description_kinds(description, track.language.as_deref());
            if description.to_lowercase().contains("comment") {
                assert_eq!(kinds, vec![DescriptionKind::Commentary], "{file}: {description}");
                commentary += 1;
            } else {
                assert_eq!(kinds, vec![DescriptionKind::Dialogue], "{file}: {description} ({:?})", track.language);
                dialogue += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    assert_eq!((commentary, dialogue), (12, 76));
}

#[test]
fn description_kind_spellings_round_trip() {
    let spellings = ["commentary", "audio_description", "sdh", "isolated_score", "music_and_effects", "dialogue"];
    assert_eq!(DescriptionKind::ALL.map(DescriptionKind::as_str), spellings);
    for kind in DescriptionKind::ALL {
        let text = kind.as_str();
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&kind).unwrap(), format!("\"{text}\""));
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<DescriptionKind>(&format!("\"{text}\"")).unwrap(), kind);
        assert_eq!(text.parse::<DescriptionKind>(), Ok(kind));
    }
    assert_eq!("Sdh".parse::<DescriptionKind>(), Err("'Sdh' is not a description kind".to_string()));
}
```

- [ ] **Step 32: Implement the description kinds**

Insert into `crates/core/src/lookup/mod.rs`, directly above Task 3's two lines `#[cfg(test)]` / `mod tests;`:

```rust
/// A TheDiscDB description's meaning (8.1 last bullet, D14, 8.7 "the one TheDiscDB describes as subtitles or SDH"):
/// "comment" gives Commentary; "audio desc", "descriptive", "DVS", "visually impaired" give AudioDescription; "SDH",
/// "hearing" give Sdh; "isolated score", "score only" give IsolatedScore; "music and effects", "music & effects", "M&E"
/// give MusicAndEffects; "subtitle", or a description that after trimming and case-folding equals the track's own
/// `language` (TheDiscDB's language name: "English"; Knowing's "ENglish" included), gives Dialogue. All
/// case-insensitive, substring matches, in this order; a text can carry several. IsolatedScore, MusicAndEffects and
/// Dialogue are provisional: TheDiscDB's wording for them is not yet known (8.1's last bullet names no such word; every
/// subtitle description in the 18 answers and the pinned files is a bare language name). Def: T4. Use: T8, T9, T10.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum DescriptionKind {
    Commentary,
    AudioDescription,
    Sdh,
    IsolatedScore,
    MusicAndEffects,
    Dialogue,
}

impl DescriptionKind {
    /// The serde spelling (snake_case of the variant). Spec 8.1.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            DescriptionKind::Commentary => "commentary",
            DescriptionKind::AudioDescription => "audio_description",
            DescriptionKind::Sdh => "sdh",
            DescriptionKind::IsolatedScore => "isolated_score",
            DescriptionKind::MusicAndEffects => "music_and_effects",
            DescriptionKind::Dialogue => "dialogue",
        }
    }

    /// Every kind, in the order `description_kinds` tests them. Spec 8.1.
    pub const ALL: [DescriptionKind; 6] = [
        DescriptionKind::Commentary,
        DescriptionKind::AudioDescription,
        DescriptionKind::Sdh,
        DescriptionKind::IsolatedScore,
        DescriptionKind::MusicAndEffects,
        DescriptionKind::Dialogue,
    ];
}

impl std::str::FromStr for DescriptionKind {
    type Err = String;

    /// Only the `as_str` spellings.
    fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<DescriptionKind, String> {
        DescriptionKind::ALL
            .into_iter()
            .find(|kind| kind.as_str() == text)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("'{text}' is not a description kind"))
    }
}

/// The phrases of each description kind, lower-case (spec 8.1 last bullet and D14; see DescriptionKind).
const COMMENTARY_PHRASES: [&str; 1] = ["comment"];
const AUDIO_DESCRIPTION_PHRASES: [&str; 4] = ["audio desc", "descriptive", "dvs", "visually impaired"];
const SDH_PHRASES: [&str; 2] = ["sdh", "hearing"];
const ISOLATED_SCORE_PHRASES: [&str; 2] = ["isolated score", "score only"];
const MUSIC_AND_EFFECTS_PHRASES: [&str; 3] = ["music and effects", "music & effects", "m&e"];
const DIALOGUE_PHRASES: [&str; 1] = ["subtitle"];

/// True when `text` contains one of `phrases`.
fn mentions(text: &str, phrases: &[&str]) -> bool {
    phrases.iter().any(|phrase| text.contains(*phrase))
}

/// The kinds `text` names, in DescriptionKind's order, each once; `language` is the track's own TheDiscDB `language`
/// ("English"), which a bare-language description equals. Spec 8.1 last bullet, D14, 8.7. Def: T4. Use: T8, T9, T10.
pub fn description_kinds(text: &str, language: Option<&str>) -> Vec<DescriptionKind> {
    let folded = text.trim().to_lowercase();
    let own_language = language.map(|language| language.trim().to_lowercase()).filter(|language| !language.is_empty());
    let mut kinds = Vec::new();
    if mentions(&folded, &COMMENTARY_PHRASES) {
        kinds.push(DescriptionKind::Commentary);
    }
    if mentions(&folded, &AUDIO_DESCRIPTION_PHRASES) {
        kinds.push(DescriptionKind::AudioDescription);
    }
    if mentions(&folded, &SDH_PHRASES) {
        kinds.push(DescriptionKind::Sdh);
    }
    if mentions(&folded, &ISOLATED_SCORE_PHRASES) {
        kinds.push(DescriptionKind::IsolatedScore);
    }
    if mentions(&folded, &MUSIC_AND_EFFECTS_PHRASES) {
        kinds.push(DescriptionKind::MusicAndEffects);
    }
    if mentions(&folded, &DIALOGUE_PHRASES) || own_language.as_deref() == Some(folded.as_str()) {
        kinds.push(DescriptionKind::Dialogue);
    }
    kinds
}
```

```rust
/// A TheDiscDB movie entry in the API's shape whose media has a title and a year but no TMDb ID.
fn without_tmdb_id(title: &str, year: i32) -> DiscDbRecord {
    serde_json::from_str(&format!(
        r#"{{"media": {{"title": "{title}", "full_title": "{title}", "year": {year}, "type": "Movie", "external_ids": {{}}}}, "titles": []}}"#

}

}

fn movie_record(id: i64, title: &str, release_date: &str, runtime: Option<u32>) -> TmdbRecord {

}

#[test]
fn an_entry_that_states_no_kind_is_never_narrowed_by_the_structural_kind() {
    // TheDiscDB's media has a title and a year but no type: the structural kind may only pick the result shown
    // (settled items 5 and 6), so two same-year results of different kinds stay ambiguous.
    let fingerprint: DiscDbRecord = serde_json::from_str(
        r#"{"media": {"title": "Short Circuit", "full_title": "Short Circuit", "year": 1986, "external_ids": {}}, "titles": []}"#,
    )
    .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(fingerprint.kind(), None);
    let results = search(&[
        ("movie", 1001, "Short Circuit", "Short Circuit", "1986-05-09"),
        ("tv", 1003, "Short Circuit", "Short Circuit", "1986-01-24"),
    ]);
    let inputs = LookupInputs { discdb_by_fingerprint: Some(&fingerprint), search: Some(&results), ..LookupInputs::default() };
    let identity = identify(&inputs, Kind::Movie, &RuntimeFacts::default(), &Settings::default());
    assert_eq!(
        (identity.step, identity.confidence, identity.tmdb, identity.review),
        (IdentityStep::TmdbSeveral, 0.50, None, Some(ReviewReason::IdentityAmbiguous))
    );
    assert_eq!(identity.plausible, vec![movie(1001), tv(1003)]);
    assert_eq!(
        identity.evidence,
        sentences(&[
            "TheDiscDB knows the fingerprint",
            "TheDiscDB gives no TMDb ID: TMDb is searched with its title 'Short Circuit' and year 1986",
            "2 of 2 search results are plausible: movie 1001, tv 1003",
        ])
    );
}

#[test]
fn an_entry_without_a_tmdb_id_never_takes_a_result_of_another_year_or_kind() {
    let fingerprint = without_tmdb_id("Short Circuit", 1986);
    for (media_type, id, date) in [("movie", 1002, "2021-03-01"), ("tv", 1003, "1986-01-24")] {
        let results = search(&[(media_type, id, "Short Circuit", "Short Circuit", date)]);
        let inputs =
            LookupInputs { discdb_by_fingerprint: Some(&fingerprint), search: Some(&results), ..LookupInputs::default() };
        let identity = identify(&inputs, Kind::Movie, &RuntimeFacts::default(), &Settings::default());
        assert_eq!(
            (identity.step, identity.confidence, identity.review),
            (IdentityStep::TmdbSeveral, 0.50, Some(ReviewReason::IdentityAmbiguous))
        );
        let expected = format!("{media_type} {id} is not TheDiscDB's kind and year");
        assert_eq!(identity.evidence.last().map(String::as_str), Some(expected.as_str()));
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_structural_kind_picks_the_result_shown_but_several_plausible_stay_step_5() {
    let name = label("THE OFFICE S3D3");
    let record = tv_record(2316, "The Office", &[(3, &OFFICE_SEASON_3[..])]);
    let two = search(&[
        ("tv", 2316, "The Office", "The Office", "2005-03-24"),
        ("movie", 3003, "The Office", "The Office", "2010-01-01"),
    ]);
    let inputs = LookupInputs { name: Some(&name), search: Some(&two), record: Some(&record), ..LookupInputs::default() };
    let identity = identify(&inputs, Kind::Tv, &episode_groups(&OFFICE_GROUPS_S), &Settings::default());
    // Spec 8.1 row 5 "TMDb search with several plausible results": preferring the structural kind picks the show
    // shown for review, and its runtime check runs and passes, but two plausible results are never step 4.
    assert_eq!(
        (identity.step, identity.confidence, identity.tmdb, identity.runtime_check),
        (IdentityStep::TmdbSeveral, 0.50, Some(tv(2316)), Some(true))
    );
    assert_eq!(identity.review, Some(ReviewReason::IdentityAmbiguous));
    assert_eq!(identity.plausible, vec![tv(2316), movie(3003)]);
    assert_eq!(
        identity.evidence,
        sentences(&[
            "name 'THE OFFICE S3D3' cleaned to 'THE OFFICE'",
            "season 3 parsed from the name",
            "disc 3 parsed from the name",
            "2 of 2 search results are plausible: tv 2316, movie 3003",
            "preferring tv results leaves tv 2316",
            "the runtime check passes",
        ])
    );
    // Two shows of that name stay two: step 5 with no result picked, and every plausible result listed.
    let three = search(&[
        ("tv", 2316, "The Office", "The Office", "2005-03-24"),
        ("movie", 3003, "The Office", "The Office", "2010-01-01"),
        ("tv", 2996, "The Office", "The Office", "2001-07-09"),
    ]);
    let inputs = LookupInputs { name: Some(&name), search: Some(&three), record: Some(&record), ..LookupInputs::default() };
    let identity = identify(&inputs, Kind::Tv, &episode_groups(&OFFICE_GROUPS_S), &Settings::default());
    assert_eq!(
        (identity.step, identity.tmdb, identity.plausible),
        (IdentityStep::TmdbSeveral, None, vec![tv(2316), movie(3003), tv(2996)])
    );
}

#[test]
fn the_runtime_check_is_the_one_of_the_results_own_kind() {
    // The structure said movie, but the one plausible result is a show: its TV check runs over the episode groups.
    let name = label("THE OFFICE S3D3");
    let record = tv_record(2316, "The Office", &[(3, &OFFICE_SEASON_3[..])]);
    let results = search(&[("tv", 2316, "The Office", "The Office", "2005-03-24")]);
    let facts = RuntimeFacts {
        feature_seconds: vec![5400],
        longest_rival_seconds: None,
        episode_group_seconds: OFFICE_GROUPS_S.to_vec(),
    };
    assert!(!movie_runtime_ok(&facts, Some(22)), "a movie check over the same facts would fail");
    let inputs = LookupInputs { name: Some(&name), search: Some(&results), record: Some(&record), ..LookupInputs::default() };
    let identity = identify(&inputs, Kind::Movie, &facts, &Settings::default());
    assert_eq!(
        (identity.step, identity.tmdb, identity.runtime_check),
        (IdentityStep::TmdbOne, Some(tv(2316)), Some(true))
    );
}

#[test]
fn the_tv_runtime_check_reads_the_parsed_season_else_the_whole_series() {
    let record = tv_record(2316, "The Office", &[(1, &OFFICE_SEASON_1[..]), (3, &OFFICE_SEASON_3[..])]);
    let results = search(&[("tv", 2316, "The Office", "The Office", "2005-03-24")]);
    // Season 3 parsed: its 22-minute median matches the 22-minute groups.
    let season_three = label("THE OFFICE S3D3");
    let inputs = LookupInputs { name: Some(&season_three), search: Some(&results), record: Some(&record), ..LookupInputs::default() };
    let identity = identify(&inputs, Kind::Tv, &episode_groups(&OFFICE_GROUPS_S), &Settings::default());
    assert_eq!((identity.step, identity.runtime_check), (IdentityStep::TmdbOne, Some(true)));
    // No season parsed: the whole series' median is (30 + 30) / 2 = 30 minutes, more than 15% from 22.
    let no_season = label("THE OFFICE");
    let inputs = LookupInputs { name: Some(&no_season), search: Some(&results), record: Some(&record), ..LookupInputs::default() };
    let identity = identify(&inputs, Kind::Tv, &episode_groups(&OFFICE_GROUPS_S), &Settings::default());
    assert_eq!(
        (identity.step, identity.review, identity.runtime_check),
        (IdentityStep::TmdbSeveral, Some(ReviewReason::IdentityAmbiguous), Some(false))
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_pending_lookup_does_not_lower_the_step_reached() {
    // TheDiscDB answered by fingerprint; its other lookup is still pending.
    let fingerprint = by_fingerprint(JOHN_WICK_UHD_BY_FINGERPRINT);
    let inputs = LookupInputs { discdb_by_fingerprint: Some(&fingerprint), discdb_pending: true, ..LookupInputs::default() };
    let identity = identify(&inputs, Kind::Movie, &RuntimeFacts::default(), &Settings::default());
    assert_eq!((identity.step, identity.confidence, identity.lookup_pending), (IdentityStep::DiscdbOne, 0.95, true));
    assert_eq!(identity.evidence[0], "the TheDiscDB lookup is pending");
    // TMDb unreachable: planning proceeds on structure alone, the identity is unknown and pending.
    let name = label("JOHN_WICK_UHD");
    let inputs = LookupInputs { name: Some(&name), tmdb_pending: true, ..LookupInputs::default() };
    let identity = identify(&inputs, Kind::Movie, &features(&[JOHN_WICK_MAIN_S]), &Settings::default());
    assert_eq!((identity.step, identity.lookup_pending), (IdentityStep::Nothing, true));
    assert_eq!(
        identity.evidence,
        sentences(&[
            "the TMDb lookup is pending",
            "name 'JOHN_WICK_UHD' cleaned to 'JOHN WICK'",
            "no TMDb search answer is in hand",
        ])
    );
    // The search is in hand but the record is pending: step 5 on what is in hand.
    let results = search(&JOHN_WICK_RESULTS);
    let inputs = LookupInputs { name: Some(&name), search: Some(&results), tmdb_pending: true, ..LookupInputs::default() };
    let identity = identify(&inputs, Kind::Movie, &features(&[JOHN_WICK_MAIN_S]), &Settings::default());
    assert_eq!(
        (identity.step, identity.tmdb, identity.lookup_pending),
        (IdentityStep::TmdbSeveral, Some(movie(245891)), true)
    );
}

#[test]

    let inputs = LookupInputs { discdb_by_fingerprint: Some(&fingerprint), ..LookupInputs::default() };
    let identity = identify(&inputs, Kind::Movie, &RuntimeFacts::default(), &Settings::default());
    let text = serde_json::to_string(&identity).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        text,
        concat!(
            r#"{"step":"discdb_one","confidence":0.95,"tmdb":{"kind":"movie","id":245891},"title":"John Wick","#,
            r#""year":2014,"original_language":null,"review":null,"plausible":[],"runtime_check":null,"#,
            r#""lookup_pending":false,"evidence":["TheDiscDB knows the fingerprint","TheDiscDB names movie 245891"]}"#
        )
    );
    assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<Identity>(&text).unwrap(), identity);
}
```

```rust
/// What the lookups gave (recorded, synthetic, or live in phase 2). `pending` flags say the answer is not in yet (8.1
/// "the lookup is recorded as pending"). Def: T4. Use: T7, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct LookupInputs<'a> {
    /// The disc's own name, built by the caller with `name::disc_name` (a generic name is signalled by
    /// `DiscName.generic`, not by None).
    pub name: Option<&'a name::DiscName>,
    /// `/api/discid/{id}`: the first record of the array that has titles, or None (a miss, or no disc ID: a DVD).
    pub discdb_by_disc_id: Option<&'a discdb::DiscDbRecord>,
    /// `/api/dischash/{hash}`.
    pub discdb_by_fingerprint: Option<&'a discdb::DiscDbRecord>,
    pub discdb_pending: bool,
    /// The search 8.1 runs on the cleaned name (or on TheDiscDB's title and year when the entry has no TMDb ID).
    pub search: Option<&'a tmdb::TmdbSearch>,
    /// The record fetched for the identity in hand.
    pub record: Option<&'a tmdb::TmdbRecord>,
    pub tmdb_pending: bool,
    /// Step 1: the TMDb identity of a remembered decision for this fingerprint (`Remembered.tmdb`); plan::plan fills it
    /// from PlanInputs.remembered.
    pub remembered: Option<tmdb::TmdbIdentity>,
    /// The owner's Set identity (spec 11), before step 1; plan::plan fills it from PlanInputs.overrides.
    pub reviewed: Option<tmdb::TmdbIdentity>,
}

/// The identity 8.1 fixes at planning time. Def: T4. Use: T7, T11, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Identity {
    pub step: IdentityStep,
    pub confidence: f64,
    pub tmdb: Option<tmdb::TmdbIdentity>,
    /// From the record when fetched, else from TheDiscDB's media, else from the one plausible result.
    pub title: Option<String>,
    pub year: Option<i32>,
    pub original_language: Option<String>,
    pub review: Option<crate::review::ReviewReason>,
    /// The plausible results' identities (several in step 5; one in step 4).
    pub plausible: Vec<tmdb::TmdbIdentity>,
    /// Whether a runtime check ran and what it said (None: not applicable, no record, or no runtime).
    pub runtime_check: Option<bool>,
    /// Pending lookups (8.1: planning proceeds on structure alone; the file phase waits in AwaitingLookup).
    pub lookup_pending: bool,
    /// One sentence per piece of evidence, in order ("TheDiscDB knows the fingerprint", "name 'JOHN_WICK_UHD' cleaned to
    /// 'JOHN WICK'").
    pub evidence: Vec<String>,
}

/// Spec 8.1 steps 1 to 6 in order, after the owner's review: `inputs.reviewed` is Some (Reviewed, 1.00, that
/// identity); `inputs.remembered` is Some (Remembered, 1.00, that identity); TheDiscDB by both disc ID and fingerprint
/// (0.99: both records present and their TMDb IDs equal, or one of them lacking an ID) or by one (0.95); else the
/// search on a non-generic cleaned name: exactly one plausible result and the runtime check passes (0.90, or 0.84 plus
/// identity_ambiguous when tmdb_only_autofile is off); several plausible results or a failed or impossible runtime
/// check (0.50, identity_ambiguous); else nothing (0, identity_unknown). The runtime check run is the one for the
/// plausible result's own TmdbKind (movie_runtime_ok for Movie, tv_runtime_ok for Tv), whatever `kind` is ("Movies and
/// TV are searched together"); `kind` (the structural kind) is used only to prefer results of that kind when several
/// are plausible. A generic name is never searched. A pending lookup does not lower the step reached by the answers in
/// hand; it sets lookup_pending. A TheDiscDB entry without a TMDb ID is searched by its title (`inputs.search` is that
/// search): exactly one plausible result after preferring TheDiscDB's kind and then its year keeps the TheDiscDB step
/// with that result's identity, but one result whose kind or year contradicts TheDiscDB's is step 5 with that identity;
/// several give step 5, none step 6; when neither TheDiscDB record has a TMDb ID the fingerprint's title is searched,
/// unless only the disc ID record has one; an entry with neither a TMDb ID nor a title falls through to the disc name's
/// search. In the disc name's search, preferring the structural kind only picks the result shown (`tmdb`, and the
/// runtime check run on it): several plausible results stay step 5 (8.1 row 5), and `plausible` lists them all. Reads
/// only `settings.tmdb_only_autofile`. Def: T4. Use: T7.
pub fn identify(
    inputs: &LookupInputs<'_>,
    kind: Kind,
    runtime: &RuntimeFacts,
    settings: &crate::settings::Settings,
) -> Identity {
    let mut evidence = Vec::new();
    if inputs.discdb_pending {
        evidence.push("the TheDiscDB lookup is pending".to_string());
    }
    if inputs.tmdb_pending {
        evidence.push("the TMDb lookup is pending".to_string());
    }
    if let Some(disc_name) = inputs.name {
        evidence.push(format!("name '{}' cleaned to '{}'", disc_name.raw, disc_name.cleaned));
        if let Some(season) = disc_name.season {
            evidence.push(format!("season {season} parsed from the name"));
        }
        if let Some(disc) = disc_name.disc {
            evidence.push(format!("disc {disc} parsed from the name"));
        }
    }
    let found = find_identity(inputs, kind, runtime, &mut evidence);
    let (confidence, review) = identity_confidence(found.step, settings);
    let (title, year, original_language) = describe_identity(found.tmdb, inputs.record, found.media, found.result);
    Identity {
        step: found.step,
        confidence,
        tmdb: found.tmdb,
        title,
        year,
        original_language,
        review,
        plausible: found.plausible,
        runtime_check: found.runtime_check,
        lookup_pending: inputs.discdb_pending || inputs.tmdb_pending,
        evidence,
    }
}

/// The step `identify` reached and what it rests on: the TheDiscDB record whose media may name the work, and the one
/// plausible search result.
struct IdentityFound<'a> {
    step: IdentityStep,
    tmdb: Option<tmdb::TmdbIdentity>,
    media: Option<&'a discdb::DiscDbRecord>,
    result: Option<&'a tmdb::TmdbSearchResult>,
    plausible: Vec<tmdb::TmdbIdentity>,
    runtime_check: Option<bool>,
}

impl<'a> IdentityFound<'a> {
    /// `step` with nothing found yet.
    fn at(step: IdentityStep) -> IdentityFound<'a> {
        IdentityFound { step, tmdb: None, media: None, result: None, plausible: Vec::new(), runtime_check: None }
    }
}

/// "movie 245891", "tv 1437".
fn identity_text(identity: tmdb::TmdbIdentity) -> String {
    format!("{} {}", identity.kind.as_str(), identity.id)
}

/// The identities of `found`, joined by ", ".
fn identity_list(found: &[(tmdb::TmdbIdentity, &tmdb::TmdbSearchResult)]) -> String {
    found.iter().map(|(identity, _)| identity_text(*identity)).collect::<Vec<String>>().join(", ")
}

/// Steps 1 to 6 in order (see `identify`).
fn find_identity<'a>(
    inputs: &LookupInputs<'a>,
    kind: Kind,
    runtime: &RuntimeFacts,
    evidence: &mut Vec<String>,
) -> IdentityFound<'a> {
    if let Some(identity) = inputs.reviewed {
        evidence.push(format!("the owner set the identity to {}", identity_text(identity)));
        return IdentityFound {
            tmdb: Some(identity),
            media: discdb_media_for(inputs, identity),
            ..IdentityFound::at(IdentityStep::Reviewed)
        };
    }
    if let Some(identity) = inputs.remembered {
        evidence.push(format!("a remembered decision names {}", identity_text(identity)));
        return IdentityFound {
            tmdb: Some(identity),
            media: discdb_media_for(inputs, identity),
            ..IdentityFound::at(IdentityStep::Remembered)
        };
    }
    if let Some((step, record)) = discdb_match(inputs, evidence) {
        if let Some(identity) = record.tmdb_identity() {
            evidence.push(format!("TheDiscDB names {}", identity_text(identity)));
            return IdentityFound { tmdb: Some(identity), media: Some(record), ..IdentityFound::at(step) };
        }
        if let Some((title, year)) = record.title_and_year() {
            let with_year = year.map(|year| format!(" and year {year}")).unwrap_or_default();
            evidence.push(format!("TheDiscDB gives no TMDb ID: TMDb is searched with its title '{title}'{with_year}"));
            return search_by_entry(inputs, step, record, &title, year, evidence);
        }
        evidence.push("TheDiscDB gives neither a TMDb ID nor a title".to_string());
    }
    search_by_name(inputs, kind, runtime, evidence)
}

/// A TheDiscDB record in hand whose TMDb ID is `identity` (fingerprint first), for the title and year of a reviewed
/// or remembered identity.
fn discdb_media_for<'a>(inputs: &LookupInputs<'a>, identity: tmdb::TmdbIdentity) -> Option<&'a discdb::DiscDbRecord> {
    [inputs.discdb_by_fingerprint, inputs.discdb_by_disc_id]
        .into_iter()
        .flatten()
        .find(|record| record.tmdb_identity() == Some(identity))
}

/// Steps 2 and 3: the step and the record it rests on. Both records with different TMDb IDs give step 3 with the
/// fingerprint's record (the fingerprint is the primary key, spec 5 and 8.1), and the disagreement is written to the
/// evidence; both records with one or no ID give step 2 with the record that has the ID (the fingerprint's when
/// neither has one, unless only the disc ID record has a title).
fn discdb_match<'a>(
    inputs: &LookupInputs<'a>,
    evidence: &mut Vec<String>,
) -> Option<(IdentityStep, &'a discdb::DiscDbRecord)> {
    match (inputs.discdb_by_disc_id, inputs.discdb_by_fingerprint) {
        (Some(by_id), Some(by_fingerprint)) => {
            evidence.push("TheDiscDB knows the disc ID and the fingerprint".to_string());
            match (by_id.tmdb_identity(), by_fingerprint.tmdb_identity()) {
                (Some(of_id), Some(of_fingerprint)) if of_id != of_fingerprint => {
                    evidence.push(format!(
                        "TheDiscDB's disc ID record names {} and its fingerprint record {}: the fingerprint's is used",
                        identity_text(of_id),
                        identity_text(of_fingerprint)
                    ));
                    Some((IdentityStep::DiscdbOne, by_fingerprint))
                }
                (Some(_), None) => Some((IdentityStep::DiscdbBoth, by_id)),
                (None, None) if by_fingerprint.title_and_year().is_none() && by_id.title_and_year().is_some() => {
                    Some((IdentityStep::DiscdbBoth, by_id))
                }
                _ => Some((IdentityStep::DiscdbBoth, by_fingerprint)),
            }
        }
        (Some(by_id), None) => {
            evidence.push("TheDiscDB knows the disc ID".to_string());
            Some((IdentityStep::DiscdbOne, by_id))
        }
        (None, Some(by_fingerprint)) => {
            evidence.push("TheDiscDB knows the fingerprint".to_string());
            Some((IdentityStep::DiscdbOne, by_fingerprint))
        }
        (None, None) => None,
    }
}

/// The search results with an identity (a movie or a show) that are plausible for `text`, in the answer's order, with
/// the evidence sentence naming them.
fn plausible_results<'a>(
    search: &'a tmdb::TmdbSearch,
    text: &str,
    evidence: &mut Vec<String>,
) -> Vec<(tmdb::TmdbIdentity, &'a tmdb::TmdbSearchResult)> {
    let found: Vec<(tmdb::TmdbIdentity, &tmdb::TmdbSearchResult)> = search
        .results
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|result| result.identity().map(|identity| (identity, result)))
        .filter(|(_, result)| name::plausible(result, text))
        .collect();
    let mut sentence = format!("{} of {} search results are plausible", found.len(), search.results.len());
    if !found.is_empty() {
        sentence.push_str(": ");
        sentence.push_str(&identity_list(&found));
    }
    evidence.push(sentence);
    found
}

/// Several plausible results narrowed to those of `kind`, then to those of `year`, each only when some but not all
/// match (see `identify`); the kind narrowing is skipped when `kind` is None (a TheDiscDB entry that states no kind,
/// whose search the structural kind never narrows). The disc name's search uses the result only to pick the identity
/// shown; the entry's search takes it as its answer.
fn prefer_results<'a>(
    found: Vec<(tmdb::TmdbIdentity, &'a tmdb::TmdbSearchResult)>,
    kind: Option<Kind>,
    year: Option<i32>,
    evidence: &mut Vec<String>,
) -> Vec<(tmdb::TmdbIdentity, &'a tmdb::TmdbSearchResult)> {
    let mut picked = found;
    if let (true, Some(kind)) = (picked.len() > 1, kind) {
        let wanted = tmdb::TmdbKind::from(kind);
        let of_kind: Vec<(tmdb::TmdbIdentity, &tmdb::TmdbSearchResult)> =
            picked.iter().copied().filter(|(identity, _)| identity.kind == wanted).collect();
        if !of_kind.is_empty() && of_kind.len() < picked.len() {
            evidence.push(format!("preferring {} results leaves {}", wanted.as_str(), identity_list(&of_kind)));
            picked = of_kind;
        }
    }
    if let (true, Some(year)) = (picked.len() > 1, year) {
        let of_year: Vec<(tmdb::TmdbIdentity, &tmdb::TmdbSearchResult)> =
            picked.iter().copied().filter(|(_, result)| result.year() == Some(year)).collect();
        if !of_year.is_empty() && of_year.len() < picked.len() {
            evidence.push(format!("preferring results from {year} leaves {}", identity_list(&of_year)));
            picked = of_year;
        }
    }
    picked
}

/// A TheDiscDB entry without a TMDb ID, searched by its title and year (8.1 "If the entry has no TMDb ID, TMDb is
/// searched with the entry's title and year"). TMDb's `/search/multi` takes no year, so the year is checked here: one
/// plausible result whose kind or year contradicts what TheDiscDB states (8.2 "TheDiscDB states the kind") is step 5
/// with that result's identity, never the TheDiscDB step.
fn search_by_entry<'a>(
    inputs: &LookupInputs<'a>,
    step: IdentityStep,
    record: &'a discdb::DiscDbRecord,
    title: &str,
    year: Option<i32>,
    evidence: &mut Vec<String>,
) -> IdentityFound<'a> {
    let Some(search) = inputs.search else {
        evidence.push("no TMDb search answer is in hand".to_string());
        return IdentityFound::at(IdentityStep::Nothing);
    };
    let found = plausible_results(search, title, evidence);
    let picked = prefer_results(found, record.kind(), year, evidence);
    match picked.as_slice() {
        [] => IdentityFound::at(IdentityStep::Nothing),
        [(identity, result)] => {
            let wrong_kind = record.kind().is_some_and(|stated| tmdb::TmdbKind::from(stated) != identity.kind);
            let wrong_year = matches!((year, result.year()), (Some(stated), Some(found)) if stated != found);
            if wrong_kind || wrong_year {
                evidence.push(format!("{} is not TheDiscDB's kind and year", identity_text(*identity)));
                IdentityFound {
                    tmdb: Some(*identity),
                    result: Some(*result),
                    plausible: vec![*identity],
                    ..IdentityFound::at(IdentityStep::TmdbSeveral)
                }
            } else {
                IdentityFound {
                    tmdb: Some(*identity),
                    media: Some(record),
                    result: Some(*result),
                    plausible: vec![*identity],
                    ..IdentityFound::at(step)
                }
            }
        }
        several => IdentityFound {
            plausible: several.iter().map(|(identity, _)| *identity).collect(),
            ..IdentityFound::at(IdentityStep::TmdbSeveral)
        },
    }
}

/// Steps 4 to 6: the search on the disc's own cleaned name. Step 4 needs exactly one plausible result (8.1 row 4):
/// when several are plausible, preferring the structural kind may pick the one shown, but the step stays 5 (row 5).
fn search_by_name<'a>(
    inputs: &LookupInputs<'a>,
    kind: Kind,
    runtime: &RuntimeFacts,
    evidence: &mut Vec<String>,
) -> IdentityFound<'a> {
    let Some(disc_name) = inputs.name else {
        evidence.push("the disc has no name: TMDb is not searched".to_string());
        return IdentityFound::at(IdentityStep::Nothing);
    };
    if disc_name.generic {
        evidence.push(format!("name '{}' is generic: TMDb is not searched", disc_name.raw));
        return IdentityFound::at(IdentityStep::Nothing);
    }
    let Some(search) = inputs.search else {
        evidence.push("no TMDb search answer is in hand".to_string());
        return IdentityFound::at(IdentityStep::Nothing);
    };
    let found = plausible_results(search, &disc_name.cleaned, evidence);
    let several = found.len() > 1;
    let every_plausible: Vec<tmdb::TmdbIdentity> = found.iter().map(|(identity, _)| *identity).collect();
    let picked = prefer_results(found, Some(kind), None, evidence);
    match picked.as_slice() {
        [] => IdentityFound::at(IdentityStep::Nothing),
        [(identity, result)] => {
            let runtime_check = check_runtime(*identity, inputs.record, runtime, disc_name.season, evidence);
            let step = if runtime_check == Some(true) && !several {
                IdentityStep::TmdbOne
            } else {
                IdentityStep::TmdbSeveral
            };
            IdentityFound {
                tmdb: Some(*identity),
                result: Some(*result),
                plausible: every_plausible,
                runtime_check,
                ..IdentityFound::at(step)
            }
        }
        _ => IdentityFound { plausible: every_plausible, ..IdentityFound::at(IdentityStep::TmdbSeveral) },
    }
}

/// The runtime check of `identity`'s own kind over its fetched record: None when no record of that identity is in
/// hand, or when the record has no runtime (a movie) or no episode runtime for the parsed season, or for the whole
/// series when none was parsed (a show). The evidence sentence of the last case names the season it looked in.
fn check_runtime(
    identity: tmdb::TmdbIdentity,
    record: Option<&tmdb::TmdbRecord>,
    runtime: &RuntimeFacts,
    season: Option<u32>,
    evidence: &mut Vec<String>,
) -> Option<bool> {
    let Some(record) = record.filter(|record| record.identity == identity) else {
        evidence.push(format!("no runtime check: no TMDb record for {}", identity_text(identity)));
        return None;
    };
    let outcome = match identity.kind {
        tmdb::TmdbKind::Movie => record.runtime.map(|minutes| movie_runtime_ok(runtime, Some(minutes))),
        tmdb::TmdbKind::Tv => {
            let minutes = record.episode_runtimes(season);
            if minutes.is_empty() {
                None
            } else {
                Some(tv_runtime_ok(runtime, &minutes))
            }
        }
    };
    evidence.push(match outcome {
        Some(true) => "the runtime check passes".to_string(),
        Some(false) => "the runtime check fails".to_string(),
        None => match (identity.kind, season) {
            (tmdb::TmdbKind::Movie, _) => {
                format!("no runtime check: the TMDb record for {} has no runtime", identity_text(identity))
            }
            (tmdb::TmdbKind::Tv, Some(n)) => format!(
                "no runtime check: the TMDb record for {} has no episode runtime for season {n}",
                identity_text(identity)
            ),
            (tmdb::TmdbKind::Tv, None) => {
                format!("no runtime check: the TMDb record for {} has no episode runtime", identity_text(identity))
            }
        },
    });
    outcome
}

/// Title, year and original language of the identity reached: from the fetched record when its identity is that one,
/// else from TheDiscDB's media, else from the one plausible result; the original language only from the record.
fn describe_identity(
    identity: Option<tmdb::TmdbIdentity>,
    record: Option<&tmdb::TmdbRecord>,
    media: Option<&discdb::DiscDbRecord>,
    result: Option<&tmdb::TmdbSearchResult>,
) -> (Option<String>, Option<i32>, Option<String>) {
    let Some(identity) = identity else {
        return (None, None, None);
    };
    if let Some(record) = record.filter(|record| record.identity == identity) {
        return (Some(record.title.clone()), record.year, record.original_language.clone());
    }
    if let Some((title, year)) = media.and_then(|media| media.title_and_year()) {
        return (Some(title), year, None);
    }
    if let Some(result) = result {
        let title = result.display_title();
        return ((!title.is_empty()).then(|| title.to_string()), result.year(), None);
    }
    (None, None, None)
}
```
