Not cross-task items, all private to this task: `kind::group_key`, `kind::concatenates`, `movie::LABEL_PREFIX`, `movie::split_language`, `movie::is_language_code`, `movie::cut_of`, `movie::label_text`, `movie::coverage`, `movie::same_edition_name`, `movie::item_edition`, `movie::find_word_ignoring_ascii_case`, `movie::EDITION_TRIM`, `movie::choose_title`, `movie::longest_group`, `movie::THEATRICAL_KEY`; `as_str`, `ALL` and `FromStr` on `KindSource`, `TitleRule` and `Mode` (the closed-set convention of the interfaces file); the test-only module `plan::fixtures`.

Where this task settles what the spec and the interfaces leave open (each choice is pinned by a test below):

1. **`MoviePlan` carries each feature's duration.** Rule 4 (`runtime_sanity(plan, runtime_min)`) compares "a feature's duration" with TMDb's runtime, but `Feature` holds no duration and `runtime_sanity` takes no `Disc`, so `MoviePlan` has the field `feature_seconds: Vec<Option<u32>>` (each feature's `Title::seconds`, in feature order), placed after `features` exactly as the interfaces file gives it; every function of this task fills it, and Task 7 may fill `RuntimeFacts.feature_seconds` from it. `Feature` keeps exactly its four fields, so code that builds a `Feature` (Task 13's call of `edition_names`) is unaffected.
2. **Rule 4 drops the plan only when every feature is off.** The interfaces say "every feature's duration is more than 10%"; the spec says "a feature chosen by rule 3". Rule 3 gives 0.85 only to a single feature, so the two readings differ only for a plan already at 0.60 with several features, where "every" avoids a second review on a disc of several films. A feature without a duration is never off; a runtime of 0 minutes is treated as unknown. The interfaces file records this reading as Open point 35 for the owner, and `runtime_sanity_holds_while_any_feature_is_close` pins it (with the spec's "any" reading its `one_close` case would drop to 0.60 with `title_ambiguous`).
3. **An unnamed cut is not theatrical; a cut named theatrical is.** `Feature.theatrical` is "true when `edition` is None or names the theatrical cut", which `is_theatrical` decides as a name containing the word Theatrical, ignoring ASCII case: 8.4 says only a cut the evidence names "as anything other than theatrical" always carries its name, so TheDiscDB's `Theatrical Version`, `Theatrical Edition` or `Theatrical` is the theatrical cut (filed without a name when alone, and keyed `theatrical` for earlier copies), pinned by `an_edition_naming_the_theatrical_cut_is_theatrical`. `is_theatrical` is public so Task 13 uses this one test rather than comparing with `THEATRICAL_CUT`; Task 7's `assigned_entries` still compares with the constant (an owner Cut named `Theatrical Version` is not theatrical there), and Task 13 Step 2 swaps that comparison for `is_theatrical`. The exception is an unnamed cut (a label with an unrecognised suffix, or a second TheDiscDB main movie without an edition name), whose edition is None and `theatrical` false: otherwise `edition_names` would file it as a second "Theatrical Cut". Its filed name stays None until the owner names it in review (8.4 "else from the owner in review").
4. **The edition a TheDiscDB item names.** The item title with the media title removed (the first occurrence that stands as whole words, compared ignoring ASCII case), then brackets, dashes, colons, commas and spaces trimmed from both ends; an item title that does not contain the media title is the edition whole; a record without a media title (the pinned form) names no edition from its items, since the film's own title cannot be told from an edition there.
5. **Label suffixes.** After `FPL_MainFeature` (optionally after `SEG_` or `SEG `) one `_` is dropped; a trailing `_XXX`, or a whole suffix `XXX`, of three ASCII letters that is a three-letter code of `lang::ISO639` (case-insensitive) is the language (`_EXT` is not one: `ext` is no code); the rest is compared case-insensitively with `R`, `UR`, `EXT`, `Narrative`; anything else is `Other` as written. A suffix that is only a language code is `Suffix::Language` and belongs to the cut without a suffix. The cuts `none` and `_R` stay two cuts, as the table's rows are read literally; since the table names both "Theatrical Cut", a disc carrying both labels is planned at 0.60 with `title_ambiguous` and the evidence sentence `two cuts are both named Theatrical Cut` rather than at 0.90, because two features of one edition name would file to colliding paths. The interfaces file asks the owner about it (Review Focus 8); `two_cuts_with_the_same_edition_name_are_ambiguous` pins it. Rule 1 has the same guard, through the same helper (`same_edition_name`, which compares the names `edition_names` would file: "Theatrical Cut" for every theatrical cut, else the edition, unnamed cuts skipped): TheDiscDB main movies `Film` and `Film (Theatrical Cut)` are both the theatrical cut, so `by_database` plans them at 0.60 with `title_ambiguous` and the same evidence sentence rather than at 0.98, pinned by `two_main_movies_with_the_same_edition_name_are_ambiguous`.
6. **Coverage of the wanted languages.** A variant covers English when one of its audio streams carries `eng`, and the original language when `Wanted.original_is_english` is false and one of its audio streams carries one of the original's codes; its coverage is the number of those two it covers.
7. **Rule 3.4's superset test** runs over the titles still in the running: those with chapters when any title of the group has chapters, else all of them. When several titles pass it (identical streams), the first in title order is chosen. A group where none passes keeps its first remaining title as the feature, at 0.60 with `title_ambiguous`.
8. **Groups.** A title with no segment map (attribute 26 absent) is a group of its own, keyed `#<title number>`, so two such titles never merge; so is a DVD title without attribute 24 (no pinned log has one), since its segment map alone (`1` is common, as a DVD's segments restart in every title) would merge it with another such title. A disc with no candidate title gives a structure plan with no feature, 0.60 and `title_ambiguous`.
9. **Play all** (8.3 rule 3.1) uses each other group at most once and never uses or tests a truncated group; a group whose segments equal one other group's (a map written `1-2` beside one written `1,2`) is not a play-all title. The parts may be any other groups taken in any group order, as long as their segments follow one another (Chernobyl disc 1's `4,11,12` is its groups `4`, `11` and `12`, which come in the reverse group order). On the pinned logs it finds Chernobyl disc 1's extras playlist `4,11,12`, Chernobyl disc 2's `11,12` and Smile's deleted-scenes playlist `596,597` (title 117), so on Smile rule 3 alone would answer TV; rules 1 and 2 come first there. This follows the spec literally, but any movie disc with an extras play-all and neither a TheDiscDB match nor Java labels would be planned as TV: the interfaces file asks the owner whether 3.1 should be limited to play-all titles made of episode-length groups (Review Focus 7), and `a_play_all_group_makes_the_structure_rule_answer_tv` pins the literal reading until then. Segment playlists count too: on the Expendables log 11 of title 41's 17 segments are candidate groups (SEG FPL_xx titles), and only its six segments under two minutes keep rule 3.1 from calling the feature itself a play-all title; a limit by episode length alone would not prevent that (segments 290 and 294 last 1574 and 1591 seconds), so the owner may prefer requiring the parts to pass structure_says_tv's 15% spread. `a_feature_whose_segments_are_listed_as_playlists_is_play_all_under_the_literal_reading` shows that consequence on a synthetic disc.
10. **Earlier filed copies.** `LibraryFacts.earlier_edition_names` maps a cut key (`theatrical`, or the lower-cased edition name) to the edition name that copy was filed under; an empty name means it was filed with no edition, and this cut then carries none either.

```rust
        parse_dischash(&corpus_text(&name), &name).expect("the answer parses").expect("the answer is a hit")
    }

    pub(crate) fn pinned_record(relative: &str) -> DiscDbRecord {
        serde_json::from_str(&corpus_text(relative)).expect("the pinned record parses")
    }
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the candidate filter**

In `crates/core/src/plan/kind.rs`, insert before the line `#[cfg(test)]`:

```rust
/// 8.2's candidate filter: menu loops out (`is_menu_loop`), titles shorter than settings.minlength_s out, titles without a
/// duration out; the rest in title order. Reads `settings.minlength_s` only. Def: T5. Use: T5, T7, phase 2 (6.3 step 6a's
/// fallback list, 11's Assign titles).
pub fn candidate_filter(disc: &Disc, settings: &Settings) -> Vec<u32> {
    disc.titles
        .values()
        .filter(|title| !is_menu_loop(title))
        .filter(|title| title.seconds.map_or(false, |seconds| seconds >= settings.minlength_s))
        .map(|title| title.number)
        .collect()
}

/// A title with no audio stream, with more than one chapter every two minutes (`chapters as f64 > seconds as f64 / 120.0`, 0 s
/// counts as a loop when it has chapters, and so does a title without a duration), or whose segment map repeats one clip
/// (every segment equal and two or more of them). Spec 8.2. Def: T5. Use: T5.
pub fn is_menu_loop(title: &Title) -> bool {
    if title.streams_of(StreamKind::Audio).is_empty() {
        return true;
    }
    let seconds = f64::from(title.seconds.unwrap_or(0));
    if f64::from(title.chapters) > seconds / 120.0 {
        return true;
    }
    title.segments.len() >= 2 && title.segments.iter().all(|&segment| segment == title.segments[0])
}
```

```rust
    fn group(key: &str, map: &str, titles: &[u32], seconds: u32) -> Group {

            segment_map: map.to_string(),

            truncated: false,
```

```rust
/// Titles with identical segment maps (8.2). On a DVD the key is (attribute 24, segment map) because its segments restart at
/// 1 in every title (Review Focus 1); attribute 24 is unique per DVD title, so on a DVD every title is its own group. Def: T5. Use: T5, T6, T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Group {
    /// The group's key as text ("280,284,299" or, on a DVD, "01:1-29"); "#<title number>" for a title with no segment map,
    /// and for a DVD title without attribute 24.
    pub key: String,
    /// The representative's attribute 26 as the scan wrote it.
    pub segment_map: String,
    /// `audio::titles::segments` of it.
    pub segments: Vec<i64>,
    /// The members in title order; the first is the representative.
    pub titles: Vec<u32>,
    /// "a group's duration is that of its titles": the longest member's seconds.
    pub seconds: u32,
    /// The segment map ends in "..." (MakeMKV truncated it).
    pub truncated: bool,
}

/// The groups of `candidates`, in order of first title. A candidate the disc lacks is skipped; a title without a segment
/// map is a group of its own, and so is a DVD title without attribute 24. Spec 8.2. Def: T5. Use: T5, T6, T7.
pub fn groups(disc: &Disc, candidates: &[u32]) -> Vec<Group> {
    let mut found: Vec<Group> = Vec::new();
    for &number in candidates {
        let Some(title) = disc.titles.get(&number) else {
            continue;
        };
        let key = group_key(title, disc.is_dvd);
        let seconds = title.seconds.unwrap_or(0);
        match found.iter_mut().find(|group| group.key == key) {
            Some(group) => {
                group.titles.push(number);
                group.seconds = group.seconds.max(seconds);
            }
            None => found.push(Group {
                key,
                segment_map: title.segment_map.clone(),
                segments: title.segments.clone(),
                titles: vec![number],
                seconds,
                truncated: title.truncated,
            }),
        }
    }
    found
}

/// A title's group key: its segment map; on a DVD prefixed by its DVD title number (attribute 24) and ':'; "#<number>"
/// when it has no segment map, or is a DVD title without attribute 24, so such titles never merge.
fn group_key(title: &Title, dvd: bool) -> String {
    if title.segment_map.is_empty() {
        return format!("#{}", title.number);
    }
    if dvd {
        match title.dvd_title.as_deref() {
            Some(number) => format!("{number}:{}", title.segment_map),
            None => format!("#{}", title.number),
        }
    } else {
        title.segment_map.clone()
    }
}
```

The play-all test with `2,1` expects `Some(2)`: the parts may come from the other groups in any group order, only the segments must follow in order (`2,1` is group `2` then group `1`). The case `a_missing_part` (`2,3,1`) fails because no group is `3`. The case `interleaved` (`1,3,2,4`) holds every segment of the groups `1,2` and `3,4`, but not one group's segments after the other's, so it is not a play-all title: a matcher that compared segment sets instead of sequences would accept it.

```rust
/// Spec 8.2: the shortest episode length, 15 minutes, included.
pub const EPISODE_MIN_S: u32 = 15 * 60;
/// Spec 8.2: the longest episode length, 120 minutes, included.
pub const EPISODE_MAX_S: u32 = 120 * 60;
/// Spec 8.2: the longest episode-length group is at most 15% longer than the shortest.
pub const TV_SPREAD: f64 = 0.15;

/// The groups lasting between 15 and 120 minutes inclusive, in group order. Spec 8.2. Def: T5. Use: T5, T6, T7 (fills
/// RuntimeFacts.episode_group_seconds).
pub fn episode_length_groups(groups: &[Group]) -> Vec<&Group> {
    groups.iter().filter(|group| (EPISODE_MIN_S..=EPISODE_MAX_S).contains(&group.seconds)).collect()
}

/// Three or more episode-length groups and the longest at most 15% longer than the shortest (`longest <= shortest * 1.15`).
/// Spec 8.2. Def: T5. Use: T5.
pub fn structure_says_tv(groups: &[Group]) -> bool {
    let episodes = episode_length_groups(groups);
    if episodes.len() < 3 {
        return false;
    }
    let shortest = episodes.iter().map(|group| group.seconds).min().unwrap_or(0);
    let longest = episodes.iter().map(|group| group.seconds).max().unwrap_or(0);
    f64::from(longest) <= f64::from(shortest) * (1.0 + TV_SPREAD)
}

/// Spec 8.3 rule 3.1: the index of a group whose segment list is the concatenation of two or more other groups' lists, whose
/// segments follow one another in the whole list (the parts may be any other groups in any group order, each used once;
/// truncated groups never count); None when none is. Not applied on a DVD (segments restart per title). A truncated group
/// is never the play-all title either. The first such group in group order is returned. Def: T5. Use: T5, T6.
pub fn play_all(groups: &[Group], dvd: bool) -> Option<usize> {
    if dvd {
        return None;
    }
    (0..groups.len()).find(|&index| {
        let whole = &groups[index];
        if whole.truncated || whole.segments.is_empty() {
            return false;
        }
        let mut used = vec![false; groups.len()];
        used[index] = true;
        concatenates(&whole.segments, groups, &mut used, 0)
    })
}

/// True when `rest` is the segments of two or more (counting `parts` already taken) unused, untruncated, non-empty groups
/// one after another.
fn concatenates(rest: &[i64], groups: &[Group], used: &mut [bool], parts: usize) -> bool {
    if rest.is_empty() {
        return parts >= 2;
    }
    for (index, group) in groups.iter().enumerate() {
        if used[index] || group.truncated || group.segments.is_empty() || !rest.starts_with(&group.segments) {
            continue;
        }
        used[index] = true;
        if concatenates(&rest[group.segments.len()..], groups, used, parts + 1) {
            return true;
        }
        used[index] = false;
    }
    false
}

/// How the kind was decided (8.2's three sources plus the movie default and 8.3 rule 3.1's play-all). Def: T5. Use: T7.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum KindSource {
    Discdb,
    Structure,
    SeasonMarker,
    PlayAll,
    Default,
}

impl KindSource {
    /// Every source, in the order 8.2 and 8.3 rule 3.1 name them.
    pub const ALL: [KindSource; 5] =
        [KindSource::Discdb, KindSource::Structure, KindSource::SeasonMarker, KindSource::PlayAll, KindSource::Default];

    /// The serde spelling.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            KindSource::Discdb => "discdb",
            KindSource::Structure => "structure",
            KindSource::SeasonMarker => "season_marker",
            KindSource::PlayAll => "play_all",
            KindSource::Default => "default",
        }
    }
}

impl std::str::FromStr for KindSource {
    type Err = String;

    /// Only the `as_str` spellings.
    fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<KindSource, String> {
        KindSource::ALL
            .into_iter()
            .find(|source| source.as_str() == text)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("'{text}' is not a kind source"))
    }
}

/// 8.2's decision: TheDiscDB's kind when it knows the disc; else Tv when structure_says_tv or the name has a season marker;
/// else Movie. (Rule 3.1's play-all turns a Movie into Tv later, in plan::plan.) Def: T5. Use: T7.
pub fn disc_kind(discdb: Option<&DiscDbRecord>, groups: &[Group], name: Option<&DiscName>) -> (Kind, KindSource) {
    if let Some(kind) = discdb.and_then(|record| record.kind()) {
        return (kind, KindSource::Discdb);
    }
    if structure_says_tv(groups) {
        return (Kind::Tv, KindSource::Structure);
    }
    if name.map_or(false, |name| name.season_marker) {
        return (Kind::Tv, KindSource::SeasonMarker);
    }
    (Kind::Movie, KindSource::Default)
}

```

In `crates/core/src/plan/movie.rs`, insert before the line `#[cfg(test)]`:

```rust
/// What every label starts with (8.3 rule 2), after an optional `SEG_` or `SEG `.
const LABEL_PREFIX: &str = "FPL_MainFeature";

/// The edition name of the theatrical or main cut (8.3 rule 2's table, 8.4). Def: T5. Use: T7, T13.
pub const THEATRICAL_CUT: &str = "Theatrical Cut";

/// 8.3 rule 2's suffix table. `Language` is a suffix that is only a language code (a dub variant of the cut without a
/// suffix); `Other` keeps the suffix as written. Def: T5. Use: T5.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Suffix {
    None,
    R,
    Ur,
    Ext,
    Narrative,
    Language(String),
    Other(String),
}

/// One parsed FPL_MainFeature label (8.3 rule 2): the scan title it is on, its suffix, and the three-letter language code
/// split off its end (lower-cased). Def: T5. Use: T5.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Label {
    pub title: u32,
    pub suffix: Suffix,
    pub language: Option<String>,
}

/// A title comment (attribute 49) starting `FPL_MainFeature` (optionally preceded by `SEG_` or `SEG `): its suffix, with a
/// trailing `_XXX` three-letter language code split off as `language`. None for any other comment. One `_` after the prefix
/// is dropped; `R`, `UR`, `EXT` and `Narrative` are compared ignoring ASCII case; a three-letter code counts when it is one
/// of `lang::ISO639`'s. Def: T5. Use: T5.
pub fn parse_label(title: u32, comment: &str) -> Option<Label> {
    let text = comment.strip_prefix("SEG_").or_else(|| comment.strip_prefix("SEG ")).unwrap_or(comment);
    let rest = text.strip_prefix(LABEL_PREFIX)?;
    let rest = rest.strip_prefix('_').unwrap_or(rest);
    let (body, language) = split_language(rest);
    let suffix = match body.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
        "" => match &language {
            Some(code) => Suffix::Language(code.clone()),
            None => Suffix::None,
        },
        "r" => Suffix::R,
        "ur" => Suffix::Ur,
        "ext" => Suffix::Ext,
        "narrative" => Suffix::Narrative,
        _ => Suffix::Other(body.to_string()),
    };
    Some(Label { title, suffix, language })
}

/// The suffix without its trailing language code, and that code lower-cased: the whole suffix when it is a code, else the
/// part after its last `_` when that is one.
fn split_language(rest: &str) -> (&str, Option<String>) {
    if is_language_code(rest) {
        return ("", Some(rest.to_ascii_lowercase()));
    }
    if let Some(at) = rest.rfind('_') {
        let code = &rest[at + 1..];
        if is_language_code(code) {
            return (&rest[..at], Some(code.to_ascii_lowercase()));
        }
    }
    (rest, None)
}

/// Three ASCII letters that, lower-cased, are one of the three-letter codes of `lang::ISO639`.
fn is_language_code(text: &str) -> bool {
    if text.len() != 3 || !text.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_alphabetic()) {
        return false;
    }
    let code = text.to_ascii_lowercase();
    ISO639.iter().any(|(_, codes)| codes.contains(&code.as_str()))
}

/// The table's edition name: None and R "Theatrical Cut", Ur "Unrated Cut", Ext "Extended Cut"; Narrative and Language give
/// None (ignored or a variant), Other gives None (an unnamed cut). Def: T5. Use: T5.
pub fn edition_of(suffix: &Suffix) -> Option<&'static str> {
    match suffix {
        Suffix::None | Suffix::R => Some(THEATRICAL_CUT),
        Suffix::Ur => Some("Unrated Cut"),
        Suffix::Ext => Some("Extended Cut"),
        Suffix::Narrative | Suffix::Language(_) | Suffix::Other(_) => None,
    }
}
```

```rust
    fn record(media_title: Option<&str>, items: &[&str]) -> DiscDbRecord {
```

```rust
/// Which rule of 8.3 chose the features. Def: T5. Use: T7.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum TitleRule {
    Database,
    Labels,
    Structure,
}

impl TitleRule {
    /// The three rules, in 8.3's order.
    pub const ALL: [TitleRule; 3] = [TitleRule::Database, TitleRule::Labels, TitleRule::Structure];

    /// The serde spelling.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            TitleRule::Database => "database",
            TitleRule::Labels => "labels",
            TitleRule::Structure => "structure",
        }
    }
}

impl std::str::FromStr for TitleRule {
    type Err = String;

    /// Only the `as_str` spellings.
    fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<TitleRule, String> {
        TitleRule::ALL.into_iter().find(|rule| rule.as_str() == text).ok_or_else(|| format!("'{text}' is not a title rule"))
    }
}

/// Spec 8.3 rule 1: the disc database names the title, 0.98.
pub const DATABASE_TITLE_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.98;
/// Spec 8.3 rule 2: exactly one cut, or two or more cuts with different recognised suffixes, 0.90.
pub const LABELS_TITLE_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.90;
/// Spec 8.3 rule 3.5: one rival, which is the feature, 0.85.
pub const STRUCTURE_TITLE_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.85;
/// Spec 8.3: every ambiguous outcome (an unnamed cut, an ambiguous group, several rivals), 0.60.
pub const AMBIGUOUS_TITLE_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.60;
/// Spec 8.3 rule 3.3: a kept group within 10% of the longest kept group's duration is a rival.
pub const RIVAL_BAND: f64 = 0.10;
/// Spec 8.3 rule 3.6: rivals whose segment difference is at most 0.25 cannot be told apart.
pub const SEGMENT_DIFFERENCE_MAX: f64 = 0.25;
/// Spec 8.3 rule 4: a structural feature more than 10% from TMDb's runtime is in doubt.
pub const RUNTIME_SANITY_BAND: f64 = 0.10;

/// One feature or cut to rip. Spec 8.3, 8.4. Def: T5. Use: T7, T11, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Feature {
    pub title: u32,
    /// The edition name as the evidence gives it (TheDiscDB's item title beyond the media title, else the label table, or
    /// None for the theatrical or only cut); `edition_names` turns it into the filed name.
    pub edition: Option<String>,
    /// True when `edition` is None or names the theatrical cut (contains the word Theatrical; `is_theatrical`), except an
    /// unnamed cut (an Other label suffix, or a later TheDiscDB MainMovie with no edition), which has edition None and
    /// theatrical false.
    pub theatrical: bool,
    /// The titles of its group (rule 3) or cut (rule 2) that were not chosen.
    pub siblings: Vec<u32>,
}

/// The movie titles of 8.3 with their confidence and reasons. Def: T5. Use: T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct MoviePlan {
    pub rule: TitleRule,
    pub features: Vec<Feature>,
    /// Each feature's duration (`Title::seconds`), in feature order; rule 4 reads it, and the planner may fill
    /// `RuntimeFacts.feature_seconds` from it.
    pub feature_seconds: Vec<Option<u32>>,
    pub confidence: f64,
    pub reviews: Vec<ReviewReason>,
    pub notes: Vec<Noted>,
    /// Rule 3's rival groups (keys), for the evidence and the runtime facts.
    pub rivals: Vec<String>,
    pub evidence: Vec<String>,
}

/// Rule 1: applies only when TheDiscDB marks at least one MainMovie and every MainMovie title matches a scan title in
/// `matches`; one Feature per MainMovie, in database index order (0.98). Each Feature's edition is its item title with the
/// media title and surrounding brackets or dashes removed; when that leaves nothing, `disc.java_in_use` holds and the scan
/// title's comment (attribute 49) parses as a label, `edition_of(label.suffix)` (8.4 "else from the label table":
/// Expendables 3's title 41 `FPL_MainFeature_UR` gets "Unrated Cut"); `theatrical` as Feature's doc says. Two or more
/// MainMovies of which a later one still has no edition: 0.60 with unnamed_cut; two features given the same edition name
/// make it 0.60 with title_ambiguous (Review Focus 8). None when TheDiscDB marks no main movie or any MainMovie title does
/// not reconcile. Def: T5. Use: T5, T7.
pub fn by_database(record: &DiscDbRecord, matches: &BTreeMap<u32, u32>, disc: &Disc) -> Option<MoviePlan> {
    let main_movies = record.main_movies();
    if main_movies.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let media_title = record.media.as_ref().and_then(|media| media.title.as_deref());
    let mut features = Vec::new();
    let mut feature_seconds = Vec::new();
    let mut evidence = Vec::new();
    let mut unnamed = false;
    for (position, main_movie) in main_movies.iter().enumerate() {
        let number = *matches.get(&main_movie.index)?;
        let title = disc.titles.get(&number)?;
        evidence.push(format!("TheDiscDB's main movie {} is scan title {number}", main_movie.index));
        let item_title = main_movie.item.as_ref().map_or("", |item| item.title.as_str());
        let mut edition = item_edition(item_title, media_title);
        if let Some(name) = &edition {
            evidence.push(format!("edition '{name}' from TheDiscDB's item title '{item_title}'"));
        } else if disc.java_in_use {
            if let Some(comment) = title.comment.as_deref() {
                if let Some(label) = parse_label(number, comment) {
                    edition = edition_of(&label.suffix).map(str::to_string);
                    if let Some(name) = &edition {
                        evidence.push(format!("edition '{name}' from the label {comment} of title {number}"));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        let later_unnamed = position > 0 && edition.is_none();
        if later_unnamed {
            unnamed = true;
            evidence.push(format!("scan title {number} is a further main movie with no edition name"));
        }
        let theatrical = !later_unnamed && is_theatrical(edition.as_deref());
        features.push(Feature { title: number, edition, theatrical, siblings: Vec::new() });
        feature_seconds.push(title.seconds);
    }
    // Two main movies given the same edition name would file to one path (Review Focus 8).
    let same_name = same_edition_name(&features);
    if let Some(name) = &same_name {
        evidence.push(format!("two cuts are both named {name}"));
    }
    let mut reviews = Vec::new();
    if unnamed {
        reviews.push(ReviewReason::UnnamedCut);
    }
    if same_name.is_some() {
        reviews.push(ReviewReason::TitleAmbiguous);
    }
    let confidence = if reviews.is_empty() { DATABASE_TITLE_CONFIDENCE } else { AMBIGUOUS_TITLE_CONFIDENCE };
    Some(MoviePlan {
        rule: TitleRule::Database,
        features,
        feature_seconds,
        confidence,
        reviews: sorted_unique(reviews),
        notes: Vec::new(),
        rivals: Vec::new(),
        evidence,
    })
}

/// An edition name that names the theatrical or main cut (8.4): none at all, or a name containing the word Theatrical
/// (ignoring ASCII case), such as TheDiscDB's "Theatrical Version". The one test of "theatrical" for every rule and caller.
/// Def: T5. Use: T5, T13.
pub fn is_theatrical(edition: Option<&str>) -> bool {
    edition.map_or(true, |name| find_word_ignoring_ascii_case(name, "theatrical").is_some())
}

/// The first edition name two features would both be filed under (8.4, as `edition_names` names them): "Theatrical Cut"
/// for a theatrical cut, else its edition; an unnamed cut (not theatrical, no edition) is skipped. Rules 1 and 2 lower
/// their confidence when there is one, since two features of one name would file to one path (Review Focus 8).
fn same_edition_name(features: &[Feature]) -> Option<String> {
    let mut named: BTreeSet<&str> = BTreeSet::new();
    features
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|feature| if feature.theatrical { Some(THEATRICAL_CUT) } else { feature.edition.as_deref() })
        .find(|name| !named.insert(*name))
        .map(str::to_string)
}

/// What is trimmed from both ends of an item title once the media title is out: brackets, hyphens, en and em dashes,
/// colons and commas (spaces too).
const EDITION_TRIM: &str = "()[]-:,\u{2013}\u{2014}";

/// The edition an item title names beyond the media title (8.4 "Edition names come from TheDiscDB's title for the item"):
/// the item title with the media title's first whole-word occurrence (ignoring ASCII case) removed, then `EDITION_TRIM`
/// and spaces trimmed from both ends; an item title that does not contain the media title is the edition whole. None when
/// nothing is left, or when there is no media title (the pinned form), since the film's own title cannot be told from an
/// edition there.
fn item_edition(item_title: &str, media_title: Option<&str>) -> Option<String> {
    let media = media_title.map(str::trim).filter(|media| !media.is_empty())?;
    let item = item_title.trim();
    let rest = match find_word_ignoring_ascii_case(item, media) {
        Some(at) => format!("{}{}", &item[..at], &item[at + media.len()..]),
        None => item.to_string(),
    };
    let edition = rest.trim_matches(|c: char| c.is_whitespace() || EDITION_TRIM.contains(c));
    (!edition.is_empty()).then(|| edition.to_string())
}

/// The byte offset of the first occurrence of `needle` in `haystack` that equals it ignoring ASCII case and is neither
/// preceded nor followed by a letter or digit.
fn find_word_ignoring_ascii_case(haystack: &str, needle: &str) -> Option<usize> {
    let last = haystack.len().checked_sub(needle.len())?;
    (0..=last).find(|&at| {
        let end = at + needle.len();
        haystack.is_char_boundary(at)
            && haystack.is_char_boundary(end)
            && haystack[at..end].eq_ignore_ascii_case(needle)
            && !haystack[..at].chars().next_back().map_or(false, char::is_alphanumeric)
            && !haystack[end..].chars().next().map_or(false, char::is_alphanumeric)
    })
}
```

```rust
/// Rule 2: only when `disc.java_in_use`; labels grouped by suffix without the language code, one cut per group, in order of
/// each cut's lowest title number; within a cut the variant whose audio covers the most of `wanted`'s languages, then the
/// one without a language suffix, then the lower title number; Narrative variants ignored. Exactly one cut 0.90; several
/// with recognised suffixes 0.90 as editions, except that two cuts given the same edition name (the `none` and `_R` rows
/// are both "Theatrical Cut") make it 0.60 with title_ambiguous (Review Focus 8); any Other suffix 0.60 with unnamed_cut.
/// None when no label is found. When Java was not reported, returns None and plan::plan adds the note
/// LabelRuleUnavailable. Def: T5. Use: T5, T7.
pub fn by_labels(disc: &Disc, wanted: &Wanted) -> Option<MoviePlan> {
    if !disc.java_in_use {
        return None;
    }
    let labels: Vec<(Label, &Title)> = disc
        .titles
        .values()
        .filter_map(|title| parse_label(title.number, title.comment.as_deref()?).map(|label| (label, title)))
        .filter(|(label, _)| label.suffix != Suffix::Narrative)
        .collect();
    if labels.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    // The labels are in title order, so a cut's first label is its lowest title number.
    let mut cuts: Vec<(Suffix, Vec<usize>)> = Vec::new();
    for (index, (label, _)) in labels.iter().enumerate() {
        let cut = cut_of(&label.suffix);
        match cuts.iter_mut().find(|(key, _)| *key == cut) {
            Some((_, members)) => members.push(index),
            None => cuts.push((cut, vec![index])),
        }
    }
    let mut features = Vec::new();
    let mut feature_seconds = Vec::new();
    let mut evidence = Vec::new();
    let mut unnamed = false;
    for (cut, members) in &cuts {
        let chosen = *members.iter().max_by_key(|&&index| {
            let (label, title) = &labels[index];
            (coverage(title, wanted), label.language.is_none(), std::cmp::Reverse(label.title))
        })?;
        let (label, title) = &labels[chosen];
        let titles: Vec<u32> = members.iter().map(|&index| labels[index].0.title).collect();
        evidence.push(format!("label cut {}: titles {titles:?}, title {} chosen", label_text(cut), label.title));
        let edition = edition_of(cut).map(str::to_string);
        let is_unnamed = matches!(cut, Suffix::Other(_));
        unnamed |= is_unnamed;
        let theatrical = !is_unnamed && is_theatrical(edition.as_deref());
        let siblings = titles.iter().copied().filter(|&number| number != label.title).collect();
        features.push(Feature { title: label.title, edition, theatrical, siblings });
        feature_seconds.push(title.seconds);
    }
    // Two cuts given the same edition name (the table's `none` and `_R` rows) would file to one path (Review Focus 8).
    let same_name = same_edition_name(&features);
    let mut reviews = Vec::new();
    if unnamed {
        reviews.push(ReviewReason::UnnamedCut);
    }
    if let Some(name) = &same_name {
        reviews.push(ReviewReason::TitleAmbiguous);
        evidence.push(format!("two cuts are both named {name}"));
    }
    let confidence = if reviews.is_empty() { LABELS_TITLE_CONFIDENCE } else { AMBIGUOUS_TITLE_CONFIDENCE };
    Some(MoviePlan {
        rule: TitleRule::Labels,
        features,
        feature_seconds,
        confidence,
        reviews: sorted_unique(reviews),
        notes: Vec::new(),
        rivals: Vec::new(),
        evidence,
    })
}

/// The cut a suffix belongs to: a dub variant (a suffix that is only a language code) belongs to the cut without a suffix.
fn cut_of(suffix: &Suffix) -> Suffix {
    match suffix {
        Suffix::Language(_) => Suffix::None,
        other => other.clone(),
    }
}

/// A cut's label as a disc writes it, for the evidence.
fn label_text(cut: &Suffix) -> String {
    match cut {
        Suffix::None => LABEL_PREFIX.to_string(),
        Suffix::R => format!("{LABEL_PREFIX}_R"),
        Suffix::Ur => format!("{LABEL_PREFIX}_UR"),
        Suffix::Ext => format!("{LABEL_PREFIX}_EXT"),
        Suffix::Narrative => format!("{LABEL_PREFIX}_Narrative"),
        Suffix::Language(code) => format!("{LABEL_PREFIX}_{}", code.to_ascii_uppercase()),
        Suffix::Other(text) => format!("{LABEL_PREFIX}_{text}"),
    }
}

/// How many of the wanted languages a title's audio covers: English when an audio stream carries an English code, and the
/// original language when it is not English and an audio stream carries one of its codes (8.3 rule 2, 8.6 "Languages").
fn coverage(title: &Title, wanted: &Wanted) -> usize {
    let audio = title.streams_of(StreamKind::Audio);
    let languages: Vec<&str> = audio.iter().filter_map(|stream| stream.language.as_deref()).collect();
    let english = languages.iter().any(|code| wanted.english.iter().any(|english| english == code));
    let original = !wanted.original_is_english && languages.iter().any(|code| wanted.is_original(code));
    usize::from(english) + usize::from(original)
}
```

```rust
/// What rule 3 found. Def: T5. Use: T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum StructureOutcome {
    /// Rule 3.1: the group at this index of the groups is a "play all" title, so the disc is TV (8.5).
    PlayAll { group: usize },
    Plan(MoviePlan),
}

/// Rule 3 on the groups: 3.1 play-all (the disc is TV); 3.2 keep groups >= settings.feature_min_minutes, else the longest; 3.3
/// rivals within RIVAL_BAND of the longest kept; 3.4 in each rival the title with chapters, then the one whose audio and
/// subtitle stream signatures (kind, language, codec family, channels) are a superset of every other's, else 0.60
/// title_ambiguous; 3.5 one rival 0.85; 3.6 every pair's segment_difference <= 0.25 gives 0.60 title_ambiguous; 3.7 else 0.60
/// multiple_features. Reads `settings.feature_min_minutes` only. No group at all (no candidate) gives a plan with no
/// feature, 0.60 and title_ambiguous. Def: T5. Use: T5, T7.
pub fn by_structure(disc: &Disc, groups: &[Group], settings: &Settings) -> StructureOutcome {
    if let Some(group) = play_all(groups, disc.is_dvd) {
        return StructureOutcome::PlayAll { group };
    }
    if groups.is_empty() {
        return StructureOutcome::Plan(MoviePlan {
            rule: TitleRule::Structure,
            features: Vec::new(),
            feature_seconds: Vec::new(),
            confidence: AMBIGUOUS_TITLE_CONFIDENCE,
            reviews: vec![ReviewReason::TitleAmbiguous],
            notes: Vec::new(),
            rivals: Vec::new(),
            evidence: vec!["no title passed the candidate filter".to_string()],
        });
    }
    let mut evidence = Vec::new();
    let minimum = u64::from(settings.feature_min_minutes) * 60;
    let long: Vec<&Group> = groups.iter().filter(|group| u64::from(group.seconds) >= minimum).collect();
    let kept: Vec<&Group> = if long.is_empty() {
        let longest = longest_group(groups);
        evidence.push(format!(
            "no group is at least {} minutes long; the longest, {}, is kept",
            settings.feature_min_minutes, longest.key
        ));
        vec![longest]
    } else {
        evidence.push(format!(
            "groups at least {} minutes long: {} of {}",
            settings.feature_min_minutes,
            long.len(),
            groups.len()
        ));
        long
    };
    let longest = kept.iter().map(|group| group.seconds).max().unwrap_or(0);
    let rivals: Vec<&Group> = kept
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|group| within(f64::from(group.seconds), f64::from(longest), RIVAL_BAND))
        .collect();
    let mut features = Vec::new();
    let mut feature_seconds = Vec::new();
    let mut reviews = Vec::new();
    for group in &rivals {
        let (chosen, how, clear) = choose_title(disc, group);
        if !clear {
            reviews.push(ReviewReason::TitleAmbiguous);
        }
        evidence.push(format!("rival group {}: title {chosen} ({how})", group.key));
        let siblings = group.titles.iter().copied().filter(|&number| number != chosen).collect();
        features.push(Feature { title: chosen, edition: None, theatrical: true, siblings });
        feature_seconds.push(disc.titles.get(&chosen).and_then(|title| title.seconds));
    }
    if rivals.len() >= 2 {
        let mut largest: f64 = 0.0;
        for (index, first) in rivals.iter().enumerate() {
            for second in &rivals[index + 1..] {
                largest = largest.max(segment_difference(&first.segments, &second.segments));
            }
        }
        evidence.push(format!(
            "{} rivals; the largest segment difference between two of them is {largest:.2}",
            rivals.len()
        ));
        reviews.push(if largest <= SEGMENT_DIFFERENCE_MAX {
            ReviewReason::TitleAmbiguous
        } else {
            ReviewReason::MultipleFeatures
        });
    }
    let confidence = if rivals.len() == 1 && reviews.is_empty() {
        STRUCTURE_TITLE_CONFIDENCE
    } else {
        AMBIGUOUS_TITLE_CONFIDENCE
    };
    StructureOutcome::Plan(MoviePlan {
        rule: TitleRule::Structure,
        features,
        feature_seconds,
        confidence,
        reviews: sorted_unique(reviews),
        notes: Vec::new(),
        rivals: rivals.iter().map(|group| group.key.clone()).collect(),
        evidence,
    })
}

/// The first group with the longest duration (`groups` is not empty).
fn longest_group(groups: &[Group]) -> &Group {
    let mut longest = &groups[0];
    for group in &groups[1..] {
        if group.seconds > longest.seconds {
            longest = group;
        }
    }
    longest
}

/// Rule 3.4 within one rival group: (the title chosen, how, whether the choice is clear). A group of one title is clear;
/// otherwise the titles with chapters stay in the running when any has chapters (all of them when none has), one left is
/// chosen, and among several the first whose stream signatures are a superset of every other remaining title's is chosen;
/// when none is, the first remaining title is kept and the choice is not clear.
fn choose_title(disc: &Disc, group: &Group) -> (u32, &'static str, bool) {
    let members: Vec<&Title> = group.titles.iter().filter_map(|number| disc.titles.get(number)).collect();
    if members.len() <= 1 {
        return (group.titles[0], "its only title", true);
    }
    let with_chapters: Vec<&Title> = members.iter().copied().filter(|title| title.chapters > 0).collect();
    let remaining = if with_chapters.is_empty() { members } else { with_chapters };
    if remaining.len() == 1 {
        return (remaining[0].number, "the title with chapters", true);
    }
    let signatures: Vec<BTreeSet<_>> = remaining.iter().map(|title| title.signature_set()).collect();
    let covering = (0..remaining.len()).find(|&index| {
        (0..remaining.len()).all(|other| other == index || signatures[index].is_superset(&signatures[other]))
    });
    match covering {
        Some(index) => (remaining[index].number, "its streams cover every other title's", true),
        None => (remaining[0].number, "no title's streams cover every other's", false),
    }
}

/// Segments in exactly one of the two lists, divided by the longer list's length; 0.0 for two empty lists. Spec 8.3 rule 3.6. Def: T5. Use: T5.
pub fn segment_difference(a: &[i64], b: &[i64]) -> f64 {
    let longer = a.len().max(b.len());
    if longer == 0 {
        return 0.0;
    }
    let left: BTreeSet<i64> = a.iter().copied().collect();
    let right: BTreeSet<i64> = b.iter().copied().collect();
    left.symmetric_difference(&right).count() as f64 / longer as f64
}
```

- [ ] **Step 32: Write rule 4 and the rule order**

In `crates/core/src/plan/movie.rs`, insert before the line `#[cfg(test)]`:

```rust
/// Rule 4: a plan from rule 3 whose every feature's duration (`plan.feature_seconds`) is more than 10% from
/// `runtime_min * 60` drops to 0.60 with title_ambiguous (Open point 35); rule 1 and 2 plans and None runtimes are
/// returned unchanged. A runtime of 0 minutes counts as none, and a feature without a duration is never more than 10% off,
/// so a plan with one keeps its confidence. Def: T5. Use: T7.
pub fn runtime_sanity(mut plan: MoviePlan, runtime_min: Option<u32>) -> MoviePlan {
    let runtime = match runtime_min {
        Some(runtime) if runtime > 0 => runtime,
        _ => return plan,
    };
    if plan.rule != TitleRule::Structure || plan.feature_seconds.is_empty() {
        return plan;
    }
    let target = f64::from(runtime) * 60.0;
    let every_feature_off = plan
        .feature_seconds
        .iter()
        .all(|seconds| seconds.map_or(false, |seconds| !within(f64::from(seconds), target, RUNTIME_SANITY_BAND)));
    if !every_feature_off {
        return plan;
    }
    plan.confidence = plan.confidence.min(AMBIGUOUS_TITLE_CONFIDENCE);
    plan.reviews.push(ReviewReason::TitleAmbiguous);
    plan.reviews = sorted_unique(plan.reviews);
    plan.evidence.push(format!("no feature is within 10% of the TMDb runtime of {runtime} minutes"));
    plan
}

/// First applicable rule (8.3): by_database, else by_labels, else by_structure. Def: T5. Use: T7.
pub fn movie_plan(disc: &Disc, discdb: Option<&DiscDbRecord>, matches: &BTreeMap<u32, u32>, groups: &[Group], wanted: &Wanted, settings: &Settings) -> StructureOutcome {
    if let Some(plan) = discdb.and_then(|record| by_database(record, matches, disc)) {
        return StructureOutcome::Plan(plan);
    }
    if let Some(plan) = by_labels(disc, wanted) {
        return StructureOutcome::Plan(plan);
    }
    by_structure(disc, groups, settings)
}
```

```rust
/// What phase 2 reads from the library for 8.4 (RP18). Def: T5. Use: T7, T11, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct LibraryFacts {
    /// "the film's library folder already holds an edition-named file".
    pub folder_has_edition_named_file: bool,
    /// Earlier filed copies of this film: cut key ("theatrical", or the lower-cased edition name) to the edition name used
    /// ("" when that copy was filed without an edition name; this cut then gets None).
    pub earlier_edition_names: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    /// Spec 7: the final path already exists and is not this job's file. Phase 2 checks the plain path (no copy label);
    /// under the owner's Resolve collision "keep both" it must also check the copy-labelled path (`- 2160p 2`) before
    /// filing and hold the job with path_collision when that one is taken too (Open point 39).
    pub path_collision: bool,
}

/// The cut key of the theatrical or main cut in `LibraryFacts.earlier_edition_names`.
const THEATRICAL_KEY: &str = "theatrical";

/// 8.4's three rules, per feature in order: a non-theatrical cut always carries its name, even when it is the only cut; the
/// theatrical cut carries "Theatrical Cut" only when `features.len() >= 2` or `facts.folder_has_edition_named_file`; an
/// earlier filed copy's name (`earlier_edition_names`) replaces either. Names are raw here; naming::edition_label sanitises
/// and caps them. An earlier name "" gives None; an unnamed cut (not theatrical, no edition) gives None until review names
/// it. Def: T5. Use: T7, T13.
pub fn edition_names(features: &[Feature], facts: &LibraryFacts) -> Vec<Option<String>> {
    features
        .iter()
        .map(|feature| {
            let key = if feature.theatrical {
                Some(THEATRICAL_KEY.to_string())
            } else {
                feature.edition.as_ref().map(|name| name.to_lowercase())
            };
            if let Some(name) = key.as_ref().and_then(|key| facts.earlier_edition_names.get(key)) {
                return (!name.is_empty()).then(|| name.clone());
            }
            if !feature.theatrical {
                return feature.edition.clone();
            }
            (features.len() >= 2 || facts.folder_has_edition_named_file).then(|| THEATRICAL_CUT.to_string())
        })
        .collect()
}
```

```rust
pub mod kind;
pub mod movie;

pub use crate::lookup::Kind;
pub use kind::{Group, KindSource};

use crate::settings::Settings;

/// 6.2 or 6.3: Direct rips the planned titles; Copy backs up the whole disc and decides after review. Spec 6.2, 6.3, 8.8.
/// Def: T5. Use: T7, T14, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Mode {
    Direct,
    Copy,
}

impl Mode {
    /// Both modes, Direct first.
    pub const ALL: [Mode; 2] = [Mode::Direct, Mode::Copy];

    /// The serde spelling.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Mode::Direct => "direct",
            Mode::Copy => "copy",
        }
    }
}

impl std::str::FromStr for Mode {
    type Err = String;

    /// Only the `as_str` spellings.
    fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<Mode, String> {
        Mode::ALL.into_iter().find(|mode| mode.as_str() == text).ok_or_else(|| format!("'{text}' is not a mode"))
    }
}

/// Direct when `title_confidence >= settings.auto_threshold`, else Copy (6.2, 6.3, 8.8). Reads `settings.auto_threshold`
/// only. Def: T5. Use: T7.
pub fn mode(title_confidence: f64, settings: &Settings) -> Mode {
    if title_confidence >= settings.auto_threshold {
        Mode::Direct
    } else {
        Mode::Copy
    }
}
```

```rust
/// Titles with identical segment maps (8.2). On a DVD the key is (attribute 24, segment map) because its segments restart at

}

/// order; None when none is. Not applied on a DVD (segments restart per title). Def: T5. Use: T5, T6.
pub fn play_all(groups: &[Group], dvd: bool) -> Option<usize>;
```

Also used, in test builds only: Task 5's `crate::plan::fixtures` (`pub(crate)`, the plan module's shared test inputs; one copy): `pinned`, `api_record`, the log paths `CHERNOBYL_1`, `CHERNOBYL_2`, `FIREFLY_1`, `FIREFLY_2`, the answer hashes `CHERNOBYL_1_API`, `CHERNOBYL_2_API`, `FIREFLY_1_API`, and the stream rows `VIDEO` and `ENG_PGS`. Firefly disc 2's answer hash is not among them until Task 7 adds it, so `plan/tv.rs`'s tests hold it as one local constant until Task 7 Step 6 replaces it with the fixtures import.

Produces (exactly the `core::plan::tv (Task 6)` and `core::remembered (Task 6)` entries of the Shared interfaces; Tasks 7, 8, 10, 11, 13, 14 and 15 rely on them):

```rust
// lazymkv_core::plan::tv (Task 6; crates/core/src/plan/tv.rs)
/// An episode assignment: season and one or more episode numbers (multi-episode titles, 8.5). `season` None means not
/// known (no season parsed and no session found): review asks for it (8.5); never 0, which is the specials season (8.9
/// `Season 00`). Def: T6. Use: T7, T11, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Episode { pub season: Option<u32>, pub episodes: Vec<u32>, pub name: Option<String> }
/// "12-13" gives [12, 13], "4" gives [4], "01" gives [1]; empty for anything else. Def: T6. Use: T6.
pub fn parse_episode_numbers(text: &str) -> Vec<u32>;

/// One title assigned or suggested. Spec 8.5. Def: T6. Use: T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct EpisodeTitle { pub title: u32, pub episode: Episode, pub suggested: bool }

pub const MAPPED_TV_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.98;
pub const UNMAPPED_TV_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.60;

/// Def: T6. Use: T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct TvPlan {
    pub mapped: bool,
    pub episodes: Vec<EpisodeTitle>,
    pub confidence: f64,
    pub reviews: Vec<ReviewReason>,
    /// Play-all titles dropped (8.5 "play all titles are dropped").
    pub dropped_play_all: Vec<u32>,
    pub evidence: Vec<String>,
}
/// 8.5 first bullet: every Episode item that `matches` reconciles becomes an EpisodeTitle (season from `item.season` parsed as
/// a number, None when absent, which plan::plan fills from the disc name's season; episodes from
/// `parse_episode_numbers(item.episode)`; name from `item.title`); every play-all group's titles are dropped (`kind::play_all`
/// applied again until it finds none); 0.98. None when the record has no reconciled Episode item, when any Episode item
/// matches no scan title (as Open point 4 for MainMovies), or when a reconciled Episode item on a title that is not
/// play-all names no episode number (D1); plan::plan then plans the disc as unmapped. Def: T6. Use: T7.
pub fn by_discdb(record: &DiscDbRecord, matches: &BTreeMap<u32, u32>, groups: &[Group], dvd: bool) -> Option<TvPlan>;
/// 8.5 "play all titles are dropped": every play-all group (8.3 rule 3.1, `kind::play_all`, found again until none is;
/// never on a DVD) is removed. Returns the remaining groups and the dropped titles, sorted. Def: T6. Use: T6, T7.
pub fn without_play_all(groups: &[Group], dvd: bool) -> (Vec<Group>, Vec<u32>);
/// Spec 8.5 "pre-assigned to episodes by runtime as a suggestion": the groups' representatives in title order, assigned
/// from episode `start`: each takes the next episode, or the next two when its duration is within TV_RUNTIME_TOLERANCE of
/// the sum of the next two episodes' runtimes and not within it of the next one's; an episode without a runtime takes one
/// title. Returns (title, episode numbers) pairs. Def: T6. Use: T6.
pub fn suggest_by_runtime(groups: &[&Group], episodes: &[TmdbEpisode], start: u32) -> Vec<(u32, Vec<u32>)>;
/// 8.5 second bullet: 0.60 with tv_unmapped; the episode-length groups' representatives are suggested from `start` (the
/// session's next unassigned episode, or 1), through `suggest_by_runtime` when `episodes` (the season's TMDb episodes) are
/// given, else one episode each in title order; `suggested: true`; in `season` (None when no season was parsed and no
/// session was found). Episode numbers run on from `start` without skipping episodes the session assigned later in the
/// season; review confirms every suggestion (0.60, tv_unmapped). Def: T6. Use: T7.
pub fn unmapped(groups: &[Group], season: Option<u32>, start: u32, episodes: Option<&TmdbSeason>) -> TvPlan;

/// A season session (8.5, spec 5's `<tmdb show id>-s<NN>.json`); persistence is phase 2 (RP17). Def: T6. Use: T7, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct StreamSignature { pub kind: StreamKind, pub language: Option<String>, pub codec: Family, pub channels: Option<u32>, pub position: u32 }
/// The signature of `streams[index]` (position counts earlier streams with the same kind, language, codec and channels). Def: T6. Use: T6, T8, T10, T13.
pub fn signature(streams: &[Stream], index: usize) -> StreamSignature;

/// An audio override (spec 11 "Override tracks": keep with order and default, drop, or mark as commentary, which drops it). Def: T6. Use: T8, T13, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "action")]
pub enum AudioOverride { Drop, Keep { order: u32, default: bool }, Commentary }
/// A subtitle override (spec 11: keep with a role, or drop). Def: T6. Use: T10, T13, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "action")]
pub enum SubtitleOverride { Drop, Keep { role: SubtitleRole } }
/// One remembered audio override: the stream's signature and the action, flattened into one JSON object
/// (`{"signature": {...}, "action": "keep", "order": 1, "default": true}`). A list, not a map: serde_json writes no map
/// keyed by a struct. Spec 5. Def: T6. Use: T8, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct AudioOverrideEntry { pub signature: StreamSignature, #[serde(flatten)] pub action: AudioOverride }
/// The same for subtitles. Spec 5. Def: T6. Use: T10, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct SubtitleOverrideEntry { pub signature: StreamSignature, #[serde(flatten)] pub action: SubtitleOverride }

/// The remembered-decisions file (spec 5): the TMDb identity (its `kind` is the kind; no second field), the titles, the
/// overrides. Round-trips through serde_json (`a_remembered_file_round_trips_through_json`). Def: T6. Use: T7, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Remembered {
    pub fingerprint: String,
    pub tmdb: TmdbIdentity,
    pub titles: Vec<RememberedTitle>,
    pub audio: Vec<AudioOverrideEntry>,
    pub subtitles: Vec<SubtitleOverrideEntry>,
}
// A remembered or review decision sets the confidence it covers to lookup::REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE (1.00); no second constant here.
/// The remembered title is this scan title: `disc::same_source(&title_source(rem.source_file, rem.dvd_title), &title.source())`
/// (source file on a Blu-ray; on a DVD, both source files None, attribute 24 equal as numbers), `disc::segment_maps_agree`,
/// and duration within `disc::DURATION_MATCH_S`; never by title key. Def: T6. Use: T6, T7.
pub fn match_title(remembered: &RememberedTitle, title: &Title) -> bool;
/// Every scan title matched to a remembered title, title number to role (a remembered title is used once). Def: T6. Use: T7.
pub fn apply_titles<'a>(remembered: &'a Remembered, disc: &Disc) -> BTreeMap<u32, &'a TitleRole>;
/// Stream number to override for every stream whose signature has an entry. Def: T6. Use: T8.
pub fn apply_audio<'a>(overrides: &'a [AudioOverrideEntry], streams: &[Stream]) -> BTreeMap<u32, &'a AudioOverride>;
/// The same for subtitles. Def: T6. Use: T10.
pub fn apply_subtitles<'a>(overrides: &'a [SubtitleOverrideEntry], streams: &[Stream]) -> BTreeMap<u32, &'a SubtitleOverride>;

/// Spec 11 "Resolve collision". Def: T6. Use: T13.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Collision { KeepBoth, Replace, Discard }
impl Collision { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; pub const ALL: [Collision; 3]; }
/// Only the three spec spellings; Err "'x' is not a collision action (keep_both, replace or discard)".
impl std::str::FromStr for Collision { type Err = String; fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<Collision, String>; }

/// One title of the owner's Assign titles: the scan title number and its role, flattened into one JSON object
/// (`{"title": 3, "role": "episodes", "season": 3, "episodes": [12, 13]}`). Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T7, T13, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct TitleOverrideEntry { pub title: u32, #[serde(flatten)] pub role: TitleRole }
/// One track of the owner's Override tracks: the scan title and stream numbers and the action, flattened into one JSON
/// object (`{"title": 0, "stream": 1, "action": "keep", "order": 0, "default": true}`). Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T13, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct AudioTrackOverride { pub title: u32, pub stream: u32, #[serde(flatten)] pub action: AudioOverride }
/// The same for subtitles. Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct SubtitleTrackOverride { pub title: u32, pub stream: u32, #[serde(flatten)] pub action: SubtitleOverride }

/// The owner's review decisions on one job (spec 11 Set identity, Assign titles, Override tracks, Resolve collision); each
/// sets the confidence it covers to 1.00 (8.8). Assign titles and Override tracks are lists of entries keyed by the scan's
/// title number (and stream number) of this job, sorted by those keys, one entry per key. Def: T6. Use: T7, T13, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Overrides {
    /// Set identity.
    pub identity: Option<TmdbIdentity>,
    /// The season review asked for (8.5) when the plan has none.
    pub season: Option<u32>,
    /// Assign titles: one entry per title, sorted by title number.
    pub titles: Vec<TitleOverrideEntry>,
    /// Override tracks: one entry per scan title and stream, sorted by title, then stream.
    pub audio: Vec<AudioTrackOverride>,
    pub subtitles: Vec<SubtitleTrackOverride>,
    /// Resolve collision.
    pub collision: Option<Collision>,
}
impl Overrides {
    /// The role the owner's Assign titles gives scan title `title`, if it names it. Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T13.
    pub fn title_role(&self, title: u32) -> Option<&TitleRole>;
    /// The owner's audio overrides of scan title `title` by scan stream number (the form `AudioFacts.reviewed` takes);
    /// None when no entry names the title. Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T13.
    pub fn audio_of(&self, title: u32) -> Option<BTreeMap<u32, AudioOverride>>;
    /// The same for subtitles (`SubtitleFacts.reviewed`). Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T13.
    pub fn subtitles_of(&self, title: u32) -> Option<BTreeMap<u32, SubtitleOverride>>;
}
```

`Collision`'s closed-set members (`as_str`, `ALL`, `FromStr`) are in the shared entries, as the plan's conventions require of every closed set of spec strings.

Where this task settles what the spec and the interfaces leave open (each choice is pinned by a test below):

1. **Play-all titles.** In `by_discdb` every play-all group's titles are dropped (`tv::without_play_all`, which applies `kind::play_all` again until it finds none and which Task 7's `plan` also calls; never on a DVD, where `play_all` is not applied), even when TheDiscDB labels such a title an Episode item: 8.5 says "play all titles are dropped" in the plural and without exception. `dropped_play_all` lists them in title order. A disc with an extras play-all that comes first in group order beside an episodes play-all drops both (`every_play_all_title_is_dropped`), so the mapped and the unmapped paths of one plan treat play-alls alike. On the pinned Chernobyl logs this is title 6 of disc 1 (`4,11,12`, made of the groups of titles 29, 28 and 27, which the group list holds after it and in reverse order) and title 7 of disc 2 (`11,12`); neither disc has a second one. `unmapped` takes no DVD flag, so it cannot find a play-all itself: the caller passes the groups it wants suggested (Task 7's `plan` leaves out every group rule 3.1 names play-all).
2. **Episode numbers.** `parse_episode_numbers` reads a whole number (surrounding whitespace ignored, leading zeros allowed) or a range `a-b` with `a <= b` as every number from `a` to `b`, at most 100 of them (`MAX_EPISODE_SPAN`); TheDiscDB's answers are network data and a wider range is not a title's episodes. Anything else (`E4`, `13-12`, `12-`, an empty text) gives no number, and a reconciled Episode item with no number (on a title that is not play-all) makes `by_discdb` return None (D1), as an unmatched one does (point 9): mapping that title to no episode, or leaving it off a Direct job while the other episodes file at 0.98, would both lose the episode TheDiscDB placed there.
3. **Order and names.** `by_discdb` keeps database index order (the order of `match_titles`' keys); `unmapped` keeps title order; `plan::plan` orders the planned titles. TheDiscDB's item title is trimmed; a suggestion's name is TMDb's episode name, the names of a two-episode suggestion joined with `" / "`, and None without TMDb episodes. A season is read from `item.season` as a whole number (`"01"` is 1, `"0"` is the specials season), None when absent or not a number.
4. **The runtime suggestion.** An episode's runtime is looked up in the season's TMDb episodes by `episode_number`; an episode TMDb does not list counts as one without a runtime. A title takes the next two episodes only when both have runtimes, its duration is within 15% of their sum and not within 15% of the first one's (`lookup::within`, `TV_RUNTIME_TOLERANCE`).
5. **Season sessions.** `find` with a parsed season returns that show's session for the season whether it is open or closed (8.5 "a disc finds its session by show ID and the season number"); without a parsed season only open sessions count. `assign` records the disc's fingerprint once, replaces an episode's earlier assignment (the owner's latest Assign titles wins) and closes the session once every episode from 1 to `episode_count` is assigned; without an episode count only `close` closes it, and a closed session stays closed.
6. **Overrides by signature.** `apply_audio` considers only the title's audio streams and `apply_subtitles` only its subtitle streams, so an entry whose signature names another kind never lands on a stream; an entry that matches no stream is ignored. The signature's language is `Stream.language` as Task 2 gives it (attribute 3 lower-cased), not normalised further: a remembered decision is replayed on the same pressing, whose scan spells it the same way.
7. **Title matching.** `match_title` follows spec 5 and Review Focus 1 exactly (source, segment map, duration within `disc::DURATION_MATCH_S`, never the title key; a title without a duration or a remembered title without a source never matches). `apply_titles` walks the scan's titles in number order and gives each the first remembered title not yet used that matches it.
8. **No setting is read here.** Neither file takes `&Settings`; the tests call Task 5's `candidate_filter` with `Settings::default()` only to build the groups the planner builds.
9. **An Episode item the scan does not show.** `by_discdb` returns None when any Episode item of the record (`DiscDbRecord::episodes`) matches no scan title, so `plan::plan` plans the disc as unmapped (0.60, `tv_unmapped`, whole-disc copy) instead of filing the other episodes at 0.98 in Direct mode, which would leave that episode off the job (8.8 "Limits of D1", D1, R1). This is Open point 4's rule for MainMovies applied to episodes, pinned by `an_episode_item_that_matches_no_scan_title_leaves_the_disc_unmapped`. An Episode item that matches a play-all title is reconciled (the title is then dropped by 8.5), and one that matches a title but names no episode number makes `by_discdb` return None (D1), as an unmatched one does (point 2), pinned by `an_episode_item_without_an_episode_number_leaves_the_disc_unmapped`; the play-all check comes first, so an Episode item on a dropped play-all title needs no number.
10. **Review overrides per title.** `Overrides.audio` and `Overrides.subtitles` are keyed by scan title number, then scan stream number, because one `Overrides` covers a whole job (`DecisionInputs.overrides`, `Event::ReviewApproved`) and stream numbers restart in every title (`Stream.number` is 0-based within the title): spec 11's Override tracks is a choice about one title's tracks. They are lists of entries (`AudioTrackOverride`, `SubtitleTrackOverride`, and `TitleOverrideEntry` for Assign titles), sorted by their keys, not integer-keyed maps, because `Overrides` travels inside Task 14's internally tagged `Event`, where serde cannot read an integer map key back (the interfaces' "Keyed collections"). Tasks 8 and 10 take one title's map (`AudioFacts.reviewed`, `SubtitleFacts.reviewed`), which Task 13 builds with `overrides.audio_of(title.number)` and `overrides.subtitles_of(title.number)`; `title_role` finds one title's Assign titles entry.

All tests read only synthetic inputs and the public fixtures `corpus/thediscdb/series/**/discNN.txt` and `corpus/thediscdb-api/dischash-*.json`, so they run on every OS and in CI. The Office's TheDiscDB answer is in the private evidence clone, so (RP21) its unit test uses a made-up disc of the same shape: one two-episode title, a deleted-scenes item that carries the same two episodes, an unlisted database index between matched ones, two unlisted trailing indices, and a database order that differs from scan order. Every playlist, segment map, duration, size, name and ID in it is made up. Task 15's `tests/plan.rs` checks the recorded answer.

```rust
//! and the season session record with its pure functions `find`, `suggest`, `assign` and `close` (persistence is
//! phase 2). Task 7's planner calls `by_discdb`, `unmapped`, `find`, `SeasonSession::next_unassigned` and `assign`;
//! `suggest` and `close` serve phase 2's review (Assign titles, the owner's close); Tasks 11 and 13 read `Episode`
//! through the plan. No setting is read here.

    /// The made-up disc's scan: SHOW_TITLES, each with one English stereo audio stream.
    fn show_disc() -> Disc {
        let sizes: Vec<String> = SHOW_TITLES.iter().map(|row| row.4.to_string()).collect();
        let attrs: Vec<Vec<(u32, &str)>> = SHOW_TITLES
            .iter()

            .collect();
        let streams: &[(u32, &[(u32, &str)])] = &[(0, ENGLISH_STEREO)];
        let titles: Vec<(u32, &[(u32, &str)], &[(u32, &[(u32, &str)])])> =
            SHOW_TITLES.iter().zip(&attrs).map(|(row, attrs)| (row.0, attrs.as_slice(), streams)).collect();
        let text = scan_text(&[(1, "Blu-ray disc"), (2, "EXAMPLE SHOW S2D3"), (32, "EXAMPLE SHOW S2D3")], &titles);
        disc(&parse(&text)).unwrap()
    }
```

```rust
/// An episode assignment: season and one or more episode numbers (multi-episode titles, 8.5). `season` None means not
/// known (no season parsed and no session found): review asks for it (8.5); never 0, which is the specials season (8.9
/// `Season 00`). Def: T6. Use: T7, T11, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Episode {
    /// The season number (0 is the specials season); None when not known.
    pub season: Option<u32>,
    /// The episode numbers in TMDb's aired order (8.5): one, or two or more for a multi-episode title.
    pub episodes: Vec<u32>,
    /// TheDiscDB's item title (trimmed), or TMDb's episode names for a suggestion; None when neither gives one.
    pub name: Option<String>,
}

/// The widest range `parse_episode_numbers` reads as one title's episodes. TheDiscDB's answers are network data: a
/// wider range is a malformed answer, and reading it would allocate without bound.
const MAX_EPISODE_SPAN: u32 = 100;

/// A whole number of ASCII digits, surrounding whitespace ignored ("01" is 1); None for anything else or a number
/// above u32::MAX.
fn whole_number(text: &str) -> Option<u32> {
    let text = text.trim();
    if text.is_empty() || !text.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit()) {
        return None;
    }
    text.parse().ok()
}

/// "12-13" gives [12, 13], "4" gives [4], "01" gives [1]; empty for anything else. A range `a-b` with `a <= b` gives
/// every number from a to b (TheDiscDB's multi-episode form), at most MAX_EPISODE_SPAN of them. Spec 8.5. Def: T6. Use: T6.
pub fn parse_episode_numbers(text: &str) -> Vec<u32> {
    match text.split_once('-') {
        None => whole_number(text).map(|number| vec![number]).unwrap_or_default(),
        Some((first, last)) => match (whole_number(first), whole_number(last)) {
            (Some(first), Some(last)) if first <= last && last - first < MAX_EPISODE_SPAN => (first..=last).collect(),
            _ => Vec::new(),
        },
    }
}

/// The episode as 8.9 codes it ("S03E12-E13"; "E05 (season unknown)" without a season), with its name in double
/// quotes when it has one: the form of every evidence sentence here.
fn describe(episode: &Episode) -> String {
    let numbers: Vec<String> = episode.episodes.iter().map(|number| format!("E{number:02}")).collect();
    let code = match episode.season {
        Some(season) => format!("S{season:02}{}", numbers.join("-")),
        None => format!("{} (season unknown)", numbers.join("-")),
    };
    match &episode.name {
        Some(name) => format!("{code} \"{name}\""),
        None => code,
    }
}

/// One title assigned or suggested. Spec 8.5. Def: T6. Use: T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct EpisodeTitle {
    /// The scan's title number.
    pub title: u32,
    pub episode: Episode,
    /// True for 8.5's runtime suggestions (review confirms them); false for TheDiscDB's map.
    pub suggested: bool,
}

/// Spec 8.5: the title confidence when TheDiscDB maps the disc. Def: T6. Use: T7.
pub const MAPPED_TV_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.98;
/// Spec 8.5: the title confidence otherwise, with tv_unmapped. Def: T6. Use: T7.
pub const UNMAPPED_TV_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.60;

/// The TV titles of 8.5 with their confidence and review reasons. Def: T6. Use: T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct TvPlan {
    /// True when TheDiscDB's Episode items gave the titles (`by_discdb`); false for suggestions (`unmapped`).
    pub mapped: bool,
    /// `by_discdb`: in database index order; `unmapped`: in title order. plan::plan orders the planned titles.
    pub episodes: Vec<EpisodeTitle>,
    /// MAPPED_TV_CONFIDENCE or UNMAPPED_TV_CONFIDENCE.
    pub confidence: f64,
    /// Empty, or [TvUnmapped] (8.5, 8.8).
    pub reviews: Vec<ReviewReason>,
    /// Play-all titles dropped (8.5 "play all titles are dropped").
    pub dropped_play_all: Vec<u32>,
    /// The plan's sentences: by_discdb one per mapped title in database index order, then one per dropped play-all title;
    /// unmapped the confidence and suggestion-method sentences, "season unknown" when it is, then one per suggested title
    /// in title order.
    pub evidence: Vec<String>,
}

/// 8.5 first bullet: every Episode item that `matches` reconciles becomes an EpisodeTitle (season from `item.season` parsed as
/// a number, None when absent, which plan::plan fills from the disc name's season; episodes from
/// `parse_episode_numbers(item.episode)`; name from `item.title`); every play-all group's titles are dropped (`kind::play_all`
/// applied again until it finds none); 0.98. None when the record has no reconciled Episode item, when any Episode item
/// matches no scan title (as Open point 4 for MainMovies), or when a reconciled Episode item on a title that is not
/// play-all names no episode number (D1); plan::plan then plans the disc as unmapped. A Direct job holds only its planned
/// titles (8.8 "Limits of D1"), so mapping the rest would file the disc without that episode. An Episode item whose
/// episode text gives no number makes `by_discdb` return None (D1), as an unmatched one does; a title of a group
/// `kind::play_all` finds is dropped even when TheDiscDB labels it an Episode item (the play-all check comes first, so
/// such an item never needs a number), and `play_all` is never applied on a DVD. Def: T6. Use: T7.
pub fn by_discdb(record: &DiscDbRecord, matches: &BTreeMap<u32, u32>, groups: &[Group], dvd: bool) -> Option<TvPlan> {
    // D1 ("When unsure, ... queue the disc for review"): an episode TheDiscDB describes but the scan does not show leaves
    // the disc unmapped, as 8.3 rule 1 needs every MainMovie to reconcile (Open point 4).
    if record.episodes().iter().any(|db| !matches.contains_key(&db.index)) {
        return None;
    }
    // 8.5 "play all titles are dropped": every play-all group (8.3 rule 3.1), found again until none is, as plan::plan does.
    let (_, dropped_play_all) = without_play_all(groups, dvd);
    let mut episodes = Vec::new();
    let mut evidence = Vec::new();
    for (&index, &title) in matches {
        let Some(item) = record.titles.iter().find(|db| db.index == index).and_then(|db| db.item.as_ref()) else {
            continue;
        };
        if item.item_type != ItemType::Episode || dropped_play_all.contains(&title) {
            continue;
        }
        let numbers = parse_episode_numbers(item.episode.as_deref().unwrap_or(""));
        if numbers.is_empty() {
            // D1: an episode title TheDiscDB cannot number would be left off a Direct job; plan the disc as unmapped.
            return None;
        }
        let name = item.title.trim();
        let episode = Episode {
            season: item.season.as_deref().and_then(whole_number),
            episodes: numbers,
            name: if name.is_empty() { None } else { Some(name.to_string()) },
        };
        evidence.push(format!("TheDiscDB maps title {title} to {}", describe(&episode)));
        episodes.push(EpisodeTitle { title, episode, suggested: false });
    }
    if episodes.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    for title in &dropped_play_all {
        evidence.push(format!(
            "play-all title {title} dropped (8.5): its segment map is the concatenation of other groups' maps"
        ));
    }
    Some(TvPlan { mapped: true, episodes, confidence: MAPPED_TV_CONFIDENCE, reviews: Vec::new(), dropped_play_all, evidence })
}

/// 8.5 "play all titles are dropped": every play-all group (8.3 rule 3.1, `kind::play_all`, found again until none is;
/// never on a DVD) is removed. Returns the remaining groups and the dropped titles, sorted. Def: T6. Use: T6, T7.
pub fn without_play_all(groups: &[Group], dvd: bool) -> (Vec<Group>, Vec<u32>) {
    let mut rest: Vec<Group> = groups.to_vec();
    let mut dropped: Vec<u32> = Vec::new();
    while let Some(index) = play_all(&rest, dvd) {
        dropped.extend(rest.remove(index).titles);
    }
    dropped.sort_unstable();
    (rest, dropped)
}
```
