- [ ] **Step 8: Implement the runtime suggestions and the unmapped plan (spec 8.5 second bullet)**

Insert into `crates/core/src/plan/tv.rs`, after the end of `by_discdb` (its closing `}`) and before `#[cfg(test)]`:

```rust

/// Spec 8.5 "pre-assigned to episodes by runtime as a suggestion": the groups' representatives in title order, assigned
/// from episode `start`: each takes the next episode, or the next two when its duration is within TV_RUNTIME_TOLERANCE of
/// the sum of the next two episodes' runtimes and not within it of the next one's; an episode without a runtime takes one
/// title. Returns (title, episode numbers) pairs. An episode is looked up in `episodes` by its `episode_number`; one TMDb
/// does not list counts as an episode without a runtime. Def: T6. Use: T6.
pub fn suggest_by_runtime(groups: &[&Group], episodes: &[TmdbEpisode], start: u32) -> Vec<(u32, Vec<u32>)> {
    let runtime_s = |number: u32| {
        episodes
            .iter()
            .find(|episode| episode.episode_number == number)
            .and_then(|episode| episode.runtime)
            .map(|minutes| f64::from(minutes) * 60.0)
    };
    let mut ordered: Vec<&Group> = groups.iter().copied().filter(|group| !group.titles.is_empty()).collect();
    ordered.sort_by_key(|group| group.titles[0]);
    let mut next = start;
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(ordered.len());
    for group in ordered {
        let seconds = f64::from(group.seconds);
        let after = next.saturating_add(1);
        let two = match (runtime_s(next), runtime_s(after)) {
            (Some(first), Some(second)) => {
                within(seconds, first + second, TV_RUNTIME_TOLERANCE) && !within(seconds, first, TV_RUNTIME_TOLERANCE)
            }
            _ => false,
        };
        if two {
            out.push((group.titles[0], vec![next, after]));
            next = after.saturating_add(1);
        } else {
            out.push((group.titles[0], vec![next]));
            next = after;
        }
    }
    out
}

/// 8.5 second bullet: 0.60 with tv_unmapped; the episode-length groups' representatives are suggested from `start` (the
/// session's next unassigned episode, or 1), through `suggest_by_runtime` when `episodes` (the season's TMDb episodes) are
/// given, else one episode each in title order; `suggested: true`; in `season` (None when no season was parsed and no
/// session was found). Episode numbers run on from `start` without skipping episodes the session assigned later in the
/// season; review confirms every suggestion (0.60, tv_unmapped). A suggestion's name is TMDb's episode name, a
/// two-episode suggestion's names joined with " / ".
/// The caller passes the groups to suggest: a play-all group (8.3 rule 3.1) is left out by plan::plan, since this
/// function has no DVD flag to find one. Def: T6. Use: T7.
pub fn unmapped(groups: &[Group], season: Option<u32>, start: u32, episodes: Option<&TmdbSeason>) -> TvPlan {
    let tmdb: &[TmdbEpisode] = match episodes {
        Some(listed) => &listed.episodes,
        None => &[],
    };
    let pairs = suggest_by_runtime(&episode_length_groups(groups), tmdb, start);
    let how = if tmdb.is_empty() {
        "one episode each in title order (no TMDb episodes for the season)"
    } else {
        "by TMDb's episode runtimes"
    };
    let mut evidence = vec![
        "no TheDiscDB episode map: title confidence 0.60 with tv_unmapped (8.5)".to_string(),
        format!("episode-length titles suggested from episode {start}: {}, {how}", pairs.len()),
    ];
    if season.is_none() {
        evidence.push("season unknown: review asks for it (8.5)".to_string());
    }
    let mut titles = Vec::with_capacity(pairs.len());
    for (title, numbers) in pairs {
        let names: Vec<&str> = numbers
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|number| tmdb.iter().find(|episode| episode.episode_number == *number))
            .filter_map(|episode| episode.name.as_deref())
            .filter(|name| !name.trim().is_empty())
            .collect();
        let name = if names.is_empty() { None } else { Some(names.join(" / ")) };
        let episode = Episode { season, episodes: numbers, name };
        evidence.push(format!("title {title} suggested as {}", describe(&episode)));
        titles.push(EpisodeTitle { title, episode, suggested: true });
    }
    TvPlan {
        mapped: false,
        episodes: titles,
        confidence: UNMAPPED_TV_CONFIDENCE,
        reviews: sorted_unique(vec![ReviewReason::TvUnmapped]),
        dropped_play_all: Vec::new(),
        evidence,
    }
}
```

```rust
/// One assigned episode of a season session: the episode number and the disc fingerprint and scan title it was assigned
/// from. Spec 8.5. Def: T6. Use: T6, T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct AssignedEpisode {
    /// The episode number (the key: one entry per episode).
    pub episode: u32,
    /// The fingerprint of the disc it was assigned from.
    pub fingerprint: String,
    /// The scan title number on that disc.
    pub title: u32,
}

/// A season session (8.5, spec 5's `<tmdb show id>-s<NN>.json`); persistence is phase 2 (RP17). Def: T6. Use: T7, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct SeasonSession {
    /// TMDb's show ID (the TV half of a TmdbIdentity).
    pub show_id: i64,
    /// The season number (0 is specials).
    pub season: u32,
    /// Fingerprints of the discs seen, in order.
    pub discs: Vec<String>,
    /// The assigned episodes, one entry per episode, sorted by episode number (`assign` keeps the order). A list of
    /// entries, not a map keyed by the episode number: the session is part of the plan document, which serde reads back
    /// inside buffered content that cannot give an integer map key (the interfaces' "Keyed collections").
    pub assigned: Vec<AssignedEpisode>,
    /// TMDb's episode count for the season; None when TMDb gave none (the session then closes only by `close`).
    pub episode_count: Option<u32>,
    /// Closed when every episode is assigned or the owner closed it (8.5).
    pub closed: bool,
}

impl SeasonSession {
    /// An open session with no disc and no episode assigned. Spec 8.5. Def: T6. Use: T6, T7.
    pub fn new(show_id: i64, season: u32, episode_count: Option<u32>) -> SeasonSession {
        SeasonSession { show_id, season, discs: Vec::new(), assigned: Vec::new(), episode_count, closed: false }
    }

    /// The assignment of `episode`, if any. Spec 8.5. Def: T6. Use: T6.
    pub fn get(&self, episode: u32) -> Option<&AssignedEpisode> {
        self.assigned.iter().find(|entry| entry.episode == episode)
    }

    /// The lowest episode number from 1 that is not assigned. Spec 8.5. Def: T6. Use: T6, T7.
    pub fn next_unassigned(&self) -> u32 {
        (1..=u32::MAX).find(|&episode| self.get(episode).is_none()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX)
    }

    /// `<show_id>-s<NN>.json` (spec 5). Def: T6. Use: phase 2.
    pub fn file_name(&self) -> String {
        format!("{}-s{:02}.json", self.show_id, self.season)
    }
}

/// What `find` found. Spec 8.5. Def: T6. Use: T7.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum Found<'a> {
    /// The show's session for the parsed season (open or closed).
    Session(&'a SeasonSession),
    /// Without a parsed season: the show's only open session.
    SingleOpen(&'a SeasonSession),
    /// No session for the show (and parsed season): suggestions start at the first episode; without a parsed season
    /// review asks for it (8.5).
    None,
    /// Without a parsed season, the show has several open sessions: review asks for the season.
    Ambiguous,
}

/// By show ID and the parsed season; without a parsed season the show's single open session; Ambiguous when several are
/// open. With a parsed season the first session of that show and season is returned whether open or closed. Spec 8.5.
/// Def: T6. Use: T7.
pub fn find<'a>(sessions: &'a [SeasonSession], show_id: i64, season: Option<u32>) -> Found<'a> {
    match season {
        Some(season) => sessions
            .iter()
            .find(|session| session.show_id == show_id && session.season == season)
            .map_or(Found::None, Found::Session),
        None => {
            let open: Vec<&SeasonSession> =
                sessions.iter().filter(|session| session.show_id == show_id && !session.closed).collect();
            match open.as_slice() {
                [] => Found::None,
                [only] => Found::SingleOpen(*only),
                _ => Found::Ambiguous,
            }
        }
    }
}

/// `n` episode numbers from the session's next unassigned episode (from 1 without a session), skipping assigned ones.
/// Spec 8.5 "Suggestions start at the session's next unassigned episode". Def: T6. Use: phase 2 (review's Assign titles).
pub fn suggest(session: Option<&SeasonSession>, n: usize) -> Vec<u32> {
    let assigned = |episode: u32| session.map_or(false, |session| session.get(episode).is_some());
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(n);
    let mut episode = session.map_or(1, SeasonSession::next_unassigned);
    while out.len() < n {
        if !assigned(episode) {
            out.push(episode);
        }
        match episode.checked_add(1) {
            Some(next) => episode = next,
            None => break,
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Records the disc and its episodes; `episodes` are (episode number, scan title number) pairs; closes the session when
/// every episode of `episode_count` is assigned. The fingerprint is recorded once; an episode assigned again takes the
/// new disc and title (the owner's latest assignment); a closed session stays closed. Spec 8.5. Def: T6. Use: T7, phase 2.
pub fn assign(session: &mut SeasonSession, fingerprint: &str, episodes: &[(u32, u32)]) {
    if !session.discs.iter().any(|seen| seen == fingerprint) {
        session.discs.push(fingerprint.to_string());
    }
    for &(episode, title) in episodes {
        let entry = AssignedEpisode { episode, fingerprint: fingerprint.to_string(), title };
        // Kept sorted by episode number; an episode assigned again is replaced in place.
        match session.assigned.iter().position(|seen| seen.episode >= episode) {
            Some(index) if session.assigned[index].episode == episode => session.assigned[index] = entry,
            Some(index) => session.assigned.insert(index, entry),
            None => session.assigned.push(entry),
        }
    }
    if let Some(count) = session.episode_count {
        if (1..=count).all(|episode| session.get(episode).is_some()) {
            session.closed = true;
        }
    }
}

/// The owner's close (8.5 "or when the owner closes it"). Def: T6. Use: phase 2.
pub fn close(session: &mut SeasonSession) {
    session.closed = true;
}
```

```rust
//! segment map, duration and role; audio and subtitle overrides keyed by the stream's signature) and spec 11's review
//! actions (Set identity, Assign titles, Override tracks, Resolve collision, Remember), RP16: the types, the title match
//! (source file, segment map and duration within 2 s, never the title key) and the override lookups by signature. A
//! remembered or review decision sets the confidence it covers to 1.00 (`lookup::REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE`, spec 5 and
//! 8.8). Persistence is phase 2. Used by the planner (Task 7), the audio and subtitle rules (Tasks 8 and 10), the
//! decision (Task 13) and the job reducer (Task 14).

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::str::FromStr;

use crate::codec::Family;
use crate::disc::{same_source, segment_maps_agree, title_source, Disc, Stream, StreamKind, Title, DURATION_MATCH_S};
use crate::lookup::tmdb::TmdbIdentity;
use crate::tracks::SubtitleRole;

    fn json_of<T: serde::Serialize>(value: &T) -> String {
        serde_json::to_string(value).unwrap()
    }

    /// Writes `value` as JSON and reads it back: the same value.
    fn round_trips<T>(value: &T)
    where
        T: serde::Serialize + serde::de::DeserializeOwned + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug,
    {
        assert_eq!(&serde_json::from_str::<T>(&json_of(value)).unwrap(), value);
    }

    /// The signature of an English stereo Dolby Digital stream at `position` among identical ones.
    fn eng_ac3_2(position: u32) -> StreamSignature {
        StreamSignature { kind: StreamKind::Audio, language: Some("eng".to_string()), codec: Family::Ac3, channels: Some(2), position }
    }

    /// The signature of an English PGS subtitle stream at `position` among identical ones.
    fn eng_pgs(position: u32) -> StreamSignature {
        StreamSignature { kind: StreamKind::Subtitles, language: Some("eng".to_string()), codec: Family::Pgs, channels: None, position }
    }

    fn remembered_title(
        source_file: Option<&str>,
        dvd_title: Option<&str>,

            segment_map: segment_map.to_string(),

        TitleRole::Episodes { season, episodes: numbers.to_vec() }
    }

        let vobsub =
            StreamSignature { kind: StreamKind::Subtitles, language: Some("eng".to_string()), codec: Family::VobSub, channels: None, position: 0 };
        Remembered {
            fingerprint: FIREFLY_1_API.to_string(),
            tmdb: TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::Tv, id: 1437 },
            titles: vec![
                remembered_title(None, Some("01"), "1-2,3,4-6,7-10,11-15,16-20,21-24,25", 5186, episodes(1, &[1])),
                remembered_title(None, Some("02"), "1,2-6,7-11,12-14,15", 2554, episodes(1, &[2])),
                remembered_title(None, Some("03"), "1-4,5-10,11-14,15", 2627, episodes(1, &[3])),
                remembered_title(None, Some("05"), "1,2", 7, TitleRole::Ignored),

    #[test]
    fn title_roles_are_written_with_the_spec_spellings() {
        let roles = [
            (TitleRole::Feature, r#"{"role":"feature"}"#),
            (TitleRole::Cut { edition: "Unrated Cut".to_string() }, r#"{"role":"cut","edition":"Unrated Cut"}"#),

        assert_eq!(

                r#"{{"kind":{},"language":"eng","codec":{},"channels":2,"position":1}}"#,
                json_of(&StreamKind::Audio),
                json_of(&Family::Ac3)
            )
        );
        let video = StreamSignature { kind: StreamKind::Video, language: None, codec: Family::Hevc, channels: None, position: 0 };
        assert_eq!(
            json_of(&video),
            format!(
                r#"{{"kind":{},"language":null,"codec":{},"channels":null,"position":0}}"#,

        assert_eq!(
            json_of(&sdh),
            format!(r#"{{"signature":{subtitles},"action":"keep","role":{}}}"#, json_of(&SubtitleRole::Sdh))
        );
        round_trips(&sdh);
        let dropped = SubtitleOverrideEntry { signature: eng_pgs(0), action: SubtitleOverride::Drop };
        assert_eq!(json_of(&dropped), format!(r#"{{"signature":{subtitles},"action":"drop"}}"#));
        round_trips(&dropped);
    }

    #[test]

        assert_eq!(Collision::ALL.map(Collision::as_str), ["keep_both", "replace", "discard"]);
        for collision in Collision::ALL {

        }
        assert_eq!(

        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_remembered_file_round_trips_through_json() {
```

```rust
/// A title's role in a remembered or review decision (spec 5; 11 "Assign titles", with an editable edition name). Def: T6. Use: T7, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "role")]
pub enum TitleRole {
    /// The film's feature (its only or main cut).
    Feature,
    /// A named cut (8.4), its edition name as the owner left it; naming::edition_label sanitises and caps it.
    Cut { edition: String },
    /// One or more episodes of a season (8.5; season 0 is the specials season).
    Episodes { season: u32, episodes: Vec<u32> },
    /// Not filed.
    Ignored,
}

/// One title of a remembered decision (spec 5: "for each title its source file, segment map, duration, role"); `dvd_title`
/// is attribute 24, the DVD's identity of a title (Review Focus 1). Def: T6. Use: T6, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct RememberedTitle {
    /// Attribute 16 (a Blu-ray's playlist, "00800.mpls"); None on a DVD.
    pub source_file: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 24 as MakeMKV wrote it ("01"); None on a Blu-ray.
    pub dvd_title: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 26 as text (it may end in "...").
    pub segment_map: String,
    /// Attribute 9 in seconds.
    pub seconds: u32,
    pub role: TitleRole,
}

/// A stream's signature (spec 5): kind, language, codec family, channels, position among identical streams (0-based). Def: T6. Use: T8, T10, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct StreamSignature {
    /// Attribute 1.
    pub kind: StreamKind,
    /// Attribute 3 lower-cased (`Stream.language`); None when absent.
    pub language: Option<String>,
    /// The codec family of attributes 5, 6 and 7 (`Stream.codec.family`).
    pub codec: Family,
    /// Attribute 14.
    pub channels: Option<u32>,
    /// How many earlier streams of the title share the four fields above.
    pub position: u32,
}

/// An audio override (spec 11 "Override tracks": keep with order and default, drop, or mark as commentary, which drops it). Def: T6. Use: T8, T13, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "action")]
pub enum AudioOverride {
    /// Not kept.
    Drop,
    /// Kept at `order` among the kept audio tracks (0 first); the default track when `default`.
    Keep { order: u32, default: bool },
    /// Marked as commentary: dropped (spec 11).
    Commentary,
}

/// A subtitle override (spec 11: keep with a role, or drop). Def: T6. Use: T10, T13, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "action")]
pub enum SubtitleOverride {
    /// Not kept.
    Drop,
    /// Kept as the forced, regular or SDH (subtitles for the deaf and hard of hearing) track.
    Keep { role: SubtitleRole },
}

/// One remembered audio override: the stream's signature and the action, flattened into one JSON object
/// (`{"signature": {...}, "action": "keep", "order": 1, "default": true}`). A list, not a map: serde_json writes no map
/// keyed by a struct. Spec 5. Def: T6. Use: T8, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct AudioOverrideEntry {
    pub signature: StreamSignature,
    #[serde(flatten)]
    pub action: AudioOverride,
}

/// The same for subtitles. Spec 5. Def: T6. Use: T10, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct SubtitleOverrideEntry {
    pub signature: StreamSignature,
    #[serde(flatten)]
    pub action: SubtitleOverride,
}

/// The remembered-decisions file (spec 5): the TMDb identity (its `kind` is the kind; no second field), the titles, the
/// overrides. Round-trips through serde_json (`a_remembered_file_round_trips_through_json`). Def: T6. Use: T7, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Remembered {
    /// The disc's fingerprint (spec 5), the file's name.
    pub fingerprint: String,
    pub tmdb: TmdbIdentity,
    pub titles: Vec<RememberedTitle>,
    pub audio: Vec<AudioOverrideEntry>,
    pub subtitles: Vec<SubtitleOverrideEntry>,
}

/// Spec 11 "Resolve collision". Def: T6. Use: T13.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Collision {
    /// Keep both: the new file gets a distinguishing label such as `- 2160p 2`.
    KeepBoth,
    /// Replace the existing file after an explicit confirmation (it is moved into the job's staging folder and kept).
    Replace,
    /// Discard the job.
    Discard,
}

impl Collision {
    /// The spec spelling, as serde writes it: "keep_both", "replace", "discard". Spec 11.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Collision::KeepBoth => "keep_both",
            Collision::Replace => "replace",
            Collision::Discard => "discard",
        }
    }

    /// The three actions in spec 11's order.
    pub const ALL: [Collision; 3] = [Collision::KeepBoth, Collision::Replace, Collision::Discard];
}

impl FromStr for Collision {
    type Err = String;

    /// Only the three spec spellings. Spec 11.
    fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<Collision, String> {
        Collision::ALL
            .into_iter()
            .find(|collision| collision.as_str() == text)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("'{text}' is not a collision action (keep_both, replace or discard)"))
    }
}

/// One title of the owner's Assign titles: the scan title number and its role, flattened into one JSON object
/// (`{"title": 3, "role": "episodes", "season": 3, "episodes": [12, 13]}`). Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T7, T13, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct TitleOverrideEntry {
    /// The scan title number (the key).
    pub title: u32,
    #[serde(flatten)]
    pub role: TitleRole,
}

/// One track of the owner's Override tracks: the scan title and stream numbers and the action, flattened into one JSON
/// object (`{"title": 0, "stream": 1, "action": "keep", "order": 0, "default": true}`). Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T13, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct AudioTrackOverride {
    /// The scan title number (the first key).
    pub title: u32,
    /// The scan stream number within that title (the second key; `Stream.number` restarts in every title).
    pub stream: u32,
    #[serde(flatten)]
    pub action: AudioOverride,
}

/// The same for subtitles. Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct SubtitleTrackOverride {
    /// The scan title number (the first key).
    pub title: u32,
    /// The scan stream number within that title (the second key).
    pub stream: u32,
    #[serde(flatten)]
    pub action: SubtitleOverride,
}

/// The owner's review decisions on one job (spec 11 Set identity, Assign titles, Override tracks, Resolve collision); each
/// sets the confidence it covers to 1.00 (8.8). Assign titles and Override tracks are lists of entries keyed by the scan's
/// title number (and stream number) of this job, sorted by those keys, one entry per key: lists, not integer-keyed maps,
/// because `Event::ReviewApproved` carries them inside an internally tagged enum, whose buffered content cannot give an
/// integer map key (the interfaces' "Keyed collections"). Def: T6. Use: T7, T13, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Overrides {
    /// Set identity.
    pub identity: Option<TmdbIdentity>,
    /// The season review asked for (8.5) when the plan has none.
    pub season: Option<u32>,
    /// Assign titles: one entry per title, sorted by title number.
    pub titles: Vec<TitleOverrideEntry>,
    /// Override tracks: one entry per scan title and stream, sorted by title, then stream.
    pub audio: Vec<AudioTrackOverride>,
    pub subtitles: Vec<SubtitleTrackOverride>,
    /// Resolve collision.
    pub collision: Option<Collision>,
}

impl Overrides {
    /// The role the owner's Assign titles gives scan title `title`, if it names it. Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T13.
    pub fn title_role(&self, title: u32) -> Option<&TitleRole> {
        self.titles.iter().find(|entry| entry.title == title).map(|entry| &entry.role)
    }

    /// The owner's audio overrides of scan title `title` by scan stream number (the form `AudioFacts.reviewed` takes);
    /// None when no entry names the title. Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T13.
    pub fn audio_of(&self, title: u32) -> Option<BTreeMap<u32, AudioOverride>> {
        let streams: BTreeMap<u32, AudioOverride> = self
            .audio
            .iter()
            .filter(|entry| entry.title == title)
            .map(|entry| (entry.stream, entry.action.clone()))
            .collect();
        (!streams.is_empty()).then_some(streams)
    }

    /// The same for subtitles (`SubtitleFacts.reviewed`). Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T13.
    pub fn subtitles_of(&self, title: u32) -> Option<BTreeMap<u32, SubtitleOverride>> {
        let streams: BTreeMap<u32, SubtitleOverride> = self
            .subtitles
            .iter()
            .filter(|entry| entry.title == title)
            .map(|entry| (entry.stream, entry.action.clone()))
            .collect();
        (!streams.is_empty()).then_some(streams)
    }
}
```

Insert into `crates/core/src/remembered.rs`, immediately after the closing `}` of `impl FromStr for Collision` (so before `/// One title of the owner's Assign titles`):

```rust

/// The signature of `streams[index]` (position counts earlier streams with the same kind, language, codec and channels).
/// `index` must be below `streams.len()`: callers pass a title's own stream list and an index into it. Spec 5. Def: T6.
/// Use: T6, T8, T10, T13.
pub fn signature(streams: &[Stream], index: usize) -> StreamSignature {
    let stream = &streams[index];
    let identical = |other: &&Stream| {
        other.kind == stream.kind
            && other.language == stream.language
            && other.codec.family == stream.codec.family
            && other.channels == stream.channels
    };
    StreamSignature {
        kind: stream.kind,
        language: stream.language.clone(),
        codec: stream.codec.family,
        channels: stream.channels,
        position: streams[..index].iter().filter(identical).count() as u32,
    }
}

/// Stream number to action for every stream of `kind` among `streams` whose signature has an entry (the first entry with
/// that signature); streams of other kinds are never looked up, so an entry whose signature names another kind is
/// never applied.
fn by_signature<'a, A>(entries: &[(&'a StreamSignature, &'a A)], streams: &[Stream], kind: StreamKind) -> BTreeMap<u32, &'a A> {
    let mut out = BTreeMap::new();
    for (index, stream) in streams.iter().enumerate() {
        if stream.kind != kind {
            continue;
        }
        let wanted = signature(streams, index);
        if let Some(entry) = entries.iter().find(|entry| *entry.0 == wanted) {
            out.insert(stream.number, entry.1);
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Stream number to override for every stream whose signature has an entry. Only the audio streams of `streams` are
/// looked up. Spec 5, 11. Def: T6. Use: T8.
pub fn apply_audio<'a>(overrides: &'a [AudioOverrideEntry], streams: &[Stream]) -> BTreeMap<u32, &'a AudioOverride> {
    let entries: Vec<(&StreamSignature, &AudioOverride)> =
        overrides.iter().map(|entry| (&entry.signature, &entry.action)).collect();
    by_signature(&entries, streams, StreamKind::Audio)
}

/// The same for subtitles: only the subtitle streams of `streams` are looked up. Spec 5, 11. Def: T6. Use: T10.
pub fn apply_subtitles<'a>(overrides: &'a [SubtitleOverrideEntry], streams: &[Stream]) -> BTreeMap<u32, &'a SubtitleOverride> {
    let entries: Vec<(&StreamSignature, &SubtitleOverride)> =
        overrides.iter().map(|entry| (&entry.signature, &entry.action)).collect();
    by_signature(&entries, streams, StreamKind::Subtitles)
}
```

- [ ] **Step 24: Implement the title match (spec 5 "Titles are matched by source file, segment map and duration within 2 s, never by title key")**

Insert into `crates/core/src/remembered.rs`, immediately after the closing `}` of `apply_subtitles`:

```rust

/// The remembered title is this scan title: `disc::same_source(&title_source(rem.source_file, rem.dvd_title), &title.source())`
/// (source file on a Blu-ray; on a DVD, both source files None, attribute 24 equal as numbers), `disc::segment_maps_agree`,
/// and duration within `disc::DURATION_MATCH_S`; never by title key. A scan title without a duration, or a remembered
/// title with neither a source file nor attribute 24, never matches. Def: T6. Use: T6, T7.
pub fn match_title(remembered: &RememberedTitle, title: &Title) -> bool {
    let source = title_source(remembered.source_file.as_deref(), remembered.dvd_title.as_deref());
    same_source(&source, &title.source())
        && segment_maps_agree(&remembered.segment_map, &title.segment_map)
        && title.seconds.map_or(false, |seconds| seconds.abs_diff(remembered.seconds) <= DURATION_MATCH_S)
}

/// Every scan title matched to a remembered title, title number to role (a remembered title is used once). The scan's
/// titles are taken in number order, each given the first remembered title not yet used that matches it. Spec 5, 6.1
/// step 2 ("A new job applies any remembered decisions"). Def: T6. Use: T7.
pub fn apply_titles<'a>(remembered: &'a Remembered, disc: &Disc) -> BTreeMap<u32, &'a TitleRole> {
    let mut used = vec![false; remembered.titles.len()];
    let mut out = BTreeMap::new();
    for (&number, title) in &disc.titles {
        let found = (0..remembered.titles.len()).find(|&at| !used[at] && match_title(&remembered.titles[at], title));
        if let Some(at) = found {
            used[at] = true;
            out.insert(number, &remembered.titles[at].role);
        }
    }
    out
}
```

```rust
    /// Spec 8.9 "Title and year always come from the same TMDb record as the ID": the Work for naming. Def: T3. Use: T11, T13.
    pub fn work(&self) -> Work;
}

/// `/movie/{id}` text (with `external_ids` appended or embedded as `append_to_response` gives it). Def: T3. Use: T15.
pub fn parse_movie(text: &str, shown: &str) -> Result<TmdbRecord, String>;
/// `/tv/{id}` text; `seasons[].episodes` are read when present (a test fixture or a merged season call). Def: T3. Use: T15.
pub fn parse_tv(text: &str, shown: &str) -> Result<TmdbRecord, String>;

// lazymkv_core::lookup::name (T4)
/// The disc's own name with the evidence parsed from it before cleaning. Def: T4. Use: T4 (identify), T5 (season marker), T6 (season), T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct DiscName {
    pub raw: String,
    pub source: NameSource,
    /// `parse_season(raw)`.
    pub season: Option<u32>,
    /// `parse_disc_number(raw)`.
    pub disc: Option<u32>,
    /// `clean(raw)`.
    pub cleaned: String,
    /// `is_generic(raw, cleaned)`.
    pub generic: bool,
    /// `has_season_marker(raw)` (8.2).
    pub season_marker: bool,
}
/// The bdmt name when Some and not blank, else the volume label when Some and not blank, else None. The caller builds it
/// once (`disc_name(bdmt, disc.volume_label.as_deref())`), searches TMDb with its `cleaned`, and passes it as
/// `LookupInputs.name`; `plan::plan` reads it from there and copies it into `PlanEvidence.name`. Def: T4. Use: T7 (tests), T15.
pub fn disc_name(bdmt: Option<&str>, volume_label: Option<&str>) -> Option<DiscName>;

// lazymkv_core::lookup identification (T4)
/// Spec 8.1's table rows, after the owner's review: Reviewed is spec 11's Set identity (8.8 "A review decision sets the
/// confidences it covers to 1.00"). Def: T4. Use: T7, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum IdentityStep { Reviewed, Remembered, DiscdbBoth, DiscdbOne, TmdbOne, TmdbSeveral, Nothing }
impl IdentityStep { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; pub const ALL: [IdentityStep; 7]; }

/// The confidence constants of 8.1 steps 1 to 6 and the cap of "When tmdb_only_autofile is off"; a review decision is
/// REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE too (1.00, 8.8). Def: T4. Use: T4, T7, T8, T10, T13.
pub const REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 1.00;
pub const DISCDB_BOTH_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.99;
pub const DISCDB_ONE_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.95;
pub const TMDB_ONE_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.90;
pub const TMDB_ONE_CAPPED_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.84;
pub const TMDB_SEVERAL_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.50;
pub const NOTHING_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.0;
/// (confidence, review reason) of a step: Reviewed and Remembered 1.00; reads settings.tmdb_only_autofile for TmdbOne (0.84
/// and IdentityAmbiguous when off); TmdbSeveral gives IdentityAmbiguous, Nothing gives IdentityUnknown. Def: T4. Use: T4, T7.
pub fn identity_confidence(step: IdentityStep, settings: &Settings) -> (f64, Option<ReviewReason>);

/// What the runtime checks compare against (8.1 "Runtime check"): the planned features' or cuts' durations (8.3, 8.4), the
/// longest rival when none is planned, and the durations of the disc's episode-length groups (8.2). The planner fills it
/// from the structural pass before the TMDb match (6.1 step 5's order). Def: T4. Use: T4, T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct RuntimeFacts { pub feature_seconds: Vec<u32>, pub longest_rival_seconds: Option<u32>, pub episode_group_seconds: Vec<u32> }

pub const MOVIE_RUNTIME_TOLERANCE: f64 = 0.03;
pub const TV_RUNTIME_TOLERANCE: f64 = 0.15;
/// Movies: at least one of `feature_seconds` (else `longest_rival_seconds`) within 3% of `runtime_min * 60`; false without a
/// runtime or without any duration. Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub fn movie_runtime_ok(facts: &RuntimeFacts, runtime_min: Option<u32>) -> bool;
/// TV: the median of `episode_runtimes_min` within 15% of the median of `episode_group_seconds / 60`; false when either list is
/// empty. The median of an even count is the mean of the two middle values. Def: T4. Use: T4.
pub fn tv_runtime_ok(facts: &RuntimeFacts, episode_runtimes_min: &[u32]) -> bool;
/// |a - b| <= tolerance * b. Def: T4. Use: T4, T5 (rule 4's 10%), T6 (suggest_by_runtime's 15%).
pub fn within(a: f64, b: f64, tolerance: f64) -> bool;

/// A TheDiscDB description's meaning (8.1 last bullet, D14, 8.7 "the one TheDiscDB describes as subtitles or SDH"):
/// "comment" gives Commentary; "audio desc", "descriptive", "DVS", "visually impaired" give AudioDescription; "SDH",
/// "hearing" give Sdh; "isolated score", "score only" give IsolatedScore; "music and effects", "music & effects", "M&E" give
/// MusicAndEffects; "subtitle", or a description that after trimming and case-folding equals the track's own `language`
/// (TheDiscDB's language name: "English"; Knowing's "ENglish" included), gives Dialogue. All case-insensitive, substring
/// matches, in this order; a text can carry several. IsolatedScore, MusicAndEffects and Dialogue are provisional: TheDiscDB's
/// wording for them is not yet known (8.1's last bullet names no such word; every subtitle description in the 18 answers
/// and the pinned files is a bare language name). Def: T4. Use: T8, T9, T10.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum DescriptionKind { Commentary, AudioDescription, Sdh, IsolatedScore, MusicAndEffects, Dialogue }
pub fn description_kinds(text: &str, language: Option<&str>) -> Vec<DescriptionKind>;

/// What the lookups gave (recorded, synthetic, or live in phase 2). `pending` flags say the answer is not in yet (8.1 "the
/// lookup is recorded as pending"). Def: T4. Use: T7, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct LookupInputs<'a> {
    /// The disc's own name, built by the caller with `name::disc_name` (a generic name is signalled by `DiscName.generic`, not by None).
    pub name: Option<&'a DiscName>,
    /// `/api/discid/{id}`: the first record of the array that has titles, or None (a miss, or no disc ID: a DVD).
    pub discdb_by_disc_id: Option<&'a DiscDbRecord>,
    /// `/api/dischash/{hash}`.
    pub discdb_by_fingerprint: Option<&'a DiscDbRecord>,
    pub discdb_pending: bool,
    /// The search 8.1 runs on the cleaned name (or on TheDiscDB's title and year when the entry has no TMDb ID).
    pub search: Option<&'a TmdbSearch>,
    /// The record fetched for the identity in hand.
    pub record: Option<&'a TmdbRecord>,
    pub tmdb_pending: bool,
    /// Step 1: the TMDb identity of a remembered decision for this fingerprint (`Remembered.tmdb`); plan::plan fills it from
    /// PlanInputs.remembered.
    pub remembered: Option<TmdbIdentity>,
    /// The owner's Set identity (spec 11), before step 1; plan::plan fills it from PlanInputs.overrides.
    pub reviewed: Option<TmdbIdentity>,
}

/// The identity 8.1 fixes at planning time. Def: T4. Use: T7, T11, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Identity {
    pub step: IdentityStep,
    pub confidence: f64,
    pub tmdb: Option<TmdbIdentity>,
    /// From the record when fetched, else from TheDiscDB's media, else from the one plausible result.
    pub title: Option<String>,
    pub year: Option<i32>,
    pub original_language: Option<String>,
    pub review: Option<ReviewReason>,
    /// The plausible results' identities (several in step 5; one in step 4).
    pub plausible: Vec<TmdbIdentity>,
    /// Whether a runtime check ran and what it said (None: not applicable, no record, or no runtime).
    pub runtime_check: Option<bool>,
    /// Pending lookups (8.1: planning proceeds on structure alone; the file phase waits in AwaitingLookup).
    pub lookup_pending: bool,
    /// One sentence per piece of evidence, in order ("TheDiscDB knows the fingerprint", "name 'JOHN_WICK_UHD' cleaned to 'JOHN WICK'").
    pub evidence: Vec<String>,
}

/// Spec 8.1 steps 1 to 6 in order, after the owner's review: `inputs.reviewed` is Some (Reviewed, 1.00, that identity);
/// `inputs.remembered` is Some (Remembered, 1.00, that identity); TheDiscDB by both disc ID and fingerprint (0.99: both
/// records present and their TMDb IDs equal, or one of them lacking an ID) or by one (0.95); else the search on a
/// non-generic cleaned name: exactly one plausible result and the runtime check passes (0.90, or 0.84 plus
/// identity_ambiguous when tmdb_only_autofile is off); several plausible results or a failed or impossible runtime check
/// (0.50, identity_ambiguous); else nothing (0, identity_unknown). The runtime check run is the one for the plausible
/// result's own TmdbKind (movie_runtime_ok for Movie, tv_runtime_ok for Tv), whatever `kind` is ("Movies and TV are searched
/// together"); `kind` (the structural kind) is used only to prefer results of that kind when several are plausible. A
/// generic name is never searched. A pending lookup does not lower the step reached by the answers in hand; it sets
/// lookup_pending. Def: T4. Use: T7.
pub fn identify(inputs: &LookupInputs<'_>, kind: Kind, runtime: &RuntimeFacts, settings: &Settings) -> Identity;

// lazymkv_core::plan::kind (T5)
/// How the kind was decided (8.2's three sources plus the movie default and 8.3 rule 3.1's play-all). Def: T5. Use: T7.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum KindSource { Discdb, Structure, SeasonMarker, PlayAll, Default }

/// 8.2's candidate filter: menu loops out (`is_menu_loop`), titles shorter than settings.minlength_s out, titles without a
/// duration out; the rest in title order. Def: T5. Use: T5, T7, phase 2 (6.3 step 6a's fallback list, 11's Assign titles).
pub fn candidate_filter(disc: &Disc, settings: &Settings) -> Vec<u32>;
/// A title with no audio stream, with more than one chapter every two minutes (`chapters as f64 > seconds as f64 / 120.0`, 0 s
/// counts as a loop when it has chapters), or whose segment map repeats one clip (every segment equal and two or more of
/// them). Spec 8.2. Def: T5. Use: T5.
pub fn is_menu_loop(title: &Title) -> bool;

/// Titles with identical segment maps (8.2). On a DVD the key is (attribute 24, segment map) because its segments restart at
/// 1 in every title (Review Focus 1); attribute 24 is unique per DVD title, so on a DVD every title is its own group. Def: T5. Use: T5, T6, T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Group {
    /// The group's key as text ("280,284,299" or, on a DVD, "01:1-29"); "#<title number>" for a title with no segment map,
    /// and for a DVD title without attribute 24.
    pub key: String,
    pub segment_map: String,
    pub segments: Vec<i64>,
    /// The members in title order; the first is the representative.
    pub titles: Vec<u32>,
    /// "a group's duration is that of its titles": the longest member's seconds.
    pub seconds: u32,
    pub truncated: bool,
}
/// The groups of `candidates`, in order of first title. Def: T5. Use: T5, T6, T7.
pub fn groups(disc: &Disc, candidates: &[u32]) -> Vec<Group>;

/// Spec 8.2: the shortest episode length, 15 minutes, included.
pub const EPISODE_MIN_S: u32 = 15 * 60;
/// Spec 8.2: the longest episode length, 120 minutes, included.
pub const EPISODE_MAX_S: u32 = 120 * 60;
pub const TV_SPREAD: f64 = 0.15;
/// The groups lasting between 15 and 120 minutes inclusive, in group order. Def: T5. Use: T5, T6, T7 (fills RuntimeFacts.episode_group_seconds).
pub fn episode_length_groups(groups: &[Group]) -> Vec<&Group>;
/// Three or more episode-length groups and the longest at most 15% longer than the shortest (`longest <= shortest * 1.15`). Def: T5. Use: T5.
pub fn structure_says_tv(groups: &[Group]) -> bool;
/// Spec 8.3 rule 3.1: the index of a group whose segment list is the concatenation of two or more other groups' lists, whose
/// segments follow one another in the whole list (the parts may be any other groups in any group order, each used once;
/// truncated groups never count); None when none is. Not applied on a DVD (segments restart per title). Def: T5. Use: T5, T6.
pub fn play_all(groups: &[Group], dvd: bool) -> Option<usize>;
/// 8.2's decision: TheDiscDB's kind when it knows the disc; else Tv when structure_says_tv or the name has a season marker;
/// else Movie. (Rule 3.1's play-all turns a Movie into Tv later, in plan::plan.) Def: T5. Use: T7.
pub fn disc_kind(discdb: Option<&DiscDbRecord>, groups: &[Group], name: Option<&DiscName>) -> (Kind, KindSource);

// lazymkv_core::plan::movie (T5)
/// Which rule of 8.3 chose the features. Def: T5. Use: T7.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum TitleRule { Database, Labels, Structure }

/// 8.3 rule 2's suffix table. Def: T5. Use: T5.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Suffix { None, R, Ur, Ext, Narrative, Language(String), Other(String) }
/// One parsed FPL_MainFeature label (8.3 rule 2). Def: T5. Use: T5.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Label { pub title: u32, pub suffix: Suffix, pub language: Option<String> }
/// A title comment (attribute 49) starting `FPL_MainFeature` (optionally preceded by `SEG_` or `SEG `): its suffix, with a
/// trailing `_XXX` three-letter language code split off as `language`. None for any other comment. Def: T5. Use: T5.
pub fn parse_label(title: u32, comment: &str) -> Option<Label>;
/// The table's edition name: None and R "Theatrical Cut", Ur "Unrated Cut", Ext "Extended Cut"; Narrative and Language give
/// None (ignored or a variant), Other gives None (an unnamed cut). Def: T5. Use: T5.
pub fn edition_of(suffix: &Suffix) -> Option<&'static str>;

/// Spec 8.3 rule 1: the disc database names the title, 0.98.
pub const DATABASE_TITLE_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.98;
/// Spec 8.3 rule 2: exactly one cut, or two or more cuts with different recognised suffixes, 0.90.
pub const LABELS_TITLE_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.90;
/// Spec 8.3 rule 3.5: one rival, which is the feature, 0.85.
pub const STRUCTURE_TITLE_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.85;
/// Spec 8.3: every ambiguous outcome (an unnamed cut, an ambiguous group, several rivals), 0.60.
pub const AMBIGUOUS_TITLE_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.60;
pub const RIVAL_BAND: f64 = 0.10;
pub const SEGMENT_DIFFERENCE_MAX: f64 = 0.25;
pub const RUNTIME_SANITY_BAND: f64 = 0.10;

/// One feature or cut to rip. Def: T5. Use: T7, T11, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Feature {
    pub title: u32,
    /// The edition name as the evidence gives it (TheDiscDB's item title beyond the media title, else the label table, or
    /// None for the theatrical or only cut); `edition_names` turns it into the filed name.
    pub edition: Option<String>,
    /// True when `edition` is None or names the theatrical cut (contains the word Theatrical; `is_theatrical`), except an
    /// unnamed cut (an Other label suffix, or a later TheDiscDB MainMovie with no edition), which has edition None and
    /// theatrical false.
    pub theatrical: bool,
    /// The titles of its group (rule 3) or cut (rule 2) that were not chosen.
    pub siblings: Vec<u32>,
}

/// The movie titles of 8.3 with their confidence and reasons. Def: T5. Use: T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct MoviePlan {
    pub rule: TitleRule,
    pub features: Vec<Feature>,
    /// Each feature's duration (`Title::seconds`), in feature order; rule 4 reads it, and the planner may fill
    /// `RuntimeFacts.feature_seconds` from it.
    pub feature_seconds: Vec<Option<u32>>,
    pub confidence: f64,
    pub reviews: Vec<ReviewReason>,
    pub notes: Vec<Noted>,
    /// Rule 3's rival groups (keys), for the evidence and the runtime facts.
    pub rivals: Vec<String>,
    pub evidence: Vec<String>,
}

/// Rule 1: applies only when TheDiscDB marks at least one MainMovie and every MainMovie title matches a scan title in
/// `matches`; one Feature per MainMovie, in database index order (0.98). Each Feature's edition is its item title with the
/// media title and surrounding brackets or dashes removed; when that leaves nothing, `disc.java_in_use` holds and the scan
/// title's comment (attribute 49) parses as a label, `edition_of(label.suffix)` (8.4 "else from the label table":
/// Expendables 3's title 41 `FPL_MainFeature_UR` gets "Unrated Cut"); `theatrical` as Feature's doc says. Two or more
/// MainMovies of which a later one still has no edition: 0.60 with unnamed_cut; two features given the same edition name
/// make it 0.60 with title_ambiguous (Review Focus 8). None when TheDiscDB marks no main movie or any MainMovie title does
/// not reconcile. Def: T5. Use: T5, T7.
pub fn by_database(record: &DiscDbRecord, matches: &BTreeMap<u32, u32>, disc: &Disc) -> Option<MoviePlan>;
/// Rule 2: only when `disc.java_in_use`; labels grouped by suffix without the language code, one cut per group, in order of
/// each cut's lowest title number; within a cut the variant whose audio covers the most of `wanted`'s languages, then the
/// one without a language suffix, then the lower title number; Narrative variants ignored. Exactly one cut 0.90; several
/// with recognised suffixes 0.90 as editions, except that two cuts given the same edition name (the `none` and `_R` rows
/// are both "Theatrical Cut") make it 0.60 with title_ambiguous (Review Focus 8); any Other suffix 0.60 with unnamed_cut.
/// None when no label is found. When Java was not reported, returns None and plan::plan adds the note
/// LabelRuleUnavailable. Def: T5. Use: T5, T7.
pub fn by_labels(disc: &Disc, wanted: &Wanted) -> Option<MoviePlan>;
/// What rule 3 found. Def: T5. Use: T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum StructureOutcome { PlayAll { group: usize }, Plan(MoviePlan) }
/// Rule 3 on the groups: 3.1 play-all (the disc is TV); 3.2 keep groups >= settings.feature_min_minutes, else the longest; 3.3
/// rivals within RIVAL_BAND of the longest kept; 3.4 in each rival the title with chapters, then the one whose audio and
/// subtitle stream signatures (kind, language, codec family, channels) are a superset of every other's, else 0.60
/// title_ambiguous; 3.5 one rival 0.85; 3.6 every pair's segment_difference <= 0.25 gives 0.60 title_ambiguous; 3.7 else 0.60
/// multiple_features. Def: T5. Use: T5, T7.
pub fn by_structure(disc: &Disc, groups: &[Group], settings: &Settings) -> StructureOutcome;
/// Segments in exactly one of the two lists, divided by the longer list's length; 0.0 for two empty lists. Spec 8.3 rule 3.6. Def: T5. Use: T5.
pub fn segment_difference(a: &[i64], b: &[i64]) -> f64;
/// Rule 4: a plan from rule 3 whose every feature's duration (`plan.feature_seconds`) is more than 10% from
/// `runtime_min * 60` drops to 0.60 with title_ambiguous (Open point 35); rule 1 and 2 plans and None runtimes are
/// returned unchanged. Def: T5. Use: T7.
pub fn runtime_sanity(plan: MoviePlan, runtime_min: Option<u32>) -> MoviePlan;
/// First applicable rule (8.3): by_database, else by_labels, else by_structure. Def: T5. Use: T7.
pub fn movie_plan(disc: &Disc, discdb: Option<&DiscDbRecord>, matches: &BTreeMap<u32, u32>, groups: &[Group], wanted: &Wanted, settings: &Settings) -> StructureOutcome;

/// What phase 2 reads from the library for 8.4 (RP18). Def: T5. Use: T7, T11, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct LibraryFacts {
    /// "the film's library folder already holds an edition-named file".
    pub folder_has_edition_named_file: bool,
    /// Earlier filed copies of this film: cut key ("theatrical", or the lower-cased edition name) to the edition name used
    /// ("" when that copy was filed without an edition name; this cut then gets None).
    pub earlier_edition_names: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    /// Spec 7: the final path already exists and is not this job's file. Phase 2 checks the plain path (no copy label);
    /// under the owner's Resolve collision "keep both" it must also check the copy-labelled path (`- 2160p 2`) before
    /// filing and hold the job with path_collision when that one is taken too (Open point 39).
    pub path_collision: bool,
}
/// 8.4's three rules, per feature in order: a non-theatrical cut always carries its name, even when it is the only cut; the
/// theatrical cut carries "Theatrical Cut" only when `features.len() >= 2` or `facts.folder_has_edition_named_file`; an
/// earlier filed copy's name (`earlier_edition_names`) replaces either. Names are raw here; naming::edition_label sanitises
/// and caps them. Def: T5. Use: T7, T13.
pub fn edition_names(features: &[Feature], facts: &LibraryFacts) -> Vec<Option<String>>;
pub const THEATRICAL_CUT: &str = "Theatrical Cut";
/// An edition name that names the theatrical or main cut (8.4): none at all, or a name containing the word Theatrical
/// (ignoring ASCII case), such as TheDiscDB's "Theatrical Version". The one test of "theatrical" for every rule and caller.
/// Def: T5. Use: T5, T13.
pub fn is_theatrical(edition: Option<&str>) -> bool;

// lazymkv_core::plan::tv (T6)
/// An episode assignment: season and one or more episode numbers (multi-episode titles, 8.5). `season` None means not
/// known (no season parsed and no session found): review asks for it (8.5); never 0, which is the specials season (8.9
/// `Season 00`). Def: T6. Use: T7, T11, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Episode { pub season: Option<u32>, pub episodes: Vec<u32>, pub name: Option<String> }
/// "12-13" gives [12, 13], "4" gives [4], "01" gives [1]; empty for anything else. Def: T6. Use: T6.
pub fn parse_episode_numbers(text: &str) -> Vec<u32>;

/// One title assigned or suggested. Spec 8.5. Def: T6. Use: T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct EpisodeTitle { pub title: u32, pub episode: Episode, pub suggested: bool }

pub const MAPPED_TV_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.98;
pub const UNMAPPED_TV_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.60;

/// Def: T6. Use: T7.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct TvPlan {
    pub mapped: bool,
    pub episodes: Vec<EpisodeTitle>,
    pub confidence: f64,
    pub reviews: Vec<ReviewReason>,
    /// Play-all titles dropped (8.5 "play all titles are dropped").
    pub dropped_play_all: Vec<u32>,
    pub evidence: Vec<String>,
}
/// 8.5 first bullet: every Episode item that `matches` reconciles becomes an EpisodeTitle (season from `item.season` parsed as
/// a number, None when absent, which plan::plan fills from the disc name's season; episodes from
/// `parse_episode_numbers(item.episode)`; name from `item.title`); every play-all group's titles are dropped (`kind::play_all`
/// applied again until it finds none); 0.98. None when the record has no reconciled Episode item, when any Episode item
/// matches no scan title (as Open point 4 for MainMovies), or when a reconciled Episode item on a title that is not
/// play-all names no episode number (D1); plan::plan then plans the disc as unmapped. Def: T6. Use: T7.
pub fn by_discdb(record: &DiscDbRecord, matches: &BTreeMap<u32, u32>, groups: &[Group], dvd: bool) -> Option<TvPlan>;
/// 8.5 "play all titles are dropped": every play-all group (8.3 rule 3.1, `kind::play_all`, found again until none is;
/// never on a DVD) is removed. Returns the remaining groups and the dropped titles, sorted. Def: T6. Use: T6, T7.
pub fn without_play_all(groups: &[Group], dvd: bool) -> (Vec<Group>, Vec<u32>);
/// Spec 8.5 "pre-assigned to episodes by runtime as a suggestion": the groups' representatives in title order, assigned
/// from episode `start`: each takes the next episode, or the next two when its duration is within TV_RUNTIME_TOLERANCE of
/// the sum of the next two episodes' runtimes and not within it of the next one's; an episode without a runtime takes one
/// title. Returns (title, episode numbers) pairs. Def: T6. Use: T6.
pub fn suggest_by_runtime(groups: &[&Group], episodes: &[TmdbEpisode], start: u32) -> Vec<(u32, Vec<u32>)>;
/// 8.5 second bullet: 0.60 with tv_unmapped; the episode-length groups' representatives are suggested from `start` (the
/// session's next unassigned episode, or 1), through `suggest_by_runtime` when `episodes` (the season's TMDb episodes) are
```

```rust
    pub fingerprint: Option<&'a str>,

/// 6.1 step 5 in order: candidates and groups (8.2); the kind; the structural pass (8.3 rules 1 to 3, or 8.5) to fill
/// RuntimeFacts, running by_labels with `wanted_languages(None)` (8.3 rule 3.1's play-all makes the disc TV unless
/// TheDiscDB states it is a movie, 8.2, when rule 3 runs again without the play-all groups; every play-all group is left
/// out of the episode-length groups, 8.5 "play all titles are dropped"); identify (8.1) over `inputs.lookups` with
/// `remembered` set to `inputs.remembered.map(|r| r.tmdb)` and `reviewed` to `inputs.overrides.and_then(|o| o.identity)`;
/// when `identity.original_language` is Some and not English, by_labels runs again with
/// `wanted_languages(identity.original_language)` and its features replace the first pass's (cuts, editions and confidence
/// never change between the passes, only the variant chosen within a cut); `Plan.wanted` is
/// `wanted_languages(identity.original_language)` for every title rule (English only when the original language is unknown
/// or English); rule 4; a remembered decision (`remembered::apply_titles`, when every remembered title that is not
/// Ignored matches a scan title) or the owner's Assign titles (`overrides.titles`, which win) replace the planned titles
/// and set title confidence to 1.00, and Set identity or a remembered identity sets identity confidence to 1.00;
/// `overrides.season` fills a planned episode whose season is None (else the disc name's season does); the mode; reviews
/// and notes gathered (8.8: identity and title confidence are fixed here; a search identity, TmdbOne or TmdbSeveral, whose
/// kind is not the planned kind adds identity_ambiguous, a provisional rule left to the owner). `Plan.titles` order
/// (which fixes the keys' NN through `title_key(position, ..)`): movies in feature order (database index order for rule
/// 1, each cut's lowest title number for rule 2, group order for rule 3), TV by (season, first episode) with season None
/// last in title order. The identity is confirmed when its step is Reviewed, Remembered, DiscdbBoth or DiscdbOne (8.5
/// "when its identity is confirmed (by TheDiscDB or in review)"). With a mapped TV plan and the identity confirmed (or
/// episodes assigned by a remembered decision or the owner), a TMDb show identity and a season, `Plan.session` is
/// `tv::find(..)`'s session or `SeasonSession::new(show_id, season, the record's episode_count for that season)`, with
/// the plan's episodes assigned (`assign` with the fingerprint, when given); with an unmapped plan the found session
/// gives `start` (and the season when none was parsed), and when the identity is confirmed and the season is known,
/// `Plan.session` is that session or a new one with the disc recorded and no episode assigned (`assign` with the
/// fingerprint and no pair; spec 11 Set identity "attaches the disc to a season session"); None otherwise. Err only when
/// the disc has no title at all. Def: T7. Use: T15.
pub fn plan(inputs: &PlanInputs<'_>) -> Result<Plan, String>;

/// Spec 7 "Space checks": 5% over the planned titles' sizes before a Direct rip. Def: T7. Use: phase 2.
pub const DIRECT_SPACE_MARGIN: f64 = 0.05;
/// Spec 7 "Space checks": 2% over the disc size before a whole-disc copy. Def: T7. Use: phase 2.
pub const COPY_SPACE_MARGIN: f64 = 0.02;
/// Spec 7 "Space checks": 5% over the files to be written before extraction or remux. Def: T7. Use: phase 2.
pub const WRITE_SPACE_MARGIN: f64 = 0.05;
/// Bytes needed on staging for the plan's mode: Direct, the sum of `PlannedTitle.size` (a title without a size counts 0)
/// times 1.05; Copy, `disc_size` times 1.02; rounded up. Def: T7. Use: phase 2.
pub fn staging_bytes_needed(plan: &Plan, disc_size: u64) -> u64;
/// `bytes` times 1.05, rounded up (before extraction or remux). Def: T7. Use: phase 2.
pub fn write_bytes_needed(bytes: u64) -> u64;
```

Where this task settles what the spec and the interfaces leave open (each choice is pinned by a test below):

1. **Which TheDiscDB record the titles are matched against.** The fingerprint's record when there is one, else the disc ID's (8.1: the fingerprint is the primary key; Open point 3: the fingerprint's record wins). `a_thediscdb_record_by_disc_id_alone_plans_like_one_by_fingerprint` and `thediscdb_by_disc_id_and_fingerprint_gives_0_99` pin it.
2. **`Plan.wanted`.** `wanted_languages(identity.original_language)` for every title rule, not only when rule 2 ran twice: the audio and subtitle rules (Tasks 8, 13) read it, and a database-planned Spanish film (`pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd` in "Expected plans": "wanted eng and spa") needs Spanish there. The interfaces file's `plan` doc says the same (an earlier "the first's when there is no second" would have left such a film English-only). Pinned by `a_database_identity_takes_its_original_language_from_the_tmdb_record`; for an English original `Plan.wanted` is English only (`original_is_english`, `original` empty), whatever `original_two_letter` holds (`the_label_variant_is_rechosen_once_the_original_language_is_known`).
3. **Edition names in the plan.** `PlannedRole::Feature.edition` is the filed name of 8.4 (`movie::edition_names` over `PlanInputs.library`), so a lone theatrical cut has None (Smile) and Expendables' main movie has `Unrated Cut`. Two or more structural rivals (rule 3) carry no edition name: rule 3 names no cut and such a plan is held for review, where the owner names cuts (8.4 "else from the owner in review"); without this, `edition_names` would call both rivals "Theatrical Cut". An unnamed cut (rule 1 or 2, `unnamed_cut`) also has edition None and is not theatrical; a consumer that runs `edition_names` again must keep the plan's editions for it, as for structural rivals (Task 13's `filed_edition` does both).
4. **The LabelRuleUnavailable note** (10.2 ToolMissing: "when MakeMKV did not report using it, label rule 8.3.2 does not apply and a note records why") is raised when rule 2 was reached (rule 1 gave no plan, or rule 3 found a play-all title) on a Blu-ray scan without `MSG:3344`. A DVD has no Java menus and never gets it; a disc that rule 1 planned does not need it; a disc made TV by TheDiscDB, its structure or its season marker never reaches rule 2 and does not get it either (`an_unmapped_tv_disc_is_suggested_by_runtime_at_0_60_with_tv_unmapped` pins that absence on a Blu-ray without Java).
5. **Every play-all group** (8.3 rule 3.1, `tv::without_play_all`, which applies `kind::play_all` again until it finds none, since 8.5 says "play all titles are dropped" in the plural) is left out of the episode-length groups that `RuntimeFacts.episode_group_seconds` and `tv::unmapped` read; they stay in `PlanEvidence.groups`. A disc with an extras play-all beside an episodes play-all suggests neither (`every_play_all_title_is_dropped_from_the_suggestions`), and a play-all title on a disc rule 3 finds is never suggested (`a_play_all_title_makes_a_movie_disc_tv_and_is_never_suggested`).
6. **Seasons.** A planned episode without a season takes `overrides.season`, else the disc name's season. For an unmapped disc the session `tv::find` returns gives the suggestions' start and, when it was found without a parsed season (the show's single open session, 8.5), the season too; with several open sessions and no parsed season the suggestions start at episode 1 with no season, and review asks for it (8.5 "failing that"; `with_several_open_sessions_and_no_parsed_season_review_asks_for_the_season`). An unmapped disc's suggested episodes are never assigned in a session. Spec 11 says Set identity "For TV this also attaches the disc to a season session", and 8.5 that "A disc joins a session when its identity is confirmed (by TheDiscDB or in review)": so an unmapped TV disc whose identity is confirmed (step Reviewed, Remembered, DiscdbBoth or DiscdbOne; a remembered decision is an earlier review's) and whose season is known gets `Plan.session`, the found session or a new one, with the disc recorded and no episode assigned (`tv::assign(.., fingerprint, &[])`); a search identity (TmdbOne, TmdbSeveral) is not confirmed and attaches nothing (`set_identity_attaches_an_unmapped_disc_to_its_season_session_without_episodes`, `an_unmapped_disc_continues_its_season_session_from_the_next_unassigned_episode`). The same rule holds for a mapped disc: TheDiscDB's map joins the season session only when the identity is confirmed. A TheDiscDB entry without a TMDb ID whose one plausible search result has another year is step 5 (Task 4: 0.50, `identity_ambiguous`, with that result's show identity); its mapped episodes are planned at 0.98 but recorded in no session (`a_mapped_disc_whose_identity_is_not_confirmed_joins_no_session`).
7. **Assigned titles** (a remembered decision's matched titles, or the owner's Assign titles when it names any title, which then wins whole) replace the planned titles at 1.00 and take the title rule's review reasons with them; an Ignored title and a title number the scan lacks are left out with a sentence; a Cut keeps its name and a Feature is the theatrical or main cut, both through `edition_names`; only episodes make the disc TV and only features a movie (`kind_source` is not changed: it records how the scan looked; when the assigned titles change the kind, the sentence `the assigned titles make the disc TV`, or `... a movie`, records it, pinned by `assigned_episodes_make_a_tv_plan_that_joins_the_season_session`). Assigned episodes with a TMDb show identity join the season session as a mapped disc's do (8.5 "when its identity is confirmed (by TheDiscDB or in review)"). A remembered decision applies only when every one of its titles that is not Ignored matches a scan title: spec 5 says it "sets the confidence it covers to 1.00", and one that matches only some of its titles does not cover this scan (taken at 1.00 it would make a Direct job that silently leaves the other titles out, 8.8 "Limits of D1"). The titles are then planned, with the sentence `the remembered decision matches only <n> of its <m> titles: the titles are planned` (`a_remembered_decision_that_matches_only_some_of_its_titles_leaves_the_planned_titles`); the remembered identity still applies. `assigned_entries` decides whether an assigned Cut is theatrical with `edition.as_str() == THEATRICAL_CUT`, which is provisional: Task 5's `movie::is_theatrical` is the one test (so a Cut named "Theatrical Version" is theatrical), and Task 13's Step 2 swaps the comparison for it; no Task 7 test depends on the difference.
8. **`title_key` when the source is missing.** A Blu-ray title without attribute 16, or a DVD title without attribute 24, is keyed `title<scan title number>` with two digits (`t02-title07`); no recorded or pinned scan has such a title.
9. **Space needs** are computed in integer arithmetic (`bytes * (100 + percent)`, divided by 100 rounding up, at most `u64::MAX`), so a 67,757,930,496-byte title needs exactly 71,145,827,021 bytes.
10. **Synthetic TMDb answers.** No TMDb search answer or full record is recorded anywhere; the tests build them with Task 2's `search_json`, `tmdb_movie_json` and `tmdb_tv_json`, which follow TMDb's documented `/search/multi`, `/movie/{id}` and `/tv/{id}` shapes. Phase 2's client verifies the shapes live.
11. **A play-all title on a disc TheDiscDB calls a movie.** 8.2 says "TheDiscDB states the kind when it knows the disc", so 8.3 rule 3.1's "treat the disc as TV" applies only when the kind came from structure, a season marker or the movie default. When TheDiscDB's record says Movie but rule 1 gives no plan (its MainMovie does not reconcile, Open point 4, or it marks none) and rule 3 finds a play-all title (an extras play-all, as on Smile and Chernobyl, Task 5 point 9), the disc stays a movie and rule 3 runs again without the play-all groups, one at a time until it plans; the sentence `8.3 rule 3.1: group <key> is a play-all title, but TheDiscDB states the disc is a movie (8.2)` records it. Pinned by `a_play_all_title_on_a_disc_thediscdb_calls_a_movie_leaves_it_a_movie`.
12. **A search identity of the other kind than the planned disc** (open: the spec does not settle it; recorded for the owner). 8.1's runtime check is the plausible result's own kind's (Task 4), so a one-episode disc of a show with feature-length episodes (one group of about 100 minutes, no season marker) is planned as a movie (8.2's default; rule 3 at 0.85) while TMDb's one plausible result, a show, passes its TV check at step 4 (0.90). Nothing would hold that plan: mode Direct and no review reason, and Task 13 could file it on a movie path. Until the owner rules, D1 decides (hold the disc when unsure): when the step is TmdbOne or TmdbSeveral and the identity's kind is not the planned kind (after any assigned titles), `plan` adds `identity_ambiguous` and the sentence `the TMDb identity is TV but the disc is planned as a movie` (or the reverse). A TheDiscDB, remembered or reviewed identity is not checked: TheDiscDB states the kind (8.2), and the owner chose the other two. Pinned by `a_search_identity_of_the_other_kind_than_the_planned_disc_is_held`.

```rust
/// Direct when `title_confidence >= settings.auto_threshold`, else Copy (6.2, 6.3, 8.8). Reads `settings.auto_threshold`
/// only. Def: T5. Use: T7.
pub fn mode(title_confidence: f64, settings: &Settings) -> Mode {
    if title_confidence >= settings.auto_threshold {
        Mode::Direct
    } else {
        Mode::Copy
    }
}

/// Spec 5: `t<NN>-<source file stem>` ("t00-00800") or `t<NN>-title<attribute 24>` on a DVD ("t00-title01"); `order` is the
/// title's position in `Plan.titles`. `NN` is `order` written with at least two digits; attribute 24 keeps MakeMKV's
/// spelling ("01", Open point 18), so keys stay stable across scans of the same disc. A Blu-ray title without attribute 16,
/// or a DVD title without attribute 24, is keyed `title<scan title number, two digits>` ("t02-title07"). Def: T7.
/// Use: T7, T13, T16.
pub fn title_key(order: usize, title: &Title, dvd: bool) -> String {
    let source = if dvd {
        title.dvd_title.as_deref().map(str::trim).filter(|number| !number.is_empty()).map(|number| format!("title{number}"))
    } else {
        title.source_file.as_deref().map(file_stem).filter(|stem| !stem.is_empty()).map(str::to_string)
    };
    let source = source.unwrap_or_else(|| format!("title{:02}", title.number));
    format!("t{order:02}-{source}")
}

/// A source file's name without its folder and without its last extension ("00800.mpls" gives "00800", "00001.m2ts"
/// gives "00001"); a name that starts with its only dot is kept whole.
fn file_stem(source_file: &str) -> &str {
    let name = source_file.rsplit(|c: char| c == '/' || c == '\\').next().unwrap_or(source_file);
    match name.rfind('.') {
        Some(at) if at > 0 => &name[..at],
        _ => name,
    }
}
```
