```rust
    /// 0.70 and 0.30: the provisional alignment bands (8.7).
    pub subs_same_min: f64,
    pub subs_diff_max: f64,
    /// 64: image-subtitle packets this small clear the screen (8.7).
    pub sub_clear_max_bytes: i64,
    /// Combined (8.9).
    pub edition_style: EditionStyle,
    /// false: add the square-bracket ID tag (8.9).
    pub jellyfin10_compat: bool,
    /// 7: days raw data of filed jobs is kept (7).
    pub retention_days: u32,
    /// true: D16.
    pub keep_tuning_evidence: bool,
    /// None; required while keep_tuning_evidence is on; not inside staging_root or a library root (7, 14).
    pub tuning_root: Option<String>,
    /// 1, 10, 120, 30, 300, 20, 30 (spec 14, in its order).
    pub file_phase_concurrency: u32,
    pub drive_settle_s: u32,
    pub drive_ready_timeout_s: u32,
    pub scan_timeout_min: u32,
    pub stall_timeout_s: u32,
    pub read_error_rate: u32,
    pub exit_wait_min: u32,
    /// "2.0.0": lowest supported MakeMKV (9.1).
    pub makemkv_min_version: String,
    pub tool_paths: ToolPaths,
}
impl Default for Settings { fn default() -> Settings; }

/// The notes of spec 8.6, 8.7, 8.9, 7, 6.3, 10.2, D9 and RP7. Def: T1. Use: T5, T8, T10, T11, T13, T14.

#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]

    PossibleCommentary,          // 8.6 step 6, naming the track
```

```rust
/// Spec 8.6 steps 1 to 6 and "Content" (RP7), in order: drop (derived 2048; flags 1, 2, 4; secondary 512; duplicates by

/// Commentary, AudioDescription, IsolatedScore or MusicAndEffects through `descriptions` when the alignment is unique;
/// unwanted language; a remembered or review Drop or Commentary); keep the rest and any no-language stream; rank with
/// `rank_key`; guards G1 and G2; order by language (original first when settings.original_language_first and the
/// original is not English, else English first; no language last), default on the very first track, original flag on
/// the original-language tracks (the English ones for an English work); notes possible_commentary,
/// lossless_original_available, no_english_audio, lossy_before_lossless (D9); reviews original_language_missing,
/// no_wanted_audio; verdicts apply only when `facts.verdict_reference` and the decision's `reference` are both Some (a
/// title without a kept original-language or English track has nothing to judge, spec 8.6 "Content"): when they differ
/// (spec 15: evidence measured against another reference than the rule's own choice), or `facts.veto_holds` is true
/// (D21: the rule confirms no commentary on the title), only audio_reference_unclear is raised and no verdict is mapped;
/// otherwise, for the kept streams in a wanted language (Original or English group; no-language streams are not judged,
/// spec 8.6 "Content"), ReferenceUnclear adds audio_reference_unclear, Commentary and CommentaryCrossLanguage add
/// commentary_detected (nothing dropped, D15), AdPattern, NoteCommentary and NoteAd add notes; a remembered or review
/// Keep { order, default } fixes the order and the default. Confidence 0.95, or
/// lookup::REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE (1.00) when every audio stream of the title has a remembered or review override. At
/// planning time `facts` is empty and the ffprobe criterion is skipped (8.3). Def: T8. Use: T13, T16.
pub fn decide_audio(title: &Title, wanted: &Wanted, facts: &AudioFacts<'_>, settings: &Settings) -> AudioDecision;
/// 8.6 step 3's sort key (ascending): (channels descending, tier, object descending, sample size descending, sample rate
/// descending, bitrate descending for lossy only, disc position); with settings.prefer_most_channels off, tier comes before
/// channels. An unknown tier sorts after Low; a lossy track without bitrate text sorts after every lossy track with one.
/// The product's copy beside audio::reference::rank (Global Constraints). Def: T8. Use: T8.
pub fn rank_key(track: &AudioTrack, settings: &Settings) -> (i64, i64, i64, i64, i64, i64, i64);
/// G1: a lossy track at G1_MAX_KBPS or less (or with no bitrate) never before a lossless track of the same language. G2: a
/// lossy top track with <= 2 channels that is not first of its language and beats the first on channel count but on no later
/// criterion gives way to the first. Returns the language's tracks reordered. Def: T8. Use: T8.
pub fn guards(ranked: Vec<AudioTrack>, settings: &Settings) -> Vec<AudioTrack>;
/// Spec 8.6 step 1: TheDiscDB's whole track list (every kind, index order) against the title's whole stream list (scan
/// order), pairwise on kind (`DiscDbTrack::kind`), language (`norm_lang` of `language_code` against `norm_lang` of attribute
/// 3; video compares no language), codec as attribute 7 (`Stream.codec_long == DiscDbTrack.name`) and channels
/// (`DiscDbTrack::channels` against attribute 14, audio only); tried on all streams and on the streams without flag 2048;
/// Some only when exactly one of the two aligns completely (equal lengths, every pair equal). A title without derived
/// streams has one list, tried once (Full when it aligns); an empty TheDiscDB track list never aligns. The map is scan
/// stream number to TheDiscDB track index. Def: T8. Use: T8.
pub fn align_descriptions(title: &Title, discdb: &DiscDbTitle) -> Option<(Alignment, BTreeMap<u32, u32>)>;
/// Every scan stream (any kind) whose aligned TheDiscDB track has a description, to `lookup::description_kinds(description,
/// track.language)`; with the alignment used. Empty and None without a record or without a unique alignment. Def: T8. Use: T8, T9, T10.
pub fn descriptions(title: &Title, discdb: Option<&DiscDbTitle>) -> (Option<Alignment>, BTreeMap<u32, Vec<DescriptionKind>>);
```

Beyond the shared entries, `LangGroup` and `Alignment` get the closed-set members the plan's conventions require of every closed set of spec strings (`as_str`, `ALL`, `FromStr`); they are additive and no other task depends on them. `guards` names its settings parameter `_settings` in the implementation, because the guards apply whatever the D9 setting says (spec 8.6 step 4); the signature is the shared one.

Where this task settles what the spec and the interfaces leave open (each choice is pinned by a test below):

1. **The two alignment lists of 8.6 step 1.** When a title has no derived stream (every DVD, and many extras), the full stream list and the list without derived streams are the same list, so it is tried once and an alignment is `Full`. Read literally, "exactly one of the two must align completely" would refuse every such title, Knowing's flagged and described commentary included. When the title has derived streams the two lists differ in length, so at most one can align; a title whose TheDiscDB track list is empty never aligns. Every pinned record aligns `Full` (TheDiscDB lists MakeMKV's derived cores and forced-only streams); `WithoutDerived` is tested on Smile's record with its 19 derived tracks removed.
2. **Pairing a TheDiscDB track with a stream.** Kind through `DiscDbTrack::kind`; language as `norm_lang` of both sides (so `ger` pairs with `deu`; a video track compares no language); codec as `DiscDbTrack.name == Stream.codec_long` (attribute 7); channels, audio only, as `DiscDbTrack::channels() == Stream.channels` (both None also pairs, a layout TheDiscDB names otherwise never does). `descriptions` lists every aligned stream whose track has a non-blank description, with `lookup::description_kinds` of it (possibly empty).
3. **Step 1's order and its labels.** The bullets are tried in the spec's order and the first that holds names the reason: derived, flagged (the bits 1, 2 and 4 that are set), secondary, duplicate, described (the first of Commentary, AudioDescription, IsolatedScore, MusicAndEffects in `DescriptionKind` order), unwanted language. D13's duplicate compares a stream's MD5 with the earlier audio streams that were kept (every bullet of step 1 and the overrides passed; `decide_audio` records a stream's MD5 only once it is kept), and `of` is the first of them with the same MD5, so `of` always names a kept copy and one copy is always kept: when the first of two identical streams is dropped for its language, its description or an override, the second is not a duplicate of it and is kept.
4. **Overrides.** The owner's Override tracks (`facts.reviewed`, only for the title's audio streams) win over remembered ones (`remembered::apply_audio`). A Keep override keeps its stream even where step 1 would drop it; a Drop or Commentary override drops a stream step 1 keeps (`Remembered` or `Reviewed`), and where step 1 drops it too, step 1's reason is recorded. Keep orders are target positions (0 first): overridden tracks take their positions in (order, rule position) order, a position already taken or past the end goes to the next free one, and the other tracks fill the rest in the rule's order. The default track is the first whose override says `default: true`; when none says so, it is the very first track (8.6 step 5). Confidence is 1.00 only when the title has at least one audio stream and every one has an override.
5. **Language groups.** A kept stream belongs to Original when its code is one of `Wanted.original`, to English when `lang::is_english`, else to NoLanguage. Ranking, the guards, "first of its language" and the notes work per group. A stream kept only by a Keep override in a language that is not wanted is ordered with the no-language tracks (its override fixes its place anyway). The original flag goes to the Original group, or to the English group for an English work (TMDb's code `en`, read from `Wanted.original_two_letter` through `lang::is_english`); a work whose original language is unknown, `xx` or missing from the ISO 639 table has `original_is_english` set (English is its reference language and its first group) but is not an English work, so none of its tracks gets the original flag (8.6 step 5 names English works only).
6. **The object criterion.** Spec 8.3 says "any use of the audio ranking in 8.6 skips its ffprobe criterion" at planning time, so step 3.3 reads ffprobe's profile only (`codec::object_audio`). After ordering, a track takes attribute 7's object (`Codec.object`) when ffprobe's profile names none (no profile, or a profile in which `codec::object_audio` finds no extension; the profile spellings are unverified, EXP-06 not run), for its `object` field and its name (8.10 "TrueHD Atmos 7.1"), so a DTS:X stream whose profile ffprobe gives as plain "DTS-HD MA" keeps attribute 7's DTS:X in its object and its name; a profile that names an extension wins. The ranking never reads attribute 7.
7. **The guards.** G1 moves every weak track (lossy at `G1_MAX_KBPS` or less, or without a bit rate) that is ranked before the language's last lossless track to just after it, keeping both groups' order. G2's "beats the first track on channel count but on no later criterion" compares criteria 2 to 5 of the spec's list (tier, object, depth and rate, bit rate), whatever `prefer_most_channels` says; bit rate counts only when the first track is lossy too, because 3.5 ranks lossy tracks only (a lossy top track would otherwise always "beat" a lossless first track on it, and step 4's case of a lossless mono original behind a lossy stereo track would never be guarded). G2 is applied after G1.
8. **Notes, gaps and the reference.** Notes are judged on the final order, per group, in the spec's bullet order: `possible_commentary` per track, `lossless_original_available` per group (the group's first track lossy, a lossless one with fewer channels after it; no stream named), `no_english_audio`, then D9's `lossy_before_lossless` once per group, naming the first lossy track placed before a lossless one with fewer channels. The gaps are judged on the kept tracks: `original_language_missing` when the original language is wanted and no kept track is in it; `no_wanted_audio` when nothing is kept. The programme reference is taken from the rule's order (before Keep orders): the first Original track, else the first English one, else None.
9. **Verdicts.** They apply only when `facts.verdict_reference` is Some and the decision has a reference. A title without a kept original-language or English track has no reference and nothing to judge (8.6 "Content"), so its verdicts add nothing, although phase 0's `programme_reference` measures such a title against a stream of any language for the dataset. When the measured reference is not the decision's reference, nothing is applied and `audio_reference_unclear` is raised. When the veto holds, `audio_reference_unclear` is raised and no verdict is applied (D21: "the rule confirms no commentary on the title"; `audio::rule::results` has already turned every candidate into `reference-unclear`). Otherwise each verdict of a kept stream in the Original or English group maps per RP7: 8.6 "Content" measures the streams in a wanted language, and `audio::reference::wanted` says the app does not judge the no-language candidates phase 0 measures, so a verdict on a no-language stream (or on an unwanted-language stream kept by a Keep override, which is in the NoLanguage group) adds nothing. `duplicate`, `keep` and `not-judged` add nothing (D13's drop is by MD5). A verdict note is not added twice for the same note and stream.
10. **Names.** `<display> [Atmos|DTS:X] <layout>` with `codec::channel_layout`; the layout is left out when the channel count is unknown (attribute 14 absent reads 0).

Every test reads only synthetic scans built with `testsupport::scan_text` and the public pinned fixtures `corpus/thediscdb/movie/Knowing (2009)/2010-dvd/disc01.{txt,json}` and `corpus/thediscdb/movie/Smile (2022)/2022-4k/disc01.{txt,json}`, so all run on every OS and in CI. Facts read from the fixtures for the expectations below: Knowing's title 0 (`B1`, attribute 24 `01`) has 8 streams and no derived one: video `Mpeg2`, English Dolby Digital 5.1 at `448 Kb/s` (stream 1), Spanish Dolby Digital 5.1 (stream 2), English Dolby Digital stereo at `192 Kb/s` with flags `1` (stream 3), and four DVD subtitle streams; its TheDiscDB title 0 lists the same 8 tracks with the descriptions `ENglish` (1), `Spanish` (2) and `Director Commentary` (3). Smile's title 14 (`00040.mpls`, `FPL_MainFeature`) has 47 streams: video, TrueHD Atmos 7.1 (attribute 7 `TrueHD Atmos`, `128 Kb/s`, 24-bit, flags 1024; stream 1), the derived Dolby Digital 5.1 core (flags 2304; stream 2), Dolby Digital 5.1 English at `640 Kb/s` (stream 3), Dolby Digital 5.1 German, Spanish, French (two), Italian and Japanese (streams 4 to 9), Dolby Digital stereo English at `224 Kb/s` (stream 10), and 36 PGS streams of which 18 are derived forced-only (flags 6144: the even streams 12 to 46); its TheDiscDB title 14 lists the same 47 tracks, stream 10 described `Commentary by Director Parker Finn`. The Office's twin tracks are a synthetic copy of the layout of its title 1 (`00004.mpls`, S03E15): streams 1 and 3 (DTS-HD MA 5.1, flags 1024) and their cores 2 and 4 (DTS 5.1 at `1.5 Mb/s`, flags 2304). Their packet MD5s in the tests are made up (`aaaa0000000000000000000000000001` for streams 1 and 3, `bbbb0000000000000000000000000002` for streams 2 and 4): D13 needs only that identical streams carry equal strings, and the recorded values stay in the private evidence clone.

```rust
//! Tests of core::tracks::audio (spec 8.6 steps 1 to 6 and "Content", D9, D13, D15, D21, RP7). The pinned logs and
//! TheDiscDB records of Knowing (DVD) and Smile (UHD) are read from corpus/thediscdb; every other title is built
//! with testsupport::scan_text. The Office's twin tracks are a synthetic copy of the layout of its title 1 (S03E15)
//! with made-up packet MD5s.

use std::fs;
use std::path::Path;

use serde_json::json;

use super::*;
use crate::disc::{disc, Disc};
use crate::lookup::discdb::{parse_dischash, DiscDbRecord};
use crate::robot::parse;
use crate::testsupport::scan_text;

/// The text of a file under the repository's `corpus` folder.
fn corpus(path: &str) -> String {
    let path = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../corpus").join(path);
    fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{}: {error}", path.display()))
}

/// Knowing's pinned DVD: `disc01.txt` (the scan) and `disc01.json` (TheDiscDB's record).
const KNOWING: &str = "thediscdb/movie/Knowing (2009)/2010-dvd/disc01";
/// Smile's pinned UHD.
const SMILE: &str = "thediscdb/movie/Smile (2022)/2022-4k/disc01";

/// The typed disc of a scan's text.
fn pinned_disc(text: &str) -> Disc {
    disc(&parse(text)).unwrap()
}

/// A pinned TheDiscDB record (an object with a non-empty `Titles` is a hit).
fn pinned_record(stem: &str) -> DiscDbRecord {
    let shown = format!("{stem}.json");
    parse_dischash(&corpus(&shown), &shown).unwrap().unwrap()
}

/// TheDiscDB's title `index` of a record.
fn db_title(record: &DiscDbRecord, index: u32) -> DiscDbTitle {
    record.titles.iter().find(|title| title.index == index).unwrap().clone()
}

/// One stream's attributes as (attribute id, value) pairs; a later pair overrides an earlier one with the same id,
/// as the scan's last line wins.
type Attrs = Vec<(u32, &'static str)>;

/// A Blu-ray video stream: AVC 1080p.
fn video() -> Attrs {
    vec![(1, "Video"), (5, "V_MPEG4/ISO/AVC"), (6, "Mpeg4"), (7, "Mpeg4 AVC High@L4.1"), (19, "1920x1080")]
}

/// An audio stream: language (attribute 3, left out when ""), codec attributes 5, 6 and 7, channels (14), bit rate
/// text (13, left out when "") and a sample rate of 48000 (17).
fn audio(
    language: &'static str,
    id: &'static str,
    short: &'static str,
    long: &'static str,
    channels: &'static str,
    bitrate: &'static str,
) -> Attrs {
    let mut attrs = vec![(1, "Audio")];
    if !language.is_empty() {
        attrs.push((3, language));
    }
    attrs.extend([(5, id), (6, short), (7, long), (14, channels), (17, "48000")]);
    if !bitrate.is_empty() {
        attrs.push((13, bitrate));
    }
    attrs
}

/// A Dolby Digital (AC-3) stream.
fn dd(language: &'static str, channels: &'static str, bitrate: &'static str) -> Attrs {
    audio(language, "A_AC3", "DD", "Dolby Digital", channels, bitrate)
}

/// Title 0 of a one-title Blu-ray scan (1:40:00, `00800.mpls`, segment map `1`) whose streams are numbered from 0 in
/// the order given.
fn title_of(streams: &[Attrs]) -> Title {
    let numbered: Vec<(u32, &[(u32, &str)])> =
        streams.iter().enumerate().map(|(number, attrs)| (number as u32, attrs.as_slice())).collect();
    let attrs: &[(u32, &str)] = &[(9, "1:40:00"), (16, "00800.mpls"), (26, "1")];
    let text = scan_text(&[(1, "Blu-ray disc")], &[(0, attrs, numbered.as_slice())]);
    disc(&parse(&text)).unwrap().titles[&0].clone()
}

#[test]
fn the_audio_confidence_is_0_95_and_g1s_line_is_256_kbps() {
    assert_eq!(AUDIO_CONFIDENCE, 0.95);
    assert_eq!(G1_MAX_KBPS, 256);
}

#[test]
fn the_language_groups_and_alignments_spell_as_serde_writes_them() {
    for (group, text) in
        [(LangGroup::Original, "original"), (LangGroup::English, "english"), (LangGroup::NoLanguage, "no_language")]
    {
        assert_eq!(group.as_str(), text);
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(group).unwrap(), json!(text));
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_value::<LangGroup>(json!(text)).unwrap(), group);
        assert_eq!(text.parse::<LangGroup>(), Ok(group));
    }
    assert_eq!(LangGroup::ALL, [LangGroup::Original, LangGroup::English, LangGroup::NoLanguage]);
    assert_eq!(
        "English".parse::<LangGroup>(),
        Err("\"English\" is not a language group (spec 8.6 step 5)".to_string())
    );
    for (alignment, text) in [(Alignment::Full, "full"), (Alignment::WithoutDerived, "without_derived")] {
        assert_eq!(alignment.as_str(), text);
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(alignment).unwrap(), json!(text));
        assert_eq!(text.parse::<Alignment>(), Ok(alignment));
    }
    assert_eq!(Alignment::ALL, [Alignment::Full, Alignment::WithoutDerived]);
    assert_eq!("partial".parse::<Alignment>(), Err("\"partial\" is not an alignment (spec 8.6 step 1)".to_string()));
}

#[test]
fn a_drop_reason_is_written_with_its_why_tag() {
    let cases = [
        (AudioDrop::Derived, json!({"why": "derived"})),
        (AudioDrop::Flagged { flags: 1 }, json!({"why": "flagged", "flags": 1})),
        (AudioDrop::Secondary, json!({"why": "secondary"})),
        (AudioDrop::Duplicate { of: 1 }, json!({"why": "duplicate", "of": 1})),
        (AudioDrop::Described { kind: DescriptionKind::Commentary }, json!({"why": "described", "kind": "commentary"})),
        (AudioDrop::UnwantedLanguage, json!({"why": "unwanted_language"})),
        (AudioDrop::Remembered, json!({"why": "remembered"})),
        (AudioDrop::Reviewed, json!({"why": "reviewed"})),
    ];
    for (reason, value) in cases {
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(&reason).unwrap(), value);
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_value::<AudioDrop>(value).unwrap(), reason);
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_record_without_the_derived_streams_aligns_without_derived() {
    let disc = pinned_disc(&corpus(&format!("{SMILE}.txt")));
    let title = &disc.titles[&14];
    let mut record = db_title(&pinned_record(SMILE), 14);
    let derived: Vec<u32> =
        title.streams.iter().filter(|stream| stream.flags.has(Flags::DERIVED)).map(|stream| stream.number).collect();
    record.tracks.retain(|track| !derived.contains(&track.index));
    assert_eq!(record.tracks.len(), 28);
    let (alignment, map) = align_descriptions(title, &record).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(alignment, Alignment::WithoutDerived);
    assert_eq!(map.len(), 28);
    assert_eq!(map.get(&1), Some(&1));
    assert_eq!(map.get(&2), None);
    assert_eq!(map.get(&3), Some(&3));
    assert_eq!(map.get(&10), Some(&10));
    assert_eq!(map.get(&12), None);
    assert_eq!(map.get(&45), Some(&45));
    let expected: BTreeMap<u32, u32> = title
        .streams
        .iter()
        .filter(|stream| !stream.flags.has(Flags::DERIVED))
        .map(|stream| (stream.number, stream.number))
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(map, expected);
    assert_eq!(
        descriptions(title, Some(&record)),
        (Some(Alignment::WithoutDerived), BTreeMap::from([(10, vec![DescriptionKind::Commentary])]))
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_record_of_another_length_or_with_one_track_different_aligns_neither_way() {
    let disc = pinned_disc(&corpus(&format!("{KNOWING}.txt")));
    let feature = &disc.titles[&0];
    let record = db_title(&pinned_record(KNOWING), 0);
    // Title 3 (a featurette) has 4 streams against the record's 8 tracks.
    assert_eq!(disc.titles[&3].streams.len(), 4);
    assert_eq!(align_descriptions(&disc.titles[&3], &record), None);
    assert_eq!(descriptions(&disc.titles[&3], Some(&record)), (None, BTreeMap::new()));
    // The Spanish 5.1 track (index 2) named stereo: the channels differ.
    let mut stereo = record.clone();
    stereo.tracks.iter_mut().find(|track| track.index == 2).unwrap().audio_type = Some("Stereo".to_string());
    assert_eq!(align_descriptions(feature, &stereo), None);
    // The English 5.1 track (index 1) tagged French: the languages differ.
    let mut french = record.clone();
    french.tracks.iter_mut().find(|track| track.index == 1).unwrap().language_code = Some("fra".to_string());
    assert_eq!(align_descriptions(feature, &french), None);
    // The video track (index 0) named another codec: attribute 7 differs.
    let mut codec_name = record.clone();
    codec_name.tracks.iter_mut().find(|track| track.index == 0).unwrap().name = Some("Mpeg4".to_string());
    assert_eq!(align_descriptions(feature, &codec_name), None);
    assert_eq!(descriptions(feature, Some(&codec_name)), (None, BTreeMap::new()));
}
```

```rust
/// Facts the file phase measured for one title, keyed by SCAN stream number (the dev crate and phase 2 map file tracks
/// back through verify::stream_of_track). At planning time it is `AudioFacts::default()`: no MD5, no profile, no
/// verdict. Spec 8.6, 6.4 steps 9 and 10a. Def: T8. Use: T13, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct AudioFacts<'a> {
    /// 6.4 step 10a: the packet MD5 of every audio stream (D13). Empty at planning time.
    pub md5: BTreeMap<u32, String>,
    /// 6.4 step 9: ffprobe's profile per audio stream ("DTS-HD MA", "DTS-HD MA + DTS:X"; the Atmos spelling is
    /// unverified). Empty at planning time (8.3: the ffprobe criterion is skipped).
    pub ffprobe_profile: BTreeMap<u32, String>,

    pub discdb: Option<&'a DiscDbTitle>,

    /// scan streams).
    pub verdicts: BTreeMap<u32, Verdict>,
    /// Whether D21's veto held for the title.

    /// The scan stream the verdicts were measured against: the level folder's `main=` stream
    /// (audio::reference::programme_reference in phase 0's harness) mapped to a scan stream; None when there are no
    /// verdicts.
    pub verdict_reference: Option<u32>,
    /// The remembered overrides for this fingerprint (spec 5).
    pub remembered: Option<&'a [AudioOverrideEntry]>,
    /// The owner's Override tracks for this title (spec 11), by scan stream; they win over remembered ones.
    pub reviewed: Option<&'a BTreeMap<u32, AudioOverride>>,
}

/// Why an audio stream was dropped, in spec 8.6 step 1's bullet order (D13, RP7, spec 5 and 11 overrides); written
/// with its reason under "why" (`{"why": "flagged", "flags": 1}`). Def: T8. Use: T13, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "why")]
pub enum AudioDrop {
    /// Flag 2048: a stream MakeMKV derived from another (the AC-3 or DTS core of a lossless track).
    Derived,
    /// Flags 1, 2 or 4 (director's comments, alternate director's comments, visually impaired); `flags` holds the
    /// ones of the three that are set.
    Flagged {
        /// The set bits among 1, 2 and 4.
        flags: u32,
    },
    /// Flag 512: secondary (picture-in-picture) audio.
    Secondary,
    /// D13: the same packet MD5 as the earlier stream `of`, the copy that is kept.
    Duplicate {
        /// The scan stream kept.
        of: u32,
    },
    /// TheDiscDB describes it as a commentary, an audio description, an isolated score or a music-and-effects track
    /// (8.1, D14), its track list aligning uniquely.
    Described {
        /// The first of those kinds the description names.
        kind: DescriptionKind,
    },
    /// A language that is not wanted (R4).
    UnwantedLanguage,
    /// A remembered decision drops it or marks it as commentary (spec 5).
    Remembered,
    /// The owner's Override tracks drops it or marks it as commentary (spec 11).
    Reviewed,
}

/// Which language group a kept track belongs to (8.6 step 5's order); the derived order is Original, English,
/// NoLanguage. Def: T8. Use: T11, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum LangGroup {
    /// The work's original language when it is not English (R4).
    Original,
    /// English (attribute 3 "eng" or "en").
    English,
    /// No language code, or a code that names none ("und"): kept and placed last (8.6 "Languages", step 5).
    NoLanguage,
}

impl LangGroup {
    /// Every group, in the derived order. Spec 8.6 step 5.
    pub const ALL: [LangGroup; 3] = [LangGroup::Original, LangGroup::English, LangGroup::NoLanguage];

    /// "original", "english" or "no_language", the string serde writes. Spec 8.6 step 5.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            LangGroup::Original => "original",
            LangGroup::English => "english",
            LangGroup::NoLanguage => "no_language",
        }
    }
}

impl FromStr for LangGroup {
    type Err = String;

    /// Only the `as_str` spellings; otherwise Err `"<text>" is not a language group (spec 8.6 step 5)`.
    fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<LangGroup, String> {
        LangGroup::ALL
            .into_iter()
            .find(|group| group.as_str() == text)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("\"{text}\" is not a language group (spec 8.6 step 5)"))
    }
}

/// A kept audio track with everything 8.6 and 8.10 need. Def: T8. Use: T11, T13, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct AudioTrack {
    /// The scan stream number.
    pub stream: u32,
    /// Attribute 3 lower-cased (None when absent).
    pub language: Option<String>,
    /// The language group (8.6 step 5).
    pub group: LangGroup,
    /// `codec::codec` of attributes 5, 6 and 7.
    pub codec: Codec,
    /// Attribute 14 (0 when absent).
    pub channels: u32,
    /// `codec::tier` of the family and the bit rate (8.6 step 3.2); None for an unknown codec.
    pub tier: Option<Tier>,
    /// From ffprobe's profile, else the scan's attribute 7.
    pub object: Option<ObjectAudio>,
    /// Attribute 18, the bit depth.
    pub sample_size: Option<u32>,
    /// Attribute 17, the sample rate.
    pub sample_rate: Option<u32>,
    /// `codec::bitrate_kbps` of attribute 13.
    pub bitrate_kbps: Option<u32>,
    /// Lowest disc position among the language's surviving streams (8.6 "Position": computed after step 1's drops).
    pub first_of_language: bool,
    /// 8.10: "<display> [Atmos|DTS:X] <layout>", for example "TrueHD Atmos 7.1".
    pub name: String,
    /// The default flag (8.6 step 5: the very first track).
    pub default: bool,
    /// The original flag (8.6 step 5: the original-language tracks; for an English work the English ones).
    pub original: bool,
}

/// Track confidence for audio (8.6: "0.95, because nothing is dropped on a guess"). Def: T8. Use: T13.
pub const AUDIO_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.95;
/// Guard G1's line (8.6 step 4): a lossy track at this rate or less never comes before a lossless one (a fixed value of
/// spec 14). Def: T8. Use: T8.
pub const G1_MAX_KBPS: u32 = 256;

/// How TheDiscDB's track list aligned with the scan's streams (8.6 step 1). Def: T8. Use: T8, T10, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Alignment {
    /// Against the title's full stream list.
    Full,
    /// Against the list without derived streams (flag 2048).
    WithoutDerived,
}

impl Alignment {
    /// Both alignments, in the order step 1 tries them. Spec 8.6 step 1.
    pub const ALL: [Alignment; 2] = [Alignment::Full, Alignment::WithoutDerived];

    /// "full" or "without_derived", the string serde writes. Spec 8.6 step 1.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Alignment::Full => "full",
            Alignment::WithoutDerived => "without_derived",
        }
    }
}

impl FromStr for Alignment {
    type Err = String;

    /// Only the `as_str` spellings; otherwise Err `"<text>" is not an alignment (spec 8.6 step 1)`.
    fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<Alignment, String> {
        Alignment::ALL
            .into_iter()
            .find(|alignment| alignment.as_str() == text)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("\"{text}\" is not an alignment (spec 8.6 step 1)"))
    }
}

/// The audio decision of one title (spec 8.6, 6.4 step 11). Def: T8. Use: T11, T13, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct AudioDecision {
    /// In final order (8.6 step 5), flags set.
    pub kept: Vec<AudioTrack>,
    /// Every dropped audio stream with its reason, in scan order.
    pub dropped: Vec<(u32, AudioDrop)>,
    /// The programme reference (8.6 "Content"): the first original-language track of the rule's order, else the first
    /// English one; None when no original-language or English track is kept (no-language tracks are never the
    /// reference).
    pub reference: Option<u32>,
    /// `facts.verdict_reference`, copied so the document shows what the verdicts were measured against.
    pub verdict_reference: Option<u32>,
    /// The notes of 8.6 step 6, D9 and RP7, in the order raised.
    pub notes: Vec<Noted>,
    /// Sorted and unique (`review::sorted_unique`).
    pub reviews: Vec<ReviewReason>,
    /// AUDIO_CONFIDENCE, or 1.00 when every audio stream has a remembered or review override.
    pub confidence: f64,
    /// How TheDiscDB's track list aligned; None when it did not align uniquely (descriptions unused) or there is no
    /// record.
    pub description_alignment: Option<Alignment>,
}

/// A TheDiscDB track and a scan stream agree on kind, language (`norm_lang` of both; video compares none), codec
/// (attribute 7 against the track's `name`) and, for audio, channels.
fn same_track(track: &DiscDbTrack, stream: &Stream) -> bool {
    if track.kind() != Some(stream.kind) {
        return false;
    }
    if stream.kind != StreamKind::Video
        && norm_lang(track.language_code.as_deref()) != norm_lang(stream.language.as_deref())
    {
        return false;
    }
    if track.name.as_deref().unwrap_or("") != stream.codec_long {
        return false;
    }
    stream.kind != StreamKind::Audio || track.channels() == stream.channels
}

/// The track list aligns with the stream list completely: equal lengths and every pair the same track.
fn aligns(tracks: &[&DiscDbTrack], streams: &[&Stream]) -> bool {
    tracks.len() == streams.len() && tracks.iter().zip(streams).all(|(track, stream)| same_track(track, stream))
}

/// Scan stream number to TheDiscDB track index, pair by pair.
fn pairs(tracks: &[&DiscDbTrack], streams: &[&Stream]) -> BTreeMap<u32, u32> {
    streams.iter().zip(tracks).map(|(stream, track)| (stream.number, track.index)).collect()
}

/// Spec 8.6 step 1: TheDiscDB's whole track list (every kind, index order) against the title's whole stream list (scan
/// order), pairwise on kind (`DiscDbTrack::kind`), language (`norm_lang` of `language_code` against `norm_lang` of
/// attribute 3; video compares no language), codec as attribute 7 (`Stream.codec_long == DiscDbTrack.name`) and
/// channels (`DiscDbTrack::channels` against attribute 14, audio only); tried on all streams and on the streams without
/// flag 2048; Some only when exactly one of the two aligns completely. A title without derived streams has one list,
/// tried once (`Full` when it aligns); an empty track list never aligns. The map is scan stream number to TheDiscDB
/// track index. Def: T8. Use: T8.
pub fn align_descriptions(title: &Title, discdb: &DiscDbTitle) -> Option<(Alignment, BTreeMap<u32, u32>)> {
    let mut tracks: Vec<&DiscDbTrack> = discdb.tracks.iter().collect();
    tracks.sort_by_key(|track| track.index);
    if tracks.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let full: Vec<&Stream> = title.streams.iter().collect();
    let without: Vec<&Stream> = title.streams.iter().filter(|stream| !stream.flags.has(Flags::DERIVED)).collect();
    let full_aligns = aligns(&tracks, &full);
    if without.len() == full.len() {
        return full_aligns.then(|| (Alignment::Full, pairs(&tracks, &full)));
    }
    match (full_aligns, aligns(&tracks, &without)) {
        (true, false) => Some((Alignment::Full, pairs(&tracks, &full))),
        (false, true) => Some((Alignment::WithoutDerived, pairs(&tracks, &without))),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Every scan stream (any kind) whose aligned TheDiscDB track has a description that is not blank, to
/// `lookup::description_kinds(description, track.language)` (possibly empty); with the alignment used. Empty and None
/// without a record or without a unique alignment. Spec 8.6 step 1, 8.1 last bullet, D14. Def: T8. Use: T8, T9, T10.
pub fn descriptions(title: &Title, discdb: Option<&DiscDbTitle>) -> (Option<Alignment>, BTreeMap<u32, Vec<DescriptionKind>>) {
    let Some(record) = discdb else {
        return (None, BTreeMap::new());
    };
    let Some((alignment, paired)) = align_descriptions(title, record) else {
        return (None, BTreeMap::new());
    };
    let mut described = BTreeMap::new();
    for (stream, index) in paired {
        let Some(track) = record.tracks.iter().find(|track| track.index == index) else {
            continue;
        };
        if let Some(text) = track.description.as_deref().filter(|text| !text.trim().is_empty()) {
            described.insert(stream, description_kinds(text, track.language.as_deref()));
        }
    }
    (Some(alignment), described)
}
```

```rust
/// MakeMKV's attributes 5, 6 and 7 of the codecs the rank and guard tests use.
const AC3: (&str, &str, &str) = ("A_AC3", "DD", "Dolby Digital");
const TRUEHD: (&str, &str, &str) = ("A_TRUEHD", "TrueHD", "TrueHD");
const LPCM: (&str, &str, &str) = ("A_LPCM", "LPCM", "LPCM");
const AAC: (&str, &str, &str) = ("A_AAC", "AAC", "AAC");
/// A codec the table does not know (Family::Unknown, no tier).
const OPUS: (&str, &str, &str) = ("A_OPUS", "Opus", "Opus");

/// A kept English track at 48000 Hz for the rank and guard tests, its tier from the codec and the bit rate.
fn ranked(
    stream: u32,
    attrs: (&str, &str, &str),
    channels: u32,
    bitrate_kbps: Option<u32>,
    sample_size: Option<u32>,
    first_of_language: bool,
) -> AudioTrack {
    let codec = codec(attrs.0, attrs.1, attrs.2);
    let tier_of = tier(codec.family, bitrate_kbps);
    AudioTrack {
        stream,
        language: Some("eng".to_string()),
        group: LangGroup::English,
        codec,
        channels,
        tier: tier_of,
        object: None,
        sample_size,
        sample_rate: Some(48000),
        bitrate_kbps,
        first_of_language,
        name: String::new(),
        default: false,
        original: true,
    }
}

/// The stream numbers of tracks, in order.
fn streams_of(tracks: &[AudioTrack]) -> Vec<u32> {
    tracks.iter().map(|track| track.stream).collect()
}
```

```rust
/// Spec 8.6 step 3's criteria of one track as sort components; a smaller value sorts first.
struct Criteria {
    /// 3.1: more channels first.
    channels: i64,
    /// 3.2: the tier's rank (`tier_rank`).
    tier: i64,
    /// 3.3: an object-based extension first.
    object: i64,
    /// 3.4: the deeper, then the faster sampled track first (unknown sorts last).
    sample_size: i64,
    sample_rate: i64,
    /// 3.5: the higher bit rate first, lossy tracks only (0 for every lossless track; 1, after every rate, for a
    /// lossy track without bit rate text).
    bitrate: i64,
    /// 3.6: the earlier disc position first.
    position: i64,
}

/// The criteria of `track`.
fn criteria(track: &AudioTrack) -> Criteria {
    Criteria {
        channels: -i64::from(track.channels),
        tier: tier_rank(track.tier),
        object: if track.object.is_some() { 0 } else { 1 },
        sample_size: -i64::from(track.sample_size.unwrap_or(0)),
        sample_rate: -i64::from(track.sample_rate.unwrap_or(0)),
        bitrate: if track.codec.lossless {
            0
        } else {
            match track.bitrate_kbps {
                Some(kbps) => -i64::from(kbps),
                None => 1,
            }
        },
        position: i64::from(track.stream),
    }
}

/// Lossless 0, high-rate lossy 1, other lossy 2, low 3; an unknown tier 4, after low (spec 8.6 step 3.2).
fn tier_rank(tier: Option<Tier>) -> i64 {
    match tier {
        Some(Tier::Lossless) => 0,
        Some(Tier::HighRateLossy) => 1,
        Some(Tier::OtherLossy) => 2,
        Some(Tier::Low) => 3,
        None => 4,
    }
}

/// 8.6 step 3's sort key (ascending): (channels descending, tier, object descending, sample size descending, sample rate
/// descending, bitrate descending for lossy only, disc position); with settings.prefer_most_channels off, tier comes before
/// channels. An unknown tier sorts after Low; a lossy track without bitrate text sorts after every lossy track with one.
/// Reads `prefer_most_channels` (D9). The product's copy beside audio::reference::rank (Global Constraints). Def: T8.
/// Use: T8.
pub fn rank_key(track: &AudioTrack, settings: &Settings) -> (i64, i64, i64, i64, i64, i64, i64) {
    let c = criteria(track);
    if settings.prefer_most_channels {
        (c.channels, c.tier, c.object, c.sample_size, c.sample_rate, c.bitrate, c.position)
    } else {
        (c.tier, c.channels, c.object, c.sample_size, c.sample_rate, c.bitrate, c.position)
    }
}

/// G1's weak track: lossy at G1_MAX_KBPS or less, or without a bit rate.
fn g1_weak(track: &AudioTrack) -> bool {
    !track.codec.lossless
        && match track.bitrate_kbps {
            Some(kbps) => kbps <= G1_MAX_KBPS,
            None => true,
        }
}

/// G1: every weak track ranked before the last lossless track moves to just after it; the order within the moved
/// tracks and within the others is kept.
fn g1(ranked: Vec<AudioTrack>) -> Vec<AudioTrack> {
    let Some(last_lossless) = ranked.iter().rposition(|track| track.codec.lossless) else {
        return ranked;
    };
    let mut front = Vec::new();
    let mut moved = Vec::new();
    let mut back = Vec::new();
    for (index, track) in ranked.into_iter().enumerate() {
        if index < last_lossless && g1_weak(&track) {
            moved.push(track);
        } else if index <= last_lossless {
            front.push(track);
        } else {
            back.push(track);
        }
    }
    front.extend(moved);
    front.extend(back);
    front
}

/// G2: a lossy top track with two channels or fewer that is not the first of its language and beats the first track
/// on channel count but on none of criteria 2 to 5 (tier, object, depth and rate, bit rate) gives way to it. Bit rate
/// counts only when the first track is lossy too: 3.5 ranks lossy tracks only, and `criteria` gives every lossless
/// track 0, which any lossy rate would beat. The top track is already known to be lossy.
fn g2(mut tracks: Vec<AudioTrack>) -> Vec<AudioTrack> {
    let applies = match tracks.first() {
        Some(top) => !top.codec.lossless && top.channels <= 2 && !top.first_of_language,
        None => false,
    };
    if !applies {
        return tracks;
    }
    let Some(first) = tracks.iter().position(|track| track.first_of_language) else {
        return tracks;
    };
    let (a, b) = (criteria(&tracks[0]), criteria(&tracks[first]));
    let later = a.tier < b.tier
        || a.object < b.object
        || a.sample_size < b.sample_size
        || a.sample_rate < b.sample_rate
        || (!tracks[first].codec.lossless && a.bitrate < b.bitrate);
    if a.channels < b.channels && !later {
        let track = tracks.remove(first);
        tracks.insert(0, track);
    }
    tracks
}

/// G1: a lossy track at G1_MAX_KBPS or less (or with no bitrate) never before a lossless track of the same language. G2: a
/// lossy top track with <= 2 channels that is not first of its language and beats the first on channel count but on no later
/// criterion gives way to the first. Returns the language's tracks reordered. `ranked` is one language's tracks in rank
/// order with `first_of_language` set; G1 applies before G2. The guards apply whatever the D9 setting says (spec 8.6 step
/// 4), so no setting is read. Def: T8. Use: T8.
pub fn guards(ranked: Vec<AudioTrack>, _settings: &Settings) -> Vec<AudioTrack> {
    g2(g1(ranked))
}
```

```rust
/// `attrs` with one more attribute, which overrides an earlier one with the same id.
fn with(mut attrs: Attrs, id: u32, value: &'static str) -> Attrs {
    attrs.push((id, value));
    attrs
}

/// A TrueHD stream, 24-bit.
fn truehd(language: &'static str, channels: &'static str) -> Attrs {
    with(audio(language, "A_TRUEHD", "TrueHD", "TrueHD", channels, ""), 18, "24")
}

/// A DTS-HD Master Audio stream, 24-bit.
fn dts_hd_ma(language: &'static str, channels: &'static str) -> Attrs {
    with(audio(language, "A_DTS", "DTS-HD MA", "DTS-HD Master Audio", channels, ""), 18, "24")
}

/// A DTS stream.
fn dts(language: &'static str, channels: &'static str, bitrate: &'static str) -> Attrs {
    audio(language, "A_DTS", "DTS", "DTS", channels, bitrate)
}

/// An E-AC-3 stream, with MakeMKV's documented short name (not yet seen in a recording).
fn eac3(language: &'static str, channels: &'static str, bitrate: &'static str) -> Attrs {
    audio(language, "A_EAC3", "E-AC3", "Dolby Digital Plus", channels, bitrate)
}

/// An LPCM stream of this bit depth and sample rate.
fn lpcm(language: &'static str, channels: &'static str, depth: &'static str, rate: &'static str) -> Attrs {
    with(with(audio(language, "A_LPCM", "LPCM", "LPCM", channels, ""), 17, rate), 18, depth)
}

/// The decision with no facts (planning time) and the default settings, for a work whose TMDb original language is
/// `original`.
fn decide(title: &Title, original: Option<&str>) -> AudioDecision {
    decide_audio(title, &wanted_languages(original), &AudioFacts::default(), &Settings::default())
}

/// The kept streams, in final order.
fn order_of(decision: &AudioDecision) -> Vec<u32> {
    decision.kept.iter().map(|track| track.stream).collect()
}

/// The kept tracks' names, in final order.
fn names(decision: &AudioDecision) -> Vec<&str> {
    decision.kept.iter().map(|track| track.name.as_str()).collect()
}

/// The notes as (note, stream) pairs, in the order raised.
fn noted(decision: &AudioDecision) -> Vec<(Note, Option<u32>)> {
    decision.notes.iter().map(|noted| (noted.note, noted.stream)).collect()
}

/// The kept tracks' default flags, in final order.
fn defaults(decision: &AudioDecision) -> Vec<bool> {
    decision.kept.iter().map(|track| track.default).collect()
}

/// The kept tracks' original flags, in final order.
fn originals(decision: &AudioDecision) -> Vec<bool> {
    decision.kept.iter().map(|track| track.original).collect()
}

/// Knowing's feature (title 0) of a scan text.
fn knowing_feature(text: &str) -> Title {
    pinned_disc(text).titles[&0].clone()
}

/// The Office's title 1 (S03E15) as its scan lays it out: video, DTS-HD MA 5.1 (stream 1), its DTS core (2), a second
/// DTS-HD MA 5.1 (3), its core (4), PGS English (5) and the derived forced-only PGS (6).
fn office_title_1() -> Title {
    let hd_ma = with(with(dts_hd_ma("eng", "6"), 2, "Surround 5.1"), 22, "1024");
    let core = with(with(dts("eng", "6", "1.5 Mb/s"), 2, "Surround 5.1"), 22, "2304");
    let pgs: Attrs = vec![(1, "Subtitles"), (3, "eng"), (5, "S_HDMV/PGS"), (6, "PGS"), (7, "HDMV PGS Subtitles")];
    title_of(&[video(), hd_ma.clone(), core.clone(), hd_ma, core, pgs.clone(), with(pgs, 22, "6144")])
}

/// Made-up packet MD5s of `office_title_1`'s twins (D13 needs only that identical streams carry equal strings): streams 1
/// and 3 share one, their cores 2 and 4 another.
fn twin_md5() -> BTreeMap<u32, String> {
    BTreeMap::from([
        (1, "aaaa0000000000000000000000000001".to_string()),
        (2, "bbbb0000000000000000000000000002".to_string()),
        (3, "aaaa0000000000000000000000000001".to_string()),
        (4, "bbbb0000000000000000000000000002".to_string()),
    ])
}

        vec![Noted {
            note: Note::PossibleCommentary,
            stream: Some(10),
            detail: "stream 10 (Dolby Digital 2.0) is lossy with two channels or fewer and is not the first eng stream on the disc"
                .to_string(),
        }]
    );
    let mut dropped = vec![(2, AudioDrop::Derived)];
    dropped.extend((4..=9).map(|stream| (stream, AudioDrop::UnwantedLanguage)));
    assert_eq!(decision.dropped, dropped);
    assert_eq!(decision.description_alignment, None);
    assert_eq!(decision.reviews, Vec::new());
}

#[test]
fn every_flag_of_step_1_drops_its_stream() {
    let stereo = || dd("eng", "2", "192 Kb/s");
    let title = title_of(&[
        video(),
        dd("eng", "6", "640 Kb/s"),
        with(stereo(), 22, "2"),
        with(stereo(), 22, "4"),
        with(stereo(), 22, "5"),
        with(stereo(), 22, "512"),
        with(dts("eng", "6", "1.5 Mb/s"), 22, "2304"),
        with(stereo(), 22, "2049"),
        with(stereo(), 22, "65536"),
    ]);
    let decision = decide(&title, Some("en"));
    assert_eq!(
        decision.dropped,
        vec![
            (2, AudioDrop::Flagged { flags: 2 }),
            (3, AudioDrop::Flagged { flags: 4 }),
            (4, AudioDrop::Flagged { flags: 5 }),
            (5, AudioDrop::Secondary),
            (6, AudioDrop::Derived),
            (7, AudioDrop::Derived),
        ]
    );
    // 65536 is a bit spec 9.5 does not name: ignored, so stream 8 is kept.
    assert_eq!(order_of(&decision), vec![1, 8]);
    assert_eq!(noted(&decision), vec![(Note::PossibleCommentary, Some(8))]);
}

#[test]
fn an_exact_duplicate_by_md5_is_dropped_and_the_first_copy_kept() {
    let title = office_title_1();
    let facts = AudioFacts { md5: twin_md5(), ..AudioFacts::default() };
    let decision = decide_audio(&title, &wanted_languages(Some("en")), &facts, &Settings::default());
    assert_eq!(
        decision,
        AudioDecision {
            kept: vec![AudioTrack {
                stream: 1,
                language: Some("eng".to_string()),
                group: LangGroup::English,
                codec: codec("A_DTS", "DTS-HD MA", "DTS-HD Master Audio"),
                channels: 6,
                tier: Some(Tier::Lossless),
                object: None,
                sample_size: Some(24),
                sample_rate: Some(48000),
                bitrate_kbps: None,
                first_of_language: true,
                name: "DTS-HD MA 5.1".to_string(),
                default: true,
                original: true,
            }],
            dropped: vec![(2, AudioDrop::Derived), (3, AudioDrop::Duplicate { of: 1 }), (4, AudioDrop::Derived)],
            reference: Some(1),
            verdict_reference: None,
            notes: Vec::new(),
            reviews: Vec::new(),
            confidence: 0.95,
            description_alignment: None,
        }
    );
    // At planning time no MD5 is known: both lossless copies are kept.
    let planned = decide(&title, Some("en"));
    assert_eq!(order_of(&planned), vec![1, 3]);
    assert_eq!(planned.dropped, vec![(2, AudioDrop::Derived), (4, AudioDrop::Derived)]);
    assert_eq!(planned.notes, Vec::new());
}

#[test]
fn the_copy_of_a_stream_dropped_for_its_language_is_kept_so_one_copy_survives() {

        ..AudioFacts::default()
    };
    let decision = decide_audio(&title, &wanted_languages(Some("en")), &facts, &Settings::default());

}

#[test]
fn thediscdb_descriptions_drop_audio_description_isolated_score_and_music_and_effects_and_keep_the_rest() {
    let stereo = || dd("eng", "2", "192 Kb/s");
    let title = title_of(&[video(), dd("eng", "6", "640 Kb/s"), stereo(), stereo(), stereo(), stereo()]);
    let track = |index: u32, audio_type: &str, description: &str| {
        json!({"index": index, "type": "Audio", "name": "Dolby Digital", "audio_type": audio_type,
               "language_code": "eng", "language": "English", "description": description})
    };
    let record: DiscDbTitle = serde_json::from_value(json!({
        "index": 0,
        "tracks": [
            {"index": 0, "type": "Video", "name": "Mpeg4 AVC High@L4.1"},
            track(1, "Surround 5.1", "English"),
            track(2, "Stereo", "Descriptive Audio"),
            track(3, "Stereo", "Isolated Score"),
            track(4, "Stereo", "Music and Effects"),
            track(5, "Stereo", "Stereo Mix")
        ]
    }))
    .unwrap();
    let facts = AudioFacts { discdb: Some(&record), ..AudioFacts::default() };
    let decision = decide_audio(&title, &wanted_languages(Some("en")), &facts, &Settings::default());
    assert_eq!(
        decision.dropped,
        vec![
            (2, AudioDrop::Described { kind: DescriptionKind::AudioDescription }),
            (3, AudioDrop::Described { kind: DescriptionKind::IsolatedScore }),
            (4, AudioDrop::Described { kind: DescriptionKind::MusicAndEffects }),
        ]
    );
    // "English" is a dialogue description and "Stereo Mix" names no kind: both kept.
    assert_eq!(order_of(&decision), vec![1, 5]);
    assert_eq!(noted(&decision), vec![(Note::PossibleCommentary, Some(5))]);
    assert_eq!(decision.description_alignment, Some(Alignment::Full));
}

#[test]
fn a_stream_in_an_unwanted_language_is_dropped_and_streams_without_one_are_kept_last() {
    let title = title_of(&[
        video(),
        dd("fra", "6", "640 Kb/s"),
        dd("und", "2", "192 Kb/s"),
        dd("eng", "2", "192 Kb/s"),
        dd("", "6", "640 Kb/s"),
    ]);
    let decision = decide(&title, Some("en"));
    assert_eq!(decision.dropped, vec![(1, AudioDrop::UnwantedLanguage)]);
    assert_eq!(order_of(&decision), vec![3, 4, 2]);
    let groups: Vec<LangGroup> = decision.kept.iter().map(|track| track.group).collect();
    assert_eq!(groups, vec![LangGroup::English, LangGroup::NoLanguage, LangGroup::NoLanguage]);
    let languages: Vec<Option<&str>> = decision.kept.iter().map(|track| track.language.as_deref()).collect();
    assert_eq!(languages, vec![Some("eng"), None, Some("und")]);
    let firsts: Vec<bool> = decision.kept.iter().map(|track| track.first_of_language).collect();
    assert_eq!(firsts, vec![true, false, true]);
    assert_eq!(defaults(&decision), vec![true, false, false]);
    assert_eq!(originals(&decision), vec![true, false, false]);
    assert_eq!(decision.reference, Some(3));
    assert_eq!(decision.notes, Vec::new());
    assert_eq!(decision.reviews, Vec::new());
}

#[test]
fn an_object_based_track_ranks_first_when_ffprobe_reports_it_and_not_at_planning_time() {
    let title = title_of(&[
        video(),
        truehd("eng", "8"),
        with(audio("eng", "A_TRUEHD", "TrueHD", "TrueHD Atmos", "8", ""), 18, "24"),
    ]);
    let planned = decide(&title, Some("en"));
    assert_eq!(order_of(&planned), vec![1, 2]);
    assert_eq!(names(&planned), vec!["TrueHD 7.1", "TrueHD Atmos 7.1"]);
    assert_eq!(planned.kept[1].object, Some(ObjectAudio::Atmos));
    let probed = AudioFacts {
        ffprobe_profile: BTreeMap::from([(1, "TrueHD".to_string()), (2, "Dolby TrueHD + Dolby Atmos".to_string())]),
        ..AudioFacts::default()
    };
    let decision = decide_audio(&title, &wanted_languages(Some("en")), &probed, &Settings::default());
    assert_eq!(order_of(&decision), vec![2, 1]);
    assert_eq!(names(&decision), vec!["TrueHD Atmos 7.1", "TrueHD 7.1"]);
    // A profile that names no extension does not rank the track first (3.3 reads ffprobe only), but its name and
    // object still take attribute 7's Atmos: the profile spellings are unverified (EXP-06).
    let plain = AudioFacts {
        ffprobe_profile: BTreeMap::from([(1, "TrueHD".to_string()), (2, "TrueHD".to_string())]),
        ..AudioFacts::default()
    };
    let decision = decide_audio(&title, &wanted_languages(Some("en")), &plain, &Settings::default());
    assert_eq!(order_of(&decision), vec![1, 2]);
    assert_eq!(names(&decision), vec!["TrueHD 7.1", "TrueHD Atmos 7.1"]);
    assert_eq!(decision.kept[1].object, Some(ObjectAudio::Atmos));
}
```

```rust
/// The flags of 8.6 step 1's second bullet: director's comments, alternate director's comments, visually impaired.
const COMMENTARY_FLAGS: u32 = Flags::DIRECTORS_COMMENTS | Flags::ALT_DIRECTORS_COMMENTS | Flags::VISUALLY_IMPAIRED;

/// The described kinds 8.6 step 1 drops (R6, D14); every other described track is kept.
const DROPPED_DESCRIPTIONS: [DescriptionKind; 4] = [
    DescriptionKind::Commentary,
    DescriptionKind::AudioDescription,
    DescriptionKind::IsolatedScore,
    DescriptionKind::MusicAndEffects,
];

/// Spec 8.6 steps 1 to 6 and "Content" (RP7), in order: drop (derived 2048; flags 1, 2, 4; secondary 512; duplicates by
/// equal MD5, one copy kept: `Duplicate { of }` names the first earlier stream with that MD5 that was kept; described
/// Commentary, AudioDescription, IsolatedScore or MusicAndEffects through `descriptions` when the alignment is unique;
/// unwanted language; a remembered or review Drop or Commentary); keep the rest and any no-language stream; rank with
/// `rank_key`; guards G1 and G2; order by language (original first when settings.original_language_first and the
/// original is not English, else English first; no language last), default on the very first track, original flag on
/// the original-language tracks (the English ones for an English work); notes possible_commentary,
/// lossless_original_available, no_english_audio, lossy_before_lossless (D9); reviews original_language_missing,
/// no_wanted_audio; verdicts apply only when `facts.verdict_reference` and the decision's `reference` are both Some (a
/// title without a kept original-language or English track has nothing to judge, spec 8.6 "Content"): when they differ
/// (spec 15: evidence measured against another reference than the rule's own choice), or `facts.veto_holds` is true
/// (D21: the rule confirms no commentary on the title), only audio_reference_unclear is raised and no verdict is mapped;
/// otherwise, for the kept streams in a wanted language (Original or English group; no-language streams are not judged,
/// spec 8.6 "Content"), ReferenceUnclear adds audio_reference_unclear, Commentary and CommentaryCrossLanguage add
/// commentary_detected (nothing dropped, D15), AdPattern, NoteCommentary and NoteAd add notes; a remembered or review
/// Keep { order, default } fixes the order and the default. Confidence 0.95, or
/// lookup::REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE (1.00) when every audio stream of the title has a remembered or review override. At
/// planning time `facts` is empty and the ffprobe criterion is skipped (8.3). Reads the settings `prefer_most_channels`
/// and `original_language_first` (D9). Def: T8. Use: T13, T16.
pub fn decide_audio(title: &Title, wanted: &Wanted, facts: &AudioFacts<'_>, settings: &Settings) -> AudioDecision {
    let audio = title.streams_of(StreamKind::Audio);
    let (description_alignment, described) = descriptions(title, facts.discdb);
    let mut dropped = Vec::new();
    let mut kept_streams: Vec<&Stream> = Vec::new();
    let mut packets: Vec<(u32, String)> = Vec::new();
    for stream in &audio {
        match rule_drop(stream, wanted, facts, &described, &packets) {
            Some(why) => dropped.push((stream.number, why)),
            None => {
                if let Some(md5) = facts.md5.get(&stream.number) {
                    packets.push((stream.number, md5.clone()));
                }
                kept_streams.push(*stream);
            }
        }
    }
    let tracks: Vec<AudioTrack> = kept_streams.iter().map(|stream| track_of(stream, wanted, facts)).collect();
    let ordered = rank_and_order(tracks, wanted, settings);
    let reference = reference_of(&ordered);
    let kept = finish(ordered, wanted);
    let notes = notes_of(&kept);
    let reviews = gaps(&kept, wanted);
    AudioDecision {
        kept,
        dropped,
        reference,
        verdict_reference: facts.verdict_reference,
        notes,
        reviews: sorted_unique(reviews),
        confidence: AUDIO_CONFIDENCE,
        description_alignment,
    }
}

/// Step 1's reason to drop `stream`, or None: the bullets in the spec's order, the first that holds naming the reason.
/// `packets` holds the MD5 of every earlier stream that was kept (`decide_audio` adds a stream's MD5 only once the stream
/// is kept), so a duplicate names a kept copy and one copy always survives (D13).
fn rule_drop(
    stream: &Stream,
    wanted: &Wanted,
    facts: &AudioFacts<'_>,
    described: &BTreeMap<u32, Vec<DescriptionKind>>,
    packets: &[(u32, String)],
) -> Option<AudioDrop> {
    if stream.flags.has(Flags::DERIVED) {
        return Some(AudioDrop::Derived);
    }
    if stream.flags.commentary() {
        return Some(AudioDrop::Flagged { flags: stream.flags.0 & COMMENTARY_FLAGS });
    }
    if stream.flags.has(Flags::SECONDARY_AUDIO) {
        return Some(AudioDrop::Secondary);
    }
    if let Some(md5) = facts.md5.get(&stream.number) {
        if let Some((of, _)) = packets.iter().find(|(_, seen)| seen == md5) {
            return Some(AudioDrop::Duplicate { of: *of });
        }
    }
    let kind = described
        .get(&stream.number)
        .and_then(|kinds| kinds.iter().copied().find(|kind| DROPPED_DESCRIPTIONS.contains(kind)));
    if let Some(kind) = kind {
        return Some(AudioDrop::Described { kind });
    }
    match stream.language.as_deref() {
        Some(code) if !is_no_language(Some(code)) && !wanted.contains(code) => Some(AudioDrop::UnwantedLanguage),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// The language group of a kept stream's attribute 3 (8.6 "Languages"): the original language's codes, English, or no
/// language (no code, a code naming none, or an unwanted code kept by an override).
fn group_of(language: Option<&str>, wanted: &Wanted) -> LangGroup {
    match language {
        Some(code) if !is_no_language(Some(code)) && wanted.is_original(code) => LangGroup::Original,
        Some(code) if !is_no_language(Some(code)) && is_english(code) => LangGroup::English,
        _ => LangGroup::NoLanguage,
    }
}

/// A kept stream as a track: its facts, its object from ffprobe's profile only (the ranking's 3.3), the flags and the
/// name filled by `finish`.
fn track_of(stream: &Stream, wanted: &Wanted, facts: &AudioFacts<'_>) -> AudioTrack {
    AudioTrack {
        stream: stream.number,
        language: stream.language.clone(),
        group: group_of(stream.language.as_deref(), wanted),
        codec: stream.codec.clone(),
        channels: stream.channels.unwrap_or(0),
        tier: tier(stream.codec.family, stream.bitrate_kbps),
        object: object_audio(facts.ffprobe_profile.get(&stream.number).map(String::as_str)),
        sample_size: stream.sample_size,
        sample_rate: stream.sample_rate,
        bitrate_kbps: stream.bitrate_kbps,
        first_of_language: false,
        name: String::new(),
        default: false,
        original: false,
    }
}

/// Spec 8.6 step 5's language order: the original language first when `original_language_first` is on and the work is
/// not English, else English first; no language last.
fn group_order(wanted: &Wanted, settings: &Settings) -> [LangGroup; 3] {
    if settings.original_language_first && !wanted.original_is_english {
        [LangGroup::Original, LangGroup::English, LangGroup::NoLanguage]
    } else {
        [LangGroup::English, LangGroup::Original, LangGroup::NoLanguage]
    }
}

/// Steps 3 to 5: per language in step 5's order, "first of its language" set (8.6 "Position"), ranked with `rank_key`,
/// then guarded.
fn rank_and_order(tracks: Vec<AudioTrack>, wanted: &Wanted, settings: &Settings) -> Vec<AudioTrack> {
    let mut ordered = Vec::with_capacity(tracks.len());
    for group in group_order(wanted, settings) {
        let mut members: Vec<AudioTrack> = tracks.iter().filter(|track| track.group == group).cloned().collect();
        let first = members.iter().map(|track| track.stream).min();
        for track in &mut members {
            track.first_of_language = Some(track.stream) == first;
        }
        members.sort_by_key(|track| rank_key(track, settings));
        ordered.extend(guards(members, settings));
    }
    ordered
}

/// The programme reference (8.6 "Content"): the first original-language track of the rule's order, else the first
/// English one; None when neither is kept.
fn reference_of(ordered: &[AudioTrack]) -> Option<u32> {
    ordered
        .iter()
        .find(|track| track.group == LangGroup::Original)
        .or_else(|| ordered.iter().find(|track| track.group == LangGroup::English))
        .map(|track| track.stream)
}

/// 8.10's audio name: the display name, the object-based extension, the channel layout (left out when the count is
/// unknown).
fn track_name(codec: &Codec, object: Option<ObjectAudio>, channels: u32) -> String {
    let mut name = codec.display.clone();
    if let Some(object) = object {
        name.push(' ');
        name.push_str(object.as_str());
    }
    if channels > 0 {
        name.push(' ');
        name.push_str(&channel_layout(channels));
    }
    name
}

/// Step 5's flags and 8.10's names on the final order: attribute 7's object for a track whose ffprobe profile names
/// none (no profile, or one without a known extension: the spellings are unverified, EXP-06), the name, the default flag
/// on the very first track, and the original flag on the original-language tracks, or on the English ones for an
/// English work (TMDb's code "en"). A work whose original language is unknown, "xx" or missing from the ISO 639 table
/// is not an English work and has no Original group, so none of its tracks gets the original flag (8.6 step 5).
fn finish(mut ordered: Vec<AudioTrack>, wanted: &Wanted) -> Vec<AudioTrack> {
    let english_work = wanted.original_two_letter.as_deref().is_some_and(is_english);
    for (position, track) in ordered.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        track.object = track.object.or(track.codec.object);
        track.name = track_name(&track.codec, track.object, track.channels);
        track.default = position == 0;
        track.original = if english_work {
            track.group == LangGroup::English
        } else {
            track.group == LangGroup::Original
        };
    }
    ordered
}

/// The language a note names: attribute 3, or "no-language".
fn language_word(track: &AudioTrack) -> &str {
    track.language.as_deref().filter(|code| !is_no_language(Some(*code))).unwrap_or("no-language")
}

/// The kept tracks of one group, in final order.
fn group_members(kept: &[AudioTrack], group: LangGroup) -> Vec<&AudioTrack> {
    kept.iter().filter(|track| track.group == group).collect()
}

/// Step 6's notes and D9's note on the final order, in the spec's bullet order.
fn notes_of(kept: &[AudioTrack]) -> Vec<Noted> {
    let mut notes = Vec::new();
    for track in kept {
        if !track.codec.lossless && track.channels <= 2 && !track.first_of_language {
            notes.push(Noted {
                note: Note::PossibleCommentary,
                stream: Some(track.stream),
                detail: format!(
                    "stream {} ({}) is lossy with two channels or fewer and is not the first {} stream on the disc",
                    track.stream,
                    track.name,
                    language_word(track)
                ),
            });
        }
    }
    let mut groups: Vec<LangGroup> = Vec::new();
    for track in kept {
        if !groups.contains(&track.group) {
            groups.push(track.group);
        }
    }
    for &group in &groups {
        let members = group_members(kept, group);
        let top = members[0];
        if top.codec.lossless {
            continue;
        }
        if let Some(lossless) = members.iter().find(|track| track.codec.lossless && track.channels < top.channels) {
            notes.push(Noted {
                note: Note::LosslessOriginalAvailable,
                stream: None,
                detail: format!(
                    "the first {} track, stream {} ({}), is lossy while stream {} ({}) is lossless with fewer channels",
                    language_word(top),
                    top.stream,
                    top.name,
                    lossless.stream,
                    lossless.name
                ),
            });
        }
    }
    let english = kept.iter().any(|track| track.group == LangGroup::English);
    let original = kept.iter().any(|track| track.group == LangGroup::Original);
    if !english && original {
        notes.push(Noted {
            note: Note::NoEnglishAudio,
            stream: None,
            detail: "no English audio stream is kept; the original-language audio is".to_string(),
        });
    }
    for &group in &groups {
        let members = group_members(kept, group);
        for (index, track) in members.iter().enumerate() {
            if track.codec.lossless {
                continue;
            }
            let later = members[index + 1..].iter().find(|other| other.codec.lossless && other.channels < track.channels);
            if let Some(lossless) = later {
                notes.push(Noted {
                    note: Note::LossyBeforeLossless,
                    stream: Some(track.stream),
                    detail: format!(
                        "stream {} ({}) is lossy and placed before the lossless stream {} ({}), which has fewer channels (D9)",
                        track.stream, track.name, lossless.stream, lossless.name
                    ),
                });
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    notes
}

/// Step 6's gaps, judged on the kept tracks: original_language_missing when the original language is wanted and no
/// kept track is in it; no_wanted_audio when nothing is kept.
fn gaps(kept: &[AudioTrack], wanted: &Wanted) -> Vec<ReviewReason> {
    let mut reviews = Vec::new();
    if !wanted.original_is_english && !kept.iter().any(|track| track.group == LangGroup::Original) {
        reviews.push(ReviewReason::OriginalLanguageMissing);
    }
    if kept.is_empty() {
        reviews.push(ReviewReason::NoWantedAudio);
    }
    reviews
}
```

```rust
/// The decision of `verdict_title` for an English work with these verdicts, measured against `reference`, and the veto.
fn with_verdicts(verdicts: &[(u32, Verdict)], reference: Option<u32>, veto_holds: bool) -> AudioDecision {
    let facts = AudioFacts {
        verdicts: verdicts.iter().copied().collect(),
        verdict_reference: reference,
        veto_holds,
        ..AudioFacts::default()
    };
    decide_audio(&verdict_title(), &wanted_languages(Some("en")), &facts, &Settings::default())
}
```

```rust
/// Adds `note` for `stream` unless a note of the same kind already names that stream.
fn push_note(notes: &mut Vec<Noted>, note: Note, stream: u32, detail: String) {
    if !notes.iter().any(|noted| noted.note == note && noted.stream == Some(stream)) {
        notes.push(Noted { note, stream: Some(stream), detail });
    }
}

/// Spec 8.6 "Content" with RP7's mapping. Nothing without a measured reference. Nothing when the decision has no
/// reference (no wanted-language track: nothing to judge, spec 8.6 Content). Verdicts measured against another stream
/// than the decision's `reference` are not applied and raise audio_reference_unclear (spec 15). When D21's veto holds the
/// rule confirms no commentary on the title: audio_reference_unclear and nothing else. Otherwise, for the kept streams
/// in a wanted language (Original or English group; no-language streams are not judged, spec 8.6 Content):
/// reference-unclear raises audio_reference_unclear; commentary and commentary-cross-language raise
/// commentary_detected and drop nothing (D15); ad-pattern and note-ad note possible_audio_description; note-commentary
/// notes possible_commentary; duplicate, keep and not-judged add nothing (D13's drop is by MD5).
fn apply_verdicts(
    facts: &AudioFacts<'_>,
    reference: Option<u32>,
    kept: &[AudioTrack],
    notes: &mut Vec<Noted>,
    reviews: &mut Vec<ReviewReason>,
) {
    let Some(measured) = facts.verdict_reference else {
        return;
    };
    let Some(reference) = reference else {
        return;
    };
    if reference != measured || facts.veto_holds {
        reviews.push(ReviewReason::AudioReferenceUnclear);
        return;
    }
    for (&stream, &verdict) in &facts.verdicts {
        if !kept.iter().any(|track| track.stream == stream && track.group != LangGroup::NoLanguage) {
            continue;
        }
        match verdict {
            Verdict::ReferenceUnclear => reviews.push(ReviewReason::AudioReferenceUnclear),
            Verdict::Commentary | Verdict::CommentaryCrossLanguage => reviews.push(ReviewReason::CommentaryDetected),
            Verdict::AdPattern => push_note(
                notes,
                Note::PossibleAudioDescription,
                stream,
                format!("the content rule found the audio-description pattern on stream {stream} (ad-pattern)"),
            ),
            Verdict::NoteAd => push_note(
                notes,
                Note::PossibleAudioDescription,
                stream,
                format!("the content rule notes a possible audio description on stream {stream} (note-ad)"),
            ),
            Verdict::NoteCommentary => push_note(
                notes,
                Note::PossibleCommentary,
                stream,
                format!("the content rule notes a possible commentary on stream {stream} (note-commentary)"),
            ),
            Verdict::Duplicate | Verdict::Keep | Verdict::NotJudged => {}
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
/// Where an audio override came from: a remembered decision (spec 5) or the owner's Override tracks (spec 11).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Source {
    Remembered,
    Reviewed,
}

/// Scan stream number to override for the title's audio streams: the remembered ones through
/// `remembered::apply_audio`, then the owner's, which win; an override naming a stream that is not audio is ignored.
fn overrides_of(title: &Title, facts: &AudioFacts<'_>) -> BTreeMap<u32, (AudioOverride, Source)> {
    let mut overrides = BTreeMap::new();
    if let Some(entries) = facts.remembered {
        for (stream, action) in apply_audio(entries, &title.streams) {
            overrides.insert(stream, (action.clone(), Source::Remembered));
        }
    }
    if let Some(reviewed) = facts.reviewed {
        let audio = title.streams_of(StreamKind::Audio);
        for (stream, action) in reviewed {
            if audio.iter().any(|candidate| candidate.number == *stream) {
                overrides.insert(*stream, (action.clone(), Source::Reviewed));
            }
        }
    }
    overrides
}

/// Step 1's outcome with the override: a Keep keeps the stream whatever step 1 says; otherwise step 1's reason stands;
/// a Drop or Commentary drops a stream step 1 keeps, labelled by where the override came from.
fn settle(rule: Option<AudioDrop>, action: Option<&(AudioOverride, Source)>) -> Option<AudioDrop> {
    match (rule, action) {
        (_, Some((AudioOverride::Keep { .. }, _))) => None,
        (Some(why), _) => Some(why),
        (None, Some((AudioOverride::Drop | AudioOverride::Commentary, Source::Remembered))) => Some(AudioDrop::Remembered),
        (None, Some((AudioOverride::Drop | AudioOverride::Commentary, Source::Reviewed))) => Some(AudioDrop::Reviewed),
        (None, None) => None,
    }
}

/// Spec 11's Keep orders (0 first): the overridden tracks in (order, rule position) order each take the first free
/// position at or after their order; the other tracks fill the remaining positions in the rule's order.
fn keep_orders(ordered: Vec<AudioTrack>, overrides: &BTreeMap<u32, (AudioOverride, Source)>) -> Vec<AudioTrack> {
    let total = ordered.len();
    let mut pinned: Vec<(u32, usize, AudioTrack)> = Vec::new();
    let mut free: Vec<AudioTrack> = Vec::new();
    for (index, track) in ordered.into_iter().enumerate() {
        match overrides.get(&track.stream) {
            Some((AudioOverride::Keep { order, .. }, _)) => pinned.push((*order, index, track)),
            _ => free.push(track),
        }
    }
    pinned.sort_by_key(|(order, index, _)| (*order, *index));
    let mut pinned = pinned.into_iter().peekable();
    let mut free = free.into_iter();
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(total);
    while out.len() < total {
        let position = u32::try_from(out.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
        let due = pinned.peek().is_some_and(|(order, _, _)| *order <= position);
        let next = if due {
            pinned.next().map(|(_, _, track)| track)
        } else {
            free.next().or_else(|| pinned.next().map(|(_, _, track)| track))
        };
        match next {
            Some(track) => out.push(track),
            None => break,
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Spec 11's Keep default: when an override says `default: true`, the first such track in final order is the default
/// and no other; otherwise step 5's default (the very first track) stands.
fn override_defaults(kept: &mut [AudioTrack], overrides: &BTreeMap<u32, (AudioOverride, Source)>) {
    let chosen = kept
        .iter()
        .map(|track| track.stream)
        .find(|stream| matches!(overrides.get(stream), Some((AudioOverride::Keep { default: true, .. }, _))));
    if let Some(chosen) = chosen {
        for track in kept.iter_mut() {
            track.default = track.stream == chosen;
        }
    }
}

/// Spec 8.6's 0.95, or 1.00 (8.8: a review decision sets the confidence it covers) when the title has audio and every
/// audio stream has a remembered or review override.
fn confidence_of(audio: &[&Stream], overrides: &BTreeMap<u32, (AudioOverride, Source)>) -> f64 {
    if !audio.is_empty() && audio.iter().all(|stream| overrides.contains_key(&stream.number)) {
        REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE
    } else {
        AUDIO_CONFIDENCE
    }
}
```

```rust
/// Facts for one title's subtitle streams, keyed by SCAN stream number. Def: T9. Use: T10, T13, T16, T18.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct SubtitleFacts<'a> {
    /// 6.4 step 10: event start times per stream (align::events with settings.sub_clear_max_bytes for image streams, 0 for text streams). A stream absent here has no evidence (step 10 skipped: one English stream).
    pub events: BTreeMap<u32, Vec<f64>>,
    /// Streams MakeMKV removed as empty (MSG:4047 mapped to scan streams).
```
