```rust
    #[test]
    fn a_stream_flagged_forced_comes_after_the_forced_only_streams() {
        let title = dvd(&[VIDEO, ENG_VOBSUB, ENG_VOBSUB_FORCED_ONLY, ENG_VOBSUB_FORCED]);
        let forty = times(40, 500.0, 30.0);
        let with_forced_only = facts(vec![(1, regular_events()), (2, forced_events()), (3, forty.clone())]);
        let decision = decide_subtitles(&title, &with_forced_only, &Settings::default());
        assert_eq!(
            decision.kept,
            vec![
                SubtitleTrack { parent: Some(1), ..track(2, SubtitleRole::Forced, Some(20), "flag") },
                track(1, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(1000), "count"),
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(decision.dropped, vec![(3, SubtitleDrop::ExtraForced)]);
        assert_eq!((decision.case, decision.confidence), (SubtitleCase::OneFull, 0.90));

        let flagged_only =
            SubtitleFacts { removed: BTreeSet::from([2]), ..facts(vec![(1, regular_events()), (3, forty)]) };
        let decision = decide_subtitles(&title, &flagged_only, &Settings::default());
        assert_eq!(
            decision.kept,
            vec![track(3, SubtitleRole::Forced, Some(40), "flag"), track(1, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(1000), "count")]
        );
        assert_eq!(decision.dropped, vec![(2, SubtitleDrop::DerivedForcedOnlyEmpty)]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_separately_authored_short_track_is_the_last_forced_source() {
        let title = dvd(&[VIDEO, ENG_VOBSUB, ENG_VOBSUB_FORCED, ENG_VOBSUB]);
        let thirty = times(30, 600.0, 30.0);
        let flagged = facts(vec![(1, regular_events()), (2, times(40, 500.0, 30.0)), (3, thirty.clone())]);
        let decision = decide_subtitles(&title, &flagged, &Settings::default());
        assert_eq!(
            decision.kept,
            vec![track(2, SubtitleRole::Forced, Some(40), "flag"), track(1, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(1000), "count")]
        );
        assert_eq!(decision.dropped, vec![(3, SubtitleDrop::ExtraForced)]);

        // The flagged stream has no events: the separately authored one is forced, by its count.
        let empty_flag = facts(vec![(1, regular_events()), (2, vec![]), (3, thirty)]);
        let decision = decide_subtitles(&title, &empty_flag, &Settings::default());
        assert_eq!(
            decision.kept,
            vec![track(3, SubtitleRole::Forced, Some(30), "count"), track(1, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(1000), "count")]
        );
        assert_eq!(decision.dropped, vec![(2, SubtitleDrop::NoEvents)]);
        assert_eq!((decision.case, decision.confidence), (SubtitleCase::OneFull, 0.90));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_stream_flagged_forced_is_never_a_dialogue_track_even_when_full() {
        // A DVD episode: 300 dialogue events, and a stream flagged forced (4096 without 2048) whose 40 events start with
        // the dialogue's first 40. 40 is at least 10% of 300, but the flag makes it a forced source (8.7 "Forced"), never
        // a full track: it neither joins the dialogue group nor turns the dialogue track into SDH.
        let title = dvd(&[VIDEO, ENG_VOBSUB, ENG_VOBSUB_FORCED]);
        let evidence = facts(vec![(1, times(300, 10.0, 6.0)), (2, times(40, 10.0, 6.0))]);
        let decision = decide_subtitles(&title, &evidence, &Settings::default());
        assert_eq!(
            decision.kept,
            vec![track(2, SubtitleRole::Forced, Some(40), "flag"), track(1, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(300), "count")]
        );
        assert_eq!(decision.full, vec![1]);
        assert_eq!(decision.pairs, vec![]);
        assert_eq!(decision.dropped, vec![]);
        assert_eq!(decision.dialogue_pick, Some(DialoguePick::OneFull));
        assert_eq!((decision.case, decision.confidence), (SubtitleCase::OneFull, 0.90));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_track_that_is_not_full_with_150_events_or_more_is_dropped_with_a_note() {
        // 2,000 dialogue events make a track full from 200 events: 149 and 150 are both not full.
        let title = bluray(&[VIDEO, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS]);
        let evidence = facts(vec![
            (1, times(2000, 10.0, 3.0)),
            (2, times(149, 20.0, 30.0)),
            (3, times(150, 21.0, 30.0)),
        ]);
        let decision = decide_subtitles(&title, &evidence, &Settings::default());
        assert_eq!(
            decision.kept,
            vec![track(2, SubtitleRole::Forced, Some(149), "count"), track(1, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(2000), "count")]
        );
        assert_eq!(decision.dropped, vec![(3, SubtitleDrop::Partial)]);
        assert_eq!(
            decision.notes,
            vec![Noted {
                note: Note::PartialSubtitleDropped,
                stream: Some(3),
                detail: "stream 3: 150 events, not full (the largest English track has 2000) and 150 or more (8.7 \
                         \"Other tracks\")"
                    .to_string(),
            }]
        );
        assert_eq!(decision.reviews, vec![]);
        assert_eq!((decision.case, decision.confidence), (SubtitleCase::OneFull, 0.90));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_pair_in_the_between_band_raises_subtitle_ambiguous() {
        let title = bluray(&[VIDEO, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS_FORCED_ONLY, ENG_PGS]);
        let (a, b) = between_events();
        let decision = decide_subtitles(&title, &facts(vec![(1, a), (2, forced_events()), (3, b)]), &Settings::default());
        assert_eq!(decision.pairs, vec![(1, 3, 0.5, Band::Between)]);
        assert_eq!(decision.groups, vec![vec![1], vec![3]]);
        assert_eq!(decision.dialogue_pick, Some(DialoguePick::ForcedParent));
        // Stream 3 is outside the picked group, but its pair with the group's track 1 is undecided (8.7 "In between"):
        // nothing confirms it as commentary, so it is kept as regular under the review, not dropped (D20).
        assert_eq!(
            decision.kept,
            vec![
                SubtitleTrack { parent: Some(1), ..track(2, SubtitleRole::Forced, Some(20), "flag") },
                track(1, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(1000), "alignment"),
                track(3, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(1100), "alignment"),
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(decision.dropped, vec![]);
        assert_eq!(decision.reviews, vec![ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous]);
        assert_eq!((decision.case, decision.confidence), (SubtitleCase::Ambiguous, 0.60));
    }

    #[test]
    fn two_full_tracks_in_different_groups_with_nothing_to_pick_raise_subtitle_ambiguous() {
        let title = bluray(&[VIDEO, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS]);
        let decision =
            decide_subtitles(&title, &facts(vec![(1, regular_events()), (2, commentary_events())]), &Settings::default());
        assert_eq!(decision.pairs, vec![(1, 2, 0.0, Band::Different)]);
        assert_eq!(decision.groups, vec![vec![1], vec![2]]);
        // No rule picks a group: the first stands in for the regular and SDH roles, under review. Nothing confirms the
        // other group's track as commentary, so it is kept as regular too, not dropped by its position (D15, D20).
        assert_eq!((decision.dialogue_group, decision.dialogue_pick), (Some(0), None));
        assert_eq!(
            decision.kept,
            vec![
                track(1, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(1000), "alignment"),
                track(2, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(800), "alignment"),
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(decision.dropped, vec![]);
        assert_eq!(decision.reviews, vec![ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous]);
        assert_eq!((decision.case, decision.confidence), (SubtitleCase::Ambiguous, 0.60));
    }

    #[test]
    fn two_largest_groups_of_equal_size_are_no_pick() {
        // Streams 1 and 2 are the dialogue and its SDH copy; 3 is a commentary (2.5 s off the dialogue) and 4 the same
        // commentary with 100 more events 2 s after its first 100 (900 events). Two groups of two: neither is the
        // largest, Task 9's `dialogue_group` picks nothing, and position never decides (D15): subtitle_ambiguous, and
        // no full track is dropped (D20). The first group stands in for the regular and SDH roles.
        let title = bluray(&[VIDEO, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS]);
        let evidence = facts(vec![
            (1, regular_events()),
            (2, sdh_events()),
            (3, commentary_events()),
            (4, merged(commentary_events(), times(100, 14.5, 6.0))),
        ]);
        let decision = decide_subtitles(&title, &evidence, &Settings::default());
        assert_eq!(decision.groups, vec![vec![1, 2], vec![3, 4]]);
        assert_eq!(
            decision.pairs,
            vec![
                (1, 2, 1.0, Band::Same),
                (1, 3, 0.0, Band::Different),
                (1, 4, 0.0, Band::Different),
                (2, 3, 0.0, Band::Different),
                (2, 4, 0.0, Band::Different),
                (3, 4, 1.0, Band::Same),
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!((decision.dialogue_group, decision.dialogue_pick), (Some(0), None));
        assert_eq!(
            decision.kept,
            vec![
                track(1, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(1000), "alignment"),
                track(3, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(800), "alignment"),
                track(4, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(900), "alignment"),
                track(2, SubtitleRole::Sdh, Some(1200), "alignment"),
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(decision.dropped, vec![]);
        assert_eq!(decision.reviews, vec![ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous]);
        assert_eq!((decision.case, decision.confidence), (SubtitleCase::Ambiguous, 0.60));
    }

    #[test]
    fn more_than_two_tracks_in_the_dialogue_group_raise_subtitle_ambiguous() {
        // Stream 3 is the dialogue plus 100 cues 4 s after the first 100 dialogue events: 1,100 events, the same group.
        let title = bluray(&[VIDEO, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS]);
        let evidence = facts(vec![
            (1, regular_events()),
            (2, sdh_events()),
            (3, merged(regular_events(), times(100, 14.0, 6.0))),
        ]);
        let decision = decide_subtitles(&title, &evidence, &Settings::default());
        assert_eq!(decision.groups, vec![vec![1, 2, 3]]);
        assert_eq!(
            decision.pairs,
            vec![(1, 2, 1.0, Band::Same), (1, 3, 1.0, Band::Same), (2, 3, 1000.0 / 1100.0, Band::Same)]
        );
        // The two with the most events are kept: 2 (1,200) is SDH, 3 (1,100) regular; 1 (1,000) is dropped.
        assert_eq!(
            decision.kept,
            vec![
                track(3, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(1100), "alignment"),
                track(2, SubtitleRole::Sdh, Some(1200), "alignment"),
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(decision.dropped, vec![(1, SubtitleDrop::ExtraDialogueTrack)]);
        assert_eq!(decision.reviews, vec![ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous]);
        assert_eq!((decision.case, decision.confidence), (SubtitleCase::Ambiguous, 0.60));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_track_described_sdh_is_one_of_the_two_kept_from_a_group_of_three() {
        // The three aligned tracks of the test above (1,000, 1,200 and 1,100 events). TheDiscDB describes stream 1, the
        // one with the fewest events, as "English SDH" and the others as "English": a description saying SDH overrides
        // the count (8.7 "Regular and SDH"), so stream 1 is kept as SDH and the extra track is stream 3.
        let title = bluray(&[VIDEO, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS]);
        let record: DiscDbTitle = serde_json::from_value(json!({
            "index": 0,
            "source_file": "00800.mpls",
            "segment_map": "1",
            "duration": "1:00:00",
            "tracks": [
                {"index": 0, "type": "Video", "name": "Mpeg4 AVC High@L4.1"},
                {"index": 1, "type": "Subtitles", "name": "HDMV PGS Subtitles", "language_code": "eng",
                 "language": "English", "description": "English SDH"},
                {"index": 2, "type": "Subtitles", "name": "HDMV PGS Subtitles", "language_code": "eng",
                 "language": "English", "description": "English"},
                {"index": 3, "type": "Subtitles", "name": "HDMV PGS Subtitles", "language_code": "eng",
                 "language": "English", "description": "English"}
            ]
        }))
        .unwrap();
        let evidence = SubtitleFacts {
            discdb: Some(&record),
            ..facts(vec![
                (1, regular_events()),
                (2, sdh_events()),
                (3, merged(regular_events(), times(100, 14.0, 6.0))),
            ])
        };
        let decision = decide_subtitles(&title, &evidence, &Settings::default());
        assert_eq!(decision.groups, vec![vec![1, 2, 3]]);
        assert_eq!(decision.dialogue_pick, Some(DialoguePick::Described));
        assert_eq!(
            decision.kept,
            vec![
                track(2, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(1200), "description"),
                track(1, SubtitleRole::Sdh, Some(1000), "description"),
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(decision.dropped, vec![(3, SubtitleDrop::ExtraDialogueTrack)]);
        assert_eq!(decision.reviews, vec![ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous]);
        assert_eq!((decision.case, decision.confidence), (SubtitleCase::Ambiguous, 0.60));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_track_thediscdb_describes_as_commentary_is_dropped_and_never_grouped() {
        // Stream 3 is timed on the dialogue (the 1,100 events of the tests above), so by timing alone it would be the
        // third track of the dialogue group and kept as regular. TheDiscDB describes it as "Commentary" (and streams 1
        // and 2 not at all): a database entry confirms commentary (R6, D15), so it is set aside and dropped, and the
        // dialogue group is the largest group of the other two.
        let title = bluray(&[VIDEO, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS]);
        let record: DiscDbTitle = serde_json::from_value(json!({
            "index": 0,
            "source_file": "00800.mpls",
            "segment_map": "1",
            "duration": "1:00:00",
            "tracks": [
                {"index": 0, "type": "Video", "name": "Mpeg4 AVC High@L4.1"},
                {"index": 1, "type": "Subtitles", "name": "HDMV PGS Subtitles", "language_code": "eng",
                 "language": "English"},
                {"index": 2, "type": "Subtitles", "name": "HDMV PGS Subtitles", "language_code": "eng",
                 "language": "English"},
                {"index": 3, "type": "Subtitles", "name": "HDMV PGS Subtitles", "language_code": "eng",
                 "language": "English", "description": "Commentary"}
            ]
        }))
        .unwrap();
        let evidence = SubtitleFacts {
            discdb: Some(&record),
            ..facts(vec![
                (1, regular_events()),
                (2, sdh_events()),
                (3, merged(regular_events(), times(100, 14.0, 6.0))),
            ])
        };
        let decision = decide_subtitles(&title, &evidence, &Settings::default());
        assert_eq!(
            decision,
            SubtitleDecision {
                kept: vec![
                    track(1, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(1000), "alignment"),
                    track(2, SubtitleRole::Sdh, Some(1200), "alignment"),
                ],
                dropped: vec![(3, SubtitleDrop::OutsideDialogueGroup)],
                set_aside: vec![(3, "described as commentary by TheDiscDB (R6)".to_string())],
                full: vec![1, 2],
                groups: vec![vec![1, 2]],
                dialogue_group: Some(0),
                dialogue_pick: Some(DialoguePick::Largest),
                pairs: vec![(1, 2, 1.0, Band::Same)],
                case: SubtitleCase::Alignment,
                confidence: 0.85,
                notes: vec![],
                reviews: vec![],
            }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn subs_tolerance_ms_decides_whether_two_tracks_align() {
        let title = bluray(&[VIDEO, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS]);
        let evidence = facts(vec![(1, regular_events()), (2, commentary_events())]);
        // 300 ms (the default): 2.5 s apart, different groups, nothing picks one.
        let strict = decide_subtitles(&title, &evidence, &Settings::default());
        assert_eq!(strict.pairs, vec![(1, 2, 0.0, Band::Different)]);
        assert_eq!(strict.reviews, vec![ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous]);
        // 3,000 ms: every commentary event starts within 3 s of a dialogue event, one group, the larger track SDH.
        let loose = decide_subtitles(&title, &evidence, &Settings { subs_tolerance_ms: 3000, ..Settings::default() });
        assert_eq!(loose.pairs, vec![(1, 2, 1.0, Band::Same)]);
        assert_eq!(loose.groups, vec![vec![1, 2]]);
        assert_eq!(
            kept_roles(&loose),
            vec![(2, SubtitleRole::Regular, "alignment".to_string()), (1, SubtitleRole::Sdh, "alignment".to_string())]
        );
        assert_eq!(loose.reviews, vec![]);
        assert_eq!((loose.case, loose.confidence), (SubtitleCase::Alignment, 0.85));
    }

    #[test]
    fn subs_same_min_is_the_lowest_share_of_the_same_band() {
        let title = bluray(&[VIDEO, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS_FORCED_ONLY, ENG_PGS]);
        let (a, b) = between_events();
        let evidence = facts(vec![(1, a), (2, forced_events()), (3, b)]);
        // 0.70 (the default): 0.5 is between.
        let default = decide_subtitles(&title, &evidence, &Settings::default());
        assert_eq!(default.pairs, vec![(1, 3, 0.5, Band::Between)]);
        assert_eq!(default.reviews, vec![ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous]);
        // 0.50: 0.5 is at least subs_same_min, so the two tracks share a group and the larger is SDH.
        let lowered = decide_subtitles(&title, &evidence, &Settings { subs_same_min: 0.5, ..Settings::default() });
        assert_eq!(lowered.pairs, vec![(1, 3, 0.5, Band::Same)]);
        assert_eq!(lowered.groups, vec![vec![1, 3]]);
        assert_eq!(
            lowered.kept,
            vec![
                SubtitleTrack { parent: Some(1), ..track(2, SubtitleRole::Forced, Some(20), "flag") },
                track(1, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(1000), "alignment"),
                track(3, SubtitleRole::Sdh, Some(1100), "alignment"),
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(lowered.reviews, vec![]);
        assert_eq!((lowered.case, lowered.confidence), (SubtitleCase::Alignment, 0.85));
    }

    #[test]
    fn subs_diff_max_is_the_highest_share_of_the_different_band() {
        let title = bluray(&[VIDEO, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS_FORCED_ONLY, ENG_PGS]);
        let (a, b) = between_events();
        let evidence = facts(vec![(1, a), (2, forced_events()), (3, b)]);
        // 0.30 (the default): 0.5 is between.
        let default = decide_subtitles(&title, &evidence, &Settings::default());
        assert_eq!(default.reviews, vec![ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous]);
        // 0.50: 0.5 is at most subs_diff_max, so the tracks are in different groups and the forced parent picks.
        let raised = decide_subtitles(&title, &evidence, &Settings { subs_diff_max: 0.5, ..Settings::default() });
        assert_eq!(raised.pairs, vec![(1, 3, 0.5, Band::Different)]);
        assert_eq!(raised.groups, vec![vec![1], vec![3]]);
        assert_eq!(raised.dialogue_pick, Some(DialoguePick::ForcedParent));
        assert_eq!(raised.dropped, vec![(3, SubtitleDrop::OutsideDialogueGroup)]);
        assert_eq!(raised.reviews, vec![]);
        assert_eq!((raised.case, raised.confidence), (SubtitleCase::Alignment, 0.85));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_decision_serialises_with_the_spec_spellings_and_reads_back() {
        let title = bluray(&[VIDEO, ENG_PGS, SPA_PGS]);
        let decision = decide_subtitles(&title, &facts(vec![(1, regular_events())]), &Settings::default());
        let value = serde_json::to_value(&decision).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            value,
            json!({
                "kept": [{
                    "stream": 1, "role": "regular", "name": "English", "forced": false, "hearing_impaired": false,
                    "default": false, "events": 1000, "closed_captions": false, "parent": null, "decided_by": "count"
                }],
                "dropped": [[2, {"why": "other_language"}]],
                "set_aside": [],
                "full": [1],
                "groups": [[1]],
                "dialogue_group": 0,
                "dialogue_pick": "one_full",
                "pairs": [],
                "case": "one_full",
                "confidence": 0.9,
                "notes": [],
                "reviews": []
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_value::<SubtitleDecision>(value).unwrap(), decision);
    }
```

```rust
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ the rule

    /// How a kept track was decided (`SubtitleTrack.decided_by`): by its flags (a derived forced-only stream, a DVD stream
    /// flagged forced), by TheDiscDB's description, by event counts (the one full track, a separately authored forced
    /// track), by alignment (two or more full tracks), by the closed-caption type, or as the one English stream.
    const BY_FLAG: &str = "flag";
    const BY_DESCRIPTION: &str = "description";
    const BY_COUNT: &str = "count";
    const BY_ALIGNMENT: &str = "alignment";
    const BY_CLOSED_CAPTIONS: &str = "closed_captions";
    const BY_SINGLE: &str = "single";

    /// The set-aside sentence of a DVD stream flagged director's comments.
    const DIRECTORS_COMMENTS_LINE: &str = "DVD stream flagged director's comments (flags 1 or 2; 8.7 \"Set aside first\")";
    /// The set-aside sentence of the DVD closed-caption stream.
    const CLOSED_CAPTIONS_LINE: &str = "DVD closed-caption stream (codec CC; 8.7 \"Set aside first\")";
    /// The set-aside sentence of a counted stream TheDiscDB describes as commentary (R6, D15). It is dropped as
    /// OutsideDialogueGroup: Task 9's `SubtitleDrop` has no variant for a described drop.
    const DESCRIBED_COMMENTARY_LINE: &str = "described as commentary by TheDiscDB (R6)";

    /// The set-aside sentence of a derived forced-only stream.
    fn forced_only_line(parent: Option<u32>) -> String {
        match parent {
            Some(parent) => {
                format!("derived forced-only stream of stream {parent} (flags 4096 and 2048; 8.7 \"Set aside first\")")
            }
            None => "derived forced-only stream with no preceding stream of its language (flags 4096 and 2048; 8.7 \
                     \"Set aside first\")"
                .to_string(),
        }
    }

    /// The detail of a partial_subtitle_dropped note.
    fn partial_line(stream: u32, events: usize, largest: usize) -> String {
        format!(
            "stream {stream}: {events} events, not full (the largest English track has {largest}) and \
             {FORCED_MAX_EVENTS} or more (8.7 \"Other tracks\")"
        )
    }

    /// The event start times 6.4 step 10 gave for `stream`; none for a stream MakeMKV removed as empty (MSG:4047) or one
    /// the step did not measure.
    fn events_of<'f>(facts: &'f SubtitleFacts<'_>, stream: u32) -> &'f [f64] {
        if facts.removed.contains(&stream) {
            return &[];
        }
        facts.events.get(&stream).map(Vec::as_slice).unwrap_or(&[])
    }

    /// Attribute 22 of `stream` (no flags when the title has no such stream).
    fn flags_of(title: &Title, stream: u32) -> Flags {
        title
            .streams
            .iter()
            .find(|candidate| candidate.number == stream)
            .map(|candidate| candidate.flags)
            .unwrap_or_default()
    }

    /// A kept track with the name and flags of its role (8.7, 8.10).
    fn track(
        facts: &SubtitleFacts<'_>,
        stream: u32,
        role: SubtitleRole,
        decided_by: &str,
        parent: Option<u32>,
        closed_captions: bool,
    ) -> SubtitleTrack {
        SubtitleTrack {
            stream,
            role,
            name: role.name().to_string(),
            forced: role == SubtitleRole::Forced,
            hearing_impaired: role == SubtitleRole::Sdh,
            default: false,
            events: facts.events.get(&stream).map(Vec::len),
            closed_captions,
            parent,
            decided_by: decided_by.to_string(),
        }
    }

    /// Spec 8.7 in full, in order: `set_aside`; a counted stream in the file that TheDiscDB describes as commentary
    /// (not as dialogue or SDH) is set aside and dropped (OutsideDialogueGroup; R6, D15); events from `facts.events`;
    /// full = `is_full` against the largest English track's events (a stream flagged forced, 4096 without 2048, is
    /// never full: its flag makes it a forced source); `alignment_groups` over the full tracks with the three bands (a
    /// Between pair raises subtitle_ambiguous); `dialogue_group` with the parents of forced-only streams that have
    /// events and `tracks::audio::descriptions` (None, two largest groups of equal size included, raises
    /// subtitle_ambiguous, and the first group stands in for the regular and SDH roles); regular and SDH (up to two:
    /// more events is SDH, a description saying SDH overrides; the closed-caption stream is SDH when the group has
    /// none; more than two gives subtitle_ambiguous, and a track described SDH is one of the two kept); full tracks
    /// outside a picked group dropped (OutsideDialogueGroup; with no pick, or with a Between band against a track of
    /// the picked group, they are kept as regular under the review, never dropped unconfirmed or by position); forced
    /// (first: a forced-only stream with events whose parent is the regular track, then the SDH track's; then a DVD
    /// stream flagged forced; then a separately authored track that is not full with fewer than FORCED_MAX_EVENTS
    /// events); other not-full tracks with FORCED_MAX_EVENTS or more events dropped with partial_subtitle_dropped,
    /// those with no events dropped NoEvents; `text_disagreements` (subtitle_ambiguous and one subtitle_text_disagrees
    /// note per stream); the confidence case; remembered then review overrides applied last (decided_by "remembered" or
    /// "reviewed"; an override naming a stream that is not an English or no-language subtitle stream is ignored), with
    /// confidence lookup::REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE (1.00) and subtitle_ambiguous cleared when every English and
    /// no-language subtitle stream of the title still in the file (not in facts.removed) has an override
    /// (other-language streams are dropped by 8.7's first sentence; the case unchanged). A title with one English
    /// stream and no events keeps it as Regular "English" (row 14 (b) fallback), case OneFull; when that stream is
    /// flagged forced (4096 without 2048) it is kept as Forced by its flag, case FlagsOrDescriptions.
    ///
    /// Where the spec leaves a choice (Task 10's list): `set_aside`'s five lists say which stream is which; a counted
    /// stream TheDiscDB describes as commentary is set aside and dropped; a stream MakeMKV removed (`facts.removed`)
    /// has no events and is not kept; with groups but no pick (two equal largest groups included) the first group
    /// stands in for the regular and SDH roles under subtitle_ambiguous and the other groups' full tracks are kept as
    /// regular, and so is a full track in the in-between band with a track of a picked group; two dialogue tracks with
    /// equal event counts raise subtitle_ambiguous (the first in scan order is regular); a description saying SDH makes
    /// a one-track group SDH and keeps its track among the two of a larger group; every forced source needs at least
    /// one event but the one English stream in the file flagged forced; a not-full track that is not the forced track
    /// is dropped as NoEvents with no events and as ExtraForced with fewer than FORCED_MAX_EVENTS. Spec 8.7, D15, D20,
    /// R5, R6. Def: T10. Use: T13, T16, T18.
    pub fn decide_subtitles(title: &Title, facts: &SubtitleFacts<'_>, settings: &Settings) -> SubtitleDecision {
        let aside = set_aside(title);
        // The English and no-language subtitle streams (Task 9's `english_or_none`, the one copy): the streams 8.7 judges.
        let english: BTreeSet<u32> = title
            .streams_of(StreamKind::Subtitles)
            .iter()
            .filter(|stream| english_or_none(stream.language.as_deref()))
            .map(|stream| stream.number)
            .collect();
        let mut dropped: BTreeMap<u32, SubtitleDrop> = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut aside_lines: Vec<(u32, String)> = Vec::new();
        let mut reviews: Vec<ReviewReason> = Vec::new();
        let mut notes: Vec<Noted> = Vec::new();

        // 8.7's first sentence: every stream in another language is dropped, forced-only ones included.
        for &stream in &aside.other_language {
            dropped.insert(stream, SubtitleDrop::OtherLanguage);
        }
        // "Set aside first": a DVD stream flagged director's comments (flags 1 or 2) is dropped.
        for &stream in &aside.directors_comments {
            dropped.insert(stream, SubtitleDrop::DirectorsComments);
            aside_lines.push((stream, DIRECTORS_COMMENTS_LINE.to_string()));
        }
        // "Set aside first": the derived forced-only streams with their parents, and the closed-caption stream.
        let forced_only: &[(u32, Option<u32>)] = &aside.forced_only;
        for &(stream, parent) in forced_only {
            aside_lines.push((stream, forced_only_line(parent)));
        }
        let closed_captions = aside.closed_captions;
        if let Some(stream) = closed_captions {
            aside_lines.push((stream, CLOSED_CAPTIONS_LINE.to_string()));
        }
        let counted: &[u32] = &aside.counted;
        // The counted streams still in the file: MakeMKV removes an empty stream and says so (MSG:4047, 6.2 step 7).
        let present: Vec<u32> = counted.iter().copied().filter(|stream| !facts.removed.contains(stream)).collect();
        // R6 and D15: a counted stream in the file that TheDiscDB describes as commentary (and not as dialogue or SDH)
        // is confirmed commentary. It takes no part in alignment or grouping and is dropped, whatever its count.
        let (_, described) = descriptions(title, facts.discdb);
        let commentary: Vec<u32> = present
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|stream| {
                described.get(stream).is_some_and(|kinds| {
                    kinds.contains(&DescriptionKind::Commentary)
                        && !kinds.iter().any(|kind| matches!(kind, DescriptionKind::Dialogue | DescriptionKind::Sdh))
                })
            })
            .collect();
        for &stream in &commentary {
            dropped.insert(stream, SubtitleDrop::OutsideDialogueGroup);
            aside_lines.push((stream, DESCRIBED_COMMENTARY_LINE.to_string()));
        }
        // The streams in the file left to judge by counts, flags and timing.
        let left_to_judge: Vec<u32> = present.iter().copied().filter(|stream| !commentary.contains(stream)).collect();

        // "Events": a track is full with at least 10% as many events as the largest English track.
        let count = |stream: u32| events_of(facts, stream).len();
        let largest = counted.iter().map(|&stream| count(stream)).max().unwrap_or(0);
        // A stream flagged forced (4096 without 2048) is never full: its flag makes it a forced source ("Forced"; the
        // confidence table's first row lets flags decide), so it never joins a dialogue group. Nor is a stream
        // described as commentary.
        let full: Vec<u32> = counted
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|&stream| {
                !commentary.contains(&stream)
                    && !flags_of(title, stream).forced_authored()
                    && is_full(count(stream), largest)
            })
            .collect();

        // "Alignment": every pair of full tracks with its band; a pair in between raises subtitle_ambiguous.
        let mut pairs: Vec<(u32, u32, f64, Band)> = Vec::new();
        for (at, &a) in full.iter().enumerate() {
            for &b in &full[at + 1..] {
                let (share, which) = band(events_of(facts, a), events_of(facts, b), settings);
                pairs.push((a, b, share, which));
            }
        }
        let full_events: Vec<(u32, &[f64])> = full.iter().map(|&stream| (stream, events_of(facts, stream))).collect();
        let (groups, between) = alignment_groups(&full_events, settings);
        if between {
            reviews.push(ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous);
        }

        // "Dialogue group": with groups and no pick, subtitle_ambiguous, and the first group stands in for the regular
        // and SDH roles.
        let forced_parents: Vec<u32> = forced_only
            .iter()
            .filter(|(stream, _)| count(*stream) > 0)
            .filter_map(|(_, parent)| *parent)
            .collect();
        // Task 9's dialogue_group picks nothing when two or more groups tie for the largest size (D15): no pick.
        let (dialogue_index, dialogue_pick) = match dialogue_group(&groups, &forced_parents, &described) {
            Some((index, pick)) => (Some(index), Some(pick)),
            None if !groups.is_empty() => {
                reviews.push(ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous);
                (Some(0), None)
            }
            None => (None, None),
        };
        let mut group: Vec<u32> = dialogue_index.map(|index| groups[index].clone()).unwrap_or_default();
        group.sort_unstable();

        // "Regular and SDH": up to two tracks of the group. More than two raise subtitle_ambiguous; the tracks a
        // TheDiscDB description calls SDH are kept first ("A TheDiscDB description saying SDH overrides the count"),
        // then those with the most events (ties by scan order), and the others are dropped.
        let says_sdh =
            |stream: u32| described.get(&stream).is_some_and(|kinds| kinds.contains(&DescriptionKind::Sdh));
        let mut chosen = group.clone();
        if chosen.len() > 2 {
            reviews.push(ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous);
            let mut by_events = chosen.clone();
            by_events.sort_by(|a, b| says_sdh(*b).cmp(&says_sdh(*a)).then(count(*b).cmp(&count(*a))).then(a.cmp(b)));
            let keep: BTreeSet<u32> = by_events.iter().take(2).copied().collect();
            for &stream in &chosen {
                if !keep.contains(&stream) {
                    dropped.insert(stream, SubtitleDrop::ExtraDialogueTrack);
                }
            }
            chosen.retain(|stream| keep.contains(stream));
        }
        let by_events_rule = if full.len() >= 2 { BY_ALIGNMENT } else { BY_COUNT };
        let mut regular: Option<(u32, &'static str)> = None;
        let mut sdh: Option<(u32, &'static str)> = None;
        match chosen.as_slice() {
            [one] => {
                if says_sdh(*one) {
                    sdh = Some((*one, BY_DESCRIPTION));
                } else {
                    regular = Some((*one, by_events_rule));
                }
            }
            [a, b] => match (says_sdh(*a), says_sdh(*b)) {
                (true, false) => {
                    sdh = Some((*a, BY_DESCRIPTION));
                    regular = Some((*b, BY_DESCRIPTION));
                }
                (false, true) => {
                    sdh = Some((*b, BY_DESCRIPTION));
                    regular = Some((*a, BY_DESCRIPTION));
                }
                _ => {
                    if count(*a) == count(*b) {
                        reviews.push(ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous);
                    }
                    let (fewer, more) = if count(*b) >= count(*a) { (*a, *b) } else { (*b, *a) };
                    regular = Some((fewer, by_events_rule));
                    sdh = Some((more, by_events_rule));
                }
            },
            _ => {}
        }
        // Section 17 row 14 (b)'s fallback: one English stream and no events (6.4 step 10 is skipped) is kept as
        // "English", unless it is flagged forced (4096 without 2048): its flag makes it the forced track, below. Two or
        // more streams in the file and no full track leave no group: subtitle_ambiguous.
        if groups.is_empty() {
            match left_to_judge.as_slice() {
                [only] if count(*only) == 0 && !flags_of(title, *only).forced_authored() => {
                    regular = Some((*only, BY_SINGLE))
                }
                [] | [_] => {}
                _ => reviews.push(ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous),
            }
        }

        // "Commentary or trivia": a full track outside the dialogue group is dropped (R6). With no pick there is no
        // dialogue group to be outside of and nothing confirms the track as commentary: it is kept as regular under the
        // review already raised (D20: an unconfirmed one is kept and reviewed; D15: never decided by position). The
        // same holds with a pick for a track whose band with a track of the group is Between: 8.7 calls that pair
        // undecided and has raised subtitle_ambiguous for it. Only a track Different from every track of a picked group
        // is dropped.
        let mut unconfirmed: Vec<u32> = Vec::new();
        for &stream in &full {
            if group.contains(&stream) {
                continue;
            }
            let between_group = pairs.iter().any(|&(a, b, _, which)| {
                which == Band::Between && ((a == stream && group.contains(&b)) || (b == stream && group.contains(&a)))
            });
            if dialogue_pick.is_none() || between_group {
                unconfirmed.push(stream);
            } else {
                dropped.insert(stream, SubtitleDrop::OutsideDialogueGroup);
            }
        }
        // The closed-caption stream is SDH by type, kept when the dialogue group has no SDH track.
        let mut kept_closed_captions = None;
        if let Some(stream) = closed_captions {
            if sdh.is_none() {
                kept_closed_captions = Some(stream);
            } else {
                dropped.insert(stream, SubtitleDrop::ClosedCaptionsUnused);
            }
        }

        // "Forced": at most one, in the spec's order; every source needs at least one event but the lone stream
        // flagged forced below.
        let regular_stream = regular.map(|(stream, _)| stream);
        let sdh_stream = sdh.map(|(stream, _)| stream);
        let mut forced: Option<(u32, Option<u32>, &'static str)> = None;
        for dialogue in [regular_stream, sdh_stream].into_iter().flatten() {
            if forced.is_none() {
                forced = forced_only
                    .iter()
                    .find(|(stream, parent)| *parent == Some(dialogue) && count(*stream) > 0)
                    .map(|&(stream, parent)| (stream, parent, BY_FLAG));
            }
        }
        let rest: Vec<u32> = counted
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|stream| {
                !full.contains(stream)
                    && Some(*stream) != regular_stream
                    && Some(*stream) != sdh_stream
                    && !dropped.contains_key(stream)
            })
            .collect();
        // A stream flagged forced needs events, unless it is the only English stream in the file left to judge (6.4
        // step 10 does not run for one English stream, and a stream flagged forced is never full, so there is no
        // group): its flag alone makes it forced.
        if forced.is_none() {
            forced = rest
                .iter()
                .copied()
                .find(|&stream| {
                    flags_of(title, stream).forced_authored()
                        && (count(stream) > 0 || (groups.is_empty() && left_to_judge == [stream]))
                })
                .map(|stream| (stream, None, BY_FLAG));
        }
        if forced.is_none() {
            forced = rest
                .iter()
                .copied()
                .find(|&stream| count(stream) > 0 && count(stream) < FORCED_MAX_EVENTS)
                .map(|stream| (stream, None, BY_COUNT));
        }
        let forced_stream = forced.map(|(stream, _, _)| stream);
        // "Other tracks": not full with FORCED_MAX_EVENTS events or more, dropped with partial_subtitle_dropped; a stream
        // with no events (MakeMKV removed it, or 6.4 step 10 measured nothing) is dropped NoEvents; the other shorter
        // ones that are not the forced track are dropped as extra forced candidates.
        for &stream in &rest {
            if Some(stream) == forced_stream {
                continue;
            }
            if count(stream) >= FORCED_MAX_EVENTS {
                dropped.insert(stream, SubtitleDrop::Partial);
                notes.push(Noted {
                    note: Note::PartialSubtitleDropped,
                    stream: Some(stream),
                    detail: partial_line(stream, count(stream), largest),
                });
            } else if count(stream) == 0 {
                dropped.insert(stream, SubtitleDrop::NoEvents);
            } else {
                dropped.insert(stream, SubtitleDrop::ExtraForced);
            }
        }
        for &(stream, _) in forced_only {
            if Some(stream) != forced_stream {
                let why = if count(stream) > 0 {
                    SubtitleDrop::DerivedForcedOnlyUnused
                } else {
                    SubtitleDrop::DerivedForcedOnlyEmpty
                };
                dropped.insert(stream, why);
            }
        }

        let mut kept: Vec<SubtitleTrack> = Vec::new();
        if let Some((stream, parent, by)) = forced {
            kept.push(track(facts, stream, SubtitleRole::Forced, by, parent, false));
        }
        if let Some((stream, by)) = regular {
            kept.push(track(facts, stream, SubtitleRole::Regular, by, None, false));
        }
        if let Some((stream, by)) = sdh {
            kept.push(track(facts, stream, SubtitleRole::Sdh, by, None, false));
        }
        for &stream in &unconfirmed {
            kept.push(track(facts, stream, SubtitleRole::Regular, BY_ALIGNMENT, None, false));
        }
        if let Some(stream) = kept_closed_captions {
            kept.push(track(facts, stream, SubtitleRole::Sdh, BY_CLOSED_CAPTIONS, None, true));
        }

        // The confidence table: a review first; then nothing left to count (no English stream at all, or flags
        // decided); then every counted stream kept by its flag or its description, or dropped by its description; then
        // the number of full tracks.
        let case = if reviews.contains(&ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous) {
            SubtitleCase::Ambiguous
        } else if present.is_empty() {
            if english.is_empty() {
                SubtitleCase::NoEnglish
            } else {
                SubtitleCase::FlagsOrDescriptions
            }
        } else if present.iter().all(|stream| {
            commentary.contains(stream)
                || kept.iter().any(|kept_track| {
                    kept_track.stream == *stream && matches!(kept_track.decided_by.as_str(), BY_FLAG | BY_DESCRIPTION)
                })
        }) {
            SubtitleCase::FlagsOrDescriptions
        } else if full.len() >= 2 {
            SubtitleCase::Alignment
        } else {
            SubtitleCase::OneFull
        };

        kept.sort_by_key(|kept_track| (kept_track.role, kept_track.stream));
        aside_lines.sort_by_key(|(stream, _)| *stream);
        SubtitleDecision {
            kept,
            dropped: dropped.into_iter().collect(),
            set_aside: aside_lines,
            full,
            groups,
            dialogue_group: dialogue_index,
            dialogue_pick,
            pairs,
            case,
            confidence: confidence(case),
            notes,
            reviews: sorted_unique(reviews),
        }
    }
```

```rust
    /// The detail of a subtitle_text_disagrees note: what the text reads and what the counts and timing decided.
    fn text_line(stream: u32, read: Role, kept: Option<SubtitleRole>) -> String {
        let counts = match kept {
            Some(role) => format!("keep it as {}", role.as_str()),
            None => "drop it".to_string(),
        };
        format!("stream {stream}: the text reads {}, the counts {counts} (8.7 \"Text\")", read.as_str())
    }
```

```rust
    /// `decided_by` of a track a remembered decision keeps (spec 5), and of one the owner's Override tracks keeps (spec 11).
    const BY_REMEMBERED: &str = "remembered";
    const BY_REVIEWED: &str = "reviewed";

    /// The overrides of the title's English and no-language subtitle streams (`english`, the set `decide_subtitles`
    /// builds with `english_or_none`), by scan stream: the remembered ones (spec 5, matched by stream signature through
    /// `remembered::apply_subtitles`), then the owner's (spec 11), which replace a remembered one on the same stream;
    /// each with the `decided_by` it gives. An override naming a stream that is not one of the title's subtitle streams
    /// is ignored, and so is one naming another language's stream: 8.7's first sentence drops it, and `SubtitleRole`
    /// names only English roles (8.7, 8.10).
    fn overrides_of(
        title: &Title,
        facts: &SubtitleFacts<'_>,
        english: &BTreeSet<u32>,
    ) -> BTreeMap<u32, (SubtitleOverride, &'static str)> {
        let mut out = BTreeMap::new();
        if let Some(entries) = facts.remembered {
            for (stream, action) in apply_subtitles(entries, &title.streams) {
                if english.contains(&stream) {
                    out.insert(stream, (action.clone(), BY_REMEMBERED));
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(reviewed) = facts.reviewed {
            for (stream, action) in reviewed {
                if english.contains(stream) {
                    out.insert(*stream, (action.clone(), BY_REVIEWED));
                }
            }
        }
        out
    }
```

```rust
// lazymkv_core::settings (T1)
/// Spec 8.9's edition layout. Spec 14 `edition_style`. Def: T1. Use: T11.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum EditionStyle { Combined, Plex, Jellyfin }
impl EditionStyle { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; pub const ALL: [EditionStyle; 3]; }
impl std::str::FromStr for EditionStyle { type Err = String; fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<EditionStyle, String>; }
/// Every key of spec 14 with its default (`Settings::default()` is the table's Default column). A settings file may name
/// only the keys it changes: absent keys take the default (`#[serde(default)]`); an unknown key is refused
/// (`deny_unknown_fields`). Def: T1. Use: every rule.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Settings {
    /// Spec 7; None until set. Required by the engine, not by any rule here.
    pub staging_root: Option<String>,
    pub movies_root: Option<String>,
    pub tv_root: Option<String>,
    /// 120: MakeMKV minimum title length, seconds (8.2's candidate filter reads it).
    pub minlength_s: u32,
    /// 1024: MakeMKV read cache, MB.
    pub cache_mb: u32,
    /// 0.85: confidence needed to file automatically (8.8, 6.2, 6.3).
    pub auto_threshold: f64,
    /// 45: shortest title considered a feature, minutes (8.3 rule 3.2).
    pub feature_min_minutes: u32,
    /// true: D9, a TMDb-only identification may file automatically (8.1's 0.84 cap when false).
    pub tmdb_only_autofile: bool,
    /// true: D9, channel count before fidelity tier (8.6 step 3).
    pub prefer_most_channels: bool,
    /// true: D9, original-language audio first for non-English works (8.6 step 5).
    pub original_language_first: bool,
    /// 300: start-time tolerance for subtitle alignment, ms (8.7).
    pub subs_tolerance_ms: u32,
    /// 0.70 and 0.30: the provisional alignment bands (8.7).
    pub subs_same_min: f64,
    pub subs_diff_max: f64,
    /// 64: image-subtitle packets this small clear the screen (8.7).
    pub sub_clear_max_bytes: i64,
    /// Combined (8.9).
    pub edition_style: EditionStyle,
    /// false: add the square-bracket ID tag (8.9).
    pub jellyfin10_compat: bool,
    /// 7: days raw data of filed jobs is kept (7).
    pub retention_days: u32,
    /// true: D16.
    pub keep_tuning_evidence: bool,
    /// None; required while keep_tuning_evidence is on; not inside staging_root or a library root (7, 14).
    pub tuning_root: Option<String>,
    /// 1, 10, 120, 30, 300, 20, 30 (spec 14, in its order).
    pub file_phase_concurrency: u32,
    pub drive_settle_s: u32,
    pub drive_ready_timeout_s: u32,
    pub scan_timeout_min: u32,
    pub stall_timeout_s: u32,
    pub read_error_rate: u32,
    pub exit_wait_min: u32,
    /// "2.0.0": lowest supported MakeMKV (9.1).
    pub makemkv_min_version: String,
    pub tool_paths: ToolPaths,
}
impl Default for Settings { fn default() -> Settings; }

/// What the table says about one stream's codec. Def: T1. Use: T2 (Stream.codec), T8, T11, T12.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Codec {
    pub family: Family,
    /// The display name 8.10 uses ("TrueHD", "DTS-HD MA", "DTS", "Dolby Digital", "Dolby Digital Plus", "DTS-HD HR",
    /// "LPCM", "FLAC", "MPEG Audio", "AAC", "HEVC", "AVC", "MPEG-2", "VC-1", "PGS", "VobSub", "Closed Captions");
    /// attribute 6, else 7, else 5, for Unknown.
    pub display: String,
    /// From attribute 7 at scan time: "TrueHD Atmos" gives Atmos, a 7 containing "DTS:X" gives DtsX (spelling not yet seen).
    pub object: Option<ObjectAudio>,

}
/// The table row for MakeMKV's attributes 5 (codec id), 6 (short) and 7 (long); never fails: an unknown trio is
/// Family::Unknown with `display` as the doc of `Codec` says. Rows from the recordings: V_MPEGH/ISO/HEVC, V_MPEG4/ISO/AVC,
/// V_MPEG2, A_TRUEHD, A_DTS with short "DTS-HD MA" / "DTS-HD HR" / "DTS", A_AC3, S_HDMV/PGS, S_VOBSUB, S_CC608/DVD; rows the
/// spec names but no recording shows, with MakeMKV's documented spellings: A_EAC3 "E-AC3", A_PCM or A_LPCM "LPCM", A_FLAC
/// "FLAC", A_MPEG/L2 "Mpeg", A_AAC "AAC", and V_MS/VFW/WVC1, VC-1 (ruling RP26; matched on attribute 5 alone, its
/// attributes 6 and 7 not yet seen in a recording). Spec 8.6 "Codecs". Def: T1. Use: T2.
pub fn codec(id: &str, short: &str, long: &str) -> Codec;

/// Attribute 22 as a bitmask (spec 9.5). Unknown bits are kept in the value and ignored by every query. Def: T2. Use: T6 (signature), T8, T9, T10, T12.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Flags(pub u32);
impl Flags {
    pub const DIRECTORS_COMMENTS: u32 = 1;
    pub const ALT_DIRECTORS_COMMENTS: u32 = 2;
    pub const VISUALLY_IMPAIRED: u32 = 4;
    pub const CORE_AUDIO: u32 = 256;
    pub const SECONDARY_AUDIO: u32 = 512;
    pub const HAS_CORE_AUDIO: u32 = 1024;
    /// The same bit as audio::labels::DERIVED (pinned by a test: `Flags::DERIVED as i64 == audio::labels::DERIVED`).
    pub const DERIVED: u32 = 2048;
    pub const FORCED: u32 = 4096;
    /// The bits 9.5 names; every other bit (16384, 32768, 65536 seen) is ignored.
    pub const KNOWN: u32 = 1 | 2 | 4 | 256 | 512 | 1024 | 2048 | 4096;
    /// `robot::int_attr(attrs, 22)` as Flags (0 for an absent or empty attribute); Err with int_attr's text when attribute 22
    /// is not a number (never seen), and Err `attribute 22 is <n>, outside the flag range 0 to 4294967295` when it is
    /// negative or above u32::MAX. Spec 9.5.
    pub fn of(attrs: &Attrs) -> Result<Flags, String>;
    /// True when `bit` is one or more known bits and every one of them is set; false when `bit` is 0 or holds any bit
    /// outside KNOWN. Spec 9.5.
    pub fn has(self, bit: u32) -> bool;
    /// Flags 1, 2 or 4 (8.6 step 1's "director's comments, alternate director's comments or visually impaired").
    pub fn commentary(self) -> bool;
    /// 4096 and 2048 together (8.7 "derived forced-only").
    pub fn derived_forced_only(self) -> bool;
    /// 4096 without 2048 (8.7 "a DVD stream flagged forced").
    pub fn forced_authored(self) -> bool;
    /// The known bits only.
    pub fn known(self) -> u32;
}

    pub language: Option<String>,

    /// Attribute 14.
    pub channels: Option<u32>,
    /// Attributes 17 and 18.
    pub sample_rate: Option<u32>,
    pub sample_size: Option<u32>,
    /// Attribute 19 "WxH" as (width, height).
    pub video_size: Option<(u32, u32)>,
    /// Attribute 22 (`Flags::of`).
    pub flags: Flags,
    /// Attribute 30 ("PGS English  (forced only)", "CC->Text English ( Lossy conversion )").
    pub tree_info: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 40 ("stereo", "5.1(side)", "7.1").
    pub layout_name: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 41 (only on a converted stream: "Text") and 42 ("( Lossless conversion )", "( Lossy conversion )").
```

Also used: `unicode_normalization::UnicodeNormalization` (NFC for 8.9; `unicode-normalization` is already a `lazymkv-core` dependency, used by `subtitle::text`), and `serde` with `serde_json` (the derives and the serialisation tests). No new dependency.

Produces (exactly the `core::naming (Task 11)` and `core::tracks::layout (Task 11)` entries of the Shared interfaces; Tasks 12, 13 and 16 rely on them):

```rust
// lazymkv_core::naming (Task 11; crates/core/src/naming.rs)
/// 8.9: 2000 or more "2160p", 1000 or more "1080p", 700 or more "720p", 576 "576p", anything else "480p". Def: T11. Use: T11, T13.
pub fn resolution_label(height: u32) -> &'static str;

// `Work` is `core::lookup::tmdb::Work` (Task 3); naming reads it and defines nothing of its own for it.

/// A final path as components under a root, joined with the root's separator. Def: T11. Use: T13, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct NamedPath { pub root: String, pub components: Vec<String>, pub path: String }

/// Movies (8.9): `<root>\Title (Year) {tmdb-ID}[ compat]\Title (Year) {tmdb-ID}[ compat] - <Res>[ <n>][ <Ed> {edition-<Ed>}].mkv`
/// by settings.edition_style (combined, plex: edition folder, jellyfin: ` - <Res> <Ed>`); `edition` already through
/// edition_label; a year of None writes no " (Year)"; `copy` Some(n) appends " n" after the resolution label (`- 2160p 2`,
/// spec 11 Resolve collision "keep both"). Notes: compat_tag_omitted when the tag cannot be built. Def: T11. Use: T13.
pub fn movie_path(root: &str, work: &Work, resolution: &str, edition: Option<&str>, copy: Option<u32>, settings: &Settings) -> (NamedPath, Vec<Noted>);
/// TV (8.9): `<root>\Show (Year) {tmdb-ID}[ compat]\Season NN\Show (Year) - SNNENN[-ENN][ <n>] - Episode Title.mkv`; season 0 is
/// `Season 00` (specials); the compat tag only on the show folder; the episode title through episode_title, omitted with its
/// " - " when None; `copy` Some(n) appends " n" after the episode code (spec 11). Def: T11. Use: T13.
pub fn tv_path(root: &str, work: &Work, season: u32, episodes: &[u32], episode_name: Option<&str>, copy: Option<u32>, settings: &Settings) -> (NamedPath, Vec<Noted>);
/// 8.9's second tag when settings.jellyfin10_compat: " [tmdbid-ID]", or for a year-like ID (1900..=2099) " [imdbid-ttID]"
/// (movies) or " [tvdbid-ID]" (shows). None in exactly two cases: compat is off, or the ID is year-like and the IMDb (movie)
/// or TVDB (show) ID is absent; only the second makes the caller add compat_tag_omitted. It does not depend on the year. Def: T11. Use: T11.
pub fn compat_tag(work: &Work, settings: &Settings) -> Option<String>;
/// 1900..=2099. Def: T11. Use: T11.
pub fn year_like(id: i64) -> bool;
/// 8.9 sanitisation of one component: NFC; ':' to " -"; `/ \ | ? * " < >` and control characters removed; when
/// `strip_brackets`, `[ ] { }` removed (titles and edition names); spaces collapsed; leading spaces and periods dropped (no
/// component is a hidden dot-name; a choice beyond 8.9's list, Review Focus 10); trailing spaces and periods trimmed; a
/// reserved device name (case-insensitive, its stem before any extension) gets "_" appended to the stem; capped at 255 bytes
/// on a character boundary. Def: T11. Use: T11, T13.
pub fn sanitise(component: &str, strip_brackets: bool) -> String;
pub const RESERVED_NAMES: [&str; 30];
pub const COMPONENT_MAX_BYTES: usize = 255;
pub const EDITION_MAX_CHARS: usize = 32;
pub const EPISODE_TITLE_MAX_CHARS: usize = 90;

/// Def: T11. Use: T11, T13.
pub fn edition_label(name: &str) -> String;
/// 8.9's character rules with brackets removed (NFC, ':' to " -", forbidden and control characters, collapsed spaces), without
/// the component rules (reserved names, 255 bytes), then the first 90 characters, trailing spaces and periods trimmed (8.9).
/// Def: T11. Use: T11, T13.
pub fn episode_title(name: &str) -> String;
/// Components joined under `root` with '\\' when the root holds a backslash or starts with "\\\\", else '/'. Def: T11. Use: T11.
pub fn join(root: &str, components: &[String]) -> String;

// lazymkv_core::tracks::layout (Task 11; crates/core/src/tracks/layout.rs)
/// One track of the final file (8.10). Def: T11. Use: T12, T13, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct OutputTrack { pub stream: u32, pub kind: StreamKind, pub language: Option<String>, pub name: Option<String>, pub default: bool, pub forced: bool, pub hearing_impaired: bool, pub original: bool }

/// Def: T11. Use: T12, T13, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Layout { pub tracks: Vec<OutputTrack>, pub chapters_kept: bool }

/// decision's order with its flags and names, subtitles forced, regular, SDH with their scan language tag (none for a
/// no-language stream) and their names; every default flag explicit; `default_subtitle` applied; chapters kept. Def: T11.
/// Use: T13, T16.
pub fn layout(title: &Title, audio: &AudioDecision, subtitles: &SubtitleDecision) -> Layout;
```

And, not cross-task items: the private helpers listed under **Files**, each with its own doc comment in the code below.

Where this task settles what the spec and the interfaces leave open (each choice is pinned by a test below):

1. **The character rules and the component rules.** Spec 8.9 lists the rules for "every path component". The ones about characters (NFC, `:` to ` -`, the forbidden and control characters, the brackets of titles and edition names, collapsed spaces) apply to a title, an edition name or an episode title wherever it sits in a component; the ones about a component's end (trailing spaces and periods), reserved device names and the 255-byte cap apply to the whole component. So `movie_path` and `tv_path` clean the title with the private `clean` (through `title_within`, point 4) and then `sanitise` the built component: a period inside a component is kept (`Crazy, Stupid, Love. (2011) {tmdb-50646}`, pinned by `a_period_inside_a_component_is_kept`).
2. **`edition_label` and `episode_title` are `clean(name, true)`, cut, then trimmed of trailing spaces and periods**, as the shared interfaces say: the character rules without the component rules (reserved names, 255 bytes). `sanitise(name, true)` would differ only for a name that is exactly a device name, which it would turn into `Aux_` although the name never stands alone as a component (the component it ends up in, `Film (2010) {tmdb-12345} - 2160p Aux {edition-Aux}.mkv`, is not reserved). Pinned by `edition_label_never_appends_an_underscore_to_a_word_that_is_a_device_name`.
3. **Leading spaces and periods.** The space collapse also drops leading spaces (a title that begins with `:` would otherwise begin with a space); the spec names only trailing ones. `sanitise` also drops leading periods, a choice beyond 8.9's list for the owner to confirm (Review Focus 10): a name that begins with `.` is a hidden entry on the Linux NAS and under Samba's default `hide dot files`, and the servers' library scans skip hidden entries, so a title such as TMDb's `...And Justice for All` (1979) would file a film that neither library shows (R1). Both components go through `sanitise`, so the file name still begins with the folder name. The rule runs before the reserved-name rule (`.con` gives `con_`). Pinned by `leading_periods_are_dropped_so_no_component_is_hidden` and `a_leading_period_is_dropped_so_the_folder_is_not_hidden`.
4. **The 255-byte cap takes its bytes from the title, never from what follows it.** Spec 8.9 requires that a movie's file name begins with its folder name (the compat bullet, and D11's `<folder name> - <label>` versions), and the servers match on the `{tmdb-ID}` tag, so cutting a built component from its end is wrong. `movie_path` measures what follows the title in its longest component, the file name (` (Year) {tmdb-ID}[ compat]`, the edition style's parts, ` - <Res>[ n]` and `.mkv`); `tv_path` takes the larger of what follows the show's title in the show folder (` (Year) {tmdb-ID}[ compat]`) and in the file name up to the episode code (` (Year) - SNNENN[-ENN][ n]` and `.mkv`). The private `title_within` cuts the cleaned title to 255 bytes less that, on a character boundary (`cap_bytes`), and trims the trailing spaces and periods the cut leaves (an uncut title keeps its trailing period, point 1). Each built component is still capped at 255 bytes (the file name's stem at 251, so `.mkv` stays); for TV that cap takes the episode title from the end, the least needed part, which is already cut to 90 characters. A 300-character ASCII movie title keeps 227 characters (folder 243 bytes, file name 255), a title of 100 three-byte characters keeps 75, and a 300-character show title keeps 235; no TMDb title comes near that. Pinned by `a_long_title_is_cut_so_both_components_keep_their_tags_within_255_bytes` and `a_long_show_title_keeps_the_show_tag_and_the_episode_code`.
5. **Episode codes.** One episode is `S03E16`; two or more are the lowest and the highest number, `S03E12-E13` (spec 8.9's `S01E01-E02`; three episodes give `S01E01-E03`, the range form both servers read); an empty list writes the season code alone (`S03`), so `tv_path` never fails. The copy label goes after the episode code (`S03E16 2`), as the interfaces say; spec 11 shows only the movie form.
6. **An empty or blank edition is no edition**, and an episode title that cleans to nothing (`???`) is left out with its ` - `.
7. **The `compat_tag_omitted` note** names no stream and says `TMDb ID <id> reads as a year to Jellyfin 10.x and TMDb gives no IMDb ID: the compatibility tag is left out` (TVDB for a show); an IMDb ID that is an empty string counts as absent.
8. **`join`** adds no separator after a root that already ends in `/` or `\`, and joins under an empty root with `/` and no leading separator.
9. **The layout's tracks.** 3D video (attribute 6 containing `MVC`) is left out, as the job profile (`profile::ALL_TRACKS_SELECTION`, `-sel:mvcvideo`) and `reconcile::expected_rows` leave it out, so the layout matches the file `verify_final` checks; every other video stream is kept in scan order, the first with the default flag. Video and subtitle tracks never carry the original flag (8.6 step 5 sets it on audio). Every track is tagged the same way (8.10: "Every kept track has a language tag, except streams with no language"): video and subtitle tracks with attribute 3 of their scan stream, audio tracks with the decision's `AudioTrack.language` (Task 8's copy of attribute 3); no tag for a stream with no code, an empty code or `und` (8.6 "Languages": "A stream with no code or `und`" belongs to no language; `-` counts as no code), a no-language subtitle stream that 8.7 counted as English included (pinned by `subtitles_are_ordered_forced_regular_sdh_with_their_own_language_tag`). The tag follows 8.6's definition, not Task 8's grouping: `zxx`, `mul` and `mis` are ISO 639-2 codes that `mkvmerge` accepts, so they keep their tag although `lang::is_no_language` (the ported NO_LANGUAGE table) groups them with no language for the order (pinned by `a_no_language_audio_track_has_no_language_tag`). The audio name is the audio decision's `AudioTrack.name`, which Task 8 builds as `<display>[ <Atmos|DTS:X>] <layout>` and tests; the layout carries it unchanged, and its test gives names no builder would produce, so it tests the carrying and nothing of Task 8's rule.
10. **The default audio for the default-subtitle rule** is the kept audio track flagged default, else the first kept track; it is English when its code is `eng` or `en` (`lang::is_english`). A title with no kept audio, or whose default audio has no language, counts as not English, so the regular English track (else the SDH track, point 11) is default.
11. **`default_subtitle`** returns the forced track's stream when the default audio is English, and None when no forced track is kept (no subtitle is default). When the default audio is not English it returns the regular English track's stream, else the SDH track's. Spec 8.10 names only the regular track and leaves open the title whose only English dialogue track is SDH (a single dialogue track TheDiscDB describes as SDH, 8.7's description override): with None there, a Spanish film would play with Spanish audio and no English subtitles, against what the rule is for. The SDH fallback is a choice the owner may overturn: it awaits the owner's ruling, and Review Focus 9 of the plan's header carries the question. With only a forced track kept and other audio, no subtitle is default; the SDH track is never default beside a kept regular track. Pinned by `with_other_audio_and_no_regular_track_the_sdh_track_is_the_default_subtitle` and `with_other_audio_and_only_a_forced_track_no_subtitle_is_default`.
12. **`SubtitleTrack.default`** is not written back: `layout` takes the decisions by reference, and the default subtitle is in the `Layout`'s `OutputTrack.default`. The field stays false; the Layout is the one place that holds the default subtitle (the shared interfaces' doc of the field says so).
13. **Settings read**: `edition_style` (by `movie_path`) and `jellyfin10_compat` (by `compat_tag`, through `movie_path` and `tv_path`). Each is exercised at its default (`Combined`, off) and at every other value (`Plex`, `Jellyfin`; on).

```rust
/// The resolution label of spec 8.9, from the height of the first video track (`disc::Title::video_height`, the H of
/// attribute 19): 2000 or more is "2160p", 1000 or more "1080p", 700 or more "720p", exactly 576 "576p", anything
/// else "480p". Every movie file carries it (D11), so the 1080p disc of a combo pack files beside the 2160p copy.
pub fn resolution_label(height: u32) -> &'static str {
    if height >= 2000 {
        "2160p"
    } else if height >= 1000 {
        "1080p"
    } else if height >= 700 {
        "720p"
    } else if height == 576 {
        "576p"
    } else {
        "480p"
    }
}

```

```rust
/// The device names Windows reserves (spec 8.9 "a reserved device name gets `_` appended"), as Microsoft's "Naming
/// Files, Paths, and Namespaces" lists them: CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM0 to COM9, COM with a superscript 1, 2 or 3
/// (U+00B9, U+00B2, U+00B3), LPT0 to LPT9 and LPT with a superscript 1, 2 or 3. Compared ignoring ASCII case only, so
/// the superscript digits must match exactly.
pub const RESERVED_NAMES: [&str; 30] = [
    "CON", "PRN", "AUX", "NUL", "COM0", "COM1", "COM2", "COM3", "COM4", "COM5", "COM6", "COM7", "COM8", "COM9",
    "COM\u{b9}", "COM\u{b2}", "COM\u{b3}", "LPT0", "LPT1", "LPT2", "LPT3", "LPT4", "LPT5", "LPT6", "LPT7", "LPT8", "LPT9",
    "LPT\u{b9}", "LPT\u{b2}", "LPT\u{b3}",
];

/// Spec 8.9 "each component capped at 255 bytes": UTF-8 bytes, cut on a character boundary.
pub const COMPONENT_MAX_BYTES: usize = 255;

/// Spec 8.4: edition names are "capped at 32 characters" (Unicode scalar values, counted after NFC).
pub const EDITION_MAX_CHARS: usize = 32;

/// Spec 8.9 "Episode titles are cut to 90 characters" (Unicode scalar values, counted after NFC).
pub const EPISODE_TITLE_MAX_CHARS: usize = 90;

/// The characters spec 8.9 removes from every component.
const FORBIDDEN: [char; 8] = ['/', '\\', '|', '?', '*', '"', '<', '>'];

/// The characters spec 8.9 removes from titles and edition names.
const BRACKETS: [char; 4] = ['[', ']', '{', '}'];

/// Spec 8.9's sanitisation of one path component, in this order: Unicode NFC; `:` replaced by " -"; `/ \ | ? * " < >`
/// and control characters removed; with `strip_brackets` (a title or an edition name), `[ ] { }` removed; runs of
/// spaces collapsed to one; leading spaces and periods dropped (a name that begins with `.` is hidden on the NAS and
/// skipped by the servers' scans; a choice beyond 8.9's list); trailing spaces and periods trimmed; a reserved device name
/// (`RESERVED_NAMES`, judged on the stem before the first `.`, ignoring ASCII case and the stem's trailing spaces)
/// gets `_` appended to its stem (`con.mkv` gives `con_.mkv`); capped at COMPONENT_MAX_BYTES on a character boundary,
/// and trimmed again of the trailing spaces and periods the cap may leave.
pub fn sanitise(component: &str, strip_brackets: bool) -> String {
    sanitise_within(component, strip_brackets, COMPONENT_MAX_BYTES)
}

/// An edition name as spec 8.4 files it: "sanitised like titles and capped at 32 characters". The character rules of
/// `sanitise` with brackets removed, the first EDITION_MAX_CHARS characters, trailing spaces and periods trimmed. The
/// reserved-name rule is left to the component the name ends up in (an edition `Aux` stays `Aux`). `movie_path` takes
/// its edition through this function.
pub fn edition_label(name: &str) -> String {
    capped_text(name, EDITION_MAX_CHARS)
}

/// An episode title as spec 8.9 files it: the character rules of `sanitise` with brackets removed (a slash in
/// `Part One/Part Two` is removed), the first EPISODE_TITLE_MAX_CHARS characters, trailing spaces and
/// periods trimmed. `tv_path` takes its episode name through this function.
pub fn episode_title(name: &str) -> String {
    capped_text(name, EPISODE_TITLE_MAX_CHARS)
}

/// `sanitise` with a byte cap of `max_bytes`: the file name's stem is capped at 251 bytes so ".mkv" fits in 255.
fn sanitise_within(component: &str, strip_brackets: bool, max_bytes: usize) -> String {
    let cleaned = clean(component, strip_brackets);
    let visible = cleaned.trim_start_matches(|ch: char| ch == '.' || ch == ' ');
    let named = with_reserved_suffix(trim_end_spaces_and_periods(visible));
    trim_end_spaces_and_periods(cap_bytes(&named, max_bytes)).to_string()
}

/// `clean` with brackets removed, cut to `max_chars` characters, trailing spaces and periods trimmed before and after the cut.
fn capped_text(text: &str, max_chars: usize) -> String {
    let cleaned = clean(text, true);
    let cut = cap_chars(trim_end_spaces_and_periods(&cleaned), max_chars);
    trim_end_spaces_and_periods(cut).to_string()
}

/// The character rules of spec 8.9 on a piece of text: NFC, `:` to " -", the forbidden and control characters
/// removed, brackets removed when `strip_brackets`, runs of spaces collapsed, leading and trailing spaces dropped.
/// Periods are kept: only a component's end is trimmed of them.
fn clean(text: &str, strip_brackets: bool) -> String {
    let normalised: String = text.nfc().collect();
    let mut kept = String::with_capacity(normalised.len() + 8);
    for ch in normalised.chars() {
        if ch == ':' {
            kept.push_str(" -");
        } else if !(FORBIDDEN.contains(&ch) || ch.is_control() || (strip_brackets && BRACKETS.contains(&ch))) {
            kept.push(ch);
        }
    }
    collapse_spaces(&kept)
}

/// The words of `text` between spaces, joined by one space: runs of spaces collapsed, leading and trailing ones dropped.
fn collapse_spaces(text: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
    for word in text.split(' ').filter(|word| !word.is_empty()) {
        if !out.is_empty() {
            out.push(' ');
        }
        out.push_str(word);
    }
    out
}

/// `text` without its trailing spaces and periods.
fn trim_end_spaces_and_periods(text: &str) -> &str {
    text.trim_end_matches(|ch: char| ch == ' ' || ch == '.')
}

/// The longest prefix of `text` of at most `max_bytes` bytes that ends on a character boundary.
fn cap_bytes(text: &str, max_bytes: usize) -> &str {
    if text.len() <= max_bytes {
        return text;
    }
    let mut end = max_bytes;
    while !text.is_char_boundary(end) {
        end -= 1;
    }
    &text[..end]
}

/// The first `max_chars` characters of `text`.
fn cap_chars(text: &str, max_chars: usize) -> &str {
    match text.char_indices().nth(max_chars) {
        Some((end, _)) => &text[..end],
        None => text,
    }
}

/// `component` with `_` appended to its stem (the text before the first `.`, without trailing spaces) when the stem is
/// a reserved device name; otherwise unchanged.
fn with_reserved_suffix(component: &str) -> String {
    let (stem, rest) = match component.find('.') {
        Some(dot) => component.split_at(dot),
        None => (component, ""),
    };
    let stem = stem.trim_end_matches(' ');
    if RESERVED_NAMES.iter().any(|name| name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(stem)) {
        format!("{stem}_{rest}")
    } else {
        component.to_string()
    }
}
```

```rust
/// Spec 8.9: "Jellyfin 10.x reads a number between 1900 and 2099 as a year", so such a TMDb ID cannot be its tag.
pub fn year_like(id: i64) -> bool {
    (1900..=2099).contains(&id)
}

/// Spec 8.9's second ID tag, with its leading space, when settings.jellyfin10_compat is on: " [tmdbid-<TMDb ID>]";
/// for a year-like TMDb ID, " [imdbid-<IMDb ID>]" for a movie (the IMDb ID as TMDb gives it, "tt0004242") or
/// " [tvdbid-<TVDB ID>]" for a show. None in exactly two cases: compat is off, or the ID is year-like and the IMDb
/// (movie) or TVDB (show) ID is absent or empty; only the second makes `movie_path` and `tv_path` add the note
/// compat_tag_omitted. The year plays no part. Reads settings.jellyfin10_compat.
pub fn compat_tag(work: &Work, settings: &Settings) -> Option<String> {
    if !settings.jellyfin10_compat {
        return None;
    }
    if !year_like(work.tmdb_id) {
        return Some(format!(" [tmdbid-{}]", work.tmdb_id));
    }
    match work.kind {
        TmdbKind::Movie => work.imdb_id.as_deref().filter(|id| !id.is_empty()).map(|id| format!(" [imdbid-{id}]")),
        TmdbKind::Tv => work.tvdb_id.map(|id| format!(" [tvdbid-{id}]")),
    }
}

```

```rust
                "Film (2010) {tmdb-12345} [tmdbid-12345] - 2160p Extended Cut {edition-Extended Cut}.mkv",
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            path.path,
            r"\\unas-pro\media\Movies\Film (2010) {tmdb-12345} [tmdbid-12345]\Film (2010) {tmdb-12345} [tmdbid-12345] - 2160p Extended Cut {edition-Extended Cut}.mkv"
        );
        assert!(path.components[1].starts_with(&path.components[0]));
        assert!(notes.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_compat_tag_sits_right_after_the_tmdb_tag_in_every_style() {
        let edition = Some("Extended Cut");
        let (plex, _) = movie_path(MOVIES, &film(), "2160p", edition, None, &styled(EditionStyle::Plex, true));
        assert_eq!(

            [
                "Film (2010) {tmdb-12345} [tmdbid-12345] {edition-Extended Cut}",

        );

        assert_eq!(

            ["Film (2010) {tmdb-12345} [tmdbid-12345]", "Film (2010) {tmdb-12345} [tmdbid-12345] - 2160p Extended Cut.mkv"]
        );

        let work = movie(1999, "Film", Some(2010), Some("tt1234567"));

        assert_eq!(
            parts(&path),
            ["Film (2010) {tmdb-1999} [imdbid-tt1234567]", "Film (2010) {tmdb-1999} [imdbid-tt1234567] - 1080p.mkv"]
        );

    #[test]
    fn a_year_like_movie_id_without_an_imdb_id_omits_the_tag_with_a_note() {
        let work = movie(1999, "Film", Some(2010), None);
        let (path, notes) = movie_path(MOVIES, &work, "1080p", None, None, &styled(EditionStyle::Combined, true));
        assert_eq!(parts(&path), ["Film (2010) {tmdb-1999}", "Film (2010) {tmdb-1999} - 1080p.mkv"]);
        assert_eq!(
            notes,

                note: Note::CompatTagOmitted,

        assert_eq!(parts(&path), ["Film (2010) {tmdb-1999}", "Film (2010) {tmdb-1999} - 1080p.mkv"]);
        assert!(notes.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_movie_title_is_sanitised_in_both_components() {

    #[test]
    fn a_period_inside_a_component_is_kept() {

    #[test]
    fn a_long_title_is_cut_so_both_components_keep_their_tags_within_255_bytes() {
        let long = movie(1, &"A".repeat(300), Some(2000), None);
        let (path, _) = movie_path("/srv/media/Movies", &long, "1080p", None, None, &Settings::default());
        let folder = format!("{} (2000) {{tmdb-1}}", "A".repeat(227));
        assert_eq!(path.components, [folder.clone(), format!("{folder} - 1080p.mkv")]);
        assert_eq!(path.components[0].len(), 243);
        assert_eq!(path.components[1].len(), 255);
        assert!(path.components[1].starts_with(&path.components[0]));
        assert!(path.components[1].ends_with(" - 1080p.mkv"));
        assert_eq!(path.path, format!("/srv/media/Movies/{folder}/{folder} - 1080p.mkv"));
        let wide = movie(1, &"\u{65e5}".repeat(100), Some(2000), None);
        let (path, _) = movie_path("/srv/media/Movies", &wide, "1080p", None, None, &Settings::default());
        let folder = format!("{} (2000) {{tmdb-1}}", "\u{65e5}".repeat(75));
        assert_eq!(path.components, [folder.clone(), format!("{folder} - 1080p.mkv")]);
        assert_eq!(path.components[1].len(), 253);
    }
```

In `crates/core/src/naming.rs`, find the line
