```rust
/// The final file's extension; the 255-byte cap of a file name keeps it.
const EXTENSION: &str = ".mkv";

/// A final path (spec 8.9) as sanitised components under a library root, and the components joined under the root
/// with the root's own separator (`join`). Task 13 puts it in the `FileDecision`; phase 2 files to `path`.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct NamedPath {
    /// The library root as the settings give it (`movies_root` or `tv_root`), unchanged.
    pub root: String,
    /// The components under the root, each through `sanitise`, in order: the work's folder (and for TV the season
    /// folder), then the file name.
    pub components: Vec<String>,
    /// `join(root, components)`.
    pub path: String,
}

/// The components joined under `root`: with '\\' when the root holds a backslash (a drive path `D:\Media` or a UNC
/// path `\\server\share`, which starts with two), else with '/'; no separator is added after a root that already ends
/// in one, and under an empty root the components are joined with '/' without a leading separator. `core` never asks
/// the host which separator it uses (spec 8.9's paths are the share's).
pub fn join(root: &str, components: &[String]) -> String {
    let separator = if root.contains('\\') { '\\' } else { '/' };
    let mut path = root.to_string();
    for component in components {
        if !path.is_empty() && !path.ends_with('/') && !path.ends_with('\\') {
            path.push(separator);
        }
        path.push_str(component);
    }
    path
}

/// Spec 8.9's movie path under `root` (settings.movies_root): the folder `Title (Year) {tmdb-ID}[ compat]` and the
/// file `Title (Year) {tmdb-ID}[ compat] - <Res>[ <n>]`, laid out by settings.edition_style when `edition` is given:
/// Combined appends ` <Ed> {edition-<Ed>}` to the file name; Plex appends ` {edition-<Ed>}` to the folder and the file
/// name before ` - <Res>`; Jellyfin appends ` <Ed>` to the file name. `work` is the TMDb record's Work (title, year and
/// ID from one record); `resolution` is `resolution_label`'s; `edition` is already through `edition_label` (8.4), and
/// None, empty or blank means no edition; a year of None writes no " (Year)"; `copy` Some(n) appends " n" after the
/// resolution label (`- 2160p 2`, spec 11 "Resolve collision", keep both). The compat tag is `compat_tag`'s, in both
/// components; when compat is on and the tag cannot be built, the note compat_tag_omitted is returned. The title goes
/// through the character rules with brackets removed and is cut by `title_within` so that the file name, the longer
/// component, fits in 255 bytes with everything after the title: the file name always begins with the folder name and
/// keeps its tags and labels. Each component then goes through `sanitise`. Reads settings.edition_style and
/// settings.jellyfin10_compat.
pub fn movie_path(
    root: &str,
    work: &Work,
    resolution: &str,
    edition: Option<&str>,
    copy: Option<u32>,
    settings: &Settings,
) -> (NamedPath, Vec<Noted>) {
    let mut notes = Vec::new();
    let tag = compat_or_note(work, settings, &mut notes);
    // ` (Year) {tmdb-ID}[ compat]`: what follows the title in both components.
    let tagged = format!("{} {{tmdb-{}}}{tag}", year_suffix(work), work.tmdb_id);
    let label = match copy {
        Some(n) => format!("{resolution} {n}"),
        None => resolution.to_string(),
    };
    let edition = edition.map(str::trim).filter(|name| !name.is_empty());
    // What follows the title in the folder and in the file name's stem.
    let (folder, stem) = match (edition, settings.edition_style) {
        (None, _) => (tagged.clone(), format!("{tagged} - {label}")),
        (Some(name), EditionStyle::Combined) => (tagged.clone(), format!("{tagged} - {label} {name} {{edition-{name}}}")),
        (Some(name), EditionStyle::Plex) => {
            let folder = format!("{tagged} {{edition-{name}}}");
            let stem = format!("{folder} - {label}");
            (folder, stem)
        }
        (Some(name), EditionStyle::Jellyfin) => (tagged.clone(), format!("{tagged} - {label} {name}")),
    };
    let title = title_within(&work.title, stem.len() + EXTENSION.len());
    let components = vec![sanitise(&format!("{title}{folder}"), false), file_name(&format!("{title}{stem}"))];
    (named(root, components), notes)
}

/// `compat_tag`'s tag, or "" with the note compat_tag_omitted pushed when compat is on and the tag cannot be built
/// (a year-like TMDb ID without an IMDb ID for a movie or a TVDB ID for a show; spec 8.9).
fn compat_or_note(work: &Work, settings: &Settings, notes: &mut Vec<Noted>) -> String {
    if let Some(tag) = compat_tag(work, settings) {
        return tag;
    }
    if settings.jellyfin10_compat {
        let other = match work.kind {
            TmdbKind::Movie => "IMDb",
            TmdbKind::Tv => "TVDB",
        };
        notes.push(Noted {
            note: Note::CompatTagOmitted,
            stream: None,
            detail: format!(
                "TMDb ID {} reads as a year to Jellyfin 10.x and TMDb gives no {other} ID: the compatibility tag is left out",
                work.tmdb_id
            ),
        });
    }
    String::new()
}

/// " (Year)", or "" for a work without a year: what follows the title in `Title (Year)` (spec 8.9).
fn year_suffix(work: &Work) -> String {
    match work.year {
        Some(year) => format!(" ({year})"),
        None => String::new(),
    }
}

/// The work's title through the character rules with brackets removed (its periods kept; only a component's end is
/// trimmed), cut on a character boundary so that `suffix_bytes` more bytes still fit in COMPONENT_MAX_BYTES; a title the
/// cut shortens is trimmed of the trailing spaces and periods the cut leaves. The caller passes the bytes that follow the
/// title in its longest component, so spec 8.9's 255-byte cap takes bytes from the title and never from the ID tags, the
/// labels or the episode code after it.
fn title_within(title: &str, suffix_bytes: usize) -> String {
    let cleaned = clean(title, true);
    let budget = COMPONENT_MAX_BYTES.saturating_sub(suffix_bytes);
    if cleaned.len() <= budget {
        return cleaned;
    }
    trim_end_spaces_and_periods(cap_bytes(&cleaned, budget)).to_string()
}

/// A file name: the stem sanitised within 255 bytes less the extension's 4, then ".mkv".
fn file_name(stem: &str) -> String {
    format!("{}{EXTENSION}", sanitise_within(stem, false, COMPONENT_MAX_BYTES - EXTENSION.len()))
}

/// The NamedPath of `components` under `root`.
fn named(root: &str, components: Vec<String>) -> NamedPath {
    let path = join(root, &components);
    NamedPath { root: root.to_string(), components, path }
}
```

```rust
/// Spec 8.9's TV path under `root` (settings.tv_root): the show folder `Show (Year) {tmdb-ID}[ compat]`, the season
/// folder `Season NN` (season 0 is `Season 00`, the specials), and the file `Show (Year) - SNNENN[-ENN][ <n>][ - Episode
/// Title]`. One episode writes `S03E16`; two or more write the lowest and the highest (`S03E12-E13`, 8.9's
/// multi-episode form); an empty list writes the season code alone. The compat tag (`compat_tag`) is on the show
/// folder only, never on the season folder or the file, with the note compat_tag_omitted when compat is on and the
/// tag cannot be built. `episode_name` goes through `episode_title`; when it is None or cleans to nothing, the title
/// and its " - " are left out. `copy` Some(n) appends " n" after the episode code (spec 11 "Resolve collision", keep
/// both). A year of None writes no " (Year)". The show's title is cut by `title_within` so that the show folder and the
/// file name up to its episode code fit in 255 bytes; the file name's own cap then takes any excess from the episode
/// title at its end. Reads settings.jellyfin10_compat.
pub fn tv_path(
    root: &str,
    work: &Work,
    season: u32,
    episodes: &[u32],
    episode_name: Option<&str>,
    copy: Option<u32>,
    settings: &Settings,
) -> (NamedPath, Vec<Noted>) {
    let mut notes = Vec::new();
    let tag = compat_or_note(work, settings, &mut notes);
    let year = year_suffix(work);
    // What follows the show's title in the show folder, and in the file name up to the episode title.
    let folder = format!("{year} {{tmdb-{}}}{tag}", work.tmdb_id);
    let mut code = format!("{year} - {}", episode_code(season, episodes));
    if let Some(n) = copy {
        code = format!("{code} {n}");
    }
    let show = title_within(&work.title, folder.len().max(code.len() + EXTENSION.len()));
    let season_folder = format!("Season {season:02}");
    let mut stem = format!("{show}{code}");
    if let Some(name) = episode_name.map(episode_title).filter(|name| !name.is_empty()) {
        stem = format!("{stem} - {name}");
    }
    let components = vec![sanitise(&format!("{show}{folder}"), false), sanitise(&season_folder, false), file_name(&stem)];
    (named(root, components), notes)
}

/// `SNNENN` for one episode, `SNNENN-ENN` from the lowest to the highest of two or more, `SNN` for none (spec 8.9).
fn episode_code(season: u32, episodes: &[u32]) -> String {
    match (episodes.iter().min(), episodes.iter().max()) {
        (Some(first), Some(last)) if first != last => format!("S{season:02}E{first:02}-E{last:02}"),
        (Some(first), _) => format!("S{season:02}E{first:02}"),
        _ => format!("S{season:02}"),
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Track metadata in the final file (design spec 8.10): the file's tracks in order (video as the scan lists it,
//! audio in 8.6's order, subtitles forced, regular, SDH), each with its language tag and name and the four flags
//! `mkvmerge` sets (default, forced, hearing-impaired, original), every default flag explicit, the default-subtitle
//! rule, and chapters kept. Pure (RP19): it reads the scan's title and the decisions of Tasks 8 (audio) and 10
//! (subtitles). Written from the spec (RP20). Task 12's `verify_final` checks a partial file against the layout,
//! Task 13 puts it in the `FileDecision`, Task 16 prints it.

use crate::disc::{StreamKind, Title};
use crate::lang::is_english;
use crate::tracks::audio::AudioDecision;
use crate::tracks::subtitle::SubtitleDecision;

#[cfg(test)]

    use super::*;

    use crate::tracks::subtitle::{SubtitleCase, SubtitleTrack};
    use serde_json::Value;

    /// MakeMKV's attributes 5, 6 and 7 for the fixtures' codecs.
    const HEVC: (&str, &str, &str) = ("V_MPEGH/ISO/HEVC", "MpegH", "MpegH HEVC Main10@L5.1");
    const HEVC_ENHANCEMENT: (&str, &str, &str) =
        ("V_MPEGH/ISO/HEVC", "MpegH", "MpegH HEVC Main10@L5.1 (dvhe.07.06 BL+FEL+RPU)");
    const AVC: (&str, &str, &str) = ("V_MPEG4/ISO/AVC", "Mpeg4", "Mpeg4 AVC High@L4.1");
    const MVC: (&str, &str, &str) = ("V_MPEG4/ISO/MVC", "Mpeg4 MVC", "Mpeg4 MVC High@L4.1");
    const TRUEHD_ATMOS: (&str, &str, &str) = ("A_TRUEHD", "TrueHD", "TrueHD Atmos");
    const DTS_HD_MA: (&str, &str, &str) = ("A_DTS", "DTS-HD MA", "DTS-HD Master Audio");
    const AC3: (&str, &str, &str) = ("A_AC3", "DD", "Dolby Digital");
    const PGS: (&str, &str, &str) = ("S_HDMV/PGS", "PGS", "HDMV PGS Subtitles");

    /// A scan stream with only the attributes the layout reads (kind, language, codec).
    fn stream(number: u32, kind: StreamKind, language: Option<&str>, (id, short, long): (&str, &str, &str)) -> Stream {
        Stream {
            number,
            kind,
            name: None,
            language: language.map(str::to_string),
            codec: codec(id, short, long),
            codec_id: id.to_string(),
            codec_short: short.to_string(),
            codec_long: long.to_string(),
            bitrate_text: None,
            bitrate_kbps: None,
            channels: None,
            sample_rate: None,
            sample_size: None,
            video_size: None,
            flags: Flags::default(),
            tree_info: None,
            layout_name: None,
            output_codec: None,
            conversion: None,
        }
    }

    /// Title 0 with `chapters` chapters and `streams`.
    fn title(chapters: u32, streams: Vec<Stream>) -> Title {
        Title {
            number: 0,
            name: None,
            chapters,
            seconds: Some(7140),
            size: None,
            source_file: Some("00800.mpls".to_string()),
            dvd_title: None,
            segment_count: None,
            segment_map: String::new(),
            segments: Vec::new(),
            truncated: false,
            output_name: None,
            comment: None,
            streams,
        }
    }

    /// A kept audio track named `name`: the layout copies the name the audio decision gives (Task 8 builds it as 8.10's
    /// "<display>[ <Atmos|DTS:X>] <layout>" and tests that rule), so the fixtures give it.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    fn audio_track(
        stream: u32,
        language: Option<&str>,
        group: LangGroup,
        (id, short, long): (&str, &str, &str),
        channels: u32,
        name: &str,
        default: bool,
        original: bool,
    ) -> AudioTrack {
        let codec = codec(id, short, long);
        let object = codec.object;
        AudioTrack {
            stream,
            language: language.map(str::to_string),
            group,
            codec,
            channels,
            tier: None,
            object,
            sample_size: None,
            sample_rate: None,
            bitrate_kbps: None,
            first_of_language: true,
            name: name.to_string(),
            default,
            original,
        }
    }

    /// An audio decision keeping `kept` in that order.
    fn audio(kept: Vec<AudioTrack>) -> AudioDecision {
        let reference = kept.first().map(|track| track.stream);
        AudioDecision {
            kept,
            dropped: Vec::new(),
            reference,
            verdict_reference: None,
            notes: Vec::new(),
            reviews: Vec::new(),
            confidence: 0.95,
            description_alignment: None,
        }
    }

    /// A kept subtitle track in `role`, flagged and named as 8.7 says.
    fn subtitle(stream: u32, role: SubtitleRole) -> SubtitleTrack {
        SubtitleTrack {
            stream,
            role,
            name: role.name().to_string(),
            forced: role == SubtitleRole::Forced,
            hearing_impaired: role == SubtitleRole::Sdh,
            default: false,
            events: Some(if role == SubtitleRole::Forced { 40 } else { 1200 }),
            closed_captions: false,
            parent: None,
            decided_by: "count".to_string(),
        }
    }

    /// A subtitle decision keeping `kept` in that order.
    fn subtitles(kept: Vec<SubtitleTrack>) -> SubtitleDecision {
        SubtitleDecision {
            kept,
            dropped: Vec::new(),
            set_aside: Vec::new(),
            full: Vec::new(),
            groups: Vec::new(),
            dialogue_group: None,
            dialogue_pick: None,
            pairs: Vec::new(),
            case: SubtitleCase::Alignment,
            confidence: 0.85,
            notes: Vec::new(),
            reviews: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// A Spanish film: video, Spanish TrueHD Atmos, English DTS-HD MA and Dolby Digital, three English PGS streams.
    fn film_title() -> Title {
        title(
            16,
            vec![
                stream(0, StreamKind::Video, None, HEVC),
                stream(1, StreamKind::Audio, Some("spa"), TRUEHD_ATMOS),
                stream(2, StreamKind::Audio, Some("eng"), DTS_HD_MA),
                stream(3, StreamKind::Audio, Some("eng"), AC3),
                stream(4, StreamKind::Subtitles, Some("eng"), PGS),
                stream(5, StreamKind::Subtitles, Some("eng"), PGS),
                stream(6, StreamKind::Subtitles, Some("eng"), PGS),
            ],
        )
    }

    /// The film's audio as 8.6 step 5 orders it with original_language_first on: Spanish first (default, original),
    /// then English.
    fn film_audio() -> AudioDecision {
        audio(vec![
            audio_track(1, Some("spa"), LangGroup::Original, TRUEHD_ATMOS, 8, "TrueHD Atmos 7.1", true, true),
            audio_track(2, Some("eng"), LangGroup::English, DTS_HD_MA, 6, "DTS-HD MA 5.1", false, false),
            audio_track(3, Some("eng"), LangGroup::English, AC3, 2, "Dolby Digital 2.0", false, false),
        ])
    }

    /// The film's subtitles: stream 5 forced, 4 regular, 6 SDH.
    fn film_subtitles() -> SubtitleDecision {
        subtitles(vec![
            subtitle(5, SubtitleRole::Forced),
            subtitle(4, SubtitleRole::Regular),
            subtitle(6, SubtitleRole::Sdh),

    }

    /// One English audio track at `stream`, default and original (an English work).
    fn english_audio(stream: u32) -> AudioDecision {

    }

    /// (stream, default) of a layout's subtitle tracks, in file order.
    fn subtitle_defaults(layout: &Layout) -> Vec<(u32, bool)> {

            .tracks
            .iter()
            .filter(|track| track.kind == StreamKind::Subtitles)
            .map(|track| (track.stream, track.default))

    }

        assert_eq!(subtitle_defaults(&got), vec![(5, true), (4, false), (6, false)]);
        let spanish_flagged = audio(vec![
            audio_track(2, Some("eng"), LangGroup::English, DTS_HD_MA, 6, "DTS-HD MA 5.1", false, false),
            audio_track(1, Some("spa"), LangGroup::Original, TRUEHD_ATMOS, 8, "TrueHD Atmos 7.1", true, true),
        ]);
        let got = layout(&film_title(), &spanish_flagged, &film_subtitles());
        assert_eq!(subtitle_defaults(&got), vec![(5, false), (4, true), (6, false)]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_track_carries_an_explicit_default_flag() {
        let value = serde_json::to_value(layout(&film_title(), &film_audio(), &film_subtitles())).unwrap();
        let tracks = value["tracks"].as_array().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(tracks.len(), 7);
        for track in tracks {
            assert!(matches!(track["default"], Value::Bool(_)), "{track}");
        }
        let defaults = tracks.iter().filter(|track| track["default"] == Value::Bool(true)).count();
        assert_eq!(defaults, 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn chapters_are_kept() {
        assert!(layout(&film_title(), &film_audio(), &film_subtitles()).chapters_kept);
        let unchaptered = title(0, vec![stream(0, StreamKind::Video, None, HEVC)]);
        assert!(layout(&unchaptered, &audio(Vec::new()), &subtitles(Vec::new())).chapters_kept);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_layout_serialises_with_its_field_order_and_round_trips() {
        let one = Layout {
            tracks: vec![OutputTrack {
                stream: 4,
                kind: StreamKind::Subtitles,
                language: Some("eng".to_string()),
                name: Some("English (SDH)".to_string()),
                default: false,
                forced: false,
                hearing_impaired: true,
                original: false,
            }],
            chapters_kept: true,
        };
        let text = serde_json::to_string(&one).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            text,
            r#"{"tracks":[{"stream":4,"kind":"subtitles","language":"eng","name":"English (SDH)","default":false,"forced":false,"hearing_impaired":true,"original":false}],"chapters_kept":true}"#
        );
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<Layout>(&text).unwrap(), one);
    }
}
```

```rust
/// One track of the final file (spec 8.10), with the values `mkvmerge` writes for it.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct OutputTrack {
    /// The scan stream (0-based, within the title) the track comes from.
    pub stream: u32,
    /// Video, audio or subtitles.
    pub kind: StreamKind,
    /// The language tag (8.10): attribute 3 of the scan stream (for audio, the decision's copy of it); no tag for a stream
    /// with no code, an empty code or "und" (8.6 "Languages"; "-" counts as no code). "zxx", "mul" and "mis" keep their tag.
    pub language: Option<String>,
    /// The track name: None for video, the audio decision's name ("TrueHD Atmos 7.1"), the subtitle role's name
    /// ("English (Forced)", "English", "English (SDH)").
    pub name: Option<String>,
    /// The default flag, always written: the first video track, the audio decision's default track, and
    /// `default_subtitle`'s track.
    pub default: bool,
    /// The forced flag: the forced subtitle track only.
    pub forced: bool,
    /// The hearing-impaired flag: the SDH subtitle track only.
    pub hearing_impaired: bool,
    /// The original flag: the audio tracks 8.6 step 5 marks original.
    pub original: bool,
}

/// The final file's tracks and chapters (spec 8.10).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Layout {
    /// Video, then audio, then subtitles.
    pub tracks: Vec<OutputTrack>,
    /// 8.10 "Chapters are kept": always true.
    pub chapters_kept: bool,
}

/// Spec 8.10: the video streams as the scan lists them (a Dolby Vision enhancement layer kept as MakeMKV outputs it;
/// 3D video, attribute 6 containing "MVC", left out as the job profile leaves it out), the first with the default
/// flag; the audio tracks in the decision's order with its names and its default and original flags; the subtitle
/// tracks forced, regular, SDH (a stable sort by role), each tagged with attribute 3 of its scan stream (no tag for a
/// stream with no language, though 8.7 counted it as English: 8.10 "except streams with no language"), with their
/// names, forced and hearing-impaired flags, and the default flag on `default_subtitle`'s track. The default audio is the kept track flagged default, else the
/// first kept track; it is English when `lang::is_english` holds for its code, and a title without audio, or whose
/// default audio has no language, counts as not English. Every flag is explicit (8.10: MakeMKV sets its own);
/// chapters are kept.
pub fn layout(title: &Title, audio: &AudioDecision, subtitles: &SubtitleDecision) -> Layout {
    let mut tracks = Vec::new();
    let video = title.streams_of(StreamKind::Video).into_iter().filter(|stream| !stream.codec_short.contains("MVC"));
    for (position, stream) in video.enumerate() {
        tracks.push(OutputTrack {
            stream: stream.number,
            kind: StreamKind::Video,
            language: language_tag(stream.language.as_deref()),
            name: None,
            default: position == 0,
            forced: false,
            hearing_impaired: false,
            original: false,
        });
    }
    for track in &audio.kept {
        tracks.push(OutputTrack {
            stream: track.stream,
            kind: StreamKind::Audio,
            language: language_tag(track.language.as_deref()),
            name: Some(track.name.clone()),
            default: track.default,
            forced: false,
            hearing_impaired: false,
            original: track.original,
        });
    }
    let default = default_subtitle(default_audio_is_english(audio), subtitles);
    let mut kept: Vec<_> = subtitles.kept.iter().collect();
    kept.sort_by_key(|track| track.role);
    for track in kept {
        tracks.push(OutputTrack {
            stream: track.stream,
            kind: StreamKind::Subtitles,
            language: language_tag(
                title.streams.iter().find(|stream| stream.number == track.stream).and_then(|stream| stream.language.as_deref()),
            ),
            name: Some(track.name.clone()),
            default: default == Some(track.stream),
            forced: track.forced,
            hearing_impaired: track.hearing_impaired,
            original: false,
        });
    }
    Layout { tracks, chapters_kept: true }
}

/// Spec 8.10's default subtitle: the forced track when the default audio is English; when it is not, the regular
/// English track, or the SDH track when no regular track is kept (the forced track is then not default). 8.10 names
/// only the regular track; the SDH fallback serves the title whose only English dialogue track is SDH, and is a choice
/// the owner may overturn. None when the track the rule names does not exist.
pub fn default_subtitle(default_audio_is_english: bool, subtitles: &SubtitleDecision) -> Option<u32> {
    let kept = |role: SubtitleRole| subtitles.kept.iter().find(|track| track.role == role).map(|track| track.stream);
    if default_audio_is_english {
        kept(SubtitleRole::Forced)
    } else {
        kept(SubtitleRole::Regular).or_else(|| kept(SubtitleRole::Sdh))
    }
}

/// A stream's language tag: None for a stream with no language as 8.6 "Languages" defines it ("A stream with no code or
/// `und`"; an empty code or "-" counts as no code), else its code. Independent of Task 8's grouping by
/// `lang::is_no_language`: "zxx", "mul" and "mis" are ISO 639-2 codes `mkvmerge` accepts, and they keep their tag.
fn language_tag(code: Option<&str>) -> Option<String> {
    match code {
        None => None,
        Some(code) if code.is_empty() || code == "-" || code.eq_ignore_ascii_case("und") => None,
        Some(code) => Some(code.to_string()),
    }
}

/// Whether the file's default audio track is English: the kept track flagged default, else the first kept track.
fn default_audio_is_english(audio: &AudioDecision) -> bool {
    audio
        .kept
        .iter()
        .find(|track| track.default)
        .or_else(|| audio.kept.first())
        .and_then(|track| track.language.as_deref())
        .is_some_and(is_english)
}
```

Where this task settles what the spec and the interfaces leave open (each choice is pinned by a test below):

1. **The ordered match is position by position.** Spec 6.2 step 7 asks for "an ordered match on type, output codec (attributes 41 and 42), language and channels" and open point 22 says every expected track must pair in order and no extra file track is tolerated. `verify_rip` and `verify_final` pair the expected track at position i with the file's track at position i: `pairs` holds `(stream, Some(track id))` for every position the file has, `(stream, None)` past the file's last track, and every file track past the last expected one is in `extra_tracks`. A pair whose fields differ is still recorded (its sentences say why), so on a report whose `tracks_ok` is false the pairs are positions, not matches: `stream_of_track` returns None there for every track id, and `subs_streams` and `subtitle_events`, built on it, map no file track to a scan stream. The guard is in `core`, so no caller (Tasks 16 and 18) can attach packet MD5s, ffprobe profiles or subtitle events to the wrong scan stream of a rip whose tracks do not match the scan; a report that fails only on duration or chapters still maps its tracks.
2. **One sentence per difference, in a fixed form.** Track sentences come first, in track order, then the duration, then the chapters: `track <id>: type expected <kind>, file <type>` (a wrong type is reported alone, since its other fields mean nothing), `track <id>: codec expected <names joined by " or ">, file <codec>`, `track <id>: language expected <norm_lang>, file <norm_lang>`, `track <id>: channels expected <n>, file <n or none>`, `stream <n> (<kind>): missing from the file`, `track <id>: not expected (<type> <codec>)`, `duration: expected <expected> s, file <file to one decimal> s` (`5400 s`, `5320.0 s`, as the interfaces' example), `duration: the scan gives no duration (attribute 9)`, `chapters: expected <n>, file <n>`, `tracks: the scan predicts no track for this title` (`verify_rip`); `verify_final` adds `track <id>: name expected <name or none>, file <name or none>` and `track <id>: <default|forced|hearing_impaired|original> expected <bool>, file <bool>`, and for an empty layout says `tracks: the layout keeps no track` (6.4 step 14's expected tracks are the decision's layout, not the scan's).
3. **Attribute 41.** "Text" makes the stream `text_converted` with codec `SubRip/SRT` (6.2 step 7). Any other attribute 41 value is read as a MakeMKV codec ID through `codec::codec(value, "", "")` and its `mkvmerge_names` (for example `A_FLAC` gives `FLAC`); no recording shows such a value, so the test marks it "not seen". Attribute 42 alone never changes the expected codec: every recorded stream without attribute 41 has 42 `( Lossless conversion )` and arrives in its input codec.
4. **A codec the table does not know** (`Family::Unknown`) has no mkvmerge name, so its stream never verifies and the sentence says `codec expected (none known)`; the second failure raises `verify_failed` and the owner sees it, rather than a file passing unchecked. Pinned with a DTS Express stream (Task 1's Unknown `A_DTS` row: an `A_DTS` whose attributes 6 and 7 the table does not know), not seen in a recording. VC-1 video (`V_MS/VFW/WVC1`) is not such a codec: it is Task 1's family `Vc1` (ruling RP26, interfaces Open point 34), expects mkvmerge's documented name `VC-1` (not yet seen in a recording) and verifies against it; the same test pins that contrast with a VC-1 stream.
5. **MSG:4047 numbers count every selected stream**, including a stream `reconcile::expected_rows` keeps without attribute 1, which `disc::Title` leaves out (no recorded scan has one). Such a stream is never expected, but it still takes its number, so a removal after it names the right stream.
6. **What makes a report `ok`.** `duration_ok && chapters_ok && tracks_ok`. Read errors never fail verification (6.2 step 7: the title "is kept and adds the review reason `read_errors`"), and MSG:4047 indices beyond the selection are listed in `unknown_removed` without failing it, as `reconcile` lists them. A title without attribute 9 fails on duration; an empty prediction (`verify_rip`) or an empty layout (`verify_final`) never verifies.
7. **`verify_final`** compares the language on every track but video (MakeMKV and mkvmerge write `eng` or `und` on a video track and the layout carries none; 8.10 sets no video language), the name (`track_name`) on every track, the four flags with an absent property counting as false, and the duration with the 2 s band only (the source is the staged file, not the scan, so no DVD band). It checks no chapter count: 6.4 step 14 names the tracks and the duration, and `Layout` carries only `chapters_kept`; its report has `chapters_ok` true and both counts equal to the file's first edition's. Known limitation (interfaces Open point 37): 6.4 step 14 asks the file to "match the decision exactly" and 8.10 says "Chapters are kept", but `Layout` carries no chapter count, codec or channels, so a remux that drops the chapters, or that swaps two same-language audio tracks sharing a name, passes `verify_final`; phase 2's remux verification adds the staged file's chapter count (from `verify_rip`'s `file_chapters`) as an input. This task does not change the interface.
8. **`selected_streams`** refuses a title the scan has no TINFO line for (`the scan lists no title <n>`, `Disc::title`'s sentence) and passes `expected_rows`' refusal of a malformed attribute 22 through unchanged.
9. **`read_errors`** keys by the third parameter's text (the offset), keeps the first line's first parameter (the `%1` error text) and counts the lines; a MSG:2003 line without parameters is still counted, under offset `""` with message `""`, so a read error is never lost. MSG:2023 (a count of read errors of one type, 9.4 "seen but not acted on") is not a read error here.
10. **`caption_first`** places the text tracks after the last audio track, else after the last video track, else first; the other tracks and the text tracks each keep their order.
11. **`subtitle_events`** reads `index.json` as `align::index_streams` does (UTF-8 with a byte-order mark allowed, invalid bytes replaced) and each packets file strictly through `align::load_packets`; it reads only the entries `subs_streams` maps, so a packets file of an unmapped entry may be absent. Both readings are pinned by `subtitle_events_read_the_index_leniently_and_each_packets_file_strictly`. A packets file that exists but does not decode is refused with its path before the decode error, so the caller knows which of a folder's files is bad; a missing one is refused with `read_text`'s own sentence, which names it. It keys every mapped stream, English or not (Tasks 16 and 18 pick the streams 8.7 judges).
12. **Settings.** No rule here reads `Settings` (the duration bands are spec 14's fixed values: `disc::DURATION_MATCH_S` and `DVD_LONGER_MAX`); `subtitle_events` takes `sub_clear_max_bytes` as `clear_max_bytes`, and the tests run it at the default 64 and at 0.

```rust
//! Verification of a ripped title against the scan and of a remuxed final file against the decision's layout (design
//! spec 6.2 step 7, 6.4 step 14, 9.4 messages 2003 and 4047; RP11). `verify_rip` checks MakeMKV's output: the duration
//! within 2 s (on a DVD from 2 s shorter to 1% longer), the chapter count, and the tracks as an ordered match on type,
//! output codec (attributes 41 and 42), language and channels, with a text-converted caption track expected right
//! after the audio and the tracks MakeMKV removed (`MSG:4047`, counted over the selection) not expected. Read errors
//! (`MSG:2003`) are carried with their count and offsets, never the drive's name. `verify_final` checks the remuxed
//! file against the layout of 8.10. A report's pairs map file track ids back to scan streams, so the subtitle evidence
//! of 6.4 step 10 and the text rule's decisions are keyed by scan stream. Built on `reconcile`'s row builders
//! (`expected_rows`, `removed_streams`), which stay the phase 0 rule, untouched (RP6). Written from the spec (RP20); no
//! I/O (RP19): callers hand in parsed values, text or a `Tree`. Used by Tasks 13, 16 and 18.

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

    use serde_json::{json, Value};

    use crate::disc::{disc, Flags, StreamKind, Title};
    use crate::recording::files::{MkvmergeIdent, Selection, SubsIndexEntry};
    use crate::recording::{MemTree, PathKey};
    use crate::review::ReviewReason;
    use crate::robot::{parse, Scan};
    use crate::settings::Settings;
    use crate::testsupport::scan_text;
    use crate::tracks::layout::{Layout, OutputTrack};

    /// Attribute 42 of every stream MakeMKV does not convert, as the recordings write it.
    const LOSSLESS: &str = "( Lossless conversion )";
    /// Attribute 42 of the converted closed-caption stream (short-circuit-2-1988-dvd's stream 12).
    const LOSSY: &str = "( Lossy conversion )";

    /// A Blu-ray title 0 shaped like pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd's feature (its scan.txt, 2026-10-16): HEVC video; Spanish
    /// DTS-HD MA 5.1 (flags 1024) and its derived DTS core (2304); English Dolby Digital 2.0; English, English derived
    /// forced-only (6144), Spanish and Spanish derived forced-only PGS subtitles; 22 chapters; 1:59:10.
    fn bluray_scan() -> Scan {
        parse(&scan_text(
            &[(1, "Blu-ray disc")],
            &[(
                0,
                &[(8, "22"), (9, "1:59:10")],
                &[
                    (0, &[(1, "Video"), (5, "V_MPEGH/ISO/HEVC"), (6, "MpegH"), (7, "MpegH HEVC Main10@L5.1"), (22, "0"), (42, LOSSLESS)]),
                    (1, &[(1, "Audio"), (3, "spa"), (5, "A_DTS"), (6, "DTS-HD MA"), (7, "DTS-HD Master Audio"), (14, "6"), (22, "1024"), (42, LOSSLESS)]),
                    (2, &[(1, "Audio"), (3, "spa"), (5, "A_DTS"), (6, "DTS"), (7, "DTS"), (14, "6"), (22, "2304"), (42, LOSSLESS)]),
                    (3, &[(1, "Audio"), (3, "eng"), (5, "A_AC3"), (6, "DD"), (7, "Dolby Digital"), (14, "2"), (22, "0"), (42, LOSSLESS)]),
                    (4, &[(1, "Subtitles"), (3, "eng"), (5, "S_HDMV/PGS"), (6, "PGS"), (7, "HDMV PGS Subtitles"), (22, "0"), (42, LOSSLESS)]),
                    (5, &[(1, "Subtitles"), (3, "eng"), (5, "S_HDMV/PGS"), (6, "PGS"), (7, "HDMV PGS Subtitles"), (22, "6144"), (42, LOSSLESS)]),
                    (6, &[(1, "Subtitles"), (3, "spa"), (5, "S_HDMV/PGS"), (6, "PGS"), (7, "HDMV PGS Subtitles"), (22, "0"), (42, LOSSLESS)]),
                    (7, &[(1, "Subtitles"), (3, "spa"), (5, "S_HDMV/PGS"), (6, "PGS"), (7, "HDMV PGS Subtitles"), (22, "6144"), (42, LOSSLESS)]),
                ],
            )],
        ))
    }

    /// A DVD title 0 shaped like short-circuit-2-1988-dvd's feature (its scan.txt, 2026-10-16), with fewer languages:
    /// MPEG-2 video; English and French Dolby Digital 2.0; English and French VobSub subtitles; the English closed
    /// captions MakeMKV converts to text (attribute 41 "Text", 42 lossy), listed last; 28 chapters; 1:50:06.
    fn dvd_scan() -> Scan {
        parse(&scan_text(
            &[(1, "DVD disc")],
            &[(
                0,
                &[(8, "28"), (9, "1:50:06"), (24, "01")],
                &[
                    (0, &[(1, "Video"), (5, "V_MPEG2"), (6, "Mpeg2"), (7, "Mpeg2"), (22, "0"), (42, LOSSLESS)]),
                    (1, &[(1, "Audio"), (3, "eng"), (5, "A_AC3"), (6, "DD"), (7, "Dolby Digital"), (14, "2"), (22, "0"), (42, LOSSLESS)]),
                    (2, &[(1, "Audio"), (3, "fre"), (5, "A_AC3"), (6, "DD"), (7, "Dolby Digital"), (14, "2"), (22, "0"), (42, LOSSLESS)]),
                    (3, &[(1, "Subtitles"), (3, "eng"), (5, "S_VOBSUB"), (6, ""), (7, "Dvd Subtitles"), (22, "0"), (42, LOSSLESS)]),
                    (4, &[(1, "Subtitles"), (3, "fre"), (5, "S_VOBSUB"), (6, ""), (7, "Dvd Subtitles"), (22, "0"), (42, LOSSLESS)]),
                    (5, &[(1, "Subtitles"), (3, "eng"), (5, "S_CC608/DVD"), (6, "CC"), (7, "Closed Captions"), (22, "0"), (41, "Text"), (42, LOSSY)]),
                ],
            )],
        ))
    }

    /// A Blu-ray title 0 with an Atmos and a plain TrueHD track: AVC video, English TrueHD Atmos 7.1, English TrueHD 5.1;
    /// 2 chapters; 0:10:00.
    fn truehd_scan() -> Scan {
        parse(&scan_text(
            &[(1, "Blu-ray disc")],
            &[(
                0,
                &[(8, "2"), (9, "0:10:00")],
                &[
                    (0, &[(1, "Video"), (5, "V_MPEG4/ISO/AVC"), (6, "Mpeg4"), (7, "Mpeg4 AVC High@L4.1"), (22, "0"), (42, LOSSLESS)]),
                    (1, &[(1, "Audio"), (3, "eng"), (5, "A_TRUEHD"), (6, "TrueHD"), (7, "TrueHD Atmos"), (14, "8"), (22, "0"), (42, LOSSLESS)]),
                    (2, &[(1, "Audio"), (3, "eng"), (5, "A_TRUEHD"), (6, "TrueHD"), (7, "TrueHD"), (14, "6"), (22, "0"), (42, LOSSLESS)]),
                ],
            )],
        ))
    }

    /// Title `number` of `scan`, typed.
    fn title_of(scan: &Scan, number: u32) -> Title {
        disc(scan).unwrap().title(number).unwrap().clone()
    }

    #[test]
    fn selected_streams_for_all_are_every_stream_of_the_title_in_scan_order() {
        assert_eq!(selected_streams(&bluray_scan(), 0, Selection::All), Ok(vec![0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]));
        assert_eq!(selected_streams(&dvd_scan(), 0, Selection::All), Ok(vec![0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn selected_streams_for_eng_keep_english_and_no_language_audio_without_core_or_commentary_flags() {
        // Title 2: video; English DTS-HD MA (1024, kept), its derived core (2304: flag 256, dropped), English Dolby
        // Digital flagged director's comments (1, dropped), audio without a language (und, kept), Spanish audio
        // (dropped); English (kept) and French (dropped) subtitles.
        let scan = parse(&scan_text(
            &[(1, "Blu-ray disc")],
            &[(
                2,
                &[(8, "1"), (9, "0:30:00")],
                &[
                    (0, &[(1, "Video"), (5, "V_MPEG4/ISO/AVC"), (6, "Mpeg4"), (7, "Mpeg4 AVC High@L4.1")]),
                    (1, &[(1, "Audio"), (3, "eng"), (5, "A_DTS"), (6, "DTS-HD MA"), (7, "DTS-HD Master Audio"), (14, "6"), (22, "1024")]),
                    (2, &[(1, "Audio"), (3, "eng"), (5, "A_DTS"), (6, "DTS"), (7, "DTS"), (14, "6"), (22, "2304")]),
                    (3, &[(1, "Audio"), (3, "eng"), (5, "A_AC3"), (6, "DD"), (7, "Dolby Digital"), (14, "2"), (22, "1")]),
                    (4, &[(1, "Audio"), (5, "A_AC3"), (6, "DD"), (7, "Dolby Digital"), (14, "2")]),
                    (5, &[(1, "Audio"), (3, "spa"), (5, "A_AC3"), (6, "DD"), (7, "Dolby Digital"), (14, "2")]),
                    (6, &[(1, "Subtitles"), (3, "eng"), (5, "S_HDMV/PGS"), (6, "PGS"), (7, "HDMV PGS Subtitles")]),
                    (7, &[(1, "Subtitles"), (3, "fre"), (5, "S_HDMV/PGS"), (6, "PGS"), (7, "HDMV PGS Subtitles")]),
                ],
            )],
        ));
        assert_eq!(selected_streams(&scan, 2, Selection::Eng), Ok(vec![0, 1, 4, 6]));
        assert_eq!(selected_streams(&scan, 2, Selection::All), Ok(vec![0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]));
        // pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd's eng-only rip kept the English audio and both English subtitle streams.
        assert_eq!(selected_streams(&bluray_scan(), 0, Selection::Eng), Ok(vec![0, 3, 4, 5]));
        // short-circuit-2-1988-dvd's eng-only rip kept the English VobSub and the English closed captions.
        assert_eq!(selected_streams(&dvd_scan(), 0, Selection::Eng), Ok(vec![0, 1, 3, 5]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_3d_video_stream_is_never_selected() {
        let scan = parse(&scan_text(
            &[],
            &[(
                0,
                &[(8, "1"), (9, "0:10:00")],
                &[
                    (0, &[(1, "Video"), (5, "V_MPEG4/ISO/AVC"), (6, "Mpeg4"), (7, "Mpeg4 AVC High@L4.1")]),
                    (1, &[(1, "Video"), (5, "V_MPEG4/ISO/MVC"), (6, "Mpeg4 MVC"), (7, "Mpeg4 MVC High@L4.1")]),
                    (2, &[(1, "Audio"), (3, "eng"), (5, "A_AC3"), (6, "DD"), (7, "Dolby Digital"), (14, "6")]),
                ],
            )],
        ));
        assert_eq!(selected_streams(&scan, 0, Selection::All), Ok(vec![0, 2]));
        assert_eq!(selected_streams(&scan, 0, Selection::Eng), Ok(vec![0, 2]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn selected_streams_refuse_a_title_the_scan_lacks() {
        assert_eq!(selected_streams(&bluray_scan(), 7, Selection::All), Err("the scan lists no title 7".to_string()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_flag_that_is_not_a_number_is_refused_with_reconciles_sentence() {
        let scan = parse(&scan_text(
            &[],
            &[(
                0,
                &[(8, "1"), (9, "0:10:00")],
                &[(0, &[(1, "Video"), (6, "Mpeg2")]), (1, &[(1, "Audio"), (3, "eng"), (6, "DD"), (22, "x")])],
            )],
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            selected_streams(&scan, 0, Selection::All),
            Err("scan stream 0,1: attribute 22: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'x'".to_string())
        );
    }
```

```rust
use crate::reconcile::expected_rows;
use crate::recording::files::Selection;
use crate::robot::Scan;

/// The scan streams a rip with `selection` kept, in scan order: the `stream` of every row of
/// `reconcile::expected_rows(scan, title, selection)` (3D video, attribute 6 containing "MVC", left out; Eng's filter of
/// eng/und audio without flags 256 and 1|2|4 and eng subtitles). MakeMKV's `MSG:4047` numbers count these streams from
/// 0. Err "the scan lists no title <n>" when the scan has no TINFO line for `title`, and `expected_rows`' sentence when
/// a stream's attribute 22 is not a number. Spec 6.2 step 7, RP11 ("built on reconcile's row builders").
pub fn selected_streams(scan: &Scan, title: u32, selection: Selection) -> Result<Vec<u32>, String> {
    if !scan.titles.contains_key(&title) {
        return Err(format!("the scan lists no title {title}"));
    }
    Ok(expected_rows(scan, title, selection)?.into_iter().map(|row| row.stream).collect())
}
```

```rust
const TEXT_OUTPUT: &str = "Text";

/// mkvmerge's codec name for a stream converted to text ("`Text` arrives as `SubRip/SRT`"). Spec 6.2 step 7.
const TEXT_CODEC: &str = "SubRip/SRT";

/// A stream the file should hold, in file order (6.2 step 7).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct ExpectedTrack {
    /// The scan's stream number.
    pub stream: u32,
    /// Attribute 1.
    pub kind: StreamKind,
    /// The names `mkvmerge -J` may give the track's codec; any one of them matches. Empty for a codec the table does
    /// not know, which then never matches.
    pub codecs: Vec<String>,
    /// Attribute 3 as `disc::Stream` holds it (lower-cased); None on video, whose language is never compared.
    pub language: Option<String>,
    /// Attribute 14 on an audio stream; None on video and subtitles.
    pub channels: Option<u32>,
    /// Attribute 22, carried onto the output track (9.5's MakeMKV-only flags).
    pub flags: Flags,
    /// Attribute 41 is "Text": the stream arrives as a text subtitle track, right after the audio.
    pub text_converted: bool,
}

/// The title's streams in `selection` (selected_streams' result) without those `removed` (MSG:4047 indices counted over
/// the selection from 0), with a text-converted subtitle stream (attribute 41 "Text") placed right after the audio
/// streams (`caption_first`). Codecs: `codec::mkvmerge_names(codec)`, ["SubRip/SRT"] for a text-converted one, and for
/// any other attribute 41 the names of the codec ID it gives (`codec::codec(attribute 41, "", "")`); attribute 42 alone
/// changes nothing. Language attribute 3 (None on video); flags carried (9.5's MakeMKV-only flags onto the output
/// track). A selected stream the title does not hold as a typed stream (no attribute 1) is not expected but keeps its
/// place in the count. Spec 6.2 step 7.
pub fn expected_tracks(title: &Title, selection: &[u32], removed: &BTreeSet<i64>) -> Vec<ExpectedTrack> {
    let mut tracks = Vec::new();
    for (index, number) in selection.iter().enumerate() {
        let position = i64::try_from(index).unwrap_or(i64::MAX);
        if removed.contains(&position) {
            continue;
        }
        if let Some(stream) = title.streams.iter().find(|stream| stream.number == *number) {
            tracks.push(expected_track(stream));
        }
    }
    caption_first(tracks)
}

/// One stream as the file should hold it. Spec 6.2 step 7 "Output codec".
fn expected_track(stream: &Stream) -> ExpectedTrack {
    let codecs: Vec<String> = match stream.output_codec.as_deref() {
        Some(TEXT_OUTPUT) => vec![TEXT_CODEC.to_string()],
        Some(id) => mkvmerge_names(&codec(id, "", "")).iter().map(|name| name.to_string()).collect(),
        None => mkvmerge_names(&stream.codec).iter().map(|name| name.to_string()).collect(),
    };
    ExpectedTrack {
        stream: stream.number,
        kind: stream.kind,
        codecs,
        language: if stream.kind == StreamKind::Video { None } else { stream.language.clone() },
        channels: if stream.kind == StreamKind::Audio { stream.channels } else { None },
        flags: stream.flags,
        text_converted: stream.output_codec.as_deref() == Some(TEXT_OUTPUT),
    }
}

/// Moves every text_converted track to right after the last audio track (6.2 step 7 "Order"); without audio, right
/// after the last video track; without either, first. The other tracks keep their order, and so do the text tracks.
pub fn caption_first(tracks: Vec<ExpectedTrack>) -> Vec<ExpectedTrack> {
    let (text, mut others): (Vec<ExpectedTrack>, Vec<ExpectedTrack>) =
        tracks.into_iter().partition(|track| track.text_converted);
    let after = others
        .iter()
        .rposition(|track| track.kind == StreamKind::Audio)
        .or_else(|| others.iter().rposition(|track| track.kind == StreamKind::Video))
        .map_or(0, |position| position + 1);
    for (offset, track) in text.into_iter().enumerate() {
        others.insert(after + offset, track);
    }
    others
}
```

```rust
/// How much longer than the scan's duration a DVD file may run: 1% (spec 6.2 step 7, provisional, set from the two
/// DVDs of phase 0; a fixed value of spec 14).
pub const DVD_LONGER_MAX: f64 = 0.01;

/// |file - expected| <= disc::DURATION_MATCH_S, or on a DVD expected - DURATION_MATCH_S <= file <= expected * 1.01 (6.2
/// step 7). The DVD band widens the 2 s band and never narrows it: a DVD title shorter than 200 s still gets 2 s longer.
pub fn duration_ok(expected_seconds: f64, file_seconds: f64, dvd: bool) -> bool {
    let band = f64::from(DURATION_MATCH_S);
    if (file_seconds - expected_seconds).abs() <= band {
        return true;
    }
    dvd && expected_seconds - band <= file_seconds && file_seconds <= expected_seconds * (1.0 + DVD_LONGER_MAX)
}
```

In `crates/core/src/verify.rs`, find the line

and replace it with

```rust
/// MSG:2003, a read error (spec 9.4).
const READ_ERROR: u32 = 2003;

/// One read-error offset of a rip log (6.2 step 7 "with the error count and offsets"). Not `recording::ReadError` (a
/// failed file read, the error of `Tree::read`); import it as `verify::ReadError`.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct ReadError {
    /// The line's third parameter (`%3`, "1048576"); "" when the line has none.
    pub offset: String,
    /// The MSG:2003 lines at this offset.
    pub count: u32,
    /// The first line's first parameter at this offset (the `%1` error text); "" when the line has none.
    pub message: String,
}

/// Every MSG:2003 line's offset with the count of lines at that offset: `offset` is params[2]; `message` is params[0]
/// alone (the `%1` error text, "Scsi error - ILLEGAL REQUEST:READ OF SCRAMBLED SECTOR WITHOUT AUTHENTICATION"), the
/// first per offset; Message.text and params[1] (the drive's name and serial) are never kept (robot.rs: drive fields
/// never reach a golden). Offsets in order of first appearance; a line without parameters counts under "". Spec 6.2
/// step 7, 9.4.
pub fn read_errors(rip_log: &str) -> Vec<ReadError> {
    let mut errors: Vec<ReadError> = Vec::new();
    for line in parse(rip_log).messages.iter().filter(|message| message.code == READ_ERROR) {
        let offset = line.params.get(2).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
        match errors.iter_mut().find(|error| error.offset == offset) {
            Some(error) => error.count = error.count.saturating_add(1),
            None => errors.push(ReadError {
                offset,
                count: 1,
                message: line.params.first().cloned().unwrap_or_default(),
            }),
        }
    }
    errors
}
```

```rust
/// The sentence for a title without attribute 9. Spec 6.2 step 7.
const NO_DURATION: &str = "duration: the scan gives no duration (attribute 9)";

/// The sentence for a title the scan gives no stream for: nothing passes on empty input. Spec 6.2 step 7.
const NOTHING_EXPECTED: &str = "tracks: the scan predicts no track for this title";

/// What verification found. Spec 6.2 step 7 (`verify_rip`) and 6.4 step 14 (`verify_final`).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct VerifyReport {
    /// The file's duration against `expected_seconds` (`duration_ok` of 6.2 step 7 for a rip; the 2 s band for a remux).
    pub duration_ok: bool,
    /// The scan's attribute 9 (verify_rip; 0 when the scan gives none) or the source duration (verify_final), seconds.
    pub expected_seconds: f64,
    /// `ident.container.properties.duration` in nanoseconds / 1e9.
    pub file_seconds: f64,
    /// verify_rip: the file's first chapter edition against the scan's attribute 8. verify_final checks no chapters
    /// (6.4 step 14 names the tracks and the duration): true, with both counts the file's.
    pub chapters_ok: bool,
    /// The scan's attribute 8 (verify_rip), the file's count (verify_final).
    pub scan_chapters: u32,
    /// The file's first chapter edition's `num_entries` (0 without an edition).
    pub file_chapters: u32,
    /// The ordered match found no difference.
    pub tracks_ok: bool,
    /// (expected stream, file track id) in order; None where the file lacks it.
    pub pairs: Vec<(u32, Option<i64>)>,
    /// The file's tracks past the last expected one.
    pub extra_tracks: Vec<i64>,
    /// MSG:4047 indices at or beyond the selection's length, sorted (they fail nothing, as in `reconcile`).
    pub unknown_removed: Vec<i64>,
    /// One sentence per difference, in track order ("track 3: forced expected true, file false", "track 2: codec expected
    /// DTS-HD Master Audio, file AC-3"), then the duration ("duration: expected 5400 s, file 5320.0 s"), then the chapters.
    pub mismatches: Vec<String>,
    /// `read_errors` of the rip log (verify_rip); empty for a remux.
    pub read_errors: Vec<ReadError>,
    /// duration_ok, chapters_ok and tracks_ok; read errors never fail it (6.2 step 7: the title is kept).
    pub ok: bool,
}

/// What the ordered match of the expected tracks against the file's tracks found.
struct Matched {
    pairs: Vec<(u32, Option<i64>)>,
    extra_tracks: Vec<i64>,
    mismatches: Vec<String>,
}

/// The ordered match of 6.2 step 7 and 6.4 step 14, position by position: the expected track at position i against the
/// file's track at position i. A wrong type is one sentence and the track's other fields are not compared; otherwise
/// `differences` names each field that differs. An expected track past the file's last is paired with None; a file
/// track past the last expected one is extra. An empty expected list is the sentence `nothing` of its own (the caller's:
/// `NOTHING_EXPECTED` for a rip, whose tracks come from the scan; `NOTHING_KEPT` for a remux, whose come from the layout).
fn match_tracks<T>(
    expected: &[T],
    file: &[MkvTrack],
    nothing: &str,
    key: impl Fn(&T) -> (u32, StreamKind),
    differences: impl Fn(&T, &MkvTrack) -> Vec<String>,
) -> Matched {
    let mut matched = Matched { pairs: Vec::new(), extra_tracks: Vec::new(), mismatches: Vec::new() };
    for (position, want) in expected.iter().enumerate() {
        let (stream, kind) = key(want);
        match file.get(position) {
            Some(track) => {
                matched.pairs.push((stream, Some(track.id)));
                if track.r#type != kind.as_str() {
                    matched
                        .mismatches
                        .push(format!("track {}: type expected {}, file {}", track.id, kind.as_str(), track.r#type));
                } else {
                    matched.mismatches.extend(differences(want, track));
                }
            }
            None => {
                matched.pairs.push((stream, None));
                matched.mismatches.push(format!("stream {stream} ({}): missing from the file", kind.as_str()));
            }
        }
    }
    for track in file.iter().skip(expected.len()) {
        matched.extra_tracks.push(track.id);
        matched.mismatches.push(format!("track {}: not expected ({} {})", track.id, track.r#type, track.codec));
    }
    if expected.is_empty() {
        matched.mismatches.push(nothing.to_string());
    }
    matched
}

/// A rip's track against the scan's stream: codec (any of `codecs`), language (`norm_lang` on both sides; never on
/// video) and channels (property `audio_channels`, on audio). Spec 6.2 step 7.
fn rip_differences(want: &ExpectedTrack, track: &MkvTrack) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    if !want.codecs.iter().any(|name| *name == track.codec) {
        found.push(format!("track {}: codec expected {}, file {}", track.id, codec_list(&want.codecs), track.codec));
    }
    if want.kind != StreamKind::Video {
        let (expected, got) = (norm_lang(want.language.as_deref()), file_language(track));
        if expected != got {
            found.push(format!("track {}: language expected {expected}, file {got}", track.id));
        }
    }
    if let Some(channels) = want.channels {
        let got = track.properties.get("audio_channels").and_then(Value::as_i64);
        if got != Some(i64::from(channels)) {
            let shown = got.map_or_else(|| "none".to_string(), |count| count.to_string());
            found.push(format!("track {}: channels expected {channels}, file {shown}", track.id));
        }
    }
    found
}

/// The track's `language` property through `norm_lang` ("und" when absent or not text).
fn file_language(track: &MkvTrack) -> String {
    norm_lang(track.properties.get("language").and_then(Value::as_str))
}

/// The codec names a sentence shows: joined by " or ", or "(none known)" for a codec the table does not know.
fn codec_list(codecs: &[String]) -> String {
    if codecs.is_empty() {
        "(none known)".to_string()
    } else {
        codecs.join(" or ")
    }
}

/// `ident.container.properties.duration` (nanoseconds) in seconds.
fn file_duration(ident: &MkvmergeIdent) -> f64 {
    ident.container.properties.duration as f64 / 1e9
}

/// The file's chapter count: the first edition's `num_entries`, 0 without an edition.
fn chapter_entries(ident: &MkvmergeIdent) -> i64 {
    ident.chapters.first().map_or(0, |edition| edition.num_entries)
}

/// "duration: expected <expected> s, file <file, one decimal> s".
fn duration_sentence(expected_seconds: f64, file_seconds: f64) -> String {
    format!("duration: expected {expected_seconds} s, file {file_seconds:.1} s")
}

/// 6.2 step 7: duration_ok against the title's seconds; chapters `ident.chapters.first().map_or(0, |c| c.num_entries)`
/// compared with `i64::from(title.chapters)`; the ordered match of expected_tracks (removed from
/// `reconcile::removed_streams` of `rip_log`) against ident.tracks on type, codec (any of `codecs`), language
/// (`norm_lang` of property `language` on both sides; not on video) and channels (property `audio_channels`);
/// read_errors of `rip_log`. `selection` is selected_streams' result for the rip's profile; `dvd` is the disc's
/// `Disc::is_dvd`. Without a rip log nothing is removed and no read error is known.
pub fn verify_rip(title: &Title, ident: &MkvmergeIdent, selection: &[u32], rip_log: Option<&str>, dvd: bool) -> VerifyReport {
    let removed = rip_log.map(removed_streams).unwrap_or_default();
    let selected = i64::try_from(selection.len()).unwrap_or(i64::MAX);
    let unknown_removed: Vec<i64> = removed.iter().copied().filter(|&index| index >= selected).collect();
    let expected = expected_tracks(title, selection, &removed);
    let matched = match_tracks(
        &expected,
        &ident.tracks,
        NOTHING_EXPECTED,
        |track: &ExpectedTrack| (track.stream, track.kind),
        rip_differences,
    );
    let tracks_ok = matched.mismatches.is_empty();
    let mut mismatches = matched.mismatches;
    let expected_seconds = title.seconds.map_or(0.0, f64::from);
    let file_seconds = file_duration(ident);
    let duration_passes = title.seconds.is_some() && duration_ok(expected_seconds, file_seconds, dvd);
    if title.seconds.is_none() {
        mismatches.push(NO_DURATION.to_string());
    } else if !duration_passes {
        mismatches.push(duration_sentence(expected_seconds, file_seconds));
    }
    let entries = chapter_entries(ident);
    let chapters_ok = entries == i64::from(title.chapters);
    if !chapters_ok {
        mismatches.push(format!("chapters: expected {}, file {entries}", title.chapters));
    }
    VerifyReport {
        duration_ok: duration_passes,
        expected_seconds,
        file_seconds,
        chapters_ok,
        scan_chapters: title.chapters,
        file_chapters: u32::try_from(entries).unwrap_or(0),
        tracks_ok,
        pairs: matched.pairs,
        extra_tracks: matched.extra_tracks,
        unknown_removed,
        mismatches,
        read_errors: rip_log.map(read_errors).unwrap_or_default(),
        ok: duration_passes && chapters_ok && tracks_ok,
    }
}
```

```rust
/// verify_failed when `!report.ok && second_failure`; read_errors when `report.read_errors` is not empty; sorted and
/// unique (`review::sorted_unique`). Verification lowers no confidence: these reasons hold the job (open point 30).
/// Spec 6.2 step 7, 8.8.
pub fn failure_reviews(report: &VerifyReport, second_failure: bool) -> Vec<ReviewReason> {
    let mut reasons = Vec::new();
    if !report.ok && second_failure {
        reasons.push(ReviewReason::VerifyFailed);
    }
    if !report.read_errors.is_empty() {
        reasons.push(ReviewReason::ReadErrors);
    }
    sorted_unique(reasons)
}
```

```rust
/// The sentence for an empty layout: nothing passes on empty input, and 6.4 step 14's expected tracks are the decision's
/// layout, not the scan's. Spec 6.4 step 14.
const NOTHING_KEPT: &str = "tracks: the layout keeps no track";

/// A flag property of the track (`default_track`, `forced_track`, `flag_hearing_impaired`, `flag_original`); absent or
/// not a bool is false.
fn file_flag(track: &MkvTrack, key: &str) -> bool {
    track.properties.get(key).and_then(Value::as_bool).unwrap_or(false)
}

/// A remuxed track against the layout's: language (`norm_lang` on both sides; never on video, whose language 8.10 does
/// not set), name (`track_name`; absent is none), then the four flags. Spec 6.4 step 14, 8.10.
fn final_differences(want: &OutputTrack, track: &MkvTrack) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    if want.kind != StreamKind::Video {
        let (expected, got) = (norm_lang(want.language.as_deref()), file_language(track));
        if expected != got {
            found.push(format!("track {}: language expected {expected}, file {got}", track.id));
        }
    }
    let name = track.properties.get("track_name").and_then(Value::as_str);
    if want.name.as_deref() != name {
        found.push(format!(
            "track {}: name expected {}, file {}",
            track.id,
            want.name.as_deref().unwrap_or("none"),
            name.unwrap_or("none")
        ));
    }
    let flags = [
        ("default", want.default, "default_track"),
        ("forced", want.forced, "forced_track"),
        ("hearing_impaired", want.hearing_impaired, "flag_hearing_impaired"),
        ("original", want.original, "flag_original"),
    ];
    for (flag, expected, key) in flags {
        let got = file_flag(track, key);
        if got != expected {
            found.push(format!("track {}: {flag} expected {expected}, file {got}", track.id));
        }
    }
    found
}

/// 6.4 step 14: the partial file's tracks must equal the layout exactly (order, type, language through norm_lang of
/// property `language`, name from `track_name`, flags from the properties `default_track`, `forced_track`,
/// `flag_hearing_impaired`, `flag_original`, an absent key being false), and its duration be within
/// disc::DURATION_MATCH_S of `source_seconds`; each difference is a `mismatches` sentence. The video track's language is
/// not compared and no chapter count is checked (`chapters_ok` true, both counts the file's); `unknown_removed` and
/// `read_errors` are empty. An empty layout never verifies ("tracks: the layout keeps no track").
pub fn verify_final(layout: &Layout, ident: &MkvmergeIdent, source_seconds: f64) -> VerifyReport {
    let matched = match_tracks(
        &layout.tracks,
        &ident.tracks,
        NOTHING_KEPT,
        |track: &OutputTrack| (track.stream, track.kind),
        final_differences,
    );
    let tracks_ok = matched.mismatches.is_empty();
    let mut mismatches = matched.mismatches;
    let file_seconds = file_duration(ident);
    let duration_passes = (file_seconds - source_seconds).abs() <= f64::from(DURATION_MATCH_S);
    if !duration_passes {
        mismatches.push(duration_sentence(source_seconds, file_seconds));
    }
    let chapters = u32::try_from(chapter_entries(ident)).unwrap_or(0);
    VerifyReport {
        duration_ok: duration_passes,
        expected_seconds: source_seconds,
        file_seconds,
        chapters_ok: true,
        scan_chapters: chapters,
        file_chapters: chapters,
        tracks_ok,
        pairs: matched.pairs,
        extra_tracks: matched.extra_tracks,
        unknown_removed: Vec::new(),
        mismatches,
        read_errors: Vec::new(),
        ok: duration_passes && tracks_ok,
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 30: Write the failing tests of the stream mapping and `subtitle_events`**

Spec 6.4 step 10 reads "each stream's packets" from the subtitle evidence file to get "the event counts and start times for 8.7", and 8.7 reasons about scan streams (their flags, their order, their parents). The evidence names a stream by the file's track id (`subs/index.json`'s `track_id`, which an MKV's ffprobe index and its mkvmerge track id share), so the report's pairs carry it back to the scan's stream; a report whose track match failed carries none back, since its pairs are positions, not matches (settled point 1). Image streams drop packets of `sub_clear_max_bytes` (spec 14, default 64) or less, text streams count every packet, as `align::align_subs_dir` does. The fixture has the shape of short-circuit-2-1988-dvd's eng-only `subs/` folder (track 2 the text-converted captions, track 3 the VobSub; packet times and sizes as strings, as ffprobe writes them), with made-up packets: no time or size of the clone's packets files is copied into a test (RP21).

```rust
        let mut tree = MemTree::new("rec", "rec");

            Ok(BTreeMap::from([(5, vec![10.0, 12.5, 15.25])]))
        );
        // The same invalid byte in a packets file is refused, naming the file.
        let mut strict = MemTree::new("rec", "rec");
        strict.insert_file("subs/index.json", index);
        strict.insert_file("subs/sub-0.packets.json", b"{\xff}".to_vec());
        assert_eq!(
            subtitle_events(&strict, &PathKey::new("subs"), &dvd_report(), 64),
            Err("rec/subs/sub-0.packets.json: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 1: invalid start byte".to_string())
        );
    }
```

```rust
/// The scan stream a file track id stands for, through `pairs` (an ffprobe index of an MKV equals its mkvmerge track
/// id); None for a track no pair holds, and None for every track when the track match failed (`tracks_ok` false: its
/// pairs are positions, not matches). Spec 6.2 step 7, 6.4 step 10.
pub fn stream_of_track(report: &VerifyReport, track_id: i64) -> Option<u32> {
    if !report.tracks_ok {
        return None;
    }
    report.pairs.iter().find(|(_, track)| *track == Some(track_id)).map(|(stream, _)| *stream)
}

/// subs/index.json's `n` to the scan stream, through each entry's `track_id` and `stream_of_track`; entries without a
/// track_id or a pair are left out, so a report whose track match failed maps none. Spec 6.4 step 10, 8.7.
pub fn subs_streams(index: &[SubsIndexEntry], report: &VerifyReport) -> BTreeMap<i64, u32> {
    index
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|entry| {
            let stream = stream_of_track(report, entry.track_id?)?;
            Some((entry.n, stream))
        })
        .collect()
}

/// subs_dir/index.json as `align::index_streams` reads it: UTF-8 with a byte-order mark allowed, invalid bytes
/// replaced. Err is the read error's text (it names the path) or "<path>: <serde error>". The one reading
/// `subtitle_events` and decide's text decisions share. Spec 6.4 step 10, 8.7.
pub fn subs_index(tree: &dyn Tree, subs_dir: &PathKey) -> Result<Vec<SubsIndexEntry>, String> {
    let path = subs_dir.join("index.json");
    let text = read_text(tree, &path, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Replace)?;
    serde_json::from_str(&text).map_err(|error| format!("{}: {error}", tree.display(&path)))
}

/// `align::events` of every subs/index.json entry under `subs_dir` (packets through `align::load_packets`), keyed by
/// scan stream (`subs_streams`): `clear_max_bytes` (spec 14 `sub_clear_max_bytes`) for image codecs, 0 where
/// `align::is_text`. index.json is read as `align::index_streams` reads it (a byte-order mark allowed, invalid bytes
/// replaced), each packets file strictly; only mapped entries are read. Err with the read error's text for a missing
/// file (it names the path), or with the file's path before a decode error's, serde's or `align::events`' message, so a
/// failure always names its file. Spec 6.4 step 10, 8.7.
pub fn subtitle_events(
    tree: &dyn Tree,
    subs_dir: &PathKey,
    report: &VerifyReport,
    clear_max_bytes: i64,
) -> Result<BTreeMap<u32, Vec<f64>>, String> {
    let index = subs_index(tree, subs_dir)?;
    let streams = subs_streams(&index, report);
    let mut by_stream = BTreeMap::new();
    for entry in &index {
        let Some(&stream) = streams.get(&entry.n) else {
            continue;
        };
        let path = subs_dir.join(&format!("sub-{}.packets.json", entry.n));
        let shown = tree.display(&path);
        let text = read_text(tree, &path, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Strict)
            .map_err(|error| if tree.is_file(&path) { format!("{shown}: {error}") } else { error })?;
        // load_packets prefixes its syntax and serde errors with `shown` but returns the AttributeError text of a
        // top level that is not an object bare, so that one gets the path here.
        let packets = load_packets(&text, &shown)
            .map_err(|error| if error.starts_with(&shown) { error } else { format!("{shown}: {error}") })?;
        let limit = if is_text(entry.codec.as_deref()) { 0 } else { clear_max_bytes };
        let starts = events(&packets, limit).map_err(|error| format!("{shown}: {error}"))?;
        by_stream.insert(stream, starts);
    }
    Ok(by_stream)
}

/// A map keyed by subs/index.json's `n` (such as `text::decide`'s decisions) re-keyed by scan stream through `streams`
/// (subs_streams' result); keys without a stream are left out. Spec 8.7 "Text".
pub fn by_scan_stream<T: Clone>(by_n: &BTreeMap<i64, T>, streams: &BTreeMap<i64, u32>) -> BTreeMap<u32, T> {
    by_n.iter().filter_map(|(n, value)| streams.get(n).map(|stream| (*stream, value.clone()))).collect()
}
```
