```rust
//! Verification of a rip against its scan (spec 6.2 step 7, 9.4 messages 2003 and 4047; `lazymkv_core::verify`, phase 1
//! Task 12) over every rip label of the evidence clone: each label's `mkvmerge.json` against its recording's `scan.txt`
//! through the label's selection and `rip.txt`, the read errors of the DVD rip, the selection for `all` and `eng`, and
//! the subtitle streams of `subs/index.json` mapped onto scan streams with their event counts at the default
//! `sub_clear_max_bytes` and at 0. Each recording has a test with the values read from its files on 2026-10-16; a
//! recording added later is listed by recordings_without_a_test_are_listed_as_not_covered, and a rip label added later
//! by every_rip_label_of_the_clone_verifies, until they get their tests here. Without the clone, or without one
//! recording, a test prints "skipped: <reason>" and passes. A drive's name or serial (MSG:2003's second parameter, the
//! DRV lines) is never printed. Input: LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE, else corpus/owner under the repository root.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use lazymkv_core::disc::{disc, Title};
use lazymkv_core::recording::files::{rip_label, rip_labels, MkvmergeIdent, Selection, SubsIndexEntry};
use lazymkv_core::recording::{read_json, read_text, Encoding, Errors, PathKey, Tree};
use lazymkv_core::reconcile::RIP_LOG_NAMES;
use lazymkv_core::review::ReviewReason;
use lazymkv_core::robot::{parse, Scan};
use lazymkv_core::settings::Settings;
use lazymkv_core::subtitle::align::{events, is_text, load_packets};
use lazymkv_core::verify::{
    duration_ok, failure_reviews, read_errors, selected_streams, subs_streams, subtitle_events, verify_rip, ReadError,
    VerifyReport,
};
use lazymkv_dev::evidence::{skip, DiskTree};

/// The recordings with a test here.
const RECORDINGS: [&str; 4] =
    ["pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd", "short-circuit-1986-dvd", "short-circuit-2-1988-dvd", "the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray"];

/// The rip labels with a test here, as `<slug>/<label>`.
const RIP_LABELS: [&str; 9] = [
    "pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd/all-tracks",
    "pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd/eng-only",
    "pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd/rehearsal",
    "short-circuit-1986-dvd/all-tracks",
    "short-circuit-2-1988-dvd/all-tracks-2",
    "short-circuit-2-1988-dvd/eng-only",
    "the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray/e16-stereo",
    "the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray/rehearsal",
    "the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray/t3-all-tracks",
];

/// The read error short-circuit-2-1988-dvd's all-tracks-2 rip logged three times (spec 6.2 step 7).
const SCRAMBLED: &str = "Scsi error - ILLEGAL REQUEST:READ OF SCRAMBLED SECTOR WITHOUT AUTHENTICATION";

/// The evidence clone: LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE, else corpus/owner under the repository root.
fn evidence() -> PathBuf {
    match std::env::var("LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE") {
        Ok(dir) if !dir.is_empty() => PathBuf::from(dir),
        _ => Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../corpus/owner"),
    }
}

/// The slugs of the clone's recordings that have a scan.txt (never the golden folder), sorted; None, with the skip line
/// written, when the clone is absent.
fn recorded_slugs() -> Option<Vec<String>> {
    let root = evidence();
    if !root.is_dir() {
        skip(&format!("no evidence clone at {}", root.display()));
        return None;
    }
    let mut slugs = Vec::new();
    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(&root).unwrap() {
        let dir = entry.unwrap().path();
        let name = dir.file_name().unwrap().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        if name != "golden" && dir.join("scan.txt").is_file() {
            slugs.push(name);
        }
    }
    slugs.sort();
    Some(slugs)
}

/// One recording of the clone: a tree holding only its folder, the folder's key, its parsed scan and whether the scan
/// is a DVD's (`Disc::is_dvd`).
struct Rec {
    tree: DiskTree,
    dir: PathKey,
    scan: Scan,
    dvd: bool,
}

/// The recording `slug`; None, with the skip line written, when the clone or the recording is absent.
fn recording(slug: &str) -> Option<Rec> {
    let scan_path = evidence().join(slug).join("scan.txt");
    if !scan_path.is_file() {
        skip(&format!("no {} (the evidence clone or this recording is absent)", scan_path.display()));
        return None;
    }
    let tree = DiskTree::open_sub(&evidence(), "corpus/owner", slug).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{slug}: {error}"));
    let dir = PathKey::new(slug);
    let text = read_text(&tree, &dir.join("scan.txt"), Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Replace)
        .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{slug}: {error}"));
    let scan = parse(&text);
    let dvd = disc(&scan).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{slug}: {error}")).is_dvd;
    Some(Rec { tree, dir, scan, dvd })
}

/// A rip label verified as the engine verifies a rip: its title, its selection, its rip log and the report.
struct Verified {
    title: Title,
    selection: Vec<u32>,
    rip_log: String,
    report: VerifyReport,
}

/// `label` of `rec`: `rip_label` gives the title and the selection, `selected_streams` the selected streams, and
/// `verify_rip` checks `mkvmerge.json` against the scan's title with the label's rip log. A refusal fails the test.
fn verified(rec: &Rec, label: &str) -> Verified {
    let rip = rip_label(&rec.tree, &rec.dir, label).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{error}"));
    let number = u32::try_from(rip.title).unwrap();
    let title = disc(&rec.scan).unwrap().title(number).unwrap().clone();
    let selection = selected_streams(&rec.scan, number, rip.selection).unwrap();
    let folder = rec.dir.join(label);
    let ident: MkvmergeIdent =
        read_json(&rec.tree, &folder.join("mkvmerge.json")).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{label}: {error}"));
    let log = RIP_LOG_NAMES
        .iter()
        .map(|name| folder.join(name))
        .find(|path| rec.tree.is_file(path))
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{label}: no rip.txt or extract.txt"));
    let rip_log = read_text(&rec.tree, &log, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Replace).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{error}"));
    let report = verify_rip(&title, &ident, &selection, Some(rip_log.as_str()), rec.dvd);
    Verified { title, selection, rip_log, report }
}

/// The pairs of a file holding `streams` in this order as its tracks 0, 1, 2 and on.
fn pairs(streams: &[u32]) -> Vec<(u32, Option<i64>)> {
    streams.iter().enumerate().map(|(id, &stream)| (stream, Some(i64::try_from(id).unwrap()))).collect()
}

/// The report verified, with no difference.
fn assert_verified(label: &str, report: &VerifyReport) {
    assert!(report.ok, "{label}: {:?}", report.mismatches);
    assert_eq!(report.mismatches, Vec::<String>::new(), "{label}");
    assert_eq!(report.extra_tracks, Vec::<i64>::new(), "{label}");
    assert_eq!(report.unknown_removed, Vec::<i64>::new(), "{label}");
}

/// subs/index.json of `label` mapped onto scan streams.
fn subs_map(rec: &Rec, label: &str, report: &VerifyReport) -> BTreeMap<i64, u32> {
    let index: Vec<SubsIndexEntry> = read_json(&rec.tree, &rec.dir.join(label).join("subs/index.json"))
        .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{label}: {error}"));
    subs_streams(&index, report)
}

/// `seconds` to one decimal, the precision the public docs give a file's duration (RP21: never the clone's milliseconds).
fn tenths(seconds: f64) -> f64 {
    (seconds * 10.0).round() / 10.0
}

/// Per scan stream, the event count of `subtitle_events` at `clear_max_bytes`. Each stream's starts are checked against
/// `align::events` of its packets file, read here, with the limit its codec takes (0 where `align::is_text`), so the
/// keying and the limit are checked without a start time of the clone written into this file (RP21).
fn event_counts(rec: &Rec, label: &str, report: &VerifyReport, clear_max_bytes: i64) -> BTreeMap<u32, usize> {
    let subs = rec.dir.join(label).join("subs");
    let by_stream =
        subtitle_events(&rec.tree, &subs, report, clear_max_bytes).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{label}: {error}"));
    let index: Vec<SubsIndexEntry> =
        read_json(&rec.tree, &subs.join("index.json")).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{label}: {error}"));
    for (n, stream) in subs_streams(&index, report) {
        let entry = index.iter().find(|entry| entry.n == n).unwrap();
        let path = subs.join(&format!("sub-{n}.packets.json"));
        let text = read_text(&rec.tree, &path, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Strict).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{error}"));
        let packets = load_packets(&text, &rec.tree.display(&path)).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{error}"));
        let limit = if is_text(entry.codec.as_deref()) { 0 } else { clear_max_bytes };
        let starts = events(&packets, limit).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{error}"));
        assert_eq!(by_stream.get(&stream), Some(&starts), "{label}: stream {stream}");
    }
    by_stream.into_iter().map(|(stream, starts)| (stream, starts.len())).collect()
}

#[test]
fn pans_labyrinth_2006_uhd() {
    let Some(rec) = recording("pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd") else { return };
    assert!(!rec.dvd);
    assert_eq!(selected_streams(&rec.scan, 0, Selection::All).unwrap(), [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]);
    assert_eq!(selected_streams(&rec.scan, 0, Selection::Eng).unwrap(), [0, 3, 4, 5]);
    let default = Settings::default().sub_clear_max_bytes;
    assert_eq!(default, 64);

    let all = verified(&rec, "all-tracks");
    assert_eq!(all.selection, [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]);
    assert_verified("all-tracks", &all.report);
    assert_eq!(all.report.pairs, pairs(&[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6]));
    assert_eq!((all.report.expected_seconds, tenths(all.report.file_seconds)), (7150.0, 7150.1));
    assert_eq!((all.report.scan_chapters, all.report.file_chapters), (22, 22));
    assert_eq!(all.report.read_errors, Vec::<ReadError>::new());
    assert_eq!(subs_map(&rec, "all-tracks", &all.report), BTreeMap::from([(0, 4), (1, 6)]));
    assert_eq!(event_counts(&rec, "all-tracks", &all.report, default), BTreeMap::from([(4, 887), (6, 884)]));
    // The docs publish stream 4's count at limit 0 (REPORT.md: 1774 = 2 x 887), not stream 6's. event_counts checks
    // stream 6 against align::events of its packets file, and at limit 0 it counts more events than at the default.
    let at_zero = event_counts(&rec, "all-tracks", &all.report, 0);
    assert_eq!(at_zero.keys().copied().collect::<Vec<u32>>(), [4, 6]);
    assert_eq!(at_zero.get(&4), Some(&1774));
    assert!(at_zero[&6] > 884);

    let eng = verified(&rec, "eng-only");
    assert_eq!(eng.selection, [0, 3, 4, 5]);
    assert_verified("eng-only", &eng.report);
    assert_eq!(eng.report.pairs, pairs(&[0, 3, 4]));
    assert_eq!((eng.report.expected_seconds, tenths(eng.report.file_seconds)), (7150.0, 7150.1));
    assert_eq!(subs_map(&rec, "eng-only", &eng.report), BTreeMap::from([(0, 4)]));
    assert_eq!(event_counts(&rec, "eng-only", &eng.report, default), BTreeMap::from([(4, 887)]));
    assert_eq!(event_counts(&rec, "eng-only", &eng.report, 0), BTreeMap::from([(4, 1774)]));

    let rehearsal = verified(&rec, "rehearsal");
    assert_eq!(rehearsal.title.number, 1);
    assert_eq!(rehearsal.selection, [0]);
    assert_verified("rehearsal", &rehearsal.report);
    assert_eq!(rehearsal.report.pairs, pairs(&[0]));
    // The file's duration is checked only through report.ok (the 2 s band): the docs publish no figure for it.
    assert_eq!(rehearsal.report.expected_seconds, 340.0);
    assert_eq!((rehearsal.report.scan_chapters, rehearsal.report.file_chapters), (34, 34));
}

#[test]
fn short_circuit_1986_dvd() {
    let Some(rec) = recording("short-circuit-1986-dvd") else { return };
    assert!(rec.dvd);
    let all = verified(&rec, "all-tracks");
    assert_eq!(all.selection, [0, 1, 2]);
    assert_verified("all-tracks", &all.report);
    assert_eq!(all.report.pairs, pairs(&[0, 1, 2]));
    assert_eq!((all.report.expected_seconds, tenths(all.report.file_seconds)), (5904.0, 5919.9));
    assert_eq!((all.report.scan_chapters, all.report.file_chapters), (20, 20));
    // The file runs 15.9 s longer than the scan's 5904 s: the DVD band passes it, the 2 s band would not.
    assert!(!duration_ok(all.report.expected_seconds, all.report.file_seconds, false));
    assert_eq!(all.report.read_errors, Vec::<ReadError>::new());
    assert_eq!(failure_reviews(&all.report, true), Vec::<ReviewReason>::new());
    assert!(!rec.tree.exists(&rec.dir.join("all-tracks/subs")));
}

#[test]
fn short_circuit_2_1988_dvd() {
    let Some(rec) = recording("short-circuit-2-1988-dvd") else { return };
    assert!(rec.dvd);
    assert_eq!(selected_streams(&rec.scan, 0, Selection::All).unwrap(), (0..=12).collect::<Vec<u32>>());
    assert_eq!(selected_streams(&rec.scan, 0, Selection::Eng).unwrap(), [0, 1, 5, 12]);
    let default = Settings::default().sub_clear_max_bytes;

    let all = verified(&rec, "all-tracks-2");
    assert_verified("all-tracks-2", &all.report);
    // The text-converted captions (stream 12) come right after the four audio streams.
    assert_eq!(all.report.pairs, pairs(&[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 12, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11]));
    assert_eq!((all.report.expected_seconds, tenths(all.report.file_seconds)), (6606.0, 6623.6));
    assert_eq!((all.report.scan_chapters, all.report.file_chapters), (28, 28));
    assert_eq!(all.report.read_errors, vec![ReadError { offset: "1048576".to_string(), count: 3, message: SCRAMBLED.to_string() }]);
    assert_eq!(failure_reviews(&all.report, false), [ReviewReason::ReadErrors]);
    assert_eq!(
        subs_map(&rec, "all-tracks-2", &all.report),
        BTreeMap::from([(0, 12), (1, 5), (2, 6), (3, 7), (4, 8), (5, 9), (6, 10), (7, 11)])
    );
    let counts =
        BTreeMap::from([(5, 1742), (6, 1678), (7, 1736), (8, 1246), (9, 1774), (10, 1774), (11, 1775), (12, 1671)]);
    assert_eq!(event_counts(&rec, "all-tracks-2", &all.report, default), counts);
    // No VobSub packet of this disc is 64 bytes or less, and the text track counts every packet at any limit.
    assert_eq!(event_counts(&rec, "all-tracks-2", &all.report, 0), counts);

    let eng = verified(&rec, "eng-only");
    assert_eq!(eng.selection, [0, 1, 5, 12]);
    assert_verified("eng-only", &eng.report);
    assert_eq!(eng.report.pairs, pairs(&[0, 1, 12, 5]));
    assert_eq!(eng.report.read_errors, Vec::<ReadError>::new());
    assert_eq!(failure_reviews(&eng.report, false), Vec::<ReviewReason>::new());
    assert_eq!(subs_map(&rec, "eng-only", &eng.report), BTreeMap::from([(0, 12), (1, 5)]));
    assert_eq!(event_counts(&rec, "eng-only", &eng.report, default), BTreeMap::from([(5, 1742), (12, 1671)]));
}

#[test]
fn a_read_error_never_carries_the_drive_name() {
    let Some(rec) = recording("short-circuit-2-1988-dvd") else { return };
    let all = verified(&rec, "all-tracks-2");
    let log = parse(&all.rip_log);
    let read_error_lines: Vec<_> = log.messages.iter().filter(|message| message.code == 2003).collect();
    assert_eq!(read_error_lines.len(), 3);
    // Every drive field of the log: MSG:2003's second parameter and the DRV lines' text fields.
    let drive_fields: Vec<String> = read_error_lines
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|message| message.params.get(1).cloned())
        .chain(log.drives.iter().flatten().cloned())
        .filter(|field| field.len() >= 8)
        .collect();
    assert!(!drive_fields.is_empty());
    let errors = serde_json::to_string(&read_errors(&all.rip_log)).unwrap();
    let report = serde_json::to_string(&all.report).unwrap();
    let leaked = drive_fields.iter().filter(|field| errors.contains(field.as_str()) || report.contains(field.as_str())).count();
    assert_eq!(leaked, 0, "a drive field reached the read errors or the report (the field is not printed)");
}

#[test]
fn the_office_2005_s3d3_bluray() {
    let Some(rec) = recording("the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray") else { return };
    assert!(!rec.dvd);
    // Title 0 under the eng profile: the derived DTS core (2304, flag 256) is dropped.
    assert_eq!(selected_streams(&rec.scan, 0, Selection::Eng).unwrap(), [0, 1, 3, 4, 5]);
    let default = Settings::default().sub_clear_max_bytes;

    let e16 = verified(&rec, "e16-stereo");
    assert_eq!((e16.title.number, e16.selection.clone()), (0, vec![0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]));
    assert_verified("e16-stereo", &e16.report);
    assert_eq!(e16.report.pairs, pairs(&[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]));
    // File durations of the Office are checked only through report.ok (the 2 s band): the docs publish none.
    assert_eq!(e16.report.expected_seconds, 1309.0);
    // The docs publish no chapter count for this title: the report carries the scan's count and the file matches it.
    assert_eq!((e16.report.scan_chapters, e16.report.file_chapters), (e16.title.chapters, e16.title.chapters));
    assert_eq!(subs_map(&rec, "e16-stereo", &e16.report), BTreeMap::from([(0, 4)]));
    assert_eq!(event_counts(&rec, "e16-stereo", &e16.report, default), BTreeMap::from([(4, 345)]));
    assert_eq!(event_counts(&rec, "e16-stereo", &e16.report, 0), BTreeMap::from([(4, 690)]));

    let rehearsal = verified(&rec, "rehearsal");
    assert_eq!((rehearsal.title.number, rehearsal.selection.clone()), (1, vec![0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]));
    assert_verified("rehearsal", &rehearsal.report);
    assert_eq!(rehearsal.report.pairs, pairs(&[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]));
    // The docs publish no duration for this title: the expected duration is the scan's.
    assert_eq!(rehearsal.report.expected_seconds, f64::from(rehearsal.title.seconds.unwrap()));
    assert_eq!(subs_map(&rec, "rehearsal", &rehearsal.report), BTreeMap::from([(0, 5)]));
    assert_eq!(event_counts(&rec, "rehearsal", &rehearsal.report, default), BTreeMap::from([(5, 363)]));
    assert_eq!(event_counts(&rec, "rehearsal", &rehearsal.report, 0), BTreeMap::from([(5, 726)]));

    let t3 = verified(&rec, "t3-all-tracks");
    assert_eq!((t3.title.number, t3.selection.clone()), (3, vec![0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]));
    assert_verified("t3-all-tracks", &t3.report);
    assert_eq!(t3.report.pairs, pairs(&[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]));
    assert_eq!(t3.report.expected_seconds, 2564.0);
    assert_eq!(subs_map(&rec, "t3-all-tracks", &t3.report), BTreeMap::from([(0, 4)]));
    assert_eq!(event_counts(&rec, "t3-all-tracks", &t3.report, default), BTreeMap::from([(4, 710)]));
    assert_eq!(event_counts(&rec, "t3-all-tracks", &t3.report, 0), BTreeMap::from([(4, 1420)]));
}

#[test]
fn every_rip_label_of_the_clone_verifies() {
    let Some(slugs) = recorded_slugs() else { return };
    let mut seen = Vec::new();
    for slug in &slugs {
        let rec = recording(slug).unwrap();
        for rip in rip_labels(&rec.tree, &rec.dir) {
            let checked = verified(&rec, &rip.label);
            assert!(checked.report.ok, "{slug}/{}: {:?}", rip.label, checked.report.mismatches);
            seen.push(format!("{slug}/{}", rip.label));
        }
    }
    for known in RIP_LABELS {
        assert!(seen.iter().any(|label| label == known), "{known} is no longer a rip label of the clone");
    }
    for label in seen.iter().filter(|label| !RIP_LABELS.contains(&label.as_str())) {
        skip(&format!("not covered: {label} verifies but has no test in crates/dev/tests/verify.rs"));
    }
}

#[test]
fn recordings_without_a_test_are_listed_as_not_covered() {
    let Some(slugs) = recorded_slugs() else { return };
    for slug in slugs.iter().filter(|slug| !RECORDINGS.contains(&slug.as_str())) {
        skip(&format!("not covered: {slug} has a scan.txt but no test in crates/dev/tests/verify.rs"));
    }
}
```

```rust
/// One season: `season_number` (0 is specials), `episode_count`, and the episodes once the season call is merged in (empty until then). Def: T3. Use: T4, T6.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct TmdbSeason { pub season_number: u32, #[serde(default)] pub episode_count: Option<u32>, #[serde(default)] pub episodes: Vec<TmdbEpisode> }

/// The TMDb record 8.1 fetches: title, year, original language, runtime, the IMDb and TVDB IDs and, for TV, seasons and
/// episodes with runtimes. Read from `/movie/{id}` (`title`, `release_date`, `runtime`), `/tv/{id}` (`name`, `first_air_date`,
/// `seasons`), their `external_ids`, and the recording's slim `tmdb.json` (which has no runtime and no seasons). Def: T3. Use: T4 to T7, T11, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct TmdbRecord {
    pub identity: TmdbIdentity,
    /// `title` or `name`.
    pub title: String,
    /// `original_title` or `original_name`.
    pub original_title: String,
    /// The year of `release_date` or `first_air_date`; None when absent.
    pub year: Option<i32>,
    /// `original_language`, two letters ("es", "en", "xx").
    pub original_language: Option<String>,
    /// `runtime` minutes (movies); None when TMDb has none (null or 0).
    pub runtime: Option<u32>,
    /// `external_ids.imdb_id` ("tt0001417") and `external_ids.tvdb_id`.
    pub imdb_id: Option<String>,
    pub tvdb_id: Option<i64>,
    /// TV only; empty for a movie.
    pub seasons: Vec<TmdbSeason>,
}
impl TmdbRecord {
    /// The season with `season_number == n`. Def: T3. Use: T4, T6, T7.
    pub fn season(&self, n: u32) -> Option<&TmdbSeason>;
    /// Every known episode runtime of season `n`, or of every season numbered 1 or more when `n` is None (season 0, TMDb's specials, left out; 8.1 "of the whole series when no season was parsed"), in the record's order. Def: T3. Use: T4.
    pub fn episode_runtimes(&self, season: Option<u32>) -> Vec<u32>;
    /// Spec 8.9 "Title and year always come from the same TMDb record as the ID": the Work for naming. Def: T3. Use: T11, T13.
    pub fn work(&self) -> Work;
}
/// Title, year and IDs from one TMDb record, as naming reads them (8.9). Def: T3. Use: T11, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Work { pub kind: TmdbKind, pub tmdb_id: i64, pub title: String, pub year: Option<i32>, pub imdb_id: Option<String>, pub tvdb_id: Option<i64> }

// lazymkv_core::lookup identification (T4, in lookup/mod.rs)
/// Spec 8.1's table rows, after the owner's review: Reviewed is spec 11's Set identity (8.8 "A review decision sets the
/// confidences it covers to 1.00"). Def: T4. Use: T7, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum IdentityStep { Reviewed, Remembered, DiscdbBoth, DiscdbOne, TmdbOne, TmdbSeveral, Nothing }
impl IdentityStep { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; pub const ALL: [IdentityStep; 7]; }

/// The confidence constants of 8.1 steps 1 to 6 and the cap of "When tmdb_only_autofile is off"; a review decision is
/// REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE too (1.00, 8.8). Def: T4. Use: T4, T7, T8, T10, T13.
pub const REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 1.00;

/// The identity 8.1 fixes at planning time. Def: T4. Use: T7, T11, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Identity {
    pub step: IdentityStep,
    pub confidence: f64,
    pub tmdb: Option<TmdbIdentity>,
    /// From the record when fetched, else from TheDiscDB's media, else from the one plausible result.
    pub title: Option<String>,
    pub year: Option<i32>,
    pub original_language: Option<String>,
    pub review: Option<ReviewReason>,
    /// The plausible results' identities (several in step 5; one in step 4).
    pub plausible: Vec<TmdbIdentity>,
    /// Whether a runtime check ran and what it said (None: not applicable, no record, or no runtime).
    pub runtime_check: Option<bool>,
    /// Pending lookups (8.1: planning proceeds on structure alone; the file phase waits in AwaitingLookup).
    pub lookup_pending: bool,
    /// One sentence per piece of evidence, in order ("TheDiscDB knows the fingerprint", "name 'JOHN_WICK_UHD' cleaned to 'JOHN WICK'").
    pub evidence: Vec<String>,
}

// lazymkv_core::plan::kind (T5; re-exported as plan::KindSource)

#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]

// lazymkv_core::plan::movie (T5)

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum TitleRule { Database, Labels, Structure }

/// One feature or cut to rip. Def: T5. Use: T7, T11, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Feature {
    pub title: u32,
    /// The edition name as the evidence gives it (TheDiscDB's item title beyond the media title, else the label table, or
    /// None for the theatrical or only cut); `edition_names` turns it into the filed name.
    pub edition: Option<String>,
    /// True when `edition` is None or names the theatrical cut (contains the word Theatrical; `is_theatrical`), except an
    /// unnamed cut (an Other label suffix, or a later TheDiscDB MainMovie with no edition), which has edition None and
    /// theatrical false.
    pub theatrical: bool,
    /// The titles of its group (rule 3) or cut (rule 2) that were not chosen.
    pub siblings: Vec<u32>,
}

/// What phase 2 reads from the library for 8.4 (RP18). Def: T5. Use: T7, T11, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct LibraryFacts {
    /// "the film's library folder already holds an edition-named file".
    pub folder_has_edition_named_file: bool,
    /// Earlier filed copies of this film: cut key ("theatrical", or the lower-cased edition name) to the edition name used
    /// ("" when that copy was filed without an edition name; this cut then gets None).
    pub earlier_edition_names: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    /// Spec 7: the final path already exists and is not this job's file. Phase 2 checks the plain path (no copy label);
    /// under the owner's Resolve collision "keep both" it must also check the copy-labelled path (`- 2160p 2`) before
    /// filing and hold the job with path_collision when that one is taken too (Open point 39).
    pub path_collision: bool,
}
/// 8.4's three rules, per feature in order: a non-theatrical cut always carries its name, even when it is the only cut; the
/// theatrical cut carries "Theatrical Cut" only when `features.len() >= 2` or `facts.folder_has_edition_named_file`; an
/// earlier filed copy's name (`earlier_edition_names`) replaces either. Names are raw here; naming::edition_label sanitises
/// and caps them. Def: T5. Use: T7, T13.
pub fn edition_names(features: &[Feature], facts: &LibraryFacts) -> Vec<Option<String>>;
/// An edition name that names the theatrical or main cut (8.4): none at all, or a name containing the word Theatrical
/// (ignoring ASCII case), such as TheDiscDB's "Theatrical Version". The one test of "theatrical" for every rule and caller.
/// Def: T5. Use: T5, T13.
pub fn is_theatrical(edition: Option<&str>) -> bool;

// lazymkv_core::remembered (T6)
/// A title's role in a remembered or review decision (spec 5; 11 "Assign titles", with an editable edition name). Def: T6. Use: T7, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "role")]
pub enum TitleRole { Feature, Cut { edition: String }, Episodes { season: u32, episodes: Vec<u32> }, Ignored }

/// One title of a remembered decision (spec 5: "for each title its source file, segment map, duration, role"); `dvd_title`
/// is attribute 24, the DVD's identity of a title (Review Focus 1). Def: T6. Use: T6, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct RememberedTitle { pub source_file: Option<String>, pub dvd_title: Option<String>, pub segment_map: String, pub seconds: u32, pub role: TitleRole }

/// A stream's signature (spec 5): kind, language, codec family, channels, position among identical streams (0-based). Def: T6. Use: T8, T10, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct StreamSignature { pub kind: StreamKind, pub language: Option<String>, pub codec: Family, pub channels: Option<u32>, pub position: u32 }
/// The signature of `streams[index]` (position counts earlier streams with the same kind, language, codec and channels). Def: T6. Use: T6, T8, T10, T13.
pub fn signature(streams: &[Stream], index: usize) -> StreamSignature;

/// An audio override (spec 11 "Override tracks": keep with order and default, drop, or mark as commentary, which drops it). Def: T6. Use: T8, T13, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "action")]
pub enum AudioOverride { Drop, Keep { order: u32, default: bool }, Commentary }
/// A subtitle override (spec 11: keep with a role, or drop). Def: T6. Use: T10, T13, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "action")]
pub enum SubtitleOverride { Drop, Keep { role: SubtitleRole } }
/// One remembered audio override: the stream's signature and the action, flattened into one JSON object
/// (`{"signature": {...}, "action": "keep", "order": 1, "default": true}`). A list, not a map: serde_json writes no map
/// keyed by a struct. Spec 5. Def: T6. Use: T8, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct AudioOverrideEntry { pub signature: StreamSignature, #[serde(flatten)] pub action: AudioOverride }
/// The same for subtitles. Spec 5. Def: T6. Use: T10, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct SubtitleOverrideEntry { pub signature: StreamSignature, #[serde(flatten)] pub action: SubtitleOverride }

/// The remembered-decisions file (spec 5): the TMDb identity (its `kind` is the kind; no second field), the titles, the
/// overrides. Round-trips through serde_json (`a_remembered_file_round_trips_through_json`). Def: T6. Use: T7, T13, T15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Remembered {
    pub fingerprint: String,
    pub tmdb: TmdbIdentity,
    pub titles: Vec<RememberedTitle>,
    pub audio: Vec<AudioOverrideEntry>,
    pub subtitles: Vec<SubtitleOverrideEntry>,
}
// A remembered or review decision sets the confidence it covers to lookup::REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE (1.00); no second constant here.
/// The remembered title is this scan title: `disc::same_source(&title_source(rem.source_file, rem.dvd_title), &title.source())`
/// (source file on a Blu-ray; on a DVD, both source files None, attribute 24 equal as numbers), `disc::segment_maps_agree`,
/// and duration within `disc::DURATION_MATCH_S`; never by title key. Def: T6. Use: T6, T7.
pub fn match_title(remembered: &RememberedTitle, title: &Title) -> bool;
/// Every scan title matched to a remembered title, title number to role (a remembered title is used once). Def: T6. Use: T7.
pub fn apply_titles<'a>(remembered: &'a Remembered, disc: &Disc) -> BTreeMap<u32, &'a TitleRole>;
/// Stream number to override for every stream whose signature has an entry. Def: T6. Use: T8.
pub fn apply_audio<'a>(overrides: &'a [AudioOverrideEntry], streams: &[Stream]) -> BTreeMap<u32, &'a AudioOverride>;
/// The same for subtitles. Def: T6. Use: T10.
pub fn apply_subtitles<'a>(overrides: &'a [SubtitleOverrideEntry], streams: &[Stream]) -> BTreeMap<u32, &'a SubtitleOverride>;

/// Spec 11 "Resolve collision". Def: T6. Use: T13.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Collision { KeepBoth, Replace, Discard }

/// One title of the owner's Assign titles: the scan title number and its role, flattened into one JSON object
/// (`{"title": 3, "role": "episodes", "season": 3, "episodes": [12, 13]}`). Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T7, T13, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct TitleOverrideEntry { pub title: u32, #[serde(flatten)] pub role: TitleRole }
/// One track of the owner's Override tracks: the scan title and stream numbers and the action, flattened into one JSON
/// object (`{"title": 0, "stream": 1, "action": "keep", "order": 0, "default": true}`). Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T13, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct AudioTrackOverride { pub title: u32, pub stream: u32, #[serde(flatten)] pub action: AudioOverride }
/// The same for subtitles. Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct SubtitleTrackOverride { pub title: u32, pub stream: u32, #[serde(flatten)] pub action: SubtitleOverride }

/// The owner's review decisions on one job (spec 11 Set identity, Assign titles, Override tracks, Resolve collision); each
/// sets the confidence it covers to 1.00 (8.8). Assign titles and Override tracks are lists of entries keyed by the scan's
/// title number (and stream number) of this job, sorted by those keys, one entry per key. Def: T6. Use: T7, T13, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Overrides {
    /// Set identity.
    pub identity: Option<TmdbIdentity>,
    /// The season review asked for (8.5) when the plan has none.
    pub season: Option<u32>,
    /// Assign titles: one entry per title, sorted by title number.
    pub titles: Vec<TitleOverrideEntry>,
    /// Override tracks: one entry per scan title and stream, sorted by title, then stream.
    pub audio: Vec<AudioTrackOverride>,
    pub subtitles: Vec<SubtitleTrackOverride>,
    /// Resolve collision.
    pub collision: Option<Collision>,
}
impl Overrides {
    /// The role the owner's Assign titles gives scan title `title`, if it names it. Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T13.
    pub fn title_role(&self, title: u32) -> Option<&TitleRole>;
    /// The owner's audio overrides of scan title `title` by scan stream number (the form `AudioFacts.reviewed` takes);
    /// None when no entry names the title. Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T13.
    pub fn audio_of(&self, title: u32) -> Option<BTreeMap<u32, AudioOverride>>;
    /// The same for subtitles (`SubtitleFacts.reviewed`). Spec 11. Def: T6. Use: T13.
    pub fn subtitles_of(&self, title: u32) -> Option<BTreeMap<u32, SubtitleOverride>>;
}

// lazymkv_core::tracks::audio (T8)
/// Facts the file phase measured for one title, keyed by SCAN stream number (the dev crate and phase 2 map file tracks
/// back through verify::stream_of_track). Def: T8. Use: T13, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct AudioFacts<'a> {
    /// 6.4 step 10a: the packet MD5 of every audio stream (D13). Empty at planning time.
    pub md5: BTreeMap<u32, String>,
    /// 6.4 step 9: ffprobe's profile per audio stream ("DTS-HD MA", "DTS-HD MA + DTS:X"; the Atmos spelling is unverified). Empty at planning time (8.3: the ffprobe criterion is skipped).
    pub ffprobe_profile: BTreeMap<u32, String>,
    /// TheDiscDB's title when it reconciles (8.6 step 1's descriptions).
    pub discdb: Option<&'a DiscDbTitle>,
    /// The content rule's verdict (`audio::rule::Verdict`) per candidate stream and whether D21's veto held (from
    /// audio::rule::results, mapped to scan streams).
    pub verdicts: BTreeMap<u32, Verdict>,
    pub veto_holds: bool,
    /// The scan stream the verdicts were measured against: the level folder's `main=` stream (audio::reference::programme_reference
    /// in phase 0's harness) mapped to a scan stream; None when there are no verdicts.
    pub verdict_reference: Option<u32>,
    /// The remembered overrides for this fingerprint (spec 5).
    pub remembered: Option<&'a [AudioOverrideEntry]>,
    /// The owner's Override tracks for this title (spec 11), by scan stream; they win over remembered ones. Task 13 passes
    /// `overrides.audio_of(title.number)` (that title's entries of `Overrides.audio`, by stream).
    pub reviewed: Option<&'a BTreeMap<u32, AudioOverride>>,
}

/// Why a stream was dropped (8.6 step 1, D13, RP7, spec 5 and 11 overrides). Def: T8. Use: T13, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "why")]
pub enum AudioDrop { Derived, Flagged { flags: u32 }, Secondary, Duplicate { of: u32 }, Described { kind: DescriptionKind }, UnwantedLanguage, Remembered, Reviewed }

/// Which language group a kept track belongs to (8.6 step 5's order). Def: T8. Use: T11, T13.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum LangGroup { Original, English, NoLanguage }

/// A kept audio track with everything 8.6 and 8.10 need. Def: T8. Use: T11, T13, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct AudioTrack {
    pub stream: u32,
    pub language: Option<String>,
    pub group: LangGroup,
    pub codec: Codec,
    pub channels: u32,
    pub tier: Option<Tier>,
    /// From ffprobe's profile, else the scan's attribute 7.
    pub object: Option<ObjectAudio>,
    pub sample_size: Option<u32>,
    pub sample_rate: Option<u32>,
    pub bitrate_kbps: Option<u32>,
    /// Lowest disc position among the language's surviving streams (8.6 "Position": computed after step 1's drops).
    pub first_of_language: bool,
    /// 8.10: "<display> [Atmos|DTS:X] <layout>", for example "TrueHD Atmos 7.1".
    pub name: String,
    pub default: bool,
    pub original: bool,
}

pub const AUDIO_CONFIDENCE: f64 = 0.95;
pub const G1_MAX_KBPS: u32 = 256;

/// How TheDiscDB's track list aligned with the scan's streams (8.6 step 1). Def: T8. Use: T8, T10, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Alignment { Full, WithoutDerived }

/// Def: T8. Use: T11, T13, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct AudioDecision {
    /// In final order (8.6 step 5), flags set.
    pub kept: Vec<AudioTrack>,
    pub dropped: Vec<(u32, AudioDrop)>,
    /// The programme reference (8.6 "Content"): the first kept original-language track, else the first English one; None when nothing is kept.
    pub reference: Option<u32>,
    /// `facts.verdict_reference`, copied so the document shows what the verdicts were measured against.
    pub verdict_reference: Option<u32>,
    pub notes: Vec<Noted>,
    pub reviews: Vec<ReviewReason>,
    pub confidence: f64,
    /// How TheDiscDB's track list aligned; None when it did not align uniquely (descriptions unused) or there is no record.
    pub description_alignment: Option<Alignment>,
}

/// Spec 8.6 steps 1 to 6 and "Content" (RP7), in order: drop (derived 2048; flags 1, 2, 4; secondary 512; duplicates by
/// equal MD5, one copy kept: `Duplicate { of }` names the first earlier stream with that MD5 that was kept; described
/// Commentary, AudioDescription, IsolatedScore or MusicAndEffects through `descriptions` when the alignment is unique;
/// unwanted language; a remembered or review Drop or Commentary); keep the rest and any no-language stream; rank with
/// `rank_key`; guards G1 and G2; order by language (original first when settings.original_language_first and the
/// original is not English, else English first; no language last), default on the very first track, original flag on
/// the original-language tracks (the English ones for an English work); notes possible_commentary,
/// lossless_original_available, no_english_audio, lossy_before_lossless (D9); reviews original_language_missing,
/// no_wanted_audio; verdicts apply only when `facts.verdict_reference` is Some: when it differs from the decision's
/// `reference` (spec 15: evidence measured against another reference than the rule's own choice), or `facts.veto_holds`
/// is true (D21: the rule confirms no commentary on the title), only audio_reference_unclear is raised and no verdict
/// is mapped; otherwise, for the kept streams, ReferenceUnclear adds audio_reference_unclear, Commentary and
/// CommentaryCrossLanguage add commentary_detected (nothing dropped, D15), AdPattern, NoteCommentary and NoteAd add
/// notes; a remembered or review Keep { order, default } fixes the order and the default. Confidence 0.95, or
/// lookup::REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE (1.00) when every audio stream of the title has a remembered or review override. At
/// planning time `facts` is empty and the ffprobe criterion is skipped (8.3). Def: T8. Use: T13, T16.

/// Spec 8.7 in full, in order: `set_aside`; events from `facts.events`; full = `is_full` against the largest English
/// track's events (a stream flagged forced, 4096 without 2048, is never full: its flag makes it a forced source);
/// `alignment_groups` over the full tracks with the three bands (a Between pair raises subtitle_ambiguous);
/// `dialogue_group` with the parents of forced-only streams that have events and `tracks::audio::descriptions` (None raises
/// subtitle_ambiguous, and the first group stands in for the regular and SDH roles); regular and SDH (up to two: more
/// events is SDH, a description saying SDH overrides; the closed-caption stream is SDH when the group has none; more than
/// two gives subtitle_ambiguous); full tracks outside a picked group dropped (OutsideDialogueGroup; with no pick they are
/// kept as regular under the review, never dropped by position); forced (first: a forced-only stream with events whose
/// parent is the regular track, then the SDH track's; then a DVD stream flagged forced; then a separately authored track
/// that is not full with fewer than FORCED_MAX_EVENTS events); other not-full tracks with FORCED_MAX_EVENTS or more events
/// dropped with partial_subtitle_dropped, those with no events dropped NoEvents; `text_disagreements` (subtitle_ambiguous
/// and one subtitle_text_disagrees note per stream); the confidence case; remembered then review overrides applied last
/// (decided_by "remembered" or "reviewed"; an override naming a stream that is not an English or no-language subtitle
/// stream is ignored), with confidence lookup::REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE (1.00) and subtitle_ambiguous cleared when every
/// English and no-language subtitle stream of the title still in the file (not in facts.removed) has an override
/// (other-language streams are dropped by 8.7's first sentence; the case unchanged). A title with one English stream and
/// no events keeps it as Regular "English" (row 14 (b) fallback), case OneFull. Def: T10. Use: T13, T16, T18.
pub fn decide_subtitles(title: &Title, facts: &SubtitleFacts<'_>, settings: &Settings) -> SubtitleDecision;
```

```rust
/// record's original language; R4, 8.6 "Languages") and decide_subtitles (facts with `reviewed` set from
/// `overrides.audio_of(title.number)` and `overrides.subtitles_of(title.number)`), layout, the path (movie_path for a
/// feature, tv_path for an episode, by the filed role: the owner's Assign titles when it names any title, which then wins
/// whole as in a re-plan (Err for a planned title it ignores or does not name), else the planned role; no path when the
/// record's kind does not match the role (a movie record for a feature, a show record for an episode); resolution from
/// title.video_height, the edition through edition_names and edition_label; a planned Episode with season None builds no
/// path (path None) and adds tv_unmapped;
/// overrides.collision KeepBoth (copy Some(2) while the collision exists) and Replace leave path_collision unraised;
/// Discard never reaches decide, the engine discards the job), the three confidences (identity and

/// = min(audio, subtitle) after the remembered and review overrides set the parts they cover to 1.00), reviews = plan's

/// 24, segment map, seconds and role): the owner's Assign titles whole, in title order (Ignored included, a title the scan lacks left out), when it names
/// any title, else every planned title under its planned role (Err for an episode without a season or episode numbers,
/// and for a feature without an edition in a plan of two or more features: an unnamed cut or structural rival the owner
/// must name first, 8.4), every kept and dropped audio and subtitle stream of `decisions` as an override entry keyed by
/// `remembered::signature`. Def: T13. Use: phase 2.
pub fn remember(fingerprint: &str, disc: &Disc, plan: &Plan, decisions: &[FileDecision], overrides: &Overrides) -> Result<Remembered, String>;
```

And, not a cross-task item: `Disposition` also gets the closed-set methods every enum of spec strings has (Conventions): `pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str` ("auto_file", "needs_review"), `pub const ALL: [Disposition; 2]` and `impl std::str::FromStr for Disposition`.

Where this task settles what the spec and the interfaces leave open (each choice is pinned by a test below):

1. **The role a title is filed under.** The owner's Assign titles (`overrides.titles`), when it names any title, wins whole, as in Task 7's re-plan (`assigned_roles` and `assigned_entries`, its settled point 7) and the interfaces' `plan` doc: Open point 32 requires the decision and a re-plan to apply the owner's review decisions the same way, so a job approved at the disposition gate files exactly the titles a re-plan would. `Feature` is a feature without an edition and `Cut { edition }` a feature with that edition (both through `plan::assigned_feature`, the one copy of the mapping, which Step 2 moves out of Task 7's `assigned_entries` so both call it), `Episodes { season, episodes }` an episode with no name of its own (as Task 7's `assigned_entries` builds it, so `episode_name` takes TMDb's name, exactly as a re-plan files it), and `Ignored` is refused (`decide` returns Err: nothing is filed for an ignored title). A planned title the assignment does not name is refused too (Err: nothing is filed for it), never filed under its planned role beside the owner's titles (`a_planned_title_the_owners_assign_titles_leaves_out_is_not_filed`). An assigned title the scan lacks is left out, as in Task 7's `assigned_entries`, so it is no feature of the job and changes no edition name (`an_assigned_title_the_scan_lacks_is_left_out_of_the_editions`); `DecisionInputs.disc` is the scan that check reads. Without an Assign titles, the planned role stands. A planned episode without a season takes `overrides.season` (8.5 "review asks for it"). The path follows that role (a feature through `movie_path` under `movies_root`, an episode through `tv_path` under `tv_root`), so an owner who turns a planned movie title into episodes and sets the show's identity gets a TV path (`the_owners_episode_assignment_on_a_movie_plan_files_under_tv_root_with_a_show_identity`); `plan.kind` is not consulted a second time. The record's kind must match the role (8.1 "the two kinds number their records separately"; 8.9 takes title and year from the identity's record): a feature needs a movie record and an episode a show record, else no path is built (choice 3), so a movie's ID never names a show folder and a show's ID never a movie folder (`a_role_whose_kind_differs_from_the_records_builds_no_path`).
2. **The edition name.** `edition_names` (8.4) runs at decide time over the job's features (the owner's Assign titles, when it names any title, whole and in title order through `plan::assigned_feature`, as Task 7's `assigned_entries` builds them, a title the scan lacks left out; else the plan's features in plan order), with the `LibraryFacts` of decide time, so a library folder that gained an edition-named file since planning, or an earlier filed copy of the cut (8.4's third bullet, `earlier_edition_names`), is honoured (`an_earlier_filed_copy_name_is_used_at_decide_time`). The plan holds Task 7's filed names, not the evidence's raw ones (Task 7's settled point 3: `PlannedRole::Feature.edition` is `edition_names` over the planning-time library facts), so `job_features` rebuilds each planned feature's `theatrical` flag from what the plan holds: a feature whose name names the theatrical cut (`is_theatrical`, Task 5's one test of "theatrical") is theatrical, any other name is a cut that `edition_names` gives back unchanged, and a feature with no edition is theatrical only in a plan of one feature. In a plan of two or more features Task 7 names the theatrical cut "Theatrical Cut", so a feature left without a name there is an unnamed cut (Task 5's settled point 3, `unnamed_cut`, 8.3 rule 1 or 2), a structural rival (rule 3 names no cut) or a cut whose earlier filed copy had no edition (`earlier_edition_names` maps it to ""); it is not theatrical, so it keeps no edition until the owner names it (8.4 "else from the owner in review") and is never filed as a second "Theatrical Cut" on the theatrical cut's path (`an_unnamed_cut_keeps_no_edition_name_beside_the_theatrical_cut`, `two_structural_rivals_get_no_edition_name_until_the_owner_names_them`). An assigned title is built from the assignment alone: `Feature` is the main cut, theatrical, and `Cut { edition }` is theatrical only when `is_theatrical` says its name names the theatrical cut. The second pass therefore changes only what the library facts of decide time change. The name then goes through `edition_label` (sanitised, 32 characters); a label that sanitises to nothing is no edition.
3. **When no path is built.** Without a TMDb record, without a TMDb identity, without the root for the role (`settings.movies_root`, `settings.tv_root`; both are None in spec 14's defaults), without a video height (a feature's `<Res>`), when the record's kind does not match the role (choice 1: a feature with a show record, an episode with a movie record), and for an episode without a season or without an episode number (which also raises `tv_unmapped`, 8.5). A decision without a path is `NeedsReview` even when it has no review reason and every confidence passes: 8.8's "files automatically only if" is a necessary condition, and a job with no final path cannot be filed. No review reason of 8.8's closed set names this case, so none is invented: the interfaces file records it as Open point 38 for the plan's owner (Task 14's NeedsReview notification may then carry an empty list until the owner adds a reason).
4. **The record must be the identity's own.** The identity is `overrides.identity`, else `plan.identity.tmdb`. A record of another identity is refused with a sentence (8.9 "Title and year always come from the same TMDb record as the ID"); a record with no identity in hand is not used (no path).
5. **Resolve collision (spec 11).** `KeepBoth` passes `copy: Some(2)` while `library.path_collision` holds (the file name gains ` 2` after the resolution label, `- 2160p 2`, or after the episode code, `S03E15 2`; `keep_both_on_an_episode_puts_the_copy_label_after_the_episode_code`); when the colliding file is gone by decide time (removed before approval), the new file takes the plain path, since a ` 2` label would distinguish it from nothing. `Replace` keeps the path. After either, `library.path_collision` raises no `path_collision` (the owner resolved it). `Discard` is refused: the engine discards the job and never asks for a decision. Without a resolution, `library.path_collision` raises `path_collision` (spec 7 "A path collision with any other file adds the review reason `path_collision`"). `LibraryFacts.path_collision` is one fact about one path, the plain one (no copy label), which is the path phase 2 checks before calling `decide`; the label is always 2, so a third copy (a `- 2160p 2` file already there) is not seen by `decide`. Phase 2 therefore also checks the copy-labelled path under `KeepBoth` before filing and, when that one is taken too, does not file and holds the job with `path_collision` (spec 7: lazymkv never overwrites a file it did not create). The `LibraryFacts.path_collision` doc and Open point 39 of the interfaces file say so; a second library fact for the labelled path is left to the plan's owner rather than added here, since `LibraryFacts` is Task 5's type.
6. **`read_errors` exactly when the rip logged read errors.** The reason is removed from whatever was carried in (`rip_reviews`, the plan) and added only when `inputs.read_errors` is not empty; the offsets are carried unchanged. Verification lowers no confidence (Open point 30): `verify_failed`, `read_errors` and `copy_hash_errors` hold the job through the review reason alone.
7. **The episode title.** The plan's (TheDiscDB's item title), else TMDb's name of the episode when the title holds exactly one episode, else none (`tv_path` then omits it with its ` - `). A multi-episode title without a name of its own gets none: joining TMDb's names would invent a title.
8. **Confidences.** Identity is 1.00 (`lookup::REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE`) when `overrides.identity` is Some, title 1.00 when `overrides.titles` is not empty (8.8 "A review decision sets the confidences it covers to 1.00"), track is `track_confidence` of the two decisions, which already carry 1.00 where the remembered and review overrides cover every stream (Tasks 8 and 10). The same two review decisions answer the plan's review reasons they cover, which `decide` leaves out: Set identity answers `identity_unknown` and `identity_ambiguous`, Assign titles answers `title_ambiguous`, `multiple_features`, `unnamed_cut` and `tv_unmapped`. Other tasks treat a review decision the same way (Task 7's assigned titles take the title rule's review reasons with them; Task 10 clears `subtitle_ambiguous` when overrides cover every stream), and without it a Copy-mode job held for one of these reasons and approved with the answer would be held a second time at the disposition gate (Task 14's `DecisionDone { NeedsReview }`) for a reason the owner already answered. The `tv_unmapped` that `decide` raises itself for a filed episode that still lacks its season or episode numbers stays, and the owner's season alone is no assignment, so it answers nothing (`the_owners_season_fills_a_planned_episode_without_one`).
9. **`remember` (spec 11 Remember, spec 5's file).** When the owner's Assign titles names any title, it is stored whole, exactly its entries in title order (`Ignored` included), instead of the planned titles: the decision and a re-plan apply it that way (choice 1), so a planned title it leaves out is not remembered, and a title it names that the scan lacks is left out, as in Task 7's `assigned_entries` (`remember_leaves_out_an_assigned_title_the_scan_lacks`). Otherwise planned roles are stored as `Feature` (a feature without an edition in a plan of one feature), `Cut { edition }` (any edition, "Theatrical Cut" included), and `Episodes` (the episode's season, else `overrides.season`; Err without a season or without an episode number). A feature without an edition in a plan of two or more features is an unnamed cut or a structural rival (choice 2), which spec 5's roles cannot express: `TitleRole::Feature` means the theatrical or main cut, and Task 7's `assigned_entries` would read it back as such and name it "Theatrical Cut" beside the real one, two features on one path at title confidence 1.00. `remember` refuses it with Err until the owner names it (`an_unnamed_cut_cannot_be_remembered_until_the_owner_names_it`). Every kept audio track is `Keep { order, default }` with `order` its 0-based position in the decision's final order (Task 8's target positions, 0 first); every dropped audio stream is `Drop`, or `Commentary` when the owner marked it so; every kept subtitle track is `Keep { role }` and every dropped one `Drop`. A signature already stored (a second title with the same streams) is not stored again: the first decision wins. Err for a job without any identity, a title without a duration (spec 5 stores the duration), a decision whose key is not in the plan, or a stream the scan title lacks.
10. **Settings read.** `decide` reads `auto_threshold` (through `disposition`), `movies_root` and `tv_root` itself, and hands the settings to the rules it calls (`edition_style` and `jellyfin10_compat` reach `movie_path` and `tv_path`; `original_language_first` and `prefer_most_channels` reach `decide_audio`). The tests exercise `auto_threshold` at 0.85 and 0.95, both roots unset and set, `edition_style` at `combined`, `plex` and `jellyfin`, `jellyfin10_compat` off and on.
11. **The wanted languages (R4, 8.6 "Languages").** The audio rule takes the wanted languages of the identity the job is filed under. They are the plan's (`Plan.wanted`, computed at planning from the planning identity's original language, which Task 7 takes from the record when fetched, else from TheDiscDB's media), except when the owner's Set identity names another work than the plan's and its record is given: then `wanted_languages(record.original_language)`. Without this, a disc planned with `identity_unknown` (English only, `wanted_languages(None)`) and given a Spanish film's identity at the disposition gate would drop the Spanish original track as an unwanted language, raise no `original_language_missing` (`original_is_english` holds for None) and file automatically without it (`the_owners_set_identity_brings_the_original_language_into_the_audio_rule`). For the plan's own identity the plan's set stands, since it may hold TheDiscDB's original language where the record has none; a re-plan with the same overrides gives the same set (Open point 32).

All tests read synthetic scans built with `testsupport::scan_text` and synthetic TMDb records in TMDb's documented shape (`/movie/{id}`, `/tv/{id}` with a season merged; phase 2's client verifies the shape live), so they run on every OS and in CI. The film is spec 8.9's own example, `Film (2010) {tmdb-12345}`; the show borrows The Office's names (TMDb 2316, season 3) with made-up sizes. Expected paths are spec 8.9's patterns applied to these inputs.

```rust
/// Spec 11's Assign titles as a feature for 8.4's `edition_names`: `Feature` is the theatrical or main cut (no edition),
/// `Cut { edition }` a feature with the owner's name, theatrical when `movie::is_theatrical` says the name names the
/// theatrical cut (Task 5's one test of "theatrical"); None for episodes and Ignored. The one copy of this mapping: the
/// re-plan's `assigned_entries` and the decision (`decision::decide` and its `job_features`) both call it, so a job
/// approved at the disposition gate is filed as a re-plan would plan it (Open point 32). Spec 11, 8.4. Def: T13.
/// Use: T13 (`decision::decide`, `job_features`, and Task 7's `assigned_entries` as Task 13 rewrites it).
pub(crate) fn assigned_feature(number: u32, role: &TitleRole) -> Option<Feature> {
    match role {
        TitleRole::Feature => Some(Feature { title: number, edition: None, theatrical: true, siblings: Vec::new() }),
        TitleRole::Cut { edition } => Some(Feature {
            title: number,
            edition: Some(edition.clone()),
            theatrical: is_theatrical(Some(edition.as_str())),
            siblings: Vec::new(),
        }),
        TitleRole::Episodes { .. } | TitleRole::Ignored => None,
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement the confidences, the disposition and the track confidence (spec 8.8, 8.7)**

Insert this block into `crates/core/src/decision.rs` between the line `use crate::verify::ReadError;` and the blank line before `#[cfg(test)]`:

```rust

/// The three confidences of spec 8.8 for one title: identity and title as the plan fixed them at 6.1 step 5 (1.00
/// where the owner's Set identity or Assign titles covers them), and track, which "does not exist until the Decide
/// step": the lower of the audio and subtitle confidences (8.7). Spec 8.8. Def: T13. Use: T16.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Confidences {
    /// The plan's identity confidence (8.1), or 1.00 after the owner's Set identity.
    pub identity: f64,
    /// The plan's title confidence (8.3, 8.5), or 1.00 after the owner's Assign titles.
    pub title: f64,
    /// `track_confidence` of the audio and subtitle decisions.
    pub track: f64,
}

/// What 8.8 does with a decided job: file it automatically, or hold it for review with its rip or disc copy kept
/// (D1). Spec 8.8. Def: T13. Use: T14, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Disposition {
    /// No review reason and every confidence at or above `auto_threshold`.
    AutoFile,
    /// Any review reason, or any confidence below `auto_threshold` (the job enters NeedsReview, 6.4 step 12).
    NeedsReview,
}

impl Disposition {
    /// Both values, in 8.8's order.
    pub const ALL: [Disposition; 2] = [Disposition::AutoFile, Disposition::NeedsReview];

    /// The serde spelling: "auto_file" or "needs_review".
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Disposition::AutoFile => "auto_file",
            Disposition::NeedsReview => "needs_review",
        }
    }
}

impl std::str::FromStr for Disposition {
    type Err = String;

    /// Only the two spellings of `as_str`.
    fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<Disposition, String> {
        Disposition::ALL
            .into_iter()
            .find(|value| value.as_str() == text)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("'{text}' is not a disposition (auto_file, needs_review)"))
    }
}

/// AutoFile only with no review reason and every confidence >= settings.auto_threshold (8.8: "A job files
/// automatically only if it has no review reason and all three confidences are at or above `auto_threshold`").
/// Reads settings.auto_threshold only. Def: T13. Use: T13, T16.
pub fn disposition(confidences: &Confidences, reviews: &[ReviewReason], settings: &Settings) -> Disposition {
    let threshold = settings.auto_threshold;
    let confident = [confidences.identity, confidences.title, confidences.track].into_iter().all(|value| value >= threshold);
    if reviews.is_empty() && confident {
        Disposition::AutoFile
    } else {
        Disposition::NeedsReview
    }
}

/// The lower of the two (8.7 "The job's track confidence is the lower of the audio and subtitle values"); each
/// already carries 1.00 where remembered or review overrides cover every one of its streams (Tasks 8 and 10).
/// Spec 8.7, 8.8. Def: T13. Use: T13.
pub fn track_confidence(audio: &AudioDecision, subtitles: &SubtitleDecision) -> f64 {
    audio.confidence.min(subtitles.confidence)
}
```

```rust
        &[(1, "Audio"), (3, "eng"), (5, "A_DTS"), (6, "DTS-HD MA"), (7, "DTS-HD Master Audio"), (14, "6")];
    const ENG_AC3_6CH: &[(u32, &str)] =
        &[(1, "Audio"), (3, "eng"), (5, "A_AC3"), (6, "DD"), (7, "Dolby Digital"), (13, "640 Kb/s"), (14, "6")];
    const SPA_AC3_2CH: &[(u32, &str)] =
        &[(1, "Audio"), (3, "spa"), (5, "A_AC3"), (6, "DD"), (7, "Dolby Digital"), (13, "192 Kb/s"), (14, "2")];
    const ENG_PGS: &[(u32, &str)] = &[(1, "Subtitles"), (3, "eng"), (5, "S_HDMV/PGS"), (6, "PGS"), (7, "HDMV PGS Subtitles")];
    const SPA_PGS: &[(u32, &str)] = &[(1, "Subtitles"), (3, "spa"), (5, "S_HDMV/PGS"), (6, "PGS"), (7, "HDMV PGS Subtitles")];
    const ENG_VOBSUB: &[(u32, &str)] = &[(1, "Subtitles"), (3, "eng"), (5, "S_VOBSUB"), (7, "Dvd Subtitles")];

    /// The film's UHD Blu-ray: titles 0 and 1 two cuts (UHD video, English DTS-HD MA 5.1, English PGS), title 2 a
    /// Blu-ray title with Spanish tracks beside the English ones, title 3 one whose only audio is Spanish, title 4 one
    /// without a duration (attribute 9).
    fn film_disc() -> Disc {
        let cut: &[(u32, &[(u32, &str)])] = &[(0, UHD_VIDEO), (1, ENG_DTS_HD_MA_6CH), (2, ENG_PGS)];
        let mixed: &[(u32, &[(u32, &str)])] =
            &[(0, HD_VIDEO), (1, ENG_AC3_6CH), (2, SPA_AC3_2CH), (3, ENG_PGS), (4, SPA_PGS)];
        let spanish: &[(u32, &[(u32, &str)])] = &[(0, HD_VIDEO), (1, SPA_AC3_2CH), (2, ENG_PGS)];
        let t0: &[(u32, &str)] =
            &[(2, "Film"), (8, "24"), (9, "1:58:42"), (11, "40000000000"), (16, "00800.mpls"), (26, "1,2,3")];
        let t1: &[(u32, &str)] =
            &[(2, "Film"), (8, "26"), (9, "2:06:10"), (11, "42000000000"), (16, "00801.mpls"), (26, "1,2,4")];
        let t2: &[(u32, &str)] = &[(8, "20"), (9, "1:40:00"), (11, "30000000000"), (16, "00802.mpls"), (26, "5")];
        let t3: &[(u32, &str)] = &[(8, "18"), (9, "1:35:00"), (11, "28000000000"), (16, "00803.mpls"), (26, "6")];
        let t4: &[(u32, &str)] = &[(8, "1"), (11, "1000000"), (16, "00804.mpls"), (26, "7")];
        let text = scan_text(
            &[(1, "Blu-ray disc"), (2, "Film"), (32, "FILM")],
            &[(0, t0, cut), (1, t1, cut), (2, t2, mixed), (3, t3, spanish), (4, t4, cut)],
        );
        disc(&parse(&text)).unwrap()
    }

    /// A Blu-ray of three episode titles (HD video, English Dolby Digital 5.1, English PGS).
    fn office_disc() -> Disc {
        let streams: &[(u32, &[(u32, &str)])] = &[(0, HD_VIDEO), (1, ENG_AC3_6CH), (2, ENG_PGS)];
        let t0: &[(u32, &str)] = &[(8, "6"), (9, "0:21:37"), (11, "4800000000"), (16, "00001.mpls"), (26, "1")];
        let t1: &[(u32, &str)] = &[(8, "6"), (9, "0:21:30"), (11, "4700000000"), (16, "00002.mpls"), (26, "2")];
        let t3: &[(u32, &str)] = &[(8, "12"), (9, "0:43:05"), (11, "9500000000"), (16, "00004.mpls"), (26, "4")];
        let text = scan_text(
            &[(1, "Blu-ray disc"), (2, "THE OFFICE S3D3"), (32, "THE OFFICE S3D3")],
            &[(0, t0, streams), (1, t1, streams), (3, t3, streams)],
        );
        disc(&parse(&text)).unwrap()
    }

    /// A DVD of two titles that share the segment map "1" and the duration 1:38:12 (Review Focus 1): no attribute 16,
    /// attribute 24 "01" and "02", so only attribute 24 tells them apart.
    fn dvd_disc() -> Disc {
        let streams: &[(u32, &[(u32, &str)])] = &[(0, DVD_VIDEO), (1, ENG_AC3_6CH), (2, ENG_VOBSUB)];
        let t0: &[(u32, &str)] = &[(8, "20"), (9, "1:38:12"), (11, "6000000000"), (24, "01"), (26, "1")];
        let t1: &[(u32, &str)] = &[(8, "2"), (9, "1:38:12"), (11, "700000000"), (24, "02"), (26, "1")];
        let text = scan_text(&[(1, "DVD disc"), (32, "DVD_VIDEO")], &[(0, t0, streams), (1, t1, streams)]);
        disc(&parse(&text)).unwrap()
    }

    /// A `/movie/{id}` record as TMDb documents it, already parsed.
    fn film_record(id: i64, title: &str, year: i32, imdb_id: Option<&str>) -> TmdbRecord {
        TmdbRecord {
            identity: TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::Movie, id },
            title: title.to_string(),
            original_title: title.to_string(),
            year: Some(year),
            original_language: Some("en".to_string()),
            runtime: Some(119),
            imdb_id: imdb_id.map(str::to_string),
            tvdb_id: None,
            seasons: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// A `/tv/{id}` record with season 3's episodes 15 and 16 merged from `/tv/{id}/season/3`.
    fn office_record() -> TmdbRecord {
        TmdbRecord {
            identity: OFFICE,
            title: "The Office".to_string(),
            original_title: "The Office".to_string(),
            year: Some(2005),
            original_language: Some("en".to_string()),
            runtime: None,
            imdb_id: Some("tt0002316".to_string()),
            tvdb_id: Some(102316),
            seasons: vec![TmdbSeason {
                season_number: 3,
                episode_count: Some(25),
                episodes: vec![
                    TmdbEpisode { episode_number: 15, name: Some("Phyllis' Wedding".to_string()), runtime: Some(22) },
                    TmdbEpisode { episode_number: 16, name: Some("Business School".to_string()), runtime: Some(22) },
                ],
            }],
        }
    }

    fn feature_role(edition: Option<&str>) -> PlannedRole {
        PlannedRole::Feature { edition: edition.map(str::to_string) }
    }

    fn episode_role(season: Option<u32>, episodes: &[u32], name: Option<&str>) -> PlannedRole {
        PlannedRole::Episode(Episode { season, episodes: episodes.to_vec(), name: name.map(str::to_string) })
    }

    /// A plan as 6.1 step 5 leaves it: TheDiscDB knew the disc (identity 0.95, title 0.98, Direct), an English work,
    /// the given titles in the given order with their keys (spec 5), no review reason and no note.
    fn plan_of(disc: &Disc, kind: Kind, tmdb: Option<TmdbIdentity>, roles: &[(u32, PlannedRole)]) -> Plan {
        let titles = roles
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(order, (number, role))| {
                let title = disc.title(*number).unwrap();
                PlannedTitle {
                    key: title_key(order, title, disc.is_dvd),
                    title: *number,
                    role: role.clone(),
                    seconds: title.seconds,
                    size: title.size,
                    source_file: title.source_file.clone(),
                    suggested: false,
                    remembered: false,
                }
            })
            .collect();
        Plan {
            identity: Identity {
                step: IdentityStep::DiscdbOne,
                confidence: 0.95,
                tmdb,
                title: None,
                year: None,
                original_language: Some("en".to_string()),
                review: None,
                plausible: Vec::new(),
                runtime_check: None,
                lookup_pending: false,
                evidence: Vec::new(),
            },
            kind,
            kind_source: KindSource::Discdb,
            titles,
            mode: Mode::Direct,
            identity_confidence: 0.95,
            title_confidence: 0.98,
            reviews: Vec::new(),
            notes: Vec::new(),
            wanted: wanted_languages(Some("en")),
            session: None,
            evidence: PlanEvidence {
                name: None,
                candidates: roles.iter().map(|(number, _)| *number).collect(),
                groups: Vec::new(),
                rivals: Vec::new(),
                title_rule: match kind {
                    Kind::Movie => Some(TitleRule::Database),
                    Kind::Tv => None,
                },
                labels: Vec::new(),
                discdb_matches: Vec::new(),
                sentences: Vec::new(),
            },
        }
    }

    /// Spec 14's defaults with both library roots set.
    fn settings() -> Settings {
        Settings { movies_root: Some(MOVIES.to_string()), tv_root: Some(SHOWS.to_string()), ..Settings::default() }
    }

    /// The inputs of the planned title `number`: no measured facts, no rip review, no read error, no override.
    fn inputs<'a>(
        plan: &'a Plan,
        disc: &'a Disc,
        number: u32,
        record: Option<&'a TmdbRecord>,
        library: &'a LibraryFacts,
        settings: &'a Settings,
    ) -> DecisionInputs<'a> {
        DecisionInputs {
            plan,
            disc,
            planned: plan.titles.iter().find(|planned| planned.title == number).unwrap(),
            title: disc.title(number).unwrap(),
            audio: AudioFacts::default(),
            subtitles: SubtitleFacts::default(),
            record,
            library,
            rip_reviews: Vec::new(),
            read_errors: Vec::new(),
            overrides: None,
            settings,
        }
    }

    fn path_of(decision: &FileDecision) -> &str {
        decision.path.as_ref().expect("the decision has a final path").path.as_str()
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_movie_title_gets_its_tracks_layout_path_and_confidences_and_files_automatically() {
        let disc = film_disc();
        let plan = plan_of(&disc, Kind::Movie, Some(FILM), &[(0, feature_role(None))]);
        let record = film_record(12345, "Film", 2010, Some("tt0012345"));
        let library = LibraryFacts::default();
        let settings = settings();
        let decision = decide(&inputs(&plan, &disc, 0, Some(&record), &library, &settings)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decision.title_key, "t00-00800");
        assert_eq!(decision.audio.kept.iter().map(|track| track.stream).collect::<Vec<u32>>(), vec![1]);
        assert_eq!(decision.audio.confidence, 0.95);
        assert_eq!(
            decision.subtitles.kept.iter().map(|track| (track.stream, track.role)).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            vec![(2, SubtitleRole::Regular)]
        );
        assert_eq!(decision.subtitles.confidence, 0.90);
        // 8.10: the video track is default, then the default English audio; the default audio is English and no forced
        // track is kept, so no subtitle track is default (`default_subtitle` gives None); chapters are kept.
        assert_eq!(
            decision.layout.tracks.iter().map(|track| (track.stream, track.kind, track.default)).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            vec![(0, StreamKind::Video, true), (1, StreamKind::Audio, true), (2, StreamKind::Subtitles, false)]
        );
        assert!(decision.layout.chapters_kept);
        assert_eq!(decision.resolution.as_deref(), Some("2160p"));
        assert_eq!(decision.edition, None);
        assert_eq!(
            decision.path,
            Some(NamedPath {
                root: MOVIES.to_string(),
                components: vec![
                    "Film (2010) {tmdb-12345}".to_string(),
                    "Film (2010) {tmdb-12345} - 2160p.mkv".to_string(),
                ],
                path: r"\\nas\media\Movies\Film (2010) {tmdb-12345}\Film (2010) {tmdb-12345} - 2160p.mkv".to_string(),
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(decision.confidences, Confidences { identity: 0.95, title: 0.98, track: 0.90 });
        assert!(decision.reviews.is_empty(), "{:?}", decision.reviews);
        assert!(decision.notes.is_empty(), "{:?}", decision.notes);
        assert!(decision.read_errors.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(decision.disposition, Disposition::AutoFile);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_second_cut_is_filed_under_its_edition_name_in_the_combined_style() {
        let disc = film_disc();
        let plan = plan_of(
            &disc,
            Kind::Movie,
            Some(FILM),
            &[(0, feature_role(Some("Theatrical Cut"))), (1, feature_role(Some("Unrated Cut")))],
        );
        let record = film_record(12345, "Film", 2010, Some("tt0012345"));
        let library = LibraryFacts::default();
        let settings = settings();
        assert_eq!(settings.edition_style, EditionStyle::Combined);
        let theatrical = decide(&inputs(&plan, &disc, 0, Some(&record), &library, &settings)).unwrap();
        let unrated = decide(&inputs(&plan, &disc, 1, Some(&record), &library, &settings)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(theatrical.edition.as_deref(), Some("Theatrical Cut"));
        assert_eq!(
            path_of(&theatrical),
            r"\\nas\media\Movies\Film (2010) {tmdb-12345}\Film (2010) {tmdb-12345} - 2160p Theatrical Cut {edition-Theatrical Cut}.mkv"
        );
        assert_eq!(unrated.title_key, "t01-00801");
        assert_eq!(unrated.edition.as_deref(), Some("Unrated Cut"));
        assert_eq!(
            path_of(&unrated),
            r"\\nas\media\Movies\Film (2010) {tmdb-12345}\Film (2010) {tmdb-12345} - 2160p Unrated Cut {edition-Unrated Cut}.mkv"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_unnamed_cut_keeps_no_edition_name_beside_the_theatrical_cut() {
        // Task 7's plan of two labelled cuts, FPL_MainFeature and FPL_MainFeature_DC (8.3 rule 2): the first is the
        // "Theatrical Cut", the second an unnamed cut (edition None, not theatrical) held with `unnamed_cut`.
        let disc = film_disc();
        let mut plan =
            plan_of(&disc, Kind::Movie, Some(FILM), &[(0, feature_role(Some("Theatrical Cut"))), (1, feature_role(None))]);
        plan.evidence.title_rule = Some(TitleRule::Labels);
        plan.title_confidence = 0.60;
        plan.mode = Mode::Copy;
        plan.reviews = vec![ReviewReason::UnnamedCut];
        let record = film_record(12345, "Film", 2010, Some("tt0012345"));
        let library = LibraryFacts::default();
        let settings = settings();
        let theatrical = decide(&inputs(&plan, &disc, 0, Some(&record), &library, &settings)).unwrap();
        let unnamed = decide(&inputs(&plan, &disc, 1, Some(&record), &library, &settings)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(theatrical.edition.as_deref(), Some("Theatrical Cut"));
        // Not a second "Theatrical Cut": the owner names it in review (8.4), and the two files never share a path.
        assert_eq!(unnamed.edition, None);
        assert_eq!(
            path_of(&unnamed),
            r"\\nas\media\Movies\Film (2010) {tmdb-12345}\Film (2010) {tmdb-12345} - 2160p.mkv"
        );
        assert_ne!(path_of(&unnamed), path_of(&theatrical));
        assert_eq!(unnamed.reviews, vec![ReviewReason::UnnamedCut]);
        assert_eq!(unnamed.disposition, Disposition::NeedsReview);
    }

    fn read_errors_are_carried_with_their_offsets_and_raise_read_errors() {
        let disc = film_disc();
        let plan = plan_of(&disc, Kind::Movie, Some(FILM), &[(0, feature_role(None))]);
        let record = film_record(12345, "Film", 2010, Some("tt0012345"));
        let library = LibraryFacts::default();
        let settings = settings();
        let errors = vec![ReadError { offset: "1048576".to_string(), count: 3, message: SCRAMBLED.to_string() }];
        let mut input = inputs(&plan, &disc, 0, Some(&record), &library, &settings);
        input.rip_reviews = vec![ReviewReason::ReadErrors];
        input.read_errors = errors.clone();
        let decision = decide(&input).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decision.reviews, vec![ReviewReason::ReadErrors]);
        assert_eq!(decision.read_errors, errors);
        assert_eq!(decision.confidences, Confidences { identity: 0.95, title: 0.98, track: 0.90 });
        assert_eq!(decision.disposition, Disposition::NeedsReview);
    }

        assert_eq!(held.confidences.track, 0.90);

                title: 0,
                stream: 1,
                action: AudioOverride::Keep { order: 0, default: true },
            }],
            subtitles: vec![SubtitleTrackOverride {
                title: 0,
                stream: 2,
                action: SubtitleOverride::Keep { role: SubtitleRole::Regular },
            }],
            ..Overrides::default()

        assert_eq!(approved.confidences, Confidences { identity: 0.95, title: 0.98, track: 1.00 });
        assert_eq!(approved.disposition, Disposition::AutoFile);
    }
```
