```rust
        let library = LibraryFacts::default();
        let settings = settings();
        let decision = decide(&inputs(&plan, &disc, 0, Some(&record), &library, &settings)).unwrap();
        let value = serde_json::to_value(&decision).unwrap();
        let keys: Vec<&str> = value.as_object().unwrap().keys().map(String::as_str).collect();
        assert_eq!(
            keys,
            [
                "title_key",
                "audio",
                "subtitles",
                "layout",
                "resolution",
                "edition",
                "path",
                "confidences",
                "reviews",
                "notes",
                "read_errors",
                "disposition",
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(value["edition"], Value::Null);
        assert_eq!(value["confidences"], json!({"identity": 0.95, "title": 0.98, "track": 0.90}));
        assert_eq!(value["disposition"], json!("auto_file"));
        let back: FileDecision = serde_json::from_value(value).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(back, decision);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_owners_set_identity_brings_the_original_language_into_the_audio_rule() {
        // Planned with identity_unknown (English only), then given a Spanish film's identity at the disposition gate.
        let disc = film_disc();
        let mut plan = plan_of(&disc, Kind::Movie, None, &[(2, feature_role(None))]);
        plan.identity.step = IdentityStep::Nothing;
        plan.identity.original_language = None;
        plan.identity_confidence = 0.0;
        plan.reviews = vec![ReviewReason::IdentityUnknown];
        plan.wanted = wanted_languages(None);
        let spanish_film = TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::Movie, id: 54321 };
        let record = TmdbRecord {
            original_language: Some("es".to_string()),
            ..film_record(54321, "El Film", 2010, Some("tt0054321"))
        };
        let library = LibraryFacts::default();
        let settings = settings();
        let overrides = Overrides { identity: Some(spanish_film), ..Overrides::default() };
        let mut input = inputs(&plan, &disc, 2, Some(&record), &library, &settings);
        input.overrides = Some(&overrides);
        let decision = decide(&input).unwrap();
        // Title 2's Spanish Dolby Digital stereo (stream 2) is the original language: kept, first, default, original.
        assert_eq!(decision.audio.kept.iter().map(|track| track.stream).collect::<Vec<u32>>(), vec![2, 1]);
        let first = &decision.audio.kept[0];
        assert_eq!((first.stream, first.default, first.original), (2, true, true));
        assert!(!decision.audio.dropped.iter().any(|(stream, _)| *stream == 2), "{:?}", decision.audio.dropped);
        assert!(decision.reviews.is_empty(), "{:?}", decision.reviews);
        assert_eq!(
            path_of(&decision),
            r"\\nas\media\Movies\El Film (2010) {tmdb-54321}\El Film (2010) {tmdb-54321} - 1080p.mkv"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_planned_title_the_owners_assign_titles_leaves_out_is_not_filed() {
        // Two structural rivals; the owner assigns only title 1, as a named cut. Assign titles wins whole, as in a re-plan.
        let disc = film_disc();
        let mut plan = plan_of(&disc, Kind::Movie, Some(FILM), &[(0, feature_role(None)), (1, feature_role(None))]);
        plan.evidence.title_rule = Some(TitleRule::Structure);
        plan.title_confidence = 0.60;
        plan.mode = Mode::Copy;
        plan.reviews = vec![ReviewReason::MultipleFeatures];
        let record = film_record(12345, "Film", 2010, Some("tt0012345"));
        let library = LibraryFacts::default();
        let settings = settings();
        let overrides = Overrides {
            titles: vec![TitleOverrideEntry { title: 1, role: TitleRole::Cut { edition: "Director's Cut".to_string() } }],
            ..Overrides::default()
        };
        let mut left_out = inputs(&plan, &disc, 0, Some(&record), &library, &settings);
        left_out.overrides = Some(&overrides);
        assert_eq!(
            decide(&left_out),
            Err("the owner's Assign titles does not name title 0 (t00-00800), so nothing is filed for it".to_string())
        );
        let mut named = inputs(&plan, &disc, 1, Some(&record), &library, &settings);
        named.overrides = Some(&overrides);
        let decision = decide(&named).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decision.edition.as_deref(), Some("Director's Cut"));
        assert_eq!(
            path_of(&decision),
            r"\\nas\media\Movies\Film (2010) {tmdb-12345}\Film (2010) {tmdb-12345} - 2160p Director's Cut {edition-Director's Cut}.mkv"
        );
        assert!(decision.reviews.is_empty(), "{:?}", decision.reviews);
        assert_eq!(decision.disposition, Disposition::AutoFile);
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_assigned_title_the_scan_lacks_is_left_out_of_the_editions() {
        // Task 7's `ignored_and_unknown_assigned_titles_are_left_out`, decided: the owner ignores title 0, assigns title 1
        // as the feature and names title 9, which the scan lacks. The re-plan leaves title 9 out and plans title 1 alone
        // with no edition; the decision files the same (Open point 32), never title 1 as a "Theatrical Cut" beside title 9.
        let disc = film_disc();
        assert!(disc.title(9).is_err());
        let mut plan = plan_of(&disc, Kind::Movie, Some(FILM), &[(0, feature_role(None)), (1, feature_role(None))]);
        plan.evidence.title_rule = Some(TitleRule::Structure);
        let record = film_record(12345, "Film", 2010, Some("tt0012345"));
        let library = LibraryFacts::default();
        let settings = settings();
        let overrides = Overrides {
            titles: vec![
                TitleOverrideEntry { title: 0, role: TitleRole::Ignored },
                TitleOverrideEntry { title: 1, role: TitleRole::Feature },
                TitleOverrideEntry { title: 9, role: TitleRole::Feature },
            ],
            ..Overrides::default()
        };
        let mut input = inputs(&plan, &disc, 1, Some(&record), &library, &settings);
        input.overrides = Some(&overrides);
        let decision = decide(&input).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decision.edition, None);
        assert_eq!(
            path_of(&decision),
            r"\\nas\media\Movies\Film (2010) {tmdb-12345}\Film (2010) {tmdb-12345} - 2160p.mkv"
        );
        assert_eq!(decision.confidences, Confidences { identity: 0.95, title: 1.00, track: 0.90 });
        assert_eq!(decision.disposition, Disposition::AutoFile);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_role_whose_kind_differs_from_the_records_builds_no_path() {
        let library = LibraryFacts::default();
        let settings = settings();
        // Episodes on a film's identity: a movie's TMDb ID never names a show folder.
        let film = film_disc();
        let movie_plan = plan_of(&film, Kind::Movie, Some(FILM), &[(0, feature_role(None))]);
        let film_rec = film_record(12345, "Film", 2010, Some("tt0012345"));
        let episodes = Overrides {
            titles: vec![TitleOverrideEntry { title: 0, role: TitleRole::Episodes { season: 1, episodes: vec![1] } }],
            ..Overrides::default()
        };
        let mut input = inputs(&movie_plan, &film, 0, Some(&film_rec), &library, &settings);
        input.overrides = Some(&episodes);
        let decision = decide(&input).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decision.path, None);
        assert_eq!(decision.disposition, Disposition::NeedsReview);
        // A feature on a show's identity: a show's TMDb ID never names a movie folder.
        let office = office_disc();
        let tv_plan = plan_of(&office, Kind::Tv, Some(OFFICE), &[(0, episode_role(Some(3), &[15], Some("Phyllis' Wedding")))]);
        let show = office_record();
        let feature =
            Overrides { titles: vec![TitleOverrideEntry { title: 0, role: TitleRole::Feature }], ..Overrides::default() };
        let mut input = inputs(&tv_plan, &office, 0, Some(&show), &library, &settings);
        input.overrides = Some(&feature);
        let decision = decide(&input).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(decision.path, None);
        assert_eq!(decision.disposition, Disposition::NeedsReview);
    }
```

Where the expected values come from: the film's tracks are one English lossless 5.1 stream (8.6: kept, default, no note, 0.95) and one English PGS stream with no events, which 8.7's row 14 (b) fallback keeps as Regular "English" at 0.90 (Open point 12), so the track confidence is 0.90 (8.7's last sentence); identity 0.95 and title 0.98 are the plan's (TheDiscDB by fingerprint, rule 1). The paths are 8.9's patterns: `<movies_root>\Title (Year) {tmdb-ID}\Title (Year) {tmdb-ID} - <Res>.mkv` with 3840x2160 giving `2160p` and 1920x1080 `1080p`; `combined` adds ` <Ed> {edition-<Ed>}` after the resolution, `plex` puts ` {edition-<Ed>}` in both names before ` - <Res>`; `jellyfin10_compat` inserts ` [tmdbid-ID]` after `{tmdb-ID}` in both names (8.9's own example), and for an ID between 1900 and 2099 without an IMDb ID leaves it out with `compat_tag_omitted`; TV is `<tv_root>\Show (Year) {tmdb-ID}\Season NN\Show (Year) - SNNENN[-ENN] - Episode Title.mkv`, `/` removed from the episode title; spec 11's keep both is `- 2160p 2`. The roots are UNC paths, so every separator is `\` (Open point 14). Title 3's only audio stream is Spanish on an English work, so 8.6 keeps nothing and raises `no_wanted_audio`. Title 1 beside a "Theatrical Cut" with no edition of its own is an unnamed cut (Task 5's settled point 3), so it keeps no edition and the plain path, which is not the theatrical cut's. The owner's Set identity and Assign titles set their confidences to 1.00 and answer the plan's reasons they cover (choice 8), so with track 0.90 such a job files automatically. Title 2 with the owner's Set identity of a Spanish film (choice 11) keeps its Spanish stereo track as the original language, ordered first with `original_language_first` on (8.6 step 5), and its default and original flags; English follows. A planned title the owner's Assign titles does not name is refused (choice 1), and the one assigned cut, alone in the job, carries its name as a non-theatrical cut (8.4's first bullet). A role whose kind is not the record's builds no path (choice 1, choice 3). An earlier filed copy named "Original" names the lone theatrical cut (8.4's third bullet, key `theatrical`). `jellyfin` puts ` <Ed>` after the resolution label with no `{edition-...}` tag (8.9). Keep both on an episode puts ` 2` after the episode code (Task 11's settled point 5). An assigned title the scan lacks (title 9 of the film's disc, which has titles 0 to 4) is left out of the job's features as Task 7's re-plan leaves it out, so the owner's one Feature is a lone theatrical cut with no edition and the plain path (choice 1, 8.4).

Insert this block into `crates/core/src/decision.rs` directly after the closing `}` of `track_confidence` (before the blank line and `#[cfg(test)]`):

```rust

/// Everything 6.4 step 11 decides from: the plan of 6.1 step 5 with the planned title being decided and its scan
/// title, the facts the file phase measured (6.4 steps 9 to 10a), the TMDb record for naming, the library facts (8.4,
/// 7), the rip's review reasons and read errors (6.2 step 7, 6.3), the owner's review decisions (spec 11) and the
/// settings. Spec 6.4 step 11. Def: T13. Use: T16.
pub struct DecisionInputs<'a> {
    /// The job's plan: its identity and title confidences, reviews, notes, wanted languages and titles.
    pub plan: &'a Plan,
    /// The scan the plan was made from: the owner's Assign titles leaves out a title it lacks, as Task 7's re-plan
    /// (`assigned_entries`) does (Open point 32).
    pub disc: &'a Disc,
    /// The title being decided; one of `plan.titles`.
    pub planned: &'a PlannedTitle,
    /// The scan title of `planned` (`planned.title == title.number`).
    pub title: &'a Title,
    /// 8.6's facts (MD5s, ffprobe profiles, TheDiscDB's title, content verdicts, remembered overrides); `decide` sets
    /// `reviewed` to `overrides.audio_of(title.number)` when overrides are given.
    pub audio: AudioFacts<'a>,
    /// 8.7's facts (events, removed streams, TheDiscDB's title, text decisions, remembered overrides); `decide` sets
    /// `reviewed` to `overrides.subtitles_of(title.number)` when overrides are given.
    pub subtitles: SubtitleFacts<'a>,
    /// The TMDb record for naming (None: no path can be built; the reviews already hold identity_unknown or _ambiguous).
    pub record: Option<&'a TmdbRecord>,
    /// 8.4's library facts and spec 7's path collision, read by phase 2 (RP18).
    pub library: &'a LibraryFacts,
    /// 6.2 step 7's outcome for this title's rip (verify_failed, read_errors) and 6.3's copy_hash_errors, carried in.
    pub rip_reviews: Vec<ReviewReason>,
    /// The rip's VerifyReport.read_errors (6.2 step 7 "with the error count and offsets").
    pub read_errors: Vec<ReadError>,
    /// The owner's review decisions (spec 11) at the disposition gate or on re-finalise.
    pub overrides: Option<&'a Overrides>,
    /// Spec 14; `decide` reads auto_threshold, movies_root and tv_root, and hands the rest to the rules it calls.
    pub settings: &'a Settings,
}

/// One title's file-phase decision (6.4 step 11). Not `Decision`, which is `subtitle::text::Decision`. Field order is
/// the document's key order. Def: T13. Use: T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct FileDecision {
    /// The planned title's key (spec 5).
    pub title_key: String,
    /// 8.6's decision, the owner's Override tracks applied.
    pub audio: AudioDecision,
    /// 8.7's decision, the owner's Override tracks applied. Its tracks' `default` stays false: the file's default
    /// subtitle is `layout`'s (8.10, `tracks::layout::default_subtitle`; the shared interfaces' doc of the field).
    pub subtitles: SubtitleDecision,
    /// 8.10's tracks of the final file.
    pub layout: Layout,
    /// 8.9's resolution label of the first video stream's height; None without a video height.
    pub resolution: Option<String>,
    /// 8.4's edition name as filed (through `edition_label`); None for an episode or an unnamed cut.
    pub edition: Option<String>,
    /// 8.9's final path; None when it cannot be built (no record, identity, root or video height, a record of the
    /// other kind than the role's, or an episode without season or episode number).
    pub path: Option<NamedPath>,
    pub confidences: Confidences,
    /// Sorted and unique (`review::sorted_unique`).
    pub reviews: Vec<ReviewReason>,
    /// The plan's notes, then the audio decision's, the subtitle decision's and the naming notes, in that order.
    pub notes: Vec<Noted>,
    /// The rip's read errors, carried unchanged (6.2 step 7).
    pub read_errors: Vec<ReadError>,
    pub disposition: Disposition,
}

/// Spec 11's Resolve collision "keep both": the new file's distinguishing label (`- 2160p 2`).
const KEEP_BOTH_COPY: u32 = 2;

/// 6.4 step 11 and 8.8: decide_audio (with the wanted languages of the identity the job is filed under: the plan's, or,
/// when the owner's Set identity names another work than the plan's and its record is given, `wanted_languages` of that
/// record's original language; R4, 8.6 "Languages") and decide_subtitles (facts with `reviewed` set from
/// `overrides.audio_of(title.number)` and `overrides.subtitles_of(title.number)`), layout, the path (movie_path for a
/// feature, tv_path for an episode, by the filed role: the owner's Assign titles when it names any title, which then wins
/// whole as in a re-plan (Err for a planned title it ignores or does not name), else the planned role; no path when the
/// record's kind does not match the role (a movie record for a feature, a show record for an episode); resolution from
/// title.video_height, the edition through edition_names and edition_label; a planned Episode with season None builds no
/// path (path None) and adds tv_unmapped;
/// overrides.collision KeepBoth (copy Some(2) while the collision exists) and Replace leave path_collision unraised;
/// Discard never reaches decide, the engine discards the job), the three confidences (identity and
/// title from the plan; identity 1.00 when overrides.identity is Some, title 1.00 when overrides.titles is not empty; track
/// = min(audio, subtitle) after the remembered and review overrides set the parts they cover to 1.00), reviews = plan's
/// (less the reasons the owner's review answers: identity_unknown and identity_ambiguous when overrides.identity is Some;
/// title_ambiguous, multiple_features, unnamed_cut and tv_unmapped when overrides.titles is not empty) + audio's +
/// subtitles' + rip_reviews + path_collision when library.path_collision (and not KeepBoth or Replace) + read_errors
/// exactly when `read_errors` is not empty, notes likewise, read_errors carried unchanged, disposition; NeedsReview
/// whenever path is None. Verification lowers no
/// confidence: a failed or read-error rip holds the job through its review reason, which has the same effect on the
/// disposition as a confidence below auto_threshold (8.8). The owner's Assign titles, when it names any title, gives
/// the role the title is filed under exactly as Task 7's re-plan applies it (Open point 32), and that role chooses
/// movie_path or tv_path; a decision without a path is NeedsReview (a job with no final path cannot be filed; Open point
/// 38). Err for a planned title that is not in the plan or not the scan title given, a title the owner ignored or left
/// out of an Assign titles, a discarded job, or a record of another identity than the job's. Def: T13. Use: T16.
pub fn decide(inputs: &DecisionInputs<'_>) -> Result<FileDecision, String> {
    let plan = inputs.plan;
    let planned = inputs.planned;
    let title = inputs.title;
    let settings = inputs.settings;
    let overrides = inputs.overrides;
    if !plan.titles.iter().any(|entry| entry == planned) {
        return Err(format!("the plan holds no title {} with key {}", planned.title, planned.key));
    }
    if planned.title != title.number {
        return Err(format!(
            "planned title {} ({}) cannot be decided from scan title {}",
            planned.title, planned.key, title.number
        ));
    }
    let collision = overrides.and_then(|given| given.collision);
    if collision == Some(Collision::Discard) {
        return Err(format!(
            "the owner discarded the job (spec 11 Resolve collision), so title {} ({}) is not decided",
            planned.title, planned.key
        ));
    }
    let role = filed_role(planned, overrides)?;
    let identity = overrides.and_then(|given| given.identity).or(plan.identity.tmdb);
    let record = naming_record(inputs.record, identity)?;

    // 8.6 and 8.7, with the owner's Override tracks for this title (spec 11; Overrides holds them as entries keyed by
    // title and stream, and `audio_of` and `subtitles_of` give one title's by stream), which win over the remembered ones.
    let reviewed_audio = overrides.and_then(|given| given.audio_of(title.number));
    let reviewed_subtitles = overrides.and_then(|given| given.subtitles_of(title.number));
    let mut audio_facts = inputs.audio.clone();
    let mut subtitle_facts = inputs.subtitles.clone();
    if overrides.is_some() {
        audio_facts.reviewed = reviewed_audio.as_ref();
        subtitle_facts.reviewed = reviewed_subtitles.as_ref();
    }
    // R4, 8.6 "Languages": the wanted languages of the identity the job is filed under. The plan's were computed from
    // the planning identity's original language; when the owner's Set identity names another work, its record's original
    // language replaces them (a re-plan with the same overrides computes the same set, Open point 32).
    let wanted = match record {
        Some(record) if Some(record.identity) != plan.identity.tmdb => {
            wanted_languages(record.original_language.as_deref())
        }
        _ => plan.wanted.clone(),
    };
    let audio = decide_audio(title, &wanted, &audio_facts, settings);
    let subtitles = decide_subtitles(title, &subtitle_facts, settings);
    let track_layout = layout(title, &audio, &subtitles);

    // 8.9: the resolution label, the edition (8.4), the final path; spec 11's keep both adds the copy label while the
    // collision exists (with the colliding file gone, the plain path is free).
    let resolution = title.video_height().map(|height| resolution_label(height).to_string());
    let edition = match &role {
        PlannedRole::Feature { .. } => filed_edition(plan, inputs.disc, planned.title, overrides, inputs.library),
        PlannedRole::Episode(_) => None,
    };
    let copy = (collision == Some(Collision::KeepBoth) && inputs.library.path_collision).then_some(KEEP_BOTH_COPY);
    let Filing { path, notes: path_notes, unmapped } =
        filing(&role, record, resolution.as_deref(), edition.as_deref(), copy, settings);

    // 8.8: identity and title as planned, 1.00 where the owner's review covers them; track the lower of the two rules.
    let identity_reviewed = overrides.map_or(false, |given| given.identity.is_some());
    let titles_reviewed = overrides.map_or(false, |given| !given.titles.is_empty());
    let confidences = Confidences {
        identity: if identity_reviewed { REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE } else { plan.identity_confidence },
        title: if titles_reviewed { REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE } else { plan.title_confidence },
        track: track_confidence(&audio, &subtitles),
    };

    // 8.8's review reasons: the plan's (less those the owner's Set identity or Assign titles answers), the two rules',
    // the rip's; read_errors exactly when the rip logged some.
    let answered = |reason: &ReviewReason| {
        (identity_reviewed && matches!(reason, ReviewReason::IdentityUnknown | ReviewReason::IdentityAmbiguous))
            || (titles_reviewed
                && matches!(
                    reason,
                    ReviewReason::TitleAmbiguous
                        | ReviewReason::MultipleFeatures
                        | ReviewReason::UnnamedCut
                        | ReviewReason::TvUnmapped
                ))
    };
    let mut reasons: Vec<ReviewReason> = plan
        .reviews
        .iter()
        .filter(|reason| !answered(*reason))
        .chain(&audio.reviews)
        .chain(&subtitles.reviews)
        .chain(&inputs.rip_reviews)
        .copied()
        .filter(|reason| *reason != ReviewReason::ReadErrors)
        .collect();
    if unmapped {
        reasons.push(ReviewReason::TvUnmapped);
    }
    let resolved = matches!(collision, Some(Collision::KeepBoth) | Some(Collision::Replace));
    if inputs.library.path_collision && !resolved {
        reasons.push(ReviewReason::PathCollision);
    }
    if !inputs.read_errors.is_empty() {
        reasons.push(ReviewReason::ReadErrors);
    }
    let reviews = sorted_unique(reasons);

    let mut notes: Vec<Noted> = plan.notes.iter().chain(&audio.notes).chain(&subtitles.notes).cloned().collect();
    notes.extend(path_notes);

    // 8.8's disposition; a job with no final path cannot be filed (Open point 38).
    let outcome = if path.is_some() { disposition(&confidences, &reviews, settings) } else { Disposition::NeedsReview };
    Ok(FileDecision {
        title_key: planned.key.clone(),
        audio,
        subtitles,
        layout: track_layout,
        resolution,
        edition,
        path,
        confidences,
        reviews,
        notes,
        read_errors: inputs.read_errors.clone(),
        disposition: outcome,
    })
}

/// What the naming step gave: the final path when it could be built, the naming notes (8.9's compat_tag_omitted),
/// and whether an episode lacked its season or its episode numbers (8.5's tv_unmapped).
struct Filing {
    path: Option<NamedPath>,
    notes: Vec<Noted>,
    unmapped: bool,
}

/// The role the planned title is filed under (Open point 32). The owner's Assign titles, when it names any title, wins
/// whole, as Task 7's re-plan applies it (`assigned_roles`): the title's assignment, with Err for a title it ignores and
/// for a planned title it does not name (nothing is filed for either). Without it, the plan's role. A planned episode
/// without a season takes the owner's season (8.5 "review asks for it").
fn filed_role(planned: &PlannedTitle, overrides: Option<&Overrides>) -> Result<PlannedRole, String> {
    let assigned = overrides.filter(|given| !given.titles.is_empty());
    let mut role = match assigned {
        None => planned.role.clone(),
        Some(assigned) => {
            let given = assigned.title_role(planned.title).ok_or_else(|| {
                format!(
                    "the owner's Assign titles does not name title {} ({}), so nothing is filed for it",
                    planned.title, planned.key
                )
            })?;
            assigned_role(planned.title, given).ok_or_else(|| {
                format!(
                    "the owner's Assign titles ignores title {} ({}), so nothing is filed for it",
                    planned.title, planned.key
                )
            })?
        }
    };
    if let PlannedRole::Episode(episode) = &mut role {
        if episode.season.is_none() {
            episode.season = overrides.and_then(|given| given.season);
        }
    }
    Ok(role)
}

/// Spec 11's Assign titles as a planned role: a feature or named cut through `plan::assigned_feature` (the one mapping,
/// which Task 7's re-plan also calls), or episodes (with no name of their own, as Task 7's `assigned_entries` builds
/// them; `episode_name` then takes TMDb's); None for Ignored.
fn assigned_role(number: u32, role: &TitleRole) -> Option<PlannedRole> {
    if let Some(feature) = assigned_feature(number, role) {
        return Some(PlannedRole::Feature { edition: feature.edition });
    }
    match role {
        TitleRole::Episodes { season, episodes } => {
            Some(PlannedRole::Episode(Episode { season: Some(*season), episodes: episodes.clone(), name: None }))
        }
        TitleRole::Feature | TitleRole::Cut { .. } | TitleRole::Ignored => None,
    }
}

/// The record naming may use (8.9 "Title and year always come from the same TMDb record as the ID"): the given record
/// when it is the identity's; None without a record or without an identity; Err for a record of another identity.
fn naming_record<'r>(
    record: Option<&'r TmdbRecord>,
    identity: Option<TmdbIdentity>,
) -> Result<Option<&'r TmdbRecord>, String> {
    match (record, identity) {
        (Some(record), Some(identity)) if record.identity == identity => Ok(Some(record)),
        (Some(record), Some(identity)) => Err(format!(
            "the TMDb record is {} {} but the job's identity is {} {}: title and year come from the identity's own \
             record (spec 8.9)",
            record.identity.kind.as_str(),
            record.identity.id,
            identity.kind.as_str(),
            identity.id
        )),
        _ => Ok(None),
    }
}

/// 8.4's edition name of feature `number` as filed: `edition_names` over the job's features with the library facts of
/// decide time, then `edition_label` (sanitised, 32 characters; an empty label is no edition).
fn filed_edition(
    plan: &Plan,
    disc: &Disc,
    number: u32,
    overrides: Option<&Overrides>,
    library: &LibraryFacts,
) -> Option<String> {
    let features = job_features(plan, disc, overrides);
    let index = features.iter().position(|feature| feature.title == number)?;
    let name = edition_names(&features, library).into_iter().nth(index).flatten()?;
    let label = edition_label(&name);
    if label.is_empty() {
        None
    } else {
        Some(label)
    }
}

/// The job's features and cuts for 8.4 (choice 2). The owner's Assign titles, when it names any title, wins whole: its
/// features and cuts in title order through `plan::assigned_feature`, as Task 7's `assigned_entries` builds them. Else the
/// plan's features in plan order. A planned feature holds Task 7's filed name, so it is theatrical when that name names
/// the theatrical cut (`is_theatrical`), and when it has no name only in a plan of one feature: in a plan of two or more,
/// Task 7 names the theatrical cut, and a feature left without a name is an unnamed cut, a structural rival or a cut
/// whose earlier filed copy had no edition, which keeps no edition until the owner names it (8.4). An assigned title the
/// scan lacks is left out, as Task 7's `assigned_entries` leaves it out (Open point 32).
fn job_features(plan: &Plan, disc: &Disc, overrides: Option<&Overrides>) -> Vec<Feature> {
    if let Some(titles) = overrides.map(|given| &given.titles).filter(|titles| !titles.is_empty()) {
        // A title the scan lacks is left out, as Task 7's assigned_entries leaves it out (Open point 32).
        return titles
            .iter()
            .filter(|entry| disc.titles.contains_key(&entry.title))
            .filter_map(|entry| assigned_feature(entry.title, &entry.role))
            .collect();
    }
    let planned_features =
        plan.titles.iter().filter(|entry| matches!(entry.role, PlannedRole::Feature { .. })).count();
    plan.titles
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|entry| match &entry.role {
            PlannedRole::Feature { edition } => Some(Feature {
                title: entry.title,
                edition: edition.clone(),
                theatrical: match edition.as_deref() {
                    Some(name) => is_theatrical(Some(name)),
                    None => planned_features < 2,
                },
                siblings: Vec::new(),
            }),
            PlannedRole::Episode(_) => None,
        })
        .collect()
}

/// The final path of 8.9 for the role: a feature through `movie_path` under settings.movies_root (needs a movie record
/// and a resolution), an episode through `tv_path` under settings.tv_root (needs a show record, a season and an episode
/// number; without the last two it is unmapped, 8.5). A record of the other kind builds no path: TMDb's two kinds number
/// their records separately (8.1), so a movie's ID would name a show folder, or a show's ID a movie folder (choice 1).
fn filing(
    role: &PlannedRole,
    record: Option<&TmdbRecord>,
    resolution: Option<&str>,
    edition: Option<&str>,
    copy: Option<u32>,
    settings: &Settings,
) -> Filing {
    let unbuilt = |unmapped: bool| Filing { path: None, notes: Vec::new(), unmapped };
    match role {
        PlannedRole::Feature { .. } => match (record, settings.movies_root.as_deref(), resolution) {
            (Some(record), Some(root), Some(resolution)) if record.identity.kind == TmdbKind::Movie => {
                let (path, notes) = movie_path(root, &record.work(), resolution, edition, copy, settings);
                Filing { path: Some(path), notes, unmapped: false }
            }
            _ => unbuilt(false),
        },
        PlannedRole::Episode(episode) => {
            let season = match episode.season {
                Some(season) if !episode.episodes.is_empty() => season,
                _ => return unbuilt(true),
            };
            match (record, settings.tv_root.as_deref()) {
                (Some(record), Some(root)) if record.identity.kind == TmdbKind::Tv => {
                    let name = episode_name(episode, season, record);
                    let (path, notes) =
                        tv_path(root, &record.work(), season, &episode.episodes, name.as_deref(), copy, settings);
                    Filing { path: Some(path), notes, unmapped: false }
                }
                _ => unbuilt(false),
            }
        }
    }
}

/// The episode title of 8.9: the plan's (TheDiscDB's item title), else TMDb's name of the episode when the title holds
/// exactly one episode; none for a multi-episode title without a name of its own.
fn episode_name(episode: &Episode, season: u32, record: &TmdbRecord) -> Option<String> {
    if episode.name.is_some() {
        return episode.name.clone();
    }
    let [only] = episode.episodes.as_slice() else {
        return None;
    };
    record.season(season)?.episodes.iter().find(|candidate| candidate.episode_number == *only)?.name.clone()
}
```

The durations are attribute 9 in seconds: 1:58:42 is 7122, 2:06:10 is 7570, 1:35:00 is 5700, 1:38:12 is 5892, 0:21:37 is 1297, 0:43:05 is 2585. The signatures are spec 5's (type, language, codec family, channels, position among identical streams); title 2's Spanish Dolby Digital stereo stream is dropped by 8.6 step 1 (a language that is not wanted on an English work) and its Spanish PGS stream by 8.7's first sentence. The owner's Commentary mark names title 2's English Dolby Digital 5.1, which 8.6 keeps, so the `Reviewed` drop and the remembered `Commentary` can only come from the override. The owner's Assign titles is remembered whole (choice 9), so planned title 0, which it does not name, is left out; title 3 is outside the plan and stored as `Ignored`. An assigned title the scan lacks (title 9) is left out, not refused (choice 9), as Task 7's re-plan leaves it out. A planned feature without an edition beside the "Theatrical Cut" is refused until the owner names it (choice 9). On the DVD, both titles have the segment map "1", the duration 1:38:12 and no attribute 16, so only attribute 24 ("01" against "02") tells title 0 from title 1 (Review Focus 1): the remembered title matches title 0 and not title 1.

```rust

/// Spec 11 "Remember": the decisions of a reviewed job as a remembered-decisions file: the identity
/// (overrides.identity, else plan.identity.tmdb; Err without one), the titles as RememberedTitles (source file, attribute
/// 24, segment map, seconds and role): the owner's Assign titles whole, in title order (Ignored included, a title the scan lacks left out), when it names
/// any title, else every planned title under its planned role (Err for an episode without a season or episode numbers,
/// and for a feature without an edition in a plan of two or more features: an unnamed cut or structural rival the owner
/// must name first, 8.4), every kept and dropped audio and subtitle stream of `decisions` as an override entry keyed by
/// `remembered::signature`. The owner's Assign titles is stored as the decision and a re-plan apply it (whole: a planned
/// title it does not name is not remembered, and a title it names that the scan lacks is left out); a planned feature without an edition beside another feature is not
/// `TitleRole::Feature`, which means the theatrical or main cut and would come back as a second "Theatrical Cut". A kept
/// audio track is `Keep` with its 0-based final position and its default flag, a dropped one `Drop` (or `Commentary`
/// when the owner marked it so); a kept subtitle track is `Keep` with its role, a dropped one `Drop`; a signature
/// already stored is not stored again (the first decision wins). Err for a job without an identity, a planned episode
/// without a season or episode numbers, an unnamed planned cut, a title without a duration, a decision whose key is not
/// in the plan, or a stream its scan title lacks. Spec 5, 11. Def: T13. Use: phase 2.
pub fn remember(
    fingerprint: &str,
    disc: &Disc,
    plan: &Plan,
    decisions: &[FileDecision],
    overrides: &Overrides,
) -> Result<Remembered, String> {
    let tmdb = overrides.identity.or(plan.identity.tmdb).ok_or_else(|| {
        "the job has no TMDb identity to remember: set its identity first (spec 11 Remember)".to_string()
    })?;

    // The titles (spec 5): the owner's Assign titles, when it names any title, whole and in title order (Ignored
    // included), as the decision and a re-plan apply it; else every planned title under its planned role.
    let mut titles = Vec::new();
    if overrides.titles.is_empty() {
        let features = plan.titles.iter().filter(|entry| matches!(entry.role, PlannedRole::Feature { .. })).count();
        for planned in &plan.titles {
            let role = stored_role(&planned.role, overrides.season, features).ok_or_else(|| match &planned.role {
                PlannedRole::Feature { .. } => format!(
                    "planned title {} ({}) is a cut without an edition name to remember: name it first (spec 8.4)",
                    planned.title, planned.key
                ),
                PlannedRole::Episode(_) => format!(
                    "planned title {} ({}) has no season and episode numbers to remember: assign them first (spec 8.5)",
                    planned.title, planned.key
                ),
            })?;
            titles.push(remembered_title(disc.title(planned.title)?, role)?);
        }
    } else {
        // A title the scan lacks is left out, as the decision and Task 7's re-plan leave it out (choice 9).
        for assigned in overrides.titles.iter().filter(|assigned| disc.titles.contains_key(&assigned.title)) {
            titles.push(remembered_title(disc.title(assigned.title)?, assigned.role.clone())?);
        }
    }

    let mut audio: Vec<AudioOverrideEntry> = Vec::new();
    let mut subtitles: Vec<SubtitleOverrideEntry> = Vec::new();
    for decision in decisions {
        let planned = plan
            .titles
            .iter()
            .find(|entry| entry.key == decision.title_key)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("decision {} is not a title of the plan", decision.title_key))?;
        let title = disc.title(planned.title)?;
        let reviewed_audio = overrides.audio_of(planned.title).unwrap_or_default();
        for (order, track) in decision.audio.kept.iter().enumerate() {
            let action = AudioOverride::Keep { order: order as u32, default: track.default };
            push_audio(&mut audio, stream_signature(title, track.stream)?, action);
        }
        for (stream, _) in &decision.audio.dropped {
            let action = match reviewed_audio.get(stream) {
                Some(AudioOverride::Commentary) => AudioOverride::Commentary,
                _ => AudioOverride::Drop,
            };
            push_audio(&mut audio, stream_signature(title, *stream)?, action);
        }
        for track in &decision.subtitles.kept {
            let action = SubtitleOverride::Keep { role: track.role };
            push_subtitle(&mut subtitles, stream_signature(title, track.stream)?, action);
        }
        for (stream, _) in &decision.subtitles.dropped {
            push_subtitle(&mut subtitles, stream_signature(title, *stream)?, SubtitleOverride::Drop);
        }
    }
    Ok(Remembered { fingerprint: fingerprint.to_string(), tmdb, titles, audio, subtitles })
}

/// A planned role as spec 5 stores it: the feature of a plan of one feature, a cut with its edition name ("Theatrical
/// Cut" included), or the episodes with the episode's season, else the owner's season. None for a feature without an
/// edition in a plan of `features >= 2` features (an unnamed cut or a structural rival, 8.3 and 8.4: `TitleRole::Feature`
/// means the theatrical or main cut, and Task 7 would plan it back as a second "Theatrical Cut"), and for an episode
/// without a season or without an episode number.
fn stored_role(role: &PlannedRole, season: Option<u32>, features: usize) -> Option<TitleRole> {
    match role {
        PlannedRole::Feature { edition: None } if features >= 2 => None,
        PlannedRole::Feature { edition: None } => Some(TitleRole::Feature),
        PlannedRole::Feature { edition: Some(edition) } => Some(TitleRole::Cut { edition: edition.clone() }),
        PlannedRole::Episode(episode) => {
            let season = episode.season.or(season)?;
            if episode.episodes.is_empty() {
                return None;
            }
            Some(TitleRole::Episodes { season, episodes: episode.episodes.clone() })
        }
    }
}

/// Spec 5's "for each title its source file, segment map, duration, role", with attribute 24 for a DVD (Review Focus 1).
fn remembered_title(title: &Title, role: TitleRole) -> Result<RememberedTitle, String> {
    let seconds =
        title.seconds.ok_or_else(|| format!("title {} has no duration (attribute 9) to remember", title.number))?;
    Ok(RememberedTitle {
        source_file: title.source_file.clone(),
        dvd_title: title.dvd_title.clone(),
        segment_map: title.segment_map.clone(),
        seconds,
        role,
    })
}

/// The signature of the title's stream `stream` (a scan stream number), through `remembered::signature`.
fn stream_signature(title: &Title, stream: u32) -> Result<StreamSignature, String> {
    let index = title
        .streams
        .iter()
        .position(|candidate| candidate.number == stream)
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("title {} has no stream {}", title.number, stream))?;
    Ok(signature(&title.streams, index))
}

/// Adds an audio override unless its signature is stored already (the first decision wins).
fn push_audio(entries: &mut Vec<AudioOverrideEntry>, signature: StreamSignature, action: AudioOverride) {
    if !entries.iter().any(|entry| entry.signature == signature) {
        entries.push(AudioOverrideEntry { signature, action });
    }
}

/// Adds a subtitle override unless its signature is stored already (the first decision wins).
fn push_subtitle(entries: &mut Vec<SubtitleOverrideEntry>, signature: StreamSignature, action: SubtitleOverride) {
    if !entries.iter().any(|entry| entry.signature == signature) {
        entries.push(SubtitleOverrideEntry { signature, action });
    }
}
```

```rust
/// An audio override (spec 11 "Override tracks": keep with order and default, drop, or mark as commentary, which drops it). Def: T6. Use: T8, T13, T14.

/// One title of the owner's Assign titles: the scan title number and its role, flattened into one JSON object

pub struct TitleOverrideEntry { pub title: u32, #[serde(flatten)] pub role: TitleRole }
/// One track of the owner's Override tracks: the scan title and stream numbers and the action, flattened into one JSON

// lazymkv_core::review (T1)
/// Spec 8.8's review reasons, with their serde and as_str spellings (the snake_case strings of the table). Def: T1. Use: T4 to T18.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum ReviewReason {
    IdentityUnknown, IdentityAmbiguous,            // 8.1
    TitleAmbiguous, MultipleFeatures, UnnamedCut,  // 8.3
    TvUnmapped,                                    // 8.5
    OriginalLanguageMissing, NoWantedAudio,        // 8.6
    AudioReferenceUnclear,                         // 8.6 veto, D21
    CommentaryDetected,                            // 8.6 content, RP7, row 13's fallback
    SubtitleAmbiguous,                             // 8.7
    PathCollision,                                 // 7, 8.9
    CopyHashErrors,                                // 6.3
    VerifyFailed, ReadErrors,                      // 6.2
}
impl ReviewReason { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; pub const ALL: [ReviewReason; 15]; }
impl std::str::FromStr for ReviewReason { type Err = String; fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<ReviewReason, String>; }

/// The notes of spec 8.6, 8.7, 8.9, 7, 6.3, 10.2, D9 and RP7. Def: T1. Use: T5, T8, T10, T11, T13, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Note {
    PossibleCommentary,          // 8.6 step 6, naming the track
    PossibleAudioDescription,    // RP7: ad-pattern and note-ad verdicts
    LosslessOriginalAvailable,   // 8.6 step 6
    NoEnglishAudio,              // 8.6 step 6
    LossyBeforeLossless,         // D9's first default: a lossy track with more channels placed before a lossless one
    PartialSubtitleDropped,      // 8.7 "Other tracks", naming the track
    SubtitleTextDisagrees,       // 8.7 "Text"
    CompatTagOmitted,            // 8.9
    OldFileKept,                 // 7
    TuningEvidencePending,       // 7
    DirectModeFallback,          // 6.3 step 6a and its second read failure: "a note records the switch"
    LabelRuleUnavailable,        // 8.3 rule 2 and 10.2 ToolMissing: MakeMKV did not report Java, "a note records why"
}
impl Note { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; pub const ALL: [Note; 12]; }
impl std::str::FromStr for Note { type Err = String; fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<Note, String>; }
```

Produces (exactly the `core::job (Task 14)` entry of the Shared interfaces, with its reducer table; phase 2's engine is the caller):

```rust
/// Spec 10.1's fixed waits: AwaitingNetwork "retried every 10 minutes", AwaitingLookup "retried hourly". Def: T14. Use: T14.
pub const NETWORK_RETRY_MIN: u32 = 10;
pub const LOOKUP_RETRY_MIN: u32 = 60;

/// Spec 10.2's classes. Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "PascalCase")]
pub enum FailureClass { DriveIncapable, MediaReadError, Licence, NeedsMakeMkvUpdate, NeedsNetwork, Output, LookupUnavailable, ToolMissing, Unknown }
impl FailureClass { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; pub const ALL: [FailureClass; 9]; }

/// What an Output failure was (10.2's Output row: "share unreachable, out of space, or a write error"). Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum OutputCause { ShareUnreachable, OutOfSpace, WriteError }

/// A failing step's class, and for Output its cause (None for every other class). Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Failure { pub class: FailureClass, pub output: Option<OutputCause> }

/// The programs 10.2's ToolMissing row names (4.4, plus ffmpeg of 6.4 step 10a). Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Tool { Makemkvcon, Mkvmerge, Ffprobe, Ffmpeg, Java }
impl Tool { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; pub const ALL: [Tool; 5]; }

/// Why a job is held (10.1's two NeedsReview rows). Def: T14. Use: T14.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Held { AfterCopy, DispositionGate }

/// 10.1's states. `Planned` carries the mode the plan chose; `RipVerified` and `Ejected` whether they follow a whole-disc
/// copy (then the job is held next, 6.3 step 7) or a Direct rip (then it waits for the file-phase slot, spec 6); waiting
/// states carry the state they return to; `Decided` whether the owner approved the job (8.8); Failed carries its class
/// and the state that failed. Disc-phase states: Detected, Fingerprinted, Scanned, Planned, Ripping, Copying,
/// RipVerified. File-phase states: Ejected, Extracting, Inspecting, Decided, Remuxing, Verified.
/// Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "state")]
pub enum State {
    Detected, Fingerprinted, Scanned, Planned { mode: Mode }, Ripping, Copying, RipVerified { after_copy: bool }, Ejected { after_copy: bool },
    Inspecting, Decided { approved: bool }, Remuxing, Verified, Filed,
    NeedsReview { held: Held }, Extracting,
    AwaitingShare { return_to: Box<State> }, AwaitingSpace { return_to: Box<State> }, AwaitingMakeMkv { return_to: Box<State> },
    AwaitingNetwork { return_to: Box<State> }, AwaitingLookup { return_to: Box<State> }, AwaitingTool { return_to: Box<State> },
    Failed { class: FailureClass, from: Box<State> }, Discarded,
}
impl State { pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str; pub fn is_disc_phase(&self) -> bool; pub fn is_file_phase(&self) -> bool; pub fn is_waiting(&self) -> bool; }

/// The `reason` of spec 12's `waiting` event. Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum WaitReason { Share, Space, Makemkv, Network, Lookup, Tool }

/// Spec 12's notification events, a closed set (the engine adds job_id, fingerprint, title, drive, message, time). Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "event")]
pub enum NotifyEvent {
    DiscDone, AlreadyRipped, Filed,
    NeedsReview { reasons: Vec<ReviewReason> },
    Waiting { reason: WaitReason },
    Resumed,
    Failed { class: FailureClass },
    EjectFailed,
}

/// 10.1's events, plus the engine's answers the reducer needs to walk the main line (SpaceOk for the space checks of 7,
/// FilePhaseSlot for spec 6's one-job file phase, which phase 2 also grants by delivering ReviewApproved, ReFinalise, or
/// Retry of a job that failed in its file phase; HoldForReview for 6.3 step 7's hold after a copy; FileDone for the rename
/// of 6.4 step 14). Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "event")]
pub enum Event {
    MediaArrived, MediaRemoved,
    FingerprintDone, FingerprintFailed { failure: Failure },
    ScanDone, ScanFailed { failure: Failure },
    PlanDone { mode: Mode }, PlanFailed { failure: Failure },
    SpaceOk, SpaceShort, SpaceFreed,
    TitleRipped, TitleRipFailed { failure: Failure },
    /// `last`: no planned (or assigned) title is left to rip or extract.
    TitleVerified { last: bool },
    /// 6.2 step 7: a mismatch; the first is re-ripped, the second goes on (the engine records verify_failed for the decision).
    TitleVerifyFailed { second: bool, last: bool },
    /// `hash_errors`: MSG:5079 (6.3 step 6); the engine carries copy_hash_errors into HoldForReview's reasons.
    CopyDone { scan_listed_titles: bool, hash_errors: bool }, CopyFailed { failure: Failure, second: bool },
    TitleExtracted, ExtractFailed { failure: Failure },
    Ejected, EjectFailed,
    HoldForReview { reasons: Vec<ReviewReason> },
    FilePhaseSlot,
    ProbeDone, ProbeFailed { failure: Failure },
    DecisionDone { disposition: Disposition, reasons: Vec<ReviewReason> }, DecisionFailed { failure: Failure },
    RemuxDone, RemuxFailed { failure: Failure },
    FileVerified, FileVerifyFailed { failure: Failure },
    FileDone, FileFailed { failure: Failure },
    ShareLost, ShareBack,
    LicenceMessage, VersionMessage, MakeMkvChanged, NetworkNeeded, NetworkRetry,
    LookupPending, LookupAnswered,
    ToolMissing { tool: Tool }, ToolFound { tool: Tool },
    /// Spec 11 Approve. Phase 2 delivers it only once spec 6's file-phase slot is free for this job, as FilePhaseSlot is for a
    /// Direct job in Ejected; the job holds the slot until it reaches Filed, NeedsReview, Failed or Discarded.
    ReviewApproved { overrides: Overrides },
    ReviewDiscarded,
    /// Spec 11 Retry. For a job that failed in its file phase, phase 2 delivers it only once spec 6's file-phase slot is free
    /// for this job, as for ReviewApproved.
    Retry,
    RipAgain,
    /// Spec 11 Re-finalise. Phase 2 delivers it only once spec 6's file-phase slot is free for this job, as FilePhaseSlot is
    /// for a Direct job in Ejected; the job holds the slot until it reaches Filed, NeedsReview, Failed or Discarded.
    ReFinalise,
    EngineRestart { disc_present: bool },
}

/// 10.1's actions, plus Fingerprint and Plan (the main line implies them: 10.1's list omits them), CheckSpace (section 7),
/// the resume housekeeping of "Resuming after a restart", and ArmRipAgain (6.1 step 2: the engine marks the job so the next
/// insertion of its fingerprint starts a new job). RunScan also starts 6.1 step 3's database lookups beside the scan.
/// Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "action")]
pub enum Action {
    Fingerprint, RunScan, Plan, CheckSpace, RipTitle, CopyDisc, ExtractTitle, VerifyFile, Eject, Probe, ExtractSubtitleEvidence, Decide, Remux, File,
    Notify { event: NotifyEvent }, StartTimer { minutes: u32 }, DeleteJobData,
    EmptyTitleDirectory, EmptyCopyDirectory, DeletePartialFile, WaitForDisc, RecordNote { note: Note }, ArmRipAgain,
}

/// An event the state does not take. Def: T14. Use: T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Rejected { pub state: State, pub event: Event }

/// A new job's first state and actions: (Detected, [Fingerprint]) (6.1 steps 1 and 2; the engine creates it on MediaArrived
/// when `job_lookup` gives NewJob, or before the fingerprint is known). Def: T14. Use: phase 2.
pub fn new_job() -> (State, Vec<Action>);
/// (new state, actions) for every row of the reducer table below; every other pair is Rejected. Def: T14. Use: phase 2.
pub fn reduce(state: &State, event: &Event) -> Result<(State, Vec<Action>), Rejected>;
/// "Resuming after a restart" (and the actions of a waiting state's return): Detected [Fingerprint]; Fingerprinted
/// [RunScan]; Scanned [Plan]; Planned [CheckSpace]; Decided { .. } [Decide] (Decided { approved: true } may be entered
/// with Decide pending, after approval or re-finalise; Decided { approved: false } decides again too, and is gated
/// again on NeedsReview); Ripping [EmptyTitleDirectory, RipTitle]; Extracting [EmptyTitleDirectory, ExtractTitle];
/// Copying [EmptyCopyDirectory, CopyDisc]; RipVerified (either after_copy) [Eject]; Inspecting [Probe]; Remuxing [DeletePartialFile, Remux];
/// Verified [File]; Ejected nothing (it waits for FilePhaseSlot or HoldForReview); a disc-phase state with `disc_present`
/// false [WaitForDisc]; waiting, held, failed, filed and discarded states nothing, except AwaitingNetwork
/// [StartTimer { minutes: NETWORK_RETRY_MIN }] and AwaitingLookup [StartTimer { minutes: LOOKUP_RETRY_MIN }]. The state is
/// returned unchanged. Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
pub fn resume(state: &State, disc_present: bool) -> (State, Vec<Action>);
/// 10.2's Result column: DriveIncapable, MediaReadError and Unknown give Failed { class, from }; Licence and
/// NeedsMakeMkvUpdate AwaitingMakeMkv; NeedsNetwork AwaitingNetwork; Output with OutOfSpace AwaitingSpace, with
/// ShareUnreachable, WriteError or None AwaitingShare (a write error is treated as a share fault, 10.2's last paragraph);
/// LookupUnavailable AwaitingLookup; ToolMissing AwaitingTool; each waiting state returning to `from`. Def: T14. Use: T14.
pub fn failure_outcome(failure: Failure, from: &State) -> State;
/// 10.2's last paragraph, checked in this order: the share unreachable gives Output { ShareUnreachable }; out of space
/// Output { OutOfSpace }; a write error Output { WriteError }; read errors seen, a stalled read, or a process that did not
/// exit (10.2's table, 10.4) with the share healthy MediaReadError: pass `read_errors` true for each; else Unknown.
/// Def: T14. Use: T14, phase 2.
pub fn classify_title_failure(share_healthy: bool, out_of_space: bool, write_error: bool, read_errors: bool) -> Failure;

/// Spec 5: `<fingerprint>-<n>`, n one more than the highest n among `earlier` ids of this fingerprint (ids of other
/// fingerprints and malformed ids ignored), 1 for the first. Def: T14. Use: phase 2.
pub fn job_id(fingerprint: &str, earlier: &[&str]) -> String;
/// Spec 6.1 step 2's three outcomes. Def: T14. Use: phase 2.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum JobLookup { Resume(String), AlreadyRipped(String), NewJob }
/// Spec 6.1 step 2 over the earlier jobs of this fingerprint as (job id, state, rip again armed); the one with the highest n
/// decides: Resume when it has not finished its disc phase (a disc-phase state, or a waiting state returning to one) or is
/// Failed { MediaReadError }; AlreadyRipped when it is past the disc phase (a file-phase state, NeedsReview, Filed, a
/// waiting state returning to a file-phase state, or Failed with another class from a file-phase state) and not armed;
/// NewJob otherwise (armed, Discarded, Failed with another class from a disc-phase state, or no earlier job). Def: T14.
/// Use: phase 2.
pub fn job_lookup(earlier: &[(String, State, bool)]) -> JobLookup;
```

The reducer table (`reduce`, spec 10.1 and 10.2). "Return" means: the waiting state's `return_to`, with `resume(return_to, true)`'s actions followed by `Notify { Resumed }`; phase 2 performs a disc-phase action only with the job's disc in a drive, and when the disc is gone it performs none and feeds `MediaRemoved`, which gives `[WaitForDisc]` (it does not feed the media removal its own `Eject` causes). "Outcome" means: `failure_outcome(failure, state)`, with `[Notify { Failed { class } }]` for a Failed state, and for a waiting state `[Notify { Waiting { reason } }]` preceded by `StartTimer { minutes: NETWORK_RETRY_MIN }` for AwaitingNetwork or `StartTimer { minutes: LOOKUP_RETRY_MIN }` for AwaitingLookup.

| From | Event | To | Actions |
|---|---|---|---|
| (new job, `new_job`) | | `Detected` | `[Fingerprint]` |
| `Detected` | `FingerprintDone` | `Fingerprinted` | `[RunScan]` |
| `Fingerprinted` | `ScanDone` | `Scanned` | `[Plan]` |
| `Scanned` | `PlanDone { mode }` | `Planned { mode }` | `[CheckSpace]` |
| `Planned { Direct }` | `SpaceOk` | `Ripping` | `[RipTitle]` |
| `Planned { Copy }` (10.1 "title confidence below threshold") | `SpaceOk` | `Copying` | `[CopyDisc]` |
| `Ripping` | `TitleRipped` | `Ripping` | `[VerifyFile]` |
| `Ripping` | `TitleVerified { last: false }`, or `TitleVerifyFailed { second: true, last: false }` | `Ripping` | `[RipTitle]` (the next title) |
| `Ripping` | `TitleVerifyFailed { second: false, .. }` | `Ripping` | `[RipTitle]` (the same title again, 6.2 step 7) |
| `Ripping` | `TitleVerified { last: true }`, or `TitleVerifyFailed { second: true, last: true }` | `RipVerified { after_copy: false }` | `[Eject]` |
| `RipVerified { after_copy: false }` | `Ejected` | `Ejected { after_copy: false }` | `[Notify { DiscDone }]` |
| `RipVerified { after_copy: false }` | `EjectFailed` | `Ejected { after_copy: false }` | `[Notify { EjectFailed }]` (the disc phase is over; the disc is removed by hand, 10.3, 12) |
| `Ejected { after_copy: false }` | `FilePhaseSlot` | `Inspecting` | `[Probe]` |
| `Inspecting` | `ProbeDone` | `Inspecting` | `[ExtractSubtitleEvidence, Decide]` (performed in order) |
| `Inspecting` | `DecisionDone { AutoFile, .. }` | `Decided { approved: false }` | `[CheckSpace]` |
| `Inspecting` | `DecisionDone { NeedsReview, reasons }` (10.1 "Decided, review reason or low confidence") | `NeedsReview { DispositionGate }` | `[Notify { NeedsReview { reasons } }]` |

| `Verified` | `FileDone` | `Filed` | `[Notify { Filed }]` |

| `RipVerified { after_copy: true }` | `Ejected` | `Ejected { after_copy: true }` | `[Notify { DiscDone }]` |
| `RipVerified { after_copy: true }` | `EjectFailed` | `Ejected { after_copy: true }` | `[Notify { EjectFailed }]` |

| `Copying` | `CopyFailed { failure, second: false }` | Outcome (a read failure: `Failed { MediaReadError, from: Copying }`) | as Outcome |
| `Copying` | `CopyFailed { failure: MediaReadError, second: true }` (10.1 "second read failure") | `Planned { Direct }` | `[RecordNote { DirectModeFallback }, CheckSpace]` |
| `NeedsReview { AfterCopy }` | `ReviewApproved { overrides }` | `Extracting` | `[CheckSpace]` |
| `Extracting` | `SpaceOk` | `Extracting` | `[ExtractTitle]` |
| `Extracting` | `TitleExtracted` | `Extracting` | `[VerifyFile]` |
| `Extracting` | `TitleVerified { last: false }` | `Extracting` | `[ExtractTitle]` |
| `Extracting` | `TitleVerified { last: true }` | `Inspecting` | `[Probe]` |

| `NeedsReview { .. }` | `ReviewDiscarded` | `Discarded` | `[DeleteJobData]` |
| `Filed` | `ReFinalise` | `Decided { approved: true }` | `[Decide]` |

| any disc- or file-phase state | `SpaceShort` | `AwaitingSpace { return_to: state }` | `[Notify { Waiting { Space } }]` |
| `AwaitingShare` / `AwaitingSpace` | `ShareBack` / `SpaceFreed` | Return | as Return |
| `Scanned`, `Ripping`, `Copying` | `LicenceMessage`, `VersionMessage` | `AwaitingMakeMkv { return_to: state }` | `[Notify { Waiting { Makemkv } }]` |
| `AwaitingMakeMkv` | `MakeMkvChanged` | Return | as Return |
| `Scanned`, `Ripping`, `Copying` (only these) | `NetworkNeeded` | `AwaitingNetwork { return_to: state }` | `[StartTimer { minutes: NETWORK_RETRY_MIN }, Notify { Waiting { Network } }]` |
| `AwaitingNetwork` | `NetworkRetry` | Return | as Return |
| `Ejected { .. }`, `Inspecting` | `LookupPending` | `AwaitingLookup { return_to: state }` | `[StartTimer { minutes: LOOKUP_RETRY_MIN }, Notify { Waiting { Lookup } }]` |

| any disc- or file-phase state | `ToolMissing { Mkvmerge }` | `AwaitingTool { return_to: state }` | `[Notify { Waiting { Tool } }]` |
| any file-phase state | `ToolMissing { Ffprobe }`, `ToolMissing { Ffmpeg }` | `AwaitingTool { return_to: state }` | `[Notify { Waiting { Tool } }]` |
| any disc-phase state | `ToolMissing { Ffprobe }`, `ToolMissing { Ffmpeg }` | unchanged (the disc phase runs; the job waits when it would enter Inspecting) | `[]` |
| any state | `ToolMissing { Java }` | unchanged | `[RecordNote { LabelRuleUnavailable }]` |
| `AwaitingTool` | `ToolFound { .. }` | Return | as Return |
| the state whose step failed, in the order of the events: `Detected`, `Fingerprinted`, `Scanned`, `Ripping`, `Extracting`, `Inspecting`, `Inspecting` or `Decided { .. }`, `Remuxing`, `Remuxing`, `Verified` | `FingerprintFailed`, `ScanFailed`, `PlanFailed`, `TitleRipFailed`, `ExtractFailed`, `ProbeFailed`, `DecisionFailed`, `RemuxFailed`, `FileVerifyFailed`, `FileFailed` | Outcome | as Outcome |

| `Failed { DriveIncapable, .. }` | `Retry` | Rejected (10.2 "no retry") | |

| any disc-phase state | `MediaRemoved` | unchanged | `[WaitForDisc]` |
| any disc-phase state | `MediaArrived` | unchanged | `resume(state, true)`'s actions |
| any state | `EngineRestart { disc_present }` | `resume(state, disc_present)` | its actions |

Beyond the shared entry, this task adds members the plan's conventions require of every closed set, which no other task depends on: `as_str`, `ALL` and `FromStr` for `OutputCause`, `Held` and `WaitReason`; `FromStr` for `FailureClass` and `Tool`; `NotifyEvent::as_str` (spec 12's `event` field); and a doc line on every variant of `FailureClass`, `OutputCause`, `Tool`, `Held`, `State`, `WaitReason`, `NotifyEvent`, `Event`, `Action` and `JobLookup`.

Where this task settles what the spec and the interfaces leave open (each choice is pinned by a test below):

1. **The table as disjoint rules.** `reduce` tries seven private rule functions in `RULES` (`any_state`, `direct_line`, `copy_line`, `review_line`, `waits`, `failures`, `disc_presence`), each holding a group of the table's rows. No pair of a state and an event is held by two rules, so the order of `RULES` is no precedence: `no_state_and_event_pair_is_held_by_two_rules` runs every one of 42 sample states against every one of 72 sample events and counts the rules that answer. Every pair no rule holds is `Rejected { state, event }` (the engine logs it and changes nothing).
2. **An extracted title that fails verification.** Spec 6.3 step 8 says each extracted title is "verified as in 6.2 step 7", which re-rips a title once and goes on after a second failure (the engine records `verify_failed`). The table's two `Extracting` rows for `TitleVerifyFailed` follow it: in `Extracting`, `TitleVerifyFailed { second: false, .. }` extracts the same title again, `{ second: true, last: false }` extracts the next, and `{ second: true, last: true }` goes on to `Inspecting` with `[Probe]`, as the `Ripping` rows do (`an_extracted_title_failing_verification_is_extracted_again_once_then_the_next_follows`, `the_last_extracted_title_verified_goes_on_to_inspecting_and_probes`).
3. **A second copy failure that is not a read failure.** The table switches to Direct mode only on `CopyFailed { failure: MediaReadError, second: true }` (10.1 "second read failure"); a second failure of any other class is the table's Outcome, as a first failure is (`a_second_copy_failure_that_is_not_a_read_failure_is_an_ordinary_outcome`).
4. **Timers after a restart.** A restart loses the engine's timers, so without a new one `AwaitingNetwork` ("retried every 10 minutes") and `AwaitingLookup` ("retried hourly") would never retry again. `resume` therefore gives `AwaitingNetwork` `[StartTimer { minutes: NETWORK_RETRY_MIN }]` and `AwaitingLookup` `[StartTimer { minutes: LOOKUP_RETRY_MIN }]`; every other waiting state still gives nothing (`resuming_a_wait_for_the_network_or_a_lookup_starts_its_retry_timer_again`). `reduce`'s Return never resumes a waiting state, so the table is unchanged.
5. **Which state each step failure comes from.** The table's row "the state whose step failed" lists, for each step failure, the state whose action starts that step: `FingerprintFailed` in `Detected` (it issued `Fingerprint`), `ScanFailed` in `Fingerprinted` (`RunScan`), `PlanFailed` in `Scanned` (`Plan`), `TitleRipFailed` in `Ripping`, `ExtractFailed` in `Extracting`, `ProbeFailed` in `Inspecting`, `DecisionFailed` in `Inspecting` and in `Decided` (either `approved` value: it issues `Decide` after approval and re-finalise, and again on a resume), `RemuxFailed` and `FileVerifyFailed` in `Remuxing` (`Remux`, then `VerifyFile`), `FileFailed` in `Verified` (`File`). From any other state the event is rejected (`a_step_failure_is_rejected_from_a_state_that_did_not_run_the_step`). A copy's failure is `copy_line`'s.
6. **Pairs the table leaves out are rejected, as the interface says.** Among them: `ToolMissing { Makemkvcon }` in a file-phase state other than `Extracting`; any `ToolMissing` but Java, `ShareLost` or `SpaceShort` for a held, filed, failed, discarded or waiting job; `MediaArrived` and `MediaRemoved` outside the disc phase, except `MediaArrived` for `Failed { MediaReadError }`; `RipAgain` in the disc phase. Each is pinned by a test whose name says it is rejected (for example `a_missing_makemkvcon_is_rejected_by_the_file_phase_states_that_do_not_run_it`).
7. **Job numbers.** `job_id` reads an earlier ID as the fingerprint, `-`, and one or more ASCII digits up to `u32::MAX` (`job_number`); anything else (another fingerprint, `ABC-`, `ABC-3-2`, `ABC-+4`, `ABC- 4`, a number above `u32::MAX`) is ignored, and the next number is computed in `u64`, so `ABC-4294967295` gives `ABC-4294967296`. `job_lookup` has no fingerprint argument (its list is already this fingerprint's), so it reads the number after the last `-` and skips an ID without one.
8. **Closed-set error sentences.** `FromStr` refuses an unknown text with the text in double quotes followed by `is not a failure class (spec 10.2)`, `is not an output failure cause (spec 10.2)`, `is not a tool (spec 4.4, 10.2)`, `is not a hold (spec 10.1)` or `is not a waiting reason (spec 12)` (for example `"full" is not an output failure cause (spec 10.2)`), in the form Task 1 gives `Note`.
9. **No setting is read.** Nothing in 10.1, 10.2, 12, 5 or 6.1 step 2 is a spec 14 setting (the 10-minute and hourly waits are fixed values, Global Constraints), so the reducer takes no `&Settings`.
10. **The licence, version and network rows name `Scanned`, as spec 10.1 does.** The scan itself runs while the job is `Fingerprinted` (`RunScan` is the action of entering it), so a licence, version or network message printed by the scan reaches the reducer in `Fingerprinted` and is rejected there (`a_licence_or_version_message_is_rejected_outside_scanned_ripping_and_copying`, `only_scanned_ripping_and_copying_wait_for_the_network`). Phase 2's engine either delivers it after `ScanDone` or reports the scan as `ScanFailed` with class `Licence`, `NeedsMakeMkvUpdate` or `NeedsNetwork`, which the Outcome rows already send to `AwaitingMakeMkv` or `AwaitingNetwork` returning to `Fingerprinted`.
11. **Events in JSON.** Every event round-trips through `serde_json` (`every_sample_event_round_trips_through_json`), including `ReviewApproved` with entries in the lists of `Overrides` (a title role and an audio override): spec 11's Approve reaches the engine over IPC (spec 4.5), the natural carrier of a JSON `Event`.
12. **Deciding again in `Decided`.** `Decided` is entered three ways: from `Inspecting` with the decision made (`DecisionDone { AutoFile }`), and with `Decide` still pending after approval at the disposition gate or re-finalise. `Decided { approved }` records which way the job entered: `approved: false` from `Inspecting`, `approved: true` by approval or re-finalise (8.8: the owner approved). `resume` gives either value `[Decide]` (10.1 says header-only steps "simply run again"). An approved job then checks space whatever the disposition. An unapproved one checks space only on `AutoFile`, and on `NeedsReview` it goes to the disposition gate with the `NeedsReview` notification (6.4 step 12: such a job "enters NeedsReview and stops here until approved"), because Decide's inputs, such as the settings (`auto_threshold`, the roots) and the library facts, can change between the two runs (`a_redecided_auto_filed_job_that_now_needs_review_is_held`); a restart, a Return (an Output or LookupUnavailable failure of the decision, then `ShareBack` or `LookupAnswered`) or a Retry of a failed decision therefore never remuxes without a decision that holds the owner's overrides (`resuming_decided_decides_again`, `retrying_a_failed_decision_after_approval_decides_again`).
13. **The file-phase slot after review.** Spec 6 lets one job be in the file phase at a time, and "jobs waiting for review occupy neither the drive nor the file-phase slot". The table makes only a Direct job in `Ejected { after_copy: false }` wait for `FilePhaseSlot`; an approval (into `Extracting` or `Decided`), a re-finalise (into `Decided`) and a Retry of a job that failed in its file phase enter the file phase directly. The reducer does not model the slot for them: the docs of `ReviewApproved`, `ReFinalise`, `Retry` and `FilePhaseSlot` say that phase 2 delivers those events only once the slot is free for the job, which then holds it until it reaches `Filed`, `NeedsReview`, `Failed` or `Discarded`.
14. **The disc gone when a disc-phase step would run again.** A Return and a Retry use `resume(state, true)`, and `MediaRemoved` and `MediaArrived` are rejected in waiting and failed states, so a job returning to `Ripping` or `Copying` issues `RipTitle` or `CopyDisc` whether or not its disc is in. The docs of the table's Return and Retry, of `back_to` and of `Action::WaitForDisc` say that phase 2 performs a disc-phase action only with the job's disc in a drive; when the disc is gone it performs none and feeds `MediaRemoved`, which gives `[WaitForDisc]`. Phase 2 does not feed the media removal its own `Eject` causes, which would otherwise reach `RipVerified` as a spurious `[WaitForDisc]` (a copy whose scan lists titles ejects from `RipVerified { after_copy: true }`, never from `Copying`). One window remains and is phase 2's to close, not the reducer's: `resume(RipVerified { .. }, false)` gives `[WaitForDisc]`, so an engine restart after the disc was ejected but before `Ejected` was persisted would wait for a disc that only needs ejecting. Phase 2, on finding a `RipVerified` job with no disc in any drive after a restart, feeds `Ejected` itself (the eject happened, or the owner removed the disc by hand); `resume` stays pure and unchanged, and its all-disc-phase-states test is unchanged.
15. **A job that failed in its file phase is past the disc phase.** Spec 6.1 step 2 sends `already_ripped` for "a job that is past the disc phase". A job `Failed` with a class other than `MediaReadError` from a file-phase state (for example `Failed { Unknown, from: Remuxing }`) has finished its disc phase and keeps its raw rip for Retry, so `job_lookup` reads it as past the disc phase, as it reads a waiting state returning to a file-phase state: `AlreadyRipped` unless armed (`a_job_failed_in_its_file_phase_is_already_ripped`), where it gave `NewJob` before and started a needless second rip. So that the owner can still rip such a disc again, `RipAgain` is taken by a `Failed` job whose `from` is a file-phase state, as by a filed one (spec 11 "arm a new job for a disc that was already ripped"; Open point 24 says so). A job failed in its disc phase with another class still gives `NewJob`. A waiting state returning to a file-phase state also takes `RipAgain` (state unchanged, `[ArmRipAgain]`), so that the owner is not shut out while an AwaitingTool or AwaitingShare job waits, since `job_lookup` reads it as past the disc phase; `waiting_return`, which both read, is written with the review queue's rows (Step 24). The owner can overturn this reading of 6.1 step 2.
