```rust
/// Everything the disc phase has at step 5. The disc name is `lookups.name` (the caller builds it once with
/// `lookup::name::disc_name` and searched with it). Def: T7. Use: T15.
pub struct PlanInputs<'a> {
    pub disc: &'a Disc,
    pub fingerprint: Option<&'a str>,
    pub disc_id: Option<&'a str>,
    pub lookups: LookupInputs<'a>,
    /// A remembered decision for this fingerprint (spec 5, 6.1 step 2 "A new job applies any remembered decisions").
    pub remembered: Option<&'a Remembered>,
    /// The owner's review decisions, when the plan is made again after review (phase 2 re-plans a copy job on approval).
    pub overrides: Option<&'a Overrides>,
    pub sessions: &'a [SeasonSession],
    pub library: &'a LibraryFacts,
    pub settings: &'a Settings,
}
/// 6.1 step 5 in order: candidates and groups (8.2); the kind; the structural pass (8.3 rules 1 to 3, or 8.5) to fill
/// RuntimeFacts, running by_labels with `wanted_languages(None)` (8.3 rule 3.1's play-all makes the disc TV unless
/// TheDiscDB states it is a movie, 8.2, when rule 3 runs again without the play-all groups; every play-all group is left
/// out of the episode-length groups, 8.5 "play all titles are dropped"); identify (8.1) over `inputs.lookups` with
/// `remembered` set to `inputs.remembered.map(|r| r.tmdb)` and `reviewed` to `inputs.overrides.and_then(|o| o.identity)`;
/// when `identity.original_language` is Some and not English, by_labels runs again with
/// `wanted_languages(identity.original_language)` and its features replace the first pass's (cuts, editions and confidence
/// never change between the passes, only the variant chosen within a cut); `Plan.wanted` is
/// `wanted_languages(identity.original_language)` for every title rule (English only when the original language is unknown
/// or English); rule 4; a remembered decision (`remembered::apply_titles`) or the owner's Assign titles
/// (`overrides.titles`, which win) replace the planned titles and set title confidence to 1.00, and Set identity or a
/// remembered identity sets identity confidence to 1.00; `overrides.season` fills a planned episode whose season is None
/// (else the disc name's season does); the mode; reviews and notes gathered (8.8: identity and title confidence are fixed
/// here). `Plan.titles` order (which fixes the keys' NN through `title_key(position, ..)`): movies in feature order
/// (database index order for rule 1, each cut's lowest title number for rule 2, group order for rule 3), TV by (season,
/// first episode) with season None last in title order. With a mapped TV plan (or episodes assigned by a remembered
/// decision or the owner), a TMDb show identity and a season, `Plan.session` is `tv::find(..)`'s session or
/// `SeasonSession::new(show_id, season, the record's episode_count for that season)`, with the plan's episodes assigned
/// (`assign` with the fingerprint, when given); with an unmapped plan the found session gives `start` (and the season when
/// none was parsed), and when the identity is confirmed (Reviewed, Remembered, DiscdbBoth or DiscdbOne: 8.5 "when its
/// identity is confirmed (by TheDiscDB or in review)") and the season is known, `Plan.session` is that session or a new
/// one with the disc recorded and no episode assigned (`assign` with the fingerprint and no pair; spec 11 Set identity
/// "attaches the disc to a season session"); None otherwise. Err only when the disc has no title at all. Def: T7. Use: T15.
pub fn plan(inputs: &PlanInputs<'_>) -> Result<Plan, String>;
```

```rust
/// One lookup file the command looked for: its displayed path when the answer file exists (None: no answer file is on
/// disk, because the lookup was not made or failed before the recorder wrote one; its line in lookup-status.txt says
/// which) and the answer word: `hit_rate::lookup(tree, path, status)`'s ("hit", "miss", "failed", "n/a") for a
/// recording's two TheDiscDB files; for tmdb.json no status line n/a, 404 miss, 200 with the record read hit, anything
/// else failed (`tmdb_answer`); for a pinned log "hit" when a record was read, else "n/a". Def: T15. Use: T15, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct LookupFile { pub path: Option<String>, pub answer: String }
/// The inputs found. `lookup_status` is `hit_rate::statuses` (which strips the byte-order mark) converted to a BTreeMap,
/// empty for a pinned log. Def: T15. Use: T15, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct PlanInputsSummary {
    pub scan: String,
    pub fingerprint: Option<String>,
    pub disc_id: Option<String>,
    pub bdmt: Option<String>,
    pub meta: bool,
    pub discdb_hash: LookupFile,
    pub discdb_discid: LookupFile,
    pub tmdb: LookupFile,
    pub tmdb_search: Option<String>,
    pub tmdb_record: Option<String>,
    pub lookup_status: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    pub remembered: Option<String>,
}
/// `lazymkv-dev plan`'s document: the slug or path, the inputs found, the settings in force (defaults, or --settings FILE)
/// with their problems (`Settings::validate`; printed, and the plan is made with them), and the Plan. Task 15 reads
/// --settings FILE with `Settings::from_json`, which returns the settings with validate's problems, so a file whose only
/// problems are validate's still plans; only from_json's Err refuses the file. Def: T15. Use: T15, T16, T19.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct PlanDoc { pub slug: String, pub inputs: PlanInputsSummary, pub settings: Settings, pub settings_problems: Vec<SettingsProblem>, pub plan: Plan }
/// The argument, borrowed: a resolved recording, or a bare scan file. Def: T15. Use: T15, T16.
pub enum PlanSource<'a> { Recording(&'a Recording), ScanFile(&'a std::path::Path) }
/// The optional files. Def: T15. Use: T15, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct PlanOptions { pub settings: Option<std::path::PathBuf>, pub tmdb_search: Option<std::path::PathBuf>, pub tmdb_record: Option<std::path::PathBuf>, pub remembered: Option<std::path::PathBuf> }
/// A recording (slug or directory): reads scan.txt, meta.json (fingerprint, disc_id), the first of
/// `disc::bdmt_candidates` under nav/BDMV/META/DL through `disc::bdmt_name`, thediscdb-hash.json (`parse_dischash`),
/// thediscdb-discid.json (`parse_discid`), tmdb.json (`parse_recorded`), lookup-status.txt; an absent lookup file means that
/// lookup was not made, an answer file whose status line is not 200 is not parsed (the recorder keeps the error body of a
/// 404 or a failed lookup), and only a file that exists, answered 200 or has no status line, and does not parse is
/// Refused { code: 2 }. A bare scan file
/// `<dir>/discNN.txt` is a pinned log: its fingerprint is `fingerprint::content_hash(&fingerprint::hashed_files(log))` of
/// its HSH lines; `discdb_by_fingerprint` is `corpus/thediscdb-api/dischash-<fingerprint>.json` under `repo_root(ctx.cwd)`
/// when present (it carries media), else `<dir>/discNN.json` with the same stem (no media: kind and TMDb ID then unknown);
/// `discdb_by_disc_id` is None (TheDiscDB's global_disc_id is not the disc ID, spec 5); no TMDb answer. A directory argument
/// is always a recording. Then --tmdb-search, --tmdb-record, --remembered and --settings when given; the disc name with
/// `lookup::name::disc_name(bdmt, disc.volume_label)`; PlanInputs with no sessions, no overrides and default LibraryFacts;
/// `plan::plan`. Refused { code: 2 } only; exit 3 comes from the caller's resolve_recording. Def: T15. Use: T15, T16.
pub fn plan_doc(ctx: &Ctx, source: &PlanSource<'_>, options: &PlanOptions) -> Result<PlanDoc, Refused>;
/// `plan`'s entry point: tests `ctx.abs(arg).is_file()` first (a scan file), and only otherwise calls `resolve_recording`
/// (which refuses a path-shaped argument that is not a directory, so `plan corpus/owner/x/scan.txt` would exit 2). Exit 0 when
/// the plan is printed, with or without review reasons or settings problems; 2 for an argument error or any refusal of
/// plan_doc (an unreadable scan, or a lookup, settings, TMDb or remembered file that does not parse, and also a scan that
/// cannot be typed or planned and a remembered file for another fingerprint); 3 when a slug is given and the evidence clone
/// is absent; never 1 (RP24). Def: T15. Use: T15.
pub fn run(ctx: &Ctx, args: &[String], out: &mut dyn Write, err: &mut dyn Write) -> i32;
```

`cmd::plan::run` is registered in `COMMANDS` as `("plan", cmd::plan::run as Command, "<slug|recording dir|scan file> [--evidence DIR] [--settings FILE] [--tmdb-search FILE] [--tmdb-record FILE] [--remembered FILE]")`, placed after `decide`; Task 19 adds the same row to the port spec's section 3.4 after `decide`, so `COMMANDS` stays in that section's order.

Where this task settles what the spec and the interfaces leave open (each choice is pinned by a test below):

1. **`run`'s signature.** `COMMANDS` holds `Command`, `fn(&Ctx, &[String], &mut dyn Write, &mut dyn Write) -> i32`, and every command in `crates/dev/src/cmd/` has that shape, so `run` takes the two streams, as the interfaces write it, and the row compiles (`the_command_is_registered_after_decide_with_its_synopsis`).
2. **The answer word of `tmdb.json`.** `hit_rate::lookup` reads a 200 answer as a TheDiscDB record (`thediscdb_answer`), so a valid TMDb record would read "failed". The TMDb word is `tmdb_answer`'s, as the interfaces' `LookupFile` doc says: no status line "n/a", 404 "miss", another non-200 status "failed", 200 "hit" when the file parsed and "failed" when it did not (`the_tmdb_answer_word_follows_the_lookup_status`). The two TheDiscDB files keep `hit_rate::lookup`'s word.
3. **A failed lookup is pending.** A recording whose TheDiscDB lookup (either file) or TMDb lookup reads "failed" is planned with `LookupInputs.discdb_pending` or `tmdb_pending` set, so `Identity.lookup_pending` holds (spec 8.1: an unreachable service leaves the lookup pending and planning proceeds on structure alone). An answer file whose status line is not 200 is not parsed: the recorder (`scripts/phase0/record-disc.ps1`) runs `curl -o <file>` for every HTTP status, so after a TMDb 404 tmdb.json holds TMDb's error object and after a rate-limited or failed TheDiscDB lookup the file holds the server's error text. Each file is parsed only when its lookup answered 200 or has no status line; its `LookupFile` keeps its path and its answer word, so a 404 reads "miss" and a 429 reads "failed" (pending). `a_failed_lookup_is_planned_as_pending` and `an_error_body_of_a_failed_or_missed_lookup_is_not_parsed` pin it.
4. **Settings files.** `read_settings` reads --settings FILE through `Settings::from_json` (Task 1's one reader, ruling RP22: absent keys take spec 14's defaults; an unknown key or a value that cannot be read into its type is refused naming the key; text that is not one JSON object, `[]` included, is refused) and does not repeat the parse: `from_json` returns the settings with `validate`'s problems. Only `from_json`'s `Err` refuses the file, and the command exits 2 with `<file>: <sentence>` (for a bad key `<file>: <key>: <serde's message>`); `validate`'s problems are printed and the plan is made with them, as `PlanDoc`'s doc says (spec 14's own defaults raise one, `tuning_root`).
5. **Exit codes** (ruling RP24, the Global Constraints' exit-code line). 0 whenever the plan is printed, also when it holds review reasons or settings problems (a plan that needs review is still a plan, spec 8.8); 2 for an argument error, a scan that cannot be read, typed (`disc::disc`) or planned (`plan::plan`'s Err), a lookup file that answered 200 (or has no status line) and does not parse, an option file that exists and cannot be read or does not parse, a settings file `Settings::from_json` refuses, and a remembered file for another fingerprint; 3 for a slug without the evidence clone (`resolve_recording`'s refusal, printed bare as `decide` prints it). No exit 1 (ruling RP24): nothing the command checks is a verdict.
6. **`PlanInputsSummary.bdmt`** is the displayed path of the bdmt file read (the first of `disc::bdmt_candidates` among the files of `nav/BDMV/META/DL`); the name read from it is `Plan.evidence.name.raw` with `source: Bdmt`. A recording without the folder, or with no `bdmt_*.xml` in it, has `bdmt: None` and is named by its volume label.
7. **Option files override the recording.** `--tmdb-record` replaces the recording's `tmdb.json` record, which is still read and keeps its answer word (a file with a non-null `title` is read with `parse_movie`, any other with `parse_tv`; `a_tmdb_record_file_replaces_tmdb_json_and_an_answer_without_a_status_line_is_read`); `--tmdb-search` is the search of 8.1 steps 4 and 5; `--remembered` is `PlanInputs.remembered`, refused with exit 2 when its `fingerprint` is not the disc's (ASCII case ignored; a disc without a fingerprint accepts it).
8. **A pinned log's paths.** The scan file is shown as given (`pathlib_split`), its API answer as `corpus/thediscdb-api/dischash-<fingerprint>.json` (relative to the repository root, as `EVIDENCE_SHOWN` is a fixed spelling), its pinned answer beside it (`pathlib_str_beside`), so the document never carries an absolute path of the machine it ran on. The slug of a pinned log is the scan file as given.
9. **Encodings.** `scan.txt` and a scan file are read as UTF-8 with replacement and through `text_mode` (as `decide` reads `scan.txt`); every JSON file as `utf-8-sig`, strict; a bdmt file as UTF-8 with replacement (`bdmt_name` ignores a byte-order mark itself). An existing file that cannot be read or decoded is refused with `<shown>: <error>`, an option file included (`option_text` adds the name, since the decode error alone names no file: a --settings, --tmdb-search, --tmdb-record or --remembered file that is not UTF-8 is refused as `latin.json: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xe9 ...`); a missing file is refused with Python's OSError text alone, which already names the path.

The spec rows this task's tests cover, one test or more each: RP14's three argument forms (a slug, a recording directory, a bare scan file) and the file-before-directory order of `run`; each of the recording's files (scan.txt, meta.json, the bdmt file, thediscdb-hash.json, thediscdb-discid.json, tmdb.json, lookup-status.txt) present, absent and, for the JSON files, not parsing, an error body left by a failed or missed lookup, which is not parsed, and an answer file without a lookup-status.txt line, which is parsed and used with the word "n/a"; the pinned log's two answer sources (the API answer under the repository root first, the `discNN.json` beside it second) and neither; the three option files and the settings file (with `--tmdb-record` replacing tmdb.json's record, and an option file that is not UTF-8 refused under its name); each exit code (0, 2 for every refusal named in choice 5, 3); `PlanDoc`'s key order and the `dumps` indent-1 printing; the `COMMANDS` row and its position; every "Expected plans" row of the interfaces file (nine pinned logs and four recordings). The settings this task's code reads are only passed on to the planner; the tests exercise the two the planner's outcome turns on through `--settings`, each at its default and at one other value: `auto_threshold` (0.85 gives Direct for a 0.98 title confidence, 0.99 gives Copy) and `tmdb_only_autofile` (on gives 0.90, off gives 0.84 with `identity_ambiguous`).

```rust
//! `lazymkv-dev plan <slug|recording dir|scan file> [--evidence DIR] [--settings FILE] [--tmdb-search FILE]
//! [--tmdb-record FILE] [--remembered FILE]` (ruling RP14 of the phase 1 plan; port spec 3.4): the disc phase of the
//! design spec's 6.1 step 5 for one recording or one pinned TheDiscDB scan log, printed as one JSON document,
//! `PlanDoc`: the slug or path, the inputs found, the settings in force (spec 14) with their problems, and the `Plan`
//! of `lazymkv_core::plan::plan` (the identity of 8.1, the kind of 8.2, the titles of 8.3 to 8.5, the mode of 6.2 and
//! 6.3, the identity and title confidences and the review reasons of 8.8). A recording is read from its scan.txt,
//! meta.json, nav/BDMV/META/DL/bdmt_*.xml, thediscdb-hash.json, thediscdb-discid.json, tmdb.json and
//! lookup-status.txt (spec 15 "Recordings"); a file that is absent means that lookup was not made, an answer file
//! whose lookup-status.txt line is not 200 is not parsed (the recorder keeps the error body of a 404 or a failed
//! lookup), and only a file that exists and does not parse is refused. A bare scan file (a pinned log of corpus/thediscdb) takes its
//! fingerprint from its HSH lines (spec 5) and its TheDiscDB answer from corpus/thediscdb-api under the repository
//! root, else from the discNN.json beside it, and has no TMDb answer. Exit 0 when the plan is printed, with or without
//! review reasons or settings problems (a plan that needs review is still a plan); 2 for an argument error, a scan that

//! not parse, or a remembered decision for another disc; 3 when a slug is given and the evidence clone is absent;

    fn doc_of(tmp: &Scratch, name: &str, options: &PlanOptions) -> Result<PlanDoc, Refused> {
        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(&tmp.0);

    fn refusal(tmp: &Scratch, options: &PlanOptions) -> Refused {
        match doc_of(tmp, "rec", options) {
            Ok(doc) => panic!("{} was planned", doc.slug),
            Err(refused) => refused,
        }
    }

    /// A lookup file that is there, with its answer word.
    fn found(path: &str, answer: &str) -> LookupFile {
        LookupFile { path: Some(path.to_string()), answer: answer.to_string() }
    }

    /// lookup-status.txt's lines as the document's map.
    fn statuses_of(pairs: &[(&str, &str)]) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
        pairs.iter().map(|(name, status)| (name.to_string(), status.to_string())).collect()
    }

    /// The notes of a plan, without their details.
    fn notes_of(plan: &Plan) -> Vec<Note> {
        plan.notes.iter().map(|noted| noted.note).collect()
    }

    /// A file of corpus/ by its path below it.
    fn corpus(relative: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
        let path = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../corpus").join(relative);
        fs::read(&path).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{}: {error}", path.display()))
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_recording_with_every_lookup_file_is_planned_from_thediscdb_and_its_tmdb_record() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("plan-full");
        film_recording(&tmp, "rec");
        let doc = planned(&tmp, &PlanOptions::default());
        assert_eq!(doc.slug, "rec");
        assert_eq!(
            doc.inputs,
            PlanInputsSummary {
                scan: "rec/scan.txt".to_string(),
                fingerprint: Some(FINGERPRINT.to_string()),
                disc_id: Some(DISC_ID.to_string()),
                bdmt: Some("rec/nav/BDMV/META/DL/bdmt_eng.xml".to_string()),
                meta: true,
                discdb_hash: found("rec/thediscdb-hash.json", "hit"),
                discdb_discid: found("rec/thediscdb-discid.json", "miss"),
                tmdb: found("rec/tmdb.json", "hit"),
                tmdb_search: None,
                tmdb_record: None,
                lookup_status: statuses_of(&[("dischash", "200"), ("discid", "404"), ("tmdb", "200")]),
                remembered: None,
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(doc.settings, Settings::default());
        assert_eq!(doc.settings_problems, Settings::default().validate());
        let plan = &doc.plan;
        // 8.1 step 3: TheDiscDB knows the fingerprint (the disc ID answered 404); title, year and original language
        // come from tmdb.json, the record of the same TMDb ID.
        assert_eq!(
            (plan.identity.step, plan.identity.confidence, plan.identity_confidence),
            (IdentityStep::DiscdbOne, 0.95, 0.95)
        );
        assert_eq!(plan.identity.tmdb, Some(film_identity()));
        assert_eq!((plan.identity.title.as_deref(), plan.identity.year), (Some("Made Up Film"), Some(2007)));
        assert_eq!(plan.identity.original_language.as_deref(), Some("es"));
        assert_eq!((plan.identity.review, plan.identity.lookup_pending), (None, false));
        // 8.2: TheDiscDB states the kind; 8.3 rule 1: its MainMovie reconciles with scan title 0.
        assert_eq!((plan.kind, plan.kind_source), (Kind::Movie, KindSource::Discdb));
        assert_eq!(plan.titles, vec![film_title(false)]);
        assert_eq!(plan.evidence.title_rule, Some(TitleRule::Database));
        assert_eq!(plan.evidence.discdb_matches, vec![DiscDbMatch { discdb_index: 0, title: 0 }]);
        assert_eq!((plan.title_confidence, plan.mode), (0.98, Mode::Direct));
        assert_eq!(plan.reviews, Vec::<ReviewReason>::new());
        assert_eq!(notes_of(plan), Vec::<Note>::new());
        // R4: English and the original language, Spanish.
        assert_eq!(plan.wanted, wanted_languages(Some("es")));
        assert_eq!(plan.wanted.original, vec!["spa".to_string()]);
        assert_eq!(plan.session, None);
        let name = plan.evidence.name.as_ref().expect("the bdmt file names the disc");
        assert_eq!((name.raw.as_str(), name.source), ("Made Up Film", NameSource::Bdmt));
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_absent_lookup_file_is_not_an_error_and_its_lookup_was_not_made() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("plan-bare");
        scan_only(&tmp, "rec");
        let doc = planned(&tmp, &PlanOptions::default());
        assert_eq!(
            doc.inputs,
            PlanInputsSummary {
                scan: "rec/scan.txt".to_string(),
                fingerprint: None,
                disc_id: None,
                bdmt: None,
                meta: false,
                discdb_hash: not_made(),
                discdb_discid: not_made(),
                tmdb: not_made(),
                tmdb_search: None,
                tmdb_record: None,
                lookup_status: BTreeMap::new(),
                remembered: None,
            }
        );
        let plan = &doc.plan;
        // 8.1 step 6: no answer and no search, so nothing is known (0, identity_unknown).
        assert_eq!((plan.identity.step, plan.identity_confidence), (IdentityStep::Nothing, 0.0));
        assert_eq!((plan.identity.tmdb, plan.identity.review), (None, Some(ReviewReason::IdentityUnknown)));
        // 8.2's default kind and 8.3 rule 3.5's one rival at 0.85, which still rips directly (0.85 >= 0.85).
        assert_eq!((plan.kind, plan.kind_source), (Kind::Movie, KindSource::Default));
        assert_eq!(plan.titles, vec![film_title(false)]);
        assert_eq!(plan.evidence.title_rule, Some(TitleRule::Structure));
        assert_eq!((plan.title_confidence, plan.mode), (0.85, Mode::Direct));
        assert_eq!(plan.reviews, vec![ReviewReason::IdentityUnknown]);
        // A Blu-ray that reached rule 2 without MSG:3344: the note records why the label rule did not apply (10.2).
        assert_eq!(notes_of(plan), vec![Note::LabelRuleUnavailable]);
        assert_eq!(plan.wanted, wanted_languages(None));
        let name = plan.evidence.name.as_ref().expect("the volume label names the disc");
        assert_eq!((name.raw.as_str(), name.source), ("MADE_UP_FILM", NameSource::VolumeLabel));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_failed_lookup_is_planned_as_pending() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("plan-pending");
        // TheDiscDB answered 503 and TMDb 500: neither answer is in (8.1 "the lookup is recorded as pending").
        scan_only(&tmp, "rec");
        tmp.write("rec/lookup-status.txt", "dischash 503\ntmdb movie/6537 500\n");
        let doc = planned(&tmp, &PlanOptions::default());
        assert_eq!(doc.inputs.discdb_hash, LookupFile { path: None, answer: "failed".to_string() });
        assert_eq!(doc.inputs.discdb_discid, not_made());
        assert_eq!(doc.inputs.tmdb, LookupFile { path: None, answer: "failed".to_string() });
        assert!(doc.plan.identity.lookup_pending);
        assert_eq!(
            doc.plan.identity.evidence[..2],
            ["the TheDiscDB lookup is pending".to_string(), "the TMDb lookup is pending".to_string()]
        );
        // Planning proceeds on structure alone: the step is the one the answers in hand reach.
        assert_eq!(doc.plan.identity.step, IdentityStep::Nothing);
        assert_eq!((doc.plan.title_confidence, doc.plan.mode), (0.85, Mode::Direct));
        // A failed disc ID lookup leaves TheDiscDB pending too.
        scan_only(&tmp, "rec2");
        tmp.write("rec2/lookup-status.txt", "dischash 404\ndiscid 429\n");
        let doc = doc_of(&tmp, "rec2", &PlanOptions::default()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(doc.inputs.discdb_hash, LookupFile { path: None, answer: "miss".to_string() });
        assert_eq!(doc.inputs.discdb_discid, LookupFile { path: None, answer: "failed".to_string() });
        assert!(doc.plan.identity.lookup_pending);
        // A recording whose lookups all answered is not pending.
        film_recording(&tmp, "rec3");
        assert!(!doc_of(&tmp, "rec3", &PlanOptions::default()).unwrap().plan.identity.lookup_pending);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_tmdb_answer_word_follows_the_lookup_status() {
        // No status line: the lookup was not made, whatever is on disk.
        assert_eq!(tmdb_answer(None, false), "n/a");
        assert_eq!(tmdb_answer(None, true), "n/a");
        // 404: TMDb has no such record.
        assert_eq!(tmdb_answer(Some("404"), false), "miss");
        // 200 with the record read; 200 without it, or any other status (a network error, a rate limit).
        assert_eq!(tmdb_answer(Some("200"), true), "hit");
        assert_eq!(tmdb_answer(Some("200"), false), "failed");
        assert_eq!(tmdb_answer(Some("500"), false), "failed");
        assert_eq!(tmdb_answer(Some("429"), true), "failed");
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_error_body_of_a_failed_or_missed_lookup_is_not_parsed() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("plan-error-bodies");
        film_recording(&tmp, "rec");
        // The recorder keeps the body of every status (curl -o): a rate-limited disc ID lookup leaves the server's
        // text, and a TMDb 404 leaves TMDb's error object. Neither is parsed (8.1: a failed lookup is pending, a 404
        // is a miss), and planning goes on with TheDiscDB's fingerprint answer.
        tmp.write("rec/thediscdb-discid.json", "rate limited");
        tmp.write(
            "rec/tmdb.json",
            r#"{"success": false, "status_code": 34, "status_message": "The resource you requested could not be found."}"#,
        );
        tmp.write("rec/lookup-status.txt", "dischash 200\ndiscid 429\ntmdb movie/6537 404\n");
        let doc = planned(&tmp, &PlanOptions::default());
        assert_eq!(doc.inputs.discdb_discid, found("rec/thediscdb-discid.json", "failed"));
        assert_eq!(doc.inputs.tmdb, found("rec/tmdb.json", "miss"));
        assert!(doc.plan.identity.lookup_pending);
        assert_eq!((doc.plan.identity.step, doc.plan.identity.original_language.clone()), (IdentityStep::DiscdbOne, None));
    }

        let plan = &doc.plan;
        // 8.1 step 3 by disc ID: TheDiscDB's media gives the title and year; no TMDb record, so no original language.
        assert_eq!((plan.identity.step, plan.identity_confidence), (IdentityStep::DiscdbOne, 0.95));
        assert_eq!(plan.identity.tmdb, Some(film_identity()));
        assert_eq!((plan.identity.title.as_deref(), plan.identity.year), (Some("Made Up Film"), Some(2007)));
        assert_eq!(plan.identity.original_language, None);

        assert!(

                .sentences
                .contains(&"TheDiscDB's record by disc ID is matched against the scan: 1 titles match".to_string()),
            "{:?}",

        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_english_bdmt_file_names_the_disc_before_the_volume_label() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("plan-bdmt");
        // Spec 8.1: the bdmt disc name, English first.
        film_recording(&tmp, "rec");
        tmp.write(&format!("rec/{BDMT_DIR}/bdmt_fra.xml"), bdmt_xml("Film Invente"));
        let doc = planned(&tmp, &PlanOptions::default());
        assert_eq!(doc.inputs.bdmt.as_deref(), Some("rec/nav/BDMV/META/DL/bdmt_eng.xml"));
        let name = doc.plan.evidence.name.expect("named");
        assert_eq!((name.raw.as_str(), name.source), ("Made Up Film", NameSource::Bdmt));
        // Without an English file, the first of the others in name order.
        film_recording(&tmp, "rec2");
        fs::remove_file(tmp.0.join("rec2").join(BDMT_DIR).join("bdmt_eng.xml")).unwrap();
        tmp.write(&format!("rec2/{BDMT_DIR}/bdmt_fra.xml"), bdmt_xml("Film Invente"));
        tmp.write(&format!("rec2/{BDMT_DIR}/bdmt_deu.xml"), bdmt_xml("Erfundener Film"));
        let doc = doc_of(&tmp, "rec2", &PlanOptions::default()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(doc.inputs.bdmt.as_deref(), Some("rec2/nav/BDMV/META/DL/bdmt_deu.xml"));
        let name = doc.plan.evidence.name.expect("named");
        assert_eq!((name.raw.as_str(), name.source), ("Erfundener Film", NameSource::Bdmt));
        // A bdmt file without a name element is read, and the volume label names the disc.
        film_recording(&tmp, "rec3");
        tmp.write(&format!("rec3/{BDMT_DIR}/bdmt_eng.xml"), "<disclib></disclib>");
        let doc = doc_of(&tmp, "rec3", &PlanOptions::default()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(doc.inputs.bdmt.as_deref(), Some("rec3/nav/BDMV/META/DL/bdmt_eng.xml"));
        let name = doc.plan.evidence.name.expect("named");
        assert_eq!((name.raw.as_str(), name.source), ("MADE_UP_FILM", NameSource::VolumeLabel));
        // A META/DL folder without a bdmt file: none read.
        scan_only(&tmp, "rec4");
        tmp.write(&format!("rec4/{BDMT_DIR}/notes.txt"), "not a bdmt file");
        let doc = doc_of(&tmp, "rec4", &PlanOptions::default()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(doc.inputs.bdmt, None);
        assert_eq!(doc.plan.evidence.name.map(|name| name.source), Some(NameSource::VolumeLabel));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_bare_scan_file_takes_its_thediscdb_answer_from_the_pinned_json_beside_it() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("plan-pinned");
        // No repository root above the scratch folder: the API answers are out of reach.
        assert_eq!(repo_root(&tmp.0), None, "the scratch folder must not be inside a Cargo workspace");
        for name in ["disc01.txt", "disc01.json"] {
            tmp.write(name, corpus(&format!("{JOHN_WICK_UHD}/{name}")));
        }
        let doc = scan_file_doc(&tmp, "disc01.txt");
        assert_eq!(doc.slug, "disc01.txt");
        assert_eq!(
            doc.inputs,
            PlanInputsSummary {
                scan: "disc01.txt".to_string(),
                fingerprint: Some(JOHN_WICK_UHD_API.to_string()),
                disc_id: None,
                bdmt: None,
                meta: false,
                discdb_hash: found("disc01.json", "hit"),
                discdb_discid: not_made(),
                tmdb: not_made(),
                tmdb_search: None,
                tmdb_record: None,
                lookup_status: BTreeMap::new(),
                remembered: None,
            }
        );
        let plan = &doc.plan;
        // Open point 26: the pinned form has no media, so no TMDb ID and no kind: the identity stops at step 6, the
        // kind is 8.2's default, and rule 1 still plans the MainMovie item.
        assert_eq!((plan.identity.step, plan.identity_confidence), (IdentityStep::Nothing, 0.0));
        assert_eq!((plan.kind, plan.kind_source), (Kind::Movie, KindSource::Default));
        assert_eq!(plan.evidence.title_rule, Some(TitleRule::Database));

            vec![PlannedTitle {
                key: "t00-00001".to_string(),
                title: 0,
                role: PlannedRole::Feature { edition: None },
                seconds: Some(6073),
                size: Some(67_757_930_496),
                source_file: Some("00001.mpls".to_string()),
                suggested: false,
                remembered: false,
            }]
        );
        assert_eq!((plan.title_confidence, plan.mode), (0.98, Mode::Direct));
        assert_eq!(plan.reviews, vec![ReviewReason::IdentityUnknown]);
        assert_eq!(notes_of(plan), Vec::<Note>::new());
    }

    #[test]

    #[test]
    fn a_settings_file_replaces_the_defaults_and_its_problems_are_printed_with_the_plan() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("plan-settings");
        film_recording(&tmp, "rec");
        // Spec 14's defaults: auto_threshold 0.85, so the 0.98 title confidence rips directly; keep_tuning_evidence on
        // without a tuning_root is the one problem the defaults raise.
        let doc = planned(&tmp, &PlanOptions::default());
        assert_eq!(doc.settings.auto_threshold, 0.85);
        assert_eq!(doc.settings_problems.iter().map(|problem| problem.key.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), vec!["tuning_root"]);
        assert_eq!((doc.plan.title_confidence, doc.plan.mode), (0.98, Mode::Direct));
        // A file naming two keys: every other key keeps its default, no problem is left, and 0.98 is below the bar.
        tmp.write("valid.json", r#"{"auto_threshold": 0.99, "tuning_root": "D:\\lazymkv\\tuning"}"#);
        let doc = planned(&tmp, &PlanOptions { settings: Some(PathBuf::from("valid.json")), ..PlanOptions::default() });
        assert_eq!(
            doc.settings,
            Settings {
                auto_threshold: 0.99,
                tuning_root: Some("D:\\lazymkv\\tuning".to_string()),
                ..Settings::default()
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(doc.settings_problems, Vec::<SettingsProblem>::new());
        assert_eq!((doc.plan.title_confidence, doc.plan.mode), (0.98, Mode::Copy));
        // A file whose only problem is validate's: printed, and the plan is made with those settings.
        tmp.write("unset.json", r#"{"auto_threshold": 0.99}"#);
        let doc = planned(&tmp, &PlanOptions { settings: Some(PathBuf::from("unset.json")), ..PlanOptions::default() });
        assert_eq!(doc.settings.auto_threshold, 0.99);
        assert_eq!(doc.settings_problems, Settings::default().validate());
        assert_eq!(doc.plan.mode, Mode::Copy);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_settings_file_with_an_unknown_key_or_a_wrong_type_exits_2() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("plan-bad-settings");
        film_recording(&tmp, "rec");
        let with = |file: &str| PlanOptions { settings: Some(PathBuf::from(file)), ..PlanOptions::default() };
        tmp.write("unknown.json", r#"{"bogus_key": 1}"#);
        let refused = refusal(&tmp, &with("unknown.json"));
        assert_eq!(refused.code, 2);
        assert!(refused.line.starts_with("unknown.json: bogus_key: unknown field `bogus_key`"), "{}", refused.line);
        tmp.write("wrong.json", r#"{"auto_threshold": "high"}"#);
        let refused = refusal(&tmp, &with("wrong.json"));
        assert_eq!(refused.code, 2);
        assert!(
            refused.line.starts_with("wrong.json: auto_threshold: invalid type: string \"high\", expected f64"),
            "{}",
            refused.line
        );
        tmp.write("list.json", "[1]");
        assert_eq!(
            refusal(&tmp, &with("list.json")),
            Refused { code: 2, line: "list.json: a settings file is one JSON object of spec 14's keys".to_string() }
        );
        // serde alone would read [] as a sequence into the defaults; from_json refuses it.
        tmp.write("empty.json", "[]");
        assert_eq!(
            refusal(&tmp, &with("empty.json")),
            Refused { code: 2, line: "empty.json: a settings file is one JSON object of spec 14's keys".to_string() }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn tmdb_search_and_record_files_identify_a_disc_thediscdb_does_not_know() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("plan-search");
        scan_only(&tmp, "rec");
        tmp.write("search.json", search_json(&[("movie", 6537, "Made Up Film", "Pelicula Inventada", "2007-05-20")]));
        tmp.write("movie.json", tmdb_movie_json(6537, "Made Up Film", "Pelicula Inventada", "2007-05-20", "es", Some(100)));
        let options = PlanOptions {
            tmdb_search: Some(PathBuf::from("search.json")),
            tmdb_record: Some(PathBuf::from("movie.json")),
            ..PlanOptions::default()
        };
        let doc = planned(&tmp, &options);
        assert_eq!(
            (doc.inputs.tmdb_search.as_deref(), doc.inputs.tmdb_record.as_deref()),
            (Some("search.json"), Some("movie.json"))
        );
        let plan = &doc.plan;
        // 8.1 step 4: one plausible result ("MADE UP FILM" folds to its title) whose 100 minutes are within 3% of
        // the 6000 s feature; tmdb_only_autofile is on by default (D9).
        assert!(doc.settings.tmdb_only_autofile);
        assert_eq!((plan.identity.step, plan.identity_confidence), (IdentityStep::TmdbOne, 0.90));
        assert_eq!(plan.identity.tmdb, Some(film_identity()));
        assert_eq!(plan.identity.runtime_check, Some(true));
        assert_eq!(plan.identity.original_language.as_deref(), Some("es"));
        assert_eq!(plan.reviews, Vec::<ReviewReason>::new());
        assert_eq!((plan.title_confidence, plan.mode), (0.85, Mode::Direct));
        // tmdb_only_autofile off: capped at 0.84 and held for review (8.1, D9).
        tmp.write("off.json", r#"{"tmdb_only_autofile": false}"#);
        let doc = planned(&tmp, &PlanOptions { settings: Some(PathBuf::from("off.json")), ..options.clone() });
        assert!(!doc.settings.tmdb_only_autofile);
        assert_eq!((doc.plan.identity.step, doc.plan.identity_confidence), (IdentityStep::TmdbOne, 0.84));
        assert_eq!(doc.plan.reviews, vec![ReviewReason::IdentityAmbiguous]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_tmdb_record_file_is_read_as_a_movie_when_it_has_a_title_else_as_a_show() {
        let movie = tmdb_movie_json(6537, "Made Up Film", "Pelicula Inventada", "2007-05-20", "es", Some(100));
        let record = parse_record(&movie, "movie.json").unwrap();
        assert_eq!((record.identity, record.runtime), (film_identity(), Some(100)));
        let episodes: &[(u32, &str, Option<u32>)] = &[(1, "One", Some(22)), (2, "Two", Some(23))];
        let show = tmdb_tv_json(99, "Show", "2010-01-01", "en", &[(1, episodes)]);
        let record = parse_record(&show, "tv.json").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(record.identity, TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::Tv, id: 99 });
        assert_eq!(record.episode_runtimes(Some(1)), vec![22, 23]);
        // A null title is no title: the text is read as a show, which needs a name.
        assert_eq!(
            parse_record(r#"{"id": 5, "title": null}"#, "x.json"),
            Err("x.json: the TV record 5 has no name".to_string())
        );
        assert!(parse_record("not json", "x.json").unwrap_err().starts_with("x.json: "));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_tmdb_record_file_replaces_tmdb_json_and_an_answer_without_a_status_line_is_read() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("plan-override");
        // Choice 7: --tmdb-record replaces tmdb.json's record (the given record's French wins over the slim file's
        // Spanish), while tmdb.json is still read and keeps its answer word.
        film_recording(&tmp, "rec");
        tmp.write("movie.json", tmdb_movie_json(6537, "Made Up Film", "Pelicula Inventada", "2007-05-20", "fr", Some(100)));
        let doc = planned(&tmp, &PlanOptions { tmdb_record: Some(PathBuf::from("movie.json")), ..PlanOptions::default() });
        assert_eq!(doc.inputs.tmdb, found("rec/tmdb.json", "hit"));
        assert_eq!(doc.inputs.tmdb_record.as_deref(), Some("movie.json"));
        assert_eq!(doc.plan.identity.original_language.as_deref(), Some("fr"));
        // Without lookup-status.txt no lookup has a status line: every answer file there is parsed and used, and each
        // answer word is "n/a" (`hit_rate::lookup` and `tmdb_answer` with no status).
        film_recording(&tmp, "rec2");
        fs::remove_file(tmp.0.join("rec2").join("lookup-status.txt")).unwrap();
        let doc = doc_of(&tmp, "rec2", &PlanOptions::default()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(doc.inputs.discdb_hash, found("rec2/thediscdb-hash.json", "n/a"));
        assert_eq!(doc.inputs.tmdb, found("rec2/tmdb.json", "n/a"));
        assert_eq!(doc.inputs.lookup_status, BTreeMap::new());
        assert_eq!(doc.plan.identity.step, IdentityStep::DiscdbOne);
        assert_eq!(doc.plan.identity.original_language.as_deref(), Some("es"));
        assert!(!doc.plan.identity.lookup_pending);
    }

    /// The made-up film's remembered decision (spec 5): its TMDb identity and title 0 as the feature.
    fn remembered_film(fingerprint: &str) -> Remembered {
        Remembered {
            fingerprint: fingerprint.to_string(),
            tmdb: film_identity(),
            titles: vec![RememberedTitle {
                source_file: Some("00001.mpls".to_string()),
                dvd_title: None,
                segment_map: "1".to_string(),
                seconds: 6000,
                role: TitleRole::Feature,
            }],
            audio: Vec::new(),
            subtitles: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_remembered_file_sets_the_identity_and_the_titles_to_1_00() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("plan-remembered");
        film_recording(&tmp, "rec");
        tmp.write("remembered.json", serde_json::to_string(&remembered_film(FINGERPRINT)).unwrap());
        let options = PlanOptions { remembered: Some(PathBuf::from("remembered.json")), ..PlanOptions::default() };
        let doc = planned(&tmp, &options);
        assert_eq!(doc.inputs.remembered.as_deref(), Some("remembered.json"));
        let plan = &doc.plan;
        // Spec 5, 8.1 step 1 and 8.8: a remembered decision covers the identity and the titles, each at 1.00.
        assert_eq!((plan.identity.step, plan.identity_confidence), (IdentityStep::Remembered, 1.0));
        assert_eq!(plan.identity.tmdb, Some(film_identity()));
        assert_eq!(plan.title_confidence, 1.0);
        assert_eq!(plan.titles, vec![film_title(true)]);
        assert_eq!((plan.mode, plan.reviews.clone()), (Mode::Direct, Vec::<ReviewReason>::new()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_remembered_file_for_another_fingerprint_exits_2() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("plan-remembered-other");
        film_recording(&tmp, "rec");
        let options = PlanOptions { remembered: Some(PathBuf::from("remembered.json")), ..PlanOptions::default() };
        tmp.write("remembered.json", serde_json::to_string(&remembered_film("FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF")).unwrap());
        assert_eq!(
            refusal(&tmp, &options),
            Refused {
                code: 2,
                line: "remembered.json: it remembers the disc FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, not this disc \
                       (0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF)"
                    .to_string()
            }
        );
        // The fingerprint compares ignoring ASCII case.
        let lower = FINGERPRINT.to_ascii_lowercase();
        tmp.write("remembered.json", serde_json::to_string(&remembered_film(&lower)).unwrap());
        assert_eq!(planned(&tmp, &options).plan.identity.step, IdentityStep::Remembered);
        // A disc without a fingerprint (no meta.json) takes any remembered file it is given.
        scan_only(&tmp, "rec2");
        tmp.write("remembered.json", serde_json::to_string(&remembered_film("FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF")).unwrap());
        let doc = doc_of(&tmp, "rec2", &options).unwrap();
        assert_eq!((doc.plan.identity.step, doc.plan.title_confidence), (IdentityStep::Remembered, 1.0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_option_file_that_cannot_be_read_or_parsed_exits_2() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("plan-bad-options");
        film_recording(&tmp, "rec");
        let missing = Refused { code: 2, line: "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'missing.json'".to_string() };
        let file = || Some(PathBuf::from("missing.json"));
        for options in [
            PlanOptions { settings: file(), ..PlanOptions::default() },
            PlanOptions { tmdb_search: file(), ..PlanOptions::default() },
            PlanOptions { tmdb_record: file(), ..PlanOptions::default() },
            PlanOptions { remembered: file(), ..PlanOptions::default() },
        ] {
            assert_eq!(refusal(&tmp, &options), missing, "{options:?}");
        }
        tmp.write("search.json", r#"{"results": 5}"#);
        let refused = refusal(&tmp, &PlanOptions { tmdb_search: Some(PathBuf::from("search.json")), ..PlanOptions::default() });
        assert_eq!(refused.code, 2);
        assert!(refused.line.starts_with("search.json: "), "{}", refused.line);
        tmp.write("record.json", r#"{"title": "Made Up Film"}"#);
        let refused = refusal(&tmp, &PlanOptions { tmdb_record: Some(PathBuf::from("record.json")), ..PlanOptions::default() });
        assert_eq!(refused.code, 2);
        assert!(refused.line.starts_with("record.json: ") && refused.line.contains("missing field `id`"), "{}", refused.line);
        tmp.write("remembered.json", "{}");
        let refused = refusal(&tmp, &PlanOptions { remembered: Some(PathBuf::from("remembered.json")), ..PlanOptions::default() });
        assert_eq!(refused.code, 2);
        assert!(refused.line.starts_with("remembered.json: missing field `fingerprint`"), "{}", refused.line);
        // A file that is there but not UTF-8: the decode error under the file's name (choice 9).
        tmp.write("latin.json", b"{\"title\": \"\xe9\"}");
        assert_eq!(
            refusal(&tmp, &PlanOptions { tmdb_record: Some(PathBuf::from("latin.json")), ..PlanOptions::default() }),
            Refused {
                code: 2,
                line: "latin.json: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xe9 in position 11: invalid continuation byte".to_string()
            }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_scan_that_cannot_be_read_or_typed_or_has_no_title_exits_2() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("plan-bad-scan");
        // A recording folder without scan.txt.
        tmp.write("rec/meta.json", META);
        assert_eq!(
            refusal(&tmp, &PlanOptions::default()),
            Refused { code: 2, line: "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'rec/scan.txt'".to_string() }
        );
        // Attribute 22 that is not a number: disc::disc refuses the scan, naming the title and the stream.
        tmp.write("bad/scan.txt", film_scan(BAD_STREAMS));
        let refused = doc_of(&tmp, "bad", &PlanOptions::default()).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(refused.code, 2);
        assert!(refused.line.starts_with("bad/scan.txt: title 0 stream 1: attribute 22 (flags): "), "{}", refused.line);
        // A scan with no title: plan::plan's one refusal.
        tmp.write("empty/scan.txt", scan_text_with_messages("2.0.0", false, FILM_DISC, &[]));
        assert_eq!(
            doc_of(&tmp, "empty", &PlanOptions::default()).unwrap_err(),
            Refused { code: 2, line: "empty/scan.txt: the scan lists no title, so there is nothing to plan".to_string() }
        );
    }
}
```

Create `crates/dev/tests/plan.rs` with exactly this content. The expected values are the "Expected plans" table of the interfaces file, read from the fixtures: each pinned log's attributes 9, 11, 16 and 24 for the planned titles (John Wick UHD title 0: 1:41:13 = 6073 s, 67,757,930,496 bytes, `00001.mpls`; its Blu-ray title 0: 25,234,495,488 bytes; Expendables 3 title 41: 2:11:31 = 7891 s, 28,831,358,976 bytes, `00756.mpls`, comment `FPL_MainFeature_UR`; Smile title 14: 1:55:37 = 6937 s, 79,673,339,904 bytes, `00040.mpls`; Knowing title 0: 2:01:14 = 7274 s, 7,098,400,768 bytes, DVD title `01`; Chernobyl disc 1 titles 1, 8, 7: 3534, 3896, 3707 s, `00801` to `00803.mpls`; disc 2 titles 6 and 8: 3899 and 4293 s; Firefly disc 1 titles 0, 1, 2: 5186, 2554, 2627 s, DVD titles `01` to `03`; disc 2 titles 0, 1, 2, 5: 2631, 2559, 2629, 2628 s, DVD titles `01`, `02`, `03`, `11`), the fingerprint of each log's HSH lines (each names one `corpus/thediscdb-api/dischash-*.json`), and each answer's `media` and episode items (John Wick 2014 movie 245891, The Expendables 3 2014 movie 138103, Smile 2022 movie 882598, Knowing 2009 movie 13811, Chernobyl 2019 series 87108, Firefly 2002 series 1437, with the episode titles below). For the four recordings, ruling RP21 decides what may be written here: a test in `crates/` never holds a value copied from the private clone that a reader could not derive from the public spec or the pinned MIT fixtures, so such a value is read from the clone when the test runs. Written as literals: what the interfaces' "Expected plans" table publishes (title numbers, the keys and playlists or DVD titles it gives (the pinned logs' and Pan's Labyrinth's; the Office row gives title numbers and episodes only), kinds, identity steps, the TMDb IDs 1417 and 2316, confidences, modes, review reasons, episode numbers, the names `THE OFFICE S3D3` and `DVD_VIDEO`), Pan's Labyrinth's fingerprint, disc ID and title 0 (1:59:10 = 7150 s, 55,613,952,000 bytes, `00800.mpls`), which `docs/phase0` and `corpus/scenarios` already publish, and `lookup-status.txt`'s lines (`dischash 200`, `discid 404`, `tmdb movie/1417 200` for Pan's Labyrinth, `tmdb tv/2316 200` for the Office, `dischash 404` alone for both Short Circuit discs), the files present (both Short Circuit recordings hold an empty `thediscdb-hash.json` and no `thediscdb-discid.json` or `tmdb.json`) and `nav/BDMV/META/DL/bdmt_eng.xml` (`Pan's Labyrinth`; the Office's nav tree has no META folder). Read from the clone by `clone_facts` and `episode_names`: the Office's and both Short Circuit discs' fingerprints and the Office's disc ID (`meta.json`), the seconds and size of each of their planned titles (`scan.txt` typed by `disc::disc`, attributes 9 and 11), the Office's playlist of each mapped title (attribute 16, from which its key is built), the first Short Circuit disc's volume label (the same scan's CINFO 32), and the Office's episode names (the Episode items of its `thediscdb-hash.json`, by source file).

```rust
//! `lazymkv-dev plan` (ruling RP14 of the phase 1 plan; port spec 3.4) over the nine pinned TheDiscDB scan logs of
//! corpus/thediscdb, which always run (CI included), and over the four recordings of the evidence clone, which print
//! "skipped: <reason>" and pass without it. The expectations are the "Expected plans" table of the phase 1 plan's
//! interfaces: identity, kind, titles in plan order with their keys, title confidence, mode and review reasons (design
//! spec 6.1 step 5, 8.1 to 8.5, 8.8), and the inputs each source gives (Open point 26 for a pinned log; spec 15
//! "Recordings" for a recording). Inputs: the repository's corpus/thediscdb and corpus/thediscdb-api, and the evidence
//! clone (LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE, else corpus/owner under the repository root). A value only the private clone holds (a
//! fingerprint, a disc ID, a title's duration and size, an episode name, a volume label) is read from the clone when
//! the test runs, never written here (ruling RP21 of the phase 1 plan).

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use lazymkv_core::audio::labels::is_slug;
use lazymkv_core::disc::Disc;
use lazymkv_core::lang::wanted_languages;
use lazymkv_core::lookup::name::NameSource;
use lazymkv_core::lookup::tmdb::{TmdbIdentity, TmdbKind};
use lazymkv_core::lookup::{IdentityStep, Kind};
use lazymkv_core::plan::movie::TitleRule;
use lazymkv_core::plan::tv::{AssignedEpisode, Episode, SeasonSession};
use lazymkv_core::plan::{KindSource, Mode, Plan, PlannedRole, PlannedTitle};
use lazymkv_core::recording::text_mode;
use lazymkv_core::review::{Note, ReviewReason};
use lazymkv_core::robot::parse;
use lazymkv_core::settings::Settings;
use lazymkv_dev::cmd::plan::{plan_doc, LookupFile, PlanDoc, PlanInputsSummary, PlanOptions, PlanSource};
use lazymkv_dev::evidence::{resolve_evidence, resolve_recording, skip, Ctx};

/// The nine pinned logs, below corpus/thediscdb.
const JOHN_WICK_UHD: &str = "movie/John Wick (2014)/4k-ultra-hd--blu-ray/disc01.txt";
const JOHN_WICK_BLU_RAY: &str = "movie/John Wick (2014)/4k-ultra-hd--blu-ray/disc02.txt";
const EXPENDABLES: &str = "movie/The Expendables 3 (2014)/the-expendables-3-film-collection/disc01.txt";
const SMILE: &str = "movie/Smile (2022)/2022-4k/disc01.txt";
const KNOWING: &str = "movie/Knowing (2009)/2010-dvd/disc01.txt";
const CHERNOBYL_1: &str = "series/Chernobyl (2019)/2020-4k-US/disc01.txt";
const CHERNOBYL_2: &str = "series/Chernobyl (2019)/2020-4k-US/disc02.txt";
const FIREFLY_1: &str = "series/Firefly (2002)/2003-dvd-the-complete-series/disc01.txt";
const FIREFLY_2: &str = "series/Firefly (2002)/2003-dvd-the-complete-series/disc02.txt";

/// The recordings of the evidence clone, one test each. A recording added later is listed by
/// recordings_without_a_test_are_listed_as_not_covered until it gets its test here.
const RECORDINGS: [&str; 4] =
    ["pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd", "short-circuit-1986-dvd", "short-circuit-2-1988-dvd", "the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray"];

/// The context of the pinned-log tests: crates/dev, whose repository root holds corpus/thediscdb-api.
fn pinned_ctx() -> Ctx {
    Ctx::for_test(Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")))
}

/// The context of the recording tests: the process's cwd (crates/dev under cargo test), no environment but
/// LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE.
fn context() -> Ctx {
    let mut ctx = Ctx::for_test(&std::env::current_dir().expect("a current directory"));
    if let Ok(value) = std::env::var("LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE") {
        ctx.env.insert("LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE".to_string(), value);
    }
    ctx
}

fn not_made() -> LookupFile {
    LookupFile { path: None, answer: "n/a".to_string() }
}

fn found(path: &str, answer: &str) -> LookupFile {
    LookupFile { path: Some(path.to_string()), answer: answer.to_string() }
}

/// The plan of one pinned log (below corpus/thediscdb, named from crates/dev), after checking the inputs Open point 26
/// gives it: the fingerprint of its HSH lines, which names its corpus/thediscdb-api answer, and nothing else.
fn pinned(log: &str, hash: &str) -> Plan {
    let path = format!("../../corpus/thediscdb/{log}");
    let doc = plan_doc(&pinned_ctx(), &PlanSource::ScanFile(Path::new(&path)), &PlanOptions::default())
        .unwrap_or_else(|refused| panic!("{}", refused.line));
    assert_eq!(doc.slug, path);
    assert_eq!(
        doc.inputs,
        PlanInputsSummary {
            scan: path.clone(),
            fingerprint: Some(hash.to_string()),
            disc_id: None,
            bdmt: None,
            meta: false,
            discdb_hash: found(&format!("corpus/thediscdb-api/dischash-{hash}.json"), "hit"),
            discdb_discid: not_made(),
            tmdb: not_made(),
            tmdb_search: None,
            tmdb_record: None,
            lookup_status: BTreeMap::new(),
            remembered: None,
        }
    );
    assert_eq!(doc.settings, Settings::default());
    assert_eq!(doc.settings_problems, Settings::default().validate());
    doc.plan
}

fn movie(id: i64) -> TmdbIdentity {
    TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::Movie, id }
}

fn show(id: i64) -> TmdbIdentity {
    TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::Tv, id }
}

/// 8.1 step 3, which every pinned log and two recordings reach: TheDiscDB by fingerprint at 0.95.
fn assert_discdb_one(plan: &Plan, tmdb: TmdbIdentity, title: &str, year: i32) {
    assert_eq!(
        (plan.identity.step, plan.identity.confidence, plan.identity_confidence),
        (IdentityStep::DiscdbOne, 0.95, 0.95)
    );
    assert_eq!(plan.identity.tmdb, Some(tmdb));
    assert_eq!((plan.identity.title.as_deref(), plan.identity.year), (Some(title), Some(year)));
    assert_eq!((plan.identity.review, plan.identity.lookup_pending), (None, false));
}

/// 0.98 (8.3 rule 1 or 8.5's map), Direct (0.98 >= 0.85), no review reason and no note.
fn assert_filed_automatically(plan: &Plan) {
    assert_eq!((plan.title_confidence, plan.mode), (0.98, Mode::Direct));
    assert_eq!(plan.reviews, Vec::<ReviewReason>::new());
    assert_eq!(plan.notes.iter().map(|noted| noted.note).collect::<Vec<Note>>(), Vec::<Note>::new());
}

/// A planned title as the planner writes it from the scan, neither suggested nor remembered.
fn planned(key: &str, title: u32, role: PlannedRole, seconds: u32, size: u64, source_file: Option<&str>) -> PlannedTitle {
    PlannedTitle {
        key: key.to_string(),
        title,
        role,
        seconds: Some(seconds),
        size: Some(size),
        source_file: source_file.map(str::to_string),
        suggested: false,
        remembered: false,
    }
}

fn feature(edition: Option<&str>) -> PlannedRole {
    PlannedRole::Feature { edition: edition.map(str::to_string) }
}

fn episode(season: u32, episodes: &[u32], name: &str) -> PlannedRole {
    PlannedRole::Episode(Episode { season: Some(season), episodes: episodes.to_vec(), name: Some(name.to_string()) })
}

/// The season session a mapped disc joins (8.5): one disc, its (episode, title) pairs as AssignedEpisode entries
/// in the order given (the callers pass them sorted by episode, as the session keeps them), no episode count (no
/// TMDb season record), open.
fn session(show_id: i64, season: u32, fingerprint: &str, pairs: &[(u32, u32)]) -> SeasonSession {
    SeasonSession {
        show_id,
        season,
        discs: vec![fingerprint.to_string()],
        assigned: pairs.iter().map(|&(episode, title)| AssignedEpisode { episode, fingerprint: fingerprint.to_string(), title }).collect(),
        episode_count: None,
        closed: false,
    }
}

#[test]
fn john_wick_uhd_disc01_plans_title_0_from_thediscdb() {
    let plan = pinned(JOHN_WICK_UHD, "76E63EBB5B66F73B0C37BFAB59B8ABA5");
    assert_discdb_one(&plan, movie(245891), "John Wick", 2014);
    assert_eq!((plan.kind, plan.kind_source), (Kind::Movie, KindSource::Discdb));
    // Title 8 has the same segment map (the playlist's clip); TheDiscDB's MainMovie is title 0.
    assert_eq!(plan.titles, vec![planned("t00-00001", 0, feature(None), 6073, 67_757_930_496, Some("00001.mpls"))]);
    assert_eq!(plan.evidence.title_rule, Some(TitleRule::Database));
    assert_eq!(plan.wanted, wanted_languages(None));
    assert_eq!(plan.session, None);
    assert_filed_automatically(&plan);
}

#[test]
fn john_wick_blu_ray_disc02_plans_title_0_from_thediscdb() {
    let plan = pinned(JOHN_WICK_BLU_RAY, "BB9E6C963A4E2EAAB46C748CD4C00B69");
    assert_discdb_one(&plan, movie(245891), "John Wick", 2014);
    assert_eq!((plan.kind, plan.kind_source), (Kind::Movie, KindSource::Discdb));
    assert_eq!(plan.titles, vec![planned("t00-00001", 0, feature(None), 6073, 25_234_495_488, Some("00001.mpls"))]);
    assert_eq!(plan.evidence.title_rule, Some(TitleRule::Database));
    assert_filed_automatically(&plan);
}

#[test]
fn expendables_3_plans_title_41_as_the_unrated_cut() {
    let plan = pinned(EXPENDABLES, "545411B47060B18FD7F8D94599F24708");
    assert_discdb_one(&plan, movie(138103), "The Expendables 3", 2014);
    assert_eq!((plan.kind, plan.kind_source), (Kind::Movie, KindSource::Discdb));
    // Open point 5: TheDiscDB's item title names no edition, so the label table names it (FPL_MainFeature_UR).
    assert_eq!(
        plan.titles,
        vec![planned("t00-00756", 41, feature(Some("Unrated Cut")), 7891, 28_831_358_976, Some("00756.mpls"))]
    );

/// plan_doc of one recording of the evidence clone, by slug, with the recording's folder on disk; None (after the skip
/// line) without the clone.
fn recording(slug: &str) -> Option<(PlanDoc, PathBuf)> {
    let ctx = context();
    let evidence = match resolve_evidence(&ctx, None) {
        Ok(dir) => dir,
        Err(refused) => {
            skip(&refused.line);
            return None;
        }
    };
    let evidence_arg = evidence.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
    let rec = match resolve_recording(&ctx, Some(evidence_arg.as_str()), slug) {
        Ok(rec) => rec,
        Err(refused) => {
            skip(&refused.line);
            return None;
        }
    };
    let doc = plan_doc(&ctx, &PlanSource::Recording(&rec), &PlanOptions::default())
        .unwrap_or_else(|refused| panic!("{}", refused.line));
    assert_eq!(doc.slug, slug);
    assert_eq!(doc.settings, Settings::default());
    assert_eq!(doc.settings_problems, Settings::default().validate());
    Some((doc, evidence.join(slug)))
}

/// A recording's file as every report prints it (port spec 3.4).
fn shown(slug: &str, file: &str) -> String {
    format!("corpus/owner/{slug}/{file}")
}

fn status(pairs: &[(&str, &str)]) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
    pairs.iter().map(|(name, value)| (name.to_string(), value.to_string())).collect()
}

/// What only the evidence clone holds of a recording, read from its files when the test runs (ruling RP21):
/// meta.json's fingerprint and disc ID, and scan.txt typed by `disc::disc` as `plan_doc` reads it (UTF-8 with
/// replacement, through text mode).
struct CloneFacts {
    fingerprint: String,
    disc_id: Option<String>,
    disc: Disc,
}

/// A JSON file of the recording folder `dir`, a leading byte-order mark dropped.
fn clone_json(dir: &Path, file: &str) -> serde_json::Value {
    let path = dir.join(file);
    let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{}: {error}", path.display()));
    serde_json::from_str(text.trim_start_matches('\u{feff}'))
        .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{}: {error}", path.display()))
}

/// The facts of the recording folder `dir`.
fn clone_facts(dir: &Path) -> CloneFacts {
    let meta = clone_json(dir, "meta.json");
    let scan = dir.join("scan.txt");
    let bytes = std::fs::read(&scan).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{}: {error}", scan.display()));
    let disc = lazymkv_core::disc::disc(&parse(&text_mode(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes))))
        .unwrap_or_else(|sentence| panic!("{}: {sentence}", scan.display()));
    CloneFacts {
        fingerprint: meta["fingerprint"].as_str().expect("meta.json states the fingerprint").to_string(),
        disc_id: meta["disc_id"].as_str().map(str::to_string),
        disc,
    }
}

/// A planned title of a recording whose seconds and size are the clone's scan's (attributes 9 and 11), neither
/// suggested nor remembered.
fn scanned(facts: &CloneFacts, key: &str, title: u32, role: PlannedRole, source_file: Option<&str>) -> PlannedTitle {
    let scan = facts.disc.title(title).unwrap_or_else(|sentence| panic!("{sentence}"));
    planned(
        key,
        title,
        role,
        scan.seconds.expect("the scan states the title's duration"),
        scan.size.expect("the scan states the title's size"),
        source_file,
    )
}

/// The episode names of the recording folder `dir`'s TheDiscDB answer (thediscdb-hash.json): each Episode item's
/// title, by the item's source file.
fn episode_names(dir: &Path) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
    let answer = clone_json(dir, "thediscdb-hash.json");
    answer["titles"]
        .as_array()
        .expect("the answer lists titles")
        .iter()
        .filter(|title| title["item"]["type"] == "Episode")
        .map(|title| {
            let source = title["source_file"].as_str().expect("an Episode item has a source file");
            let name = title["item"]["title"].as_str().expect("an Episode item has a title");
            (source.to_string(), name.to_string())
        })
        .collect()
}

#[test]
fn pans_labyrinth_2006_uhd() {
    let slug = "pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd";
    let Some((doc, _)) = recording(slug) else { return };
    assert_eq!(
        doc.inputs,
        PlanInputsSummary {
            scan: shown(slug, "scan.txt"),
            fingerprint: Some("6F39192C77BB1773D14982AD87B27DF6".to_string()),
            disc_id: Some("C337194670AF8C954C320875D671653F7EF2C256".to_string()),
            bdmt: Some(shown(slug, "nav/BDMV/META/DL/bdmt_eng.xml")),
            meta: true,
            discdb_hash: found(&shown(slug, "thediscdb-hash.json"), "hit"),
            discdb_discid: found(&shown(slug, "thediscdb-discid.json"), "miss"),
            tmdb: found(&shown(slug, "tmdb.json"), "hit"),
            tmdb_search: None,
            tmdb_record: None,
            lookup_status: status(&[("dischash", "200"), ("discid", "404"), ("tmdb", "200")]),
            remembered: None,
        }
    );
    let plan = doc.plan;
    // The disc ID answered 404, so 8.1 step 3 by fingerprint; tmdb.json is the same TMDb record, original es.
    assert_discdb_one(&plan, movie(1417), "Pan's Labyrinth", 2006);
    assert_eq!(plan.identity.original_language.as_deref(), Some("es"));
    assert_eq!(plan.wanted, wanted_languages(Some("es")));
    assert_eq!(plan.wanted.original, vec!["spa".to_string()]);
    assert_eq!((plan.kind, plan.kind_source), (Kind::Movie, KindSource::Discdb));
    assert_eq!(plan.titles, vec![planned("t00-00800", 0, feature(None), 7150, 55_613_952_000, Some("00800.mpls"))]);
    assert_eq!(plan.evidence.title_rule, Some(TitleRule::Database));
    let name = plan.evidence.name.as_ref().expect("the bdmt file names the disc");
    assert_eq!((name.raw.as_str(), name.source), ("Pan's Labyrinth", NameSource::Bdmt));
    assert_eq!(plan.session, None);
    assert_filed_automatically(&plan);
}

#[test]
fn the_office_2005_s3d3_bluray() {
    let slug = "the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray";
    let Some((doc, dir)) = recording(slug) else { return };
    let facts = clone_facts(&dir);
    assert!(facts.disc_id.is_some(), "the Office's meta.json states a disc ID");
    assert_eq!(
        doc.inputs,
        PlanInputsSummary {
            scan: shown(slug, "scan.txt"),
            fingerprint: Some(facts.fingerprint.clone()),
            disc_id: facts.disc_id.clone(),
            bdmt: None,
            meta: true,
            discdb_hash: found(&shown(slug, "thediscdb-hash.json"), "hit"),
            discdb_discid: found(&shown(slug, "thediscdb-discid.json"), "miss"),
            tmdb: found(&shown(slug, "tmdb.json"), "hit"),
            tmdb_search: None,
            tmdb_record: None,
            lookup_status: status(&[("dischash", "200"), ("discid", "404"), ("tmdb", "200")]),
            remembered: None,
        }
    );
    let plan = doc.plan;
    assert_discdb_one(&plan, show(2316), "The Office", 2005);
    assert_eq!((plan.kind, plan.kind_source), (Kind::Tv, KindSource::Discdb));
    // 8.5: TheDiscDB maps the six titles of the Expected plans row, ordered by episode. Each title's playlist,
    // duration and size are the clone's scan's, its episode name the clone's TheDiscDB answer's (RP21); its key is
    // its plan position and its playlist's stem.
    let names = episode_names(&dir);
    let mapped = |position: usize, title: u32, episodes: &[u32]| {
        let playlist = facts
            .disc
            .title(title)
            .unwrap_or_else(|sentence| panic!("{sentence}"))
            .source_file
            .clone()
            .expect("a Blu-ray title has attribute 16");
        let key = format!("t{position:02}-{}", playlist.trim_end_matches(".mpls"));
        let name = names.get(&playlist).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("TheDiscDB's answer names no episode for {playlist}"));
        scanned(&facts, &key, title, episode(3, episodes, name), Some(playlist.as_str()))
    };
    assert_eq!(
        plan.titles,
        vec![
            mapped(0, 3, &[12, 13]),
            mapped(1, 2, &[14]),
            mapped(2, 1, &[15]),
            mapped(3, 0, &[16]),
            mapped(4, 6, &[17]),
            mapped(5, 5, &[18]),
        ]
    );
    assert_eq!(
        plan.session,
        Some(session(2316, 3, &facts.fingerprint, &[(12, 3), (13, 3), (14, 2), (15, 1), (16, 0), (17, 6), (18, 5)]))
    );
    let name = plan.evidence.name.as_ref().expect("the volume label names the disc");
    assert_eq!(
        (name.raw.as_str(), name.source, name.season, name.disc),
        ("THE OFFICE S3D3", NameSource::VolumeLabel, Some(3), Some(3))
    );
    assert_eq!(plan.wanted, wanted_languages(Some("en")));
    assert_filed_automatically(&plan);
}

/// A Short Circuit recording: no answer in hand (TheDiscDB answered 404; no disc ID; no TMDb search is recorded), so
/// 8.1 step 6 and 8.3 rule 3.5's one feature-length title at 0.85. The fingerprint, the volume label and title 0's
/// duration and size are the clone's (RP21).
fn assert_short_circuit(doc: &PlanDoc, slug: &str, facts: &CloneFacts, generic: bool) {
    assert_eq!(
        doc.inputs,
        PlanInputsSummary {
            scan: shown(slug, "scan.txt"),
            fingerprint: Some(facts.fingerprint.clone()),
            disc_id: None,
            bdmt: None,
            meta: true,
            discdb_hash: found(&shown(slug, "thediscdb-hash.json"), "miss"),
            discdb_discid: not_made(),
            tmdb: not_made(),
            tmdb_search: None,
            tmdb_record: None,
            lookup_status: status(&[("dischash", "404")]),
            remembered: None,
        }
    );
    let plan = &doc.plan;
    assert_eq!((plan.identity.step, plan.identity_confidence), (IdentityStep::Nothing, 0.0));
    assert_eq!((plan.identity.tmdb, plan.identity.lookup_pending), (None, false));
    assert_eq!((plan.kind, plan.kind_source), (Kind::Movie, KindSource::Default));
    assert_eq!(plan.titles, vec![scanned(facts, "t00-title01", 0, feature(None), None)]);
    assert_eq!(plan.evidence.title_rule, Some(TitleRule::Structure));
    assert_eq!((plan.title_confidence, plan.mode), (0.85, Mode::Direct));
    assert_eq!(plan.reviews, vec![ReviewReason::IdentityUnknown]);
    // A DVD has no Java menus: the label rule never applies, so no note records its absence.
    assert_eq!(plan.notes.iter().map(|noted| noted.note).collect::<Vec<Note>>(), Vec::<Note>::new());
    assert_eq!(plan.wanted, wanted_languages(None));
    let volume_label = facts.disc.volume_label.as_deref().expect("the scan states the volume label (CINFO 32)");
    let found_name = plan.evidence.name.as_ref().expect("the volume label names the disc");
    assert_eq!(
        (found_name.raw.as_str(), found_name.source, found_name.generic),
        (volume_label, NameSource::VolumeLabel, generic)
    );
}

#[test]
fn short_circuit_1986_dvd() {
    let slug = "short-circuit-1986-dvd";
    let Some((doc, dir)) = recording(slug) else { return };

#[test]
fn recordings_without_a_test_are_listed_as_not_covered() {
    let ctx = context();
    let evidence = match resolve_evidence(&ctx, None) {
        Ok(dir) => dir,
        Err(refused) => return skip(&refused.line),
    };
    let mut slugs: Vec<String> = std::fs::read_dir(&evidence)
        .expect("the evidence clone is readable")
        .flatten()
        .filter(|entry| entry.path().is_dir())
        .map(|entry| entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned())
        .filter(|name| is_slug(name) && name != "golden")
        .collect();
    slugs.sort();
    for slug in slugs {
        if !RECORDINGS.contains(&slug.as_str()) {
            skip(&format!("not covered: {} (crates/dev/tests/plan.rs has no test for it)", slug));
        }
    }
}
```
