```rust
/// The recording's files the command reads (design spec section 15, "Recordings").
const SCAN_FILE: &str = "scan.txt";
const META_FILE: &str = "meta.json";
const STATUS_FILE: &str = "lookup-status.txt";
const DISCHASH_FILE: &str = "thediscdb-hash.json";
const DISCID_FILE: &str = "thediscdb-discid.json";
const TMDB_FILE: &str = "tmdb.json";
/// Where a recording's nav tree keeps the bdmt files (spec 6.1 step 2, 8.1).
const BDMT_DIR: &str = "nav/BDMV/META/DL";
/// TheDiscDB's live answers below the repository root, `dischash-<fingerprint>.json` (Open point 26), and how the
/// document names them whatever the root is.
const API_DIR: &str = "corpus/thediscdb-api";

/// One lookup file the command looked for (spec 15 "Recordings": thediscdb-hash.json, thediscdb-discid.json,
/// tmdb.json; for a pinned log its TheDiscDB answer): its displayed path when the answer file exists (None: no answer
/// file is on disk, because the lookup was not made or failed before the recorder wrote one; its line in
/// lookup-status.txt says which) and the answer word "hit", "miss", "failed" or "n/a". For a
/// recording's TheDiscDB answers the word is `hit_rate::lookup`'s; for its tmdb.json it is `tmdb_answer`'s (the same
/// words over a TMDb record); for a pinned log "hit" when a record was read, else "n/a". RP14. Def: T15. Use: T15,
/// T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct LookupFile {
    pub path: Option<String>,
    pub answer: String,
}

/// The inputs `plan_doc` found, as the document prints them (RP14). `lookup_status` is `hit_rate::statuses` (which
/// strips the byte-order mark) converted to a BTreeMap, empty for a pinned log. Field order is the output's key order.
/// Def: T15. Use: T15, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct PlanInputsSummary {
    /// The scan read: `<recording>/scan.txt` as the tree displays it, or the scan file as given.
    pub scan: String,
    /// meta.json's fingerprint (spec 5), or for a pinned log `fingerprint::content_hash` of its HSH lines.
    pub fingerprint: Option<String>,
    /// meta.json's disc ID (spec 5); None for a pinned log.
    pub disc_id: Option<String>,
    /// The bdmt file read for the disc's name (the first of `disc::bdmt_candidates`), as displayed; None without one.
    pub bdmt: Option<String>,
    /// Whether the recording has a meta.json; false for a pinned log.
    pub meta: bool,
    pub discdb_hash: LookupFile,
    pub discdb_discid: LookupFile,
    pub tmdb: LookupFile,
    /// --tmdb-search FILE and --tmdb-record FILE as given.
    pub tmdb_search: Option<String>,
    pub tmdb_record: Option<String>,
    pub lookup_status: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    /// --remembered FILE as given.
    pub remembered: Option<String>,
}

/// `lazymkv-dev plan`'s document (RP14): the slug (a recording's folder name) or the scan file as given, the inputs
/// found, the settings in force (spec 14's defaults, or --settings FILE) with their problems (`Settings::validate`;
/// printed, and the plan is made with them), and the Plan of spec 6.1 step 5. --settings FILE is read with
/// `Settings::from_json`, which returns the settings with validate's problems, so a file whose only problems are
/// validate's still plans; only from_json's Err refuses the file. Field order is the output's key order. Def: T15.
/// Use: T15, T16, T19.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct PlanDoc {
    pub slug: String,
    pub inputs: PlanInputsSummary,
    pub settings: Settings,
    pub settings_problems: Vec<SettingsProblem>,
    pub plan: Plan,
}

/// The argument, borrowed: a resolved recording (a slug or a recording folder), or a bare scan file (a pinned log).
/// RP14. Def: T15. Use: T15, T16.
pub enum PlanSource<'a> {
    Recording(&'a Recording),
    ScanFile(&'a Path),
}

/// The optional files, each taken against `Ctx::cwd` when relative. RP14. Def: T15. Use: T15, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct PlanOptions {
    /// A settings file of spec 14's keys (absent keys take their defaults).
    pub settings: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// A TMDb `/search/multi` answer for the disc's name (8.1 steps 4 and 5; TMDb's documented shape).
    pub tmdb_search: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// A TMDb `/movie/{id}` or `/tv/{id}` answer (8.1); it replaces the recording's tmdb.json.
    pub tmdb_record: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// A remembered decision for this disc's fingerprint (spec 5, 8.1 step 1).
    pub remembered: Option<PathBuf>,
}

/// What a recording or a pinned log gives before the option files: the document's inputs and the parsed answers.
struct Found {
    slug: String,
    scan: String,
    disc: Disc,
    fingerprint: Option<String>,
    disc_id: Option<String>,
    bdmt: Option<String>,
    /// The `<di:name>` of the bdmt file read.
    bdmt_name: Option<String>,
    meta: bool,
    discdb_hash: LookupFile,
    discdb_discid: LookupFile,
    tmdb: LookupFile,
    by_fingerprint: Option<DiscDbRecord>,
    /// The disc ID's answer: every record of the array, in order.
    by_disc_id: Vec<DiscDbRecord>,
    /// tmdb.json's record.
    recorded: Option<TmdbRecord>,
    lookup_status: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    discdb_pending: bool,
    tmdb_pending: bool,
}

/// The document for one recording or pinned log (RP14). A recording (slug or directory) is read from scan.txt
/// (typed by `disc::disc`), meta.json (fingerprint and disc ID), the first of `disc::bdmt_candidates` under
/// nav/BDMV/META/DL through `disc::bdmt_name`, thediscdb-hash.json (`parse_dischash`), thediscdb-discid.json
/// (`parse_discid`; its first record with titles is `discdb_by_disc_id`), tmdb.json (`parse_recorded`) and
/// lookup-status.txt (`hit_rate::statuses`); an absent lookup file means that lookup was not made, a lookup that
/// failed is pending (8.1), an answer file whose status line is not 200 is not parsed (the recorder keeps the error
/// body of a 404 or a failed lookup), and only a file that exists and does not parse is Refused { code: 2 }. A bare
/// scan file
/// `<dir>/discNN.txt` is a pinned log: its fingerprint is `fingerprint::content_hash(&fingerprint::hashed_files(log))`
/// of its HSH lines; `discdb_by_fingerprint` is `corpus/thediscdb-api/dischash-<fingerprint>.json` under
/// `repo_root(ctx.cwd)` when present (it carries media), else `<dir>/discNN.json` with the same stem (no media: kind
/// and TMDb ID then unknown); `discdb_by_disc_id` is None (TheDiscDB's global_disc_id is not the disc ID, spec 5); no
/// TMDb answer. Then --settings (defaults otherwise), --tmdb-search, --tmdb-record (which replaces tmdb.json's record)
/// and --remembered (refused when it remembers another fingerprint); the disc name with
/// `lookup::name::disc_name(bdmt, disc.volume_label)`; PlanInputs with no sessions, no overrides and default
/// LibraryFacts; `plan::plan` (its Err is Refused { code: 2 }, prefixed by the scan's path). Def: T15. Use: T15, T16.
pub fn plan_doc(ctx: &Ctx, source: &PlanSource<'_>, options: &PlanOptions) -> Result<PlanDoc, Refused> {
    let found = match source {
        PlanSource::Recording(rec) => recording_inputs(rec)?,
        PlanSource::ScanFile(path) => scan_file_inputs(ctx, path)?,
    };
    let (settings, settings_problems) = match &options.settings {
        Some(path) => read_settings(ctx, path)?,
        None => {
            let settings = Settings::default();
            let problems = settings.validate();
            (settings, problems)
        }
    };
    let search: Option<(String, TmdbSearch)> = match &options.tmdb_search {
        Some(path) => {
            let (shown, text) = option_text(ctx, path)?;
            let search = parse_search(&text, &shown).map_err(refused)?;
            Some((shown, search))
        }
        None => None,
    };
    let given_record: Option<(String, TmdbRecord)> = match &options.tmdb_record {
        Some(path) => {
            let (shown, text) = option_text(ctx, path)?;
            let record = parse_record(&text, &shown).map_err(refused)?;
            Some((shown, record))
        }
        None => None,
    };
    let remembered: Option<(String, Remembered)> = match &options.remembered {
        Some(path) => Some(read_remembered(ctx, path, found.fingerprint.as_deref())?),
        None => None,
    };
    let name = disc_name(found.bdmt_name.as_deref(), found.disc.volume_label.as_deref());
    let record = given_record.as_ref().map(|(_, record)| record).or(found.recorded.as_ref());
    let library = LibraryFacts::default();
    let inputs = PlanInputs {
        disc: &found.disc,
        fingerprint: found.fingerprint.as_deref(),
        disc_id: found.disc_id.as_deref(),
        lookups: LookupInputs {
            name: name.as_ref(),
            discdb_by_disc_id: found.by_disc_id.iter().find(|answer| !answer.titles.is_empty()),
            discdb_by_fingerprint: found.by_fingerprint.as_ref(),
            discdb_pending: found.discdb_pending,
            search: search.as_ref().map(|(_, search)| search),
            record,
            tmdb_pending: found.tmdb_pending,
            remembered: None,
            reviewed: None,
        },
        remembered: remembered.as_ref().map(|(_, remembered)| remembered),
        overrides: None,
        sessions: &[],
        library: &library,
        settings: &settings,
    };
    let planned = plan(&inputs).map_err(|sentence| refused(format!("{}: {}", found.scan, sentence)))?;
    Ok(PlanDoc {
        slug: found.slug,
        inputs: PlanInputsSummary {
            scan: found.scan,
            fingerprint: found.fingerprint,
            disc_id: found.disc_id,
            bdmt: found.bdmt,
            meta: found.meta,
            discdb_hash: found.discdb_hash,
            discdb_discid: found.discdb_discid,
            tmdb: found.tmdb,
            tmdb_search: search.map(|(shown, _)| shown),
            tmdb_record: given_record.map(|(shown, _)| shown),
            lookup_status: found.lookup_status,
            remembered: remembered.map(|(shown, _)| shown),
        },
        settings,
        settings_problems,
        plan: planned,
    })
}

/// A recording's inputs (spec 15 "Recordings"), as `plan_doc`'s doc says.
fn recording_inputs(rec: &Recording) -> Result<Found, Refused> {
    let tree: &dyn Tree = &rec.tree;
    let dir = &rec.dir;
    let scan_key = dir.join(SCAN_FILE);
    let scan = tree.display(&scan_key);
    let text = read_text(tree, &scan_key, Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Replace).map_err(refused)?;
    let typed = typed_disc(&text, &scan)?;
    let status_key = dir.join(STATUS_FILE);
    let lookup_status: BTreeMap<String, String> = statuses(tree, dir)
        .map_err(|error| refused(format!("{}: {}", tree.display(&status_key), error)))?
        .iter()
        .map(|(lookup, status)| (lookup.to_string(), status.clone()))
        .collect();
    // An answer file is parsed only when its lookup answered 200 or has no status line: the recorder keeps the body of
    // every status (curl -o), so a 404 or a failed lookup leaves TMDb's or the server's error text on disk (8.1).
    let answered = |lookup: &str| matches!(lookup_status.get(lookup).map(String::as_str), None | Some("200"));
    let meta_key = dir.join(META_FILE);
    let meta: Option<Meta> = if tree.is_file(&meta_key) {
        let parsed = read_json(tree, &meta_key).map_err(|error| refused(format!("{}: {}", tree.display(&meta_key), error)))?;
        Some(parsed)
    } else {
        None
    };
    let fingerprint = meta.as_ref().and_then(|meta| present(meta.fingerprint.as_deref()));
    let disc_id = meta.as_ref().and_then(|meta| present(meta.disc_id.as_deref()));
    let (bdmt, bdmt_text_name) = read_bdmt(tree, dir)?;
    let hash_key = dir.join(DISCHASH_FILE);
    let hash = file_text(tree, &hash_key)?;
    let by_fingerprint = match &hash {
        Some((shown, text)) if answered("dischash") => parse_dischash(text, shown).map_err(refused)?,
        _ => None,
    };
    let discid_key = dir.join(DISCID_FILE);
    let discid = file_text(tree, &discid_key)?;
    let by_disc_id = match &discid {
        Some((shown, text)) if answered("discid") => parse_discid(text, shown).map_err(refused)?,
        _ => Vec::new(),
    };
    let tmdb_key = dir.join(TMDB_FILE);
    let tmdb_file = file_text(tree, &tmdb_key)?;
    let recorded = match &tmdb_file {
        Some((shown, text)) if answered("tmdb") => Some(parse_recorded(text, shown).map_err(refused)?),
        _ => None,
    };
    let status = |lookup: &str| lookup_status.get(lookup).map(String::as_str);
    let discdb_hash = LookupFile {
        path: hash.map(|(shown, _)| shown),
        answer: lookup_answer(tree, &hash_key, status("dischash")).to_string(),
    };
    let discdb_discid = LookupFile {
        path: discid.map(|(shown, _)| shown),
        answer: lookup_answer(tree, &discid_key, status("discid")).to_string(),
    };
    let tmdb = LookupFile {
        path: tmdb_file.map(|(shown, _)| shown),
        answer: tmdb_answer(status("tmdb"), recorded.is_some()).to_string(),
    };
    // 8.1: an unreachable service leaves its lookup pending; planning proceeds on what is in hand.
    let discdb_pending = discdb_hash.answer == FAILED || discdb_discid.answer == FAILED;
    let tmdb_pending = tmdb.answer == FAILED;
    Ok(Found {
        slug: rec.slug.clone(),
        scan,
        disc: typed,
        fingerprint,
        disc_id,
        bdmt,
        bdmt_name: bdmt_text_name,
        meta: meta.is_some(),
        discdb_hash,
        discdb_discid,
        tmdb,
        by_fingerprint,
        by_disc_id,
        recorded,
        lookup_status,
        discdb_pending,
        tmdb_pending,
    })
}

/// A pinned log's inputs (Open point 26), as `plan_doc`'s doc says.
fn scan_file_inputs(ctx: &Ctx, path: &Path) -> Result<Found, Refused> {
    let shown = shown_path(path);
    let full = ctx.abs(&path.to_string_lossy());
    let text = read_file_text(&full, &shown, Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Replace).map_err(refused)?;
    let typed = typed_disc(&text, &shown)?;
    let fingerprint = content_hash(&hashed_files(&text));
    let (answer_path, record) = pinned_answer(ctx, &full, &shown, fingerprint.as_deref())?;
    let answer = if record.is_some() { HIT } else { NOT_MADE };
    Ok(Found {
        slug: shown.clone(),
        scan: shown,
        disc: typed,
        fingerprint,
        disc_id: None,
        bdmt: None,
        bdmt_name: None,
        meta: false,
        discdb_hash: LookupFile { path: answer_path, answer: answer.to_string() },
        discdb_discid: not_made(),
        tmdb: not_made(),
        by_fingerprint: record,
        by_disc_id: Vec::new(),
        recorded: None,
        lookup_status: BTreeMap::new(),
        discdb_pending: false,
        tmdb_pending: false,
    })
}

/// A pinned log's TheDiscDB answer and its shown path: the API answer of its fingerprint under the repository root
/// (`corpus/thediscdb-api/dischash-<fingerprint>.json`), else the `<stem>.json` beside the scan file, else none.
fn pinned_answer(
    ctx: &Ctx,
    full: &Path,
    shown: &str,
    fingerprint: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<(Option<String>, Option<DiscDbRecord>), Refused> {
    if let (Some(fingerprint), Some(root)) = (fingerprint, repo_root(&ctx.cwd)) {
        let name = format!("dischash-{fingerprint}.json");
        let api = root.join(API_DIR).join(&name);
        if api.is_file() {
            let api_shown = format!("{API_DIR}/{name}");
            let text = read_file_text(&api, &api_shown, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Strict)
                .map_err(|error| refused(format!("{api_shown}: {error}")))?;
            let record = parse_dischash(&text, &api_shown).map_err(refused)?;
            return Ok((Some(api_shown), record));
        }
    }
    let stem = full.file_stem().map(|stem| stem.to_string_lossy().into_owned()).unwrap_or_default();
    let name = format!("{stem}.json");
    let beside = full.with_file_name(&name);
    if !beside.is_file() {
        return Ok((None, None));
    }
    let beside_shown = pathlib_str_beside(shown, &name);
    let text = read_file_text(&beside, &beside_shown, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Strict)
        .map_err(|error| refused(format!("{beside_shown}: {error}")))?;
    let record = parse_dischash(&text, &beside_shown).map_err(refused)?;
    Ok((Some(beside_shown), record))
}

/// The bdmt file of a recording's nav tree (the first of `bdmt_candidates` among the files of nav/BDMV/META/DL) as
/// displayed, and the `<di:name>` it holds; (None, None) without one. Spec 6.1 step 2, 8.1.
fn read_bdmt(tree: &dyn Tree, dir: &PathKey) -> Result<(Option<String>, Option<String>), Refused> {
    let folder = dir.join(BDMT_DIR);
    if !tree.is_dir(&folder) {
        return Ok((None, None));
    }
    let names: Vec<String> =
        tree.list(&folder).into_iter().filter(|key| tree.is_file(key)).map(|key| key.name().to_string()).collect();
    let Some(first) = bdmt_candidates(&names).into_iter().next() else {
        return Ok((None, None));
    };
    let key = folder.join(&first);
    let shown = tree.display(&key);
    let text = read_text(tree, &key, Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Replace).map_err(|error| refused(format!("{shown}: {error}")))?;
    Ok((Some(shown), bdmt_name(&text)))
}

/// A JSON file of the recording as (shown path, text), read as utf-8-sig, strict; None when it is not a file there.
fn file_text(tree: &dyn Tree, key: &PathKey) -> Result<Option<(String, String)>, Refused> {
    if !tree.is_file(key) {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let shown = tree.display(key);
    let text =
        read_text(tree, key, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Strict).map_err(|error| refused(format!("{shown}: {error}")))?;
    Ok(Some((shown, text)))
}

/// An option file as (shown path, text): taken against ctx.cwd, read as utf-8-sig, strict. A missing file is refused
/// with Python's OSError text, which names the path (`[Errno 2] No such file or directory: '<path>'`); a file that is
/// there but cannot be read or decoded with `<shown>: <error>` (choice 9: the decode error alone names no file).
fn option_text(ctx: &Ctx, path: &Path) -> Result<(String, String), Refused> {
    let shown = shown_path(path);
    let full = ctx.abs(&path.to_string_lossy());
    let text = read_file_text(&full, &shown, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Strict)
        .map_err(|error| refused(if full.is_file() { format!("{shown}: {error}") } else { error }))?;
    Ok((shown, text))
}

/// --settings FILE (spec 14, ruling RP22): read through `Settings::from_json`, which returns the settings with
/// validate's problems; only its Err refuses the file (`<file>: <sentence>`, for a bad key `<file>: <key>: <message>`),
/// and the plan is made with the problems printed.
fn read_settings(ctx: &Ctx, path: &Path) -> Result<(Settings, Vec<SettingsProblem>), Refused> {
    let (shown, text) = option_text(ctx, path)?;
    Settings::from_json(&text).map_err(|error| refused(format!("{shown}: {error}")))
}

/// --remembered FILE (spec 5): the remembered decision, refused when it remembers another disc than `fingerprint`
/// (ASCII case ignored); a disc without a fingerprint takes it as given.
fn read_remembered(ctx: &Ctx, path: &Path, fingerprint: Option<&str>) -> Result<(String, Remembered), Refused> {
    let (shown, text) = option_text(ctx, path)?;
    let remembered: Remembered = serde_json::from_str(&text).map_err(|error| refused(format!("{shown}: {error}")))?;
    if let Some(fingerprint) = fingerprint {
        if !remembered.fingerprint.eq_ignore_ascii_case(fingerprint) {
            return Err(refused(format!(
                "{shown}: it remembers the disc {}, not this disc ({fingerprint})",
                remembered.fingerprint
            )));
        }
    }
    Ok((shown, remembered))
}

/// A TMDb record answer (8.1): `/movie/{id}` when the object has a non-null `title`, else `/tv/{id}`. Err is the
/// parser's sentence, prefixed by `shown`.
fn parse_record(text: &str, shown: &str) -> Result<TmdbRecord, String> {
    let value: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(text).map_err(|error| format!("{shown}: {error}"))?;
    if value.get("title").map_or(false, |title| !title.is_null()) {
        parse_movie(text, shown)
    } else {
        parse_tv(text, shown)
    }
}

/// tmdb.json's answer word from its lookup-status.txt line: none "n/a" (not made), 404 "miss", 200 "hit" when the
/// record was read, any other case "failed" (a 200 whose file is absent or unread, a network error, a rate limit).
fn tmdb_answer(status: Option<&str>, read: bool) -> &'static str {
    match status {
        None => NOT_MADE,
        Some("404") => MISS,
        Some("200") if read => HIT,
        Some(_) => FAILED,
    }
}

/// The typed disc of a scan's text (spec 9.4), read through text mode; `disc::disc`'s refusal is prefixed by `shown`.
fn typed_disc(text: &str, shown: &str) -> Result<Disc, Refused> {
    disc(&parse(&text_mode(text))).map_err(|sentence| refused(format!("{shown}: {sentence}")))
}

/// A meta.json text field trimmed; None when absent or blank.
fn present(text: Option<&str>) -> Option<String> {
    text.map(str::trim).filter(|text| !text.is_empty()).map(str::to_string)
}

/// A lookup that was not made.
fn not_made() -> LookupFile {
    LookupFile { path: None, answer: NOT_MADE.to_string() }
}

/// A path as pathlib prints it (Windows separators read as '/').
fn shown_path(path: &Path) -> String {
    pathlib_split(&path.to_string_lossy()).0
}

/// A refusal with exit code 2 (port spec 3.4: unreadable).
fn refused(line: String) -> Refused {
    Refused { code: 2, line }
}
```

```rust
        env_ctx.env.insert("LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE".to_string(), "clone".to_string());

        assert_eq!(code, 0);
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<PlanDoc>(&out).expect("one JSON document"), doc);
        // No clone: exit 3 with the line naming the evidence repository and where to clone it.
        let (code, out, err) = crate::testutil::call(run, &ctx, &["--evidence", "missing", "made-up-film"]);
        assert_eq!((code, out.as_str()), (3, ""));
        assert_eq!(

    #[test]
    fn the_document_is_printed_as_json_with_indent_1_and_the_key_order_of_plan_doc() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("plan-print");
        film_recording(&tmp, "rec");
        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(&tmp.0);
        let rec = resolve_recording(&ctx, None, "rec").unwrap();
        let doc = plan_doc(&ctx, &PlanSource::Recording(&rec), &PlanOptions::default()).unwrap();
        let (code, out, err) = crate::testutil::call(run, &ctx, &["rec"]);
        assert_eq!((code, err.as_str()), (0, ""));
        // pyjson::dumps with indent 1, as decide prints its document (port spec 3.4).
        assert_eq!(out, format!("{}\n", dumps(&serde_json::to_value(&doc).unwrap(), Style::INDENT1_ASCII)));
        assert!(out.contains("\n  \"identity_confidence\": 0.95,\n"), "{out}");
        assert!(out.contains("\n  \"title_confidence\": 0.98,\n"), "{out}");
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<PlanDoc>(&out).expect("the document reads back"), doc);
        let value: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&out).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(keys(&value), ["slug", "inputs", "settings", "settings_problems", "plan"]);
        assert_eq!(
            keys(&value["inputs"]),
            [
                "scan",
                "fingerprint",
                "disc_id",
                "bdmt",
                "meta",
                "discdb_hash",
                "discdb_discid",
                "tmdb",
                "tmdb_search",
                "tmdb_record",
                "lookup_status",
                "remembered"
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(keys(&value["inputs"]["discdb_hash"]), ["path", "answer"]);
        assert_eq!(keys(&value["inputs"]["lookup_status"]), ["dischash", "discid", "tmdb"]);
        assert_eq!(
            keys(&value["plan"]),
            [
                "identity",
                "kind",
                "kind_source",
                "titles",
                "mode",
                "identity_confidence",
                "title_confidence",
                "reviews",
                "notes",
                "wanted",
                "session",
                "evidence"
            ]
        );
        let settings = keys(&value["settings"]);
        assert_eq!(settings, keys(&serde_json::to_value(Settings::default()).unwrap()));
        assert_eq!((settings.first().map(String::as_str), settings.last().map(String::as_str)), (Some("staging_root"), Some("tool_paths")));
        assert_eq!(keys(&value["settings_problems"][0]), ["key", "problem"]);
        // Absent values are written as null, never left out.
        assert_eq!(value["inputs"]["tmdb_search"], serde_json::Value::Null);
        assert_eq!(value["plan"]["session"], serde_json::Value::Null);
    }

    #[test]
    fn argument_errors_are_reported_as_argparse_reports_them() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("plan-args");

        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(&tmp.0);
        let usage = format!("usage: lazymkv-dev {USAGE}\n");
        for (args, message) in [
            (&[][..], "the following arguments are required: source"),
            (&["rec", "other"][..], "unrecognized arguments: other"),
            (&["rec", "--bogus"][..], "unrecognized arguments: --bogus"),
            (&["rec", "--settings"][..], "argument --settings: expected one argument"),
        ] {
            let (code, out, err) = crate::testutil::call(run, &ctx, args);
            assert_eq!((code, out.as_str()), (2, ""), "{args:?}");
            assert_eq!(err, format!("{usage}lazymkv-dev plan: error: {message}\n"), "{args:?}");
        }
        // A refusal of plan_doc is printed under the command's name with its code.

        assert_eq!(
            (code, out.as_str(), err.as_str()),
            (2, "", "lazymkv-dev plan: error: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'missing.json'\n")
        );

    #[test]

    #[test]
    fn the_command_is_registered_after_decide_with_its_synopsis() {
        let names: Vec<&str> = crate::COMMANDS.iter().map(|(name, _, _)| *name).collect();
        let decide = names.iter().position(|name| *name == "decide").expect("decide is registered");
        assert_eq!(names.get(decide + 1), Some(&"plan"), "{names:?}");
        let (_, _, synopsis) = crate::COMMANDS[decide + 1];
        assert_eq!(
            synopsis,
            "<slug|recording dir|scan file> [--evidence DIR] [--settings FILE] [--tmdb-search FILE] [--tmdb-record FILE] \
             [--remembered FILE]"
        );
        assert_eq!(USAGE.strip_prefix("plan "), Some(synopsis));
        // dispatch reaches the command by its name.
        let tmp = Scratch::new("plan-dispatch");
        film_recording(&tmp, "rec");
        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(&tmp.0);
        let argv = vec!["plan".to_string(), "rec".to_string()];
        let (mut out, mut err) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
        assert_eq!(crate::dispatch(&ctx, &argv, &mut out, &mut err), 0);
        assert!(err.is_empty());
        assert!(String::from_utf8(out).unwrap().starts_with("{\n \"slug\": \"rec\",\n"));
    }
}
```

```rust
/// The command's name as typed.
const NAME: &str = "plan";
/// The usage line under the command's name: the COMMANDS synopsis after "plan ", with the --evidence flag every slug
/// command takes (port spec 3.4).
const USAGE: &str = "plan <slug|recording dir|scan file> [--evidence DIR] [--settings FILE] [--tmdb-search FILE] \
                     [--tmdb-record FILE] [--remembered FILE]";
/// The flags the command declares.
const FLAGS: [&str; 5] = ["--evidence", "--settings", "--tmdb-search", "--tmdb-record", "--remembered"];
/// What -h prints after the usage line.
const HELP: &str = "
The disc phase's plan (design spec 6.1 step 5) as one JSON document: the identity (8.1), the kind (8.2), the titles
(8.3 to 8.5), the mode (6.2, 6.3), the identity and title confidences and the review reasons (8.8), with the inputs
found and the settings in force (14).

arguments:
  source                a recording (a slug under the evidence clone, or a recording folder's path), or a scan
                        file (a pinned log, such as corpus/thediscdb/movie/<film>/<release>/disc01.txt)
  --evidence DIR        the evidence clone (default: LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE, else corpus/owner)
  --settings FILE       a settings file of spec 14's keys (default: spec 14's defaults)
  --tmdb-search FILE    a TMDb /search/multi answer for the disc's name
  --tmdb-record FILE    a TMDb /movie/{id} or /tv/{id} answer (replaces the recording's tmdb.json)
  --remembered FILE     a remembered decision for the disc's fingerprint (spec 5)

exit status: 0 when the plan is printed, with or without review reasons or settings problems; 2 for an argument
error, a scan that cannot be read, typed or planned, a lookup, settings, TMDb or remembered file that cannot be read
or does not parse, or a remembered decision for another disc; 3 when a slug is given and the evidence clone is
absent; never 1.
";

/// The words of one run: the source argument, --evidence and the optional files.
struct Parsed {
    source: String,
    evidence: Option<String>,
    options: PlanOptions,
}

/// The arguments as argparse reads them; Err is the message `usage_error` prints.
fn parse_args(args: &[String]) -> Result<Parsed, String> {
    let mut parsed = Args::new(args, &FLAGS);
    let evidence = parsed.flag("--evidence")?;
    let settings = parsed.flag("--settings")?.map(PathBuf::from);
    let tmdb_search = parsed.flag("--tmdb-search")?.map(PathBuf::from);
    let tmdb_record = parsed.flag("--tmdb-record")?.map(PathBuf::from);
    let remembered = parsed.flag("--remembered")?.map(PathBuf::from);
    let words = parsed.positionals()?;
    match words.as_slice() {
        [] => Err("the following arguments are required: source".to_string()),
        [source] => Ok(Parsed {
            source: source.clone(),
            evidence,
            options: PlanOptions { settings, tmdb_search, tmdb_record, remembered },
        }),
        [_, rest @ ..] => Err(format!("unrecognized arguments: {}", rest.join(" "))),
    }
}

/// `lazymkv-dev plan` (RP14, port spec 3.4): `ctx.abs(arg).is_file()` is tested first (a scan file), and only
/// otherwise `resolve_recording` (which refuses a path-shaped argument that is not a directory, so
/// `plan corpus/owner/x/scan.txt` for a missing file exits 2); its refusal is printed bare with its code (3 without
/// the clone), plan_doc's under the command's name; the document goes to stdout through `pyjson::dumps` with indent 1.
/// Exit 0 when the plan is printed, with or without review reasons or settings problems; 2 for an argument error or
/// any refusal of plan_doc (an unreadable scan, or a lookup, settings, TMDb or remembered file that does not parse, and
/// also a scan that cannot be typed or planned and a remembered file for another fingerprint); 3 when a slug is given
/// and the evidence clone is absent; never 1 (RP24). Def: T15. Use: T15.
pub fn run(ctx: &Ctx, args: &[String], out: &mut dyn Write, err: &mut dyn Write) -> i32 {
    if args.iter().any(|arg| arg == "-h" || arg == "--help") {
        let _ = writeln!(out, "usage: lazymkv-dev {}", USAGE);
        let _ = write!(out, "{}", HELP);
        return 0;
    }
    let parsed = match parse_args(args) {
        Ok(parsed) => parsed,
        Err(message) => return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, &message),
    };
    let result = if ctx.abs(&parsed.source).is_file() {
        plan_doc(ctx, &PlanSource::ScanFile(Path::new(&parsed.source)), &parsed.options)
    } else {
        let rec = match resolve_recording(ctx, parsed.evidence.as_deref(), &parsed.source) {
            Ok(rec) => rec,
            Err(refused) => {
                let _ = writeln!(err, "{}", refused.line);
                return refused.code;
            }
        };
        plan_doc(ctx, &PlanSource::Recording(&rec), &parsed.options)
    };
    let doc = match result {
        Ok(doc) => doc,
        Err(refused) => {
            let _ = writeln!(err, "lazymkv-dev {}: error: {}", NAME, refused.line);
            return refused.code;
        }
    };
    let value = match serde_json::to_value(&doc) {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(error) => {
            let _ = writeln!(err, "lazymkv-dev {}: error: {}", NAME, error);
            return 2;
        }
    };
    let _ = writeln!(out, "{}", dumps(&value, Style::INDENT1_ASCII));
    0
}
```

```rust
// lazymkv_core::settings (Task 1)
/// Every key of spec 14 with its default (`Settings::default()` is the table's Default column). A settings file may name
/// only the keys it changes: absent keys take the default (`#[serde(default)]`); an unknown key is refused
/// (`deny_unknown_fields`). Def: T1. Use: every rule.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Settings {
    /// Spec 7; None until set. Required by the engine, not by any rule here.
    pub staging_root: Option<String>,
    pub movies_root: Option<String>,
    pub tv_root: Option<String>,
    /// 120: MakeMKV minimum title length, seconds (8.2's candidate filter reads it).
    pub minlength_s: u32,
    /// 1024: MakeMKV read cache, MB.
    pub cache_mb: u32,
    /// 0.85: confidence needed to file automatically (8.8, 6.2, 6.3).
    pub auto_threshold: f64,
    /// 45: shortest title considered a feature, minutes (8.3 rule 3.2).
    pub feature_min_minutes: u32,
    /// true: D9, a TMDb-only identification may file automatically (8.1's 0.84 cap when false).
    pub tmdb_only_autofile: bool,
    /// true: D9, channel count before fidelity tier (8.6 step 3).
    pub prefer_most_channels: bool,
    /// true: D9, original-language audio first for non-English works (8.6 step 5).
    pub original_language_first: bool,
    /// 300: start-time tolerance for subtitle alignment, ms (8.7).
    pub subs_tolerance_ms: u32,
    /// 0.70 and 0.30: the provisional alignment bands (8.7).
    pub subs_same_min: f64,
    pub subs_diff_max: f64,
    /// 64: image-subtitle packets this small clear the screen (8.7).
    pub sub_clear_max_bytes: i64,
    /// Combined (8.9).
    pub edition_style: EditionStyle,
    /// false: add the square-bracket ID tag (8.9).
    pub jellyfin10_compat: bool,
    /// 7: days raw data of filed jobs is kept (7).
    pub retention_days: u32,
    /// true: D16.
    pub keep_tuning_evidence: bool,
    /// None; required while keep_tuning_evidence is on; not inside staging_root or a library root (7, 14).
    pub tuning_root: Option<String>,
    /// 1, 10, 120, 30, 300, 20, 30 (spec 14, in its order).
    pub file_phase_concurrency: u32,
    pub drive_settle_s: u32,
    pub drive_ready_timeout_s: u32,
    pub scan_timeout_min: u32,
    pub stall_timeout_s: u32,
    pub read_error_rate: u32,
    pub exit_wait_min: u32,
    /// "2.0.0": lowest supported MakeMKV (9.1).
    pub makemkv_min_version: String,
    pub tool_paths: ToolPaths,
}
impl Default for Settings { fn default() -> Settings; }

/// One refused setting: the key and a plain sentence. Spec 7 and 14. Def: T1. Use: T15 (printed when a settings file is given; phase 2 the UI).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct SettingsProblem { pub key: String, pub problem: String }

impl Settings {
    /// Every problem, in key order: staging_root inside movies_root or tv_root (or equal to one); tuning_root inside
    /// staging_root or a library root; tuning_root absent (or blank: no path component) while keep_tuning_evidence is on;
    /// auto_threshold outside 0.0..=1.0; subs_diff_max above subs_same_min; minlength_s, feature_min_minutes,
    /// file_phase_concurrency 0; makemkv_min_version not `N.N.N` (`version_triple`). Empty when valid.
    /// `Settings::default().validate()` is exactly one problem, keyed `tuning_root` (spec 14's defaults turn
    /// keep_tuning_evidence on and leave tuning_root unset); `lazymkv-dev plan` prints the problems and plans with them.
    /// Spec 7, 14. Def: T1. Use: T15.
    pub fn validate(&self) -> Vec<SettingsProblem>;
    /// A JSON settings text, read and checked (ruling RP22): keys absent from the text take Settings::default()'s value.
    /// Err, one sentence, only when the text cannot be read: text that is not JSON (serde_json's message), text that is
    /// not one JSON object (`a settings file is one JSON object of spec 14's keys`), or a key the settings lack or whose
    /// value cannot be read into its type (`<key>: <serde's message>`, the first such key in the text's order). Ok holds
    /// the settings with validate()'s problems, possibly none: a caller that needs a valid file checks the vector, and
    /// `lazymkv-dev plan` prints them and plans anyway. Spec 14. Def: T1. Use: T15.
    pub fn from_json(text: &str) -> Result<(Settings, Vec<SettingsProblem>), String>;

// lazymkv_core::lookup identification (Task 4)
/// A TheDiscDB description's meaning (8.1 last bullet, D14, 8.7 "the one TheDiscDB describes as subtitles or SDH"):
/// "comment" gives Commentary; "audio desc", "descriptive", "DVS", "visually impaired" give AudioDescription; "SDH",
/// "hearing" give Sdh; "isolated score", "score only" give IsolatedScore; "music and effects", "music & effects", "M&E" give
/// MusicAndEffects; "subtitle", or a description that after trimming and case-folding equals the track's own `language`
/// (TheDiscDB's language name: "English"; Knowing's "ENglish" included), gives Dialogue. All case-insensitive, substring
/// matches, in this order; a text can carry several. IsolatedScore, MusicAndEffects and Dialogue are provisional: TheDiscDB's
/// wording for them is not yet known (8.1's last bullet names no such word; every subtitle description in the 18 answers
/// and the pinned files is a bare language name). Def: T4. Use: T8, T9, T10.

    pub step: IdentityStep,

    /// Whether a runtime check ran and what it said (None: not applicable, no record, or no runtime).

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct FileDecision {
    pub title_key: String,
    pub audio: AudioDecision,
    pub subtitles: SubtitleDecision,

    pub edition: Option<String>,

/// 6.4 step 11 and 8.8: decide_audio (with the wanted languages of the identity the job is filed under: the plan's, or,
/// when the owner's Set identity names another work than the plan's and its record is given, `wanted_languages` of that
/// record's original language; R4, 8.6 "Languages") and decide_subtitles (facts with `reviewed` set from
/// `overrides.audio_of(title.number)` and `overrides.subtitles_of(title.number)`), layout, the path (movie_path for a
/// feature, tv_path for an episode, by the filed role: the owner's Assign titles when it names any title, which then wins
/// whole as in a re-plan (Err for a planned title it ignores or does not name), else the planned role; no path when the
/// record's kind does not match the role (a movie record for a feature, a show record for an episode); resolution from
/// title.video_height, the edition through edition_names and edition_label; a planned Episode with season None builds no
/// path (path None) and adds tv_unmapped;
/// overrides.collision KeepBoth (copy Some(2) while the collision exists) and Replace leave path_collision unraised;
/// Discard never reaches decide, the engine discards the job), the three confidences (identity and
/// title from the plan; identity 1.00 when overrides.identity is Some, title 1.00 when overrides.titles is not empty; track
/// = min(audio, subtitle) after the remembered and review overrides set the parts they cover to 1.00), reviews = plan's
/// (less the reasons the owner's review answers: identity_unknown and identity_ambiguous when overrides.identity is Some;
/// title_ambiguous, multiple_features, unnamed_cut and tv_unmapped when overrides.titles is not empty) + audio's +
/// subtitles' + rip_reviews + path_collision when library.path_collision (and not KeepBoth or Replace) + read_errors
/// exactly when `read_errors` is not empty, notes likewise, read_errors carried unchanged, disposition; NeedsReview
/// whenever path is None. Verification lowers no
/// confidence: a failed or read-error rip holds the job through its review reason, which has the same effect on the
/// disposition as a confidence below auto_threshold (8.8). Def: T13. Use: T16.
pub fn decide(inputs: &DecisionInputs<'_>) -> Result<FileDecision, String>;
/// AutoFile only with no review reason and every confidence >= settings.auto_threshold (8.8). Def: T13. Use: T13, T16.
pub fn disposition(confidences: &Confidences, reviews: &[ReviewReason], settings: &Settings) -> Disposition;

/// with their problems (`Settings::validate`; printed, and the plan is made with them), and the Plan. Task 15 reads
/// --settings FILE with `Settings::from_json`, which returns the settings with validate's problems, so a file whose only
/// problems are validate's still plans; only from_json's Err refuses the file. Def: T15. Use: T15, T16, T19.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct PlanDoc { pub slug: String, pub inputs: PlanInputsSummary, pub settings: Settings, pub settings_problems: Vec<SettingsProblem>, pub plan: Plan }
/// The argument, borrowed: a resolved recording, or a bare scan file. Def: T15. Use: T15, T16.
pub enum PlanSource<'a> { Recording(&'a Recording), ScanFile(&'a std::path::Path) }
/// The optional files. Def: T15. Use: T15, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct PlanOptions { pub settings: Option<std::path::PathBuf>, pub tmdb_search: Option<std::path::PathBuf>, pub tmdb_record: Option<std::path::PathBuf>, pub remembered: Option<std::path::PathBuf> }
/// A recording (slug or directory): reads scan.txt, meta.json (fingerprint, disc_id), the first of
/// `disc::bdmt_candidates` under nav/BDMV/META/DL through `disc::bdmt_name`, thediscdb-hash.json (`parse_dischash`),
/// thediscdb-discid.json (`parse_discid`), tmdb.json (`parse_recorded`), lookup-status.txt; an absent lookup file means that
/// lookup was not made, an answer file whose status line is not 200 is not parsed (the recorder keeps the error body of a
/// 404 or a failed lookup), and only a file that exists, answered 200 or has no status line, and does not parse is
/// Refused { code: 2 }. A bare scan file
/// `<dir>/discNN.txt` is a pinned log: its fingerprint is `fingerprint::content_hash(&fingerprint::hashed_files(log))` of
/// its HSH lines; `discdb_by_fingerprint` is `corpus/thediscdb-api/dischash-<fingerprint>.json` under `repo_root(ctx.cwd)`
/// when present (it carries media), else `<dir>/discNN.json` with the same stem (no media: kind and TMDb ID then unknown);
/// `discdb_by_disc_id` is None (TheDiscDB's global_disc_id is not the disc ID, spec 5); no TMDb answer. A directory argument
/// is always a recording. Then --tmdb-search, --tmdb-record, --remembered and --settings when given; the disc name with
/// `lookup::name::disc_name(bdmt, disc.volume_label)`; PlanInputs with no sessions, no overrides and default LibraryFacts;

pub fn plan_doc(ctx: &Ctx, source: &PlanSource<'_>, options: &PlanOptions) -> Result<PlanDoc, Refused>;
```

Where this task settles what the spec and the interfaces leave open (each choice is pinned by a test below):

1. **The title and the selection** of the decision are `doc.reconcile.title` and `doc.reconcile.selection`, the ones decide's own reconcile section used (the summary's title, and the profile's selection unless `--selection` overrode it), so the two sections never describe different streams.
2. **The title is narrowed to the rip's selection** (`verify::selected_streams`) before `decision::decide`: an eng-only rip is decided over the streams it holds, so a stream the profile left out (Pan's Labyrinth's Spanish audio under `eng-only`) is neither kept nor dropped, and the decision can raise `original_language_missing` for it. A stream the selection holds but MakeMKV removed (`MSG:4047`, the empty forced-only streams) stays in the title and reaches the subtitle rule through `SubtitleFacts.removed`, which drops it `DerivedForcedOnlyEmpty` (Task 10, choice 3). The rip is verified against the whole title (`verify_rip` filters by the selection itself).
3. **The facts.** MD5s come from every `audio-levels-20ms-*` folder of the label, in PathKey order: first its `manifest.txt` (`main=` and `cand=` lines), then its `audio-proxy.json` (each track's `source_stream` and `source.md5`), both naming ffprobe stream numbers of the file, mapped through the verify pairs; the first MD5 of a stream wins; `-` and empty are no MD5. The manifests are git-ignored side files, but `audio-proxy.json` is tracked and holds the packet MD5 of every audio stream of the file (on every level folder of the evidence clone the two agree wherever both name a stream), so a clone without the level files keeps D13's duplicate evidence, and the MD5s are the same with or without them (Short Circuit 2's `all-tracks-2` manifest names stream 1 only; its proxy names streams 1 to 4). Profiles come from `<label>/ffprobe-streams.json` (audio streams with a non-empty profile); an absent file gives none, a file that does not parse is an Err. Events come from `<label>/subs/` (`verify::subtitle_events` at the plan's `sub_clear_max_bytes`) when `subs/index.json` exists, else none. The removed streams are decide's own reconcile section's `dropped` rows (the `MSG:4047` indices counted over `reconcile::expected_rows`, the rows `verify::selected_streams` is built on), so the removal is not computed a second time. TheDiscDB's title and the TMDb record come from `cmd::plan::recorded_answers`, the answers `plan_doc` itself parsed: an answer file whose `lookup-status.txt` line is not 200 is left unparsed there (the recorder keeps the error body of a 404 or a failed lookup), so the plan and decision sections never read the answers differently. TheDiscDB's record is the fingerprint's, else the first disc-ID record with titles (`plan_doc`'s own choice), and its title is the one `lookup::discdb::match_titles` matches to the label's title. The rip's read errors and `verify::failure_reviews(&report, !report.ok)` are carried in: a recording holds one rip of the title and no second attempt can come, so the recorded rip is the last attempt there will be, and a rip that fails verification raises `verify_failed` and holds the job, as 6.2 step 7's second failure does (a rip that fails verification also maps no file track: `stream_of_track` gives None while `tracks_ok` is false, so its MD5s, profiles, events and verdicts are lost and only the hold keeps it from filing).
4. **The verdicts** come from decide's own `audio` section (no measure runs twice): the first measured folder whose `main=` stream maps onto the scan gives `verdict_reference`; a folder measured against another stream is left out with its veto; the first verdict of a stream wins; D21's veto holds when a kept folder says it holds. A skipped folder gives nothing, and so does a folder with no candidate verdict (a `main=`-only folder such as `audio-levels-20ms-1`): when no verdict was taken at all, there is no reference and no veto (`AudioFacts.verdict_reference` is None when there are no verdicts), so a main-only folder measured against another stream raises nothing.
5. **The text decisions** come from decide's own `subtitles` section, mapped through `subs/index.json` (read as `verify::subtitle_events` reads it: UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, invalid bytes replaced, so an index that gives events never skips the decision); they are used only when the plan's settings give the text rule the section ran with (`settings.text_rule() == text::Rule::default()`, Task 1's `text_rule`), so a decision with other subtitle settings never mixes in decisions of other thresholds.
6. **The TMDb record that names the file** is the recorded `tmdb.json` record as `plan_doc` parsed it (`recorded_answers`) when its identity is the plan's (`record_for_naming`), else none: Task 13's `decide` refuses a record of another identity (8.9 "Title and year always come from the same TMDb record as the ID"), and decide should then show a decision without a path rather than skip.
7. **Skips and exit codes.** The plan section is `Skipped` with `plan_doc`'s refusal line; the decision section is then `Skipped` with `no plan: ` and that line. A title the plan does not include is `the plan does not include title <n> (planned: <titles in plan order, ", "-separated, or none>)`. Any other Err of `decision_doc` (an unreadable input, `decide`'s refusal) is the skip reason. Neither section changes decide's exit code or its `reviews` (those stay the audio and subtitle sections' own: the decision's review reasons are in the decision).
8. **Library roots through `--settings FILE`.** RP14's decision section shows the final path and the disposition, and a path needs a library root, which spec 14's defaults leave unset. decide therefore takes `--settings FILE` (a JSON file naming the keys it changes, read by `plan_doc` exactly as `lazymkv-dev plan --settings FILE` reads it) and plans with `PlanOptions { settings, ..PlanOptions::default() }`; the decision takes the plan's settings. Without the flag spec 14's defaults apply, `movies_root` and `tv_root` are unset, and Task 13 builds no path and holds the job (its choice 3). A settings file `plan_doc` refuses is the plan section's skip reason, as any other refusal, and never changes decide's exit code. The evidence test keeps decide's own document at the defaults (the level measures run once per label) and makes a second decision for every label from the same plan with the owner's roots (`\\unas-pro\media\Movies`, `\\unas-pro\media\Shows`) to pin the final paths and dispositions; `a_settings_file_gives_decides_own_decision_its_final_path` pins the flag itself.
9. **`_ctx`** is not read by `decision_doc` (every input is under the recording's tree); the parameter keeps the interfaces' signature.

The fixture `recs/disc-b` is a made-up Blu-ray whose title 0 copies the layout of the Office's title 1 (`00004.mpls`, S03E15) as `corpus/owner/the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray/scan.txt` lists it: AVC video (stream 0), DTS-HD MA 5.1 with flags 1024 (1), its DTS core at `1.5 Mb/s` with flags 2304 (2), a second DTS-HD MA 5.1 (3), its core (4), PGS English (5) and a derived forced-only PGS with flags 6144 (6). Its rip label `all-tracks` holds what the Office's `rehearsal` rip holds: six tracks (MakeMKV removed the empty forced-only stream, `MSG:4047` index 6), two made-up packet MD5s (`TWIN_A` for streams 1 and 3, `TWIN_B` for their cores 2 and 4, so the twin tracks share a packet MD5 as the Office's twins do; ruling RP21 keeps the clone's own values out of `crates/`) and the ffprobe profiles `DTS-HD MA`, `DTS`, `DTS-HD MA`, `DTS`. Its label `eng-only` is the same title under the eng profile (the cores are not selected, `MSG:4047` index 4 is the forced-only stream), and `extra` rips title 1, a three-minute title the plan leaves out. The PGS stream has 40 events, each a 3000-byte packet followed by a 30-byte clear packet (spec 8.7 "Events"). No lookup is recorded, so the plan is spec 8.1 step 6 (identity 0, `identity_unknown`) and 8.3 rule 3.5 (one rival, 0.85, Direct). Two of the tests change the fixture: one records a TMDb 404 and a failed TheDiscDB lookup whose bodies the recorder kept (spec 8.1; `plan_doc` leaves both unparsed, and the decision must too), one removes the level folder's `manifest.txt` and writes its `audio-proxy.json` (the tracked file a clone without the level files still holds) with the same packet MD5s.

The expected decisions follow the rules: 8.6 step 1 drops the derived cores (flag 2048) and the exact duplicate stream 3 of stream 1 (equal MD5, D13), keeping DTS-HD MA 5.1 at 0.95; 8.7 sets the forced-only stream aside, drops it as empty, and keeps the one full English track as "English" at 0.90 (one full track); the track confidence is the lower, 0.90; there is no TMDb record, so no path, and with `identity_unknown` the job is held (8.8).

```rust
        (6, B_FORCED_ONLY),
    ];
    const B_STREAMS_1: &[(u32, &[(u32, &str)])] = &[(0, B_VIDEO), (1, B_STEREO)];
    /// Two made-up packet MD5s (ruling RP21): TWIN_A for the twin tracks 1 and 3, TWIN_B for their cores 2 and 4.
    const TWIN_A: &str = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef";
    const TWIN_B: &str = "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210";

    /// recs/disc-b's scan.txt: CINFO 1 (a Blu-ray), 2 and 32 (the name and the volume label), then the two titles.
    fn disc_b_scan() -> String {
        scan_text(
            &[(1, "Blu-ray disc"), (2, "Made Up Film"), (32, "MADE_UP_FILM")],
            &[(0, B_TITLE_0, B_STREAMS_0), (1, B_TITLE_1, B_STREAMS_1)],
        )
    }

    /// mkvmerge -J of a rip of recs/disc-b: `tracks` as (type, codec, audio channels) with ids 0, 1, 2 and on, every
    /// track English but the video ("und"); one chapter edition of `chapters` entries; the container's duration.
    fn ident_b(tracks: &[(&str, &str, Option<i64>)], chapters: i64, duration_ns: i64) -> String {
        let tracks: Vec<Value> = tracks
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(id, (kind, codec, channels))| {
                let mut properties = json!({"language": if *kind == "video" { "und" } else { "eng" }});
                if let Some(channels) = channels {
                    properties["audio_channels"] = json!(channels);
                }
                json!({"id": id, "type": kind, "codec": codec, "properties": properties})
            })
            .collect();
        json!({
            "tracks": tracks,
            "chapters": [{"num_entries": chapters}],
            "container": {"properties": {"duration": duration_ns}}
        })
        .to_string()
    }

    /// ffprobe-streams.json of a rip of recs/disc-b: the video (index 0), one DTS stream per profile, then `subtitles`
    /// PGS streams, indexed in file order.
    fn ffprobe_b(profiles: &[&str], subtitles: usize) -> String {
        let mut streams = vec![json!({"index": 0, "codec_type": "video", "codec_name": "h264", "profile": "High"})];
        for (k, profile) in profiles.iter().enumerate() {
            streams.push(
                json!({"index": k + 1, "codec_type": "audio", "codec_name": "dts", "profile": profile, "channels": 6}),
            );
        }
        for k in 0..subtitles {
            let index = profiles.len() + 1 + k;
            streams.push(json!({"index": index, "codec_type": "subtitle", "codec_name": "hdmv_pgs_subtitle"}));
        }
        json!({"streams": streams}).to_string()
    }

    /// A level folder's manifest.txt as audio-levels.ps1 writes it: the format line, the file line, then one line per
    /// (role "main" or "cand", ffprobe stream, packet MD5).
    fn manifest_b(lines: &[(&str, u32, &str)]) -> String {
        let mut text = String::from(
            "# lazymkv audio-levels v2 (experiment 13)\nfile=title_t00.mkv bytes=1 seconds=1 frame_ms=20 band_hz=300-3400\n",
        );
        for (role, stream, md5) in lines {
            text.push_str(&format!(
                "{role}={stream} codec=dts channels=6 layout=5.1(side) language=eng frames=1 md5={md5}\n"
            ));
        }
        text
    }

    /// MakeMKV's line for an empty forced-only track it removed, at output index `index` (spec 6.2 step 7, 9.4).
    fn removal(index: u32) -> String {
        format!(
            "MSG:4047,16,3,\"AV sync issue in stream {index} at 0:00:00 : Forced subtitles track #{index} turned out to \
             be empty and was removed from output file\",\"AV sync issue in stream %1 at %2 : %3\",\"{index}\",\
             \"0:00:00\",\"Forced subtitles track #{index} turned out to be empty and was removed from output file\"\n"
        )
    }

    /// The label's subs/: index.json with one English PGS stream, n 0 = file track `track_id`, and its 40 events 3 s
    /// apart, each a 3000-byte packet followed by a 30-byte clear packet.
    fn subs_b(label: &Path, track_id: i64) {
        let index = json!([{"n": 0, "track_id": track_id, "language": "eng", "codec": "HDMV PGS", "track_name": null,
                            "forced": false, "default": false}]);
        write(&label.join("subs/index.json"), index.to_string());
        let mut packets = Vec::new();
        for k in 0..40_i64 {
            let t = 10.0 + 3.0 * k as f64;
            packets.push(json!({"pts_time": format!("{:.6}", t), "duration_time": "2.000000", "size": "3000"}));
            packets.push(json!({"pts_time": format!("{:.6}", t + 2.0), "duration_time": "N/A", "size": "30"}));
        }
        write(&label.join("subs/sub-0.packets.json"), json!({"packets": packets}).to_string());
    }

    /// recs/disc-b under `root`: scan.txt and the rip labels all-tracks (title 0, every stream), eng-only (title 0, the
    /// eng profile) and extra (title 1).
    fn disc_b(root: &Path) {
        let rec = root.join("recs/disc-b");
        write(&rec.join("scan.txt"), disc_b_scan());
        let summary = |title: i64, profile: &str| {
            json!({"ok": true, "title": title, "profile": format!("C:\\made-up\\{profile}")}).to_string()
        };
        let video = ("video", "AVC/H.264/MPEG-4p10", None);
        let hd_ma = ("audio", "DTS-HD Master Audio", Some(6));
        let core = ("audio", "DTS", Some(6));
        let pgs = ("subtitles", "HDMV PGS", None);

        let all = rec.join("all-tracks");
        write(&all.join("rip-summary.json"), summary(0, "all-tracks.mmcp.xml"));
        write(&all.join("mkvmerge.json"), ident_b(&[video, hd_ma, core, hd_ma, core, pgs], 5, 3_000_500_000_000));
        write(&all.join("rip.txt"), removal(6));
        write(&all.join("ffprobe-streams.json"), ffprobe_b(&["DTS-HD MA", "DTS", "DTS-HD MA", "DTS"], 1));
        write(
            &all.join("audio-levels-20ms-1-2-3-4/manifest.txt"),
            manifest_b(&[("main", 1, TWIN_A), ("cand", 2, TWIN_B), ("cand", 3, TWIN_A), ("cand", 4, TWIN_B)]),
        );
        subs_b(&all, 5);

        let eng = rec.join("eng-only");
        write(&eng.join("rip-summary.json"), summary(0, "eng-only.mmcp.xml"));
        write(&eng.join("mkvmerge.json"), ident_b(&[video, hd_ma, hd_ma, pgs], 5, 3_000_500_000_000));
        write(&eng.join("rip.txt"), removal(4));
        write(&eng.join("ffprobe-streams.json"), ffprobe_b(&["DTS-HD MA", "DTS-HD MA"], 1));
        write(&eng.join("audio-levels-20ms-1-2/manifest.txt"), manifest_b(&[("main", 1, TWIN_A), ("cand", 2, TWIN_A)]));
        subs_b(&eng, 3);

        let extra = rec.join("extra");
        write(&extra.join("rip-summary.json"), summary(1, "all-tracks.mmcp.xml"));
        write(&extra.join("mkvmerge.json"), ident_b(&[video, ("audio", "AC-3", Some(2))], 1, 180_200_000_000));
        write(&extra.join("rip.txt"), RIP);
    }

    /// decide_doc over recs/disc-b (named by its path) with cwd `root`, no OCR text, the profile's selection and no
    /// settings file (spec 14's defaults).
    fn doc_b(root: &Path, label: &str) -> DecideDoc {
        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(root);
        let rec = resolve_recording(&ctx, None, "recs/disc-b").unwrap();
        decide_doc(&ctx, &rec, label, None, None, None).unwrap()
    }

    /// The decision section's document; panics with the reason when it was skipped.
    fn results_of(entry: &DecisionEntry) -> &DecisionDoc {
        match entry {
            DecisionEntry::Results(found) => found,
            DecisionEntry::Skipped { skipped } => panic!("the decision was skipped: {skipped}"),
        }
    }

    /// The kept subtitle tracks as (scan stream, role, events).
    fn kept_subtitles(decision: &FileDecision) -> Vec<(u32, SubtitleRole, Option<usize>)> {
        decision.subtitles.kept.iter().map(|track| (track.stream, track.role, track.events)).collect()
    }

    /// The scan streams of the final file's tracks, in order (8.10).
    fn layout_streams(decision: &FileDecision) -> Vec<u32> {
        decision.layout.tracks.iter().map(|track| track.stream).collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_plan_section_is_lazymkv_dev_plans_document_for_the_recording() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("plan-section");
        let root = tmp.0.clone();
        disc_b(&root);
        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(&root);
        let rec = resolve_recording(&ctx, None, "recs/disc-b").unwrap();
        let doc = decide_doc(&ctx, &rec, "all-tracks", None, None, None).unwrap();
        let expected = plan_doc(&ctx, &PlanSource::Recording(&rec), &PlanOptions::default()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(doc.plan, PlanEntry::Results(expected.clone()));
        // decide plans with spec 14's defaults.
        assert_eq!(expected.settings, Settings::default());
        // Spec 8.1 step 6 (no lookup recorded), 8.2 (a movie by default), 8.3 rule 3.5 (one rival at 0.85), 6.1 step 5's
        // mode at 0.85, spec 5's title key.
        let plan = &expected.plan;
        assert_eq!((plan.identity.step, plan.identity_confidence, plan.identity.tmdb), (IdentityStep::Nothing, 0.0, None));
        assert_eq!(plan.kind, Kind::Movie);
        let titles: Vec<(u32, &str)> = plan.titles.iter().map(|planned| (planned.title, planned.key.as_str())).collect();
        assert_eq!(titles, [(0, "t00-00800")]);
        assert_eq!((plan.title_confidence, plan.mode), (0.85, Mode::Direct));
        assert_eq!(plan.reviews, [ReviewReason::IdentityUnknown]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_decision_maps_the_rips_files_onto_the_scan_streams() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("decision-facts");
        let root = tmp.0.clone();
        disc_b(&root);
        let doc = doc_b(&root, "all-tracks");
        let all = results_of(&doc.decision);
        assert_eq!(all.title_key, "t00-00800");
        assert!(all.verify.ok, "{:?}", all.verify.mismatches);
        // Every selected stream but the removed forced-only one is in the file, track id = position.
        let pairs: Vec<(u32, Option<i64>)> = (0..6).map(|stream| (stream, Some(i64::from(stream)))).collect();
        assert_eq!(all.verify.pairs, pairs);
        assert_eq!(
            all.facts,
            FactsSummary {
                md5_streams: vec![1, 2, 3, 4],
                profile_streams: vec![1, 2, 3, 4],
                event_streams: vec![5],
                verdict_streams: Vec::new(),
                verdict_reference: None,
                text_streams: Vec::new(),
                removed: vec![6],
            }
        );
        // The eng profile left the cores out: file tracks 1, 2 and 3 are scan streams 1, 3 and 5, and MSG:4047's index
        // 4 counts the selection [0, 1, 3, 5, 6], so it is stream 6.
        let doc = doc_b(&root, "eng-only");
        let eng = results_of(&doc.decision);
        assert!(eng.verify.ok, "{:?}", eng.verify.mismatches);
        assert_eq!(eng.verify.pairs, vec![(0, Some(0)), (1, Some(1)), (3, Some(2)), (5, Some(3))]);
        assert_eq!(
            eng.facts,
            FactsSummary {
                md5_streams: vec![1, 3],
                profile_streams: vec![1, 3],
                event_streams: vec![5],
                verdict_streams: Vec::new(),
                verdict_reference: None,
                text_streams: Vec::new(),
                removed: vec![6],
            }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_twin_tracks_of_a_rip_are_dropped_as_duplicates_by_their_md5() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("decision-twins");
        let root = tmp.0.clone();
        disc_b(&root);
        let doc = doc_b(&root, "all-tracks");
        let decided = results_of(&doc.decision);
        let decision = &decided.decision;
        assert_eq!(decision.title_key, "t00-00800");
        // 8.6 step 1: the cores are derived (2048); stream 3's packets equal stream 1's (D13): one copy is kept.
        let kept: Vec<(u32, &str)> = decision.audio.kept.iter().map(|track| (track.stream, track.name.as_str())).collect();
        assert_eq!(kept, [(1, "DTS-HD MA 5.1")]);
        assert_eq!(
            decision.audio.dropped,
            vec![(2, AudioDrop::Derived), (3, AudioDrop::Duplicate { of: 1 }), (4, AudioDrop::Derived)]
        );
        assert_eq!(decision.audio.confidence, 0.95);
        // 8.7: the forced-only stream is set aside and MakeMKV removed it as empty; the one full track is "English".
        assert_eq!(kept_subtitles(decision), [(5, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(40))]);
        assert_eq!(decision.subtitles.dropped, vec![(6, SubtitleDrop::DerivedForcedOnlyEmpty)]);
        assert_eq!(decision.subtitles.confidence, 0.90);
        // 8.8: identity and title from the plan, track the lower of 0.95 and 0.90; no TMDb record, so no path.
        assert_eq!(decision.confidences, Confidences { identity: 0.0, title: 0.85, track: 0.90 });
        assert_eq!(decision.reviews, [ReviewReason::IdentityUnknown]);
        assert_eq!(decision.path, None);
        assert_eq!(decision.disposition, Disposition::NeedsReview);
        assert_eq!(layout_streams(decision), [0, 1, 5]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_rip_with_the_eng_selection_is_decided_over_its_selected_streams_only() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("decision-eng");
        let root = tmp.0.clone();
        disc_b(&root);
        let doc = doc_b(&root, "eng-only");
        let decision = &results_of(&doc.decision).decision;
        // The cores (2, 4) are not in this rip: they are neither kept nor dropped; the twin is dropped by its MD5.
        let kept: Vec<u32> = decision.audio.kept.iter().map(|track| track.stream).collect();
        assert_eq!(kept, [1]);
        assert_eq!(decision.audio.dropped, vec![(3, AudioDrop::Duplicate { of: 1 })]);
        assert_eq!(kept_subtitles(decision), [(5, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(40))]);
        assert_eq!(decision.subtitles.dropped, vec![(6, SubtitleDrop::DerivedForcedOnlyEmpty)]);
        assert_eq!(layout_streams(decision), [0, 1, 5]);
        // The all-tracks rip of the same title makes the same final file.
        let doc = doc_b(&root, "all-tracks");
        assert_eq!(layout_streams(&results_of(&doc.decision).decision), [0, 1, 5]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_refused_plan_skips_both_new_sections_and_leaves_decides_exit_code() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("plan-refused");
        let root = tmp.0.clone();
        disc_b(&root);
        // A lookup file that exists and does not parse is the one input plan_doc refuses for a recording (Task 15).
        write(&root.join("recs/disc-b/thediscdb-hash.json"), "{");
        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(&root);
        let rec = resolve_recording(&ctx, None, "recs/disc-b").unwrap();
        let refused = plan_doc(&ctx, &PlanSource::Recording(&rec), &PlanOptions::default()).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(refused.code, 2);
        let doc = decide_doc(&ctx, &rec, "all-tracks", None, None, None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(doc.plan, PlanEntry::Skipped { skipped: refused.line.clone() });
        assert_eq!(doc.decision, DecisionEntry::Skipped { skipped: format!("no plan: {}", refused.line) });
        // decide still prints its document and exits with the reconciler's code.
        let (code, out, err) = run_in(&root, &["recs/disc-b", "all-tracks"]);
        assert_eq!((code, err.as_str()), (0, ""));
        let value: Value = serde_json::from_str(&out).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(value["plan"], json!({"skipped": refused.line}));
        assert_eq!(value["decision"], json!({"skipped": format!("no plan: {}", refused.line)}));
        assert_eq!(value["reviews"], json!([]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_answer_the_plan_leaves_unread_is_left_unread_by_the_decision() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("decision-unread-answers");
        let root = tmp.0.clone();
        disc_b(&root);
        // The recorder keeps the body of every status (spec 8.1): TMDb's error body of a 404, and the server's page of a
        // failed TheDiscDB lookup. plan_doc parses an answer only when its status line is 200 or absent (Task 15), and
        // the decision takes the answers plan_doc parsed, so neither section parses these bodies.
        write(&root.join("recs/disc-b/lookup-status.txt"), "dischash 500\ntmdb movie/4242 404\n");
        write(&root.join("recs/disc-b/thediscdb-hash.json"), "<html>Internal Server Error</html>");
        write(
            &root.join("recs/disc-b/tmdb.json"),
            json!({"success": false, "status_code": 34,
                   "status_message": "The resource you requested could not be found."})
            .to_string(),
        );
        let doc = doc_b(&root, "all-tracks");
        let PlanEntry::Results(plan) = &doc.plan else {
            panic!("the plan was skipped: {:?}", doc.plan);
        };
        let answers = (plan.inputs.discdb_hash.answer.as_str(), plan.inputs.tmdb.answer.as_str());
        assert_eq!(answers, ("failed", "miss"));
        // No record names the file: the decision is made without a path, and held (8.8).
        let decided = results_of(&doc.decision);
        assert_eq!(decided.decision.path, None);
        assert_eq!(decided.decision.disposition, Disposition::NeedsReview);
    }

    /// A level folder's audio-proxy.json as the recorder writes it, reduced to what decide reads: per (ffprobe stream,
    /// packet MD5) one track whose `source_stream` and `source.md5` they are.
    fn proxy_b(tracks: &[(u32, &str)]) -> String {
        let tracks: Vec<Value> = tracks
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(k, (stream, md5))| {
                json!({"track": k, "source_stream": stream, "series": format!("track-{k}.txt"),
                       "source": {"codec": "dts", "channels": 6, "md5": md5}})
            })
            .collect();
        let count = tracks.len();
        json!({"format": "lazymkv audio proxy v1", "source": {"file": "title_t00.mkv", "audio_streams": count},
               "tracks": tracks})
        .to_string()
    }
```
