```rust
/// The content rule's verdicts as the decision takes them (spec 8.6 "Content", RP7): per scan stream, the stream they
/// were measured against, and whether D21's veto held for it.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
struct ContentVerdicts {
    by_stream: BTreeMap<u32, Verdict>,
    reference: Option<u32>,
    veto_holds: bool,
}

/// The file phase of one rip label (RP14, spec 6.4 step 11), as phase 2's engine will run it after a Direct rip. The
/// label's title (`doc.reconcile.title`, with the selection decide used) must be one of `plan`'s titles (Err "the plan
/// does not include title <n> (planned: <titles>)"). <slug>/scan.txt is typed (`disc::disc`) and the rip's
/// mkvmerge.json is verified against the scan's title with the rip log (`verify::verify_rip`, spec 6.2 step 7), whose
/// pairs map every file track onto its scan stream. The title is narrowed to the selected streams, so a rip with the
/// eng selection is decided over the streams it holds. The facts: every level folder's manifest.txt and
/// audio-proxy.json give the packet MD5s (6.4 step 10a, D13), ffprobe-streams.json the audio profiles (6.4 step 9),
/// subs/ the event start times at `plan.settings.sub_clear_max_bytes` (`verify::subtitle_events`, 8.7), decide's
/// reconcile section the streams MakeMKV removed (its `dropped` rows, `MSG:4047`), decide's audio section the content
/// rule's verdicts against their `main=` stream (RP7), decide's subtitles section the text rule's decisions (8.7
/// "Text"), and the lookup answers as the plan section parsed them (`cmd::plan::recorded_answers`) TheDiscDB's matched
/// title (`lookup::discdb::match_titles`) and the TMDb record that names the file when it is the plan's identity
/// (8.9); the rip's read errors and `verify::failure_reviews(&report, !report.ok)` are carried in (the recorded rip is
/// the last attempt there will be, so a rip that fails verification raises verify_failed, as 6.2 step 7's second
/// failure does). The settings are the plan's; `LibraryFacts` are the defaults (phase 2 reads the library, RP18).
/// `decision::decide` then gives the FileDecision. Err with the sentence of an input that cannot be read, or decide's.
/// `_ctx` is not read: every input is under the recording's tree.
pub fn decision_doc(
    _ctx: &Ctx,
    rec: &Recording,
    label: &str,
    plan: &PlanDoc,
    doc: &DecideDoc,
) -> Result<DecisionDoc, String> {
    let tree: &dyn Tree = &rec.tree;
    let label_dir = rec.dir.join(label);
    let number = doc.reconcile.title;
    let planned = planned_title(&plan.plan, number)?;
    let scan = read_scan_in(tree, &rec.dir.join("scan.txt"), Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Replace)?;
    let typed = disc::disc(&scan)?;
    let scanned = typed.title(number)?;
    let selection = selected_streams(&scan, number, doc.reconcile.selection)?;
    let ident = read_ident(tree, &label_dir.join("mkvmerge.json"))?;
    let rip_text = read_rip_log(tree, &label_dir)?.map(|(_, text)| text);
    let report = verify_rip(scanned, &ident, &selection, rip_text.as_deref(), typed.is_dvd);
    let mut title = scanned.clone();
    title.streams.retain(|stream| selection.contains(&stream.number));
    let settings = &plan.settings;
    // MSG:4047's removals as decide's own reconcile section counted them (6.2 step 7): not computed a second time.
    let removed: BTreeSet<u32> = doc.reconcile.dropped.iter().map(|row| row.stream).collect();
    let md5 = level_md5s(tree, &label_dir, &report)?;
    let profiles = ffprobe_profiles(tree, &label_dir, &report)?;
    let events = subtitle_starts(tree, &label_dir, &report, settings.sub_clear_max_bytes)?;
    let verdicts = ContentVerdicts::default();
    let text: BTreeMap<u32, TextDecision> = BTreeMap::new();
    // The lookup answers exactly as the plan section parsed them (a non-200 answer is left unparsed there).
    let answers = recorded_answers(rec).map_err(|refused| refused.line)?;
    let record: Option<TmdbRecord> = None;
    let (rip_reviews, read_errors): (Vec<ReviewReason>, Vec<ReadError>) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
    // TheDiscDB's record as plan_doc chose it: the fingerprint's, else the first disc-ID record with titles.
    let discdb = answers
        .by_fingerprint
        .as_ref()
        .or_else(|| answers.by_disc_id.iter().find(|record| !record.titles.is_empty()))
        .and_then(|record| discdb_title(record, &typed, number));
    let facts = FactsSummary {
        md5_streams: md5.keys().copied().collect(),
        profile_streams: profiles.keys().copied().collect(),
        event_streams: events.keys().copied().collect(),
        verdict_streams: verdicts.by_stream.keys().copied().collect(),
        verdict_reference: verdicts.reference,
        text_streams: text.keys().copied().collect(),
        removed: removed.iter().copied().collect(),
    };
    let library = LibraryFacts::default();
    let inputs = DecisionInputs {
        plan: &plan.plan,
        disc: &typed,
        planned,
        title: &title,
        audio: AudioFacts {
            md5,
            ffprobe_profile: profiles,
            discdb,
            verdicts: verdicts.by_stream,
            veto_holds: verdicts.veto_holds,
            verdict_reference: verdicts.reference,
            remembered: None,
            reviewed: None,
        },
        subtitles: SubtitleFacts {
            events,
            removed,
            discdb,
            text: (!text.is_empty()).then_some(&text),
            remembered: None,
            reviewed: None,
        },
        record: record.as_ref(),
        library: &library,
        rip_reviews,
        read_errors,
        overrides: None,
        settings,
    };
    let decision = file_decision(&inputs)?;
    Ok(DecisionDoc { title_key: planned.key.clone(), verify: report, facts, decision })
}

/// The plan's title `number` (Plan.titles, spec 6.1 step 5); Err "the plan does not include title <n> (planned: <the
/// planned titles in plan order, or none>)" for a title the plan left out (a Direct-mode job holds only its planned
/// titles, 8.8).
fn planned_title(plan: &Plan, number: u32) -> Result<&PlannedTitle, String> {
    plan.titles.iter().find(|planned| planned.title == number).ok_or_else(|| {
        let planned: Vec<String> = plan.titles.iter().map(|planned| planned.title.to_string()).collect();
        let list = if planned.is_empty() { "none".to_string() } else { planned.join(", ") };
        format!("the plan does not include title {number} (planned: {list})")
    })
}

/// The rip's MakeMKV log and its path: the first of RIP_LOG_NAMES beside mkvmerge.json, read as compare_tracks.main
/// reads it (UTF-8, invalid bytes replaced, newlines as text mode gives them); None when the label has neither.
fn read_rip_log(tree: &dyn Tree, label_dir: &PathKey) -> Result<Option<(PathKey, String)>, String> {
    match RIP_LOG_NAMES.iter().map(|name| label_dir.join(name)).find(|path| tree.exists(path)) {
        Some(path) => {
            let text = text_mode(&read_text(tree, &path, Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Replace)?);
            Ok(Some((path, text)))
        }
        None => Ok(None),
    }
}

/// A file track number as text ("1", the spelling of manifest.txt and of the audio section) to its scan stream through
/// the verify report's pairs (an ffprobe index of an MKV equals its mkvmerge track id).
fn track_stream(text: &str, report: &VerifyReport) -> Option<u32> {
    text.trim().parse::<i64>().ok().and_then(|track| stream_of_track(report, track))
}

/// The packet MD5 of every audio stream the label's level folders hold (6.4 step 10a, D13), keyed by scan stream: over
/// every audio-levels-20ms-* folder in PathKey order, first the `md5=` of each manifest.txt line with `main=` or
/// `cand=`, then the `source.md5` of each audio-proxy.json track by its `source_stream` (both ffprobe stream numbers of
/// the file, mapped through the verify pairs); the first MD5 of a stream wins; `-` or empty is no MD5. The manifests are
/// git-ignored side files, like the level series, but audio-proxy.json is tracked and holds the same MD5s for every
/// audio stream of the file, so a clone without the level files keeps them. Err when a manifest cannot be read or an
/// audio-proxy.json does not parse.
fn level_md5s(tree: &dyn Tree, label_dir: &PathKey, report: &VerifyReport) -> Result<BTreeMap<u32, String>, String> {
    let mut md5 = BTreeMap::new();
    for folder in tree.glob(label_dir, LEVEL_FOLDERS) {
        if !tree.is_dir(&folder) {
            continue;
        }
        let manifest = read_manifest(tree, &folder)?;
        let main = manifest.main.iter().map(|fields| (fields, "main"));
        let lines = main.chain(manifest.cands.iter().map(|fields| (fields, "cand")));
        for (fields, key) in lines {
            let stream = fields.get(key).and_then(|text| track_stream(text, report));
            first_md5(&mut md5, stream, fields.get("md5").map(|text| text.trim()));
        }
        let proxy_path = folder.join("audio-proxy.json");
        if tree.is_file(&proxy_path) {
            let text = read_text(tree, &proxy_path, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Strict)?;
            let proxy = parse_proxy(&text).map_err(|error| format!("{}: {}", tree.display(&proxy_path), error))?;
            for track in &proxy.tracks {
                let stream = track.source_stream.as_i64().and_then(|index| stream_of_track(report, index));
                let digest = track.source.as_ref().and_then(|source| source.get("md5")).and_then(|value| value.as_str());
                first_md5(&mut md5, stream, digest.map(str::trim));
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(md5)
}

/// Records `digest` as the MD5 of `stream` unless the stream already has one; a missing stream, a missing digest, an
/// empty one or `-` records nothing.
fn first_md5(md5: &mut BTreeMap<u32, String>, stream: Option<u32>, digest: Option<&str>) {
    let digest = digest.filter(|text| !text.is_empty() && *text != "-");
    if let (Some(stream), Some(digest)) = (stream, digest) {
        md5.entry(stream).or_insert_with(|| digest.to_string());
    }
}

/// ffprobe's profile of every audio stream of the file (6.4 step 9: "DTS-HD MA", "DTS"), from
/// <label>/ffprobe-streams.json, keyed by scan stream; streams without a profile are left out. Empty when the file is
/// absent; Err "<path>: <serde's message>" when it does not parse.
fn ffprobe_profiles(
    tree: &dyn Tree,
    label_dir: &PathKey,
    report: &VerifyReport,
) -> Result<BTreeMap<u32, String>, String> {
    let path = label_dir.join("ffprobe-streams.json");
    if !tree.is_file(&path) {
        return Ok(BTreeMap::new());
    }
    let probe: FfprobeStreams = read_json(tree, &path).map_err(|error| format!("{}: {}", tree.display(&path), error))?;
    Ok(probe
        .streams
        .iter()
        .filter(|stream| stream.codec_type.as_deref() == Some("audio"))
        .filter_map(|stream| {
            let profile = stream.profile.as_deref().filter(|profile| !profile.is_empty())?;
            Some((stream_of_track(report, stream.index)?, profile.to_string()))
        })
        .collect())
}

/// The event start times of every subtitle stream the label's subs/ folder holds (6.4 step 10, 8.7 "Events"), keyed by
/// scan stream: `verify::subtitle_events` at `clear_max_bytes` (spec 14 `sub_clear_max_bytes`). Empty when the label
/// has no subs/index.json (6.4 step 10 skipped, or a title without subtitles).
fn subtitle_starts(
    tree: &dyn Tree,
    label_dir: &PathKey,
    report: &VerifyReport,
    clear_max_bytes: i64,
) -> Result<BTreeMap<u32, Vec<f64>>, String> {
    let subs = label_dir.join("subs");
    if !tree.is_file(&subs.join("index.json")) {
        return Ok(BTreeMap::new());
    }
    subtitle_events(tree, &subs, report, clear_max_bytes)
}

/// The database title matched to scan title `number` (spec 8.3 "Database titles are matched to scan titles",
/// `lookup::discdb::match_titles`), whose track descriptions 8.6 step 1 and 8.7 use; None when none matches.
fn discdb_title<'r>(record: &'r DiscDbRecord, disc: &Disc, number: u32) -> Option<&'r DiscDbTitle> {
    let index = match_titles(record, disc).into_iter().find(|(_, scan)| *scan == number).map(|(index, _)| index)?;
    record.titles.iter().find(|title| title.index == index)
}

/// The content rule's verdicts of decide's audio section, as 8.6 "Content" takes them (RP7): each measured level
/// folder's `main=` stream and candidates (file track numbers, which ffprobe and mkvmerge share) mapped onto scan
/// streams through the verify report's pairs. The first folder whose main stream maps gives the reference; a folder
/// measured against another stream is left out, with its verdicts and its veto, since they answer another reference;
/// within the reference's folders the first verdict of a stream wins, and D21's veto holds when one of them says it
/// holds. A skipped folder, and a folder with no mapped candidate, gives nothing (it does not fix the reference). When
/// no verdict was taken (only main-only folders), there is no reference and no veto: AudioFacts.verdict_reference is
/// None when there are no verdicts, so nothing measured is not judged.
fn content_verdicts(audio: &[AudioEntry], report: &VerifyReport) -> ContentVerdicts {
    let mut found = ContentVerdicts::default();
    for entry in audio {
        let AudioEntry::Results(folder) = entry else {
            continue;
        };
        let Some(main) = folder.main.get("main").and_then(|text| track_stream(text, report)) else {
            continue;
        };
        let mapped: Vec<(u32, Verdict)> = folder
            .candidates
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|candidate| track_stream(&candidate.stream, report).map(|stream| (stream, candidate.verdict)))
            .collect();
        if mapped.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        if *found.reference.get_or_insert(main) != main {
            continue;
        }
        found.veto_holds |= folder.veto.holds == Some(true);
        for (stream, verdict) in mapped {
            found.by_stream.entry(stream).or_insert(verdict);
        }
    }
    if found.by_stream.is_empty() {
        found.reference = None;
        found.veto_holds = false;
    }
    found
}

```rust
/// The text rule's decisions of decide's subtitles section (8.7 "Text"), keyed by scan stream: each stream's `decide`
/// by its subs/index.json `n`, mapped through the index's track ids and the verify report's pairs
/// (`verify::subs_streams`, `verify::by_scan_stream`); a stream without a decision is left out. Empty when the section
/// was skipped (no OCR text), and when `settings.text_rule()` is not `text::Rule::default()`, the rule the section ran
/// with, since its decisions answer other thresholds (spec 14's subtitle settings, RP15). subs/index.json is read by
/// `verify::subs_index`, the reading `verify::subtitle_events` shares. Err when it cannot be read or does not parse.
fn text_decisions(
    subtitles: &SubtitleEntry,
    tree: &dyn Tree,
    label_dir: &PathKey,
    report: &VerifyReport,
    settings: &Settings,
) -> Result<BTreeMap<u32, TextDecision>, String> {
    let SubtitleEntry::Results(subs) = subtitles else {
        return Ok(BTreeMap::new());
    };
    if settings.text_rule() != TextRule::default() {
        return Ok(BTreeMap::new());
    }
    let by_n: BTreeMap<i64, TextDecision> =
        subs.streams.iter().filter_map(|stream| stream.decide.clone().map(|decided| (stream.n, decided))).collect();
    // Read as verify::subtitle_events reads it (invalid bytes replaced), so an index that gave the events never turns
    // the text into an Err that skips the decision.
    let index = subs_index(tree, &label_dir.join("subs"))?;
    Ok(by_scan_stream(&by_n, &subs_streams(&index, report)))
}

    #[test]

        let doc = doc_b(&root, "all-tracks");

        assert_eq!(decided.verify.read_errors, vec![error.clone()]);
        // The rip saved: it verifies, and is kept with read_errors (6.2 step 7); a rip that verifies raises no
        // verify_failed.
        assert!(decided.verify.ok, "{:?}", decided.verify.mismatches);
        assert_eq!(decided.decision.read_errors, vec![error]);
        assert_eq!(decided.decision.reviews, [ReviewReason::IdentityUnknown, ReviewReason::ReadErrors]);
        assert_eq!(decided.decision.disposition, Disposition::NeedsReview);

    #[test]
    fn a_rip_that_fails_verification_raises_verify_failed_and_is_held() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("decision-verify-failed");
        let root = tmp.0.clone();
        disc_b(&root);
        // The file lacks the PGS track the selection expects (6.2 step 7: the ordered match fails).
        let video = ("video", "AVC/H.264/MPEG-4p10", None);
        let hd_ma = ("audio", "DTS-HD Master Audio", Some(6));
        let core = ("audio", "DTS", Some(6));
        let ident = ident_b(&[video, hd_ma, core, hd_ma, core], 5, 3_000_500_000_000);
        write(&root.join("recs/disc-b/all-tracks/mkvmerge.json"), ident);
        let doc = doc_b(&root, "all-tracks");
        let decided = results_of(&doc.decision);
        assert!(!decided.verify.ok);
        // The recorded rip is the last attempt there will be: verify_failed holds the job, as a second failure does.
        let reviews = &decided.decision.reviews;
        assert!(reviews.contains(&ReviewReason::VerifyFailed), "{:?}", reviews);
        assert_eq!(decided.decision.disposition, Disposition::NeedsReview);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_settings_file_gives_decides_own_decision_its_final_path() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("decision-settings");
        let root = tmp.0.clone();
        disc_b(&root);
        write(&root.join("recs/disc-b/thediscdb-hash.json"), discdb_answer());
        write(&root.join("recs/disc-b/tmdb.json"), tmdb_answer(4242));
        write(&root.join("settings.json"), json!({"movies_root": "/srv/media/Movies"}).to_string());
        let path = "/srv/media/Movies/Made Up Film (2001) {tmdb-4242}/Made Up Film (2001) {tmdb-4242} - 1080p.mkv";
        // decide_doc with the settings file (spec 14): the plan carries the root, and decide's own decision files.
        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(&root);
        let rec = resolve_recording(&ctx, None, "recs/disc-b").unwrap();
        let doc = decide_doc(&ctx, &rec, "all-tracks", None, None, Some(Path::new("settings.json"))).unwrap();
        let PlanEntry::Results(plan) = &doc.plan else {
            panic!("the plan was skipped: {:?}", doc.plan);
        };
        assert_eq!(plan.settings.movies_root.as_deref(), Some("/srv/media/Movies"));
        let decision = &results_of(&doc.decision).decision;
        assert_eq!(decision.path.as_ref().map(|named| named.path.as_str()), Some(path));
        assert_eq!(decision.disposition, Disposition::AutoFile);
        // The command takes it as --settings FILE.
        let (code, out, err) = run_in(&root, &["recs/disc-b", "all-tracks", "--settings", "settings.json"]);
        assert_eq!((code, err.as_str()), (0, ""));
        let value: Value = serde_json::from_str(&out).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(value["decision"]["decision"]["path"]["path"], json!(path));
        assert_eq!(value["decision"]["decision"]["disposition"], json!("auto_file"));
        // A settings file plan_doc refuses (an unknown key, Task 15) skips the plan with its line, and the decision.
        write(&root.join("bad-settings.json"), r#"{"bogus": 1}"#);
        let doc = decide_doc(&ctx, &rec, "all-tracks", None, None, Some(Path::new("bad-settings.json"))).unwrap();
        let PlanEntry::Skipped { skipped } = &doc.plan else {
            panic!("the plan was not skipped: {:?}", doc.plan);
        };
        assert!(skipped.starts_with("bad-settings.json: bogus: "), "{}", skipped);
        assert_eq!(doc.decision, DecisionEntry::Skipped { skipped: format!("no plan: {skipped}") });
        let (code, _, err) = run_in(&root, &["recs/disc-b", "all-tracks", "--settings", "bad-settings.json"]);
        assert_eq!((code, err.as_str()), (0, ""));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_printed_document_reads_back_whole() {
        let tmp = Scratch::new("decision-read-back");
        let root = tmp.0.clone();
        disc_b(&root);
        write(&root.join("recs/disc-b/thediscdb-hash.json"), discdb_answer());
        write(&root.join("recs/disc-b/tmdb.json"), tmdb_answer(4242));
        let doc = doc_b(&root, "all-tracks");
        // TheDiscDB's matches are a list of entries sorted by database index (the interfaces' "Keyed collections").
        let PlanEntry::Results(plan) = &doc.plan else {
            panic!("the plan was skipped: {:?}", doc.plan);
        };
        assert_eq!(plan.plan.evidence.discdb_matches, vec![DiscDbMatch { discdb_index: 0, title: 0 }]);
        let (code, out, err) = run_in(&root, &["recs/disc-b", "all-tracks"]);
        assert_eq!((code, err.as_str()), (0, ""));
        let read: DecideDoc = serde_json::from_str(&out).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(read, doc);
        // A skipped section reads back as skipped.
        let skipped: DecisionEntry = serde_json::from_value(json!({"skipped": "made-up"})).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(skipped, DecisionEntry::Skipped { skipped: "made-up".to_string() });
    }

/// Spec 8.9 "Title and year always come from the same TMDb record as the ID": the record names the file only when it
/// is the record of the plan's identity; a record of another identity, or one without an identity in hand, names
/// nothing, so the decision is made without a path (`decision::decide` refuses a record of another identity).
fn record_for_naming(identity: Option<TmdbIdentity>, record: Option<TmdbRecord>) -> Option<TmdbRecord> {

`crates/dev/tests/decide.rs` runs decide once per rip label and compares its six sections with the goldens; it now also checks the two new sections of the same document, so no level folder is measured twice. The expected values are read from the recordings' files on 2026-10-16 and follow the rules:

- **Plans** ("Expected plans" of the phase 1 plan): Pan's Labyrinth and the Office are TheDiscDB by fingerprint (8.1 step 3, 0.95; both disc-ID lookups answered 404), with 8.3 rule 1 at 0.98 for Pan's Labyrinth's title 0 and 8.5's mapped episodes at 0.98 for the Office in episode order (title 3 is S03E12-E13, title 2 S03E14, title 1 S03E15, title 0 S03E16, title 6 S03E17, title 5 S03E18, keyed `t00-` to `t05-` and the stem of the title's playlist, which the test reads from the recording's scan when it runs, RP21); both Short Circuit DVDs have no answer (8.1 step 6, `identity_unknown`) and one structural rival (8.3 rule 3.5, 0.85), keyed `t00-title01`.
- **Facts**: MD5s from the level folders' manifests and `audio-proxy.json` files (the proxies are tracked and name every audio stream of the file: Short Circuit 2's `all-tracks-2` folder `audio-levels-20ms-1` gives streams 1 to 4), mapped through the verify pairs (Pan's Labyrinth's `all-tracks` file holds scan streams 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, so its ffprobe stream 5 is scan stream 6; its `eng-only` file holds 0, 3, 4, so ffprobe 1 is scan 3); profiles from `ffprobe-streams.json` (the DTS-HD MA and DTS streams; the Dolby Digital and DVD streams have none); events from `subs/index.json`; `MSG:4047` removals (the empty forced-only streams: Pan's Labyrinth's 5 and 7, the Office's 5, 6 and 5).
- **Audio** (8.6): the derived DTS cores are dropped (flag 2048); the Office's `rehearsal` title 1 carries twin DTS-HD MA tracks with equal packet MD5s (streams 1 and 3), so stream 3 is dropped as a duplicate of stream 1 (D13) and its core 4 as derived; Pan's Labyrinth is Spanish, so its Spanish DTS-HD MA comes first (`original_language_first`), and its `eng-only` rip holds no Spanish stream (`original_language_missing`); Short Circuit 2's French, Spanish and Portuguese tracks are unwanted (no TMDb answer: English only). The content rule's verdicts (the audio goldens: `commentary-cross-language` on Pan's Labyrinth's English stereo, `commentary` on the Office's `e16-stereo` stereo track) raise `commentary_detected` and drop nothing (D15); `note-commentary` (`t3-all-tracks`) is a note.
- **Subtitles** (8.7): one full English track kept as "English" at 0.90; the removed forced-only streams dropped empty; other languages dropped; Short Circuit 2's closed captions kept as SDH (its dialogue group has no SDH track); Short Circuit has no subtitle stream (0.95).
- **Confidences, reviews, paths**: identity and title from the plan, track the lower of 0.95 and the subtitles'; reviews the plan's, the rules' and the rip's (Short Circuit 2's `all-tracks-2` rip logged three read errors at one offset: `read_errors`); with the owner's roots the Office's S03E15 and S03E12-E13 file automatically and the others are held by a review reason, or by having no TMDb record and so no path.

Parts that depend on an input the clone may lack are skipped with their reason, never failed. The MD5s, the audio tracks kept and dropped and the audio review reasons are compared whenever the label has a level folder (every level folder keeps its `audio-proxy.json` in git, so its MD5s are there with or without the level files). The verdicts, the review reasons they raise (`commentary_detected`, `audio_reference_unclear`, left out of both sides of the review comparisons) and the disposition are compared only when every level folder was measured (its level series are git-ignored side files); the track confidence, reviews and disposition only when no OCR text was read (the text can add `subtitle_ambiguous`, 8.7 "Text"). A main-only level folder gives no verdict, so its `verdict_reference` is None (settled point 4): Pan's Labyrinth's `eng-only` and both Short Circuit 2 labels.

/// path and disposition show: decide's own document has spec 14's defaults, which set no root, so it builds no path
/// and holds every job (Task 13).
const MOVIES_ROOT: &str = r"\\unas-pro\media\Movies";
const SHOWS_ROOT: &str = r"\\unas-pro\media\Shows";
/// The review reasons only the content rule's verdicts raise (8.6 "Content", RP7): compared only when every level

/// What decide's plan and decision sections must hold for one recording: the plan, and the decision per rip label.
struct RecordingExpectation {
    plan: PlanExpectation,
    labels: Vec<(&'static str, LabelExpectation)>,
}

/// The plan section: identity step, identity confidence and TMDb identity (8.1), kind (8.2), titles in plan order with
/// their keys (spec 5), title confidence (8.3, 8.5), mode (6.1 step 5) and review reasons.
struct PlanExpectation {
    step: IdentityStep,
    identity_confidence: f64,
    tmdb: Option<TmdbIdentity>,
    kind: Kind,
    titles: Vec<(u32, String)>,
    title_confidence: f64,
    mode: Mode,
    reviews: Vec<ReviewReason>,
}

/// The decision section of one rip label: skipped with this reason, or decided.
enum LabelExpectation {
    Skipped(&'static str),
    Decided(DecisionExpectation),
}

/// A decided rip label. The lists of scan streams are sorted; `audio_kept` is in final order (8.6 step 5),

    title_key: String,

    profile_streams: Vec<u32>,
    event_streams: Vec<u32>,
    verdict_streams: Vec<u32>,

    reviews: Vec<ReviewReason>,

    path: Option<String>,
    disposition: Disposition,
}

/// Adds "<what>: <actual:?>, expected <expected:?>" to `failures` when the two differ.
fn same<T: PartialEq + Debug>(failures: &mut Vec<String>, what: &str, actual: T, expected: T) {
    if actual != expected {
        failures.push(format!("{}: {:?}, expected {:?}", what, actual, expected));
    }
}

/// `entries` sorted by scan stream (a stable sort: one entry per stream in practice).
fn sorted<T>(mut entries: Vec<(u32, T)>) -> Vec<(u32, T)> {
    entries.sort_by_key(|(stream, _)| *stream);
    entries
}

/// The plan section of one label's document against the recording's plan expectation.
fn check_plan(slug: &str, label: &str, doc: &DecideDoc, expected: &PlanExpectation, failures: &mut Vec<String>) {
    let at = format!("{}/{}: plan", slug, label);
    let plan = match &doc.plan {
        PlanEntry::Results(found) => &found.plan,
        PlanEntry::Skipped { skipped } => {
            failures.push(format!("{}: skipped ({})", at, skipped));
            return;
        }
    };
    same(failures, &format!("{at}: identity step"), plan.identity.step, expected.step);
    same(failures, &format!("{at}: identity confidence"), plan.identity_confidence, expected.identity_confidence);
    same(failures, &format!("{at}: TMDb identity"), plan.identity.tmdb, expected.tmdb);
    same(failures, &format!("{at}: kind"), plan.kind, expected.kind);
    let titles: Vec<(u32, String)> = plan.titles.iter().map(|planned| (planned.title, planned.key.clone())).collect();
    let want: Vec<(u32, String)> = expected.titles.iter().map(|(title, key)| (*title, key.to_string())).collect();
    same(failures, &format!("{at}: titles"), titles, want);
    same(failures, &format!("{at}: title confidence"), plan.title_confidence, expected.title_confidence);
    same(failures, &format!("{at}: mode"), plan.mode, expected.mode);
    same(failures, &format!("{at}: reviews"), plan.reviews.clone(), expected.reviews.clone());
}

/// The decision section of one label's document against its expectation, then a second decision from the same plan
/// with the owner's library roots for the final path and the disposition (decide's own document plans without a
/// settings file, so its decision has no path).
fn check_decision(
    ctx: &Ctx,
    rec: &Recording,
    label: &str,
    doc: &DecideDoc,
    expected: &LabelExpectation,
    failures: &mut Vec<String>,
) {
    let at = format!("{}/{}: decision", rec.slug, label);
    let (want, got) = match (expected, &doc.decision) {
        (LabelExpectation::Skipped(why), DecisionEntry::Skipped { skipped }) => {
            same(failures, &format!("{at}: skipped"), skipped.as_str(), *why);
            return;
        }
        (LabelExpectation::Skipped(why), DecisionEntry::Results(_)) => {
            failures.push(format!("{at}: decided, expected it skipped with \"{why}\""));
            return;
        }
        (LabelExpectation::Decided(_), DecisionEntry::Skipped { skipped }) => {
            failures.push(format!("{at}: skipped ({skipped}), expected a decision"));
            return;
        }
        (LabelExpectation::Decided(want), DecisionEntry::Results(got)) => (want, got),
    };
    // Every level folder keeps its audio-proxy.json in git, so the label's MD5s are here whenever a level folder is.
    let levels = !doc.audio.is_empty();
    // A level folder whose level series are absent was skipped: no verdict.
    let measured = levels && doc.audio.iter().all(|entry| matches!(entry, AudioEntry::Results(_)));
    // OCR text was read: the text may add subtitle_ambiguous (8.7 "Text").
    let text_read = matches!(doc.subtitles, SubtitleEntry::Results(_));
    // Without the verdicts, the review reasons they raise are left out of both sides.
    let judged = |reasons: &[ReviewReason]| -> Vec<ReviewReason> {
        reasons.iter().copied().filter(|reason| measured || !VERDICT_REVIEWS.contains(reason)).collect()
    };
    let decision = &got.decision;
    same(failures, &format!("{at}: title key"), got.title_key.as_str(), want.title_key.as_str());
    same(failures, &format!("{at}: verify mismatches"), got.verify.mismatches.clone(), Vec::new());
    same(failures, &format!("{at}: verify ok"), got.verify.ok, true);
    same(failures, &format!("{at}: profile streams"), got.facts.profile_streams.clone(), want.profile_streams.clone());
    same(failures, &format!("{at}: event streams"), got.facts.event_streams.clone(), want.event_streams.clone());
    same(failures, &format!("{at}: removed streams"), got.facts.removed.clone(), want.removed.clone());
    let kept: Vec<(u32, SubtitleRole)> = decision.subtitles.kept.iter().map(|track| (track.stream, track.role)).collect();
    same(failures, &format!("{at}: subtitles kept"), kept, want.subtitles_kept.clone());
    same(
        failures,
        &format!("{at}: subtitles dropped"),
        sorted(decision.subtitles.dropped.clone()),
        want.subtitles_dropped.clone(),
    );
    same(
        failures,
        &format!("{at}: identity and title confidence"),
        (decision.confidences.identity, decision.confidences.title),
        (want.confidences.0, want.confidences.1),
    );
    // decide's own document has no library root.
    same(failures, &format!("{at}: path without a library root"), decision.path.clone(), None);
    same(failures, &format!("{at}: disposition without a library root"), decision.disposition, Disposition::NeedsReview);
    if levels {
        same(failures, &format!("{at}: MD5 streams"), got.facts.md5_streams.clone(), want.md5_streams.clone());
        let audio: Vec<u32> = decision.audio.kept.iter().map(|track| track.stream).collect();
        same(failures, &format!("{at}: audio kept"), audio, want.audio_kept.clone());
        same(failures, &format!("{at}: audio dropped"), sorted(decision.audio.dropped.clone()), want.audio_dropped.clone());
        same(failures, &format!("{at}: audio reviews"), judged(&decision.audio.reviews), judged(&want.audio_reviews));
    } else {
        skip(&format!(
            "{}/{}: decision's MD5s and audio tracks not compared: the label has no level folder",
            rec.slug, label
        ));
    }
    if measured {
        same(failures, &format!("{at}: verdict streams"), got.facts.verdict_streams.clone(), want.verdict_streams.clone());
        same(failures, &format!("{at}: verdict reference"), got.facts.verdict_reference, want.verdict_reference);
    } else {
        skip(&format!(
            "{}/{}: decision's verdicts, the review reasons they raise and the disposition not compared: a level \
             folder was not measured (its level series are not here)",
            rec.slug, label
        ));
    }
    if text_read {
        skip(&format!(
            "{}/{}: decision's track confidence, reviews and disposition not compared: OCR text was read, and the \
             text can add subtitle_ambiguous (8.7 \"Text\")",
            rec.slug, label
        ));
    } else {
        same(failures, &format!("{at}: text streams"), got.facts.text_streams.clone(), Vec::new());
        same(failures, &format!("{at}: track confidence"), decision.confidences.track, want.confidences.2);
        same(failures, &format!("{at}: reviews"), judged(&decision.reviews), judged(&want.reviews));
    }
    let PlanEntry::Results(plan) = &doc.plan else {
        return;
    };
    let mut rooted = plan.clone();
    rooted.settings.movies_root = Some(MOVIES_ROOT.to_string());
    rooted.settings.tv_root = Some(SHOWS_ROOT.to_string());
    match decision_doc(ctx, rec, label, &rooted, doc) {
        Ok(found) => {
            let path = found.decision.path.as_ref().map(|named| named.path.clone());
            same(failures, &format!("{at}: final path"), path, want.path.clone());
            if measured && !text_read {
                same(failures, &format!("{at}: disposition"), found.decision.disposition, want.disposition);
            }
        }
        Err(why) => failures.push(format!("{at}: with library roots: {why}")),
    }
}

/// The typed scan.txt of `slug` in the evidence clone, read when the test runs; None, with the skip line written, when
/// the clone or the recording is absent.
fn recorded_disc(slug: &str) -> Option<Disc> {
    let evidence = match resolve_evidence(&context(), None) {
        Ok(dir) => dir,
        Err(refused) => {
            skip(&refused.line);
            return None;
        }
    };
    let path = evidence.join(slug).join("scan.txt");
    if !path.is_file() {
        skip(&format!("no {} (this recording is absent)", path.display()));
        return None;
    }
    let bytes = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{}: {}", path.display(), error));
    let text = decode_text(&bytes, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Replace)
        .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{}: {}", path.display(), error));
    Some(disc(&parse(&text)).unwrap_or_else(|sentence| panic!("{}: {}", path.display(), sentence)))
}

#[test]
fn pans_labyrinth_2006_uhd() {
    check_recording("pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd", &pans_labyrinth());
}

#[test]
fn short_circuit_1986_dvd() {
    check_recording("short-circuit-1986-dvd", &short_circuit());
}

#[test]
fn short_circuit_2_1988_dvd() {
    check_recording("short-circuit-2-1988-dvd", &short_circuit_2());
}

#[test]
fn the_office_2005_s3d3_bluray() {
    let slug = "the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray";
    let Some(disc) = recorded_disc(slug) else { return };
    check_recording(slug, &the_office(&disc));
}

The `COMMANDS` row becomes `("labels", cmd::labels::run as Command, "[--spec FILE] [--subtitles] kinds|check|set|unset|title|auto|fitted ...")`. `SubtitleKind` also implements `std::str::FromStr` (the plan's convention for every closed set: only the spellings of `KINDS`, Err `'<text>' is not one of <the ten spellings, joined by ", ">`).

Where this task settles what RP15, the spec and the interfaces leave open (each choice is pinned by a test below):

1. **The file's shape.** `subtitle-labels.json` mirrors `audio-labels.json` without its `titles` object (RP15 names none; row 14's feature and TV split is the recording's, Task 18's business): top-level keys `format`, `slug`, `tracks` and the optional `removed`; every track has exactly `label`, `stream`, `kind`, `how`, `sure`, `date`, `saw_verdict`, `note`, `style` (all required, as the audio file's keys are) and may have `history`. The two keys beyond RP15's list are ruling RP25's (Review Focus 11). `saw_verdict`, as in `audio-labels.json`, records whether the owner saw the rule's verdict before giving the label, and such a label never counts (section 17 row 14 (a): "A track counts only when its content was checked before the verdict"): it is a `bool` after `date`, checked with `sure`, and Task 18 counts only a label whose `saw_verdict` is false. `style` is `null` or `"uk"` (`SubtitleLabel.style: Option<String>`, after `note`): `"uk"` marks a UK-style SDH track (speakers by colour, sounds without brackets), which row 14 asks for if the owner has a UK disc, and Task 18 counts it towards that requirement on a counted `sdh` label only; the file accepts it on any kind, and on another kind it is kept and reported but never counted. `note` is text or `null` (`SubtitleLabel.note: Option<String>`, written as `null` when absent, as every `Option` of the plan is); the command writes `null` when `--note` is not given. A `history` entry and a `removed` entry are checked only for what reading them needs (the keys, the label, the stream, the date, and their `replaced` or `removed` date), so an older vocabulary survives in them, as `audio::labels::entry_problems(strict = false)` does. `how` and `style` are closed sets but stay `String` and `Option<String>` (the file is read from the owner's disk, may carry an older vocabulary in `history`, and is validated by `problems` against `HOW` and `null`/"uk" as `audio-labels.json`'s `how` is), an exception to the conventions' "Closed sets are enums" that mirrors the audio file (RP15, RP25); `SubtitleKind` is the enum. Calling the port's existing `py_repr_str`, `py_str` and `py_truthy` (through `crate::recording` and `audio::labels`' shared helpers) to keep `audio::labels::problems`' sentences is RP15's reuse of validation code, not a new `py_*` spelling under RP20; the new module defines no `py_*` function and no `Ordered`.
2. **`stream` is ffprobe's stream number** of the rip label's file (mkvmerge's track id, `subs/index.json`'s `track_id`), as in `audio-labels.json`, and the sentence says so; Task 18 maps it to the scan stream through `verify::stream_of_track`.
3. **The sentences** are `audio::labels::problems`' wording with the subtitle vocabulary: `kind <the value> is not in the vocabulary (lazymkv-dev labels --subtitles kinds)` and `how <the value> is not one of read, watched, packaging, menu, flag, player, thediscdb`, and `style <the value> is not null or 'uk'`. The `how` vocabulary is RP15's with ruling RP25's `flag` (a flag in MakeMKV's scan, such as the commentary flag 1 or the forced flag 4096), placed after `menu` in row 14's order ("the packaging, the menu, a flag, the player and TheDiscDB"), so the observations are five and none counts on its own (D23). `load` compares the slug with the folder's resolved name (`Tree::resolved_name` of the file's parent), not the lexical parent the audio `load` uses, so `labels --subtitles check .` run inside a recording compares the real folder name.
4. **Edits are pure and refuse a change that adds a problem** (as `audio::labels::prepare_save`): `set_track` keeps the value exactly as given (no sort, no write) when one old label of the track has the same `kind`, `how`, `sure`, `saw_verdict`, `note` and `style`; otherwise every old label of the track goes into the new entry's `history` (its own history first) with `replaced` set to the new date. `unset_track` moves every label of the track to `removed` with `removed` (the date) and `why`. Both sort the tracks stably by (label, stream). Their Err sentences carry no path (`not written: <the new problems>`, `<label> stream <n> has no label`, `unset needs --note: why the label is taken away`, `'removed' is not a list, so the label cannot be moved there`, `the file has no 'tracks' list, so nothing is changed`); the command prefixes `<slug_dir>/subtitle-labels.json: `. The slug is compared by `load` and `check`, never by an edit (`problems(.., None)`), since an edit never changes it.
5. **The command.** `--subtitles` is a main option before the command word, beside `--spec` (argparse's prefix rule: `--su` names it, `--sp` names `--spec`, `--s` is ambiguous). It takes `kinds`, `check`, `set` and `unset`; `title`, `auto` and `fitted` with `--subtitles` are an argument error. The subtitle words read no spec (what counts towards row 14, the two fitting discs included, is Task 18's). `set` has `--how` (required), `--saw-verdict yes|no` (required, as the audio `set`'s: the owner says each time whether the verdict was seen first; settled point 1), `--sure yes|no` (default yes), `--date` (default today), `--note` (default none), `--style uk` (default none, written as `null`; RP25). Its line is `labelled|unchanged <label> stream <n>: <kind> (<how>, <date>, saw verdict yes|no, sure yes|no)`, with `, style uk` before the closing parenthesis when the label has that style, with ` ('<how>' is an observation, not a check of the track's text (row 14, D23))` for the five observations (D23) and `; replaces <n> earlier label(s), kept in its history` after a replacement. `check` reads `<path>/subtitle-labels.json` (`core::subtitle::labels::FILE_NAME`, the one copy of the name, which Task 18's harness uses too) when it exists, else every `*/subtitle-labels.json`, and prints `ok <file> (<n> tracks)`, the refusal, or `<path>: no subtitle-labels.json`; exit 2 when a file is bad.
6. **Reuse.** The four audio helpers the subtitle labels call that are not about audio (the value accessors, the JSON reader, the sort key) become `pub(crate)`. As RP15 asks ("reusing the audio labels' validation code where it is shared"), the validation blocks the two files share move out of the audio functions into the `pub(crate)` helpers named under Files: the head checks (`head_problems`), the removed loop (`removed_problems`), the base entry checks (keys, label, stream, date: `base_entry_problems`) and the history loop (`history_problems`); the stream check and `sorted_list` stay private, called only by those helpers. The audio functions call them with audio's vocabulary, so their output is unchanged and their tests and goldens pass untouched. `subtitle::labels::problems`/`entry_problems` call them with the subtitle vocabulary and add only the subtitle checks (kind, how, `saw_verdict`/`sure`, note, style, and the duplicate (label, stream)). The private `how_names` becomes `pub(crate) fn names(table: &[(&str, &str)])`, called by both files. `check_lines`' labels part becomes the public `labels_check_lines`, which audio's `check_lines` and the dev crate's `subtitle_check_lines` both call. In the dev crate, the `Check` arms of `execute` and `execute_subtitles` both call one `check_paths(ctx, &paths, out, lines: fn(&dyn Tree, &PathKey) -> (Vec<String>, usize))`. Nothing is copied (the one-copy rule); `is_slug` and `date_ok` are already public.
7. **Settings.** No code of this task reads `Settings`, so there is no default-and-other-value test.

/// The names of a (name, meaning) table, in order: the `how` vocabulary of these labels and of the subtitle labels
/// (`subtitle::labels`, RP15).
pub(crate) fn names<'a>(table: &[(&'a str, &'a str)]) -> Vec<&'a str> {
    table.iter().map(|&(name, _)| name).collect()
}

/// The first checks of a labels file, shared with the subtitle labels (RP15): the top-level keys that are not in
/// `top_keys`, the format line against `format`, and the slug, compared with `folder` when it is given. Py: problems'
/// first checks.
pub(crate) fn head_problems(d: &Map<String, Value>, top_keys: &[&str], format: &str, folder: Option<&str>) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let extra: Vec<&str> = d.keys().map(String::as_str).filter(|k| !top_keys.contains(k)).collect();
    if !extra.is_empty() {
        out.push(format!("unknown top-level keys {}", sorted_list(extra)));
    }
    if get(d, "format").as_str() != Some(format) {
        out.push(format!("format is {}, not {}", repr_of(d, "format"), py_repr_str(format)));
    }
    match get(d, "slug").as_str() {
        Some(own) if is_slug(own) => {
            if let Some(folder) = folder {
                if own != folder {
                    out.push(format!("slug is {} but the file is in corpus/owner/{folder}", py_repr_str(own)));
                }
            }
        }
        _ => out.push(format!("slug {} is not lowercase letters, digits and hyphens", repr_of(d, "slug"))),
    }
    out
}

/// The problems of a labels file's `removed` list, shared with the subtitle labels (RP15): each entry read with
/// `loose` (the file's own entry check with strict false) and its `removed` date. Py: problems' removed loop.
pub(crate) fn removed_problems(d: &Map<String, Value>, loose: impl Fn(&Value, &str) -> Vec<String>) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    match d.get("removed") {
        None => {}
        Some(Value::Array(removed)) => {
            for (k, r) in removed.iter().enumerate() {
                let Some(rm) = r.as_object() else {
                    out.push(format!("removed {k}: not an object"));
                    continue;
                };
                out.extend(loose(r, &format!("removed {k}")));
                if !date_ok(get(rm, "removed")) {
                    out.push(format!("removed {k}: removed {} is not YYYY-MM-DD", repr_of(rm, "removed")));
                }
            }
        }
        Some(_) => out.push("removed is not a list".to_string()),
    }
    out
}

/// The checks every entry of a labels file has, strict or not, shared with the subtitle labels (RP15): the keys of
/// `track_keys` that are missing, the keys in neither `track_keys` nor `allowed`, the label, the stream and the date,
/// each sentence prefixed with `where_`. Py: entry_problems' first checks.
pub(crate) fn base_entry_problems(m: &Map<String, Value>, where_: &str, track_keys: &[&str], allowed: &[&str]) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let missing: Vec<&str> = track_keys.iter().copied().filter(|k| !m.contains_key(*k)).collect();
    let unknown: Vec<&str> = m.keys().map(String::as_str).filter(|k| !track_keys.contains(k) && !allowed.contains(k)).collect();
    if !missing.is_empty() {
        out.push(format!("{where_}: missing {}", sorted_list(missing)));
    }
    if !unknown.is_empty() {
        out.push(format!("{where_}: unknown keys {}", sorted_list(unknown)));
    }
    if !get(m, "label").as_str().map_or(false, is_slug) {
        out.push(format!("{where_}: label is not a rip label"));
    }
    if !is_stream_number(get(m, "stream")) {
        out.push(format!("{where_}: stream is not ffprobe's stream number (an integer, 0 or more)"));
    }
    if !date_ok(get(m, "date")) {
        out.push(format!("{where_}: date {} is not YYYY-MM-DD", repr_of(m, "date")));
    }
    out
}

/// The problems of a strict entry's `history` list, shared with the subtitle labels (RP15): each earlier label read
/// with `loose` (the file's own entry check with strict false) and its `replaced` date. Py: entry_problems' history
/// loop.
pub(crate) fn history_problems(m: &Map<String, Value>, where_: &str, loose: impl Fn(&Value, &str) -> Vec<String>) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    match m.get("history") {
        None => {}
        Some(Value::Array(history)) => {
            for (k, h) in history.iter().enumerate() {
                let Some(hm) = h.as_object() else {
                    out.push(format!("{where_}: history {k} is not an object"));
                    continue;
                };
                out.extend(loose(h, &format!("{where_} history {k}")));
                if !date_ok(get(hm, "replaced")) {
                    out.push(format!("{where_} history {k}: replaced {} is not YYYY-MM-DD", repr_of(hm, "replaced")));
                }
            }
        }
        Some(_) => out.push(format!("{where_}: history is not a list")),
    }
    out
}
```

Replace the whole of `entry_problems` and `problems`, which are adjacent: from the line `/// The problems of one track entry. strict=false (history and removed entries) checks only that the entry can be` to the closing brace of `problems` (the `}` before the empty line and `/// A title's facts. ...`), with this. The doc comments, the title checks, the kind, how, md5, saw_verdict, sure, note and film_audible checks and the duplicate check are the file's own lines, unchanged; the head, the `removed` loop, the base entry checks and the history loop are now the helpers' calls:

```rust
/// The problems of one track entry. strict=false (history and removed entries) checks only that the entry can be
/// read: its kind and how may come from an older vocabulary. A value that is not an object is read as an empty one.
/// Py: entry_problems.
pub fn entry_problems(t: &Value, where_: &str, strict: bool) -> Vec<String> {
    let empty = Map::new();
    let m = t.as_object().unwrap_or(&empty);
    let allowed: &[&str] = if strict { &OPTIONAL_KEYS } else { &LOOSE_KEYS };
    let mut out = base_entry_problems(m, where_, &TRACK_KEYS, allowed);
    if !strict {
        return out;
    }
    let kind = get(m, "kind").as_str();
    let how = get(m, "how").as_str();
    if !kind.map_or(false, |k| kind_of(k).is_some()) {
        out.push(format!("{where_}: kind {} is not in the vocabulary (lazymkv-dev labels kinds)", repr_of(m, "kind")));
    }
    if !how.map_or(false, |h| HOW.iter().any(|(name, _)| *name == h)) {
        out.push(format!("{where_}: how {} is not one of {}", repr_of(m, "how"), names(&HOW).join(", ")));
    }
    if how == Some("md5") && kind != Some("duplicate") {
        out.push(format!("{where_}: how md5 only says that a track is a duplicate"));
    }
    for key in ["saw_verdict", "sure"] {
        if !get(m, key).is_boolean() {
            out.push(format!("{where_}: {key} must be true or false"));
        }
    }
    if !m.get("note").map_or(true, Value::is_string) {
        out.push(format!("{where_}: note is not text"));
    }
    if m.contains_key("film_audible") {
        if !kind.map_or(false, |k| COMMENTARY_KINDS.contains(&k)) {
            out.push(format!("{where_}: film_audible is only for {}", COMMENTARY_KINDS.join(" and ")));
        } else if !true_false_none(m.get("film_audible")) {
            out.push(format!("{where_}: film_audible must be true, false or null"));
        }
    }
    out.extend(history_problems(m, where_, |h, w| entry_problems(h, w, false)));
    out
}

/// Every problem of a parsed labels file, one sentence each, verbatim; empty when it is valid. `slug` is the folder
/// the file is in (None: not compared). Py: problems.
pub fn problems(data: &Value, slug: Option<&str>) -> Vec<String> {
    let Some(d) = data.as_object() else { return vec!["the file is not a JSON object".to_string()] };
    let mut out = head_problems(d, &TOP_KEYS, FORMAT, slug);
    let no_titles = Map::new();
    let titles = match d.get("titles") {
        Some(Value::Object(titles)) => titles,
        _ => {
            out.push("titles is not an object".to_string());
            &no_titles
        }
    };
    for (label, t) in titles {
        let where_ = format!("title {label}");
        if !is_slug(label) {
            out.push(format!("{where_}: not a rip label"));
        }
        let Some(tm) = t.as_object() else {
            out.push(format!("{where_}: not an object"));
            continue;
        };
        let unknown: Vec<&str> = tm.keys().map(String::as_str).filter(|k| !TITLE_KEYS.contains(k)).collect();
        if !unknown.is_empty() {
            out.push(format!("{where_}: unknown keys {}", sorted_list(unknown)));
        }
        if !get(tm, "title_kind").as_str().map_or(false, |k| TITLE_KINDS.contains(&k)) {
            out.push(format!("{where_}: title_kind {} is not one of {}", repr_of(tm, "title_kind"), TITLE_KINDS.join(", ")));
        }
        if !true_false_none(tm.get("dialogue_heavy")) {
            out.push(format!("{where_}: dialogue_heavy must be true, false or null"));
        }
        if !tm.get("note").map_or(true, Value::is_string) {
            out.push(format!("{where_}: note is not text"));
        }
    }
    out.extend(removed_problems(d, |r, where_| entry_problems(r, where_, false)));
    let Some(tracks) = get(d, "tracks").as_array() else {
        out.push("tracks is not a list".to_string());
        return out;
    };
    let mut seen: Vec<(Value, Value)> = Vec::new();
    for (k, t) in tracks.iter().enumerate() {
        let Some(tm) = t.as_object() else {
            out.push(format!("track {k}: not an object"));
            continue;
        };
        let (label, stream) = (get(tm, "label").clone(), get(tm, "stream").clone());
        let where_ = format!("track {} stream {}", py_str(&label), py_str(&stream));
        out.extend(entry_problems(t, &where_, true));
        if seen.iter().any(|(l, s)| py_eq(l, &label) && py_eq(s, &stream)) {
            out.push(format!("{where_}: labelled twice"));
        }
        seen.push((label, stream));
    }
    out
}
```

Replace the whole of `check_lines`, from its doc comment's first line `` /// `labels check <root>`'s lines for one root and the number of bad files: root/audio-labels.json when it exists, `` to its closing brace, with `labels_check_lines` and the shorter `check_lines` (same lines, same order, same count of bad files):

```rust
/// The labels part of `labels check <root>`, shared with `labels --subtitles check` (RP15): root/<file_name> when it
/// exists, else every */<file_name> (never one under golden/), each "ok <file> (<what load_count says of it>)" or the
/// refusal `load_count` gives, which makes the file a bad one; "<root>: no <file_name>" when there is none. Returns
/// the lines and the number of bad files. Public because the dev crate's subtitle `check` calls it. Py: main's check
/// branch.
pub fn labels_check_lines(
    tree: &dyn Tree,
    root: &PathKey,
    file_name: &str,
    load_count: &dyn Fn(&dyn Tree, &PathKey) -> Result<String, String>,
) -> (Vec<String>, usize) {
    let mut lines = Vec::new();
    let mut bad = 0;
    let own = root.join(file_name);
    let files = if tree.exists(&own) { vec![own] } else { tree.glob(root, &format!("*/{file_name}")) };
    if files.is_empty() {
        lines.push(format!("{}: no {file_name}", tree.display(root)));
    }
    for path in &files {
        match load_count(tree, path) {
            Ok(count) => lines.push(format!("ok {} ({count})", tree.display(path))),
            Err(e) => {
                lines.push(e);
                bad += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    (lines, bad)
}

/// `labels check <root>`'s lines for one root and the number of bad files: root/audio-labels.json when it exists,
/// else every */audio-labels.json (never one under golden/), then root/audio-fitted.json when it exists.
/// Py: main's check branch.
pub fn check_lines(tree: &dyn Tree, root: &PathKey) -> (Vec<String>, usize) {
    let (mut lines, mut bad) = labels_check_lines(tree, root, "audio-labels.json", &|tree, path| {
        load(tree, path).map(|labels| format!("{} tracks, {} titles", labels.tracks.len(), labels.titles.len()))
    });
    let fitted_path = root.join("audio-fitted.json");
    if tree.exists(&fitted_path) {
        match load_fitted(tree, root, None) {
            Ok(fitted) => lines.push(format!("ok {} ({} entries)", tree.display(&fitted_path), fitted.len())),
            Err(e) => {
                lines.push(e);
                bad += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    (lines, bad)
}
```

//! "Recordings" and its `retune` paragraph, section 17 row 14, D20, D23): what each English or no-language subtitle
//! track of a rip label is, kept beside `audio-labels.json` and in its shape. The file is a `serde_json::Value` with
//! insertion order kept, so an unknown key and every character of a note survive an edit; `problems` validates the
//! value in the wording of `audio::labels::problems`, and the typed `SubtitleLabel`s are made only after it passes.
//! The edits (`set_track`, `unset_track`) are functions from the value to the new value that refuse a change adding
//! a problem; `lazymkv-dev labels --subtitles` reads and writes the file. Which labels count towards row 14 is Task
//! 18's (`retune --subtitles`): only a `read` or `watched` label given before the verdict (`saw_verdict` false) can
//! (D23, section 17 row 14 (a)), and a counted `sdh` label with `style` "uk" is row 14's UK-style SDH track (RP25).
//! The validation this file shares
//! with the audio labels (the head checks, the `removed` list, an entry's keys, label, stream and date, and its
//! history) and the helpers it needs (the value accessors, the JSON reader, the `how` names and the sort key) are
//! `audio::labels`' own, called rather than copied (RP15). Written from the spec (RP20); no I/O (RP19): files come through a
//! `Tree`. Used by Tasks 17 and 18.

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    use serde_json::{json, Value};

    use crate::recording::{MemTree, PathKey};
    use crate::testsupport::with;

    /// A subtitle label as `labels --subtitles set` writes it: how "read", sure, dated 2026-10-14, given before the
    /// verdict, no note, no style.
    fn label(name: &str, stream: i64, kind: &str) -> Value {
        json!({
            "label": name, "stream": stream, "kind": kind, "how": "read", "sure": true, "date": "2026-10-14",
            "saw_verdict": false, "note": null, "style": null,
        })
    }

    /// The typed form of `label(name, stream, kind.as_str())`.
    fn typed(name: &str, stream: i64, kind: SubtitleKind) -> SubtitleLabel {
        SubtitleLabel {
            label: name.to_string(),
            stream,
            kind,
            how: "read".to_string(),
            sure: true,
            date: "2026-10-14".to_string(),
            saw_verdict: false,
            note: None,
            style: None,
        }
    }

    /// A subtitle labels file of the recording disc-b holding `tracks`.
    fn file(tracks: Vec<Value>) -> Value {
        json!({"format": FORMAT, "slug": "disc-b", "tracks": tracks})
    }

    /// `value` (an object) without `key`.
    fn without(mut value: Value, key: &str) -> Value {
        value.as_object_mut().expect("an object").remove(key);
        value
    }

    /// A tree printed under corpus/owner holding disc-b/subtitle-labels.json with `bytes`.
    fn tree_with(bytes: &[u8]) -> MemTree {
        let mut tree = MemTree::new("corpus/owner", "owner");
        tree.insert_file("disc-b/subtitle-labels.json", bytes.to_vec());
        tree
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_kinds_are_rp15s_ten_in_order_with_what_the_owner_wants() {
        let names: Vec<&str> = KINDS.iter().map(|(kind, _, _)| *kind).collect();
        let spelled: Vec<&str> = SubtitleKind::ALL.iter().map(|kind| kind.as_str()).collect();
        assert_eq!(names, spelled);
        assert_eq!(
            names,
            ["regular", "sdh", "forced", "commentary", "trivia", "lyrics", "translation", "dub-transcript", "closed-captions", "other"]
        );
        // D20 and R5: the dialogue kinds and the forced track are kept; R6 and D20: commentary, trivia and lyrics are
        // dropped when confirmed; a track no kind describes is the owner's question.
        let wanted: Vec<&str> = KINDS.iter().map(|(_, wanted, _)| *wanted).collect();
        assert_eq!(wanted, ["keep", "keep", "keep", "drop", "drop", "drop", "keep", "keep", "keep", "ask"]);
        assert!(KINDS.iter().all(|(_, _, meaning)| !meaning.is_empty()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_sources_are_d23s_two_checks_of_the_text_and_five_observations() {
        let names: Vec<&str> = HOW.iter().map(|(how, _)| *how).collect();
        assert_eq!(names, ["read", "watched", "packaging", "menu", "flag", "player", "thediscdb"]);
        assert_eq!(HOW[4], ("flag", "a flag in MakeMKV's scan (an observation: does not count on its own, D23)"));
        let sources: Vec<&str> = COUNTING_HOW.iter().chain(OBSERVATION_HOW.iter()).copied().collect();
        assert_eq!(names, sources);
        for (how, meaning) in HOW {
            if COUNTING_HOW.contains(&how) {
                assert!(meaning.ends_with("(counts, D23)"), "{how}: {meaning}");
            } else {
                assert!(meaning.ends_with("(an observation: does not count on its own, D23)"), "{how}: {meaning}");
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_kind_is_spelled_the_same_by_as_str_serde_and_from_str() {
        for kind in SubtitleKind::ALL {
            assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(kind).unwrap(), json!(kind.as_str()));
            assert_eq!(serde_json::from_value::<SubtitleKind>(json!(kind.as_str())).unwrap(), kind);
            assert_eq!(SubtitleKind::from_str(kind.as_str()), Ok(kind));
        }
        assert_eq!(SubtitleKind::DubTranscript.as_str(), "dub-transcript");
        assert_eq!(SubtitleKind::ClosedCaptions.as_str(), "closed-captions");
        let all = "regular, sdh, forced, commentary, trivia, lyrics, translation, dub-transcript, closed-captions, other";
        assert_eq!(SubtitleKind::from_str("SDH"), Err(format!("'SDH' is not one of {all}")));
        assert_eq!(SubtitleKind::from_str("closed_captions"), Err(format!("'closed_captions' is not one of {all}")));
        assert!(serde_json::from_value::<SubtitleKind>(json!("closed_captions")).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_label_serialises_with_the_files_keys_in_order() {
        let mut dub = typed("all-tracks", 4, SubtitleKind::DubTranscript);
        assert_eq!(
            serde_json::to_string(&dub).unwrap(),
            r#"{"label":"all-tracks","stream":4,"kind":"dub-transcript","how":"read","sure":true,"date":"2026-10-14","saw_verdict":false,"note":null,"style":null}"#
        );
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(&dub).unwrap(), label("all-tracks", 4, "dub-transcript"));
        dub.note = Some("the English dub's words".to_string());
        let text = serde_json::to_string(&dub).unwrap();
        assert!(text.ends_with(r#""note":"the English dub's words","style":null}"#), "{text}");
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<SubtitleLabel>(&text).unwrap(), dub);
    }
}

The `use` lines serve Steps 4 to 16, so `cargo` warns `unused import` for `json`, `Map`, `base_entry_problems`, `get`, `head_problems`, `history_problems`, `names`, `read_value`, `removed_problems`, `repr_of`, `track_sort_key`, `py_str`, `PathKey` and `Tree` until Step 16 uses the last of them.

```rust
use std::str::FromStr;

use serde_json::{json, Map, Value};

use crate::audio::labels::{
    base_entry_problems, get, head_problems, history_problems, names, read_value, removed_problems, repr_of, track_sort_key,
};
use crate::recording::{py_repr_str, py_str, PathKey, Tree};

/// The subtitle labels file's format line, as `audio::labels::FORMAT` is the audio labels'. Spec 15, RP15.
pub const FORMAT: &str = "lazymkv subtitle labels v1";
/// The subtitle labels file's name in a recording folder, beside `audio-labels.json`; the one copy of the name, which
/// `lazymkv-dev labels --subtitles` and Task 18's harness both use. Spec 15, RP15.
pub const FILE_NAME: &str = "subtitle-labels.json";

/// (kind, what the owner wants in the final file, meaning), in RP15's order. What the owner wants follows R5, R6 and
/// D20: the dialogue kinds (regular, SDH, translation, dub transcript, closed captions) and a forced track are kept;
/// commentary is never kept (R6); trivia and lyrics are dropped when confirmed (D20); "ask" for a track no kind
/// describes. Spec 15, section 17 row 14, RP15.
pub const KINDS: [(&str, &str, &str); 10] = [
    ("regular", "keep", "plain dialogue subtitles: the words spoken, with no sound cues or speaker labels (R5, D20)"),
    ("sdh", "keep", "subtitles for the deaf and hard of hearing: the dialogue with sound cues and speaker labels (R5, D20)"),
    ("forced", "keep", "forced subtitles: only the lines for speech in another language, signs and captions (R5, 8.7)"),
    ("commentary", "drop", "a subtitled commentary (R6)"),
    ("trivia", "drop", "trivia or pop-up text (D20: dropped when confirmed)"),
    ("lyrics", "drop", "lyrics or a sing-along track (D20: dropped when confirmed)"),
    ("translation", "keep", "an English translation of the dialogue of a film in another language (R4, R5)"),
    ("dub-transcript", "keep", "a transcript of the English dub, kept beside the translation (D20)"),
    ("closed-captions", "keep", "the DVD's closed captions, which MakeMKV converts to text; SDH by type (8.7)"),
    ("other", "ask", "a track none of the kinds above describes; the note says what it is"),
];

/// (how, meaning): where a label comes from, in RP15's order with ruling RP25's `flag` after the menu, as row 14 lists
/// the observations. Row 14 and D23: a track counts only when its text was read, by OCR text or by watching it; the
/// packaging, the menu, a flag, the player and TheDiscDB are observations. Spec 17 row 14, D23, RP15, RP25.
pub const HOW: [(&str, &str); 7] = [
    ("read", "a person read its OCR text (counts, D23)"),
    ("watched", "a person watched it on screen with the programme (counts, D23)"),
    ("packaging", "the packaging says so (an observation: does not count on its own, D23)"),
    ("menu", "the disc's menu says so (an observation: does not count on its own, D23)"),
    ("flag", "a flag in MakeMKV's scan (an observation: does not count on its own, D23)"),
    ("player", "a player's track list says so (an observation: does not count on its own, D23)"),
    ("thediscdb", "TheDiscDB's track description (an observation: does not count on its own, D23)"),
];
/// D23's counting sources: the two ways a person checks a subtitle track's text. Spec 17 row 14, D23.
pub const COUNTING_HOW: [&str; 2] = ["read", "watched"];
/// Sources kept with a label as observations, never counted on their own. Spec 17 row 14, D23.
pub const OBSERVATION_HOW: [&str; 5] = ["packaging", "menu", "flag", "player", "thediscdb"];

/// RP15's kinds of subtitle track, as the owner labels them; serialised as their spellings in `KINDS`. Spec 15,
/// section 17 row 14, RP15.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
pub enum SubtitleKind {
    /// Plain dialogue subtitles.
    Regular,
    /// Subtitles for the deaf and hard of hearing.
    Sdh,
    /// Forced subtitles.
    Forced,
    /// A subtitled commentary.
    Commentary,
    /// Trivia or pop-up text.
    Trivia,
    /// Lyrics or a sing-along track.
    Lyrics,
    /// An English translation of a film in another language.
    Translation,
    /// A transcript of the English dub.
    DubTranscript,
    /// The DVD's closed captions.
    ClosedCaptions,
    /// Anything else.
    Other,
}

impl SubtitleKind {
    /// Every kind in `KINDS` order. Spec 15, section 17 row 14, RP15.
    pub const ALL: [SubtitleKind; 10] = [
        SubtitleKind::Regular,
        SubtitleKind::Sdh,
        SubtitleKind::Forced,
        SubtitleKind::Commentary,
        SubtitleKind::Trivia,
        SubtitleKind::Lyrics,
        SubtitleKind::Translation,
        SubtitleKind::DubTranscript,
        SubtitleKind::ClosedCaptions,
        SubtitleKind::Other,
    ];

    /// The kind's spelling in the file and in `KINDS`. Spec 15, section 17 row 14, RP15.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            SubtitleKind::Regular => "regular",
            SubtitleKind::Sdh => "sdh",
            SubtitleKind::Forced => "forced",
            SubtitleKind::Commentary => "commentary",
            SubtitleKind::Trivia => "trivia",
            SubtitleKind::Lyrics => "lyrics",
            SubtitleKind::Translation => "translation",
            SubtitleKind::DubTranscript => "dub-transcript",
            SubtitleKind::ClosedCaptions => "closed-captions",
            SubtitleKind::Other => "other",
        }
    }
}

impl FromStr for SubtitleKind {
    type Err = String;

    /// The kind a label spells, exactly; Err "'<text>' is not one of <the ten spellings, joined by ', '>" for anything
    /// else. Spec 15, RP15.
    fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<SubtitleKind, String> {
        SubtitleKind::ALL.into_iter().find(|kind| kind.as_str() == text).ok_or_else(|| {
            let names: Vec<&str> = SubtitleKind::ALL.iter().map(|kind| kind.as_str()).collect();
            format!("{} is not one of {}", py_repr_str(text), names.join(", "))
        })
    }
}

/// One entry of `subtitle-labels.json`, read from a file that validates; the keys in the file's order. Spec 15, RP15, RP25.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct SubtitleLabel {
    /// The rip label (the folder of the rip under the recording).
    pub label: String,
    /// ffprobe's stream number of the track in the rip label's file (mkvmerge's track id).
    pub stream: i64,
    /// What the track is.
    pub kind: SubtitleKind,
    /// Where the label comes from: one of `HOW`.
    pub how: String,
    /// Whether the owner is sure.
    pub sure: bool,
    /// When the label was given, YYYY-MM-DD.
    pub date: String,
    /// Whether the owner saw the rules' verdict on the track before giving the label; such a label never counts
    /// (section 17 row 14 (a): "checked before the verdict", D23), as in `audio-labels.json`.
    pub saw_verdict: bool,
    /// The owner's note; null in the file when there is none.
    pub note: Option<String>,
    /// "uk" for a UK-style SDH track (speakers by colour, sounds without brackets), which section 17 row 14 asks for if
    /// the owner has a UK disc; null in the file otherwise. RP25.
    pub style: Option<String>,
}

    /// The problems of disc-b's file holding the one track `entry`.
    fn track_problems(entry: Value) -> Vec<String> {
        problems(&file(vec![entry]), Some("disc-b"))
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_valid_file_has_no_problems() {
        let data = json!({
            "format": FORMAT,
            "slug": "disc-b",
            "tracks": [
                label("all-tracks", 4, "sdh"),
                with(
                    label("all-tracks", 5, "regular"),
                    "history",
                    json!([with(label("all-tracks", 5, "sdh"), "replaced", json!("2026-10-15"))]),
                ),
                with(label("eng-only", 3, "closed-captions"), "note", json!("CC->Text English ( Lossy conversion )")),
            ],
            "removed": [with(with(label("all-tracks", 6, "forced"), "removed", json!("2026-10-16")), "why", json!("wrong stream"))],
        });
        assert_eq!(problems(&data, Some("disc-b")), Vec::<String>::new());
        assert_eq!(problems(&data, None), Vec::<String>::new());

    }

- [ ] **Step 8: Implement `problems`**

In `crates/core/src/subtitle/labels.rs`, insert this before the line `#[cfg(test)]`, after the code of Step 4 (one empty line between):

```rust
/// Every key a track entry has: RP15's fields and ruling RP25's two, `saw_verdict` (as in `audio-labels.json`, section 17
/// row 14 (a)) and `style` (row 14's UK-style SDH track). Spec 15, RP15, RP25.
const TRACK_KEYS: [&str; 9] = ["label", "stream", "kind", "how", "sure", "date", "saw_verdict", "note", "style"];
/// The other key a track may have: the labels it replaced.
const OPTIONAL_KEYS: [&str; 1] = ["history"];
/// The other keys a history or removed entry may have (checked only for what reading it needs).
const LOOSE_KEYS: [&str; 4] = ["history", "replaced", "removed", "why"];
/// The file's top-level keys: `audio-labels.json`'s without `titles`.
const TOP_KEYS: [&str; 4] = ["format", "slug", "tracks", "removed"];

/// Every problem of a parsed labels file, one sentence each, in `audio::labels::problems`' wording with the
/// subtitle vocabulary; empty when it is valid. `slug` is the name of the folder the file is in (None: not compared).
/// The checks, in order: the top-level keys, the format line, the slug, the `removed` list (each entry read loosely,
/// with its `removed` date), the `tracks` list, then each track's keys, label, stream, date, kind, how,
/// saw_verdict and sure, note, style and history, and a (label, stream) labelled twice. The head, the `removed` list,
/// each entry's keys, label, stream and date, and its history are checked by the helpers `audio::labels` shares with
/// this file (`head_problems`, `removed_problems`, `base_entry_problems`, `history_problems`; RP15), so the two files
/// say those sentences through one copy of the code. Spec 15, section 17 row 14, D23, RP15, RP25.
pub fn problems(data: &Value, slug: Option<&str>) -> Vec<String> {
    let Some(d) = data.as_object() else { return vec!["the file is not a JSON object".to_string()] };
    let mut out = head_problems(d, &TOP_KEYS, FORMAT, slug);
    out.extend(removed_problems(d, |r, where_| entry_problems(r, where_, false)));
    let Some(tracks) = get(d, "tracks").as_array() else {
        out.push("tracks is not a list".to_string());
        return out;
    };
    let mut seen: Vec<(String, i64)> = Vec::new();
    for (k, t) in tracks.iter().enumerate() {
        let Some(tm) = t.as_object() else {
            out.push(format!("track {k}: not an object"));
            continue;
        };
        let where_ = format!("track {} stream {}", py_str(get(tm, "label")), py_str(get(tm, "stream")));
        out.extend(entry_problems(t, &where_, true));
        if let Some(key) = key_of(tm) {
            if seen.contains(&key) {
                out.push(format!("{where_}: labelled twice"));
            }
            seen.push(key);
        }
    }
    out
}

/// The problems of one entry, each prefixed with `where_`. `strict` false (history and removed entries) checks only
/// that the entry can be read: its keys, label, stream and date (`audio::labels::base_entry_problems` with this file's
/// keys), so its kind and how may come from an older vocabulary. A strict entry adds this file's kind, how,
/// saw_verdict and sure, note and style checks, then its history (`audio::labels::history_problems`). A value that is
/// not an object is read as an empty one. Spec 15, RP15.
fn entry_problems(t: &Value, where_: &str, strict: bool) -> Vec<String> {
    let empty = Map::new();
    let m = t.as_object().unwrap_or(&empty);
    let allowed: &[&str] = if strict { &OPTIONAL_KEYS } else { &LOOSE_KEYS };
    let mut out = base_entry_problems(m, where_, &TRACK_KEYS, allowed);
    if !strict {
        return out;
    }
    if !get(m, "kind").as_str().map_or(false, |k| SubtitleKind::from_str(k).is_ok()) {
        out.push(format!("{where_}: kind {} is not in the vocabulary (lazymkv-dev labels --subtitles kinds)", repr_of(m, "kind")));
    }
    if !get(m, "how").as_str().map_or(false, |h| HOW.iter().any(|(name, _)| *name == h)) {
        out.push(format!("{where_}: how {} is not one of {}", repr_of(m, "how"), names(&HOW).join(", ")));
    }
    for key in ["saw_verdict", "sure"] {
        if !get(m, key).is_boolean() {
            out.push(format!("{where_}: {key} must be true or false"));
        }
    }
    let note = get(m, "note");
    if !note.is_string() && !note.is_null() {
        out.push(format!("{where_}: note is not text"));
    }
    let style = get(m, "style");
    if !style.is_null() && style.as_str() != Some("uk") {
        out.push(format!("{where_}: style {} is not null or 'uk'", repr_of(m, "style")));
    }
    out.extend(history_problems(m, where_, |h, w| entry_problems(h, w, false)));
    out
}

/// An entry's (label, stream) when the label is text and the stream an integer; None otherwise (such an entry has
/// its own problems already).
fn key_of(m: &Map<String, Value>) -> Option<(String, i64)> {
    Some((m.get("label")?.as_str()?.to_string(), m.get("stream")?.as_i64()?))
}
```

- [ ] **Step 12: Implement `load`**

In `crates/core/src/subtitle/labels.rs`, insert this before the line `#[cfg(test)]`, after the code of Step 8 (one empty line between):

```rust
/// Reads and validates the labels file at `path`; the slug is compared with the resolved name of the folder the file
/// is in (`Tree::resolved_name` of its parent), so a file read through a tree rooted at its own folder is compared
/// with that folder's real name. Err "<shown>: not valid JSON (<the reason>)", "<shown>: <problems joined by '; '>", or the
/// read error's text. Spec 15, RP15.
pub fn load(tree: &dyn Tree, path: &PathKey) -> Result<Vec<SubtitleLabel>, String> {
    let shown = tree.display(path);
    let data = read_value(tree, path)?.map_err(|e| format!("{shown}: not valid JSON ({e})"))?;
    let found = problems(&data, Some(&tree.resolved_name(&path.parent())));
    if !found.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!("{shown}: {}", found.join("; ")));
    }
    data["tracks"]
        .as_array()
        .into_iter()
        .flatten()
        .map(|t| serde_json::from_value::<SubtitleLabel>(t.clone()).map_err(|e| format!("{shown}: {e}")))
        .collect()
}
