In `crates/core/src/subtitle/labels.rs`, insert this before the line `#[cfg(test)]`, after the code of Step 12 (one empty line between):

```rust
/// What `set_track` compares to decide that a label is unchanged: the date says when, not what. Spec 15, RP15.
const SUBSTANCE: [&str; 6] = ["kind", "how", "sure", "saw_verdict", "note", "style"];
/// An edit's refusal of a value that has no tracks list.
const NO_TRACKS: &str = "the file has no 'tracks' list, so nothing is changed";

/// Adds or replaces the label of (`label.label`, `label.stream`) in the file's value. One old label of the track with
/// the same kind, how, sure, saw_verdict, note and style is kept as it is, and the value is returned unchanged (not sorted, so the caller
/// sees that there is nothing to write); otherwise every old label of the track goes into the new entry's `history`
/// (each one's own history first) with `replaced` set to the new date, and the tracks are sorted stably by (label,
/// stream). Returns the new value and the problems it still has; Err "not written: <the problems the change adds>"
/// when the change adds a sentence the value did not have, and Err when the value has no tracks list. The slug is not
/// compared (an edit never changes it; `load` compares it). Spec 15, RP15, D16 ("the owner's label for a track, once
/// given, is kept with it").
pub fn set_track(data: Value, label: &SubtitleLabel) -> Result<(Value, Vec<String>), String> {
    let tracks: Vec<Value> = tracks_of(&data)?.clone();
    let before = problems(&data, None);
    let mut entry = serde_json::to_value(label).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let key = Some((label.label.clone(), label.stream));
    let is_old = |t: &Value| t.as_object().and_then(key_of) == key;
    let old: Vec<&Value> = tracks.iter().filter(|t| is_old(*t)).collect();
    if old.len() == 1 && SUBSTANCE.iter().all(|k| old[0].get(*k) == entry.get(*k)) {
        return Ok((data, before));
    }
    if !old.is_empty() {
        let mut history = Vec::new();
        for o in &old {
            if let Some(Value::Array(earlier)) = o.get("history") {
                history.extend(earlier.iter().cloned());
            }
            let mut copy: Map<String, Value> = o
                .as_object()
                .into_iter()
                .flatten()
                .filter(|(k, _)| k.as_str() != "history")
                .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), v.clone()))
                .collect();
            copy.insert("replaced".to_string(), json!(label.date));
            history.push(Value::Object(copy));
        }
        entry["history"] = Value::Array(history);
    }
    let mut kept: Vec<Value> = tracks.iter().filter(|t| !is_old(*t)).cloned().collect();
    kept.push(entry);
    kept.sort_by(|a, b| track_sort_key(a).cmp(&track_sort_key(b)));
    let mut new = data;
    new["tracks"] = Value::Array(kept);
    checked(&before, new)
}

/// Moves every label of (`label`, `stream`) to the file's `removed` list (added at the end of the file when absent),
/// each with `removed` (the date) and `why`, and sorts the tracks left as `set_track` does. Returns the new value and
/// the problems it still has; Err "<label> stream <n> has no label", "unset needs --note: why the label is taken
/// away", "'removed' is not a list, so the label cannot be moved there", "not written: <the new problems>" as `set_track`, or the
/// tracks-list refusal. As `audio::labels::unset_track` does. Spec 15, RP15, D16.
pub fn unset_track(data: Value, label: &str, stream: i64, why: &str, date: &str) -> Result<(Value, Vec<String>), String> {
    let tracks: Vec<Value> = tracks_of(&data)?.clone();
    let key = Some((label.to_string(), stream));
    let is_old = |t: &Value| t.as_object().and_then(key_of) == key;
    let old: Vec<Value> = tracks.iter().filter(|t| is_old(*t)).cloned().collect();
    if old.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!("{label} stream {stream} has no label"));
    }
    if why.is_empty() {
        return Err("unset needs --note: why the label is taken away".to_string());
    }
    let before = problems(&data, None);
    let mut kept: Vec<Value> = tracks.iter().filter(|t| !is_old(*t)).cloned().collect();
    kept.sort_by(|a, b| track_sort_key(a).cmp(&track_sort_key(b)));
    let moved: Vec<Value> = old
        .into_iter()
        .map(|o| {
            let mut m = o.as_object().cloned().unwrap_or_default();
            m.insert("removed".to_string(), json!(date));
            m.insert("why".to_string(), json!(why));
            Value::Object(m)
        })
        .collect();
    let mut new = data;
    new["tracks"] = Value::Array(kept);
    let d = new.as_object_mut().expect("a value with a tracks list is an object");
    match d.get_mut("removed") {
        None => {
            d.insert("removed".to_string(), Value::Array(moved));
        }
        Some(Value::Array(list)) => list.extend(moved),
        Some(_) => return Err("'removed' is not a list, so the label cannot be moved there".to_string()),
    }
    checked(&before, new)
}

/// The value's tracks list, or the refusal of an edit.
fn tracks_of(data: &Value) -> Result<&Vec<Value>, String> {
    data.get("tracks").and_then(Value::as_array).ok_or_else(|| NO_TRACKS.to_string())
}

/// The edited value and its problems, or Err "not written: <the problems `before` did not have, joined by '; '>".
fn checked(before: &[String], new: Value) -> Result<(Value, Vec<String>), String> {
    let after = problems(&new, None);
    let added: Vec<&str> = after.iter().filter(|p| !before.contains(*p)).map(String::as_str).collect();
    if !added.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!("not written: {}", added.join("; ")));
    }
    Ok((new, after))
}
```

The command tests run `lazymkv-dev labels` (`cmd::labels::run`) with a scratch folder as the current directory, so every path is printed as typed (`disc-b/subtitle-labels.json`). `Ctx::for_test`'s clock is 2026-10-13, so a `set` without `--date` is dated `2026-10-13`. No test writes a spec: the subtitle words read none.

Create `crates/dev/tests/labels_subtitles.rs` with exactly this content:

```rust
//! `lazymkv-dev labels --subtitles` (RP15; design spec 15 "Recordings", section 17 row 14, D20, D23) over synthetic
//! recordings in a scratch folder: `set` writes `<slug_dir>/subtitle-labels.json` beside `audio-labels.json`, keeps a
//! label with the same substance as it is, keeps a replaced label in its history, says when a source is only an
//! observation, records a UK-style SDH track with `--style uk` (RP25), and refuses a change that would add a problem; `unset` moves a label to `removed` with why and when;
//! `check` validates every subtitle labels file under a folder; `kinds` prints the vocabulary; the argument errors are
//! argparse's; the audio commands are as before. The subtitle words read no spec (what counts towards row 14 is
//! `retune --subtitles`'), so no test writes one. The last test runs `check` over the evidence clone and skips with
//! its reason without it.

use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use lazymkv_core::subtitle::labels::KINDS;
use lazymkv_core::testsupport::{Scratch, ScratchExt};
use lazymkv_dev::cmd::labels::run;
use lazymkv_dev::evidence::{repo_root, skip, Ctx};
use lazymkv_dev::COMMANDS;
use serde_json::{json, Value};

/// An audio labels file of disc-b, which no subtitle command may touch.
const AUDIO_LABELS: &str = r#"{"format": "lazymkv audio labels v1", "slug": "disc-b", "titles": {}, "tracks": []}"#;

/// disc-b/subtitle-labels.json after `labels --subtitles set disc-b all-tracks 4 sdh --how read --saw-verdict no --date 2026-10-14
/// --note "sound cues in brackets"` on a recording without one: `pyjson::write_labels`' form (indent 2, UTF-8, a
/// final newline).
const FIRST_FILE: &str = concat!(
    "{\n",
    "  \"format\": \"lazymkv subtitle labels v1\",\n",
    "  \"slug\": \"disc-b\",\n",
    "  \"tracks\": [\n",
    "    {\n",
    "      \"label\": \"all-tracks\",\n",
    "      \"stream\": 4,\n",
    "      \"kind\": \"sdh\",\n",
    "      \"how\": \"read\",\n",
    "      \"sure\": true,\n",
    "      \"date\": \"2026-10-14\",\n",
    "      \"saw_verdict\": false,\n",
    "      \"note\": \"sound cues in brackets\",\n",
    "      \"style\": null\n",
    "    }\n",
    "  ]\n",
    "}\n",
);

/// The same label as FIRST_FILE's, written on one line by hand.
const ONE_LINE_FILE: &str = concat!(
    r#"{"format":"lazymkv subtitle labels v1","slug":"disc-b","tracks":[{"label":"all-tracks","stream":4,"kind":"sdh","#,
    r#""how":"read","sure":true,"date":"2026-10-14","saw_verdict":false,"note":"sound cues in brackets","style":null}]}"#,
);

/// Runs `lazymkv-dev labels <args>` with `cwd` as the current directory; (exit code, stdout, stderr).
fn call(cwd: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> (i32, String, String) {
    let args: Vec<String> = args.iter().map(|arg| arg.to_string()).collect();
    let (mut out, mut err) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
    let code = run(&Ctx::for_test(cwd), &args, &mut out, &mut err);
    (code, String::from_utf8(out).unwrap(), String::from_utf8(err).unwrap())
}

/// A scratch folder holding the empty recording folder disc-b; returns the folder and disc-b's subtitle labels path.
fn scratch_with_disc_b(tag: &str) -> (Scratch, PathBuf) {
    let tmp = Scratch::new(tag);
    fs::create_dir_all(tmp.0.join("disc-b")).unwrap();
    let file = tmp.0.join("disc-b").join("subtitle-labels.json");
    (tmp, file)
}

/// A JSON file read back.
fn read_json(path: &Path) -> Value {
    serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(path).unwrap()).unwrap()
}

#[test]
fn the_labels_row_of_commands_names_the_subtitles_option() {
    let row = COMMANDS.iter().find(|(name, _, _)| *name == "labels").expect("labels is registered");
    assert_eq!(row.2, "[--spec FILE] [--subtitles] kinds|check|set|unset|title|auto|fitted ...");
}

#[test]
fn set_writes_a_new_subtitle_labels_file_and_leaves_the_audio_labels_alone() {
    let (tmp, file) = scratch_with_disc_b("labels-subtitles");
    tmp.write("disc-b/audio-labels.json", AUDIO_LABELS);
    let args =
        ["--subtitles", "set", "disc-b", "all-tracks", "4", "sdh", "--how", "read", "--saw-verdict", "no", "--date", "2026-10-14",
        "--note", "sound cues in brackets"];
    assert_eq!(
        call(&tmp.0, &args),
        (0, "labelled all-tracks stream 4: sdh (read, 2026-10-14, saw verdict no, sure yes)\n".to_string(), String::new())
    );
    assert_eq!(fs::read_to_string(&file).unwrap(), FIRST_FILE);
    // --saw-verdict yes, --sure no, the default date (the test clock's 2026-10-13) and no note (null).
    let args =
        ["--subtitles", "set", "disc-b", "all-tracks", "5", "regular", "--how", "watched", "--saw-verdict", "yes", "--sure", "no"];
    assert_eq!(
        call(&tmp.0, &args),
        (0, "labelled all-tracks stream 5: regular (watched, 2026-10-13, saw verdict yes, sure no)\n".to_string(), String::new())
    );
    assert_eq!(
        read_json(&file)["tracks"][1],
        json!({"label": "all-tracks", "stream": 5, "kind": "regular", "how": "watched", "sure": false, "date": "2026-10-13",
               "saw_verdict": true, "note": null, "style": null})
    );
    assert_eq!(fs::read_to_string(tmp.0.join("disc-b/audio-labels.json")).unwrap(), AUDIO_LABELS);
}

#[test]
fn set_with_the_same_substance_writes_nothing() {
    let (tmp, file) = scratch_with_disc_b("labels-subtitles");
    tmp.write("disc-b/subtitle-labels.json", ONE_LINE_FILE);
    let args =
        ["--subtitles", "set", "disc-b", "all-tracks", "4", "sdh", "--how", "read", "--saw-verdict", "no", "--date", "2026-10-20",
        "--note", "sound cues in brackets"];
    assert_eq!(
        call(&tmp.0, &args),
        (0, "unchanged all-tracks stream 4: sdh (read, 2026-10-14, saw verdict no, sure yes)\n".to_string(), String::new())
    );
    // Not rewritten: the hand-written line is still one line.
    assert_eq!(fs::read_to_string(&file).unwrap(), ONE_LINE_FILE);
}

#[test]
fn set_replaces_a_label_and_keeps_the_old_one_in_its_history() {
    let (tmp, file) = scratch_with_disc_b("labels-subtitles");
    tmp.write("disc-b/subtitle-labels.json", ONE_LINE_FILE);
    let args =
        ["--subtitles", "set", "disc-b", "all-tracks", "4", "regular", "--how", "read", "--saw-verdict", "no", "--date", "2026-10-15",
        "--note", "no cues after all"];
    assert_eq!(
        call(&tmp.0, &args),
        (
            0,
            "labelled all-tracks stream 4: regular (read, 2026-10-15, saw verdict no, sure yes); replaces 1 earlier label(s), kept in its history\n"
                .to_string(),
            String::new()
        )
    );
    assert_eq!(
        read_json(&file)["tracks"],
        json!([{
            "label": "all-tracks", "stream": 4, "kind": "regular", "how": "read", "sure": true, "date": "2026-10-15",
            "saw_verdict": false, "note": "no cues after all", "style": null,
            "history": [{"label": "all-tracks", "stream": 4, "kind": "sdh", "how": "read", "sure": true, "date": "2026-10-14", "saw_verdict": false,
                         "note": "sound cues in brackets", "style": null, "replaced": "2026-10-15"}],
        }])
    );
}

#[test]
fn set_records_a_uk_style_sdh_track_with_style_uk() {
    let (tmp, file) = scratch_with_disc_b("labels-subtitles");
    let args = [
        "--subtitles", "set", "disc-b", "all-tracks", "4", "sdh", "--how", "watched", "--saw-verdict", "no", "--date", "2026-10-14",
        "--style", "uk",
    ];
    assert_eq!(
        call(&tmp.0, &args),
        (0, "labelled all-tracks stream 4: sdh (watched, 2026-10-14, saw verdict no, sure yes, style uk)\n".to_string(), String::new())
    );
    assert_eq!(
        read_json(&file)["tracks"][0],
        json!({"label": "all-tracks", "stream": 4, "kind": "sdh", "how": "watched", "sure": true, "date": "2026-10-14",
               "saw_verdict": false, "note": null, "style": "uk"})
    );
    // The same label without --style is a new label (style null); the UK-style one is kept in its history.
    let args =
        ["--subtitles", "set", "disc-b", "all-tracks", "4", "sdh", "--how", "watched", "--saw-verdict", "no", "--date", "2026-10-15"];
    assert_eq!(
        call(&tmp.0, &args),
        (
            0,
            "labelled all-tracks stream 4: sdh (watched, 2026-10-15, saw verdict no, sure yes); replaces 1 earlier label(s), kept in its history\n"
                .to_string(),
            String::new()
        )
    );
    let written = read_json(&file);
    assert_eq!(written["tracks"][0]["style"], json!(null));
    assert_eq!(written["tracks"][0]["history"][0]["style"], json!("uk"));
}

#[test]
fn set_refuses_a_change_that_adds_a_problem_and_writes_nothing() {
    let (tmp, file) = scratch_with_disc_b("labels-subtitles");
    let cases: [(&[&str], &str); 3] = [
        (&["All-Tracks", "4", "sdh", "--date", "2026-10-14"], "track All-Tracks stream 4: label is not a rip label"),
        (&["all-tracks", "4", "sdh", "--date", "2026-13-01"], "track all-tracks stream 4: date '2026-13-01' is not YYYY-MM-DD"),
        (
            &["all-tracks", "-1", "sdh", "--date", "2026-10-14"],
            "track all-tracks stream -1: stream is not ffprobe's stream number (an integer, 0 or more)",
        ),
    ];
    for (words, problem) in cases {
        let mut args = vec!["--subtitles", "set", "disc-b"];
        args.extend_from_slice(words);
        args.extend_from_slice(&["--how", "read", "--saw-verdict", "no"]);
        assert_eq!(
            call(&tmp.0, &args),
            (2, String::new(), format!("disc-b/subtitle-labels.json: not written: {problem}\n")),
            "{words:?}"
        );
        assert!(!file.exists(), "{words:?}");
    }
}

fn check_validates_each_subtitle_labels_file() {
    let tmp = Scratch::new("labels-subtitles");
    tmp.write("corpus/disc-b/subtitle-labels.json", ONE_LINE_FILE);
    let bad = json!({"format": "lazymkv subtitle labels v1", "slug": "disc-x", "tracks": [
        {"label": "all-tracks", "stream": 4, "kind": "sdh", "how": "read", "sure": "yes", "date": "2026-10-14", "saw_verdict": false,
         "note": null, "style": null}]});
    tmp.write("corpus/disc-c/subtitle-labels.json", serde_json::to_string(&bad).unwrap());
    fs::create_dir_all(tmp.0.join("corpus/disc-d")).unwrap();
    tmp.write("corpus/disc-d/audio-labels.json", AUDIO_LABELS);
    let both = concat!(
        "ok corpus/disc-b/subtitle-labels.json (1 tracks)\n",
        "corpus/disc-c/subtitle-labels.json: slug is 'disc-x' but the file is in corpus/owner/disc-c; ",
        "track all-tracks stream 4: sure must be true or false\n",
    );
    assert_eq!(call(&tmp.0, &["--subtitles", "check", "corpus"]), (2, both.to_string(), String::new()));
    assert_eq!(
        call(&tmp.0, &["--subtitles", "check", "corpus/disc-b"]),
        (0, "ok corpus/disc-b/subtitle-labels.json (1 tracks)\n".to_string(), String::new())
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&tmp.0, &["--subtitles", "check", "corpus/disc-d"]),
        (0, "corpus/disc-d: no subtitle-labels.json\n".to_string(), String::new())
    );
    assert_eq!(call(&tmp.0, &["--subtitles", "check", "nope"]), (0, "nope: no subtitle-labels.json\n".to_string(), String::new()));
    // Run inside the recording, the slug is compared with the folder's real name.
    assert_eq!(
        call(&tmp.0.join("corpus/disc-b"), &["--subtitles", "check", "."]),
        (0, "ok subtitle-labels.json (1 tracks)\n".to_string(), String::new())
    );
}

#[test]
fn kinds_prints_the_subtitle_vocabulary_and_the_sources() {
    let tmp = Scratch::new("labels-subtitles");
    let (code, out, err) = call(&tmp.0, &["--subtitles", "kinds"]);
    assert_eq!((code, err.as_str()), (0, ""));
    let lines: Vec<&str> = out.lines().collect();
    assert_eq!(lines.len(), 11, "{out}");
    assert_eq!(lines[0], "regular          keep     plain dialogue subtitles: the words spoken, with no sound cues or speaker labels (R5, D20)");
    assert_eq!(lines[8], "closed-captions  keep     the DVD's closed captions, which MakeMKV converts to text; SDH by type (8.7)");
    for (line, (kind, wanted, meaning)) in lines.iter().zip(KINDS.iter()) {
        assert_eq!(*line, format!("{kind:<16} {wanted:<8} {meaning}"));
    }
    assert!(lines[10].starts_with("how: read = a person read its OCR text (counts, D23); watched = "), "{out}");
    assert!(lines[10].ends_with("; thediscdb = TheDiscDB's track description (an observation: does not count on its own, D23)"), "{out}");
    let (code, out, err) = call(&tmp.0, &["--subtitles", "kinds", "extra"]);
    assert_eq!((code, out.as_str()), (2, ""));
    assert!(err.lines().any(|line| line == "lazymkv-dev labels: error: unrecognized arguments: extra"), "{err}");
}

#[test]
fn help_prints_the_subtitle_synopsis() {
    let tmp = Scratch::new("labels-subtitles");
    let cases = [
        (vec!["--subtitles", "kinds", "--help"], "labels --subtitles kinds"),
        (vec!["--subtitles", "check", "-h"], "labels --subtitles check <path> ..."),
        (
            vec!["--subtitles", "set", "--help"],
            "labels --subtitles set <slug_dir> <label> <stream> <kind> --how HOW --saw-verdict yes|no [--sure yes|no] [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--note TEXT] [--style uk]",
        ),
        (vec!["--subtitles", "unset", "-h"], "labels --subtitles unset <slug_dir> <label> <stream> --note TEXT [--date YYYY-MM-DD]"),
        (vec!["--help"], "labels [--spec FILE] [--subtitles] kinds|check|set|unset|title|auto|fitted ..."),
    ];
    for (args, usage) in cases {
        assert_eq!(call(&tmp.0, &args), (0, format!("usage: lazymkv-dev {usage}\n"), String::new()), "{args:?}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn argument_errors_are_reported_as_argparse_reports_them() {
    let (tmp, file) = scratch_with_disc_b("labels-subtitles");
    let kinds = "'regular', 'sdh', 'forced', 'commentary', 'trivia', 'lyrics', 'translation', 'dub-transcript', 'closed-captions', 'other'";
    let only = "(with --subtitles, choose from 'kinds', 'check', 'set', 'unset')";
    let cases: Vec<(Vec<&str>, String)> = vec![

            vec!["--subtitles", "set", "disc-b", "all-tracks", "4", "dialogue", "--how", "read", "--saw-verdict", "no"],
            format!("lazymkv-dev labels set: error: argument kind: invalid choice: 'dialogue' (choose from {kinds})"),
        ),
        (
            vec!["--subtitles", "set", "disc-b", "all-tracks", "4", "sdh", "--how", "listened", "--saw-verdict", "no"],
            "lazymkv-dev labels set: error: argument --how: invalid choice: 'listened' (choose from 'read', 'watched', 'packaging', 'menu', 'flag', 'player', 'thediscdb')"
                .to_string(),
        ),
        (
            vec!["--subtitles", "set", "disc-b", "all-tracks", "x", "sdh", "--how", "read", "--saw-verdict", "no"],
            "lazymkv-dev labels set: error: argument stream: invalid int value: 'x'".to_string(),
        ),
        (
            vec!["--subtitles", "set", "disc-b", "all-tracks", "4", "sdh", "--how", "read", "--saw-verdict", "no", "--sure", "maybe"],
            "lazymkv-dev labels set: error: argument --sure: 'maybe': say yes or no".to_string(),
        ),
        (
            vec!["--subtitles", "set", "disc-b", "all-tracks", "4", "sdh", "--how", "read", "--saw-verdict", "no", "--style", "british"],
            "lazymkv-dev labels set: error: argument --style: invalid choice: 'british' (choose from 'uk')".to_string(),
        ),
        (
            vec!["--subtitles", "set", "disc-b", "all-tracks"],
            "lazymkv-dev labels set: error: the following arguments are required: stream, kind, --how, --saw-verdict".to_string(),
        ),
        (
            vec!["--subtitles", "set", "disc-b", "all-tracks", "4", "sdh", "--how", "read", "--saw-verdict", "perhaps"],
            "lazymkv-dev labels set: error: argument --saw-verdict: 'perhaps': say yes or no".to_string(),
        ),
        (
            vec!["--subtitles", "set", "disc-b", "all-tracks", "4", "sdh", "--how", "read", "--saw-verdict", "no", "--film-audible", "yes"],
            "lazymkv-dev labels: error: unrecognized arguments: --film-audible".to_string(),
        ),
        (
            vec!["--subtitles", "unset", "disc-b", "all-tracks", "4"],
            "lazymkv-dev labels unset: error: the following arguments are required: --note".to_string(),
        ),
        (
            vec!["--subtitles", "check"],
            "lazymkv-dev labels check: error: the following arguments are required: paths".to_string(),
        ),
        (
            vec!["--subtitles", "title", "disc-b", "t0", "--title-kind", "feature"],
            format!("lazymkv-dev labels: error: argument cmd: 'title' does not take --subtitles {only}"),
        ),
        (vec!["--subtitles", "auto", "disc-b"], format!("lazymkv-dev labels: error: argument cmd: 'auto' does not take --subtitles {only}")),
        (
            vec!["--subtitles", "fitted", ".", "disc-b", "--rule", "x"],
            format!("lazymkv-dev labels: error: argument cmd: 'fitted' does not take --subtitles {only}"),
        ),
        (
            vec!["--subtitles", "frob"],
            "lazymkv-dev labels: error: argument cmd: invalid choice: 'frob' (choose from 'kinds', 'check', 'set', 'unset', 'title', 'auto', 'fitted')"
                .to_string(),
        ),
        (vec!["--subtitles"], "lazymkv-dev labels: error: the following arguments are required: cmd".to_string()),
        (
            vec!["--s", "spec.md", "kinds"],
            "lazymkv-dev labels: error: ambiguous option: --s could match --spec, --subtitles".to_string(),
        ),
        (
            vec!["--subtitles=yes", "kinds"],
            "lazymkv-dev labels: error: argument --subtitles: ignored explicit argument 'yes'".to_string(),
        ),
    ];
    for (args, line) in cases {
        let (code, out, err) = call(&tmp.0, &args);
        assert_eq!((code, out.as_str()), (2, ""), "{args:?}");
        assert!(err.starts_with("usage: lazymkv-dev labels"), "{args:?}: {err}");
        assert!(err.lines().any(|l| l == line), "{args:?}: {err}");
    }
    assert!(!file.exists());
}

#[test]
fn the_option_takes_argparses_prefixes_reads_no_spec_and_leaves_the_audio_words_as_they_were() {
    let tmp = Scratch::new("labels-subtitles");
    let (code, out, err) = call(&tmp.0, &["--su", "kinds"]);
    assert_eq!((code, out.lines().count(), err.as_str()), (0, 11, ""));
    // nospec.md does not exist: the subtitle words never read it.
    let (code, out, err) = call(&tmp.0, &["--sp", "nospec.md", "--subtitles", "check", "nope"]);
    assert_eq!((code, out.as_str(), err.as_str()), (0, "nope: no subtitle-labels.json\n", ""));
    // Without --subtitles: the audio vocabulary, and the audio words still read the spec.
    let (code, out, err) = call(&tmp.0, &["kinds"]);
    assert_eq!((code, out.lines().count(), err.as_str()), (0, 19, ""));
    assert!(out.starts_with("main                 programme  keep     "), "{out}");
    let (code, out, err) = call(&tmp.0, &["--spec", "nospec.md", "check", "."]);
    assert_eq!((code, out.as_str()), (2, ""));
    assert!(err.starts_with("cannot read the fitting disc from nospec.md: "), "{err}");
}

#[test]
fn the_subtitle_labels_of_the_evidence_clone_validate() {
    let Some(repo) = repo_root(Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))) else {
        skip("no repository root (a Cargo.toml with [workspace]) above crates/dev");
        return;
    };
    if !repo.join("corpus").join("owner").is_dir() {
        skip("the evidence repository is not cloned at corpus/owner");
        return;
    }
    let (code, out, err) = call(&repo, &["--subtitles", "check", "corpus/owner"]);
    assert_eq!((code, err.as_str()), (0, ""), "{out}");
    assert!(
        out == "corpus/owner: no subtitle-labels.json\n" || out.lines().all(|line| line.starts_with("ok corpus/owner/")),
        "{out}"
    );
}
```

Edit 6. Replace the whole of `split_main`, from its doc comment to its closing brace:

```rust
/// The main parser's part of the command line: `--spec FILE` (also `--spec=FILE`, or a prefix of it of at least
/// three characters, as argparse's abbreviations) and `-h`/`--help` before the command word, then the command word.
/// Ok(None) asks for the help; Err is argparse's message.
fn split_main(args: &[String]) -> Result<Option<(Option<String>, String, Vec<String>)>, String> {
    let mut spec = None;
    let mut i = 0;
    while let Some(word) = args.get(i) {
        if !word.starts_with('-') || word == "-" {
            break;
        }
        let (name, inline) = match word.split_once('=') {
            Some((name, value)) => (name, Some(value.to_string())),
            None => (word.as_str(), None),
        };
        if word == "-h" || (name.len() >= 3 && "--help".starts_with(name) && inline.is_none()) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        if name.len() < 3 || !"--spec".starts_with(name) {
            return Err(format!("unrecognized arguments: {word}"));
        }
        spec = Some(match inline {
            Some(value) => value,
            None => {
                i += 1;
                args.get(i).cloned().ok_or_else(|| "argument --spec: expected one argument".to_string())?
            }
        });
        i += 1;
    }
    let cmd = args.get(i).cloned().ok_or_else(|| "the following arguments are required: cmd".to_string())?;
    if !SUBCOMMANDS.contains(&cmd.as_str()) {
        return Err(format!("argument cmd: invalid choice: {} (choose from {})", py_repr_str(&cmd), choices(&SUBCOMMANDS)));
    }
    Ok(Some((spec, cmd, args[i + 1..].to_vec())))
}
```

with:

```rust
/// The main parser's options and the command word, with what follows it.
struct Main {
    spec: Option<String>,
    subtitles: bool,
    cmd: String,
    rest: Vec<String>,
}

/// The main parser's part of the command line: `--spec FILE` (also `--spec=FILE`) and the switch `--subtitles`
/// (RP15), each also as a prefix of at least three characters that names only it (argparse's abbreviations: `--su`,
/// `--sp`; `--s` is ambiguous), and `-h`/`--help`, before the command word; then the command word, which with
/// `--subtitles` must be one of SUBTITLE_SUBCOMMANDS. Ok(None) asks for the help; Err is argparse's message.
fn split_main(args: &[String]) -> Result<Option<Main>, String> {
    let mut spec = None;
    let mut subtitles = false;
    let mut i = 0;
    while let Some(word) = args.get(i) {
        if !word.starts_with('-') || word == "-" {
            break;
        }
        let (name, inline) = match word.split_once('=') {
            Some((name, value)) => (name, Some(value.to_string())),
            None => (word.as_str(), None),
        };
        if word == "-h" || (name.len() >= 3 && "--help".starts_with(name) && inline.is_none()) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let matches: Vec<&str> =
            if name.len() >= 3 { MAIN_OPTIONS.iter().copied().filter(|option| option.starts_with(name)).collect() } else { Vec::new() };
        match matches.as_slice() {
            ["--spec"] => {
                spec = Some(match inline {
                    Some(value) => value,
                    None => {
                        i += 1;
                        args.get(i).cloned().ok_or_else(|| "argument --spec: expected one argument".to_string())?
                    }
                });
            }
            ["--subtitles"] => {
                if let Some(value) = inline {
                    return Err(format!("argument --subtitles: ignored explicit argument {}", py_repr_str(&value)));
                }
                subtitles = true;
            }
            [] => return Err(format!("unrecognized arguments: {word}")),
            _ => return Err(format!("ambiguous option: {name} could match {}", matches.join(", "))),
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    let cmd = args.get(i).cloned().ok_or_else(|| "the following arguments are required: cmd".to_string())?;
    if !SUBCOMMANDS.contains(&cmd.as_str()) {
        return Err(format!("argument cmd: invalid choice: {} (choose from {})", py_repr_str(&cmd), choices(&SUBCOMMANDS)));
    }
    if subtitles && !SUBTITLE_SUBCOMMANDS.contains(&cmd.as_str()) {
        return Err(format!(
            "argument cmd: {} does not take --subtitles (with --subtitles, choose from {})",
            py_repr_str(&cmd),
            choices(&SUBTITLE_SUBCOMMANDS)
        ));
    }
    Ok(Some(Main { spec, subtitles, cmd, rest: args[i + 1..].to_vec() }))
}
```

```rust
/// `check`'s loop over its paths, for the audio labels (`execute`) and the subtitle labels (`execute_subtitles`): each
/// path is read through a DiskTree when it is a folder, else through an empty tree (so `lines` finds no file), and
/// `lines`' lines for it are printed. Ok(2) when a file is bad, else Ok(0); Err(the OSError text) when a folder cannot
/// be opened.
fn check_paths(
    ctx: &Ctx,
    paths: &[String],
    out: &mut dyn Write,
    lines: fn(&dyn Tree, &PathKey) -> (Vec<String>, usize),
) -> Result<i32, String> {
    let mut bad = 0;
    for path in paths {
        let shown = pathlib_str(path);
        let dir = ctx.abs(path);
        let (printed, found) = if dir.is_dir() {
            let tree = DiskTree::open(&dir, &shown).map_err(|e| os_error_text(&e, &shown))?;
            lines(&tree, &PathKey::root())
        } else {
            lines(&MemTree::new(&shown, ""), &PathKey::root())
        };
        for line in printed {
            let _ = writeln!(out, "{line}");
        }
        bad += found;
    }
    Ok(if bad > 0 { 2 } else { 0 })
}

/// `labels --subtitles <cmd> <arguments>` (RP15): the owner's subtitle labels through `core::subtitle::labels`. No spec is
/// read. Exit 0, or 2 for an argument error, a recording folder that does not exist, a file that is not JSON or does
/// not validate (`check`), and a change that would add a problem.
fn run_subtitles(ctx: &Ctx, cmd: &str, rest: &[String], out: &mut dyn Write, err: &mut dyn Write) -> i32 {
    if rest.iter().any(|word| word == "-h" || word == "--help") {
        let _ = writeln!(out, "usage: lazymkv-dev {}", subtitle_usage(cmd));
        return 0;
    }
    let parsed = match parse_subtitles(cmd, rest, &ctx.today()) {
        Ok(parsed) => parsed,
        Err(Usage { sub: true, message }) => return usage_error(err, &format!("labels {cmd}"), subtitle_usage(cmd), &message),
        Err(Usage { sub: false, message }) => return usage_error(err, "labels", USAGE, &message),
    };
    match execute_subtitles(ctx, parsed, out) {
        Ok(code) => code,
        Err(line) => {
            let _ = writeln!(err, "{line}");
            2
        }
    }
}

/// A `--subtitles` command line, parsed and converted as argparse converts it.
enum SubtitleParsed {
    Kinds,
    Check { paths: Vec<String> },
    Set { slug_dir: String, label: SubtitleLabel },
    Unset { slug_dir: String, label: String, stream: i64, note: String, date: String },
}

/// The command word's arguments under `--subtitles`; `unset` takes the audio `unset`'s arguments.
fn parse_subtitles(cmd: &str, rest: &[String], today: &str) -> Result<SubtitleParsed, Usage> {
    match cmd {
        "kinds" => {
            extra(rest)?;
            Ok(SubtitleParsed::Kinds)
        }
        "check" => {
            let paths = Args::new(rest, &[]).positionals().map_err(top)?;
            required(&missing_words(&paths, &["paths"]))?;
            Ok(SubtitleParsed::Check { paths })
        }
        "set" => parse_subtitle_set(rest, today),
        _ => match parse_unset(rest, today)? {
            Parsed::Unset { slug_dir, label, stream, note, date } => Ok(SubtitleParsed::Unset { slug_dir, label, stream, note, date }),
            _ => unreachable!("parse_unset gives only Parsed::Unset"),
        },
    }
}

/// `set <slug_dir> <label> <stream> <kind> --how HOW --saw-verdict yes|no [--sure yes|no] [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--note
/// TEXT] [--style uk]`: `--saw-verdict` is required, as the audio `set`'s (section 17 row 14 (a)); `--sure` defaults to
/// yes, `--date` to today, `--note` and `--style` to none (null in the file; `--style uk` marks a UK-style SDH track,
/// RP25). Errors in the order of the audio `set`:
/// type and choice errors (positionals, then options), the missing required arguments, unrecognized arguments.
fn parse_subtitle_set(rest: &[String], today: &str) -> Result<SubtitleParsed, Usage> {
    let mut a = Args::new(rest, &["--how", "--saw-verdict", "--sure", "--date", "--note", "--style"]);
    let how = a.flag("--how").map_err(sub)?;
    let saw = a.flag("--saw-verdict").map_err(sub)?;
    let sure = a.flag("--sure").map_err(sub)?;
    let date = a.flag("--date").map_err(sub)?;
    let note = a.flag("--note").map_err(sub)?;
    let style = a.flag("--style").map_err(sub)?;
    let words = a.positionals().map_err(top)?;
    let kinds: Vec<&str> = SubtitleKind::ALL.iter().map(|kind| kind.as_str()).collect();
    let hows: Vec<&str> = subtitle_labels::HOW.iter().map(|(name, _)| *name).collect();
    let stream = words.get(2).map(|w| int_arg("stream", w)).transpose()?;
    let kind = words.get(3).map(|w| choose("kind", w, &kinds)).transpose()?;
    let how = how.map(|h| choose("--how", &h, &hows)).transpose()?;
    let saw = saw.map(|s| yes("--saw-verdict", &s, false)).transpose()?;
    let sure = sure.map(|s| yes("--sure", &s, false)).transpose()?;
    let style = style.map(|s| choose("--style", &s, &["uk"])).transpose()?;
    let mut missing = missing_words(&words, &["slug_dir", "label", "stream", "kind"]);
    if how.is_none() {
        missing.push("--how");
    }
    if saw.is_none() {
        missing.push("--saw-verdict");
    }
    required(&missing)?;
    extra(words.get(4..).unwrap_or(&[]))?;
    let kind = SubtitleKind::from_str(&kind.unwrap_or_default()).map_err(sub)?;
    Ok(SubtitleParsed::Set {
        slug_dir: words[0].clone(),
        label: SubtitleLabel {
            label: words[1].clone(),
            stream: stream.unwrap_or_default(),
            kind,
            how: how.unwrap_or_default(),
            sure: sure.map_or(true, |s| s == Some(true)),
            date: date.unwrap_or_else(|| today.to_string()),
            saw_verdict: saw == Some(Some(true)),
            note,
            style,
        },
    })
}

/// Runs one `--subtitles` command word. Ok(exit code) after printing its lines; Err(the line for stderr), exit 2.
fn execute_subtitles(ctx: &Ctx, parsed: SubtitleParsed, out: &mut dyn Write) -> Result<i32, String> {
    match parsed {
        SubtitleParsed::Kinds => {
            for line in subtitle_kinds_lines() {
                let _ = writeln!(out, "{line}");
            }
            Ok(0)
        }
        SubtitleParsed::Check { paths } => check_paths(ctx, &paths, out, subtitle_check_lines),
        SubtitleParsed::Set { slug_dir, label } => {
            let SubtitleFile { path, shown, data } = open_subtitles(ctx, &slug_dir)?;
            let (written, left) = subtitle_labels::set_track(data.clone(), &label).map_err(|e| format!("{shown}: {e}"))?;
            let changed = written != data;
            if changed {
                write_labels(&path, &written).map_err(|e| format!("{shown}: {e}"))?;
            }
            let _ = writeln!(out, "{}", subtitle_set_line(&written, &label, changed));
            print_left(out, &left);
            Ok(0)
        }
        SubtitleParsed::Unset { slug_dir, label, stream, note, date } => {
            let SubtitleFile { path, shown, data } = open_subtitles(ctx, &slug_dir)?;
            let (written, left) =
                subtitle_labels::unset_track(data, &label, stream, &note, &date).map_err(|e| format!("{shown}: {e}"))?;
            write_labels(&path, &written).map_err(|e| format!("{shown}: {e}"))?;
            let _ = writeln!(out, "unset {label} stream {stream}: the label is kept under 'removed'");
            print_left(out, &left);
            Ok(0)
        }
    }
}

/// A recording's subtitle labels file opened for a change: its path on disk, how it is printed, and its value (a new
/// file when absent: the format line, the folder's resolved name as slug, no tracks).
struct SubtitleFile {
    path: PathBuf,
    shown: String,
    data: Value,
}

/// Opens `<slug_dir>/subtitle-labels.json` for a change. A file that does not validate can still be changed (the
/// edit may not add a problem), but it must be JSON. Err "<slug_dir>: no such recording folder", "<shown>: not valid
/// JSON (<the reason>); restore it from git (git checkout -- <shown>)", or the OSError text.
fn open_subtitles(ctx: &Ctx, slug_dir: &str) -> Result<SubtitleFile, String> {
    let dir = ctx.abs(slug_dir);
    if !dir.is_dir() {
        return Err(format!("{slug_dir}: no such recording folder"));
    }
    let folder = pathlib_str(slug_dir);
    let shown = pathlib_under(&folder, subtitle_labels::FILE_NAME);
    let path = dir.join(subtitle_labels::FILE_NAME);
    if !path.exists() {
        let tree = DiskTree::open(&dir, &folder).map_err(|e| os_error_text(&e, &folder))?;
        let data = json!({"format": subtitle_labels::FORMAT, "slug": tree.resolved_name(&PathKey::root()), "tracks": []});
        return Ok(SubtitleFile { path, shown, data });
    }
    let bytes = std::fs::read(&path).map_err(|e| os_error_text(&e, &shown))?;
    let parsed = decode_text(&bytes, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Strict)
        .and_then(|text| serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&text).map_err(|e| e.to_string()));
    match parsed {
        Ok(data) => Ok(SubtitleFile { path, shown, data }),
        Err(why) => Err(format!("{shown}: not valid JSON ({why}); restore it from git (git checkout -- {shown})")),
    }
}

/// The line `--subtitles set` prints, from the entry written or kept: `labelled|unchanged <label> stream <n>: <kind>
/// (<how>, <date>, saw verdict yes|no, sure yes|no[, style <style>])` (the style only when it is not null, RP25), then for
/// an observation (D23) why it does not count, then after a replacement how
/// many earlier labels its history keeps.
fn subtitle_set_line(written: &Value, label: &SubtitleLabel, changed: bool) -> String {
    let entry = written["tracks"]
        .as_array()
        .into_iter()
        .flatten()
        .find(|t| t["label"].as_str() == Some(label.label.as_str()) && t["stream"].as_i64() == Some(label.stream))
        .cloned()
        .unwrap_or(Value::Null);
    let how = py_str(&entry["how"]);
    let style = entry["style"].as_str().map_or(String::new(), |style| format!(", style {style}"));
    let mut line = format!(
        "{} {} stream {}: {} ({how}, {}, saw verdict {}, sure {}{style})",
        if changed { "labelled" } else { "unchanged" },
        label.label,
        label.stream,
        py_str(&entry["kind"]),
        py_str(&entry["date"]),
        if py_truthy(&entry["saw_verdict"]) { "yes" } else { "no" },
        if py_truthy(&entry["sure"]) { "yes" } else { "no" },
    );
    if subtitle_labels::OBSERVATION_HOW.contains(&how.as_str()) {
        line.push_str(&format!(" ('{how}' is an observation, not a check of the track's text (row 14, D23))"));
    }
    let replaced = entry.get("history").and_then(Value::as_array).map_or(0, Vec::len);
    if changed && replaced > 0 {
        line.push_str(&format!("; replaces {replaced} earlier label(s), kept in its history"));
    }
    line
}

/// `labels --subtitles kinds`' lines: each kind, what the owner wants and its meaning (padded to 16 and 8
/// characters), then the sources.
fn subtitle_kinds_lines() -> Vec<String> {
    let mut lines: Vec<String> =
        subtitle_labels::KINDS.iter().map(|(kind, wanted, meaning)| format!("{kind:<16} {wanted:<8} {meaning}")).collect();
    let how: Vec<String> = subtitle_labels::HOW.iter().map(|(name, meaning)| format!("{name} = {meaning}")).collect();
    lines.push(format!("how: {}", how.join("; ")));
    lines
}

/// `labels --subtitles check <root>`'s lines for one root and the number of bad files: root/subtitle-labels.json when
/// it exists, else every */subtitle-labels.json (never one under golden/), each "ok <file> (<n> tracks)" or `load`'s
/// refusal; "<root>: no subtitle-labels.json" when there is none. The audio labels' `labels_check_lines`, with the
/// subtitle file's name and count (RP15).
fn subtitle_check_lines(tree: &dyn Tree, root: &PathKey) -> (Vec<String>, usize) {
    labels_check_lines(tree, root, subtitle_labels::FILE_NAME, &|tree, path| {
        subtitle_labels::load(tree, path).map(|labels| format!("{} tracks", labels.len()))
    })
}

/// The synopsis of one `--subtitles` command word (after "usage: lazymkv-dev ").
fn subtitle_usage(cmd: &str) -> &'static str {
    match cmd {
        "kinds" => "labels --subtitles kinds",
        "check" => "labels --subtitles check <path> ...",
        "set" => {
            "labels --subtitles set <slug_dir> <label> <stream> <kind> --how HOW --saw-verdict yes|no [--sure yes|no] [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--note TEXT] [--style uk]"
        }
        _ => "labels --subtitles unset <slug_dir> <label> <stream> --note TEXT [--date YYYY-MM-DD]",
    }
}
```

```rust
    pub dialogue_pick: Option<DialoguePick>,

}

/// Spec 8.7 in full, in order: `set_aside`; a counted stream in the file that TheDiscDB describes as commentary (not as
/// dialogue or SDH) is set aside and dropped (OutsideDialogueGroup; R6, D15); events from `facts.events`; full =
/// `is_full` against the largest English track's events (a stream flagged forced, 4096 without 2048, is never full: its
/// flag makes it a forced source); `alignment_groups` over the full tracks with the three bands (a Between pair raises
/// subtitle_ambiguous); `dialogue_group` with the parents of forced-only streams that have events and
/// `tracks::audio::descriptions` (None, two largest groups of equal size included, raises subtitle_ambiguous, and the
/// first group stands in for the regular and SDH roles); regular and SDH (up to two: more events is SDH, a description
/// saying SDH overrides; the closed-caption stream is SDH when the group has none; more than two gives
/// subtitle_ambiguous, and a track described SDH is one of the two kept); full tracks outside a picked group dropped
/// (OutsideDialogueGroup; with no pick, or with a Between band against a track of the picked group, they are kept as
/// regular under the review, never dropped unconfirmed or by position); forced (first: a forced-only stream with events
/// whose parent is the regular track, then the SDH track's; then a DVD stream flagged forced; then a separately
/// authored track that is not full with fewer than FORCED_MAX_EVENTS events); other not-full tracks with
/// FORCED_MAX_EVENTS or more events dropped with partial_subtitle_dropped, those with no events dropped NoEvents;
/// `text_disagreements` (subtitle_ambiguous and one subtitle_text_disagrees note per stream); the confidence case;
/// remembered then review overrides applied last (decided_by "remembered" or "reviewed"; an override naming a stream
/// that is not an English or no-language subtitle stream is ignored), with confidence lookup::REMEMBERED_CONFIDENCE
/// (1.00) and subtitle_ambiguous cleared when every English and no-language subtitle stream of the title still in the
/// file (not in facts.removed) has an override (other-language streams are dropped by 8.7's first sentence; the case
/// unchanged). A title with one English stream and no events keeps it as Regular "English" (row 14 (b) fallback), case
/// OneFull; when that stream is flagged forced (4096 without 2048) it is kept as Forced by its flag, case
/// FlagsOrDescriptions. Def: T10. Use: T13, T16, T18.
pub fn decide_subtitles(title: &Title, facts: &SubtitleFacts<'_>, settings: &Settings) -> SubtitleDecision;
```

Beside these, `Costly` gets the closed-set members the plan's conventions give every closed set (`pub const ALL: [Costly; 6]`, `pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str`, `impl FromStr`) and `pub fn meaning(self) -> &'static str` for the report; they are not used outside this task. And, not a cross-task item: `retune`'s synopsis in `COMMANDS` gains `[--subtitles] [--text DIR]`, as the Shared interfaces' last line says.

Where this task settles what the spec and the interfaces leave open (each choice is pinned by a test below):

1. **What row 14 (a) judges.** Row 14 (a) asks whether "the text rule of 8.7" gives a costly verdict, so the judged outcome of a labelled track is the text rule's decision for its stream (`text::decide` through `subs_run`): `regular`, `sdh` and `forced` place the track in that role, `drop` drops it, `keep` keeps it unplaced (it is always reviewed, so it counts as kept as regular with a review), each with the decision's own review. For a stream the text rule sets aside (the DVD closed captions, which it never reads), the judged outcome is 8.7's, since the text rule hands that stream back to 8.7. The report also shows what 8.7 decides before experiment 14 answers (`decide_subtitles`, with the text adding reviews only where the app reads it, spec 8.7 "Text" and 6.4 step 10: a title whose file holds two or more English or no-language subtitle streams; a title with one keeps it as "English" without the text, row 14 (b)'s fallback): its role and whether the title raised `subtitle_ambiguous`. `costly` judges an outcome's `role` and `review` only. `Outcome.role` is the role of the rule being judged, as the interfaces' doc of `Outcome` says.
2. **A label's `stream`** is the rip file's track id (the ffprobe stream number, as in `audio-labels.json`), mapped onto the scan stream through `verify::stream_of_track` of the verified rip. A label on a file track the rip does not have, or on a track that is not a subtitle stream, cannot be judged and says so.
3. **What counts towards row 14 (a)'s totals** (D23): a label that the harness judged, whose `how` is in `COUNTING_HOW` (`read`, `watched`), that the owner is `sure` of, that was given before the owner saw the verdict (`saw_verdict` false: ruling RP25, row 14's "checked before the verdict"), and that is not on a fitting disc (row 14's two backticked slugs). A label from an observation (`how` in `OBSERVATION_HOW`: the packaging, the menu, a flag, the player or TheDiscDB, the five of row 14, `flag` added by RP25) never counts. Every other label is still judged and reported, and a costly verdict on it still fails the run, as row 14 says of the fitting discs.
4. **"1 feature film and 1 TV episode"**: a title with a counted regular and a counted SDH track is a feature film when the recording's `tmdb.json` has a `title`, a TV episode when it has a `name` (TMDb's two spellings), else neither. "From at least 2 discs" counts distinct recordings.
5. **"1 DVD with English VobSub subtitles"** counts distinct DVD recordings (`Disc::is_dvd`) with a counted label on an English VobSub stream. **"1 UK-style SDH track"** counts the counted labels of kind `sdh` whose `style` is `"uk"` (ruling RP25: speakers by colour, sounds without brackets), and the report prints `UK-style SDH          <n> of <row 14's count> counted SDH tracks labelled style uk (only if the owner has a UK disc)`. A `style` on another kind, or on a label that does not count (an observation, a label given after the verdict, one the owner is not sure of, one on a fitting disc), is shown on its track line (`style uk` after the source) and never counted. The requirement never appears among the missing kinds, since row 14 asks for it only if the owner has a UK disc, which the harness cannot know (like row 13's audio description in the audio harness).
6. **Exit codes** (spec 15: non-zero for a costly verdict, "and, separately, when some evidence could not be read"): 2 when a subtitle labels file does not validate (the run stops, as the audio harness stops on a bad labels file); 1 on any costly verdict; 3 when there is no label at all or any labelled English or no-language track could not be judged (its rip, scan or OCR text could not be read); 0 otherwise. Spec 15's "some evidence" is followed, as the interfaces' doc of `harness` says.
7. **A label on a stream in another language** is listed in its own section and neither judged nor counted, and never changes the exit code: row 14 covers English and no-language tracks, and the owner may label the others (row 14's result names Pan's Labyrinth's Spanish track).
8. **The OCR text** is read from `<text>/<slug>/<label>/subs-ocr/sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl` (the goldens' layout, the one `tuning-fetch.ps1 -Text` copies and `decide` reads first), with `subs-ocr/sub-<n>.frames.json` of the recording. Without it the title's labels are not judged; `subs_run`'s own refusals (an English bitmap stream without OCR text) are the reason given.
9. **Settings.** `retune --subtitles` runs with `Settings::default()` (RP15 names no settings flag). The harness reads `sub_clear_max_bytes` itself and hands the settings to `decide_subtitles` (`subs_tolerance_ms`, `subs_same_min`, `subs_diff_max`) and `text_rule()`; each of the four is exercised at its default and at one other value through the harness.
10. **TheDiscDB** is not read by the harness (`SubtitleFacts.discdb` is None): no recorded answer describes a subtitle track (every subtitle track of the clone's two answers has `description: null`), so 8.7's "a TheDiscDB description saying SDH" never applies to the evidence (listed under concerns).
11. **The report's order**: labelled tracks by recording slug, rip label, then file track; the count block lists RP15's kinds in `SubtitleKind::ALL` order, then row 14's derived totals.

```rust
| 15 | later | | |\n";
```

```rust
use regex::Regex;

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ row 14 (a)'s list

/// A number in row 14: ASCII digits, or a word from one to ten (the spec spells small numbers either way).
const NUM: &str = "([0-9]+|one|two|three|four|five|six|seven|eight|nine|ten)";
/// The number words NUM allows. Not audio::labels' private WORDS and number (row 13's reader): that pair is the
/// Python's port (`py_int`, i64, Python's ValueError text), while row 14 is read from the spec alone (RP20) into u32
/// counts with this reader's own sentence.
const WORDS: [(&str, u32); 10] = [
    ("one", 1),
    ("two", 2),
    ("three", 3),
    ("four", 4),
    ("five", 5),
    ("six", 6),
    ("seven", 7),
    ("eight", 8),
    ("nine", 9),
    ("ten", 10),
];
/// Row 14 (a)'s phrases, in the row's order, `{num}` standing for NUM; a plural `s` is optional wherever the row may
/// grow past 1.
const PAIR_TITLES: &str = r"at least {num} titles? from at least {num} discs? \(at least {num} feature films? and {num} TV episodes?\) that each have both a regular and an SDH English track";
const SDH_REGULAR: &str = "at least {num} SDH and {num} regular English tracks in all";
const FORCED_WITH_EVENTS: &str = "at least {num} real forced English tracks? with events";
const COMMENTARY_TRACK: &str = "at least {num} commentary subtitle tracks?";
const DVD_VOBSUB: &str = "at least {num} DVDs? with English VobSub subtitles";
const UK_SDH: &str = "at least {num} UK-style SDH tracks?";
/// The sentence naming the discs every threshold was fitted on, and a slug in backticks inside it.
const FITTED: &str = "Every threshold was fitted on (.{0,200}?), so none of their tracks counts";
const QUOTED_SLUG: &str = "`([a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)`";

/// Row 14 (a)'s required counts read from the spec text (the first line starting "| 14 |"): titles with both regular
/// and SDH (3, from 2 discs, 1 feature, 1 TV), SDH (6), regular (6), forced with events (1), commentary (1), DVD VobSub
/// (1), UK SDH (1, only if the owner has one), the two fitting discs. Spec 17 row 14 (a), RP15. Def: T18. Use: T18.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Row14 {
    pub pair_titles: u32,
    pub pair_discs: u32,
    pub pair_features: u32,
    pub pair_tv: u32,
    pub sdh: u32,
    pub regular: u32,
    pub forced: u32,
    pub commentary: u32,
    pub dvd_vobsub: u32,
    pub uk_sdh: u32,
    pub fitting_discs: Vec<String>,
}

/// Reads row 14 (the first line of `spec_text` starting "| 14 |") with the phrases above. Err names the phrase it no
/// longer finds, so a reworded row is noticed instead of being counted against old numbers, as row 13's reader does.
/// Spec 17 row 14 (a), RP15. Def: T18. Use: T18.
pub fn exp14_requirements(spec_text: &str) -> Result<Row14, String> {
    let row = spec_text
        .lines()
        .find(|line| line.starts_with("| 14 |"))
        .ok_or_else(|| "spec section 17 has no row starting '| 14 |'".to_string())?;
    let pairs = numbers(row, PAIR_TITLES)?;
    let totals = numbers(row, SDH_REGULAR)?;
    let forced = numbers(row, FORCED_WITH_EVENTS)?;
    let commentary = numbers(row, COMMENTARY_TRACK)?;
    let dvd_vobsub = numbers(row, DVD_VOBSUB)?;
    let uk_sdh = numbers(row, UK_SDH)?;
    let unnamed = || "spec section 17 row 14 no longer names the discs the thresholds were fitted on".to_string();
    let sentence = Regex::new(FITTED)
        .expect("the fitted pattern is valid")
        .captures(row)
        .map(|caps| caps[1].to_string())
        .ok_or_else(unnamed)?;
    let fitting_discs: Vec<String> = Regex::new(QUOTED_SLUG)
        .expect("the slug pattern is valid")
        .captures_iter(&sentence)
        .map(|caps| caps[1].to_string())
        .collect();
    if fitting_discs.is_empty() {
        return Err(unnamed());
    }
    Ok(Row14 {
        pair_titles: pairs[0],
        pair_discs: pairs[1],
        pair_features: pairs[2],
        pair_tv: pairs[3],
        sdh: totals[0],
        regular: totals[1],
        forced: forced[0],
        commentary: commentary[0],
        dvd_vobsub: dvd_vobsub[0],
        uk_sdh: uk_sdh[0],
        fitting_discs,
    })
}

/// The numbers `template` (with `{num}` for NUM) finds in `row`, one per group, in order; Err names the phrase.
fn numbers(row: &str, template: &str) -> Result<Vec<u32>, String> {
    let pattern = template.replace("{num}", NUM);
    let caps = Regex::new(&pattern).expect("row 14's patterns are valid").captures(row).ok_or_else(|| {
        format!("spec section 17 row 14 no longer contains the phrase /{pattern}/; update core::subtitle::labels")
    })?;
    caps.iter().skip(1).map(|group| number(group.map_or("", |found| found.as_str()))).collect()
}

/// A count written in digits or as a word from one to ten. Kept apart from audio::labels' private `number`, which
/// gives an i64 through `py_int` with Python's ValueError text; this one gives a u32 with row 14's own sentence.
fn number(text: &str) -> Result<u32, String> {
    if let Ok(count) = text.parse::<u32>() {
        return Ok(count);
    }
    WORDS
        .iter()
        .find(|(word, _)| *word == text)
        .map(|&(_, count)| count)
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("spec section 17 row 14: {text} is not a count"))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;
```

```rust
        assert_eq!("dropped".parse::<Costly>(), Err("not a costly verdict: dropped".to_string()));
        let meanings: Vec<&str> = Costly::ALL.iter().map(|verdict| verdict.meaning()).collect();
        assert_eq!(
            meanings,
            [
                "a dialogue track dropped, with or without a review",
                "an SDH track placed as regular without review",
                "a regular track placed as SDH without review",
                "a track that is not forced flagged forced without review",
                "a forced track placed as regular or SDH without review",
                "a commentary, trivia or lyrics track kept without review",
            ]
        );
    }
}
```

```rust
// ------------------------------------------------------------------ the costly verdicts

/// Row 14's costly verdicts, in the row's order. Spec 17 row 14 (a). Def: T18. Use: T18.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Costly {
    DialogueDropped,
    SdhAsRegular,
    RegularAsSdh,
    ForcedWrongly,
    ForcedAsDialogue,
    UnwantedKept,
}

impl Costly {
    /// Every costly verdict, in row 14's order. Spec 17 row 14 (a).
    pub const ALL: [Costly; 6] = [
        Costly::DialogueDropped,
        Costly::SdhAsRegular,
        Costly::RegularAsSdh,
        Costly::ForcedWrongly,
        Costly::ForcedAsDialogue,
        Costly::UnwantedKept,
    ];

    /// The verdict's snake_case spelling, its serde name. Spec 17 row 14 (a).
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Costly::DialogueDropped => "dialogue_dropped",
            Costly::SdhAsRegular => "sdh_as_regular",
            Costly::RegularAsSdh => "regular_as_sdh",
            Costly::ForcedWrongly => "forced_wrongly",
            Costly::ForcedAsDialogue => "forced_as_dialogue",
            Costly::UnwantedKept => "unwanted_kept",
        }
    }

    /// What the verdict is, in row 14's words, for the report's COSTLY lines. Spec 17 row 14 (a).
    pub fn meaning(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Costly::DialogueDropped => "a dialogue track dropped, with or without a review",
            Costly::SdhAsRegular => "an SDH track placed as regular without review",
            Costly::RegularAsSdh => "a regular track placed as SDH without review",
            Costly::ForcedWrongly => "a track that is not forced flagged forced without review",
            Costly::ForcedAsDialogue => "a forced track placed as regular or SDH without review",
            Costly::UnwantedKept => "a commentary, trivia or lyrics track kept without review",
        }
    }
}

impl std::str::FromStr for Costly {
    type Err = String;

    /// Exactly the `as_str` spellings. Spec 17 row 14 (a).
    fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<Costly, String> {
        Costly::ALL
            .into_iter()
            .find(|verdict| verdict.as_str() == text)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("not a costly verdict: {text}"))
    }
}

/// What the rules gave a labelled track: the role the judged rule places it in (None = dropped) and whether a review
/// was raised. The harness builds two per track: the text rule's (what row 14 (a) judges; for a
/// stream the text rule sets aside, 8.7's) and 8.7's as the app decides before experiment 14 answers (shown beside it).
/// Spec 17 row 14 (a), 8.7 "Text". Def: T18. Use: T18.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Outcome {
    pub role: Option<SubtitleRole>,
    pub review: bool,
}

/// Row 14's dialogue kinds: dropping one is costly, with or without a review.
const DIALOGUE_KINDS: [SubtitleKind; 5] = [
    SubtitleKind::Regular,
    SubtitleKind::Sdh,
    SubtitleKind::Translation,
    SubtitleKind::DubTranscript,
    SubtitleKind::ClosedCaptions,
];
/// Row 14's unwanted kinds: keeping one without review is costly.
const UNWANTED_KINDS: [SubtitleKind; 3] = [SubtitleKind::Commentary, SubtitleKind::Trivia, SubtitleKind::Lyrics];

/// The costly verdict, if any, of one labelled track's outcome, checked in row 14's order (the first that applies): a
/// dialogue kind (regular, sdh, translation, dub-transcript, closed-captions) dropped; sdh as Regular or regular as Sdh
/// without review; Forced without review on a non-forced kind, or a forced kind as Regular or Sdh without review;
/// commentary, trivia or lyrics kept without review. Reads `role` and `review` only. Spec 17 row 14 (a). Def: T18.
/// Use: T18.
pub fn costly(kind: SubtitleKind, outcome: &Outcome) -> Option<Costly> {
    let quiet = !outcome.review;
    match outcome.role {
        None if DIALOGUE_KINDS.contains(&kind) => Some(Costly::DialogueDropped),
        Some(SubtitleRole::Regular) if quiet && kind == SubtitleKind::Sdh => Some(Costly::SdhAsRegular),
        Some(SubtitleRole::Sdh) if quiet && kind == SubtitleKind::Regular => Some(Costly::RegularAsSdh),
        Some(SubtitleRole::Forced) if quiet && kind != SubtitleKind::Forced => Some(Costly::ForcedWrongly),
        Some(SubtitleRole::Regular | SubtitleRole::Sdh) if quiet && kind == SubtitleKind::Forced => {
            Some(Costly::ForcedAsDialogue)
        }
        Some(_) if quiet && UNWANTED_KINDS.contains(&kind) => Some(Costly::UnwantedKept),
        _ => None,
    }
}
```
