- [ ] **Step 14: Write the failing tests of `retune --subtitles` and of the harness over the evidence clone**

The clone tests use the rips of Task 12's `crates/dev/tests/verify.rs`: pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd's `eng-only`, short-circuit-2-1988-dvd's `all-tracks-2` and the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray's `e16-stereo`, `rehearsal` and `t3-all-tracks`. The labels given are spec section 17 row 14's result column: the three SDH tracks of the Office, Pan's Labyrinth's English track (a translation of a Spanish film) and Short Circuit 2's English VobSub track, with its closed-caption stream. A labelled track is named by what the public spec says of it, never by a number read from the clone (RP21): the first English entry of the rip's `subs/index.json` with a given mkvmerge codec name (`HDMV PGS`, `VobSub`, or `SubRip/SRT` for the closed captions MakeMKV converts to text, spec 6.2 step 7). Its file track, its scan stream and its event count are derived when the test runs, from the copied files the harness reads (`found`: the rip verified with `verify_rip` over `selected_streams`, `subs_streams`, and `subtitle_events` with spec 14's `sub_clear_max_bytes`), and each expected line is built from them. The clone holds no `subtitle-labels.json` yet, so the test builds them in memory over copies of the files the harness reads.

No stream of these titles carries a flag but the forced-only streams' 6144 (each Office title's and Pan's Labyrinth's forced-only stream is removed by MSG:4047), and the two TheDiscDB answers describe no subtitle track. So 8.7 (Task 10) keeps each title's one full English track as regular (`OneFull`) and the DVD's closed captions as SDH, with no review. With the OCR text (`LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT`), the text rule's decisions are the goldens' (`<slug>/golden/<label>/subs.json`, written from that OCR text): `sdh` without review on the three Office tracks, `regular` without review on Pan's Labyrinth's and Short Circuit 2's English tracks, the closed captions set aside; the judged outcomes give no costly verdict, as the row's result column says. The 8.7 column shows no review on the Office tracks although the text says sdh: each Office title's file and Pan's Labyrinth's hold one English subtitle stream, where the app does not read the text (6.4 step 10, 8.7 "Text", row 14 (b)'s fallback), so `decide_subtitles` gets no text there; Short Circuit 2's file holds two (the VobSub track and the closed captions), and there the text agrees with 8.7. The test checks each OCR file's SHA-1 against the golden's `text_sha1` and skips when it differs.

Create `crates/dev/tests/retune_subtitles.rs` with exactly this content:

```rust
//! `lazymkv-dev retune --subtitles` (RP15; spec 15 "Rules against the stored evidence"; section 17 row 14; 8.7 "Text";
//! phase 1 Task 18): row 14 of the design spec read by `exp14_requirements`; the command over a synthetic evidence
//! folder and OCR text written to a scratch folder (always run); and the subtitle harness over the evidence clone (each
//! prints "skipped: <reason>" and passes when an input is absent): the clone as it is, the clone's rips with the labels
//! of row 14's result column and no OCR text, and the same with the OCR text the goldens were written from. Inputs:
//! LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE, else corpus/owner under the repository root; LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT, laid out as
//! <DIR>/<slug>/<label>/subs-ocr/sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl.

use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use serde_json::{json, Value};

use lazymkv_core::disc::disc;
use lazymkv_core::recording::files::{rip_label, MkvmergeIdent, SubsIndexEntry};
use lazymkv_core::recording::{read_json, read_text, Encoding, Errors, MemTree, PathKey, Tree};
use lazymkv_core::robot::parse;
use lazymkv_core::settings::Settings;
use lazymkv_core::subtitle::labels::{exp14_requirements, harness, Row14, SubtitleHarness, FORMAT};
use lazymkv_core::testsupport::{scan_text, sha1_hex, write, Scratch};
use lazymkv_core::verify::{selected_streams, subs_streams, subtitle_events, verify_rip};
use lazymkv_dev::cmd::retune::run;
use lazymkv_dev::evidence::{skip, Ctx, DiskTree, EVIDENCE_SHOWN};

/// The design spec, relative to this crate.
const DESIGN_SPEC: &str = "../../docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-04-lazymkv-design.md";

/// retune's usage line, as every argument error prints it.
const USAGE_LINE: &str = "usage: lazymkv-dev retune [--evidence DIR] [--set NAME=VALUE] [--snapshot FILE] [--compare FILE] [--spec FILE] [--allow-unmeasured] [--subtitles] [--text DIR]";

/// Made-up English lines for the OCR text (no line of any real subtitle), as in core's harness tests: alone in its
/// title, this dialogue is placed as regular by the text rule without a review.
const LINES: [&str; 6] = [
    "The cat and the dog went to the shop.",
    "You know that is not what I said.",
    "We have to go back to the house now.",
    "It was the best day of the year.",
    "He said that you would be there.",
    "What do you want me to do with this.",
];

/// MakeMKV's log of the synthetic rip: one made-up message, no MSG:4047 removal.
const RIP: &str = "MSG:5011,0,0,\"made-up line\",\"made-up line\"\n";

/// The synthetic disc's title and streams: 2 chapters, 10 minutes, a playlist; AVC video and one English PGS stream.
const BD_TITLE: &[(u32, &str)] = &[(8, "2"), (9, "0:10:00"), (16, "00001.mpls")];
const AVC: &[(u32, &str)] = &[(1, "Video"), (5, "V_MPEG4/ISO/AVC"), (6, "Mpeg4"), (7, "Mpeg4 AVC High@L4.1")];
const ENG_PGS: &[(u32, &str)] = &[(1, "Subtitles"), (3, "eng"), (5, "S_HDMV/PGS"), (6, "PGS"), (7, "HDMV PGS Subtitles")];

/// One labelled track of the clone's rips: the first English subs/index.json entry with this mkvmerge codec name, the
/// kind row 14's result column gives it, and the words the report gives it: 8.7's role, and the text rule's role once
/// the goldens' OCR text is read.
struct Labelled {
    codec: &'static str,
    kind: &'static str,
    rule: &'static str,
    text: &'static str,
}

/// mkvmerge's codec name of the closed captions MakeMKV converts to text (spec 6.2 step 7): a text stream, never read
/// by OCR.
const CAPTIONS_CODEC: &str = "SubRip/SRT";

/// The Office's SDH track: 8.7 keeps it as regular (one full English track), the text rule reads it as sdh.
const OFFICE_SDH: &[Labelled] = &[Labelled { codec: "HDMV PGS", kind: "sdh", rule: "regular", text: "sdh" }];

/// The clone's rips labelled here, with row 14's result column: (slug, rip label, labelled tracks). Each track's file
/// track, scan stream and event count are derived when the test runs (`found`), never written here (RP21).
const OVERLAY: [(&str, &str, &[Labelled]); 5] = [
    (
        "pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd",
        "eng-only",
        &[Labelled { codec: "HDMV PGS", kind: "translation", rule: "regular", text: "regular" }],
    ),
    (
        "short-circuit-2-1988-dvd",
        "all-tracks-2",
        &[
            Labelled { codec: CAPTIONS_CODEC, kind: "closed-captions", rule: "sdh", text: "set aside" },
            Labelled { codec: "VobSub", kind: "regular", rule: "regular", text: "regular" },
        ],
    ),
    ("the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray", "e16-stereo", OFFICE_SDH),
    ("the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray", "rehearsal", OFFICE_SDH),
    ("the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray", "t3-all-tracks", OFFICE_SDH),
];

/// The report of the synthetic evidence below with its OCR text (core's runs::the_report_counts_each_kind... gives the
/// same layout for three recordings).
const REPORT: [&str; 35] = [
    "subtitle labels: corpus/owner: 1 recordings with subtitle-labels.json, 1 labelled tracks: 1 judged, 0 not judged, 0 in another language",
    "rule: 8.7 with sub_clear_max_bytes 64, subs_tolerance_ms 300, subs_same_min 0.7, subs_diff_max 0.3; the text rule (EXP-14-design.md section 3) with the same four and its other thresholds as in the code, all provisional",
    "",
    "Tracks (the owner's label; 8.7 as the app decides before experiment 14 answers; the text rule as row 14 (a) judges it):",
    "  disc-a/eng-only stream 1 (scan stream 1, 40 events): labelled sdh (read); 8.7 regular; text regular; COSTLY sdh_as_regular",
    "",
    "Experiment 14 (spec section 17 row 14 (a); tracks that count: judged here, labelled from text read or watched before the verdict, the owner sure, never on the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray or pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd; the packaging, the menu, a flag, the player and TheDiscDB are observations and do not count on their own, D23):",
    "  regular               0 of 6",
    "  sdh                   1 of 6",
    "  forced                0, with events 0 of 1",
    "  commentary            0 of 1",
    "  trivia                0 (every one the owner has; checked by hand)",
    "  lyrics                0 (every one the owner has; checked by hand)",
    "  translation           0 (every second translation the owner has; checked by hand)",
    "  dub-transcript        0 (every one the owner has; checked by hand)",
    "  closed-captions       0 (with its DVD's VobSub tracks)",
    "  other                 0",
    "  regular and SDH       0 of 3 titles, from 0 of 2 discs; feature films 0 of 1, TV episodes 0 of 1",
    "  DVD VobSub            0 of 1 DVDs with a counted English VobSub track",
    "  UK-style SDH          0 of 1 counted SDH tracks labelled style uk (only if the owner has a UK disc)",
    "  placed, no review     1 of 1 judged tracks (row 14 (a) asks for at least half)",
    "  costly verdicts       1",
    "  as it stands: no: 1 costly verdict(s)",
    "  not counted: none",
    "",
    "Costly verdicts (row 14 (a): the text rule's verdict, or 8.7's for a stream the text rule sets aside):",
    "  COSTLY disc-a/eng-only stream 1: labelled sdh, an SDH track placed as regular without review",
    "",
    "Labels that cannot be judged:",
    "  none",
    "",
    "Labels in another language (row 14 judges English and no-language tracks only):",
    "  none",
    "",
    "RESULT FAILED: 1 costly verdict(s): disc-a/eng-only stream 1 (sdh_as_regular)",
];

/// The report as the command prints it: every line of REPORT ending in a newline.
fn printed_report() -> String {
    REPORT.iter().map(|line| format!("{line}\n")).collect()
}

/// The design spec's path.
fn spec_path() -> PathBuf {
    Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join(DESIGN_SPEC)
}

/// Writes `<root>/corpus/disc-a`, a film with one English PGS stream (scan stream 1, file track 1) of 40 events labelled
/// sdh from its read text before the verdict, with no style (RP25), and its OCR text under `<root>/text/disc-a/eng-only/subs-ocr/`.
fn write_disc_a(root: &Path) {
    let rec = root.join("corpus/disc-a");
    write(&rec.join("scan.txt"), scan_text(&[(1, "Blu-ray disc")], &[(0, BD_TITLE, &[(0, AVC), (1, ENG_PGS)])]));
    write(&rec.join("tmdb.json"), json!({"title": "Made Up Film", "original_language": "en"}).to_string());
    let labels = json!({"format": FORMAT, "slug": "disc-a", "tracks": [
        {"label": "eng-only", "stream": 1, "kind": "sdh", "how": "read", "sure": true, "date": "2026-10-16",
         "saw_verdict": false, "note": null, "style": null}
    ]});
    write(&rec.join("subtitle-labels.json"), labels.to_string());
    let label = rec.join("eng-only");
    write(&label.join("rip-summary.json"), json!({"ok": true, "title": 0, "profile": "C:\\made-up\\eng-only.mmcp.xml"}).to_string());
    let ident = json!({
        "tracks": [
            {"id": 0, "type": "video", "codec": "AVC/H.264/MPEG-4p10", "properties": {}},
            {"id": 1, "type": "subtitles", "codec": "HDMV PGS", "properties": {"language": "eng"}}
        ],
        "chapters": [{"num_entries": 2}],
        "container": {"properties": {"duration": 600_000_000_000_i64}}
    });
    write(&label.join("mkvmerge.json"), ident.to_string());
    write(&label.join("rip.txt"), RIP);
    let index = json!([{"n": 0, "track_id": 1, "language": "eng", "codec": "HDMV PGS", "track_name": null,
                        "forced": false, "default": false}]);
    write(&label.join("subs/index.json"), index.to_string());
    let mut packets = Vec::new();
    let mut ocr = String::new();
    for k in 0..40_usize {
        let t = 10.0 + 3.0 * k as f64;
        packets.push(json!({"pts_time": format!("{t:.6}"), "duration_time": "2.000000", "size": "3000"}));
        packets.push(json!({"pts_time": format!("{:.6}", t + 2.0), "duration_time": "N/A", "size": "30"}));
        ocr.push_str(&json!({"frame": k, "t": t, "pts": t, "lines": [LINES[k % 6]]}).to_string());
        ocr.push('\n');
    }
    write(&label.join("subs/sub-0.packets.json"), json!({"packets": packets}).to_string());
    write(&root.join("text/disc-a/eng-only/subs-ocr/sub-0.ocr.jsonl"), ocr);
}

/// `retune` with cwd `root` and the environment `env`: (exit code, stdout, stderr).
fn call(root: &Path, args: &[&str], env: &[(&str, String)]) -> (i32, String, String) {
    let mut ctx = Ctx::for_test(root);
    for (name, value) in env {
        ctx.env.insert(name.to_string(), value.clone());
    }
    let args: Vec<String> = args.iter().map(|arg| arg.to_string()).collect();
    let (mut out, mut err): (Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
    let code = run(&ctx, &args, &mut out, &mut err);
    (code, String::from_utf8(out).unwrap(), String::from_utf8(err).unwrap())
}

/// A scratch folder with disc-a written, and its corpus, text and spec paths as the command takes them.
fn scratch(tag: &str) -> (Scratch, String, String, String) {
    let tmp = Scratch::new(tag);
    write_disc_a(&tmp.0);
    let corpus = tmp.0.join("corpus").display().to_string();
    let text = tmp.0.join("text").display().to_string();
    (tmp, corpus, text, spec_path().display().to_string())
}

/// The evidence clone: LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE, else corpus/owner under the repository root; None, with the skip line
/// written, when it is absent.
fn evidence() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let dir = match std::env::var("LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE") {
        Ok(dir) if !dir.is_empty() => PathBuf::from(dir),
        _ => Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../corpus/owner"),
    };
    if !dir.is_dir() {
        skip(&format!("no evidence clone at {}", dir.display()));
        return None;
    }
    Some(dir)
}

/// Row 14 of the design spec.
fn spec_row14() -> Row14 {
    exp14_requirements(&fs::read_to_string(spec_path()).expect("the design spec is in the repository")).expect("row 14 reads")
}

/// Copies `<root>/<rel>` into `tree` at `rel`; false when it cannot be read.
fn copy(tree: &mut MemTree, root: &Path, rel: &str) -> bool {
    match fs::read(root.join(rel)) {
        Ok(bytes) => {
            tree.insert_file(rel, bytes);
            true
        }
        Err(_) => false,
    }
}

/// Copies every `sub-*<suffix>` file of `<root>/<folder>`, in name order.
fn copy_all(tree: &mut MemTree, root: &Path, folder: &str, suffix: &str) {
    let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(root.join(folder)) else { return };
    let mut names: Vec<String> = entries
        .filter_map(|entry| entry.ok())
        .map(|entry| entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned())
        .filter(|name| name.starts_with("sub-") && name.ends_with(suffix))
        .collect();
    names.sort();
    for name in names {
        copy(tree, root, &format!("{folder}/{name}"));
    }
}

/// The labelled track `labelled` names in a rip's subs/index.json: the first English entry with its codec name.
fn english<'i>(index: &'i [SubsIndexEntry], labelled: &Labelled, at: &str) -> &'i SubsIndexEntry {
    index
        .iter()
        .find(|entry| entry.language.as_deref() == Some("eng") && entry.codec.as_deref() == Some(labelled.codec))
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{at}: no English {} stream in subs/index.json", labelled.codec))
}

/// The subs/index.json of `<slug>/<label>` in `tree`.
fn index_of(tree: &MemTree, slug: &str, label: &str) -> Vec<SubsIndexEntry> {
    read_json(tree, &PathKey::new(&format!("{slug}/{label}/subs/index.json"))).expect("subs/index.json reads")
}

/// The clone's OVERLAY rips in memory, shown as corpus/owner: for each recording scan.txt and tmdb.json, for each rip
/// label the files the harness reads (rip-summary.json, mkvmerge.json, rip.txt, subs/index.json, the packets and the
/// OCR frame counts), and a subtitle-labels.json with OVERLAY's labels on the file tracks their subs/index.json entries
/// name, each read and sure before the verdict, with no style (RP25). None, with the skip line written, when a file is
/// absent.
fn overlay(root: &Path) -> Option<MemTree> {
    let mut tree = MemTree::new(EVIDENCE_SHOWN, "owner");
    for (slug, label, _) in OVERLAY {
        let needed = [
            format!("{slug}/scan.txt"),
            format!("{slug}/{label}/rip-summary.json"),
            format!("{slug}/{label}/mkvmerge.json"),
            format!("{slug}/{label}/rip.txt"),
            format!("{slug}/{label}/subs/index.json"),
        ];
        for rel in &needed {
            if !copy(&mut tree, root, rel) {
                skip(&format!("no {} (the evidence clone lacks this recording's file)", root.join(rel).display()));
                return None;
            }
        }
        copy(&mut tree, root, &format!("{slug}/tmdb.json"));
        copy_all(&mut tree, root, &format!("{slug}/{label}/subs"), ".packets.json");
        copy_all(&mut tree, root, &format!("{slug}/{label}/subs-ocr"), ".frames.json");
    }
    let mut labels: Vec<(&str, Vec<Value>)> = Vec::new();
    for (slug, label, tracks) in OVERLAY {
        let index = index_of(&tree, slug, label);
        let entries: Vec<Value> = tracks
            .iter()
            .map(|labelled| {
                let at = format!("{slug}/{label}");
                let track = english(&index, labelled, &at).track_id.unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{at}: no track_id"));
                json!({"label": label, "stream": track, "kind": labelled.kind, "how": "read", "sure": true,
                       "date": "2026-10-16", "saw_verdict": false, "note": null, "style": null})
            })
            .collect();
        match labels.iter().position(|(known, _)| *known == slug) {
            Some(at) => labels[at].1.extend(entries),
            None => labels.push((slug, entries)),
        }
    }
    for (slug, tracks) in labels {
        let file = json!({"format": FORMAT, "slug": slug, "tracks": tracks});
        tree.insert_file(&format!("{slug}/subtitle-labels.json"), file.to_string());
    }
    Some(tree)
}

/// One OVERLAY track as the harness reports it, with what `found` derived for it.
struct Found {
    slug: &'static str,
    label: &'static str,
    labelled: &'static Labelled,
    /// subs/index.json's `n`, the file track (its `track_id`), the scan stream and the event count.
    n: i64,
    track: i64,
    stream: u32,
    events: usize,
}

impl Found {
    /// "<slug>/<rip label> stream <file track>", the report's key.
    fn key(&self) -> String {
        format!("{}/{} stream {}", self.slug, self.label, self.track)
    }

    /// The Tracks section's line of this track, with `tail` after its label.
    fn line(&self, tail: &str) -> String {
        format!(
            "  {} (scan stream {}, {} events): labelled {} (read); {tail}",
            self.key(),
            self.stream,
            self.events,
            self.labelled.kind
        )
    }
}

/// Every OVERLAY track in the report's order (slug, rip label, file track), each with its file track, scan stream and
/// event count derived from the copied files the harness reads: the rip verified with `verify_rip` over
/// `selected_streams` (with its rip.txt), subs/index.json's `n` mapped through `subs_streams`, and the events of
/// `subtitle_events` with spec 14's `sub_clear_max_bytes`. None of these values is copied from the clone into this file
/// (RP21).
fn found(tree: &MemTree) -> Vec<Found> {
    let mut all = Vec::new();
    for (slug, label, tracks) in OVERLAY {
        let at = format!("{slug}/{label}");
        let slug_dir = PathKey::new(slug);
        let rip = rip_label(tree, &slug_dir, label).expect("the rip label reads");
        let log = read_text(tree, &slug_dir.join("scan.txt"), Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Replace).expect("scan.txt reads");
        let scan = parse(&log);
        let typed = disc(&scan).expect("the scan gives a typed disc");
        let number = u32::try_from(rip.title).expect("the summary names a title");
        let title = typed.title(number).expect("the scan lists the rip's title");
        let selection = selected_streams(&scan, number, rip.selection).expect("the selection reads");
        let folder = slug_dir.join(label);
        let ident: MkvmergeIdent = read_json(tree, &folder.join("mkvmerge.json")).expect("mkvmerge.json reads");
        let rip_log = read_text(tree, &folder.join("rip.txt"), Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Replace).expect("rip.txt reads");
        let report = verify_rip(title, &ident, &selection, Some(&rip_log), typed.is_dvd);
        assert!(report.ok, "{at}: the rip does not verify: {:?}", report.mismatches);
        let index = index_of(tree, slug, label);
        let streams = subs_streams(&index, &report);
        let events = subtitle_events(tree, &folder.join("subs"), &report, Settings::default().sub_clear_max_bytes)
            .expect("the packets read");
        for labelled in tracks {
            let entry = english(&index, labelled, &at);
            let stream = *streams.get(&entry.n).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{at}: n {} maps to no scan stream", entry.n));
            all.push(Found {
                slug,
                label,
                labelled,
                n: entry.n,
                track: entry.track_id.unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{at}: n {} has no track_id", entry.n)),
                stream,
                events: events.get(&stream).map_or(0, Vec::len),
            });
        }
    }
    all.sort_by(|a, b| (a.slug, a.label, a.track).cmp(&(b.slug, b.label, b.track)));
    all
}

/// LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT when it holds the OCR text of every labelled English bitmap stream of `tree`'s OVERLAY rips (the
/// closed captions are a text stream, never read by OCR) with the SHA-1 its golden subs.json names; None, with the skip
/// line written, otherwise.
fn golden_text(root: &Path, tree: &MemTree) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let Some(dir) = std::env::var("LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT").ok().filter(|dir| !dir.is_empty()).map(PathBuf::from) else {
        skip("no OCR text (LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT is not set)");
        return None;
    };
    for track in found(tree).iter().filter(|track| track.labelled.codec != CAPTIONS_CODEC) {
        let name = format!("sub-{}.ocr.jsonl", track.n);
        let path = dir.join(track.slug).join(track.label).join("subs-ocr").join(&name);
        let Ok(bytes) = fs::read(&path) else {
            skip(&format!("no OCR text at {}", path.display()));
            return None;
        };
        let golden_path = root.join(track.slug).join("golden").join(track.label).join("subs.json");
        let golden: Option<Value> = fs::read_to_string(&golden_path).ok().and_then(|text| serde_json::from_str(&text).ok());
        let Some(golden) = golden else {
            skip(&format!("no golden {}", golden_path.display()));
            return None;
        };
        if golden["text_sha1"][name.as_str()].as_str() != Some(sha1_hex(&bytes).as_str()) {
            skip(&format!("the OCR text {} is not the one the goldens were written from", path.display()));
            return None;
        }
    }
    Some(dir)
}

/// The lines of the section whose header starts with `header`, up to the next empty line.
fn section<'h>(h: &'h SubtitleHarness, header: &str) -> Vec<&'h str> {
    let start = h
        .lines
        .iter()
        .position(|line| line.starts_with(header))
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no section {header} in {:#?}", h.lines));
    h.lines[start + 1..].iter().take_while(|line| !line.is_empty()).map(String::as_str).collect()
}

/// The one line starting with `start`.
fn line<'h>(h: &'h SubtitleHarness, start: &str) -> &'h str {
    h.lines
        .iter()
        .find(|line| line.starts_with(start))
        .map(String::as_str)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no line {start} in {:#?}", h.lines))
}

#[test]
fn retune_subtitles_prints_the_report_and_exits_1_on_a_costly_verdict() {
    let (tmp, corpus, text, spec) = scratch("retune-subs-report");
    let args = ["--subtitles", "--evidence", corpus.as_str(), "--spec", spec.as_str(), "--text", text.as_str()];
    assert_eq!(call(&tmp.0, &args, &[]), (1, printed_report(), String::new()));
}

#[test]
fn without_ocr_text_retune_subtitles_exits_3_and_says_how_to_give_it() {
    let (tmp, corpus, _, spec) = scratch("retune-subs-no-text");
    let (code, out, err) = call(&tmp.0, &["--subtitles", "--evidence", corpus.as_str(), "--spec", spec.as_str()], &[]);
    assert_eq!((code, err.as_str()), (3, ""));
    let lines: Vec<&str> = out.lines().collect();
    assert!(lines.contains(&"  disc-a/eng-only stream 1: no OCR text (give --text DIR or LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT)"), "{out}");
    assert!(
        lines.contains(
            &"  disc-a/eng-only stream 1 (scan stream 1, 40 events): labelled sdh (read); 8.7 regular; text not read; not judged"
        ),
        "{out}"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        lines.last().copied(),
        Some("RESULT FAILED: not everything was judged: 1 labelled track(s) (see Labels that cannot be judged)")
    );
}

#[test]
fn the_ocr_text_may_come_from_lazymkv_ocr_text_and_must_exist() {
    let (tmp, corpus, text, spec) = scratch("retune-subs-env");
    let args = ["--subtitles", "--evidence", corpus.as_str(), "--spec", spec.as_str()];
    assert_eq!(call(&tmp.0, &args, &[("LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT", text)]), (1, printed_report(), String::new()));
    let nope = tmp.0.join("nope").display().to_string();
    let args = ["--subtitles", "--evidence", corpus.as_str(), "--spec", spec.as_str(), "--text", nope.as_str()];
    assert_eq!(
        call(&tmp.0, &args, &[]),
        (2, String::new(), format!("the OCR text folder {nope} does not exist (give --text DIR or LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT)\n"))
    );
}

#[test]
fn subtitles_takes_no_audio_flag_and_text_needs_subtitles() {
    let (tmp, corpus, text, spec) = scratch("retune-subs-args");
    let refused = format!(
        "{USAGE_LINE}\nlazymkv-dev retune: error: argument --subtitles: not allowed with --set, --snapshot, --compare or --allow-unmeasured\n"
    );
    let audio_flags: [&[&str]; 4] =
        [&["--set", "DC_MAX=0.2"], &["--snapshot", "trial.json"], &["--compare", "old.json"], &["--allow-unmeasured"]];
    for extra in audio_flags {
        let mut args = vec!["--subtitles", "--evidence", corpus.as_str(), "--spec", spec.as_str()];
        args.extend_from_slice(extra);
        assert_eq!(call(&tmp.0, &args, &[]), (2, String::new(), refused.clone()), "{extra:?}");
    }
    let args = ["--evidence", corpus.as_str(), "--spec", spec.as_str(), "--text", text.as_str()];
    assert_eq!(
        call(&tmp.0, &args, &[]),
        (2, String::new(), format!("{USAGE_LINE}\nlazymkv-dev retune: error: argument --text: only with --subtitles\n"))
    );
}

#[test]
fn the_clone_without_subtitle_labels_has_nothing_to_judge() {
    let Some(root) = evidence() else { return };
    let mut labelled: Vec<String> = fs::read_dir(&root)
        .unwrap()
        .filter_map(|entry| entry.ok())
        .filter(|entry| entry.path().join("subtitle-labels.json").is_file())
        .map(|entry| entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned())
        .collect();
    labelled.sort();
    if !labelled.is_empty() {
        skip(&format!(
            "not covered: the clone has subtitle labels now ({}); give them a test in crates/dev/tests/retune_subtitles.rs",
            labelled.join(", ")
        ));
        return;
    }
    let tree = DiskTree::open(&root, EVIDENCE_SHOWN).unwrap();
    let h = harness(&tree, None, &spec_row14(), &Settings::default());
    assert_eq!(
        h.lines[0],
        "subtitle labels: corpus/owner: 0 recordings with subtitle-labels.json, 0 labelled tracks: 0 judged, 0 not judged, 0 in another language"
    );
    assert_eq!(h.lines.last().map(String::as_str), Some("RESULT FAILED: no subtitle label to judge (lazymkv-dev labels --subtitles set)"));
    assert_eq!((h.labelled, h.costly.len(), h.exit_code), (0, 0, 3));
}

#[test]
fn the_clones_rips_with_row_14s_labels_are_decided_by_8_7_and_wait_for_their_ocr_text() {
    let Some(root) = evidence() else { return };
    let Some(tree) = overlay(&root) else { return };
    let tracks = found(&tree);
    let h = harness(&tree, None, &spec_row14(), &Settings::default());
    let expected: Vec<String> =
        tracks.iter().map(|track| track.line(&format!("8.7 {}; text not read; not judged", track.labelled.rule))).collect();
    assert_eq!(section(&h, "Tracks ("), expected);
    let no_text = "no OCR text (give --text DIR or LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT)";
    let unjudged: Vec<String> = tracks.iter().map(|track| format!("  {}: {no_text}", track.key())).collect();
    assert_eq!(section(&h, "Labels that cannot be judged:"), unjudged);
    assert_eq!(line(&h, "  not counted: "), "  not counted: pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd 1, short-circuit-2-1988-dvd 2, the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray 3");
    assert_eq!(
        h.lines.last().map(String::as_str),
        Some("RESULT FAILED: not everything was judged: 6 labelled track(s) (see Labels that cannot be judged)")
    );
    assert_eq!((h.labelled, h.costly.len(), h.exit_code), (6, 0, 3));
}

#[test]
fn with_the_goldens_ocr_text_the_clones_labelled_tracks_get_no_costly_verdict() {
    let Some(root) = evidence() else { return };
    let Some(tree) = overlay(&root) else { return };
    let Some(text_dir) = golden_text(&root, &tree) else { return };
    let text = DiskTree::open(&text_dir, &text_dir.display().to_string()).unwrap();
    let h = harness(&tree, Some(&text as &dyn Tree), &spec_row14(), &Settings::default());
    let expected: Vec<String> = found(&tree)
        .iter()
        .map(|track| track.line(&format!("8.7 {}; text {}; placed", track.labelled.rule, track.labelled.text)))
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(section(&h, "Tracks ("), expected);
    assert_eq!(line(&h, "  regular "), "  regular               1 of 6");
    assert_eq!(line(&h, "  closed-captions "), "  closed-captions       1 (with its DVD's VobSub tracks)");
    assert_eq!(line(&h, "  DVD VobSub "), "  DVD VobSub            1 of 1 DVDs with a counted English VobSub track");
    assert_eq!(line(&h, "  placed, no review "), "  placed, no review     6 of 6 judged tracks (row 14 (a) asks for at least half)");
    assert_eq!(
        line(&h, "  as it stands: "),
        "  as it stands: not answered: too few titles with regular and SDH, discs with such titles, feature films with such a title, TV episodes with such a title, SDH tracks, regular tracks, forced tracks with events, commentary tracks"
    );
    assert_eq!(line(&h, "  not counted: "), "  not counted: pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd 1, the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray 3");
    assert_eq!(section(&h, "Costly verdicts ("), ["  none"]);
    assert_eq!(h.lines.last().map(String::as_str), Some("RESULT ok"));
    assert_eq!((h.labelled, h.placed_without_review, h.costly.len(), h.exit_code), (6, 6, 0, 0));
}
```

```rust
/// Prints `line` to stderr and returns `code`.
fn fail(err: &mut dyn Write, line: &str, code: i32) -> i32 {
    let _ = writeln!(err, "{line}");
    code
}

/// The spec file and how it is shown: --spec as given (taken against cwd), else the design spec under the repository
/// root; None when neither names one.
fn spec_file(ctx: &Ctx, flag: Option<String>) -> Option<(PathBuf, String)> {
    match flag {
        Some(given) => Some((ctx.abs(&given), given)),
        None => default_spec(ctx).map(|path| {
            let shown = path.display().to_string();
            (path, shown)
        }),
    }
}

/// `retune --subtitles`: row 14 from the spec (exit 2 when it cannot be read), the evidence (resolve_evidence's code),
/// the OCR text (--text DIR, else LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT, else none; exit 2 for a folder that is not there), then the
/// subtitle harness with spec 14's default settings; its report on stdout and its exit code. RP15, spec 15.
fn run_subtitles(
    ctx: &Ctx,
    evidence_flag: Option<&str>,
    spec_path: &Path,
    spec_shown: &str,
    text_flag: Option<&str>,
    out: &mut dyn Write,
    err: &mut dyn Write,
) -> i32 {
    let row14 = match read_text_file(spec_path, spec_shown, Encoding::Utf8Sig).and_then(|text| exp14_requirements(&text)) {
        Ok(row14) => row14,
        Err(message) => return fail(err, &message, 2),
    };
    let evidence = match resolve_evidence(ctx, evidence_flag) {
        Ok(dir) => dir,
        Err(Refused { code, line }) => return fail(err, &line, code),
    };
    let tree = match DiskTree::open(&evidence, EVIDENCE_SHOWN) {
        Ok(tree) => tree,
        Err(e) => return fail(err, &os_error_text(&e, &evidence.display().to_string()), 3),
    };
    let text = match ocr_text_dir(ctx, text_flag) {
        None => None,
        Some(dir) => {
            let shown = dir.display().to_string();
            if !dir.is_dir() {
                return fail(err, &format!("the OCR text folder {shown} does not exist {TEXT_HINT}"), 2);
            }
            match DiskTree::open(&dir, &shown) {
                Ok(tree) => Some(tree),
                Err(e) => return fail(err, &os_error_text(&e, &shown), 2),
            }
        }
    };
    let h = subtitle_harness(&tree, text.as_ref().map(|tree| tree as &dyn Tree), &row14, &Settings::default());
    for line in &h.lines {
        let _ = writeln!(out, "{line}");
    }
    h.exit_code
}
```

```rust
impl Settings {
    /// Every problem, in key order: staging_root inside movies_root or tv_root (or equal to one); tuning_root inside

    /// `Settings::default().validate()` is exactly one problem, keyed `tuning_root` (spec 14's defaults turn
    /// keep_tuning_evidence on and leave tuning_root unset); `lazymkv-dev plan` prints the problems and plans with them.
    /// Spec 7, 14. Def: T1. Use: T15.

    // the settings file `plan --settings FILE` reads

    /// Err, one sentence, only when the text cannot be read: text that is not JSON (serde_json's message), text that is

    /// the settings with validate()'s problems, possibly none: a caller that needs a valid file checks the vector, and

/// --settings FILE with `Settings::from_json`, which returns the settings with validate's problems, so a file whose only
/// problems are validate's still plans; only from_json's Err refuses the file. Def: T15. Use: T15, T16, T19.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct PlanDoc { pub slug: String, pub inputs: PlanInputsSummary, pub settings: Settings, pub settings_problems: Vec<SettingsProblem>, pub plan: Plan }
/// The argument, borrowed: a resolved recording, or a bare scan file. Def: T15. Use: T15, T16.
pub enum PlanSource<'a> { Recording(&'a Recording), ScanFile(&'a std::path::Path) }
/// The optional files. Def: T15. Use: T15, T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct PlanOptions { pub settings: Option<std::path::PathBuf>, pub tmdb_search: Option<std::path::PathBuf>, pub tmdb_record: Option<std::path::PathBuf>, pub remembered: Option<std::path::PathBuf> }
/// A recording (slug or directory): reads scan.txt, meta.json (fingerprint, disc_id), the first of
/// `disc::bdmt_candidates` under nav/BDMV/META/DL through `disc::bdmt_name`, thediscdb-hash.json (`parse_dischash`),
/// thediscdb-discid.json (`parse_discid`), tmdb.json (`parse_recorded`), lookup-status.txt; an absent lookup file means that
/// lookup was not made, an answer file whose status line is not 200 is not parsed (the recorder keeps the error body of a
/// 404 or a failed lookup), and only a file that exists, answered 200 or has no status line, and does not parse is
/// Refused { code: 2 }. A bare scan file
/// `<dir>/discNN.txt` is a pinned log: its fingerprint is `fingerprint::content_hash(&fingerprint::hashed_files(log))` of
/// its HSH lines; `discdb_by_fingerprint` is `corpus/thediscdb-api/dischash-<fingerprint>.json` under `repo_root(ctx.cwd)`
/// when present (it carries media), else `<dir>/discNN.json` with the same stem (no media: kind and TMDb ID then unknown);
/// `discdb_by_disc_id` is None (TheDiscDB's global_disc_id is not the disc ID, spec 5); no TMDb answer. A directory argument
/// is always a recording. Then --tmdb-search, --tmdb-record, --remembered and --settings when given; the disc name with
/// `lookup::name::disc_name(bdmt, disc.volume_label)`; PlanInputs with no sessions, no overrides and default LibraryFacts;
/// `plan::plan`. Refused { code: 2 } only; exit 3 comes from the caller's resolve_recording. Def: T15. Use: T15, T16.
pub fn plan_doc(ctx: &Ctx, source: &PlanSource<'_>, options: &PlanOptions) -> Result<PlanDoc, Refused>;
/// `plan`'s entry point: tests `ctx.abs(arg).is_file()` first (a scan file), and only otherwise calls `resolve_recording`
/// (which refuses a path-shaped argument that is not a directory, so `plan corpus/owner/x/scan.txt` would exit 2). Exit 0 when
/// the plan is printed, with or without review reasons or settings problems; 2 for an argument error or any refusal of
/// plan_doc (an unreadable scan, or a lookup, settings, TMDb or remembered file that does not parse, and also a scan that
/// cannot be typed or planned and a remembered file for another fingerprint); 3 when a slug is given and the evidence clone
/// is absent; never 1 (RP24). Def: T15. Use: T15.
pub fn run(ctx: &Ctx, args: &[String], out: &mut dyn Write, err: &mut dyn Write) -> i32;

// crates/dev/src/cmd/decide.rs additions (Task 16)
/// The file phase for one rip label: the verify report that maps the file onto the scan, the facts built from the label's
/// files (md5 from the level folders' manifests, profiles from ffprobe-streams.json through `stream_of_track`, events through
/// `verify::subtitle_events`, verdicts from the `audio` section with their `main=` reference, text decisions from the
/// `subtitles` section through `verify::by_scan_stream`), and the FileDecision. Def: T16. Use: T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct DecisionDoc { pub title_key: String, pub verify: VerifyReport, pub facts: FactsSummary, pub decision: FileDecision }
/// Which scan streams each fact covered. Def: T16. Use: T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct FactsSummary { pub md5_streams: Vec<u32>, pub profile_streams: Vec<u32>, pub event_streams: Vec<u32>, pub verdict_streams: Vec<u32>, pub verdict_reference: Option<u32>, pub text_streams: Vec<u32>, pub removed: Vec<u32> }
/// A section that can be skipped, as decide.rs's AudioEntry and SubtitleEntry are. Def: T16. Use: T16.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(untagged)]
pub enum PlanEntry { Results(PlanDoc), Skipped { skipped: String } }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(untagged)]
pub enum DecisionEntry { Results(DecisionDoc), Skipped { skipped: String } }
/// `DecideDoc` gains, after `reviews`: `pub plan: PlanEntry` and `pub decision: DecisionEntry`. `decide_doc` fills both after
/// `reviews`: `plan_doc(ctx, &PlanSource::Recording(rec), &PlanOptions::default())` (Skipped with the refusal's line when it
/// refuses), then `decision_doc` (Skipped with its Err sentence when the plan does not include the label's title or an
/// input cannot be read). The existing goldens stay safe because tests/decide.rs compares section by section. Def: T16. Use: T16.
pub fn decision_doc(ctx: &Ctx, rec: &Recording, label: &str, plan: &PlanDoc, doc: &DecideDoc) -> Result<DecisionDoc, String>;
```

````markdown
# Phase 1: the decision core

Phase 1 of the design spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-04-lazymkv-design.md`, section 16, row "1. Decision
core") delivers `core`, with a command that reads a recording and prints the plan, decisions, confidences and review
reasons as JSON, tested on any OS. It was built in two parts. The first was the Rust port of phase 0's Python
analysers (pull request krcm0209/lazymkv#2; its design is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-rust-port-design.md`, and
[`rust-port-tests.md`](rust-port-tests.md) maps its tests). The second, on the branch `phase-1-decision-core`, built
the rest of `core` from the design spec, and the command: `lazymkv-dev plan` for the disc phase, and two new sections
of `lazymkv-dev decide` for the file phase.

Nothing the second part added runs an external program, reads a disc, touches a share or uses the network. Every new
rule is a pure function in `crates/core` over typed inputs: the parsed scan, the recorded or synthetic TheDiscDB and TMDb (The
Movie Database) answers, and explicit input structs for the facts the engine will measure in phase 2 (packet MD5
sums, ffprobe profiles, subtitle events, the content and text verdicts, library facts, the owner's review decisions).
`crates/dev` reads the recordings and fills those structs.

## What `core` holds

| Module | Design spec | What it decides |
|---|---|---|
| `settings` | 14, 7 | Every setting with its default; a settings file names only the keys it changes; the checks of the roots (a staging root inside a library root, the tuning root) and of the values the rules divide by or compare against |
| `review` | 8.8, and the notes of 8.6, 8.7, 8.9 and 7 | The closed sets of review reasons and notes, with the spec's spellings |
| `codec` | 8.6 "Codecs", 8.10 | MakeMKV's codec names (attributes 5, 6 and 7) to a family, a fidelity tier and a display name; the bitrate of attribute 13; channel layouts; the object-based extension (Atmos, DTS:X); mkvmerge's names for the verification |
| `lang` (extended) | 8.6 "Languages", R4 | The wanted languages: English and the original language |
| `disc` | 9.4, 9.5, 5, 6.1 step 2 | The typed disc model over the parsed scan: titles, streams, flags, the MakeMKV version, Java use, the `bdmt` disc name, title matching by source file, segment map and duration |
| `lookup` (`discdb`, `tmdb`, `name`) | 8.1 | TheDiscDB and TMDb answers, the disc name and its cleaning, plausibility, the runtime checks, the identity and its confidence |
| `plan` (`kind`, `movie`, `tv`) | 6.1 step 5, 8.2 to 8.5, 5, 7 | The disc kind, the feature or the cuts (by TheDiscDB, by the Java playlist labels, by structure), editions, TV episodes and season sessions, title keys, the mode (direct or whole-disc copy), the space needed |
| `remembered` | 5, 11 | Remembered decisions and the owner's review decisions (overrides), matched to a new scan |
| `tracks` (`audio`, `subtitle`, `layout`) | 8.6, 8.7, 8.10 | The audio tracks kept, dropped and ordered; the English subtitle roles, the forced track and the subtitle confidence; the names, flags and order of the tracks in the final file |
| `naming` | 8.9, 8.4, 11 | Library paths for films, editions and episodes; the compatibility tag; sanitisation; the copy label of a second copy |
| `verify` | 6.2 step 7, 6.4 step 14 | A ripped or remuxed file against the scan or the decision; read errors |
| `decision` | 6.4 step 11, 8.8, 11 | One title's file decision: tracks, path, the three confidences (identity, title, track), review reasons, notes and the disposition (auto-file or review) |
| `job` | 10.1, 10.2, 5, 12 | The job state reducer: states, events, actions, the waiting states and the state each returns to, failure classes, resume rules, the job ID |
| `subtitle::labels` | 15, 17 row 14 | The owner's subtitle labels file and the subtitle harness that `retune --subtitles` runs |

The port's modules keep their behaviour: `core::reconcile` and its goldens are byte-identical (it is the Python's
rule; `verify` is the product's rule beside it), and so are `decide`'s six existing sections and their goldens.
`fingerprint` gained `hashed_files` (the `HSH:` lines of a TheDiscDB scan log, moved there from a test so `plan` can
fingerprint a pinned log) and `recording::files::Tmdb` gained the optional fields of the recorded `tmdb.json`.

## Running it

The commands are in the `lazymkv-dev` binary (`crates/dev`). On a machine with the Rust toolchain:

```bash
cargo run -q -p lazymkv-dev -- --help
```

On the Mac, which has no toolchain, every command runs on the mini PC through `scripts/box.sh`, which mirrors the
tree there first:

```bash
scripts/box.sh cargo run -q -p lazymkv-dev -- --help
```

A slug (`pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd`) is read under the evidence clone: `corpus/owner/`, or `--evidence DIR`, or the
`LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE` environment variable; without it a slug exits 3 with a line naming the evidence repository. The
mini PC keeps a mirror of the clone at `C:\lazymkv\evidence\owner`, reached through a junction:

```bash
scripts/box.sh "(if not exist corpus mkdir corpus)&& mklink /J corpus\owner C:\lazymkv\evidence\owner&& set LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE=C:\lazymkv\evidence\owner&& cargo run -q -p lazymkv-dev -- plan pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd"
```

`plan` and `decide` print their documents as JSON with an indent of 1 and ASCII escapes, as `decide` printed it before
phase 1; `labels` and `retune` print text lines.

### `lazymkv-dev plan`

```
lazymkv-dev plan <slug|recording dir|scan file> [--evidence DIR] [--settings FILE] [--tmdb-search FILE] [--tmdb-record FILE] [--remembered FILE]
```

The disc phase of design spec 6.1 step 5, over what a recording holds. The argument is one of:

- a slug or a recording directory: `scan.txt`, `meta.json` (the fingerprint and the disc ID), the disc name in
  `nav/BDMV/META/DL/bdmt_*.xml`, `thediscdb-hash.json`, `thediscdb-discid.json`, `tmdb.json` and `lookup-status.txt`.
  A lookup file that is absent means that lookup was not made, and is not an error; an answer file that
  `lookup-status.txt` records as 200 (or that has no status line) and does not parse is (exit 2); an answer recorded
  with another status (a 404, a failed lookup) is not parsed. A directory is always read as a recording.
- a bare scan log, such as one of the pinned public logs `corpus/thediscdb/<kind>/<work>/<release>/discNN.txt`: its
  fingerprint comes from the log's `HSH` lines, TheDiscDB's answer from `corpus/thediscdb-api/dischash-<fingerprint>.json`
  when that file exists (it carries the TMDb ID and the kind), else from the `discNN.json` beside the log (which does
  not), and there is no TMDb answer. TheDiscDB's disc-ID lookup is not made, because TheDiscDB's `global_disc_id` is
  not the disc ID of design spec 5.

The options:

- `--settings FILE`: a JSON object of design spec 14's keys. Absent keys keep their defaults; an unknown key or a
  wrong type refuses the file (exit 2, `<file>: <key>: <problem>`). The problems of the checks of the roots and
  values are printed in `settings_problems`, and the plan is made with the settings anyway. The defaults themselves raise exactly one
  problem, keyed `tuning_root`: section 14 turns `keep_tuning_evidence` on and leaves `tuning_root` unset, which the
  engine will refuse.
- `--tmdb-search FILE` and `--tmdb-record FILE`: a TMDb search answer (`/search/multi`) and a TMDb record (`/movie/{id}`,
  or `/tv/{id}` with its seasons and the season's episodes). No search answer and no full record is recorded anywhere
  in the evidence (the recorded `tmdb.json` is a slim form without runtimes or seasons), so these files are written by
  hand in TMDb's documented shapes; phase 2's client checks the shapes against the live service.
- `--remembered FILE`: a remembered-decisions file (`core::remembered::Remembered` as JSON), as the engine will keep
  one per fingerprint (design spec 5 and 11).

The document has the keys `slug`, `inputs` (which files were found and what each lookup answered), `settings`,
`settings_problems` and `plan`. The plan's keys are `identity` (the step of 8.1 that decided, the confidence, the TMDb
identity, title, year, original language, the step's review reason, the plausible results, the runtime check,
whether a lookup is pending, and one sentence per piece of evidence), `kind` and `kind_source`, `titles` (each with its key, title number, role,
duration, size and source file, and whether it was suggested or remembered), `mode`, `identity_confidence`,
`title_confidence`, `reviews`, `notes`, `wanted` (the wanted languages), `session` (the TV season session) and
`evidence` (what the planner saw).

Exit codes: 0 when the document was printed, with or without review reasons or settings problems; 2 for an
argument error, a scan that cannot be read, typed or planned, a lookup file (answered 200 or without a status line), a
settings file, a TMDb file (`--tmdb-search`, `--tmdb-record`) or a remembered file that does not parse, or a remembered
file for another fingerprint; 3 when a slug is given and the evidence clone is absent; never 1: nothing `plan` checks is
a verdict.

For example, over John Wick's pinned ultra-high-definition (UHD) log (run on any machine, the log is in this repository):

```bash
cargo run -q -p lazymkv-dev -- plan "corpus/thediscdb/movie/John Wick (2014)/4k-ultra-hd--blu-ray/disc01.txt"
```

TheDiscDB knows the log's fingerprint, so the identity is step `discdb_one` at 0.95 (TMDb movie 245891); the
database rule picks title 0 (`00001.mpls`), whose key is `t00-00001`; the title confidence is 0.98, the mode is
`direct` and there is no review reason.

The plans the tests pin, one per pinned log and per recording of the evidence clone (`crates/dev/tests/plan.rs`; the
recordings' rows skip without the clone):

| Log or recording | Identity | Kind | Title rule and titles (in `Plan.titles` order) | Title confidence, mode | Reviews |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| John Wick UHD, `disc01.txt` | discdb_one 0.95, movie 245891 | movie | database: title 0 (00001.mpls; title 8 has the same segment map), key `t00-00001` | 0.98, Direct | none |
| John Wick Blu-ray, `disc02.txt` | discdb_one 0.95, movie 245891 | movie | database: title 0 (00001.mpls), key `t00-00001` | 0.98, Direct | none |
| Expendables 3, `disc01.txt` | discdb_one 0.95, movie 138103 | movie | database: title 41 (00756.mpls), edition `Unrated Cut` (from the Java label table, `FPL_MainFeature_UR`; see Choices the owner should confirm) | 0.98, Direct | none |
| Smile, `disc01.txt` | discdb_one 0.95, movie 882598 | movie | database: title 14 (00040.mpls) | 0.98, Direct | none |
| Knowing DVD, `disc01.txt` | discdb_one 0.95, movie 13811 | movie | database: title 0 (attribute 24 `"01"`), key `t00-title01` | 0.98, Direct | none |
| Chernobyl disc 1, `disc01.txt` | discdb_one 0.95, tv 87108 | tv | mapped: title 1 S01E01, title 8 S01E02, title 7 S01E03 | 0.98, Direct | none; name `CHERNOBYL_D1`, disc 1, no season |
| Chernobyl disc 2, `disc02.txt` | discdb_one 0.95, tv 87108 | tv | mapped: title 6 S01E04, title 8 S01E05 | 0.98, Direct | none |
| Firefly disc 1, `disc01.txt` | discdb_one 0.95, tv 1437 | tv | mapped (attribute 24): title 0 S01E01, title 1 S01E02, title 2 S01E03 | 0.98, Direct | none |
| Firefly disc 2, `disc02.txt` | discdb_one 0.95, tv 1437 | tv | mapped (attribute 24): titles 0, 1, 2, 5 as S01E04 to S01E07 | 0.98, Direct | none |
| `pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd` (clone) | discdb_one 0.95 (discid answered 404), movie 1417, original `es`, wanted eng and spa | movie | database: title 0 (00800.mpls); name from `bdmt_eng.xml` | 0.98, Direct | none |
| `the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray` (clone) | discdb_one 0.95, tv 2316 | tv | mapped: title 3 S03E12-E13, title 2 S03E14, title 1 S03E15, title 0 S03E16, title 6 S03E17, title 5 S03E18 (ordered by episode); season 3 and disc 3 from `THE OFFICE S3D3` | 0.98, Direct | none |
| `short-circuit-1986-dvd` (clone) | nothing 0 (no answers; no search recorded) | movie | structure: one rival, title 0 | 0.85, Direct | identity_unknown |
| `short-circuit-2-1988-dvd` (clone) | nothing 0 (`DVD_VIDEO` is generic) | movie | structure: title 0 (1:50:06) | 0.85, Direct | identity_unknown |

All nine pinned logs have their TheDiscDB answer in `corpus/thediscdb-api`: the fingerprint of each log's `HSH` lines
is the `ContentHash` of its `discNN.json` and names one of the nine `dischash-*.json` answers there, so every pinned
row's identity and kind are TheDiscDB's.

### `lazymkv-dev decide`

```
lazymkv-dev decide (<slug> <label> | --rec DIR) [--text DIR] [--selection all|eng] [--settings FILE] [--evidence DIR]
```

The port's command, for one rip label of a recording. Its six sections, `slug`, `label`, `reconcile`, `audio`,
`subtitles` and `reviews`, and their goldens are unchanged. Phase 1 appends two, and adds `--settings FILE`: a JSON
file of design spec 14's keys, read as `plan --settings FILE` reads it, that the `plan` and `decision` sections both
use in place of the defaults.

- `plan`: the `plan` command's document for the recording, with the default settings or those `--settings FILE`
  names, or `{"skipped": "<reason>"}` when it refuses.
- `decision`: the file phase (design spec 6.4 step 11) for the label's title, or `{"skipped": "<reason>"}` when the
  plan does not include that title or an input cannot be read. It holds `title_key`; `verify`, the report that maps
  the file's tracks onto the scan's streams (6.2 step 7); `facts`, which scan streams each measured fact covered (the
  packet MD5 sums from the level folders' manifests, the ffprobe profiles, the subtitle events of `subs/`, the content
  verdicts of the `audio` section and their reference, the text decisions of the `subtitles` section, the streams the
  rip removed); and `decision`: the audio and subtitle tracks kept and dropped, their order, flags and names
  (`layout`), the resolution, the edition, the final path, the three confidences, the review reasons, the notes, the
  read errors and the disposition (`auto_file` or `needs_review`). With the default settings no library root is set,
  so `decide` builds no path (`path` is null) and every decision is held for review; the tests make a second decision
  with the owner's roots to pin the paths. When the `plan` section is skipped, the `decision` section is skipped with
  `no plan: ` and the same line.

The text decisions are there only when OCR (optical character recognition) text is found (`--text DIR`, or `LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT`), as for the port's
`subtitles` section. The top-level `reviews` stays the port's union of the audio verdicts' and the subtitle
decisions' reasons; the decision's own `reviews` are the product's (8.8). The exit codes are the port's: 0; 1 when a
reconcile verdict is no; 2 for an argument error, an unreadable input or a folder that is not a rip label; 3 for a
slug without the evidence clone. A skipped section never changes the exit code.

### `lazymkv-dev labels --subtitles`

The owner's subtitle labels live beside the audio labels in a recording: `<slug>/subtitle-labels.json`, whose format
line is `lazymkv subtitle labels v1`. Each entry names a track by its rip label and stream and says:

- `kind`: one of `regular`, `sdh`, `forced`, `commentary`, `trivia`, `lyrics`, `translation`, `dub-transcript`,
  `closed-captions`, `other`;
- `how` the owner knows it: `read` or `watched` (the owner read or watched the track's text; only these two count,
  decision D23), or one of the observations `packaging`, `menu`, `flag` (a flag in MakeMKV's scan), `player`, `thediscdb`;
- `sure`, `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `saw_verdict` (a label given after seeing the verdict never counts) and `note`;
- `style`: `uk` for a UK-style SDH track (speakers by colour, sounds without brackets; ruling RP25), else null.

`lazymkv-dev labels --subtitles kinds` lists the kinds and sources; `set`, `unset` and `check` add or replace one
entry, remove one (recording why and when, as the audio labels' `unset` does) and check a file. The problems are the audio labels' sentences with
"subtitle" for "audio", and the validation is shared with them. The exit codes are `labels`' own: 0, or 2 for an
argument error, a file that does not validate or a change that would add a problem. `lazymkv-dev --help` prints the
synopsis.

### `lazymkv-dev retune --subtitles`

```
lazymkv-dev retune [--evidence DIR] [--set NAME=VALUE ...] [--snapshot FILE] [--compare FILE] [--spec FILE] [--allow-unmeasured] [--subtitles] [--text DIR]
```

`--subtitles` takes only `--evidence`, `--spec` and `--text`; with `--set`, `--snapshot`, `--compare` or
`--allow-unmeasured` it is an argument error (exit 2). The subtitle thresholds are design spec 14's defaults
(`Settings::default().text_rule()`).

With `--subtitles`, the subtitle harness of design spec 15 (ruling RP15 below). For every labelled English or
no-language subtitle track of every rip label in the evidence, it verifies the rip against the scan and judges the
track by the subtitle text rule of 8.7 "Text" over the OCR text found under `--text DIR` (or `LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT`). For
a stream the text rule sets aside (the DVD closed captions), it judges the classifier of 8.7 instead. Beside each
judged track it shows what the classifier of 8.7 decides from the `subs/` events. A track without OCR text is listed
as not judged. It then reports:

- the count per kind of the labels made by reading or watching (D23) that the owner is sure of and gave before seeing the verdict (`saw_verdict` false; ruling RP25), against the kinds section 17 row 14 requires, and row 14's UK-style SDH track, counted from the counted `sdh` labels whose `style` is `uk`,
  read from the spec text as the audio harness reads row 13 (`--spec`, default the design spec under the repository
  root); a label on one of the two discs row 14 names as fitting discs is reported but never counted;
- the costly verdicts as row 14 defines them, each without a review: a dialogue track dropped
  (`dialogue_dropped`), SDH (subtitles for the deaf and hard of hearing) placed as regular (`sdh_as_regular`) or regular as SDH (`regular_as_sdh`), a track
  forced wrongly (`forced_wrongly`), a forced track placed as dialogue (`forced_as_dialogue`), and a commentary, trivia
  or lyrics track kept (`unwanted_kept`);
- how many labelled tracks the rules placed without a review.

It exits 1 on any costly verdict; 2 for an argument error, a spec problem or a subtitle labels file that does not
validate; 3 when there is no label, or when any labelled English or no-language track could not be judged (its rip,
scan or OCR text could not be read; for example without the evidence clone or without `--text`).

## Rulings of the phase 1 plan

The plan recorded these rulings (RP1 to RP9 are the port's, in its design). The owner can overturn any of them.

- RP10. Phase 1 is design spec section 16's decision core and nothing of phase 2. The items the spec marks "to be
  designed in phase 1" that concern the engine (D17's bundling table in 4.4 and 19, the app's own recording format,
  the form of the tuning evidence, the decoding of bitmap subtitles for OCR, code signing) are phase 2 design work.
- RP11. The verification rule of 6.2 step 7 and 6.4 step 14 (closed captions first, the DVD duration band from 2 s
  shorter to 1% longer, the codec through attributes 41 and 42, `MSG:4047` mapped through the selection, MakeMKV-only
  flags carried onto the output tracks) is a new module, `core::verify`. `core::reconcile` and its goldens stay
  byte-identical, and `lazymkv-dev reconcile` keeps it.
- RP12. The job state reducer of 10.1 is in `core`: every state, event and action of 10.1, the transition table, the
  waiting states' return states and the resume rules, with a test per transition and per resume rule. The engine
  performs the actions in phase 2.
- RP13. Identification (8.1) is pure over recorded or synthetic answers. The DVD disc ID (libdvdread's) stays
  unimplemented, as design spec 5 says, since nothing could check it; a DVD is looked up by its fingerprint alone.
- RP14. The command is `lazymkv-dev plan` (the disc phase) and `decide`'s two new sections (the file phase), with
  `decide`'s existing sections and goldens unchanged. Phase 2 folds both into `lazymkvctl`.
- RP15. Design spec 15's "the subtitle text rule's thresholds (8.7) are brought under `retune` in phase 1" is
  `subtitle-labels.json`, `lazymkv-dev labels --subtitles` and `lazymkv-dev retune --subtitles` (amended by RP25).
- RP16. Remembered decisions are a `core` type with pure functions: a remembered title matches a scan title by source
  file, segment map and duration within 2 s, and the audio and subtitle overrides are keyed by the stream's signature
  (type, language, codec, channels, position among identical streams). Keeping them is phase 2's.
- RP17. Season sessions (8.5) are a `core` record with pure functions (`find`, `suggest`, `assign`, `close`); keeping
  them is phase 2's.
- RP18. Edition naming (8.4) takes "the library folder already holds an edition-named file" and "an earlier filed copy
  of that cut" as inputs (`LibraryFacts`); reading the library is phase 2's.
- RP19. `core` stays free of I/O: every new function takes parsed values, text or a `Tree` (the dev crate's tree over
  the disk, or an in-memory one in tests). No new crate.
- RP20. The new modules are written from the spec, not from any Python. New JSON documents use the struct's field
  order and the spec's spellings, and keyed collections are sorted maps (in a type written as JSON, sorted lists of
  named entries: RP23).
- RP21. No test in `crates/` holds a byte copy of, or a value read only from, `corpus/owner`; dev tests over the clone
  read it at run time.
- RP22. `Settings::from_json` is the one reader of a settings file. It refuses, in one sentence naming the key, only
  text that is not one JSON object or a key it cannot read (a key the settings lack, or a value of the wrong type);
  otherwise it returns the settings with the problems the checks of design spec 14 and section 7 find, and
  `lazymkv-dev plan` prints those problems and plans anyway.
- RP23. A type written as JSON (the plan, the decision, the remembered decisions, the season session, the job's
  events and the commands' documents) holds no map keyed by a number, since serde cannot read one back through an
  untagged or flattened type; it holds a list of named entries sorted by their key (`title`, `stream`, or both).
  Types never written as JSON keep their maps.
- RP24. `lazymkv-dev plan` exits 0 (planned, with or without review reasons or settings problems), 2 (an argument
  error, an unreadable scan, or a lookup, settings, TMDb or remembered file that does not parse) and 3 (a slug given
  and the evidence clone absent), never 1; `decide` keeps 0, 1, 2, 3 with the port spec's meanings.
- RP25. Amends RP15: besides `label`, `stream`, `kind`, `how`, `sure`, `date` and `note`, a subtitle label has the
  required `saw_verdict` (a label given after seeing the rule's verdict never counts, as with the audio labels) and
  `style` (null, or `uk` for row 14's UK-style SDH track), and `how` gains the observation `flag`.
  `labels --subtitles set` takes `--saw-verdict yes|no` and `--style uk`; `retune --subtitles` counts only labels
  read or watched, sure and given before the verdict, and counts the UK-style SDH track from `style`.
- RP26. VC-1 video (`V_MS/VFW/WVC1`) is a codec family of its own, matched on attribute 5 alone, with the display
  and mkvmerge name `VC-1`, and no tier.
- RP27. Four note names the design spec describes only in words keep the plan's spellings until the owner confirms
  them: `possible_audio_description` (the port's ruling RP7), `lossy_before_lossless` (decision D9),
  `direct_mode_fallback` (6.3 step 6a) and `label_rule_unavailable` (8.3 rule 2 with 10.2).

## Choices the owner should confirm

The plan settled these where the spec leaves a choice open; each is pinned by a test, and each can be changed by
changing that test and its rule. The first four are open questions the plan puts to the owner; until the owner rules,
the plan keeps the reading given.

- Open question: a movie disc with an extras play-all. Read literally, 8.3 rule 3.1 makes any group whose segments are
  two or more other groups' in order a play-all title, and the disc then TV. Smile's deleted-scenes playlist (title
  117) is one. Without a TheDiscDB match or Java labels, such a movie disc is planned as TV, unless TheDiscDB states it
  is a movie. The owner may limit 3.1 to play-all titles whose parts are episode-length (15 to 120 minutes).
- Open question: two label cuts with the same edition name. 8.3 rule 2's table names both the plain `FPL_MainFeature`
  row and the `_R` row "Theatrical Cut". A disc carrying both is planned at 0.60 with `title_ambiguous` ("two cuts are
  both named Theatrical Cut") rather than 0.90; two TheDiscDB main movies that would be filed under one name get the
  same 0.60 rather than 0.98. The owner may rule that they are one cut, or that 0.90 stands.
- Open question: the default subtitle when the default audio is not English and no regular English track is kept.
  8.10 names only the regular track; the plan makes the SDH track the default. The owner may rule that no subtitle is
  default.
- Open question: leading periods in a path component. 8.9 trims trailing spaces and periods only, so a title that
  begins with periods (`...And Justice for All`) would give a folder and a file hidden on the share. The plan drops
  leading periods as well as leading spaces (`And Justice for All (1979) {tmdb-ID}`). The owner may confirm it or rule
  another treatment.
- A TMDb record without a runtime (or a season without episode runtimes) fails 8.1's runtime check, so step 4 cannot
  pass and step 5 applies (0.50, `identity_ambiguous`).
- Identity step 2 (TheDiscDB by both disc ID and fingerprint, 0.99) needs both records and, when both carry a TMDb ID,
  the same one; with different IDs the fingerprint's record wins at step 3 (0.95) and the disagreement is written to
  the identity's evidence.
- 8.3 rule 1 ("reconciles with the scan") means every `MainMovie` title of TheDiscDB's record matches a scan title;
  if one matches none, the record falls to rule 2. A `MainMovie`'s edition comes from its item title, else from the
  Java label table (Expendables 3's `FPL_MainFeature_UR` gives `Unrated Cut`).
- 8.3 rule 2 runs before identification with English only, and again with the original language once TMDb gives it;
  only the variant chosen within a cut can change between the two passes.
- On a DVD, TheDiscDB's `source_file` is the DVD title number (attribute 24), compared as a number; DVD title groups
  are keyed by attribute 24 and the segment map, because a DVD's segment numbers restart in every title.
- The closed-caption stream of a DVD is recognised by its codec (`S_CC608/DVD`), not by attribute 41 alone.
- Three TheDiscDB description kinds are provisional, because TheDiscDB's wording for them is not yet known: isolated
  score, music and effects, and a plain subtitle description (one containing "subtitle", or one equal to the track's
  own language name).
- The object-based audio extension is read from ffprobe's profile ("Atmos", "DTS:X"), else from attribute 7
  ("TrueHD Atmos"); both spellings are provisional until experiment 6 runs.
- In 8.6's ranking, a lossy track without bitrate text comes after every lossy track with one, and guard G1 treats it
  as at or below 256 kb/s.
- A title with exactly one English subtitle stream and no subtitle events keeps it as regular "English" at 0.90.
- The text rule's disagreement (8.7 "Text") compares roles only, and one review note names every disagreeing stream.
- Library paths use the root's own separator (a backslash when the root holds one or is a UNC (universal naming convention) path, else a slash);
  `core` never asks the host. The 255-byte cap cuts on a character boundary after Unicode normalisation form C (NFC).
- `Settings` also refuses an `auto_threshold` outside 0 to 1, `subs_diff_max` above `subs_same_min`, and a zero
  `minlength_s`, `feature_min_minutes` or `file_phase_concurrency`.
- The verification needs every expected track to pair in order and tolerates no extra track in the file; read errors
  are kept by offset with their count and the error text only, never the drive's name or serial number.
- Verification lowers no confidence: a failed or read-error rip holds the job through its review reason
  (`verify_failed`, `read_errors`).
- The owner's review decisions each cover one confidence and set it to 1.00; a re-plan and the file decision both
  apply them, so a job approved at the disposition gate needs no re-plan.
- 10.1's two transitions to `Ripping` from `Copying` pass through the direct plan's space check, and a failed eject
  ends the disc phase like an eject and sends `eject_failed` instead of `disc_done`.
- VC-1 video (`V_MS/VFW/WVC1`) is a codec family of its own (ruling RP26), matched on attribute 5 alone because no
  recording shows its attributes 6 and 7, and its rip verifies against mkvmerge's documented name `VC-1`, a spelling
  not yet seen either.
- 8.3 rule 4 lowers a rule 3 plan only when every feature is more than 10% from TMDb's runtime.
- TheDiscDB maps a TV disc only when every Episode item matches a scan title; otherwise the disc is unmapped (0.60,
  `tv_unmapped`, whole-disc copy).
- A decision without a path (no library root for its role, no TMDb identity, or a feature without a video height) is
  held for review with no review reason, since 8.8's closed set has none for it. An episode without a season or
  episode number has no path either, and raises `tv_unmapped`.

## Left for phase 2

- The `platform`, `tools`, `clients` and `engine` crates and `lazymkvctl` (design spec 4.2 and 16, row 2), which
  perform the job reducer's actions and fold `plan`, `decide` and `retune` into `lazymkvctl`.
- Keeping remembered decisions, season sessions and jobs; reading the library for `LibraryFacts` and path collisions.
- The TheDiscDB and TMDb clients, and the live check of the TMDb shapes that phase 1's synthetic answers follow.
- The DVD disc ID, the decoding of bitmap subtitles for OCR (decision D22), the app's own recording format and the
  form of the tuning evidence, D17's bundling table and code signing (RP10, RP13).
- The chapter count in the check of a remuxed file (`verify_final` checks the tracks and the duration only).

`cargo test --workspace -- --list` on the mini PC (Windows), on the tree of commit `@COMMIT@`, lists @TOTAL@ tests: @CORE@ in `lazymkv-core`, @DEV@ in `lazymkv-dev`, @CAPTURE@ in `lazymkv-capture` and @FAKE@ in `fake-tools`.

The lists are the mini PC's: a test compiled only on Windows (such as `lazymkv-capture`'s eject test) is in them, and a test compiled only on Unix is not.

Design spec 15 asks for a test of every rule of section 8 for its normal case and for each guard, review reason and
confidence row, and a test per transition and per resume rule of the state reducer; the plan's tasks hold to that.
The tests are:

- unit tests at the bottom of each module (or in a sibling `tests.rs` for `tracks::audio`, `tracks::subtitle`, `job`
  and `lookup`), over synthetic scans and answers and over the pinned TheDiscDB logs (`corpus/thediscdb`) and API
  answers (`corpus/thediscdb-api`); these always run;
- `crates/core/tests/thediscdb_corpus.rs`, the pinned logs as a corpus;
- the `lazymkv-dev` integration tests: `lookup_answers.rs` (the recorded TheDiscDB and TMDb answers of the evidence
  clone), `disc_model.rs` (the disc model over every recording's `scan.txt`),
  `verify.rs` (the recordings' rips against their scans), `plan.rs` (the command over the nine pinned logs, which
  always run, and the four recordings), `decide.rs` (the port's golden comparisons, unchanged, and the new `plan`
  and `decision` sections, including the Office's twin tracks dropped as duplicates by their packet MD5 sums),
  `labels_subtitles.rs` and `retune_subtitles.rs` (the subtitle labels and harness, over a synthetic recording and
  over the evidence clone).

```bash
````

```bash
ADDED=$((TOTAL - BASE))
[ "$TOTAL" -eq $((CORE + DEV + CAPTURE + FAKE)) ] && echo "sum ok" || echo "SUM DIFFERS"
sed -i '' -e "s/@COMMIT@/$COMMIT/g" -e "s/@TOTAL@/$TOTAL/g" -e "s/@CORE@/$CORE/g" -e "s/@DEV@/$DEV/g" -e "s/@CAPTURE@/$CAPTURE/g" -e "s/@FAKE@/$FAKE/g" -e "s/@BASE@/$BASE/g" -e "s/@ADDED@/$ADDED/g" docs/phase1/decision-core.md
grep -n '@[A-Z]*@' docs/phase1/decision-core.md || echo "no token left"
grep -n 'lists [0-9][0-9]* tests' docs/phase1/decision-core.md
grep -n 'listed [0-9][0-9]*, so' docs/phase1/decision-core.md
```
